spheres.full_exact_source_text: # Sphere of Blacksmith Qi Expression: Primary — Forge Qi; Supporting — Metal Qi, Fire Qi, Earth-Ore Qi, Refinement Qi. “A sword is not born when the edge becomes sharp. A sword is born when the ore accepts a name and the fire agrees to remember it.” Sphere Type: Crafting, Strategic, and Support Sphere Rules Baseline: 2024 fifth-edition rules (5.5e) Primary Paths: Qi Cultivation and Body Refining Secondary Path: Spirit Awakening Resource: CP, tools, materials, time, and Forge Marks Common Effects: forging, repair, battlefield tempering, edge-setting, armor fitting, material refinement, flaw-reading, tool consecration, weapon birth, spirit-awakening of objects, furnace projects, sect armories, temporary item improvements ## Blacksmith Dao Blacksmith is the cultivation of the accepted ordeal. A novice believes forging is striking metal until it changes shape. An adept understands that the hammer does not command the material. The hammer asks a question. The fire reveals the answer. The quench records the vow. A great blacksmith does not merely make weapons. They read flaws. They feed impurities to the fire. They strike only where the structure can bear truth. They cool a thing at the moment when it will remember its form. They listen for the first breath of an item spirit. The Sphere of Blacksmith governs: reading flaws in weapons, armor, tools, vessels, and materials; improving a workpiece through a visible process; battlefield repair and emergency tempering; sharpening, balancing, fitting, hardening, softening, and quenching; preparing objects to receive forged techniques, talisman scripts, formations, item spirits, or sect marks; turning raw material into useful form; creating temporary improvements quickly and permanent improvements through projects; awakening the story of a tool without replacing item-crafting systems. The Blacksmith does not win because they make a better number appear on an item. The Blacksmith wins because they know what a thing is trying to become, and they make the world pay the price required for that becoming. ### Sphere Sentence Blacksmith cultivators claim a workpiece, read its flaw, place Forge Marks through heat and hammering, and spend those marks to repair, temper, awaken, or unmake what the material is ready to become. ## Sphere Boundaries Blacksmith governs workpieces, tools, material flaws, forging sequences, repairs, temporary improvements, item preparation, and crafting projects. Metal governs immediate metal resonance, hardness, edges, armor pressure, conduction, and metallic answer. Fire governs flame, heat, combustion, burning transformation, and fiery pressure. Creation governs making objects from nothing or transforming material broadly. Earth governs foundation, burden, ground, stone, and carried weight. Glass governs transparent faultlines, panes, shattering, and refracted consequence. Talismans governs scripted formulas, stored techniques, and paper/jade/cloth inscriptions. Formations governs maintained arrays, rooms, workshops, furnace halls, sect infrastructure, and place-based systems. Sect Stewardship governs organizational access, petitions, resources, duties, and armory authority. Blacksmith can cooperate with all of these, but does not replace them. ### Blacksmith and Metal | Sphere | Primary Theme | | --- | --- | | Blacksmith | Transform a workpiece through process and flaw-reading | | Metal | Control metallic resonance, edge, hardness, conduction, and ringing answer | | Blacksmith + Metal | Spirit ore, ringing hammers, faultless alloys, resonant weapons, armor that remembers impact | A Blacksmith does not automatically manipulate distant metal. A Metal cultivator does not automatically craft permanent gear. ### Blacksmith and Fire | Sphere | Primary Theme | | --- | --- | | Blacksmith | Forge sequence, workpiece, flaw, temper, quench, name | | Fire | Heat, combustion, flame pressure, burning transformation | | Blacksmith + Fire | Furnace mastery, clean quenching, fire-fed refining, impossible heat control, artifact birth | A Blacksmith can use ordinary fire, furnace heat, CP, friction, spiritual heat, or cold-forge techniques as the fiction permits. A Fire cultivator can burn hot enough to ruin a blade unless they also learn how to listen to the material. ### No Formal Affinity Requirement This draft does not introduce a formal affinity subsystem. In-world, masters may still say that the best smiths often have Metal and Fire resonance. That means they usually possess Metal, Fire, related Insights, appropriate Path features, or story training. A character without Metal or Fire can still cultivate Blacksmith. They may be a cold-forge body refiner, a bone-and-jade crafter, a spirit-listening repairer, a sect armorer, or a talismanic toolmaker. ## Core Blacksmith Rules ### 2024 Fifth-Edition Baseline This sphere uses the 2024 fifth-edition rules baseline. Blacksmith talents supplement the normal rules for: Ability Checks; Tool Proficiencies; Help; Study; Search; Utilize; Improvised Damage; Object Armor Class and Hit Points; Magic Items; Weapon attacks; Armor and Shields; Crafting and downtime. A Blacksmith talent changes a normal rule only when it explicitly says so. ### Blacksmith Key Ability and Save DC Your Blacksmith key ability is Intelligence. Your Blacksmith Save DC is: 8 + Intelligence modifier + Proficiency Bonus A Path synergy, Insight, sect inheritance, or GM-approved cultivation method may replace Intelligence for some or all Blacksmith effects. ### Tool Proficiency When you learn Blacksmith, gain proficiency with Smith’s Tools. If you already have Smith’s Tools proficiency, gain proficiency with one of the following instead: Carpenter’s Tools; Jeweler’s Tools; Leatherworker’s Tools; Mason’s Tools; Tinker’s Tools; Weaver’s Tools; Woodcarver’s Tools; one relevant artisan’s tool approved by the GM. A Blacksmith technique may use a different tool if the workpiece calls for it. Smith’s Tools remain the default. ### Workpieces A workpiece is the object, material, tool, weapon, armor, shield, vessel, component, or prepared item you are currently forging, repairing, tempering, or unmaking. A workpiece can be: one weapon; one shield; one suit of armor; one tool; one object you can hold; one object you can touch; one damaged object; one batch of raw materials small enough to fit on your working surface; one vehicle part, gate, chain, bell, cauldron, furnace component, or similar object with GM permission. A creature is not a workpiece unless a talent explicitly allows body forging, graft work, or spirit-vessel work. A magic item can be a workpiece only if a talent allows it or the GM approves the attempt. Blacksmith can repair, tune, fit, or prepare many magic items, but cannot freely rewrite artifacts. ### Legal Working Surfaces Unless a talent says otherwise, you can work on a workpiece only if at least one of the following is true: you hold it; you touch it; it rests on a stable surface within your reach; it is worn or carried by a willing creature within your reach; it is part of a workshop, forge, anvil, tool bench, or prepared crafting station you are using. A hostile creature’s worn or carried equipment is not a legal workpiece unless you touch it with an attack, disarm it, seize it, or use a talent that explicitly targets hostile gear. ### Projected Blacksmithing Blacksmith is normally a contact, tool, and process sphere. You cannot forge an object at range by default. A technique is Projected if it lets you apply Blacksmith effects to a workpiece beyond reach or without a legal working surface. Projected Blacksmithing requires one of the following: Qi Cultivation; Spirit Awakening; a Blacksmith talent that says it is Projected; a Cultivation Insight; a forged technique; a Formation, furnace hall, puppet hammer, spirit anvil, sect tool, or GM-granted breakthrough. Body Refining Blacksmith begins with hands, breath, bones, hammer rhythm, heat resistance, grip, carried tools, and direct contact. It does not automatically grant ranged forging. ### Forge Marks Forge Marks are the central Blacksmith chassis. A Forge Mark represents heat, pressure, flaw recognition, material readiness, a hammer rhythm, or a half-born improvement waiting to be quenched. Unless a talent says otherwise: a workpiece can hold a number of Forge Marks from you equal to your Proficiency Bonus; a Forge Mark lasts for 1 minute during action scenes; outside action scenes, Forge Marks last until the current crafting scene ends; if a workpiece leaves your reach for more than 1 round, its Forge Marks remain but you cannot spend them until it becomes a legal workpiece again; you can remove your Forge Marks from one workpiece at any time, no action required. Forge Marks are not damage. Forge Marks are not automatically magical. A creature can usually see or hear that you are working a marked workpiece: ringing blows, heat shimmer, sparks, pressure, chanting, grinding, polish, or spiritual smoke. ### Temporary Temper Many Blacksmith talents grant a Temporary Temper. A Temporary Temper is a short-lived improvement to a workpiece. Unless a talent says otherwise: a workpiece can benefit from only one Temporary Temper from you at a time; applying a new Temporary Temper from you ends the previous one on that workpiece; a Temporary Temper lasts for 1 minute in action scenes; outside action scenes, it lasts for one scene or until the object is used for the purpose you prepared it for; a Temporary Temper does not make a nonmagical item magical unless the talent says so; a Temporary Temper does not permanently increase item value. ### Permanent Work Permanent improvements require time, materials, tools, and GM approval. Blacksmith talents may reduce difficulty, open options, diagnose materials, stabilize work, or provide project benefits. They do not automatically grant permanent magic items for free. A permanent item may require: rare ore; monster bone; spirit jade; fire source; furnace hall; helper disciples; talisman script; formation array; sect approval; a forged technique; downtime; CXP or narrative cost; a quest to obtain a missing material. ### Item Spirit Seeds Some higher-Realm Blacksmith talents refer to an item spirit seed. An item spirit seed is not a full NPC by default. It is the first sign that an object has begun to remember purpose. An item spirit seed may appear as: a bell tone; a warmth in the grip; a faint reflected shape; a repeated dream; a tool that sits correctly in the hand; a weapon that refuses an unworthy swing; a furnace mark that remains after cleaning. Awakening a true item spirit requires GM approval and usually a project. ### Blacksmith Damage and Safety Blacksmith can harm objects and sometimes creatures by exploiting flaws. Unless a talent says otherwise: Blacksmith does not ignore object damage thresholds; Blacksmith does not bypass immunity or resistance granted by an item, feature, artifact, or story protection; Blacksmith cannot destroy a worn or carried magic item without a talent, project, or GM permission; Blacksmith does not allow a character to craft above the campaign’s intended item economy. ## Base Sphere Abilities ### Blacksmith Training When you learn Blacksmith: gain Smith’s Tools proficiency or one alternate artisan’s tool proficiency as described above; gain the Read the Flaw ability; gain the Set the Workpiece ability; gain the Hammer the Mark ability; choose one Mortal Realm Blacksmith talent for which you meet the prerequisites. ### Read the Flaw Action Type: Multi-Mode Canonical Action Type: Multi-Mode Factory Combat Bucket: action Timing Detail: Action or 1 minute Factory Routing: combat_action_plus_procedure_variant Split Review Decision: single_combat_action_plus_procedure_variant Recommended Factory Realization: procedures=ONE_MINUTE_EXAMINATION Range: Touch or reach Target: One legal workpiece Cost: None Study one workpiece. Make an Intelligence check using Smith’s Tools against a DC set by the GM. If the workpiece is part of a creature’s equipment, the DC is normally the creature’s Armor Class or your Blacksmith Save DC, whichever is higher. On a success, learn two of the following: whether the object is damaged; whether the object is nonmagical, magical, or artifact-level; whether the object is poorly made, ordinary, fine, masterwork, spiritual, or anomalous; one material used in the object; whether the object has a hidden flaw; whether the object has been repaired before; whether the object is under an active magical or sphere effect; whether the object is suitable for a Blacksmith talent you know; what kind of tool, furnace, or material would help improve it; whether the object is resisting your work. If you spend 1 minute instead of an Action, also place 1 Forge Mark on the workpiece on a successful check. You may use Read the Flaw without a check on a nonmagical object you own, made, or have worked on for at least 10 minutes. ### Set the Workpiece Action Type: Bonus Action Factory Combat Bucket: bonus_action Factory Routing: combat_action_row Range: Touch or reach Target: One legal workpiece Duration: 1 minute or current crafting scene Cost: None Choose one legal workpiece as your current workpiece. Until the effect ends: you can place Forge Marks on that workpiece; you can spend Forge Marks from that workpiece; you have Advantage on checks made to repair, adjust, fit, or identify that workpiece; you cannot have more than one current workpiece unless a talent says otherwise. If you choose a new current workpiece, the old one stops being current but keeps any Forge Marks already on it until those marks expire. ### Hammer the Mark Action Type: Bonus Action Factory Combat Bucket: bonus_action Factory Routing: combat_action_row Range: Touch or reach Target: Your current workpiece Cost: None Strike, heat, grind, align, polish, stitch, bind, chant over, or otherwise work the current workpiece. Place 1 Forge Mark on it. If you used your Action this turn to make an attack with a hammer, tool, weapon, or unarmed strike against an object or a creature’s equipment, you may use Hammer the Mark on that same target without spending a Bonus Action. A workpiece cannot exceed your normal Forge Mark limit. ### Quench the Mark Action Type: Special Trigger Canonical Action Type: Special Trigger Factory Combat Bucket: passive Timing Detail: No action unless the response says otherwise Factory Routing: triggered_passive_modifier_row Trigger: A Blacksmith talent lets you spend a Forge Mark Target: The marked workpiece Cost: Spend 1 or more Forge Marks Spend Forge Marks to activate a Blacksmith response, talent, or improvement. A quench may be literal water, oil, snow, blood, spirit breath, cold iron, furnace wind, silence, or the moment when the hammer stops. ## Blacksmith Talent Tags ### Forge Talents A Forge talent creates, improves, repairs, tempers, or prepares a workpiece. ### Flaw Talents A Flaw talent reads, exposes, worsens, redirects, or breaks a structural weakness. ### Temper Talents A Temper talent grants a temporary improvement, fitting, resistance, edge, or readiness. ### Quench Talents A Quench talent spends Forge Marks for an immediate consequence. ### Furnace Talents A Furnace talent uses heat, fuel, containment, pressure, or a prepared forge. ### Tool Talents A Tool talent improves tool use, improvised work, or workshop practice. ### Project Talents A Project talent supports downtime, strategic crafting, sect armories, permanent items, or long-term work. ### Projected Talents A Projected talent allows Blacksmith effects beyond ordinary reach or without a legal working surface. Body Refiners do not gain Projected use by default. ## Core Forge Responses You know the following Forge Responses. Unless noted otherwise, each response targets your current workpiece and spends 1 Forge Mark. ### Set Edge Action Type: Bonus Action Factory Combat Bucket: bonus_action Factory Routing: combat_action_row Target: One weapon, tool, or natural striking surface you are legally working Cost: Spend 1 Forge Mark The workpiece gains a Temporary Temper. The next time before the start of your next turn that it hits with an attack or is used for a relevant ability check, add your Proficiency Bonus to one damage roll or one check. This bonus does not stack with itself. ### Fit Armor Action Type: Bonus Action Factory Combat Bucket: bonus_action Factory Routing: combat_action_row Target: One shield, suit of armor, bracer, defensive tool, or worn protective object Cost: Spend 1 Forge Mark The workpiece gains a Temporary Temper. Choose one: the wearer gains +1 AC until the start of your next turn; the wearer reduces the next Bludgeoning, Piercing, or Slashing damage taken before the start of your next turn by your Proficiency Bonus; the wearer ignores the next 5 feet of forced movement before the start of your next turn. ### Close the Crack Action Type: Multi-Mode Canonical Action Type: Multi-Mode Factory Combat Bucket: action Timing Detail: Action or 1 minute Factory Routing: combat_action_plus_procedure_variant Split Review Decision: single_combat_action_plus_procedure_variant Recommended Factory Realization: procedures=ONE_MINUTE_REPAIR Target: One damaged object Cost: Spend 1 Forge Mark Repair the workpiece enough for use. If used in an action scene, restore Hit Points to the object equal to: 2d6 + Intelligence modifier + Proficiency Bonus If used outside an action scene, restore a larger amount as appropriate to the scene and tools, subject to GM approval. Close the Crack can make a broken mundane item usable again, but permanent restoration of a destroyed, magical, cursed, or artifact item requires a project. ### Expose the Flaw Action Type: Bonus Action Factory Combat Bucket: bonus_action Factory Routing: combat_action_row Target: One object, armor, shield, weapon, construct, barrier, or workpiece you can legally work Cost: Spend 1 Forge Mark Until the start of your next turn, the next attack roll against the target gains Advantage, or the next saving throw the target makes against an effect that would break, move, disarm, damage, or suppress it has Disadvantage. If the target is worn or carried by a hostile creature, the creature makes a Dexterity saving throw. Successful Save: The effect does not apply. Its purpose is the moment when a workpiece truly becomes what the story has prepared it to become. ## Blacksmith Drawbacks and Variant Scriptures A Blacksmith variant is an optional scripture that changes what the smith believes forging requires. Uncontrolled Fire can damage or ruin a workpiece. ### Blacksmith + Talismans Talismans can script formulas into prepared workpieces. Blacksmith can prepare the item, stabilize material, open grooves, create channels, and reduce flaws. Talismans still governs stored formula and activation. ### Blacksmith + Formations Formations can create furnace halls, sect workshops, tempering arrays, bellows courts, and armory infrastructure. Blacksmith can provide the workpieces, tools, and crafting process. Formations still governs the maintained place. ### Blacksmith + Sect Stewardship Sect Stewardship provides access, rank, requests, labor, storage, procurement, apprentices, and armory authority. Blacksmith provides the actual craft. ## Cultivation Insights ### External Hammer Breakthrough Prerequisite: Blacksmith sphere, Body Refining Path, CL 8+ You have learned to project hammer force a short distance without abandoning Body Refining principles. You may learn one Projected Blacksmith talent. When using that talent, its range is reduced to 15 feet unless the talent already has a shorter range. You must hold a hammer, tool, weapon, or anvil-token, and the workpiece must be visible. This Insight does not grant broad Qi projection. ### Fire-Metal Furnace Understanding Prerequisite: Blacksmith sphere, Metal sphere or Fire sphere, CL 6+ Choose Metal or Fire when you gain this Insight. If you choose Metal, gain Advantage on one Blacksmith check per short rest involving metal resonance, edge, armor, bell, chain, blade, or ore. If you choose Fire, gain Advantage on one Blacksmith check per short rest involving heat, refining, purifying, quenching, tempering, or furnace control. If you later learn both Metal and Fire, use this Insight twice per short rest, once for each category. This is not a formal affinity system. ### Named Tool Custodian Prerequisite: Blacksmith sphere, Name the Purpose, CL 4+ Choose one personal tool, hammer, anvil, file, tongs, needle, chisel, whetstone, furnace plate, or similar implement. While using that named tool: gain Advantage on Read the Flaw once per short rest; the tool can hold one Forge Mark; if the tool would be destroyed, reduce the damage to it by 5 x Proficiency Bonus once per long rest. Replacing the named tool requires a short quest, inheritance, purchase, or 8 hours of personal work. ### Master of Repairs Prerequisite: Blacksmith sphere, Close the Crack, CL 6+ When you use Close the Crack outside combat, repair two compatible damaged objects in the same scene instead of one. When you use Close the Crack in combat, add an extra 1d6 to the object HP restored. At CL 10+, increase the extra restoration to 2d6. ### Item-Spirit Midwife Prerequisite: Blacksmith sphere, Spirit-Listening Tap, CL 10+ When working on an item with an item spirit seed, you may spend 1 hour coaxing it. Choose one: calm a hostile or fearful seed for one scene; learn one material it desires; learn one use it dislikes; grant its bearer Advantage on one roll made with the item before the next long rest; prevent one minor item-spirit complication from worsening until the next long rest. This does not force obedience.

spheres.full_exact_source_text: # Sphere of Blood Qi Expression: Primary — Blood Qi; Supporting — Water-Vital Qi, Lineage Qi, Sacrifice Qi. “Blood remembers the shape of the body. Blood remembers the shape of the soul. Every heartbeat is an oath repeated until the body can no longer keep it.” Sphere Type: Power Sphere Primary Paths: Spirit Awakening and Body Refining Secondary Path: Qi Cultivation Rare Variant: Body Refining through Iron Blood Body or the self-restricted Closed Circulation variant Resource: CP Common Effects: Circulation, vitality, sacrifice, tracking, medicine, bloodlines, bodily control, predation, forbidden refinement The Sphere of Blood cultivates circulation, continuity, inheritance, and sacrifice. Its practitioners establish Blood Threads, sense living circulation, preserve allies, punish wounded enemies, and pay vitality when a technique is worth the price. Blood techniques that seize another creature’s body, steal a bloodline, or impose permanent control are labeled as forbidden techniques. ### CORE BLOOD RULES #### Bloodied A creature is Bloodied while it has half or fewer of its maximum HP. Some Blood talents become stronger against Bloodied creatures. Creatures without literal blood may still possess analogous fluids, sap, ichor, spiritual essence, or a meaningful vital circulation. The GM determines whether a Blood talent affects an unusual creature. Blood talents normally do not affect: Constructs without vital fluid; Elementals without meaningful circulation; temporary summons without a stable body; creatures lacking a physical or spiritual equivalent to blood. #### Blood Thread A Blood Thread is a cultivated connection to one creature’s circulation. Unless a talent says otherwise: a willing creature’s Blood Thread lasts for 1 minute; an unwilling creature’s Blood Thread lasts until the start of your next turn; you know the approximate direction of a Threaded creature while it remains within 60 feet; Blood Thread does not automatically reveal an exact square through Total Cover; Blood Thread does not automatically defeat specialized concealment, planar separation, or sealed barriers; a creature may bear only one of your Blood Threads at a time. #### Blood Sample A Blood Sample is blood, sap, ichor, spiritual residue, or another bodily trace meaningful enough to identify one creature’s circulation. A Blood Sample may support: tracking; diagnosis; bloodline study; rituals; Forged Techniques; Formation projects. A Blood Sample does not automatically bypass a creature’s saving throws or protections. #### Crimson Sacrifice Blood cultivation may be paid for with the cultivator’s own vitality. Once per turn, when activating a Blood talent that costs CP, you may replace some of that CP cost with HP. Each replaced CP costs: 5 HP This HP loss: ignores Resistance and Immunity; cannot be reduced; cannot be transferred; cannot be paid with Temporary HP; cannot reduce you below 1 HP. Crimson Sacrifice is optional. A Blood cultivator should decide carefully when a technique is worth paying for with their own life. ### BASE SPHERE ABILITIES #### Blood Thread Action Type: Action Factory Combat Bucket: action Factory Routing: combat_action_row Range: 60 feet Cost: None Choose one creature with meaningful circulation. ##### Willing Creature Apply Blood Thread automatically. The Thread lasts for 1 minute. ##### Unwilling Creature Make a ranged Cultivation Attack. Hit: Deal Piercing or Necrotic damage and apply Blood Thread until the start of your next turn. The damage is 1d8 at CL 1-4, 2d8 at CL 5-10, 3d8 at CL 11-16, and 4d8 at CL 17-20. If the target is Bloodied, add your Proficiency Bonus to one damage roll. Choose the damage type when attacking. #### Bloodsense When you learn the Blood sphere, you gain Bloodsense. You sense exposed blood, fresh wounds, and meaningful living circulation within 60 feet. You know: the direction of Bloodied creatures; whether a visible creature is injured; whether blood was spilled nearby within the last hour; whether a corpse likely died from blood loss; whether an obvious Blood Sample belongs to the same creature as another sample you have already studied. Bloodsense does not automatically reveal Invisible creatures unless blood has been freshly spilled or another talent says otherwise. #### Coagulate - Thread Talent When you learn the Blood sphere, you learn Coagulate automatically. Action Type: Bonus Action Factory Combat Bucket: bonus_action Factory Routing: combat_action_row Range: 30 feet Target: One willing creature bearing your Blood Thread Cost: 1 CP Choose one: immediately stabilize the target if it is at 0 HP; end one ordinary bleeding effect; grant Temporary HP equal to Proficiency Bonus + Path key ability modifier. At CL 11, add +1d8 Temporary HP. At CL 17, add +2d8 Temporary HP. ### BLOOD TALENT TAGS #### Thread Talents A Thread talent modifies Blood Thread or provides a new way to exploit a Threaded creature. Unless a talent says otherwise, apply only one Thread augment each time Blood Thread hits. #### Sacrifice Talents A Sacrifice talent modifies Crimson Sacrifice or provides a new way to spend vitality. #### Bloodline Talents A Bloodline talent studies, awakens, preserves, refines, or steals inherited bodily traits. #### Rite Talents A Rite talent is a ritual, sample-based practice, or longer-duration blood cultivation method. #### Forbidden Talents A Forbidden Blood talent violates another creature’s autonomy, refines stolen vitality, or depends on involuntary extraction. Learning or using a Forbidden talent may carry narrative, sect, legal, or karmic consequences. #### Unique Blood Talents A Unique Blood Talent is a distinct technique that does not require Blood Thread. #### Augments An Augment modifies another Blood effect when its additional CP cost is paid. ### MORTAL REALM BLOOD TALENTS #### Crimson Mark - Thread Augment Cost: +1 CP Duration: 1 hour When you apply Blood Thread, extend its duration to 1 hour. While the Thread persists: you know the target’s approximate direction while it remains on the same plane and within 10 miles x Proficiency Bonus; the target cannot hide from your Bloodsense merely through ordinary invisibility; sealed barriers, anti-divination techniques, and specialized concealment may still interfere. An unwilling creature makes a Constitution saving throw. Successful Save: The extended duration fails, but the ordinary Blood Thread still applies. #### Bloodletting Strike - Thread Augment Trigger: You hit with a melee attack or Blood Thread. Cost: 1 CP. Add 1d6 Necrotic damage to the triggering hit or Blood Thread damage. The target makes a Constitution saving throw. Failed Save: At the start of its next turn, it takes additional Necrotic damage equal to your Proficiency Bonus. Successful Save: No ongoing damage. A creature can suffer only one Bloodletting Strike from you at a time. #### Vital Transfusion - Unique Blood Talent Action Type: Action Factory Combat Bucket: action Factory Routing: combat_action_row Range: Touch Cost: Special You take self-damage up to the maximum shown on the Vital Transfusion Maximum table. Vital Transfusion Maximum: • CL 1-4: Up to 1d8 + your key ability modifier. • CL 5-10: Up to 2d8 + your key ability modifier. • CL 11-16: Up to 3d8 + your key ability modifier. • CL 17-20: Up to 4d8 + your key ability modifier. Roll the listed dice when you activate the talent, then choose how much self-damage to take, up to the rolled maximum. This self-damage: ignores Resistance and Immunity; cannot be reduced; cannot be transferred; cannot be paid with Temporary HP; cannot reduce you below 1 HP. One living creature you touch regains HP equal to the self-damage taken. Vital Transfusion does not restore missing limbs or remove major injuries by itself. #### Blood Hound - Rite Talent Action Type: Ritual Procedure Canonical Action Type: Ritual Procedure Factory Routing: procedure_ledger_not_combat_action Timing Detail: Ritual Time: 10 minutes Range: Touch Target: One Blood Sample Duration: 24 hours Cost: 2 CP Study one Blood Sample. For the duration: know the approximate direction of its source while the source remains on the same plane and within 100 miles; gain Advantage on checks made to track the source; recognize whether another sample came from the same creature. A protected, sealed, transformed, or magically disguised target may require a Cultivation Check. #### Blood Armament - Unique Blood Talent Action Type: Bonus Action Factory Combat Bucket: bonus_action Factory Routing: combat_action_row Range: Self Duration: 1 hour Cost: 1 CP and 1 HP Shape hardened blood into one simple or martial melee weapon with which you are proficient. The weapon: counts as magical for overcoming ordinary Resistance; may deal its normal damage type or Piercing damage; dissolves if it leaves your possession for more than 1 minute; may be dismissed without spending an Action. When you create the weapon, choose one cosmetic form such as: spear; saber; knife; bow-limb blade; claw; chain; ritual needle. Blood Armament does not grant weapon proficiency. #### Blood Ward - Unique Blood Talent Action Type: Reaction Factory Combat Bucket: reaction Factory Routing: combat_action_row Trigger: You or an ally within 30 feet takes damage Cost: 1 CP A curtain of hardened blood absorbs part of the blow. Reduce the triggering damage by the amount shown on the Blood Ward Reduction table. Blood Ward Reduction: • CL 1-4: 1d8 + your key ability modifier. • CL 5-10: 2d8 + your key ability modifier. • CL 11-16: 3d8 + your key ability modifier. • CL 17-20: 4d8 + your key ability modifier. If the protected creature is Bloodied or bears your Blood Thread, add your Proficiency Bonus to the reduction. #### Physician’s Pulse - Rite Talent Action Type: Action Factory Combat Bucket: action Factory Routing: combat_action_row Range: Touch Cost: 1 CP Examine one willing living creature. Learn whether it is affected by: ordinary bleeding; poison; disease; internal injury; unusual blood loss; foreign bloodline contamination; ordinary exhaustion; one obvious bodily curse or transformation. Physician’s Pulse provides diagnosis, not automatic removal. ### FOUNDATION REALM BLOOD TALENTS #### Blood Armor - Unique Blood Talent Prerequisite: CL 5+ Action Type: Bonus Action Factory Combat Bucket: bonus_action Factory Routing: combat_action_row Duration: 1 minute Cost: 3 CP and 5 HP Form hardened blood around your body. Gain: +2 AC; Resistance to Slashing damage; Advantage on saving throws against bleeding effects; Advantage on saving throws against forced movement caused by physical impacts. The HP cost: cannot be reduced; cannot be transferred; cannot be paid with Temporary HP. #### Crimson Wave - Unique Blood Talent Prerequisite: CL 5+ Action Type: Action Factory Combat Bucket: action Factory Routing: combat_action_row Area: 15-foot cone Cost: 3 CP Release a wave of blood, iron scent, and vital pressure. Choose Necrotic or Piercing when you activate the talent. Creatures in the area make Constitution saving throws. Failed Save: A creature takes damage based on your CL. Successful Save: The creature takes half damage. Crimson Wave Damage: • CL 5-10: 4d6 Necrotic or Piercing damage. • CL 11-16: 6d6 Necrotic or Piercing damage. • CL 17-20: 8d6 Necrotic or Piercing damage. #### Blood Mending - Unique Blood Talent Prerequisite: CL 5+ Action Type: Action Factory Combat Bucket: action Factory Routing: combat_action_row Range: Touch Cost: 3 CP Restore: 3d8 + Path key ability modifier HP You may also end one ordinary bleeding effect. A creature benefiting from Blood Mending cannot benefit again until it completes a short rest. Blood Mending repairs circulation and ordinary wounds. It does not regrow missing limbs or automatically remove major injuries, curses, or Realm-level damage. #### Shared Veins - Rite Talent Prerequisite: CL 5+ Action Type: Ritual Procedure Canonical Action Type: Ritual Procedure Factory Routing: procedure_ledger_not_combat_action Timing Detail: Ritual Time: 10 minutes Duration: 8 hours Cost: 3 CP Bind yourself and up to your Proficiency Bonus willing creatures into a shared circulation pact. While two bound creatures remain within 60 feet: each knows whether another bound creature is Bloodied; each knows the approximate direction of the others; when one bound creature receives healing, another bound creature of your choice regains HP equal to your Proficiency Bonus. A creature gains this secondary healing only once per turn. Shared Veins does not transfer conditions or damage automatically. #### Crimson Feast - Thread Talent Prerequisite: CL 5+ Trigger: You damage a Bloodied creature bearing your Blood Thread Cost: 2 CP Use Limit: Once per turn Deepen the predatory link. Deal extra Necrotic damage based on your CL. Crimson Feast Damage: • CL 5-10: 2d6 Necrotic damage. • CL 11-16: 3d6 Necrotic damage. • CL 17-20: 4d6 Necrotic damage. Regain HP equal to your Proficiency Bonus. Crimson Feast cannot heal you above half your maximum HP. Crimson Feast is not automatically forbidden, but some sects treat predatory use against unwilling creatures as suspect. #### Blood Puppet - Forbidden Thread Talent Classification: Forbidden Blood Talent Prerequisite: CL 5+ Action Type: Action Factory Combat Bucket: action Factory Routing: combat_action_row Range: 60 feet Duration: Concentration, up to 1 minute Cost: 5 CP Choose one Bloodied living creature bearing your Blood Thread. The target makes a Constitution saving throw. Failed Save: At the start of each of its turns, choose one: move it up to half its Speed; force it to drop one held object; prevent it from taking Reactions; force it to fall Prone; reduce its Speed to 0 until the end of the turn. At the end of each of its turns, it repeats the saving throw, ending the effect on a success. Successful Save: The target cannot take Reactions until the start of its next turn. Blood Puppet cannot force: self-harm; attacks; spellcasting; cultivation techniques; movement into obviously lethal hazards. #### Bloodline Reading - Bloodline Rite Prerequisite: CL 5+ Action Type: Ritual Procedure Canonical Action Type: Ritual Procedure Factory Routing: procedure_ledger_not_combat_action Timing Detail: Ritual Time: 10 minutes Range: Touch Target: One willing creature or Blood Sample Cost: 2 CP Study one body’s inherited circulation. Learn broad information: whether a meaningful bloodline, ancestry, mutation, or inherited trait exists; whether one trait appears dormant, active, damaged, or artificially altered; whether the sample has been contaminated or refined; whether two studied samples appear closely related. Bloodline Reading provides evidence, not a complete genealogy. ### CORE FORMATION REALM BLOOD TALENTS #### Crimson Court - Blood Domain “Every heartbeat in this court belongs to itself. Every heartbeat is still audible to me.” Prerequisite: CL 10+ Action Type: Action Factory Combat Bucket: action Factory Routing: combat_action_row Area: 30-foot-radius aura centered on you Duration: Concentration, up to 1 minute Cost: 7 CP Inside the Domain: ##### You and Allies gain Advantage on death saving throws; gain Resistance to Necrotic damage; receive additional healing equal to your Proficiency Bonus once per turn; know whether another allied creature inside becomes Bloodied. ##### Enemies cannot benefit from ordinary invisibility against your Bloodsense after taking damage inside the Domain; have Disadvantage on saving throws against your Blood talents while Bloodied. When a Bloodied enemy starts its turn inside, it makes a Constitution saving throw. Failed Save: Take 2d8 Necrotic damage and cannot regain HP until the start of its next turn. Successful Save: Take half damage. A creature takes this damage only once per turn. #### Heart-Seizing Grip - Forbidden Thread Talent Classification: Forbidden Blood Talent Prerequisite: CL 10+ Action Type: Action Factory Combat Bucket: action Factory Routing: combat_action_row Range: 60 feet Duration: Concentration, up to 1 minute Cost: 6 CP Choose one living creature bearing your Blood Thread. The target makes a Constitution saving throw. Failed Save: Restrained by internal pain and pressure; cannot take Reactions; take 3d8 Necrotic damage at the start of each turn; repeat the saving throw at the end of each turn, ending the effect on a success. Successful Save: take 3d8 Necrotic damage; cannot take Reactions until the start of its next turn. #### Scarlet Mist Form - Unique Blood Talent Prerequisite: CL 10+ Action Type: Bonus Action Factory Combat Bucket: bonus_action Factory Routing: combat_action_row Duration: Concentration, up to 1 minute Cost: 6 CP Transform partially into blood mist. Gain: Fly Speed 30 feet and Hover; Resistance to nonmagical Bludgeoning, Piercing, and Slashing damage; ability to move through occupied spaces as difficult terrain; ability to pass through openings as narrow as 1 inch; Advantage on checks made to escape Grappled or Restrained; ability to apply Blood Thread automatically to one creature whose space you move through, once per turn. You cannot pass through sealed barriers or solid objects. #### Bloodline Awakening - Bloodline Rite Prerequisite: CL 10+ Action Type: Ritual Procedure Canonical Action Type: Ritual Procedure Factory Routing: procedure_ledger_not_combat_action Timing Detail: Ritual Time: 1 hour Range: Touch Target: One willing creature Duration: 24 hours Cost: 5 CP Awaken one existing inherited or bodily theme. Examples include: beast ancestry; dragon blood; spirit ancestry; celestial heritage; demonic lineage; amphibious adaptation; unusual senses; hardened skin; powerful musculature. Choose one approved benefit: Darkvision 60 feet; Climb Speed equal to Speed; Swim Speed equal to Speed; Resistance to one appropriate damage type; natural weapon dealing 1d8; Advantage on one narrow category of checks; Speed +10 feet; hold breath for 1 hour. Bloodline Awakening cannot invent an unrelated ancestry. A creature gains only one Bloodline Awakening benefit at a time. #### Open the Veins - Sacrifice Talent Prerequisite: CL 10+ Action Type: Bonus Action Factory Combat Bucket: bonus_action Factory Routing: combat_action_row Duration: Until the end of your turn Cost: None Use Limit: Once per short rest Until the end of your turn: Crimson Sacrifice may replace CP multiple times instead of only once; reduce the HP cost of each replaced CP from 5 HP to 4 HP; the maximum CP replaced across the turn remains 2 x Proficiency Bonus. At the end of your turn, make a Constitution saving throw against your own Cultivation Save DC. Failed Save: Become Bloodied if you were not already Bloodied and gain one level of Exhaustion. Successful Save: No additional effect. Open the Veins cannot reduce you below 1 HP. #### Blood River Passage - Unique Blood Talent Prerequisite: CL 12+ Action Type: Bonus Action Factory Combat Bucket: bonus_action Factory Routing: combat_action_row Range: 60 feet Cost: 4 CP Move through a line of blood, blood mist, spilled vital fluid, or one of your Blood Threads. Teleport into one visible unoccupied space within range adjacent to: a creature bearing your Blood Thread; a Blood Sample you can see; a visible pool of spilled blood; your own Blood Armament; one allied creature bound through Shared Veins. Blood River Passage cannot cross a Dimensional Lock, sealed barrier, or planar boundary. ### NASCENT SOUL REALM BLOOD TALENTS #### Blood Emperor Incarnation “My blood is not inside my body. My blood is the battlefield.” Prerequisite: CL 15+ Action Type: Bonus Action Factory Combat Bucket: bonus_action Factory Routing: combat_action_row Duration: 1 minute Cost: 15 CP Use Limit: Once per long rest Become a sovereign blood-body. Gain: Fly Speed 40 feet and Hover; Resistance to Bludgeoning, Piercing, Slashing, and Necrotic damage; Immunity to ordinary bleeding effects; Blood Thread damage becomes 6d10 Necrotic or Piercing damage; Bloodsense range becomes 1 mile; Crimson Sacrifice costs 4 HP per replaced CP instead of 5 HP; apply Blood Thread automatically to one Bloodied enemy that starts its turn within 20 feet. ##### Crimson Aura When a Bloodied enemy starts its turn within 20 feet, it makes a Constitution saving throw. Failed Save: Take 4d8 Necrotic damage and you regain HP equal to half the damage dealt. Successful Save: Take half damage. You regain no HP. A creature takes this damage only once per turn. #### Rivers Run Red Prerequisite: CL 15+ Action Type: Action Factory Combat Bucket: action Factory Routing: combat_action_row Range: 120 feet Area: 30-foot-radius sphere Duration: Concentration, up to 1 minute Cost: 12 CP Use Limit: Once per long rest Create a storm of blood, iron scent, and spiritual pressure. When a creature enters for the first time on a turn or starts its turn inside, it makes a Constitution saving throw. Failed Save: Take 8d8 Necrotic or Piercing damage and become Poisoned until the start of its next turn. Successful Save: Take half damage. A creature takes this damage only once per turn. A Bloodied creature inside also counts as bearing your Blood Thread until it leaves the area. #### Bloodline Ascension - Bloodline Rite Prerequisite: Bloodline Awakening, CL 15+ Action Type: Ritual Procedure Canonical Action Type: Ritual Procedure Factory Routing: procedure_ledger_not_combat_action Timing Detail: Ritual Time: 8 hours Range: Touch Target: One willing creature Cost: 12 CP Use Limit: Once per Realm per creature Permanently awaken one latent bloodline feature. Choose one approved benefit: Darkvision 120 feet; Climb Speed; Swim Speed; Fly Speed 30 feet; Resistance to one appropriate damage type; natural weapon dealing 1d10; Speed +10 feet; +1 to one ability score within the Realm maximum; Advantage against one narrow condition or hazard; one equivalent bodily feature. A creature may receive only one permanent Bloodline Ascension benefit per Realm. The benefit must fit its ancestry, mutation, lineage, or established bodily theme. #### Heartblood Rebirth Prerequisite: CL 15+ Action Type: Reaction Factory Combat Bucket: reaction Factory Routing: combat_action_row Trigger: You would die Cost: 10 CP Use Limit: Once per long rest Transform into a blood cocoon. Until the start of your next turn: you are Incapacitated; AC becomes 15; gain Resistance to all damage except Radiant and Psychic; cannot move voluntarily. At the start of your next turn: return with 1 HP; regain CP equal to your Proficiency Bonus; gain 2d10 Temporary HP. Heartblood Rebirth fails if: your soul is destroyed; the cocoon is destroyed; a Secret effect prevents revival. ### SECRET BLOOD INHERITANCE #### Bloodline Usurpation “The dragon inherited its blood. I refined mine.” Classification: Secret Forbidden Blood Inheritance Prerequisite: CL 17+, Bloodline Ascension, forbidden blood scripture Action Type: Ritual Procedure Canonical Action Type: Ritual Procedure Factory Routing: procedure_ledger_not_combat_action Timing Detail: Ritual Time: 8 hours Range: Touch Cost: 15 CP Use Limit: Once per Realm Extract one bloodline trait from a defeated creature. Requirements: the creature died within the last hour; the body or a major Blood Sample remains available; the creature possessed a meaningful innate trait; the creature had a CL or CR at least half your CL. Choose one narrow innate trait approved by the GM. Examples: Resistance to Fire; amphibious breathing; Darkvision; Climb Speed; natural armor; one natural weapon; one sense; one movement mode; one narrow bodily adaptation. You gain the trait permanently. You may maintain a number of usurped traits equal to your Proficiency Bonus. When gaining another beyond this limit, replace one. Bloodline Usurpation cannot steal: entire monster stat blocks; Legendary actions; lair actions; spellcasting; cultivation talents; whole Paths; Secret Inheritances; unique narrative authority. Using Bloodline Usurpation is a serious forbidden practice in most orthodox sects. ### OPTIONAL BLOOD CULTIVATION VARIANTS A Blood cultivation variant changes what the cultivator believes blood is allowed to connect. These variants are mutually exclusive. They do not automatically grant bonus talents unless explicitly stated. #### Closed Circulation “My blood does not leave my body. My body does not need the world to agree.” You cannot apply Blood Thread at range. You may apply Blood Thread only to: yourself; one creature you touch; one creature you hit with an unarmed strike or melee weapon attack; one creature entering or starting its turn inside a Blood effect centered on you. You cannot use Blood Hound on an unrelated Blood Sample. Your Bloodsense range becomes 30 feet. ##### Body Refining Access A Body Refiner may learn Blood through Closed Circulation without spending the Iron Blood Body Cultivation Insight merely to gain access to the sphere. Use Constitution and Stamina for Blood talents. Closed Circulation does not grant the Iron Blood synergy unless you later learn that Insight. ##### Benefit Gain one Thread, Sacrifice, or Unique Blood talent for which you meet the prerequisites as a bonus talent. #### Physician’s Lineage “Blood is not a weapon first. It is the first diagnostic scripture written inside every living body.” You cannot learn or use Forbidden Blood talents. You cannot use Crimson Feast against an unwilling creature. ##### Benefits Gain Coagulate or one Rite talent for which you meet the prerequisites as a bonus talent. Physician’s Pulse requires no CP. Once per turn, reduce the CP cost of Coagulate, Vital Transfusion, Blood Mending, or a non-forbidden Bloodline Rite by 1, minimum 0. Add your Proficiency Bonus to one healing or Temporary HP roll from a Blood talent once per turn. #### Predator’s Communion “A heartbeat is loudest when it understands that it may stop.” You cannot use Coagulate, Vital Transfusion, or Blood Mending on another creature unless that creature is bound to you through Shared Veins. You cannot create a willing Blood Thread at range. ##### Benefits Gain one Thread or Sacrifice talent for which you meet the prerequisites as a bonus talent. When you damage a Bloodied creature bearing your Blood Thread, add your Proficiency Bonus to one damage roll once per turn. Once per turn when you reduce a Bloodied creature to 0 HP, regain HP equal to your Proficiency Bonus. Crimson Sacrifice may replace one additional CP each turn. Predator’s Communion is not automatically forbidden, but many sects treat it with suspicion. ### PATH SYNERGIES #### Spirit Awakening - Ancestral Blood Use Wisdom as your Blood key ability. Your Blood talents affect: spirits; ghosts; possessing entities; astral projections; soul-bound creatures; spirit beasts; demon beasts normally when they possess meaningful spiritual circulation. When using Bloodline Awakening: duration doubles; you may choose spiritual traits approved by the GM; Bloodsense detects possessing entities and soul-bound creatures. #### Body Refining - Iron Blood Requires the Iron Blood Body Cultivation Insight unless Blood was learned through Closed Circulation. Use Constitution and Stamina for Blood talents. When you spend CP or Stamina on Blood Armor or Coagulate: add Constitution modifier to Temporary HP gained from Coagulate; Blood Armor also grants Advantage on Strength saving throws; once per round when Stamina Guard reduces damage to 0, regain HP equal to your Proficiency Bonus. Learning Blood through Closed Circulation grants access but does not grant this synergy unless you also learn Iron Blood Body. #### Qi Cultivation - Refined Circulation Use Intelligence or Charisma as your Blood key ability. Once per turn, reduce the CP cost of one Blood talent by 1, minimum 1. When using Crimson Sacrifice: 4 HP replaces 1 CP instead of 5 HP. ### CULTIVATION INSIGHTS #### Iron Blood Body Prerequisite: Body Refining, Blood sphere, CL 4+ Learn Blood as a Body Refining discipline if you did not gain access through Closed Circulation. Use Constitution and Stamina for Blood talents. Gain the Iron Blood synergy. #### Blood Physician Prerequisite: Blood sphere, CL 8+ When using Coagulate or Blood Mending: add your Proficiency Bonus to healing or Temporary HP; remove one ordinary bleeding effect automatically; stabilize one dying creature within 30 feet without spending an Action once per round. #### Crimson Hunter Prerequisite: Blood sphere, Crimson Mark, CL 8+ When attacking a creature bearing your Crimson Mark: ignore Disadvantage caused by ordinary concealment; deal +1d8 damage once per turn if the target is Bloodied; gain Advantage on checks made to track the target. #### Bloodline Scholar Prerequisite: Blood sphere, Bloodline Reading, CL 8+ Gain Advantage on checks made to: identify ancestry; identify bodily mutations; recognize inherited traits; analyze unusual blood; perform Bloodline Awakening rituals. Bloodline Ascension costs 2 fewer CP, minimum 1. #### Controlled Sacrifice Prerequisite: Blood sphere, CL 8+ Once per short rest, when using Crimson Sacrifice, reduce HP paid by: Proficiency Bonus minimum 1 HP. If this would reduce the cost of one replaced CP below 1 HP, treat it as 1 HP. #### Vein-Script Custodian Prerequisite: Blood sphere, Formations sphere, CL 8+ When designing a Formation project, use one Thread, Bloodline, or Rite talent you know as a seed effect. This does not create the Formation automatically. The project still requires: preparation time; Blood Samples or lineage references where appropriate; materials; anchors; a core or power source; maintenance; Formation-specific vulnerabilities.

automatic_base_abilities.effect:
#### Brutal Shove
Brutal Shove is a sphere-specific maneuver. It is not the ordinary 2024 Shove option.
Action Type: Action
Canonical Action Type: Action
Factory Combat Bucket: action
Timing Detail: Special Attack
Factory Routing: combat_action_row; preserve attack-replacement detail
Target: One creature no more than one size larger than you
Replace one attack when you take the Attack action.
Make:
Strength (Athletics)
contested by the target’s:
Strength (Athletics) or Dexterity (Acrobatics)
The target chooses its skill.
Success: Choose to push the target 5 feet away or give it the Prone condition. Then:
move it an additional 5 feet for every 5 points by which your Athletics check exceeds its opposing check;
apply this additional movement even when you chose Prone;
deal Bludgeoning damage equal to your Strength modifier, minimum 0;
apply one Manhandle talent you know.
Unless a talent says otherwise, Brutal Shove obeys the normal size limit above.

automatic_base_abilities.effect:
#### Brute Maneuvers
The following are sphere-specific maneuver options. They are provided here because the 2024 core rules do not define universal Disarm, Overrun, or Shove Aside actions.
##### Disarm
Replace one attack when you take the Attack action.
Make a weapon attack roll contested by the target’s:
Strength (Athletics) or Dexterity (Acrobatics)
The target chooses its skill.
Success: The target drops one held item of your choice. This maneuver deals no damage.
You have Disadvantage if the target holds the item in two or more hands.
The target has Advantage if larger than you and Disadvantage if smaller.
##### Overrun
As an Action or Bonus Action, attempt to move through one hostile creature’s space.
Make:
Strength (Athletics)
contested by the target’s:
Strength (Athletics)
Gain Advantage if larger than the target. Suffer Disadvantage if smaller.
Success: Move through the hostile creature’s space once during this turn. Treat that space as difficult terrain, and do not end movement in an occupied space.
##### Shove Aside
Use Brutal Shove to move the target into one different legal space within your reach rather than directly away.
Make the Brutal Shove contest with Disadvantage.
