spheres.full_exact_source_text: # Sphere of Brute Qi Expression: Primary — Force-of-Body Qi; Supporting — Earth Qi, Yang Qi, Bone/Muscle Qi. Sphere Type: Martial / Body-Leverage Sphere Primary Path: Body Refining Secondary Path: Qi Cultivation or Spirit Awakening through explicit Path synergy, inherited manual, or GM-approved scripture Resource: Martial Focus, Stamina for Body Refining expressions, and CP only when a supernatural Brute talent says so Core Chassis: Special Attacks, Brutal Shove, Brute Maneuvers, Impact Collision Brute cultivates leverage. Its basic loop is to make a sphere-specific Brutal Shove, convert a strong contest result into additional movement, and turn walls, creatures, and obstacles into Impact Collisions. ### Rules Baseline This player-facing sphere uses the 2024 fifth-edition rules baseline (5.5e) together with the Tianxia cultivation rules. Use the 2024 meanings of Action, Bonus Action, Reaction, Concentration, Cover, difficult terrain, Hide, Invisible, Bloodied, Exhaustion, and Damage Threshold unless this sphere explicitly replaces or expands a rule. #### Barriers, Domains, and Formation Anchors A Barrier is a temporary supernatural barrier, including a Protection-sphere Barrier or another effect that explicitly identifies itself as a Barrier. A Domain is a high-rank cultivation effect that says it is a Domain. Ordinary dispelling, sundering, or object-breaking text does not automatically remove a Domain unless the technique explicitly says otherwise. A Formation Anchor is an anchor point explicitly created by a Formation or identified by the GM as part of a Formation project. These spheres do not create Formation Anchors automatically. ### Core Brute Rules #### Special Attacks When a talent says it is a Special Attack, replace one attack when you take the Attack action unless the talent explicitly uses a different Action Type. #### Martial Focus Until a global Martial Focus rule replaces this reminder: you may hold one Martial Focus at a time; some talents expend Martial Focus; expending Martial Focus is not an Action; you cannot expend Martial Focus if you do not currently hold it; when a talent says you regain Martial Focus, regain it only if it is absent. #### 2024 Shove Under the 2024 fifth-edition rules, Shove is one option of an Unarmed Strike. The target chooses a Strength or Dexterity saving throw against: 8 + your Strength modifier + your Proficiency Bonus On a failed save, push the target 5 feet away or give it the Prone condition. The target must be no more than one size larger than you. #### Brutal Shove Brutal Shove is a sphere-specific maneuver. It is not the ordinary 2024 Shove option. Action Type: Action Canonical Action Type: Action Factory Combat Bucket: action Timing Detail: Special Attack Factory Routing: combat_action_row; preserve attack-replacement detail Target: One creature no more than one size larger than you Replace one attack when you take the Attack action. Make: Strength (Athletics) contested by the target’s: Strength (Athletics) or Dexterity (Acrobatics) The target chooses its skill. Success: Choose to push the target 5 feet away or give it the Prone condition. Then: move it an additional 5 feet for every 5 points by which your Athletics check exceeds its opposing check; apply this additional movement even when you chose Prone; deal Bludgeoning damage equal to your Strength modifier, minimum 0; apply one Manhandle talent you know. Unless a talent says otherwise, Brutal Shove obeys the normal size limit above. #### Impact Collision Some Brute talents cause an Impact Collision. An Impact Collision occurs when forced movement would carry a creature into: a wall; a solid object; another creature; a Barrier; another obstacle that cannot be crossed. Unless a talent says otherwise: the moving creature stops in the nearest legal space; collision damage is Bludgeoning damage; a creature may collide only once during one shove sequence; an unattended object takes the same collision damage when appropriate; artifacts, Formation cores, and Realm-defining structures may resist or require a separate check. #### Brute Maneuvers The following are sphere-specific maneuver options. They are provided here because the 2024 core rules do not define universal Disarm, Overrun, or Shove Aside actions. ##### Disarm Replace one attack when you take the Attack action. Make a weapon attack roll contested by the target’s: Strength (Athletics) or Dexterity (Acrobatics) The target chooses its skill. Success: The target drops one held item of your choice. This maneuver deals no damage. You have Disadvantage if the target holds the item in two or more hands. The target has Advantage if larger than you and Disadvantage if smaller. ##### Overrun As an Action or Bonus Action, attempt to move through one hostile creature’s space. Make: Strength (Athletics) contested by the target’s: Strength (Athletics) Gain Advantage if larger than the target. Suffer Disadvantage if smaller. Success: Move through the hostile creature’s space once during this turn. Treat that space as difficult terrain, and do not end movement in an occupied space. ##### Shove Aside Use Brutal Shove to move the target into one different legal space within your reach rather than directly away. Make the Brutal Shove contest with Disadvantage. ## Base Sphere Abilities This v1.10.5 section is a parsing map, not an additional feature grant. It names the rules below that should be treated as the sphere's base package during character creation, dashboard import, Roll20 export, and combat simulation. - Special Attacks are the ordinary 2024 Fifth Edition special attack framework this sphere modifies. - Brutal Shove is the base Brute expression used to move, shove, or reposition enemies through superior leverage. - Brute Maneuvers are the base menu for converting strong contests into sphere effects. - Impact Collision is the base collision rule that makes terrain, walls, obstacles, and other creatures matter. - These names do not grant extra actions beyond the rules already printed in Core Brute Rules. ### Brute Talent Tags #### Manhandle Talents A Manhandle talent modifies one Brutal Shove. Unless a talent says otherwise: choose the talent before rolling the shove; apply it only on a successful shove; apply only one Manhandle talent to one Brutal Shove. #### Collision Talents A Collision talent improves Impact Collisions. #### Focus Talents A Focus talent recovers, expends, or modifies Martial Focus. #### Terrain Talents A Terrain talent tears, breaks, or rearranges ordinary physical terrain. #### Realm Evolutions A Realm Evolution represents leverage beyond ordinary mortal strength. #### Unique Brute Talents A Unique Brute Talent is a distinct technique that does not fit another category. ### MORTAL REALM BRUTE TALENTS #### Dizzy Spin - Manhandle The target makes a Constitution saving throw. Failed Save: It has Disadvantage on attack rolls and ability checks until the end of its next turn. Successful Save: No additional effect. #### Humiliate - Manhandle Flip, twist, or force the target into an unusable position. The target makes a Dexterity saving throw. Failed Save: Its Speed becomes 0 until the end of its next turn. Successful Save: No additional effect. #### Perpetual Motion - Manhandle Immediately make one additional shove against the same target. This additional shove: deals Brutal Shove damage normally; cannot apply a Manhandle talent; cannot trigger Perpetual Motion again. #### Robbery - Manhandle After the shove succeeds, choose one: attempt to Disarm the target; or attempt Dexterity (Sleight of Hand) against an appropriate contested check to steal one accessible object. If you possess the Scoundrel sphere, apply one appropriate Trick talent to this attempt. #### Takedown - Manhandle After the shove succeeds, if the target remains within reach, attempt to Grapple it. #### Throw - Manhandle, Focus Expend Martial Focus. The target travels an additional 10 feet in one legal direction. It then makes a Dexterity saving throw. Failed Save: Fall Prone. Successful Save: Remain standing. #### Alternative Maneuvers You do not suffer Disadvantage when using Shove Aside. When making an Overrun attempt, apply Brutal Shove damage and one Manhandle talent as though it were a Brutal Shove. #### Break Defenses Whenever you successfully shove a creature, the next attack made against it before the start of its next turn has Advantage. #### Brutal Manhandle - Focus When applying one Manhandle talent, expend Martial Focus to apply one additional Manhandle talent. You cannot apply the same Manhandle talent twice to one shove. #### Dominoes When a shove pushes a creature into another creature, immediately attempt one free shove against the second creature to knock it Prone. The second creature need not be within your reach. You cannot apply a Manhandle talent to the free shove. #### Dropkick When you finish a long jump or high jump within reach of one creature after moving at least 10 feet, gain Advantage on your next shove against it before the end of the turn. #### Focused Might - Focus Whenever you successfully shove a creature, regain Martial Focus as a Bonus Action. #### Follow-Through After you damage a creature with a melee weapon attack, shove that creature as a Bonus Action. #### Get Over Here When you control one end of a tether attached to a creature, make shove attempts against it as though it were within reach. Examples: net; lasso; rope; chain; whip; grappling hook; tether technique. On a success, move the target toward you instead of away. When using Shove Aside, movement must still bring the target at least diagonally closer. Apply Manhandle talents normally, but talents requiring natural reach function only if the target ends within natural reach. #### Greater Brute Gain Expertise in Strength (Athletics). This does not stack with another feature granting Expertise or twice your Proficiency Bonus to the same check. #### Hammer - Collision While holding Martial Focus, when a shove would move a creature into a wall, creature, or solid object no more than one size smaller than the shoved creature, create an Impact Collision. The shoved creature and the collided object or creature each take: 1d6 Bludgeoning damage Add: +1d6 for every 5 feet of forced movement that could not be completed because of the collision. #### Muscular Surge Action Type: Bonus Action Factory Combat Bucket: bonus_action Factory Routing: combat_action_row Range: Self Target: Self Duration: 1 minute Cost: None Requirement: You are not Exhausted. Psych yourself into a larger expression of strength. For the duration: add your Proficiency Bonus to your Strength score only when determining carrying capacity; add your Proficiency Bonus to your running long-jump distance; count as one size larger when determining which creatures you may Shove or Grapple. Immediately before you make one of the following Strength checks, you may end Muscular Surge without taking an action. You must choose before rolling. If you end it this way, you have Advantage on that check: climb; swim; jump; break a door; break bonds; overturn an object; perform a comparable feat of strength approved by the GM. This Advantage does not apply to an attack roll or a contested check. When Muscular Surge ends for any reason, you gain one temporary level of Exhaustion for 10 minutes. That temporary level ends when the 10 minutes expire and does not remove any other Exhaustion you possess. You cannot activate Muscular Surge while you have any level of Exhaustion. #### Shift Weight - Focus Action Type: Reaction Factory Combat Bucket: reaction Factory Routing: combat_action_row Trigger: A creature fails an attack roll or contested Strength check against you Cost: Expend Martial Focus Shove the triggering creature. ### FOUNDATION REALM BRUTE TALENTS #### Earthquake Stomp - Unique Brute Talent Prerequisite: CL 5+ Action Type: Action Factory Combat Bucket: action Factory Routing: combat_action_row Stomp the ground. Creatures other than you inside the area make Dexterity saving throws. Failed Save: Fall Prone. Successful Save: Remain standing. | Cultivation Level | Radius | | --- | --- | | 5-10 | 10 feet | | 11-16 | 15 feet | | 17-20 | 20 feet | Ordinary unsecured objects may rattle, fall, or shift at the GM’s discretion. #### Thunderous Clap - Unique Brute Talent Prerequisite: CL 5+ Action Type: Action Factory Combat Bucket: action Factory Routing: combat_action_row Cost: Expend Martial Focus Area: 30-foot-radius sphere Clap hard enough to create a thunderous shockwave. Creatures inside make Constitution saving throws. Failed Save: Take Thunder damage and become Deafened for 1d4 + 1 rounds. Successful Save: Take half damage and are not Deafened. | Cultivation Level | Damage | | --- | --- | | 5-10 | 2d8 + Strength modifier | | 11-16 | 3d8 + Strength modifier | | 17-20 | 4d8 + Strength modifier | Extinguish ordinary nonmagical flames inside the area. #### Crushing Collision - Collision Prerequisite: Hammer, CL 5+ When Hammer creates an Impact Collision, choose one: the shoved creature makes a Constitution save or becomes Dazed until the start of its next turn; the secondary creature makes a Strength save or falls Prone; increase collision damage by your Proficiency Bonus; break one ordinary unsecured object involved in the collision. Dazed: This is a Brute-specific state, not a core 2024 condition. A Dazed creature cannot take Reactions and has Disadvantage on its next attack roll before the state ends. #### Living Battering Ram - Unique Brute Talent Prerequisite: CL 5+ Action Type: Action Factory Combat Bucket: action Factory Routing: combat_action_row Move up to half your Speed in a straight line. During the movement, make one Overrun attempt against one creature in your path. On a success: apply Brutal Shove; apply one Manhandle talent; continue moving through its space; if the creature collides with an obstacle, Hammer applies if known. This movement does not provoke opportunity attacks from the target of the Overrun. #### Mighty Hurl - Manhandle Prerequisite: Throw, CL 7+ When using Throw: increase additional movement from 10 feet to 20 feet; move the target vertically, horizontally, or diagonally; if the target falls, resolve falling damage normally; if the target collides, Hammer applies if known. #### Battlefield Bowling - Collision Prerequisite: Dominoes, CL 7+ When Dominoes triggers, attempt the free shove against each creature in a contiguous line until one shove fails. Each additional shove: knocks Prone only; cannot apply Brutal Shove damage; cannot apply Manhandle talents; cannot trigger Hammer unless the creature was already being moved by the original shove. #### Rooted Stance Prerequisite: CL 7+ While holding Martial Focus: gain Advantage on checks and saving throws against forced movement; reduce forced movement affecting you by 5 feet; count as one size larger when resisting Shove and Overrun. ### CORE FORMATION REALM BRUTE TALENTS #### Terrain Trasher - Terrain Prerequisite: CL 10+ Action Type: Action Factory Combat Bucket: action Factory Routing: combat_action_row Cost: Expend Martial Focus Grab a solid surface within reach and attempt to destroy it. The surface must be: a wall; door; floor; barrier section; comparable solid structure. It cannot be: loose dirt; liquid; iron or harder material without a specific enabling feature; an artifact; a Formation core; a Realm-defining structure. Make: DC 10 Strength check Success: Tear out a section approximately your own size. Against a surface thicker than 1 foot, destroy only 1 foot of thickness per use. #### Mountain-Swing Throw - Manhandle, Collision Prerequisite: Mighty Hurl, CL 10+ When using Throw, choose one additional benefit: increase forced movement by 20 feet; throw one creature up to two sizes larger than you if you first succeed on the shove; choose one 10-foot line the target passes through; creatures inside make Dexterity saves or fall Prone; when the target collides, increase collision damage by 2d8. #### Fortress-Line Breaker - Unique Brute Talent Prerequisite: Living Battering Ram, CL 10+ Action Type: Action Factory Combat Bucket: action Factory Routing: combat_action_row Cost: Expend Martial Focus Move up to your Speed in a straight or gently curving line. During this movement: ignore nonmagical difficult terrain; attempt Overrun against each hostile creature in your path; apply Brutal Shove to each successful Overrun; apply one Manhandle talent to one successful Overrun; deal double damage to unattended mundane objects in your path. Stop if one Overrun fails or a barrier cannot be crossed. #### Meridian-Lever Reversal - Focus Prerequisite: Shift Weight, CL 10+ When Shift Weight triggers, choose one: shove the creature before resolving its missed attack’s remaining effects; move 5 feet without provoking opportunity attacks after the shove; redirect the creature into one adjacent legal space; apply one Manhandle talent to the reaction shove by expending Martial Focus again. You cannot expend Martial Focus twice unless you regained it before the second expenditure. #### Court of the Moving Mountain - Martial Domain “The mountain did not chase its enemies. It merely decided that every direction led downhill.” Prerequisite: CL 12+ Action Type: Bonus Action Factory Combat Bucket: bonus_action Factory Routing: combat_action_row Duration: 1 minute Cost: Expend Martial Focus Use Limit: Once per short rest For the duration: gain Advantage on Strength (Athletics) checks; count as one size larger for Shove, Grapple, and Overrun; reduce forced movement affecting you by 10 feet; ignore nonmagical difficult terrain created by rubble, debris, and broken ground; when Brutal Shove succeeds, move the target 5 additional feet; once per turn when a creature collides with terrain or another creature, regain Martial Focus. Court of the Moving Mountain ends early if you become Incapacitated. ### NASCENT SOUL REALM BRUTE TALENTS #### Soul Sunder - Manhandle, Realm Evolution Prerequisite: CL 15+ Use Limit: Once per creature per long rest When Brutal Shove succeeds, the target makes a Charisma saving throw. Failed Save: Hurl the target into the Ethereal Plane for rounds equal to your Proficiency Bonus. Successful Save: No additional effect. At the end of each of its turns, the target repeats the saving throw, returning early on a success. While Ethereal: move in any direction; each foot of vertical movement costs one additional foot; see and hear the original plane within 60 feet as gray and indistinct; affect and be affected only by Ethereal creatures and effects; pass through ordinary objects from the original plane. When the effect ends, return to the original plane in the corresponding space. If occupied, shunt to the nearest legal space and take Force damage equal to twice the feet moved. Soul Sunder has no effect when used from a plane that does not border the Ethereal Plane. #### Sovereign Weight Incarnation Prerequisite: CL 15+ Action Type: Bonus Action Factory Combat Bucket: bonus_action Factory Routing: combat_action_row Duration: 1 minute Cost: Expend Martial Focus Use Limit: Once per long rest Become an incarnation of impossible leverage. For the duration: count as two sizes larger for Shove, Grapple, Overrun, carrying capacity, and Brute talents; gain Resistance to Bludgeoning, Piercing, and Slashing damage; gain Advantage on Strength checks and Strength saving throws; Brutal Shove damage becomes 2d8 + Strength modifier; once per turn when you successfully shove, move the target 10 additional feet; Hammer collision damage gains +2d8; ignore ordinary forced movement unless you choose to move. #### Heaven-Crashing Throw Prerequisite: Mountain-Swing Throw, CL 15+ Action Type: Action Canonical Action Type: Action Factory Combat Bucket: action Timing Detail: Special Attack Factory Routing: combat_action_row; preserve attack-replacement detail Cost: Expend Martial Focus Use Limit: Once per long rest Make one Brutal Shove. On a success: throw the target up to 60 feet in any legal direction; ignore ordinary size limits; the target and creatures within 10 feet of its landing space make Dexterity saving throws. Failed Save: Take 8d10 Bludgeoning or Force damage and fall Prone. Successful Save: Take half damage and remain standing. The thrown target automatically fails its save if it collides with a solid surface before landing. Heaven-Crashing Throw does not automatically move: artifacts; Formation cores; Domains; creatures protected by a stronger immovability effect. Those may require a contested Cultivation Check. #### Mountain-Moving Palm Prerequisite: CL 15+ Action Type: Action Factory Combat Bucket: action Factory Routing: combat_action_row Area: 60-foot cone Cost: Expend Martial Focus Use Limit: Once per long rest Release a palm strike of overwhelming physical pressure. Creatures and unattended objects inside make Strength saving throws. Failed Save: take 8d8 Force damage; move 30 feet away from you; fall Prone. Successful Save: take half damage; move 10 feet away; remain standing. Ordinary unsecured objects, rubble, and debris move automatically. Temporary Barriers take double damage. ### SECRET BRUTE INHERITANCE #### The Hand That Repositioned Heaven “Heaven declared the mountain immovable. The cultivator placed one palm against it and asked whether Heaven intended to defend that opinion personally.” Classification: Secret Brute Inheritance Prerequisite: CL 17+, Court of the Moving Mountain, hidden mountain-moving scripture Action Type: Action Factory Combat Bucket: action Factory Routing: combat_action_row Range: Reach or 30 feet against a tethered target Cost: Expend Martial Focus Use Limit: Once per week Choose one creature, unattended object, temporary Barrier, or ordinary structure section. ##### Creature Make one Brutal Shove with Advantage. On a success: ignore ordinary size limits; move the target up to 100 feet in one legal direction; apply up to three Manhandle talents you know; treat any collision as Hammer with +6d10 collision damage; the target makes a Constitution saving throw. Failed Save: Become Stunned until the end of your next turn. Successful Save: Cannot take Reactions until the start of your next turn. ##### Object, Barrier, or Structure Make a Strength check against a GM-set DC. On a success, choose one: tear open a major breach; shift the object up to 30 feet; collapse one ordinary section; turn the object into rubble; force open one sealed mundane passage. The Hand That Repositioned Heaven does not automatically move or destroy: artifacts; Formation cores; Domains; Secret Inheritances; Realm-defining structures. Those may still be contested or meaningfully damaged according to the GM. ### OPTIONAL BRUTE VARIANTS A Brute variant changes what the practitioner believes leverage is for. These variants are mutually exclusive unless a talent says otherwise. #### Gentle Giant “Strength is proven most completely when the fragile thing survives being moved.” You may choose for Brutal Shove to deal no damage. When you do: move a willing creature without requiring a contest; move a willing target through threatened spaces without provoking opportunity attacks from one creature; use Brutal Shove to pull an ally from Grappled, Prone, or hazardous positioning when physically possible; gain Advantage on checks made to catch, carry, rescue, or reposition willing creatures. Gain Takedown or Throw as a bonus talent. Gentle Giant does not prevent you from using damaging shoves when necessary. #### Living Battering Ram “The line is not broken by argument.” You cannot learn Robbery. You cannot apply Manhandle talents through Get Over Here. ##### Benefits gain Hammer as a bonus talent; count as one size larger when colliding with ordinary objects or structures; when Hammer damages an unattended object, add Proficiency Bonus to one damage roll; Great Destroyer-style object breaking from Berserker may be used as a Forged Technique seed. #### Tether Tyrant “Distance is only reach that has not yet been reeled in.” You cannot apply Brutal Shove through unarmed strikes unless the target is within natural reach. ##### Benefits gain Get Over Here as a bonus talent; draw or ready one tether tool without spending an Action once per turn; increase tether-based shove reach by 10 feet; when a tethered target fails a shove contest by 5 or more, move 5 feet toward it without provoking opportunity attacks. ### PATH SYNERGIES #### Body Refining - Mountain-Rooted Frame Use Constitution as your Brute key ability for saving throw DCs when higher than Strength. When Stamina Guard reduces damage to 0: regain Martial Focus if absent; count as one size larger for your next Shove, Grapple, or Overrun before the end of your next turn. While holding Martial Focus, reduce forced movement affecting you by 5 feet. #### Qi Cultivation - Meridian-Lever Circulation Use Intelligence or Charisma as your Brute key ability for saving throw DCs. Once per turn when Brutal Shove succeeds: move 5 feet without provoking opportunity attacks; or reduce the CP cost of one Brute Forged Technique before the end of your next turn by 1, minimum 1. When using Get Over Here, increase tether reach by 5 feet. #### Spirit Awakening - Intent-Redirecting Hand Use Wisdom as your Brute key ability for saving throw DCs. Once per round when a hostile creature within 30 feet moves willingly, attacks, or attempts to Shove, Grapple, or Overrun: learn the direction of its committed movement or force; gain +2 on one opposing Athletics check against it before the start of your next turn; or move one willing adjacent ally 5 feet without provoking opportunity attacks. Intent-Redirecting Hand reads committed physical intent, not private thoughts. ### CULTIVATION INSIGHTS #### Mountain-Rooted Body Prerequisite: Brute sphere, CL 4+ While holding Martial Focus: count as one size larger when resisting Shove and Overrun; gain Advantage on one Strength saving throw against forced movement once per short rest; when you would fall Prone, reduce forced movement affecting you to 0 before falling. #### Tether Adept Prerequisite: Brute sphere, Get Over Here, CL 6+ Gain: Advantage on checks made to attach, maintain, or recover a tether; draw or stow one tether tool without spending an Action once per turn; when a tethered target moves willingly away from you, use your Reaction to move 5 feet toward it or attempt one contested Athletics check to reduce that movement by 5 feet. #### Battlefield Architect Prerequisite: Brute sphere, Hammer or Dominoes, CL 8+ Once per turn when you force movement, choose one: increase forced movement by 5 feet; ignore one allied creature for collision purposes; choose which legal adjacent space receives a shoved target after collision; grant one ally Advantage on its next attack against a creature you moved. #### Gentle Hand Adept Prerequisite: Brute sphere, CL 8+ When repositioning a willing ally: increase movement by 10 feet; prevent opportunity attacks from one additional creature; grant Temporary HP equal to your Proficiency Bonus; allow the ally to stand from Prone without spending movement. Use Gentle Hand Adept once per turn. #### Leverage-Script Custodian Prerequisite: Brute sphere, Formations sphere, CL 8+ When designing a Formation or martial training project, use one Brute shove, collision, tether, or terrain principle as a seed concept. This does not create the project automatically. Normal project requirements still apply.

#### Brute Maneuvers
The following are sphere-specific maneuver options. They are provided here because the 2024 core rules do not define universal Disarm, Overrun, or Shove Aside actions.
##### Disarm
Replace one attack when you take the Attack action.
Make a weapon attack roll contested by the target’s:
Strength (Athletics) or Dexterity (Acrobatics)
The target chooses its skill.
Success: The target drops one held item of your choice. This maneuver deals no damage.
You have Disadvantage if the target holds the item in two or more hands.
The target has Advantage if larger than you and Disadvantage if smaller.
##### Overrun
As an Action or Bonus Action, attempt to move through one hostile creature’s space.
Make:
Strength (Athletics)
contested by the target’s:
Strength (Athletics)
Gain Advantage if larger than the target. Suffer Disadvantage if smaller.
Success: Move through the hostile creature’s space once during this turn. Treat that space as difficult terrain, and do not end movement in an occupied space.
##### Shove Aside
Use Brutal Shove to move the target into one different legal space within your reach rather than directly away.
Make the Brutal Shove contest with Disadvantage.

automatic_base_abilities.effect:
### Base Ability: Anchor the Link
Action Type: Reaction
Factory Combat Bucket: reaction
Factory Routing: combat_action_row
Range: 30 feet
Trigger: You, an ally, a creature bearing one of your Tethers, or an object linked by your Chains would be pushed, pulled, knocked Prone, moved involuntarily, dropped, or carried into a hazard
Cost: 1 CP
You fasten a chain to a stable surface, heavy object, your own body, the ground, a wall, a formation anchor, or a spiritual point of resistance.
Choose one:
reduce forced movement by 10 feet;
grant Advantage on the triggering saving throw against forced movement or Prone;
prevent a fall if a stable anchor exists within 30 feet;
allow the target to hang safely until the start of its next turn;
prevent the target from entering a hazard if reducing the movement is enough to keep it clear.
At Core Formation Realm, reduce forced movement by 20 feet instead of 10 feet.
Anchor the Link is the defensive and containment ability of Chains. Most rescue, anti-teleport, battlefield-control, and prison talents modify this ability.

exact_name_nonheading_hits.text: Resource: Stamina for embodied martial chains; normal Path CP for power-chain expressionsCore Chassis: Links, Tethers, Bound, Anchored, Chain Objects, and Chain DomainsCore Abilities: Chain Lash, Set the Tether, Anchor the Link
Anchor the Link is the defensive and containment ability of Chains. Most rescue, anti-teleport, battlefield-control, and prison talents modify this ability.

Lash. Modifies Chain Lash.Tether. Modifies Set the Tether or creates a Tether.Anchor. Modifies Anchor the Link or Anchored.Prison. Creates containment, wards, or imprisonment.Rescue. Protects allies through chain movement or anchoring.Spirit. Affects spirits, possession, Incorporeal creatures, or soul movement.Domain. Creates a field of chain authority.Project. Creates a downtime, sect, or site-scale chain structure.Restricted. Requires specialized training, sect permission, or GM approval.Forbidden. Socially condemned or dangerous in most orthodox contexts.

While sealed, the target counts as linked for your Link-Sense and Anchor the Link. In addition, the first time each round the target attempts to teleport, become Incorporeal, possess another creature, or leave its body, it must succeed on a Charisma saving throw against your Cultivation Save DC or the attempt fails.

spheres.full_exact_source_text: # Sphere of Chains Qi Expression: Primary — Binding Qi; Supporting — Metal Qi, Earth-Anchor Qi, Karma/Obligation Qi. “A prison is not defined by walls. It is defined by the certainty that movement has consequences.” Common Name: Chains Sphere Sphere Type: Hybrid Martial / Power Control Sphere Primary Paths: Body Refining, Qi Cultivation Secondary Path: Spirit Awakening Resource: Stamina for embodied martial chains; normal Path CP for power-chain expressionsCore Chassis: Links, Tethers, Bound, Anchored, Chain Objects, and Chain DomainsCore Abilities: Chain Lash, Set the Tether, Anchor the Link Common Effects: binding, restraint, pulling, anchoring, forced movement, anti-forced-movement protection, interception, capture, battlefield geometry, imprisonment, spiritual shackles, and containment vaults ### Chains Dao Chains cultivates the law of explicit connection. A chain says: you and this place are related. You and this enemy are related. You and your oath are related. You and your attempted escape are related. Thread cuts and manipulates with subtlety. Force answers impact without needing a visible line. Gravity makes the world heavy. Karma makes violation matter. Wrestling controls through the body. Chains controls by declaring a link and making that link unavoidable. A Chains cultivator does not simply restrain a target. They decide what the target is attached to, what movement costs, what escape must overcome, and what consequence follows when the chain tightens. The central question of Chains is: What are you attached to, and what happens when you try to leave? ### What Chains Does Chains cultivators create explicit links and then make those links matter. Chains talents commonly do one or more of the following: strike with chain, hook, rope, shackle, ribbon-chain, or manifested link; place, maintain, tighten, transfer, or break Tethers; pull, push, slow, restrain, or drag enemies; rescue allies, prevent falls, or resist forced movement; bind weapons, doors, wings, mounts, prisoners, spirits, or escape routes; create chain bridges, chain armor, chain webs, prison fields, and containment domains; punish escape, teleportation, spiritual flight, or oath-breaking when the talent says so; capture enemies alive and turn battlefield geometry into a visible prison. Chains is strongest when the table can see what is connected to what. A Chains effect should usually have an obvious chain, hook, shackle, rope, talisman-link, iron cord, soul chain, jade lock, or similar image unless a talent says it is hidden. ### The Chain Cultivation Loop Chains follows a simple battlefield loop: Cast the Link -> Fix the Anchor -> Tighten the Distance -> Punish Escape -> Seal the Prison A Chains technique usually begins by creating a visible connection, then turns that connection into control. The strongest Chains methods do not merely stop movement; they define the terms under which movement is allowed. ### Sphere Boundaries Chains overlaps with several spheres, but it does not replace them. Thread. Thread is fine control, hidden lines, wire traps, puppet-like precision, and delicate manipulation. Chains is heavier, more explicit, more forceful, and more concerned with restraint, anchor, capture, and visible consequence. Force. Force creates impact, pressure, counters, and barriers without requiring a visible tether. Chains uses explicit links and restraints. A Chains effect should normally show or imply a chain, rope, shackle, ribbon, lock, hook, seal-link, or similar connection. Gravity. Gravity controls weight, attraction, repulsion, falling, and flight denial. Chains may pull or anchor a target, but it does so through a link, not by rewriting gravity. Karma. Karma binds through obligation, consequence, debt, oath, and judgment. Chains may create oath-like containment as a spiritual expression, but it should not replace Karma’s broader moral causality. Wrestling. Wrestling controls through grips, throws, holds, pins, and bodily leverage. Chains can support grapples or restrain at range, but it does not replace close-range martial grappling as a body skill. Guardian / Protection. Protection prevents harm through wards, guard positions, barriers, and sacrificial defense. Chains can rescue, intercept, and hold allies in place, but it protects by connection and positioning rather than by general aegis. Space. Space governs teleportation, distance, portals, folding, and displacement. Chains can deny or contest escape through a tether or anchor, but it does not provide general teleportation or spatial travel. Puppetry. Puppetry controls vessels, threads, command lines, and remote operation. Chains can pull and bind, but it does not create full puppet control or substitute for a puppet vessel. Earth / Metal / Iron-style Spheres. Chains may appear as iron, jade, black steel, blood-red links, or golden locks, but this does not make Chains the general sphere of metal, mining, armor craft, or earthwork. ### Rules Baseline Use the current Tianxia 5.5e conversion baseline: Use Action, Bonus Action, Reaction, Concentration, short rest, long rest, saving throws, attack rolls, conditions, and movement rules from the current rules set. Use Cultivation Level (CL), Proficiency Bonus (PB), Cultivation Save DC, Cultivation Attack Modifier, CP, and Path resource language. Forced movement cannot normally move a creature into a solid object unless a feature says otherwise. Forced movement does not normally provoke opportunity attacks unless a feature says otherwise. Teleportation, planar travel, Incorporeal movement, possession, and spiritual travel are not automatically stopped by ordinary restraint unless a feature says so. A visible chain may be a physical object, manifested qi, spiritual shackle, ribbon-chain, talisman-link, shadow-link, blood-link, jade lock, or other narrative expression appropriate to the Path. A talent that creates a breakable chain should list AC and HP. A creature larger than Huge may gain Advantage on saves against ordinary Chains talents, if the GM judges the size difference is decisive. ### Key Ability, Save DC, and Costs Use your normal Path key ability unless a feature says otherwise. Body Refining: Constitution, spending Stamina. Qi Cultivation: Intelligence or Charisma, chosen when the Path is selected, spending Qi. Spirit Awakening: Wisdom, spending Resonance. Cultivation Save DC: 8 + your Proficiency Bonus + your key ability modifier. Cultivation Attack Modifier: your Proficiency Bonus + your key ability modifier. This sphere uses CP as the general resource term. Replace CP with Stamina, Qi, or Resonance as appropriate to the character’s Path. ### Martial, Power, and Body Access Chains is a Hybrid Martial / Power sphere. When you learn Chains, choose how your version expresses unless a feature, Path, or training source says otherwise. #### Martial Chains Martial Chains are physical or semi-physical chains, hooks, ropes, weighted links, shackles, hooked blades, chain spears, iron sleeves, binding cords, prison tools, or chain-like weapons. Martial Chains are common for Body Refiners and weapon cultivators. They usually require visible motion, bodily leverage, and a plausible route between you and the target. #### Power Chains Power Chains are manifested qi chains, ghost shackles, radiant chains, black prison links, written seal chains, oath chains, shadowy hooks, lightning chains, or spirit-binding links. Power Chains are common for Qi Cultivators and Spirit Awakeners. They may appear and vanish, but they are still explicit connections. #### Body Refining Chains Body Refiners normally do not project qi outside their body. A Body Refiner using Chains should usually express Chains through: actual chain weapons or weighted cords; iron sleeves, wrist chains, hooks, shackles, or binding weapons; tendons, bones, muscles, and breath trained to act like chains; grapple-chain methods; chains attached to the body or equipment; short-range pressure-point hooks; body-to-body restraint. A Body Refiner can use Chains at the listed ranges only if their technique has a physical or embodied explanation: thrown chain, hooked weapon, weighted rope, extending chain weapon, body chain, forged armament, or a special martial scripture. Otherwise, the GM may restrict Body Refining Chains to touch, melee reach, or weapon reach. ### Core Chains Rules #### Links A Link is any chain connection created by a Chains ability. A Link may connect a creature, object, point in space, surface, anchor, ally, enemy, or chain construct. A Link is usually visible or perceptible. Even invisible Chains still leave a pressure, ringing, spiritual pull, or visible restraint when they tighten. #### Tethers A Tether is a Link with a maximum length. Unless a talent says otherwise: a Tether visibly connects two points; a Tether has a maximum length listed by the talent; a Tether breaks if its endpoints exceed that maximum length through movement the talent cannot prevent; a Tether cannot drag a creature into a solid object; a Tether does not automatically prevent teleportation, planar travel, Incorporeal movement, or possession; a creature can be affected by only one copy of the same Tether talent from you at a time; a willing creature can allow your Tether to attach without a saving throw; an unwilling creature receives any saving throw listed by the ability. #### Chain Objects Some Chains effects create a breakable Chain Object. Unless a talent lists different statistics, a Chain Object has: AC 15 + half your Proficiency Bonus, rounded down; Hit Points equal to 5 x your CL; Resistance to Bludgeoning, Piercing, and Slashing damage; Immunity to Poison and Psychic damage. If a Chain Object is destroyed, the effect creating it ends unless the talent says otherwise. #### Bound Bound is a sphere-specific state, not a standard condition. A Bound creature: has its Speed reduced by 10 feet; cannot Dash; has Disadvantage on checks made to escape Grappled, Restrained, shackled, tied, or physically bound states; cannot willingly increase the distance from the Tether beyond the Tether’s maximum length. Bound normally lasts only as long as the ability or talent that created it. #### Anchored Anchored is a sphere-specific state, not a standard condition. An Anchored creature, object, or area: cannot be forcibly moved unless the moving effect succeeds against your Cultivation Save DC or the talent lists another method; has Advantage on saving throws against being knocked Prone; cannot teleport unless it succeeds on a Charisma saving throw against your Cultivation Save DC; cannot be carried away by ordinary environmental forces if a stable anchor exists. Anchored does not automatically prevent planar travel, Incorporeal movement, possession, or spiritual escape unless a talent says otherwise. A creature may be Bound, Anchored, or both. #### Escape Attempts If a Chains talent allows escape with a check, the creature may use its Action to make a Strength (Athletics) or Dexterity (Acrobatics) check against your Cultivation Save DC unless the talent specifies a different check. Spirit-only chains may call for Charisma, Wisdom, or a Cultivation Check instead. ### Base Ability: Chain Lash Action Type: Action Factory Combat Bucket: action Factory Routing: combat_action_row Range: 30 feet Target: One creature or object Cost: None You strike with a physical chain, manifested link, hooked cord, shackle-ribbon, seal-chain, ghostly restraint, or similar expression. Make a melee or ranged Cultivation Attack roll. On a hit, the target takes Bludgeoning or Slashing damage based on your Realm: Mortal: 1d8 Foundation: 2d8 Core Formation: 3d8 Nascent Soul: 4d8 Once per turn when Chain Lash hits, choose one minor link effect: pull the target 5 feet toward you; push the target 5 feet away from you; reduce the target’s Speed by 5 feet until the start of your next turn; gain Advantage on the next check you make to Grapple the target before the start of your next turn; attach a harmless visible Link to the target until the start of your next turn. Chain Lash is the default attack expression of the sphere. Most offensive Chains talents modify Chain Lash, trigger after Chain Lash hits, or replace the minor link effect. ### Base Ability: Set the Tether Action Type: Action Factory Combat Bucket: action Factory Routing: combat_action_row Range: 30 feet Target: One creature, object, surface, or point you can see Duration: Until the start of your next turn Cost: 1 CP You throw, manifest, write, or fasten a chain that connects the target to you, to a stable surface, or to another point you can see within range. If the target is an unwilling creature, it makes a Strength saving throw. Failed Save: The target becomes Bound until the start of your next turn. The Tether has a maximum length of 30 feet. Successful Save: The target’s Speed is reduced by 5 feet until the start of your next turn. If you target a willing creature or unattended object, no saving throw is required. You may use Set the Tether to pull an unattended object weighing no more than 25 pounds x your CL up to 20 feet toward you. Set the Tether is the main binding and positioning ability. Most restraint, pulling, prison, and link talents modify this ability. ### Base Ability: Anchor the Link Action Type: Reaction Factory Combat Bucket: reaction Factory Routing: combat_action_row Range: 30 feet Trigger: You, an ally, a creature bearing one of your Tethers, or an object linked by your Chains would be pushed, pulled, knocked Prone, moved involuntarily, dropped, or carried into a hazard Cost: 1 CP You fasten a chain to a stable surface, heavy object, your own body, the ground, a wall, a formation anchor, or a spiritual point of resistance. Choose one: reduce forced movement by 10 feet; grant Advantage on the triggering saving throw against forced movement or Prone; prevent a fall if a stable anchor exists within 30 feet; allow the target to hang safely until the start of its next turn; prevent the target from entering a hazard if reducing the movement is enough to keep it clear. At Core Formation Realm, reduce forced movement by 20 feet instead of 10 feet. Anchor the Link is the defensive and containment ability of Chains. Most rescue, anti-teleport, battlefield-control, and prison talents modify this ability. ### Realm Progression Mortal Realm: Basic chain strikes, short tethers, pulls, hooks, escapes, and rescue lines. Chains is useful but not absolute. Foundation Realm: Sustained restraints, breakable chain objects, chain armor, linked targets, stronger counters, and battlefield rescue. Core Formation Realm: Domains, prisons, chain webs, clone constructs, heavenly anchors, and serious anti-escape effects. Nascent Soul Realm: Sovereign chain incarnation, battlefield-scale imprisonment, structure-dragging chains, prison projects, and conceptual heaven-binding inheritance. ### Talent Tags Lash. You cannot create purely spiritual or qi-only Chains unless a forged technique specifically allows it. Your Chain Lash range is limited by your weapon, thrown chain, or physical chain route. If no such route exists, Chain Lash range becomes melee reach. You gain Chain-Breaker’s Lesson or Weighted Links as a bonus talent. This scripture is common among Body Refiners, wardens, bounty hunters, and prison-weapon cultivators. ### Visible Bond Scripture Your Chains are always visible and audible when active. They ring, scrape, glow, drag, or display written links. You cannot hide the use of a Chains talent. Creatures observing you know that a Chains technique is being used and can identify its general direction and target. You gain Link-Sense or Restraining Hook as a bonus talent. This scripture is respected among orthodox prison halls because it makes binding lawful, witnessed, and difficult to disguise. ### Bound Anchor Scripture Your Chains require a stable anchor. Whenever you use Set the Tether, Chain Lash at range, or a talent that creates a Tether, you must attach the chain to one of the following: your body; a held chain weapon; the ground; a wall; a stable object; a formation anchor; a willing ally; a prepared prison seal. If no stable anchor exists, the talent fails but does not spend CP. You gain Anchor the Link improvements: once per short rest, you may use Anchor the Link without spending CP. ### Merciful Captor Scripture Your Chains are cultivated to capture rather than kill. Your Chain Lash and Chains talents cannot reduce a living creature below 1 Hit Point unless you choose to break this scripture. If you break it, you lose the benefit of this drawback until you complete a long rest and perform a repentance or re-centering rite. You gain Manacle Method or Rescue Line as a bonus talent. When you knock a creature unconscious with a Chains attack, you may immediately use Set the Tether on it without spending CP. ### Severed Prison Scripture You reject prisons and focus only on motion, rescue, and battlefield chains. You cannot learn talents with the Prison tag except Chain the Door and Manacle Method. You gain Hooked Step or Pulling Chain as a bonus talent. This scripture suits chain-dancers, wandering rescuers, caravan guards, and battlefield skirmishers. ### Soul-Shackle Scripture Your Chains bind spirit more easily than flesh. Your Chains talents can affect spirits, ghosts, Incorporeal creatures, possessing entities, and astral bodies normally if you can perceive them. However, your Chains have reduced physical bite. Chain Lash damage dice are reduced by one step against purely physical living targets: d8 becomes d6, d10 becomes d8. You may use Wisdom as your Chains key ability. You gain Chain-Script Seal as a bonus talent when you meet its prerequisite. This scripture is most common among Spirit Awakening wardens and exorcist-prisoners. ## Path Synergies ### Body Refining: Iron-Chain Body Body Refining Chains uses Constitution and Stamina. A Body Refiner usually needs physical chains, a chain weapon, hooks, manacles, iron sleeves, weighted cords, body chains, tendon-chain methods, or a forged martial technique to justify ranged Chains effects. While Chain Armor is active or while you Grapple a creature, you may gain the following synergy if your GM permits Path synergies: gain +1 AC; add your Constitution modifier to checks made to Grapple, Shove, or resist forced movement; your unarmed strikes may deal Chain Lash damage type if beneficial; when you successfully Grapple a creature, you may attach a harmless Link to it until the start of your next turn. Body Refining Chains should feel like iron joints, tendon cables, bone hooks, chain sleeves, and full-body leverage. ### Qi Cultivation: Refined Chain Circulation Qi Cultivation Chains uses Intelligence or Charisma and Qi. Qi Cultivators may manifest chains of refined qi, jade light, written talisman links, lightning, black iron law, golden prison-script, or ribbon-like qi cords. Suggested synergy: once per turn, reduce the CP cost of one Chains talent by 1, minimum 1; Chain Lash range increases by 10 feet; Chain Bridge may appear as stable qi links instead of physical chain. Qi Cultivation Chains is the broadest version and most naturally learns domain, prison, and battlefield geometry talents. ### Spirit Awakening: Soul Shackles Spirit Awakening Chains uses Wisdom and Resonance. Spirit Awakeners may manifest chains as soul pressure, memory links, oath shackles, spectral iron, dream manacles, ancestor-script, or spiritual jailer seals. Suggested synergy: Chains talents can affect spirits, ghosts, Incorporeal creatures, possessing entities, and astral bodies normally if you can perceive them; Heavenly Anchor may prevent a possessing spirit from leaving its host unless it succeeds on a Charisma saving throw; Link-Sense may sense spiritual tension even when the physical chain is hidden. Spirit Awakening Chains should feel like binding the intention to escape, not merely binding the ankle. ## Sphere Synergies ### Chains + Karma: Karmic Shackles A chain oath tightens when the target violates a sworn condition. Use Chains to define the link and Karma to define the consequence. ### Chains + Void: Void-Binding Chain A chain hooks into the gap where escape should have been. Use Chains to anchor the target and Void to deny shortcuts, reductions, or disappearance. ### Chains + Death: Graveyard Chains Black chains bind corpses, ghosts, and undead inside a burial ground or funerary formation. Use Chains to restrain and Death to command the grave-law. ### Chains + Lightning: Thunder Chain Prison Conductive links punish movement, escape attempts, and broken tethers. Use Chains for geometry and Lightning for reactive punishment. ### Chains + Blood: Bloodline Prison A chain marks inherited blood, family curse, or lineage debt. Use Chains for containment and Blood for lineage recognition. ### Chains + Sword: Chain-Sword Execution A target is pulled into a prepared sword line. Use Chains for forced positioning and Sword for decisive cutting pressure. ### Chains + Guardian: Rescue Line A guardian chain intercepts danger and pulls an ally out of the fatal square. Use Chains for movement and Guardian for protective timing. ### Chains + Formations: Nine-Gate Dungeon Array Chains provide gates, locks, prisoner lines, and alarm tension; Formations provide infrastructure, ward logic, and long-term site rules. ### Chains + Puppetry: Shackled Vessel Method Chains restrain a vessel’s range, disobedience, or emergency collapse while Puppetry controls the vessel’s actions. ## Cultivation Insights ### Soul Shackles Prerequisite: Spirit Awakening Path, Chains sphere, CL 4+ You may use Wisdom as your Chains key ability. Your Chains talents can affect spirits, ghosts, Incorporeal creatures, possessing entities, and astral bodies normally if you can perceive them. In addition, when you use Chain-Script Seal on a possessing entity, the host gains Advantage on the next saving throw it makes to resist possession before the end of its next turn. ### Chain-Walking Immortal Prerequisite: Chains sphere, CL 8+ You may move along your own chains as though they were stable ground. You gain the following benefits: climb at full Speed using chains; swing across gaps without checks when a valid chain route exists; use Chain Bridge once per short rest without spending CP; ignore ordinary falling damage if a valid anchor exists within 60 feet and you are not incapacitated. ### Prison Warden Prerequisite: Chains sphere, CL 8+ Your prison techniques are harder to break. Shackling Chain, Chain Prison, Chain the Door, and Prison of Nine Gates gain: +2 AC for their Chain Objects or bound structures; additional Hit Points equal to 5 x your Proficiency Bonus; a creature escaping one of your Chains talents cannot teleport until the start of its next turn. ### Hook Master Prerequisite: Chains sphere, CL 8+ Your hooks are fast, cruel, and accurate. Restraining Hook gains: range increases by 30 feet; on a failed save, you may also pull the target 5 feet; once per short rest, you may use Restraining Hook without spending CP. ### Living Anchor Prerequisite: Chains sphere, CL 8+ You can anchor others through your own stance and body. When Anchor the Link protects an ally: reduce forced movement by an additional 10 feet; grant Advantage on one saving throw against Prone, Grappled, Restrained, or forced movement; the ally may move 5 feet toward you without provoking opportunity attacks. Body Refiners often use this Insight as a signature protector method. ### Lawful Captor Prerequisite: Chains sphere When you reduce a creature to 0 Hit Points with Chain Lash or a Chains talent, you may choose to knock it unconscious and immediately bind it with mundane chains, rope, or Manacle Method if you have a free hand, chain, or equivalent tool. In addition, you have Advantage on Charisma checks made to justify lawful capture, prisoner transfer, bounty custody, or sect discipline when your use of Chains was witnessed and proportionate. ### Chain-Tool Familiarity Prerequisite: Chains sphere You gain proficiency with chain weapons, manacles, prison tools, and one artisan’s tool or martial tool related to chains, locks, hooks, or restraints. If you already have the relevant proficiency, you may add half your Proficiency Bonus to checks made to repair chains, disable shackles, evaluate prison equipment, or identify chain-based techniques. ## Forged Technique Examples ### Karmic Shackles Spheres: Chains + Karma Suggested Realm: Foundation or Core Formation You bind a target with visible chain-script and a single declared consequence. If the target violates the declared condition before the end of the scene, the Tether tightens and the target must make a Charisma saving throw. On a failure, it becomes Bound and takes Force damage equal to your CL + your key ability modifier. ### Void-Binding Chain Spheres: Chains + Void Suggested Realm: Core Formation You chain not the body, but the gap through which the body would flee. A creature Bound by this technique cannot reduce the CP cost of teleportation, escape, or movement techniques. If it teleports, it must first succeed on a Charisma saving throw against your Cultivation Save DC. ### Graveyard Chains Spheres: Chains + Death Suggested Realm: Foundation or Core Formation You drive black chain stakes into grave soil, corpse ash, coffin wood, or funerary stone. Undead and ghosts inside the prepared area have Disadvantage on checks to escape Grappled, Restrained, Bound, or Anchored states. A ghost attempting to leave the area must succeed on a Charisma saving throw. ### Thunder Chain Prison Spheres: Chains + Lightning Suggested Realm: Core Formation Your chain prison conducts punishment. The first time each round a creature attempts to escape, cut, teleport from, or forcibly break your Chain Prison, it takes Lightning damage equal to 2d8 + your key ability modifier. ### Bloodline Prison Spheres: Chains + Blood Suggested Realm: Core Formation or Nascent Soul You bind a target through inherited blood resonance. When you successfully use Chain-Script Seal on a creature whose bloodline you have identified, you may also mark a blood relative, ancestral relic, family tablet, or blood-written name as an anchor. The target has Disadvantage on the first escape check it makes while within 1 mile of that anchor. ### Chain-Sword Execution Spheres: Chains + Sword Suggested Realm: Foundation You pull the target into the line where the blade is already waiting. When Chain Lash or Pulling Chain moves a creature at least 10 feet, you may spend 1 additional CP to make one sword attack against it if it ends within your weapon reach. ### Guardian Rescue Line Spheres: Chains + Guardian Suggested Realm: Foundation Your chain is trained to answer danger before your mind finishes naming it. When an ally within 60 feet would be hit by an attack or enter a hazard, you may use Rescue Line. If this moves the ally out of the attack’s reach or area, the attack misses unless the attacker can choose a new valid target. ### Shackled Vessel Method Spheres: Chains + Puppetry Suggested Realm: Core Formation You fit a puppet vessel with prison links. The puppet cannot be moved beyond a chosen range from you unless you permit it, but it gains Advantage on saving throws against forced movement and possession. If the puppet is destroyed, the chains may preserve one important component for later repair. ## Strategic Project Seeds ### Found the Iron Warden Hall Create a sect hall responsible for prison keeping, prisoner transfer, bounty custody, and lawful binding. Possible requirements: Prison of Nine Gates; trained chain disciples; judicial or sect authority; supply of jade locks and formation anchors; negotiated prisoner laws. Possible benefits: safer prisoner transport; income from bounties and contracts; access to restricted Chains manuals; political influence with sect courts. ### Build the Chain Bridge Over the Demon Gorge Use Chain Bridge, Prison of Nine Gates, Formations, and sect labor to create a permanent crossing over a cursed ravine, demon pit, or unstable space. Complications may include: chains must be replaced each year; spirits cling to the links; a rival sect wants toll rights; the bridge also functions as a prison route; a hidden prisoner is sealed inside one anchor. ### Hunt the Escaped Nascent Soul Prisoner A powerful captive broke a prison chain but not the prisoner’s bell. The party must use Link-Sense, Prisoner’s Bell, Thousand-Mile Prisoner Line, Karma records, and witness testimony to track the escape. Possible complications: the prisoner was innocent; the prisoner is a disguised elder; someone inside the prison helped; the chain is still attached to a soul fragment; the escape route crosses a forbidden realm. ### Repair the Nine-Gate Dungeon An ancient prison formation is failing. The Chains cultivator must repair locks, feed anchor chains, negotiate with imprisoned spirits, and decide which prisoners remain sealed. Possible benefits: access to a secret inheritance; a loyal prisoner guide; a permanent sect asset; a dangerous political obligation.

### Base Ability: Chain Lash
Action Type: Action
Factory Combat Bucket: action
Factory Routing: combat_action_row
Range: 30 feet
Target: One creature or object
Cost: None
You strike with a physical chain, manifested link, hooked cord, shackle-ribbon, seal-chain, ghostly restraint, or similar expression.
Make a melee or ranged Cultivation Attack roll.
On a hit, the target takes Bludgeoning or Slashing damage based on your Realm:
Mortal: 1d8
Foundation: 2d8
Core Formation: 3d8
Nascent Soul: 4d8
Once per turn when Chain Lash hits, choose one minor link effect:
pull the target 5 feet toward you;
push the target 5 feet away from you;
reduce the target’s Speed by 5 feet until the start of your next turn;
gain Advantage on the next check you make to Grapple the target before the start of your next turn;
attach a harmless visible Link to the target until the start of your next turn.
Chain Lash is the default attack expression of the sphere. Most offensive Chains talents modify Chain Lash, trigger after Chain Lash hits, or replace the minor link effect.

automatic_base_abilities.effect:
### Base Sphere Abilities
When you learn Daemonic Cultivation, gain Demon Seed, Devour Essence, and Daemonic Augment.
#### Demon Seed
Classification: Forbidden Daemonic Root
Action Type: Bonus Action
Factory Combat Bucket: bonus_action
Factory Routing: combat_action_row
Duration: 1 minute
Cost: 1 CP or 1 Stamina
Plant or awaken a Demon Seed in your body, dantian, meridians, or soul. The Seed is a forbidden method-root, not a Demon Core. It does not make you a demon; it opens the second furnace through which the daemonic scripture can breathe.
While Demon Seed is active:
your Daemonic talents may be used;
you gain Temporary HP equal to your Proficiency Bonus + your Daemonic key ability modifier;
once per turn when you hit with a weapon attack, Unarmed Strike, or Cultivation Attack, add 1d4 Necrotic, Psychic, or Force damage;
you have Advantage on saving throws against Frightened;
you have Disadvantage on checks made to appear spiritually pure unless you suppress all visible signs.
At CL 5, the extra damage becomes 1d6.
At CL 11, the extra damage becomes 1d8.
At CL 17, the extra damage becomes 1d10.
When Demon Seed ends, if you used Overdraw during its duration, make a Wisdom saving throw against your Daemonic Save DC. On a failure, gain 1 additional Corruption.
#### Devour Essence
Classification: Forbidden Daemonic Technique
Action Type: Multi-Mode
Canonical Action Type: Multi-Mode
Factory Combat Bucket: split_required
Split Candidate Buckets: bonus_action, reaction
Timing Detail: Bonus Action or Reaction
Factory Routing: split_modes_before_character_action_programming
Split Review Decision: split_required_distinct_combat_buckets
Recommended Factory Realization: modes=BONUS_ACTION_DEVOUR->bonus_action, REACTION_DEVOUR->reaction
Range: 30 feet
Cost: None
Use Devour Essence when one of the following happens within range:
a hostile creature is reduced to 0 HP;
a creature fails a saving throw against one of your Daemonic talents;
you score a Critical Hit;
a creature bearing your demonic mark takes damage;
an ongoing summoned, possessed, spirit, fiendish, undead, or demonic effect ends.
Gain 1 Devoured Essence.
You can use Devour Essence once per round.
If the triggering creature is at least your Realm or has a CR/level equal to at least half your CL, you may instead gain 2 Devoured Essence, but you also gain 1 Corruption.
#### Daemonic Augment
Classification: Forbidden Amplification
Action Type: Special Trigger
Canonical Action Type: Special Trigger
Factory Combat Bucket: passive
Timing Detail: No Action, once per turn
Factory Routing: triggered_passive_modifier_row
Cost: 1 CP, 1 Stamina, or 1 Devoured Essence
Trigger: You use a sphere talent, weapon attack, Unarmed Strike, or Cultivation Attack that deals damage, imposes a condition, moves a creature, creates a zone, or forces a saving throw.
Twist the technique with daemonic hunger. Choose one:
add Proficiency Bonus to one damage roll;
impose Disadvantage on one Concentration saving throw caused by the triggering effect;
if the triggering effect moves a creature, increase the movement by 5 feet;
if the triggering effect creates Difficult Terrain, one creature that fails a save also cannot take Reactions until the start of your next turn;
if the triggering effect deals Necrotic, Psychic, Fire, Poison, Acid, Force, or weapon damage, ignore ordinary Resistance to one of those damage types for that instance;
mark one damaged creature until the start of your next turn. The first time you damage the marked creature before the mark ends, gain 1 Devoured Essence.
Daemonic Augment may modify non-Daemonic sphere talents, but only once per turn. This is one of the main reasons the sphere is forbidden.

automatic_base_abilities.effect:
#### Demon Seed
Classification: Forbidden Daemonic Root
Action Type: Bonus Action
Factory Combat Bucket: bonus_action
Factory Routing: combat_action_row
Duration: 1 minute
Cost: 1 CP or 1 Stamina
Plant or awaken a Demon Seed in your body, dantian, meridians, or soul. The Seed is a forbidden method-root, not a Demon Core. It does not make you a demon; it opens the second furnace through which the daemonic scripture can breathe.
While Demon Seed is active:
your Daemonic talents may be used;
you gain Temporary HP equal to your Proficiency Bonus + your Daemonic key ability modifier;
once per turn when you hit with a weapon attack, Unarmed Strike, or Cultivation Attack, add 1d4 Necrotic, Psychic, or Force damage;
you have Advantage on saving throws against Frightened;
you have Disadvantage on checks made to appear spiritually pure unless you suppress all visible signs.
At CL 5, the extra damage becomes 1d6.
At CL 11, the extra damage becomes 1d8.
At CL 17, the extra damage becomes 1d10.
When Demon Seed ends, if you used Overdraw during its duration, make a Wisdom saving throw against your Daemonic Save DC. On a failure, gain 1 additional Corruption.
