spheres.full_exact_source_text: # Sphere of Death Qi Expression: Primary — Death Qi; Supporting — Yin Qi, Grave Qi, Severance Qi, Memory Qi. “The forbidden art is not killing. Killing is common. The forbidden art is making death answer when called.” Common Name: Death Sphere Sphere Type: Power Sphere Primary Path: Qi Cultivation Secondary Path: Spirit Awakening Rare Variant: Body Refining through Corpse-Tempered Body Resource: CP Common Effects: grave Qi, withering, anti-healing, corpses, undead, ghosts, funerary rites, soul severance, mortality seals, necrotic damage, battlefield dead, forbidden command ### Death Dao Death is the cultivation of endings, remains, memory, and final authority. A Fire cultivator burns what lives. A Blood cultivator commands what flows. A Radiance cultivator reveals what has become unclean. A Death cultivator asks what remains when motion stops, what law governs the corpse, and who has the right to command what should have rested. Death is forbidden because it is one of the few spheres whose full exploitation can exceed the normal scale of a single combatant. A master of Death may gather corpses as resources, turn battlefields into infrastructure, deny healing, answer resurrection with grave law, build undead labor, command formations, interrogate remains, bind ghosts, and make an army act through one will. This does not mean every Death cultivator is evil. Orthodox Death cultivators may serve as funeral priests, tomb wardens, ghost hunters, battlefield undertakers, ancestral medium-judges, corpse preservers, exorcists, or grave architects. The forbidden line is crossed when the cultivator treats souls as raw materials, steals the dead from their rites, creates unwilling undead, or uses the grief of others as fuel. ### Sphere Boundaries Death overlaps many spheres. These boundaries keep it fresh. #### Death vs. Blood Blood governs living blood, vitality in motion, lineage, wounds, and internal life-force. Death governs the body after life has failed, grave Qi, corpses, ghosts, mortality, and the laws that prevent healing or return. Death may damage living creatures, but it does not replace Blood’s blood control, heart commands, or living circulation arts. #### Death vs. Radiance Radiance reveals and purifies spiritual corruption. Death names endings and governs remains. Radiance exorcises by overwhelming falsehood with brilliance. Death exorcises by closing the rite, severing possession, or sending the dead onward. #### Death vs. Dark and Shadow Dark hides, blinds, and swallows sight. Shadow moves through the second silhouette. Death is not darkness. A grave may be bright at noon and still answer Death. #### Death vs. Spirit Awakening Spirit Awakening is a Path. Death is a sphere. Spirit Awakening provides the soul-facing sensitivity that makes Death safer and more orthodox, but Death itself supplies grave rites, corpse command, necrotic suppression, and funerary law. #### Death vs. Life Life restores. Death prevents return, preserves remains, and negotiates endings. Death can protect a soul from abuse and prevent a corpse from rising; it should not become a general healing sphere. #### Death vs. Formations Formations build stable arrays and territory engines. Death can provide grave anchors, corpse pylons, mausoleum logic, and battlefield remains, but it does not replace Formation design. ### Core Death Rules #### Corpse, Ghost, Soul, and Grave Qi Death distinguishes four related things. Corpse: the physical remains of a dead creature. Ghost: a lingering spiritual presence, echo, remnant, or personality-fragment. Soul: the deeper self that may pass onward, reincarnate, be judged, be protected, or be bound. Grave Qi: the death-aspected residue of decay, endings, funerary rites, violence, memory, tombs, and battlefield remains. A corpse is not automatically a soul. Animating a corpse does not necessarily enslave the original soul unless the talent says so. Binding a ghost does not necessarily bind the soul unless the talent says so. The difference matters. #### Orthodox and Forbidden Death Death talents may have the Forbidden tag. A Forbidden talent is not automatically unavailable, but it should be treated as illegal, taboo, spiritually dangerous, or sect-restricted in most orthodox settings. Death becomes forbidden when it does one or more of the following: creates unwilling undead; binds, imprisons, damages, consumes, or enslaves souls; desecrates protected remains; prevents a soul’s natural passage for personal power; uses corpses without rite, consent, battlefield authority, sect sanction, or emergency necessity; turns mass death into a strategic resource without consequence. Orthodox Death is possible. It emphasizes funerary rites, exorcism, preservation, ghost guidance, corpse protection, undead suppression, ancestor pacts, and voluntary guardian dead. #### Death Save DC When a Death talent calls for a saving throw, use your Cultivation Save DC. Cultivation Save DC: 8 + your Proficiency Bonus + your key ability modifier. Qi Cultivation usually uses Intelligence or Charisma, depending on your rules chassis. Spirit Awakening uses Wisdom. Body Refining Death variants use Constitution only when a feature permits it. #### Death Attack Modifier When a Death talent calls for a Cultivation Attack roll, use your Cultivation Attack Modifier. Cultivation Attack Modifier: Proficiency Bonus + your key ability modifier. #### Death Control Limit Death’s greatest danger is action economy. Use the Death Control Limit to control how many undead assets one character can maintain. Your Death Control Limit equals your Proficiency Bonus. Each undead asset has a Control Load. Lesser Corpse Servant: 1 Control Load. Corpse Servant: 1 Control Load. Greater Corpse Servant: 2 Control Load. Grave Formation: 3 Control Load. Grave Host: 5 Control Load. Unique undead, bound ghosts, and named corpses use the Control Load listed in their talent or assigned by the GM. You cannot willingly exceed your Death Control Limit unless a talent explicitly permits it. If your limit is exceeded because of a temporary effect ending, choose which assets remain under control; the rest collapse, flee, become inert, or act according to their nature at the GM’s discretion. #### Commanding Death Servants Unless a talent says otherwise, undead assets created by your Death talents act immediately after your turn. On your turn, you may use a Bonus Action to command any number of undead assets created by your Death sphere talents that are within 60 feet and can perceive your command or are linked to your grave Qi. A commanded undead asset may take one action from its stat block. If not commanded, it takes the Dodge action and moves only to avoid obvious hazards or remain near its assigned guard point. If you are Incapacitated, Unconscious, dead, or unable to issue coherent spiritual commands, your undead assets Dodge, guard their last instruction, or become inert until you recover. Forbidden undead may instead test the binding or act according to their hunger. #### Corpse Availability Death talents that require corpses require actual corpses, remains, bones, ashes, preserved bodies, battlefield dead, or funerary relics. They do not create free corpses from nothing. The GM may classify a corpse as one of the following: Common Corpse: ordinary dead creature, animal, bandit, soldier, beast, or similar. Notable Corpse: named NPC, trained warrior, monster, cultivator, sect member, or magically altered body. Mighty Corpse: elite monster, higher-Realm cultivator, huge corpse, ancient beast, sainted ancestor, or battlefield champion. Sacred Corpse: protected by rites, vows, clan law, divine decree, imperial seal, powerful karma, or living descendants. Notable, Mighty, and Sacred corpses may require extra time, higher CP cost, contested checks, ritual permission, or story consequences. #### Death Marks Some talents create a Grave Mark. A Grave Mark is a visible or spiritually perceptible sign of mortality placed on a creature. A creature may bear only one Grave Mark from you at a time unless a talent says otherwise. If you apply a new Grave Mark to the same creature, the old one ends. #### Death Talents and Souls A Death talent affects souls only if it explicitly says it affects a soul. If a talent says it affects ghosts, undead, corpses, possessions, or grave Qi, do not assume it damages or captures the soul. Soul-affecting talents are often Forbidden or heavily regulated. ### Base Sphere Abilities #### Grave Sense Action Type: Special Trigger Canonical Action Type: Special Trigger Factory Combat Bucket: passive Timing Detail: No action; you may focus as an Action for more detail Factory Routing: triggered_passive_modifier_row Range: 30 feet Cost: None You can sense strong nearby death-signs. You can detect the presence and direction, but not exact identity, of the following within range: corpses; undead; dying creatures at 0 HP; ghosts or lingering death echoes; grave Qi; recent violent death; active Death sphere effects. As an Action, you may focus on one death-sign you can sense and learn one of the following: whether it is corpse, undead, ghost, dying creature, grave Qi, or active Death effect; whether the death was recent or old; whether a corpse has been preserved, desecrated, animated, or protected by a rite; whether an undead creature appears bound, feral, willing, commanded, or self-willed; whether a possession or soul-binding effect is present, if it is visible to Death Sense. Grave Sense does not automatically reveal hidden creatures, invisible creatures, a complete stat block, the target’s Path, the target’s Realm, or private memories. At CL 10, the range becomes 60 feet. At CL 15, the range becomes 120 feet. #### Withering Hand Action Type: Multi-Mode Canonical Action Type: Multi-Mode Factory Combat Bucket: action Timing Detail: Special Attack or Action Factory Routing: combat_action_row_with_attack_replacement_mode Split Review Decision: same_bucket_attack_replacement_mode Recommended Factory Realization: modes=MELEE_ATTACK_REPLACEMENT->action, RANGED_ACTION->action Range: Melee reach or 60 feet Target: One creature Cost: None You strike with grave Qi, either through a touch, weapon, talisman, funerary seal, or bolt of pale force. When you take the Attack action, you may replace one attack with Withering Hand, making a Cultivation Attack roll against one creature within melee reach. Alternatively, you may use an Action to make a ranged Cultivation Attack roll against one creature within 60 feet. Hit: The target takes Necrotic damage based on your CL. CL 1-4: 1d8 Necrotic damage. CL 5-10: 2d8 Necrotic damage. CL 11-16: 3d8 Necrotic damage. CL 17-20: 4d8 Necrotic damage. Once per turn when you hit a creature with Withering Hand, healing the target receives is reduced by your Proficiency Bonus until the start of your next turn. This healing reduction applies once to each healing event. It does not reduce healing below 0. #### Rouse Lesser Dead Action Type: Ritual Procedure Canonical Action Type: Ritual Procedure Factory Routing: procedure_ledger_not_combat_action Timing Detail: Ritual Time: 10 minutes Range: Touch Target: One Common corpse or suitable set of remains Duration: 8 hours, or until the servant is destroyed or dismissed Cost: 1 CP Control Load: 1 Requirement: You must have enough unused Death Control Limit to maintain the servant, and the target must be a legal corpse under the Corpse Availability rules. You animate the target with grave Qi as one Lesser Corpse Servant. It appears in the corpse's space with full Hit Points and uses the Lesser Corpse Servant stat block below. The servant is one undead asset. It counts against your Death Control Limit, acts immediately after your turn, and is commanded according to Commanding Death Servants. If it is not commanded, it takes the Dodge action and moves only as permitted by those rules. A Lesser Corpse Servant does not contain the original soul unless another talent says so. It can follow simple commands, perform labor, carry objects, open doors, keep watch, pull carts, dig, clean, guard a threshold, or fight if commanded. You may maintain only one Lesser Corpse Servant created by this base ability at a time. You may dismiss that servant without taking an action on your turn. If you complete this ritual while one of your Lesser Corpse Servants from this ability still exists, the earlier servant must be dismissed before the new one is created. If the corpse is protected, sacred, claimed, preserved, or socially taboo, animating it may be impossible without a rite, permission, or a successful opposed Cultivation Check. #### Lesser Corpse Servant Stat Block Creature Type: Undead Size: Medium or Small, matching the corpse when possible AC: 10 + your Proficiency Bonus HP: 3 x your CL + your key ability modifier Speed: 25 feet Damage Immunities: Poison Condition Immunities: Charmed, Frightened, Poisoned Senses: passive Perception 8 + your Proficiency Bonus Languages: understands your commands; cannot speak unless a feature says otherwise Grave Strike: Melee attack using your Cultivation Attack Modifier, reach 5 feet, one target. Hit: 1d6 + your key ability modifier Bludgeoning, Slashing, or Necrotic damage. Inert Servant: If not commanded, the servant takes the Dodge action. ### Death Talent Tags Death talents use the following tags. Rite: funerary, ritual, investigation, preservation, exorcism, or corpse-handling technique. Withering: improves damage, anti-healing, decay, or mortality suppression. Corpse: manipulates, preserves, animates, commands, or weaponizes corpses. Ghost: affects ghosts, possession, spirits, or death echoes. Command: improves undead servants, formations, and death control. Forbidden: crosses a taboo line in most orthodox settings. Domain: creates a persistent field or court. Realm Evolution: expands the basic functioning of the sphere at a cultivation threshold. ### Mortal Realm Talents #### Grave Chill - Withering Action Type: Action Factory Combat Bucket: action Factory Routing: combat_action_row Range: 60 feet Target: One creature Cost: 2 CP Choose one creature within range. It makes a Constitution saving throw. Failed Save: The target takes 2d6 Necrotic damage and cannot regain HP until the start of your next turn. Successful Save: The target takes half damage, and healing it receives before the start of your next turn is reduced by your Proficiency Bonus. At CL 11, the damage becomes 4d6. At CL 17, the damage becomes 6d6. #### Mark for the Grave - Withering Action Type: Bonus Action Factory Combat Bucket: bonus_action Factory Routing: combat_action_row Range: 60 feet Duration: 1 minuteConcentration: Required Cost: 2 CP Choose one creature within range. It bears your Grave Mark. The first time each turn the marked creature takes Necrotic damage from you or one of your Death servants, add your Proficiency Bonus to one damage roll. While marked, the target also has Disadvantage on the first death saving throw it makes during the duration. A creature can bear only one Grave Mark from you at a time. #### Bone Ward - Corpse Action Type: Reaction Factory Combat Bucket: reaction Factory Routing: combat_action_row Trigger: You or an ally within 30 feet takes damage Cost: 1 CP A shard of bone, ash, grave cloth, funerary paper, or pale grave Qi rises to intercept harm. Reduce the triggering damage by an amount based on your CL. CL 1-10: 1d8 + your key ability modifier. CL 11-16: 2d8 + your key ability modifier. CL 17-20: 3d8 + your key ability modifier. If a corpse, bone pile, grave marker, or funerary object is within 10 feet of the protected creature, add your Proficiency Bonus to the reduction. #### Speak with the Departed - Rite, Ghost Action Type: Ritual Procedure Canonical Action Type: Ritual Procedure Factory Routing: procedure_ledger_not_combat_action Timing Detail: Ritual Time: 10 minutes Range: Touch Target: One corpse, skull, grave marker, funerary tablet, or lingering death echo Cost: 1 CP You ask up to three brief questions of the dead or the death-imprint attached to the remains. The answer is limited to what the creature knew in life, what the corpse experienced near death, what the lingering ghost remembers, or what the remains spiritually recorded. The dead may answer in words, images, gestures, smells, cold, blood patterns, grave insects, flickering lantern light, or other signs. The effect may fail or become unclear if: the corpse is too damaged; the soul has passed beyond reach; the corpse is protected by rites; another Death cultivator has sealed it; the dead refuse to speak; the question concerns secrets protected by stronger spiritual law. #### Funerary Preservation - Rite Action Type: Ritual Procedure Canonical Action Type: Ritual Procedure Factory Routing: procedure_ledger_not_combat_action Timing Detail: Ritual Time: 10 minutes Range: Touch Target: One corpse, set of remains, grave relic, or funerary chamber Duration: 7 days Cost: 1 CP You preserve remains against decay, ordinary scavengers, mundane rot, and uncontrolled undeath. For the duration: the corpse does not naturally decay; ordinary undead cannot rise from it without overcoming your Cultivation Save DC; Speak with the Departed gains Advantage on checks involving the corpse; resurrection or reincarnation remains possible if the setting otherwise permits it; tampering with the corpse leaves a spiritual mark you can sense with Grave Sense. At CL 10, the duration becomes 30 days. At CL 15, it lasts until dismissed or ritually broken. #### Quiet Burial - Rite Action Type: Multi-Mode Canonical Action Type: Multi-Mode Factory Combat Bucket: action Timing Detail: Action or Ritual Factory Routing: combat_action_plus_ritual_variant Split Review Decision: single_combat_action_plus_procedure_variant Recommended Factory Realization: procedures=RITUAL_BURIAL_RITE Range: Touch Target: One corpse, undead remains, haunted object, or grave site Cost: 1 CP You perform a swift burial mudra, closing minor death echoes. Choose one effect: end one ordinary haunting attached to a corpse or grave object; prevent one corpse from being animated for 24 hours; cause one destroyed undead creature’s remains to become spiritually quiet; grant Advantage on one check made within the next hour to track a ghost, murderer, or necromancer through death residue; let one dying creature within reach immediately make a death saving throw with Advantage. This does not destroy a soul or defeat a powerful curse by itself. #### Death Mask - Rite Action Type: Action Factory Combat Bucket: action Factory Routing: combat_action_row Range: Self or touch Duration: 1 hour Cost: 1 CP You veil a living creature in the stillness of the grave. For the duration, the target gains Advantage on ability checks made to appear dead, avoid detection by unintelligent undead, or hide its life signs from ordinary examination. Grave Sense, Spirit Awakening techniques, Medicine checks, or a direct physical examination may contest the effect with a check against your Cultivation Save DC. When you command one or more Death servants with your Bonus Action, one commanded servant gains Temporary HP equal to your Proficiency Bonus. #### Gravebound Locus Scripture Your Death cultivation is tied to a specific tomb, ancestral tablet, graveyard, mausoleum, battlefield, or portable funerary shrine. When you are more than 1 mile per CL from your locus, Death talents that cost CP cost +1 CP. If a talent already costs 10 or more CP, it instead requires a successful Cultivation Check against DC 15 + the CP cost or the action and CP are wasted. Gain Mausoleum of Quiet Souls as a bonus talent when you meet its prerequisites. Until then, gain Funerary Preservation. You may attune a new locus with an 8-hour rite. ### Path Synergies #### Qi Cultivation - Grave Meridian Qi Cultivation treats Death as a pattern of grave Qi and mortality law. You may use Intelligence or Charisma as your Death key ability, depending on your Qi Cultivation rules. Once per turn, when you damage a creature that cannot regain HP or has healing reduced by your Death talent, add your key ability modifier to one Necrotic damage roll. When you use a Death talent that costs 2 or more CP while within 10 feet of a corpse, grave marker, funerary tablet, or Death servant, reduce the cost by 1 CP, minimum 1. #### Spirit Awakening - Funeral Soul Spirit Awakening treats Death as a threshold between soul, ghost, and reincarnation. You may use Wisdom as your Death key ability. Your Ghost and Rite talents can affect incorporeal creatures, ghosts, possessing spirits, and soul-bound entities normally when the technique’s fiction can reach them. When you use Speak with the Departed, Soul Funeral, Ghost Lantern, or Ghostly Retinue, you may ask one additional brief question, reveal one additional spiritual sign, or grant one affected ally Advantage on one saving throw against possession before the start of your next turn. #### Body Refining - Corpse-Tempered Body This synergy requires the Corpse-Tempered Body Cultivation Insight. You may use Constitution as your Death key ability and Stamina instead of CP for Death talents. When you take Necrotic damage, you may use your Reaction and spend Stamina up to your Proficiency Bonus. Reduce the damage by 1d8 per Stamina spent. If this reduces the damage to 0, you may immediately use Grave Sense without an action. Your body bears deathly signs: corpse-pale skin, tomb-cold breath, iron-black veins, bone sutures, funeral tattoos, or a heartbeat that slows when danger nears. ### Cultivation Insights #### Corpse-Tempered Body Prerequisite: Body Refining, CL 4+ You may learn the Death sphere as a Body Refining cultivator. You gain the Body Refining - Corpse-Tempered Body path synergy. You are not undead, but your body can store grave Qi without immediate rejection. You gain Resistance to Necrotic damage for 1 minute once per long rest when you use a Death talent or take Necrotic damage. #### Gravekeeper Prerequisite: Death, CL 4+ You are trained in lawful funeral practice. Gain Advantage on checks made to investigate death, identify undead, recognize possession, prepare corpses, locate hidden graves, or determine whether remains have been desecrated. Funerary Preservation no longer costs CP for Common corpses. #### Bone General Prerequisite: Corpse Servant, CL 8+ Increase your Death Control Limit by 1, but the extra capacity can be used only for Corpse Servants or Lesser Corpse Servants. When you use a Bonus Action to command Death servants, one commanded servant may move up to 10 feet before taking its action. #### Merciful Reaper Prerequisite: Death, CL 8+ When a creature dies within 30 feet, you may use your Reaction to choose one: prevent its corpse from being animated for 24 hours; preserve its soul from ordinary destruction until the next dawn; allow it to speak one final sentence; end one ordinary possession affecting its corpse; grant one ally who can hear the final breath Temporary HP equal to your Proficiency Bonus. This Insight is favored by orthodox Death cultivators. #### Tomb Architect Prerequisite: Death, Formations or Protection, CL 10+ When designing a tomb, mausoleum, graveyard, ancestor hall, corpse vault, or battlefield burial array, you may use one Death talent as a project seed. This does not create the project automatically. It provides a valid conceptual anchor for Formation, Protection, Spirit, Radiance, or Qiweaving design. #### Black-Lantern Commander Prerequisite: Death, Grave Formation, CL 12+ When you control a Grave Formation, increase its Speed by 10 feet and its maximum HP by your CL. Once per short rest, when a Grave Formation you control drops to 0 HP, it may make one Grave Assault before collapsing. #### Psychopomp’s Courtesy Prerequisite: Death, Spirit Awakening, CL 8+ When you use Soul Funeral or Quiet Burial against a ghost, undead, or possessing entity, you may choose to deal no damage. If you do, the target has Disadvantage on its saving throw if it is currently possessing a creature, desecrating remains, or preventing a soul from passing onward. If the target fails and is not destroyed, it may ask one brief question before departing or being expelled.

resolved_automatic_base_abilities.effect:
#### Rouse Lesser Dead
Action Type: Ritual Procedure
Canonical Action Type: Ritual Procedure
Factory Routing: procedure_ledger_not_combat_action
Timing Detail: Ritual
Time: 10 minutes
Range: Touch
Target: One Common corpse or suitable set of remains
Duration: 8 hours, or until the servant is destroyed or dismissed
Cost: 1 CP
Control Load: 1
Requirement: You must have enough unused Death Control Limit to maintain the servant, and the target must be a legal corpse under the Corpse Availability rules.
You animate the target with grave Qi as one Lesser Corpse Servant. It appears in the corpse's space with full Hit Points and uses the Lesser Corpse Servant stat block below.
The servant is one undead asset. It counts against your Death Control Limit, acts immediately after your turn, and is commanded according to Commanding Death Servants. If it is not commanded, it takes the Dodge action and moves only as permitted by those rules.
A Lesser Corpse Servant does not contain the original soul unless another talent says so. It can follow simple commands, perform labor, carry objects, open doors, keep watch, pull carts, dig, clean, guard a threshold, or fight if commanded.
You may maintain only one Lesser Corpse Servant created by this base ability at a time. You may dismiss that servant without taking an action on your turn. If you complete this ritual while one of your Lesser Corpse Servants from this ability still exists, the earlier servant must be dismissed before the new one is created.
If the corpse is protected, sacred, claimed, preserved, or socially taboo, animating it may be impossible without a rite, permission, or a successful opposed Cultivation Check.

spheres.full_exact_source_text: # Sphere of Destruction Qi Expression: Primary — Ruin Qi; Supporting — Thunder Qi, Fire Qi, Force Qi, Severance Qi. “Destruction is not an element. It is the moment restraint fails.” Common Name: Destruction Sphere Sphere Type: Direct Calamity / Blast Modification Sphere Primary Paths: Qi Cultivation, Body Refining Secondary Path: Spirit Awakening Resource: Normal Path CP; Stamina for embodied martial destructionCore Chassis: Destructive Blast, Destruction Dice, Blast Types, Blast Shapes, Calamity Pressure, Breakage ConsequencesCore Abilities: Destructive Blast, Deepen the Calamity, Shape the Release Common Effects: destructive attacks, area blasts, rays, explosive pearls, weapon imbuement, counterblasts, destructive auras, ruin walls, tethers, object breaking, barrier breaching, battlefield damage, and large-scale calamity ### Destruction Dao Destruction breaks, blasts, overwhelms, ends, and shatters. A cultivator of Destruction does not merely summon an element or release force. They discover what a resonance becomes when restraint is removed and the integrity of the obstacle is no longer preserved. Fire burns because it is Fire. Lightning shocks because it is Lightning. Sound shatters because vibration finds a flaw. Destruction is older and simpler than those expressions. Destruction is what happens when a thing can no longer remain itself. A Destruction cultivator asks: Where is the point at which this thing stops enduring? ### The Destruction Cultivation Loop Destruction follows a direct battlefield loop: Find the Fault -> Release Ruin -> Shape the Calamity -> Exploit Breakage -> Leave Nothing Whole A Destruction technique usually begins by identifying what must fail, then releasing ruin through a selected Type and Shape. The Type determines what kind of breakage occurs. The Shape determines how that breakage enters the battlefield. ### Sphere Boundaries Destruction overlaps with many spheres, but it does not replace them. Fire, Lightning, Cold, Water, Earth, Air, Metal, Magma, Sound, Light, Shadow, and similar elemental or substance spheres. Destruction can break things using force, rupture, pressure, fracture, or calamity. It does not grant full elemental control. Cross-sphere elemental blast types belong to their own spheres or to optional synergy/forged-technique rules, not to base Destruction. Force. Force answers impact and creates pressure, anchors, and counterpressure. Destruction uses ruin as an offensive release. It may feel forceful, but it is not general telekinesis, barriers, or reactive force doctrine. Death. Death governs endings, grave law, corpses, funerary power, and undead. Destruction can kill or break bodies, but it does not command the dead or cultivate the law of mortality. Void. Void erases, denies, hollows, and removes presence. Destruction breaks what is present. It does not automatically negate existence, erase talents, or unmake metaphysical laws. Ash / Decay. Ash and decay express ruin through aftermath, corrosion, entropy, rot, remnants, and what remains after burning. Destruction is the immediate act of breaking. Protection. Protection prevents harm and holds boundaries. Destruction breaks through boundaries. It does not create general wards or defensive aegises except through specific destructive counters. Warleader and Tactics. Destruction can clear lines, breach walls, and punish clusters. It does not coordinate allies, command units, or create strategic orders by itself. Weapon spheres. Destruction can temper a weapon with ruin, but it does not replace weapon mastery, stances, maneuvers, or martial disciplines. Alchemy. Destruction can make explosive pearls or release calamity through prepared vessels, but it does not create a general alchemy, pill, bomb, or reagent system. ### Rules Baseline This draft assumes the current Tianxia 5.5e conversion baseline: Use Action, Bonus Action, Reaction, Concentration, short rest, long rest, saving throws, attack rolls, damage types, objects, cover, and movement rules from the current rules set. Use Cultivation Level (CL), Proficiency Bonus (PB), Cultivation Save DC, Cultivation Attack Modifier, CP, and Path resource language. Forced movement cannot normally move a creature into a solid object unless a feature says otherwise. Forced movement does not normally provoke opportunity attacks unless a feature says otherwise. Area effects affect allies unless the talent says otherwise. Objects, barriers, walls, doors, formation anchors, and structures use GM-assigned durability when exact statistics are not available. A talent that creates a persistent object, wall, tether, pearl, sphere, or mantle should state how long it lasts and whether it can be destroyed. A Destruction talent never grants broad elemental control merely because its damage description resembles an element. ### Key Ability, Save DC, and Costs Use your normal Path key ability unless a feature says otherwise. Body Refining: Constitution, spending Stamina. Qi Cultivation: Intelligence or Charisma, chosen when the Path is selected, spending Qi. Spirit Awakening: Wisdom, spending Resonance. Cultivation Save DC: 8 + your Proficiency Bonus + your key ability modifier. Cultivation Attack Modifier: your Proficiency Bonus + your key ability modifier. This document uses CP as the general resource term. Replace CP with Stamina, Qi, or Resonance as appropriate to the character’s Path. ### Martial, Power, and Body Access Destruction is a Direct Calamity sphere with both martial and power expressions. #### Martial Destruction Martial Destruction expresses through body impact, weapon strikes, shattering footwork, pressure release, shockwave palms, breath bursts, explosive thrown objects, breaking fists, hammer methods, and ruin-tempered armaments. #### Power Destruction Power Destruction expresses through condensed qi, spiritual calamity, raw rupture, pressure spheres, ruin rays, explosive pearls, destructive walls, and battlefield releases. #### Body Refining Destruction Body Refiners normally do not project qi outside the body. A Body Refiner using Destruction should usually express it through: impact released from fists, feet, elbows, knees, horns, claws, weapons, or breath; thrown weapons, sling stones, explosive pearls, shockwave steps, or body-generated pressure; breaking methods that travel through contact, surfaces, weapons, or physically plausible lines; internal power released outward only at the moment of impact. A Body Refiner can use listed ranges when the technique has a physical or embodied explanation. Otherwise, the GM may restrict a Body Refining Destruction technique to touch, melee reach, weapon reach, thrown range, or a special forged method. ### Core Destruction Rules #### Destruction Dice Many Destruction features use Destruction Dice. Unless a Blast Type says otherwise, a Destruction Die is a d8. Your number of Destruction Dice is based on Cultivation Level. CL 1-4: 1 Destruction Die CL 5-10: 2 Destruction Dice CL 11-16: 3 Destruction Dice CL 17+: 4 Destruction Dice #### Blast Types and Blast Shapes A Blast Type determines what kind of ruin the blast creates: damage type, die size, rider effect, and special restrictions. A Blast Shape determines how the ruin enters the battlefield: ray, area, pearl, weapon, mantle, tether, wall, and similar geometry. When modifying one Destructive Blast, you may apply: no more than one Blast Type; no more than one Blast Shape. A talent explicitly stating otherwise creates an exception. #### Blast Shape Saving Throws Some Blast Shapes replace the ordinary Cultivation Attack with saving throws. When a Blast Shape calls for a saving throw: if the final CP cost of the Destructive Blast is 0, a successful saving throw negates the blast’s damage and Blast Type rider effects; if the final CP cost is 1 or more, a successful saving throw halves the damage and negates the Blast Type rider effects. #### Persistent Blast Safeguard A creature can suffer a particular Blast Type’s rider effect from the same ongoing Destructive Blast no more than once per turn. This safeguard applies to persistent effects such as Calamity Mantle, Wandering Calamity, Ruin-Binding Tether, Calamity Curtain, and similar ongoing releases. A creature may still take damage from an ongoing blast as permitted by the Blast Shape’s rules. #### Breakage Consequences When a Destruction effect damages an object, barrier, wall, structure, formation anchor, siege engine, cover source, or similar target, the GM determines whether the damage creates a breach, weakens cover, breaks a lock, opens a passage, collapses a section, or merely damages the target. Destruction is allowed to matter to the environment, but it should not bypass scene logic. A wooden door, stone wall, sect barrier, immortal vault, ship hull, formation pillar, and mountain ridge do not all fail the same way. #### Friendly Fire Unless a talent says otherwise, Destruction does not distinguish friend from foe. If allies stand inside a destructive area, they are affected normally. ### Core Abilities #### Destructive Blast Base Sphere Ability Action Type: Action Factory Combat Bucket: action Factory Routing: combat_action_row Range: 30 feet Target: One creature or object Duration: Instantaneous Cost: 0 CP You release cultivated destruction against one creature or object within range. Choose one Blast Type talent you possess. You may also apply no more than one Blast Shape talent you possess. If you do not apply a Blast Shape talent, release an unshaped blast: make one ranged Cultivation Attack against one creature or object within range; on a hit, the target takes your Destructive Blast damage and suffers any applicable effects of the selected Blast Type. If you know no other Blast Type, you use Unadorned Ruin. #### Deepen the Calamity Destructive Blast Augment Cost: 1 CP Instead of using the ordinary Destructive Blast progression, your Destructive Blast deals: 1 Destruction Die + 1 additional Destruction Die per 2 Cultivation Levels, rounded down. CL 1: 1 Destruction Die CL 2-3: 2 Destruction Dice CL 4-5: 3 Destruction Dice CL 6-7: 4 Destruction Dice CL 8-9: 5 Destruction Dice CL 10-11: 6 Destruction Dice CL 12-13: 7 Destruction Dice CL 14-15: 8 Destruction Dice CL 16-17: 9 Destruction Dice CL 18-19: 10 Destruction Dice CL 20: 11 Destruction Dice Deepen the Calamity makes Destruction a serious combat blast, but it also marks the release as a committed expenditure of cultivation power. Any Blast Shape saving throw uses the “final CP cost is 1 or more” rule. #### Shape the Release You shape a Destructive Blast by applying one Blast Shape talent you know. A Blast Shape may change the Action economy, range, area, targeting, duration, saving throw, weapon interaction, movement, or persistence of the blast. Unless the Blast Shape says otherwise, the selected Blast Type and all parameters are chosen when the blast is released and cannot be changed while the effect remains active. ## Default Blast Type ### Unadorned Ruin Default Destruction Blast Type Destruction Die: d8 Damage Type: Force Destruction expresses itself directly as impact, rupture, collapse, and overwhelming release. Unadorned Ruin has no additional rider effect. A cultivator who knows the Sphere of Destruction always knows Unadorned Ruin. It does not require a talent selection. #### Breaching Proof Foundation Refinement Requirement: Unadorned Ruin, Foundation Realm Unadorned Ruin deals one additional Destruction Die against objects, structures, barriers, formation anchors, siege engines, and similar constructed defenses. #### Calamity Without Ornament Nascent Soul Refinement Requirement: Breaching Proof, Nascent Soul Realm When another Destruction talent allows you to add Destruction Dice to Unadorned Ruin, increase the maximum permitted number of additional dice by one. ## Mortal Talents ### Controlled Ruin Blast Discipline Talent You learn to keep your release from scattering wastefully. When you release an unshaped Destructive Blast, increase its range to 60 feet. When you use a Blast Shape that affects an area, you may exclude yourself from the area if you are inside it. This does not exclude allies unless another talent says otherwise. ### Crushing Break Blast Type Talent Destruction Die: d8 Damage Type: Bludgeoning Your ruin manifests as direct crushing impact. A creature damaged by Crushing Break makes a Strength saving throw. On a failure, push the creature 10 feet away from the blast’s point of origin. Forced movement from Crushing Break cannot move a creature through a solid barrier. ### Fracturing Break Blast Type Talent Destruction Die: d8 Damage Type: Force Your ruin finds stress lines and worsens them. A creature damaged by Fracturing Break makes a Constitution saving throw. On a failure, the next attack roll made against that creature before the start of your next turn gains Advantage. Objects and structures damaged by Fracturing Break count as cracked until the start of your next turn. The next source of Bludgeoning, Thunder, or Force damage against such a target deals one additional Destruction Die. ### Scouring Break Blast Type Talent Destruction Die: d6 Damage Type: Slashing Your ruin tears surfaces, armor gaps, and exposed defenses. A creature damaged by Scouring Break makes a Dexterity saving throw. On a failure, it cannot take Reactions until the start of your next turn. Spaces meaningfully affected by an area Blast Shape may become littered with splinters, shards, torn stone, or cutting residue until the start of your next turn. Moving through such a space costs an additional 5 feet of movement. ### Staggering Break Blast Type Talent Destruction Die: d6 Damage Type: Thunder Your ruin hammers rhythm, breath, and balance. A creature damaged by Staggering Break makes a Constitution saving throw. On a failure, it has Disadvantage on its next Concentration saving throw before the start of your next turn. A creature that cannot hear is still affected; the damage is destructive vibration, not ordinary sound. ### Withering Break Blast Type Talent Destruction Die: d6 Damage Type: Necrotic Your ruin expresses as immediate structural exhaustion rather than grave authority. A creature damaged by Withering Break cannot regain Hit Points until the start of your next turn. This is destructive depletion, not control over death, corpses, ghosts, or undead. ### Heaven-Piercing Ray Blast Shape Talent Release your Destructive Blast as a ray. Make one ranged Cultivation Attack against one target within range. You may instead make a melee Cultivation Attack against a target within your natural reach. Augment - 1 CP: Release multiple rays as part of the same Action. CL 1-4: 2 rays CL 5-10: 3 rays CL 11-16: 4 rays CL 17+: 5 rays Make a separate Cultivation Attack for each ray. Each ray deals full damage and applies the ordinary rules of the selected Blast Type. No creature or object may be targeted by more than one ray from the same release. ### Calamity Form Blast Shape Talent You shape your destructive cultivation into a deliberate area release. Augment - 0 CP: Release your Destructive Blast in a 5-foot-radius area centered on a point within range. You may exclude yourself. Affected creatures make a Dexterity saving throw. Augment - 1 CP: Instead release your Destructive Blast as one of the following: a 30-foot cone; a 120-foot-long, 5-foot-wide line. The effect emanates from one point within range. Affected creatures make a Dexterity saving throw. ### Leaping Ruin Blast Shape Talent Your Destructive Blast arcs toward one creature or object of your choice within range. The target makes a Dexterity saving throw. Augment - 1 CP: When the first target fails its saving throw, you may spend a Bonus Action to cause the release to leap to additional targets. The blast may affect a total number of targets equal to your Proficiency Bonus. Each additional target must be: within 30 feet of the previous target; within your Destructive Blast range; visible to you; not previously affected by the same release. Each additional target makes its own Dexterity saving throw. No creature or object may be affected more than once by the same Leaping Ruin. ### Calamity Pearl Blast Shape Talent Your Destructive Blast affects one 5-foot cube within range. Creatures in that cube make a Dexterity saving throw. #### Sealed Pearl Augment - 0 CP: Instead of resolving immediately, the Destructive Blast forms as a cultivated pearl approximately the size of a sling stone. You or another creature may throw the pearl with a normal range of 20 feet and a long range of 60 feet, hurl it with a sling using the sling’s normal range, place it carefully on a surface, or deliberately shatter it. The pearl releases the stored Destructive Blast when shattered. If placed without shattering, it releases after 1 minute. A creature may shatter a pearl within reach as an Action, as a Bonus Action, or by spending 5 feet of movement while passing through its space. A creature unaware of the pearl that moves through its space has a 50 percent chance of shattering it. You cannot maintain more Sealed Pearls at one time than your Proficiency Bonus. For rules interacting with thrown alchemical items or traps, treat a Sealed Pearl as a throwable prepared formula. Augment - 1 CP: The Sealed Pearl persists for 8 hours. If you are within your Destructive Blast range of the pearl, you may cause it to release as a Reaction. At the end of the duration, the pearl either releases or dissipates. Choose which outcome occurs when creating it. Augment - 1 CP: The affected area becomes a sphere with a radius of up to 20 feet. ### Ruin-Tempered Armament Blast Shape Talent Action Type: Multi-Mode Canonical Action Type: Multi-Mode Factory Combat Bucket: split_required Split Candidate Buckets: action, bonus_action Timing Detail: Action or Bonus Action, chosen when activated Factory Routing: split_modes_before_character_action_programming Split Review Decision: split_required_distinct_combat_buckets Recommended Factory Realization: modes=ACTION_IMBUE->action, BONUS_ACTION_IMBUE->bonus_action Duration: Concentration, up to 1 minute Your Destructive Blast imbues weapons and ammunition. Choose one of the following within range: one melee weapon; one natural weapon; one unarmed strike; up to 20 pieces of ammunition. The selected weapon or ammunition deals the chosen Blast Type’s damage type instead of its ordinary damage type. Attacks made with the imbued weapon or ammunition do not deal additional Destructive Blast damage and do not apply the Blast Type’s rider effect unless stated below. After damaging a creature with an imbued weapon or piece of ammunition, the wielder may spend a Bonus Action to apply the selected Blast Type’s rider effect to that creature as though it had been damaged by the Destructive Blast. Critical hits with an imbued weapon or piece of ammunition deal additional damage of the selected Blast Type. This damage is added after resolving the critical hit and is not doubled. CL 1-4: +1d6 damage CL 5-10: +2d6 damage CL 11-16: +3d6 damage CL 17+: +4d6 damage Augment - 1 CP: Imbue a number of additional weapons, natural weapons, unarmed strikes, or sets of ammunition equal to your Proficiency Bonus. Augment - 2 CP: The imbuement persists for its remaining duration without requiring Concentration. You may apply this augment after activating the talent on your turn without using an Action. ### Returning Calamity Blast Shape Talent Augment - 1 CP: You may release your Destructive Blast as a Reaction when you are damaged by a creature within range that you can see. The creature that damaged you becomes the target of the blast. The target makes a Dexterity saving throw. On a successful save, the target takes half damage and negates the selected Blast Type’s rider effect. ### Ruin-Crossing Step Blast Shape Talent Your Destructive Blast becomes a 5-foot-wide, 10-foot-long line emanating from you. After the release resolves, you appear in the final square of the line or the nearest legal unoccupied space. Affected creatures make a Dexterity saving throw. You do not count as moving through intermediate spaces. This movement does not provoke opportunity attacks. Augment - 1 CP: Increase the length of the line by any amount up to your Destructive Blast range. Augment - 1 CP: You may appear in any legal unoccupied space along the line after the release resolves. ## Foundation Talents ### Breaching Proof Blast Type Refinement Requirement: Unadorned Ruin, Foundation Realm Unadorned Ruin deals one additional Destruction Die against objects, structures, barriers, formation anchors, siege engines, cover sources, and similar constructed defenses. If this destroys a meaningful barrier section, the GM should normally create a breach, weakened cover, exposed anchor, or other visible consequence. ### Break the Guard Blast Type Refinement Requirement: Fracturing Break or Scouring Break, Foundation Realm When a creature fails its saving throw against Fracturing Break or Scouring Break, choose one: its AC is reduced by 1 until the start of your next turn; the next attack roll against it before the start of your next turn gains Advantage; it cannot benefit from half cover until the start of your next turn. A creature can suffer only one option from Break the Guard at a time. ### Hammer Through the Line Blast Type Refinement Requirement: Crushing Break, Foundation Realm When Crushing Break pushes a creature into a solid obstacle or another creature, the pushed creature takes one additional Destruction Die of Bludgeoning damage and falls Prone. If the pushed creature collides with another creature, the second creature makes a Dexterity saving throw. On a failure, it also falls Prone. ### Ruinous Interruption Blast Type Refinement Requirement: Staggering Break, Foundation Realm A creature that fails its saving throw against Staggering Break cannot take Reactions until the start of your next turn. If the creature is Concentrating, it also has Disadvantage on the Concentration saving throw caused by the blast’s damage. ### Ashen Denial Blast Type Refinement Requirement: Withering Break, Foundation Realm A creature damaged by Withering Break cannot gain Temporary HP until the start of your next turn. If the creature already has Temporary HP, remove those Temporary HP before applying damage. ### Calamity Mantle Blast Shape Talent Duration: 1 round Your Destructive Blast becomes an aura of destructive cultivation extending 10 feet from you. While the Calamity Mantle is active, you may spend a Bonus Action to affect every other creature within the aura with your Destructive Blast. Affected creatures make a Dexterity saving throw. The Blast Type and all other parameters are selected when you activate the Calamity Mantle and cannot be changed while it remains active. Augment - 1 CP: The duration becomes Concentration, up to 1 minute. Augment - 2 CP: The Calamity Mantle persists for its remaining duration without requiring Concentration. You may apply this augment after activating the talent on your turn without using an Action. ### Wandering Calamity Blast Shape Talent Duration: 1 round Your Destructive Blast takes the form of a 5-foot-diameter sphere of cultivated calamity. The sphere appears in one legal unoccupied space within range. A creature entering the sphere’s space is affected by the blast and makes a Dexterity saving throw. A creature cannot take damage from the same Wandering Calamity more than once per turn. As a Bonus Action, move the sphere up to 30 feet. If you ram the sphere into a creature, that creature makes a Dexterity saving throw. On a success, it negates the sphere’s damage and rider effects. After attempting to ram a creature, the sphere stops moving for the turn in the space immediately before that creature. The sphere flies and is never at risk of falling. Augment - 1 CP: The duration becomes Concentration, up to 1 minute. Augment - 2 CP: The Wandering Calamity persists for its remaining duration without requiring Concentration. You may apply this augment after activating the talent on your turn without using an Action. ### Ruin-Binding Tether Blast Shape Talent Duration: Concentration, up to 1 minute Make one of the following attacks against a creature or object within 30 feet: a melee Cultivation Attack if the target is within your natural reach; a ranged Cultivation Attack otherwise. On a hit, deal your selected Destructive Blast damage and tether the target to you. The tethered target cannot willingly move farther away from you unless you allow it. While the tether persists, neither you nor the target can move more than 30 feet from the other. Either creature may attempt to drag the other through a contested Strength check. If the moving creature wins, it may move up to half its Speed while dragging the other creature. A creature at least two size categories larger than the opposing creature cannot be dragged and may move freely at full Speed while dragging the smaller creature. While the tether remains, you may spend a Bonus Action to deal the stored Destructive Blast damage to the tethered target again. The target makes a Dexterity saving throw. The Blast Type and all other parameters are selected when the tether is created and cannot be changed while it remains active. The tether has AC equal to 10 + your Proficiency Bonus, HP equal to 3 x your CL, immunity to Psychic damage, and immunity to the selected Blast Type’s damage type. The tether’s HP refreshes at the start of your turn. Augment - 2 CP: The tether persists for its remaining duration without requiring Concentration. You may apply this augment after activating the talent on your turn without using an Action. ### Calamity Curtain Blast Shape Talent Duration: Concentration, up to 1 minute Create one 5-foot-by-5-foot wall panel on a flat surface within range. A creature passing through the panel suffers the damage and effects of the selected Destructive Blast. A creature standing in the wall’s space when the panel appears makes a Dexterity saving throw. On a successful saving throw, that creature chooses which side of the wall it occupies. On a failed saving throw, you choose which side it occupies, provided the creature can fit in the selected space. The Calamity Curtain does not normally block line of effect, sight, projectiles, or thrown objects. A creature cannot take damage from the same Calamity Curtain more than once per turn. The maximum number of contiguous panels increases with your Cultivation Level. CL 1-4: 1 panel CL 5-10: 2 panels CL 11-16: 4 panels CL 17+: 8 panels Augment - 0 CP: Create a spherical or hemispherical dome instead of a linear wall. The dome’s radius cannot exceed the width or height of one panel. Augment - 1 CP: Increase the maximum width and height of each panel. CL 1-4: 10 feet x 10 feet CL 5-10: 15 feet x 15 feet CL 11-16: 20 feet x 20 feet CL 17+: 25 feet x 25 feet Augment - 1 CP: Create twice as many panels. Augment - 1 CP: The Calamity Curtain blocks sight. Moving through the wall requires an additional 5 feet of movement. At CL 11 or higher, nonmagical projectiles passing through the wall are destroyed. Augment - 2 CP: The Calamity Curtain persists for its remaining duration without requiring Concentration. You may apply this augment after activating the talent on your turn without using an Action. ## Core Formation Talents ### Catastrophe Engine Blast Discipline Talent Requirement: Core Formation Realm Once per turn when you spend CP on Deepen the Calamity, reduce the CP cost of one Blast Shape augment applied to that same Destructive Blast by 1, to a minimum of 0 CP. You cannot reduce the cost of an augment that removes Concentration. ### Collapsing Aftermath Blast Type Refinement Requirement: Core Formation Realm When your Destructive Blast destroys or drops a meaningful object, barrier, structure section, cover source, or construct to 0 Hit Points, choose one visible space adjacent to it. That space becomes hazardous wreckage until the start of your next turn. The first creature other than you to enter that space or start its turn there takes one Destruction Die of damage of the blast’s damage type. ### Ruin That Remembers Blast Shape Talent Requirement: Core Formation Realm When you damage a creature with Destructive Blast, you may spend 2 CP to leave a Ruin Trace on it for 1 minute. Once during that duration, when you damage the same creature again with Destructive Blast, consume the Ruin Trace to deal two additional Destruction Dice of the same damage type. A creature can bear only one Ruin Trace from you at a time. ### Calamity Without Mercy Blast Discipline Talent Requirement: Core Formation Realm When a creature succeeds on a saving throw against one of your Destructive Blast effects with a final CP cost of 1 or more, you may still apply one minor breakage consequence from the selected Blast Type if the GM agrees the target is physically or spiritually vulnerable to it. Examples include cracking a shield, scattering footing, dimming a temporary barrier, exposing a weak point, or interrupting a minor environmental object. This talent cannot apply a rider condition, deny healing, remove Reactions, or force movement on a successful save unless another feature says so. ### Break the Formation Anchor Blast Type Refinement Requirement: Breaching Proof, Core Formation Realm When your Destructive Blast damages a formation anchor, ward node, barrier focus, ritual object, siege engine, or similar constructed defense, you may spend 1 CP to make a Cultivation Check against the effect’s save DC or a GM-set DC. On a success, the target defense is disrupted until the start of your next turn. The GM determines the visible effect, such as lowering a barrier panel, exposing a weak point, halving cover, interrupting a ritual pulse, or making the next check against the defense with Advantage. ### Calamity Chain Reaction Blast Shape Talent Requirement: Core Formation Realm When your Destructive Blast destroys an object or reduces a creature to 0 Hit Points, you may spend 1 CP to cause fragments of ruin to burst outward. Choose one creature or object within 10 feet of the destroyed target. That creature or object takes one Destruction Die of the selected Blast Type’s damage type. If the original blast used an area Blast Shape, choose only one secondary target total. ### Unmaking Pressure Blast Type Talent Requirement: Core Formation Realm Destruction Die: d6 Damage Type: Force Your ruin presses against active protections until their shape fails. A creature damaged by Unmaking Pressure makes a Constitution saving throw. On a failure, choose one visible temporary defensive benefit affecting it, such as a temporary AC bonus, temporary damage resistance, temporary barrier layer, temporary shield effect, or similar protection. That benefit is suppressed until the start of your next turn. Unmaking Pressure cannot suppress core Path features, permanent item properties, entire spheres, plot protections, or effects the GM judges too deep to break with ordinary Destruction. ### Destructive Domain: Field of Falling Forms Domain Talent Requirement: Core Formation Realm Action Type: Action Factory Combat Bucket: action Factory Routing: combat_action_row Range: Self Area: 20-foot-radius aura Duration: Concentration, up to 1 minute Cost: 4 CP You create a temporary field where structural integrity weakens. While the domain persists: your Destructive Blast range increases by 30 feet inside the domain; objects, barriers, structures, and constructs inside the domain lose Resistance to the damage type of your selected Destructive Blast unless that Resistance comes from an artifact, major formation, or higher-Realm effect; when you damage a creature inside the domain with Destructive Blast, the creature cannot benefit from half cover until the start of your next turn. The domain does not damage creatures by itself. ## Nascent Soul Talents ### Calamity Without Ornament Blast Type Refinement Requirement: Breaching Proof, Nascent Soul Realm When another Destruction talent allows you to add Destruction Dice to Unadorned Ruin, increase the maximum permitted number of additional dice by one. In addition, once per turn when Unadorned Ruin damages an object, structure, barrier, formation anchor, or constructed defense, you may ignore Resistance to Force damage from non-artifact sources. ### Heaven-Cracking Release Blast Discipline Talent Requirement: Nascent Soul Realm When you use Deepen the Calamity, you may spend 2 additional CP to declare a Heaven-Cracking Release. Choose one of the following benefits: increase the Destructive Blast range to 300 feet for this release; double the dimensions of one Blast Shape used for this release; deal two additional Destruction Dice to objects, structures, barriers, and formation anchors; force one creature that failed its saving throw against the release to lose Reactions and have its Speed halved until the start of your next turn. You can use Heaven-Cracking Release once per short rest. ### World-Ending Line Blast Shape Talent Requirement: Nascent Soul Realm When you release Destructive Blast as a line, ray, or Ruin-Crossing Step, you may spend 3 additional CP to make it a World-Ending Line. The line becomes 10 feet wide and may extend up to 300 feet. It damages objects and structures in its path as well as creatures. A creature reduced to 0 Hit Points by this line leaves behind a visible scar of ruin, such as glassed stone, split earth, blackened air, silent vibration, or a pressure trench. World-Ending Line cannot pass through a sealed artifact barrier, major formation, or plot-level defense unless the GM permits it. ### Calamity-Sovereign Incarnation Transformation Talent Requirement: Nascent Soul Realm Action Type: Bonus Action Factory Combat Bucket: bonus_action Factory Routing: combat_action_row Duration: 1 minute Cost: 5 CP You become a temporary incarnation of destructive authority. For the duration: once on each of your turns, when you use Destructive Blast, reduce the CP cost of one Destruction augment by 1, to a minimum of 0 CP; your Destructive Blast ignores half cover; objects and structures damaged by your Destructive Blast take one additional Destruction Die; when a creature within 30 feet damages you, you may use Returning Calamity without spending additional CP, but only once per round. When the duration ends, you cannot use Calamity-Sovereign Incarnation again until you finish a long rest. ### Destructive Domain: Court of the Last Impact Domain Talent Requirement: Destructive Domain: Field of Falling Forms, Nascent Soul Realm Action Type: Action Factory Combat Bucket: action Factory Routing: combat_action_row Range: Self Area: 60-foot-radius aura Duration: Concentration, up to 1 minute Cost: 6 CP You manifest a domain where all forms remember the possibility of ending. While the domain persists: your Destructive Blast range increases by 60 feet inside the domain; you may apply one Blast Type and one Blast Shape without counting Unadorned Ruin as your Blast Type when using Unadorned Ruin; objects, barriers, structures, and formation anchors damaged by your Destructive Blast take two additional Destruction Dice; the first time each round a creature fails a saving throw against your Destructive Blast inside the domain, choose one: it falls Prone, cannot take Reactions until the start of your next turn, or cannot regain Hit Points until the start of your next turn. The domain does not automatically destroy terrain or buildings. The GM adjudicates environmental consequences from actual damage dealt. ### The Mountain Admits It Can Break Siege Talent Requirement: Nascent Soul Realm When you spend at least 10 minutes using Destructive Blast against a stationary object, wall, gate, barrier, mountain face, ship hull, formation shell, or similar target, you may conduct a siege-breaking rite. At the end of the rite, make a Cultivation Check against a GM-set DC based on the target’s scale, material, formation support, Realm, and narrative importance. On a success, you create one meaningful breach, crack, route, collapse point, exposed anchor, or tactical opening. On a failure, the target is damaged and visibly weakened, but remains functional. You cannot attempt this rite against the same target again until you change tactics, gain new leverage, obtain better information, or spend significant additional resources. ## Secret Inheritance ### Secret Inheritance: The Calamity That Needs No Element This inheritance teaches that fire, cold, thunder, acid, lightning, and shadow are all costumes. The true lesson is simpler: every form contains the proof of its ending. When you gain this Secret Inheritance, you gain the following benefits: You learn Unadorned Ruin, Breaching Proof, and Calamity Without Ornament when you meet their Realm requirements without spending additional talent selections. Once per turn when you damage an object, barrier, structure, formation anchor, or construct with Unadorned Ruin, deal one additional Destruction Die. When you use Deepen the Calamity with Unadorned Ruin, you may choose Force, Bludgeoning, Piercing, Slashing, or Thunder damage for that release. This is still considered Unadorned Ruin and does not grant control over the chosen damage type’s associated sphere. Once per long rest, when your Destructive Blast would fail to damage a barrier because of Resistance or Immunity, you may force the barrier to make a durability saving throw or equivalent GM-set check. On a failure, your blast deals half damage instead of no damage. ## Destruction Drawbacks and Variant Scriptures A Destruction drawback is an optional sphere-specific limitation that grants a bonus Destruction talent or benefit while changing how your Destruction cultivation functions. Unless the GM says otherwise: choose at most one Destruction drawback when first learning Destruction or undergoing a major Destruction initiation; Destruction drawbacks are mutually exclusive; the drawback applies to all Destruction talents you use; if a drawback grants a talent whose prerequisites you do not yet meet, you gain that talent when you meet the prerequisites; if the drawback is retrained or removed, the bonus talent or benefit is lost. These are Tianxia-specific cultivation limits, not imported casting traditions. ### Unadorned Calamity Scripture You reject all specialized Blast Types. You can use only Unadorned Ruin as your Blast Type and cannot learn other pure Destruction Blast Type talents. You gain Breaching Proof as a bonus talent when you reach Foundation Realm. At Nascent Soul Realm, you gain Calamity Without Ornament as a bonus talent. ### Hand-of-Ruin Scripture Your destructive cultivation must pass through your body or weapon. Your Destructive Blast range becomes touch, melee reach, weapon reach, or thrown weapon range as appropriate to the technique. You gain Ruin-Tempered Armament or Returning Calamity as a bonus talent. This scripture is common among Body Refiners. ### Visible Calamity Scripture Your destruction is always obvious before it lands. Whenever you use Destructive Blast, visible pressure, cracking light, thunderous vibration, black rupture, or similar signs reveal the release. You cannot use Destructive Blast stealthily unless the GM decides the environment hides it. Creatures that can see or hear you have Advantage on checks to identify you as the source of the blast. You gain Controlled Ruin or Calamity Pearl as a bonus talent. ### Slow-Building Ruin Scripture Your calamity gathers before it breaks. When you use Destructive Blast with a final CP cost of 0, its range is halved and it cannot apply a Blast Type rider effect. When you use Deepen the Calamity, add one additional Destruction Die. ### Merciful Breaker Scripture You cultivate destruction without needless slaughter. When your Destructive Blast would reduce a living creature to 0 Hit Points, you may leave it stable and unconscious instead of killing it. However, you cannot use Withering Break, Calamity Chain Reaction against creatures, World-Ending Line, or any talent the GM classifies as deliberately lethal siege destruction. You gain Controlled Ruin as a bonus talent. ### Siege-Bound Scripture Your Destruction is strongest against things that refuse to move. Your Destructive Blast deals one fewer Destruction Die against creatures, minimum one die. Your Destructive Blast deals one additional Destruction Die against objects, structures, barriers, cover, formation anchors, siege engines, and similar constructed defenses. You gain Breaching Proof as a bonus talent when you meet its prerequisites. ## Path Synergies ### Body Refining Synergies Body Refining Destruction turns the body into the point of failure. Good Body Refining expressions include: breaking fists, hammer palms, shoulder impacts, stamping shockwaves, breath bursts, or weapon-body unity; Ruin-Tempered Armament on fists, claws, horns, weapons, or thrown stones; Returning Calamity as impact reflected through muscle and bone; Calamity Pearl as condensed physical pressure, sling stones, iron pellets, or explosive medicinal pellets; Hand-of-Ruin Scripture and Siege-Bound Scripture. Body Refiners should not casually fire invisible qi artillery at long range unless a forged technique, weapon, or scripture explains the physical delivery. ### Qi Cultivation Synergies Qi Cultivation Destruction is the classic blast path. Good Qi expressions include: condensed ruin rays; explosive pearls; pressure arrays; destructive curtains; flying calamity spheres; siege-breaking rites; formation anchor disruption. Qi Cultivators are the most natural users of Calamity Form, Wandering Calamity, Calamity Curtain, Field of Falling Forms, and Court of the Last Impact. ### Spirit Awakening Synergies Spirit Awakening Destruction breaks morale, intention, spiritual posture, and the soul’s grip on form. Good Spirit expressions include: blasts that feel like a command to fail; Staggering Break as spiritual rhythm collapse; Withering Break as the soul losing the will to repair; Unmaking Pressure against temporary spiritual protections; domains that make all forms remember impermanence. Spirit Awakening Destruction should not become Mind, Death, or Void. It breaks spiritual integrity through destructive pressure, not domination, grave law, or erasure. ## Sphere Synergies Cross-sphere Destruction should be handled as synergy, not as base Destruction talents. Examples: Fire + Destruction may produce a forged Consuming Flame technique. Thread + Destruction may produce a Silken Calamity Line technique. Light + Destruction may produce Lightbreaking Ray. Void + Destruction may produce Null Collapse, if the campaign allows Forbidden sphere combinations. Force + Destruction may produce crushing impact techniques. These are not included as core Destruction talents in this draft. They should be placed in the relevant sphere manuscript, a synergy appendix, or a forged technique package requiring both spheres. ## Cultivation Insights ### Breach-Reader Prerequisite: Destruction sphere When you spend 1 minute studying an object, wall, barrier, lock, formation anchor, gate, or structural defense, you may make an Investigation check or Cultivation Check. On a success against a GM-set DC, learn one of the following: the most vulnerable visible section; whether it has Resistance or Immunity to a damage type you can use; whether breaking it is likely to create a breach, collapse, alarm, or backlash; what tool, sphere, or tactic would most efficiently damage it. ### Calamity Control Prerequisite: Destruction sphere When you use a Blast Shape that affects an area, you may choose one creature you can see in the area. That creature has Advantage on its saving throw against the blast. At Core Formation Realm, you may choose two creatures instead. ### Impact Tempering Prerequisite: Destruction sphere, Body Refining Path When you use Destructive Blast through an unarmed strike, natural weapon, or melee weapon, you may use Constitution for the Cultivation Attack even if another ability would normally apply. Once per turn, after you damage an object or structure with such an attack, deal additional damage equal to your Proficiency Bonus. ### Ruin Pearl Handler Prerequisite: Destruction sphere, Calamity Pearl You have Advantage on checks made to conceal, place, throw, sling, recover, or safely disarm your own Sealed Pearls. When a creature attempts to identify one of your Sealed Pearls before it triggers, the DC increases by 2. ### Formation Breaker Prerequisite: Destruction sphere, Foundation Realm When you damage a barrier, ward, or formation anchor with Destructive Blast, you may immediately learn whether the target was meaningfully harmed, resisted the damage, ignored the damage, or retaliated through a backlash effect. ## Forged Technique Examples ### Palm That Teaches Stone to Split Suggested Realm: Foundation Sphere: Destruction Path Fit: Body Refining You deliver Destructive Blast through a melee strike. When you hit a creature or object with an unarmed strike or melee weapon attack, you may spend 1 CP to apply Unadorned Ruin to the same target. This counts as your Destructive Blast for the turn. If the target is an object, structure, or barrier, add one Destruction Die. ### Black Pearl Under the Tongue Suggested Realm: Foundation Sphere: Destruction Path Fit: Qi Cultivation or Body Refining You condense a Calamity Pearl into a tiny bead that can be hidden, spat, dropped, or sling-thrown. Your Sealed Pearls can be made small enough to conceal in the mouth, sleeve, ring, or hollow tooth. A creature must succeed on an Investigation check against your Cultivation Save DC to find one during a casual search. If you create the pearl inside your mouth, releasing it by spitting or biting counts as drawing it. ### Thunderless Court-Breaking Ray Suggested Realm: Core Formation Sphere: Destruction Path Fit: Spirit Awakening or Qi Cultivation You release Heaven-Piercing Ray without visible flame, lightning, or sound. The target feels only the verdict that its defense has failed. When you use Heaven-Piercing Ray with Unadorned Ruin, you may spend 1 additional CP to impose Disadvantage on the target’s next Concentration saving throw before the start of your next turn. ### One Stroke Opens the Gate Suggested Realm: Nascent Soul Sphere: Destruction Path Fit: Any You refine Destruction into a single ceremonial breach. When you use The Mountain Admits It Can Break against a gate, wall, vault, seal, barrier, or formation shell, you may spend a rare material focus, sect treasure, or prepared siege anchor worth an amount set by the GM. If the rite succeeds, the breach remains stable long enough for one group to pass before the defense begins to repair, collapse, or retaliate. ## Strategic Project Seeds ### Sect Breach Doctrine Train a squad to use Destruction without collapsing the entire battlefield. Successful projects may create safe breach procedures, shared target signals, or advantage on coordinated siege actions. ### Calamity Pearl Arsenal Develop standard Sealed Pearl forms: sling pearls, mine pearls, wall pearls, pressure pearls, and emergency self-break pearls. This project may create equipment tags rather than new talents. ### Formation Demolition Manual Study enemy formations and record which anchors fail under which Blast Types. This may become a tactical manual, jade tablet, or sect secret. ### Mercy of the Breaker Develop nonlethal Destruction methods for duels, law enforcement, sect trials, and capture missions. This may justify Merciful Breaker Scripture or special nonlethal forged techniques. ## Player Notes Destruction is intentionally clean in this draft. This sphere includes pure Destruction Blast Types and Blast Shapes. Cross-sphere blast types, such as Fire + Destruction or Thread + Destruction, are not part of the base sphere. They may appear later as sphere synergies, forged techniques, secret inheritances, or optional appendices.

#### Raise the Quarantine Veil
Action Type: Action
Factory Combat Bucket: action
Factory Routing: combat_action_row
Range: 60 feet
Area: 10-foot-radius sphere
Duration: Concentration, up to 1 minute
Cost: 2 CP
You raise a visible or invisible veil of quarantine marks, medicinal smoke, spirit fever, miasma threads, salt circles, bone needles, paper seals, humming insects, or coughing ghosts.
When you create the veil, choose one mode: Containment or Outbreak.
##### Containment Mode
Choose any number of creatures in the area.
Chosen creatures gain Advantage on saving throws against Disease while they remain inside the veil.
Whenever a chosen creature starts its turn inside the veil, it may remove one Contagion Token from itself.
Disease effects created by you cannot spread from inside the veil to creatures outside the veil unless you allow it.
##### Outbreak Mode
When an enemy enters the area for the first time on a turn or starts its turn there, it must make a Constitution saving throw.
Failed Save: The creature takes 1d6 Necrotic, Poison, or Psychic damage and becomes Sickened until the start of your next turn.
Successful Save: The creature takes half damage and is not Sickened.
The damage increases by Realm.
Mortal: 1d6Foundation: 2d6Core Formation: 3d6Nascent Soul: 4d6
A creature can take this damage only once per turn.
