resolved_automatic_base_abilities.effect:
#### Restful Dream - Rite Talent
When you learn the Dreams sphere, you learn Restful Dream automatically.
Action Type: Ritual Procedure
Canonical Action Type: Ritual Procedure
Factory Routing: procedure_ledger_not_combat_action
Timing Detail: Ritual
Time: 10 minutes
Range: Touch
Target: One willing creature
Duration: Until the end of the target’s next short rest
Cost: 1 CP
Guide the target into a restorative dream during its next short rest.
After completing that rest, the target:
gains Temporary HP equal to 2 x Proficiency Bonus;
may repeat one saving throw against Frightened;
may end one ordinary nightmare, minor sleep disturbance, or minor mental-stress effect;
gains Advantage on one check made to recover from ordinary exhaustion, stress, or mental fatigue. A creature may benefit from Restful Dream only once per long rest.

automatic_base_abilities.effect:
### Reeling Step
Action Type: Bonus Action
Factory Combat Bucket: bonus_action
Factory Routing: combat_action_row
Range: Self
Cost: None
You move up to 10 feet in a loose, swaying, indirect, or foolish-looking path.
This movement does not provoke Opportunity Attacks from one creature you can see.
Before or after this movement, choose one creature within 10 feet that can see you. That creature must make a Wisdom saving throw against your Drunken Style Save DC.
Failed Save: The creature becomes Off-Rhythm from you until the start of your next turn.
Successful Save: The creature is not Off-Rhythm, but it cannot make Opportunity Attacks against you during the movement granted by this Reeling Step.
You cannot use Reeling Step if your Speed is 0.

automatic_base_abilities.effect:
### Swaying Guard
Action Type: Reaction
Factory Combat Bucket: reaction
Factory Routing: combat_action_row
Trigger: A creature you can see makes an attack roll against you
Cost: None
You loosen your body, slip the line, lean late, or let the strike pass through the place you appeared to occupy.
Use Swaying Guard in one of the following ways:
If the attacker is Off-Rhythm from you, impose Disadvantage on the triggering attack roll.
If you moved at least 5 feet since the end of your last turn, add your Proficiency Bonus to your AC against the triggering attack.
You choose after seeing the attack roll but before knowing whether the attack hits or misses.
If the triggering attack misses, you may move 5 feet. This movement does not provoke Opportunity Attacks from the triggering attacker.
You may expend Martial Focus to use Swaying Guard without spending your Reaction. Once you do so, you cannot use Swaying Guard again until the start of your next turn.

spheres.full_exact_source_text: # Sphere of Drunken Style Qi Expression: Primary — Imbalance Qi; Supporting — Wine Qi, Flow Qi, Body-Rhythm Qi, Chance Qi. “The sober eye seeks a line. The crooked step refuses to become one.” Sphere Type: Martial Sphere Primary Paths: Body Refining and Spirit Awakening Secondary Path: Qi Cultivation Resource: Martial Focus; some Chaos-Step and Path-synergy techniques may spend CP when explicitly stated Common Effects: broken rhythm, swaying defense, false openings, unpredictable footwork, feints, slips, tumbles, improvised angles, miss redirection, reaction denial, shove and trip control, accidental-looking counters, chaos-step movement ### Drunken Style Dao Drunken Style is the cultivation of deliberate misreading. A straight sword declares its line. A shield presents its face. An Iron Fist practitioner builds the body into a complete weapon. A Drunken Style cultivator lets the opponent decide what the body is doing, then punishes them for believing themselves. This sphere is not the Dao of alcohol. A master who requires wine to sway has mistaken the cup for the scripture. True Drunken Style is cultivated contradiction: relaxed tendons around unbroken intent, a falling step that becomes a kick, a stumble that hides a pivot, a laugh that masks a breath count, and a helpless-looking opening that was always the trap. A novice learns to seem unready. An adept learns to make readiness look like collapse. A master learns to make the enemy’s timing betray itself. A sovereign does not dodge Heaven’s strike. Heaven simply discovers that it aimed at the wrong moment. The core loop is: Present a false pattern. Move, sway, miss narrowly, fall, laugh, or overextend in a controlled way. Mark the enemy Off-Rhythm. The target misreads your timing, weight, or angle. Exploit the misread. Apply one Drunken Style talent to strike, slip, shove, redirect, or counter. Keep moving. The style fails when it becomes a repeated trick. After fighting a Drunken Style cultivator for two rounds, an opponent should understand one truth: The mistake was not that the cultivator was off-balance. The mistake was assuming balance was required. ### Sphere Boundaries #### Drunken Style and Iron Fist Iron Fist cultivates the body as a complete weapon. It favors stances, forms, strong striking anatomy, kicks, counters, and iron-body discipline. Drunken Style cultivates misread timing. It can punch, kick, elbow, trip, shove, and counter, but its strength comes from false openings and broken rhythm rather than perfected form. Iron Fist says, “This body is a weapon.” Drunken Style says, “This body is where your prediction failed.” #### Drunken Style and Brute Brute moves mass, wins leverage, creates forced movement, and turns bodies into impact vectors. Drunken Style can shove, trip, pull, or redirect, but it does so by exploiting overcommitment and poor timing. It does not specialize in long pushes, object collisions, or raw strength dominance. A Brute hurls an enemy through a table. A Drunken Style practitioner steps wrong, lets the enemy lean too far, and the table becomes the enemy’s idea. #### Drunken Style and Scoundrel Scoundrel cultivates the unguarded assumption through theft, Dirty Trick, substitution, hidden tools, and stolen reliances. Drunken Style cultivates the misread motion. It may feint, seem foolish, or bait an attack, but it does not steal items, steal identity, or perform broad trickery. #### Drunken Style and Twin Moons Twin Moons is the paired rhythm of two weapons, alternating pressure, mirrored strikes, and dual-flow combat. Drunken Style may use two objects or improvised weapons, but it is not a dual-wielding sphere. Its rhythm is broken rather than paired. #### Drunken Style and Wild Qi Drunken Style may look chaotic. It is not uncontrolled. When this sphere uses the word “chaos,” it means trained unpredictability, not random magical backlash. True random instability belongs to Qiweaving’s Turbulence package, wild Qi, curses, flawed inheritances, or campaign-specific drawbacks. ## Core Drunken Style Rules ### Martial Focus Drunken Style uses Martial Focus. You may have only one Martial Focus at a time. Some Drunken Style talents expend Martial Focus for stronger timing, reaction, or movement benefits. Expending Martial Focus does not require an Action unless a talent says otherwise. Martial Focus represents breath, balance, rhythm, awareness, and readiness to turn a false step into a real answer. ### Drunken Style Save DC Some Drunken Style talents require a saving throw. Your Drunken Style Save DC equals: 8 + your Proficiency Bonus + your Drunken Style key ability modifier. Unless a Path feature or Path Synergy changes this, your Drunken Style key ability is Dexterity. Body Refining practitioners may use Constitution through the Body Refining Path Synergy. Spirit Awakening practitioners may use Wisdom through the Spirit Awakening Path Synergy. ### Drunken Style Attack Forms A Drunken Style technique can be delivered through any of the following, unless a talent narrows the options: Unarmed Strike using the Damage option; improvised melee weapon; melee weapon you are wielding; thrown improvised object, if the talent explicitly allows thrown use; body checks, trips, shoulder bumps, stumbling kicks, elbows, palms, knees, and similar bodily strikes. A Drunken Style technique does not require alcohol, intoxication, poison, drunkenness, or lowered awareness. A character who is actually Poisoned or Incapacitated does not gain special benefits from this sphere unless a talent says otherwise. ### Off-Rhythm Off-Rhythm is a short tactical state caused by misreading your timing. A creature that is Off-Rhythm from you has mistaken your balance, reach, direction, intent, or attack timing. Off-Rhythm is not a condition. It is not automatically mental, charm, fear, illusion, or poison. Unless a talent says otherwise: Off-Rhythm lasts until the start of your next turn. A creature can be Off-Rhythm from you only once at a time. Applying Off-Rhythm again refreshes the duration. Many Drunken Style talents either require a target to be Off-Rhythm or apply extra effects against an Off-Rhythm target. A creature that cannot perceive you or your motion cannot become Off-Rhythm from you unless a higher-Realm talent says otherwise. ### False Opening Some talents create a False Opening. A False Opening is a deliberate-looking mistake. It might be a loose guard, overextended hand, apparent stumble, half-fall, turned back, dropped shoulder, laugh, or delayed reaction. When a talent says you create a False Opening for a creature, that creature has Advantage on the next attack roll it makes against you before the start of your next turn. If it makes that attack, it becomes Off-Rhythm from you immediately after the attack resolves, whether it hits or misses. A False Opening is risky. It is how the sphere earns stronger timing without becoming free defense. ### One Style Talent per Trigger When a Drunken Style talent modifies a single attack, miss, movement, Swaying Guard, False Opening, or Off-Rhythm trigger, apply only one Drunken Style talent to that trigger unless another talent says otherwise. ### Legal Movement Movement granted by Drunken Style must be legal. It does not move through walls, sealed Barriers, Total Cover, occupied spaces, or hostile spaces unless the talent says so. Forced movement caused by Drunken Style does not provoke Opportunity Attacks unless a talent says otherwise. ## Base Sphere Abilities ### Drunken Style Training When you first gain the Drunken Style sphere, you gain proficiency in either Acrobatics or Performance. A target repeats the saving throw at the end of each of its turns, ending the effect on itself on a success. Successful Save: The target becomes Off-Rhythm from you until the end of your next turn and cannot take Reactions until the start of your next turn. This inheritance cannot automatically override artifacts, Secret Inheritances, divine mandates, Lair actions, Legendary actions, fate-sealed attacks, or campaign-scale calamities. Against such effects, it may grant an opposed Cultivation Check, create a partial escape, redirect a lesser portion of the effect, or become the seed of a Forged Technique or larger cultivation project. ## Drunken Style Drawbacks and Variant Scriptures A Drunken Style drawback is an optional sphere-specific limitation that grants a bonus Drunken Style talent or benefit while changing how the sphere functions. Unless the GM says otherwise: choose at most one Drunken Style drawback when first learning the sphere or undergoing major Drunken Style initiation; Drunken Style drawbacks are mutually exclusive unless stated otherwise; the drawback applies to all Drunken Style talents you use; if a drawback grants a talent whose prerequisites you do not yet meet, you gain that talent when you meet its prerequisites; if the drawback is retrained or removed, the bonus talent or benefit is lost. These are Tianxia-specific cultivation restrictions inspired by drawback design. They are not imported Pathfinder casting drawbacks. ### Empty-Cup Discipline You reject props, bottles, cups, chairs, sleeves, and loose objects. Your chaos must come from the body alone. You cannot use Drunken Style talents with improvised weapons or improvised objects. You gain one Rhythm or Sway talent as a bonus talent. ### Prop-Bound Fool Your Drunken Style requires a visible prop: cup, fan, gourd, sleeve weight, broom, stool, staff, rope, bell, sandal, or similar harmless-looking object. If you are not holding or wearing your prop, you cannot use Reeling Step, Broken-Rhythm Strike, or Drunken Style talents except Swaying Guard. If your prop is destroyed, stolen, sealed away, or made inaccessible, you may bind a new prop during a short rest. You gain Accidental Weapon or Sleeve, Bowl, and Boot as a bonus talent. ### Honest Stumble You cannot create False Openings. Your style is chaotic but not baiting. Whenever a Drunken Style talent would create a False Opening, you instead move 5 feet without provoking Opportunity Attacks from one creature you can see. You gain one Counter talent as a bonus talent. ### No Stillness Scripture Your cultivation cannot hold a stable stance. If you do not move at least 5 feet during your turn, you cannot benefit from Swaying Guard until the start of your next turn. You gain Loose-Cup Footwork as a bonus talent. If you already possess it, increase Reeling Step by an additional 5 feet. ### Ridiculous Display Your style is impossible to hide. You sway, laugh, mutter, clap, sing, slap your own forehead, drag a foot, or visibly exaggerate your looseness. Using Reeling Step, Broken-Rhythm Strike, or a Drunken Style talent automatically reveals your position to creatures that can perceive you normally within 60 feet. You gain Laughing Feint as a bonus talent. ## Path Synergies ### Body Refining - Loose Body, Unbroken Root If Drunken Style is learned through Body Refining, you may use Constitution as your Drunken Style key ability. Once per turn when you use Reeling Step or Swaying Guard, choose one: gain Temporary HP equal to your Proficiency Bonus; reduce falling damage you take before the start of your next turn by an amount equal to 5 x your Proficiency Bonus; gain Advantage on the next saving throw you make before the start of your next turn to avoid being Grappled, Prone, or moved against your will. ### Qi Cultivation - Crooked Qi Thread If Drunken Style is learned through Qi Cultivation, you may use Intelligence or Charisma as your Drunken Style key ability. Once per turn when you expend Martial Focus on a Drunken Style talent, you may spend 1 CP to choose one: increase a movement granted by that talent by 10 feet; cause one Off-Rhythm creature affected by the talent to shed dim visible Qi until the start of your next turn, preventing it from benefiting from being Invisible against you; apply Off-Rhythm to one additional creature within 10 feet of the original target if that creature can perceive the same motion; reduce the CP cost of a Drunken Style Forged Technique used before the end of the turn by 1, minimum 1. ### Spirit Awakening - Laughing Soul, Broken Prediction If Drunken Style is learned through Spirit Awakening, you may use Wisdom as your Drunken Style key ability. You may apply Off-Rhythm to spirits, ghosts, incorporeal creatures, possessing entities, and spiritual projections when they can perceive your motion, intent, soul-rhythm, or spiritual pressure. Once per round when a creature becomes Off-Rhythm from you, you may learn one of the following: whether it intends to attack you before the end of its next turn; whether it currently benefits from Advantage on attack rolls from a magical, spiritual, or cultivation effect; whether it has a reaction-based defensive feature available; whether it is being guided by a possession, command, or external spiritual influence. This does not reveal thoughts, secret techniques, full tactics, Path, Realm, or complete stat block. ## Cultivation Insights ### Fool’s Balance Prerequisite: Drunken Style sphere, CL 4+ When you roll Initiative, you may immediately use Reeling Step before the first turn begins. If this applies Off-Rhythm to a creature, you regain Martial Focus if you did not already have it. ### Fall Seven Ways Prerequisite: Drunken Style sphere, Falling-Leaf Drop or Bent-Reed Recovery, CL 6+ Standing from Prone costs you only 5 feet of movement. Once per short or long rest, when you would take falling damage, you may reduce that damage to 0 and move 10 feet to a legal space at the end of the fall. ### Prop Scripture Initiate Prerequisite: Drunken Style sphere, Accidental Weapon, CL 6+ Your improvised weapons used for Drunken Style talents count as magical for the purpose of overcoming resistance and immunity to nonmagical attacks. In addition, once per turn when an improvised weapon used for a Drunken Style talent breaks, is thrown away, or is dropped, you may draw or pick up another Tiny or Small mundane object within reach. ### Impossible Recovery Prerequisite: Drunken Style sphere, Swaying Guard, CL 8+ When Swaying Guard causes an attack to miss you, you may stand from Prone, escape nonmagical Difficult Terrain, or end one effect reducing your Speed by 10 feet or less. Once per short or long rest, you may use Swaying Guard even when your Speed is 0. ### Broken-Rhythm Adept Prerequisite: Drunken Style sphere, CL 8+ Once per turn when you hit a creature that is Off-Rhythm from you, you may apply one additional Mortal Realm Rhythm talent that does not require expending Martial Focus. You cannot apply the same talent twice to the same hit. ### Crooked-Court Custodian Prerequisite: Drunken Style sphere, Court of Broken Rhythm, Formations sphere, CL 12+ When designing a Formation, training hall, ambush route, safehouse, dueling stage, or sect obstacle course, you may use one Drunken Style technique as a seed concept. Examples include false floors, misleading footstep patterns, rotating doors, staggered pressure plates, misleading practice dummies, or a courtyard whose safe route changes with rhythm. This Insight does not create a project automatically. It provides a valid conceptual seed for Formation design, Forged Techniques, sect defenses, or campaign projects.

### Swaying Guard
Action Type: Reaction
Factory Combat Bucket: reaction
Factory Routing: combat_action_row
Trigger: A creature you can see makes an attack roll against you
Cost: None
You loosen your body, slip the line, lean late, or let the strike pass through the place you appeared to occupy.
Use Swaying Guard in one of the following ways:
If the attacker is Off-Rhythm from you, impose Disadvantage on the triggering attack roll.
If you moved at least 5 feet since the end of your last turn, add your Proficiency Bonus to your AC against the triggering attack.
You choose after seeing the attack roll but before knowing whether the attack hits or misses.
If the triggering attack misses, you may move 5 feet. This movement does not provoke Opportunity Attacks from the triggering attacker.
You may expend Martial Focus to use Swaying Guard without spending your Reaction. Once you do so, you cannot use Swaying Guard again until the start of your next turn.

spheres.full_exact_source_text: # Sphere of Dual Wielding Qi Expression: Primary — Paired-Weapon Qi; Supporting — Rhythm Qi, Metal Qi, Mirror Qi. “Two weapons are not two decisions. They are one decision arriving from two directions.” Sphere Type: Martial Sphere Primary Path: Body Refining Secondary Paths: Qi Cultivation and Spirit Awakening Resource: Martial Focus Common Effects: Paired weapons, alternating pressure, ambidextrous attacks, guarded offense, rapid weapon handling, tactical follow-up attacks, multi-target combinations, paired counters, cyclone cuts, and three-weapon styles ### Dual Wielding Dao Dual Wielding is the cultivation of paired intent. A novice believes that wielding two weapons means attacking more often. An adept understands that the first weapon asks a question and the second weapon punishes the answer. One edge occupies the guard. The other finds the opening. One hand threatens. The other protects. One weapon commits. The other remains free to answer what the enemy reveals. The Sphere of Dual Wielding rewards: striking with both weapons during the same turn; deciding which weapon leads and which weapon answers; converting an ordinary follow-up attack into control, defense, movement, or support; fighting through multiple angles without treating the two weapons as interchangeable stat sticks; spending Martial Focus when perfect synchronization matters more than conserving readiness. After fighting a Dual Wielding cultivator for two rounds, an opponent should learn one lesson: Blocking the first weapon is not the same thing as surviving the exchange. ### Sphere Boundaries Dual Wielding governs paired weapons, alternating attacks, split guard, ambidextrous handling, and the tactical meaning of a follow-up strike. Sword governs decision, edge, drawing, Sword Intent, Sword Qi, flying swords, Sword Heart, and Sword Soul. A Dual Wielding cultivator may wield swords, but this sphere does not create Sword Intent or Sword Qi. Fencing governs single-weapon precision, measure, tempo, and refined one-on-one technique. Dual Wielding is not merely Fencing with an extra blade. Barrage governs projectile cadence and repeated ranged pressure. Dual Wielding may support thrown weapons, but it does not become Barrage merely because two weapons can be thrown. Guardian governs protection, interception, and defensive responsibility. Balanced Defense improves personal guard but does not replace Guardian techniques. Wrestling governs grapples, pins, throws, and bodily control. Dual Wielding can create openings for a Shove or Grapple but does not replace Wrestling. Brute governs leverage, impact, forced movement, and overwhelming physical pressure. Equipment, Smithing, and weapon-specific disciplines govern weapon construction, unusual weapon qualities, and mastery of a particular weapon form. Athletics governs movement and body positioning. Dual Wielding combines naturally with Athletics but does not replace it. ### 5.5e Weapon Rules Dual Wielding is an addition to the ordinary 5.5e weapon rules. It does not replace those rules unless a feature below explicitly says otherwise. This sphere does not automatically grant: proficiency with any weapon; the Light property; a Weapon Mastery property; the Nick mastery; the Two-Weapon Fighting Fighting Style feat; the Dual Wielder feat; an additional Bonus Action; an additional Reaction; additional attacks beyond those stated by a feature; the ability to use a Shield while both hands are occupied by weapons. The ordinary 5.5e rules for the Attack action, Bonus Actions, Reactions, Opportunity Attacks, weapon properties, Weapon Mastery properties, equipping and unequipping weapons, Unarmed Strikes, Grapples, Shoves, and improvised weapons remain in force. #### The Light Property Under ordinary 5.5e rules, when you take the Attack action on your turn and attack with a Light weapon, you may make one extra attack later on the same turn as a Bonus Action. That extra attack must use a different Light weapon. Unless another rule says otherwise, do not add a positive ability modifier to the extra attack’s damage. #### Nick Mastery Nick allows the extra attack of the Light property to occur as part of the Attack action instead of as a Bonus Action. Nick does not create a second Light-property extra attack. #### Two-Weapon Fighting Fighting Style The Two-Weapon Fighting Fighting Style feat may add your ability modifier to the damage of an extra attack made as a result of using a Light weapon, subject to that feat’s ordinary rules. #### Dual Wielder Feat The Dual Wielder feat remains a separate base-game option. Nothing in this sphere grants it automatically. If a character has both the feat and this sphere, apply each rule only where its wording permits. ### Core Dual Wielding Rules #### Qualifying Pair A Qualifying Pair is a separate one-handed melee weapon wielded in each of your hands. Unless a talent explicitly says otherwise: an Unarmed Strike is not a weapon; a natural weapon is not a separate weapon held in a hand; a Shield is not a weapon; a weapon held in two hands cannot be part of a Qualifying Pair; a Ranged weapon is not part of a Qualifying Pair; you must still satisfy the ordinary requirements of any weapon property or base-game feature you use. #### Lead Weapon and Answering Weapon 5.5e does not require permanent “main-hand” and “off-hand” designations. For Dual Wielding features, when you attack with one weapon from your Qualifying Pair during your turn, you may call it your Lead Weapon until the end of that turn. The other weapon is your Answering Weapon. You may choose a different Lead Weapon each turn. A talent may refer to the Lead Weapon, the Answering Weapon, or both. #### Paired Strike A Paired Strike is the one extra attack you make with your Answering Weapon as a result of the Light property. A feature may explicitly state that another attack counts as a Paired Strike. An attack does not count as a Paired Strike merely because you happen to make it with your second weapon. #### Pair Talents A talent with the Pair tag changes the tactical meaning of one Paired Strike. Unless a talent explicitly says otherwise: apply no more than one Pair talent during your turn; choose the Pair talent when you make or replace the Paired Strike; a Pair talent does not create a Paired Strike if you are not otherwise entitled to one; a Pair talent does not remove the normal requirement to wield the appropriate weapons; replacing a Paired Strike means the weapon attack is not made. ### Martial Focus Dual Wielding uses Martial Focus. Use the global Tianxia Martial Focus rules. Until a broader martial-sphere rule replaces this wording: you may hold one Martial Focus at a time; some talents expend Martial Focus; expending Martial Focus is not an Action; you cannot expend Martial Focus if you do not currently hold it; if a feature says you regain Martial Focus, regain it only if it is currently absent. Martial Focus is a state of physical readiness, breath, posture, and intent. It is not CP. ### Base Sphere Abilities #### Twin-Weapon Training When you learn the Dual Wielding sphere, gain Balanced Defense and Dual Draw. ##### Balanced Defense While wielding a Qualifying Pair, gain a +1 bonus to AC. For stacking purposes, treat this bonus as a Shield bonus: you do not gain this bonus while wielding a Shield; if another feature says its AC benefit does not stack with a Shield, it does not stack with Balanced Defense; Balanced Defense does not count as wielding a Shield for any other purpose; Balanced Defense does not grant Shield training or satisfy a prerequisite that requires a Shield. An Unarmed Strike or natural weapon does not qualify unless a specific rule explicitly allows it. ##### Dual Draw Whenever you would equip or unequip one weapon as part of the Attack action or another rule, you may equip or unequip two one-handed weapons instead. Equipping includes drawing or picking up a weapon. Unequipping includes sheathing, stowing, or dropping a weapon. Dual Draw does not: allow you to interact with unrelated objects; reload a weapon; activate a magic item; exceed the number of hands you actually possess; change whether a weapon is one-handed or Two-Handed. #### Paired Rhythm Once per turn, when you hit one or more creatures with both weapons from your Qualifying Pair during the same turn, regain Martial Focus. The two hits may target the same creature or different creatures. #### Ambidexterity When you make the extra attack of the Light property as a Bonus Action, you may expend Martial Focus to make that attack as part of the Attack action instead. You may use Ambidexterity only once per turn. Ambidexterity: changes the action timing of the Light-property extra attack; does not create an additional attack; does not grant an additional Bonus Action; does not move an extra attack granted only by the Dual Wielder feat; does not stack with Nick to create another Light-property extra attack. If Nick already moves your Light-property extra attack into the Attack action, you do not need to expend Martial Focus to do so. ### Dual Wielding Talent Tags #### Pair Talents A Pair talent modifies or replaces one Paired Strike. #### Guard Talents A Guard talent improves defense, counters, and the protective value of carrying two weapons. #### Rhythm Talents A Rhythm talent modifies Martial Focus, alternating attacks, weapon handling, or the relationship between your Lead Weapon and Answering Weapon. #### Realm Evolutions A Realm Evolution represents paired-weapon technique beyond ordinary martial training. #### Unique Dual Wielding Talents A Unique Dual Wielding Talent is a distinct technique that does not fit another category. ### Mortal Realm Dual Wielding Talents #### Combo Maneuvers - Pair When you would make your Paired Strike, replace it with one Unarmed Strike used only for its Grapple or Shove option. Use the ordinary 5.5e rules for that Unarmed Strike. In particular: a Shove does not require a free hand; a Grapple requires a free hand; Combo Maneuvers does not allow a weapon to maintain a Grapple; you may use Dual Draw or another legal rule to unequip a weapon before attempting the Grapple. #### Dancing Display - Pair When your Paired Strike hits a creature, your movement does not provoke Opportunity Attacks from that creature for the rest of the current turn. #### Defensive Whirl - Pair Trigger: Your Paired Strike hits a creature. Cost: Expend Martial Focus. Until the end of that creature’s next turn, it has Disadvantage on attack rolls against you. #### Dizzying Combination - Pair Trigger: Your Paired Strike hits a creature. Use Limit: Once per turn. The target must make a Dexterity saving throw against your Cultivation Save DC. Failed Save: Each of the target’s Speeds is halved for 1 minute. Successful Save: No effect. At the end of each of its turns, the affected creature repeats the saving throw, ending the effect on itself on a success. #### Following Strike - Pair When you make your Paired Strike, make one additional attack with your Answering Weapon as part of the same Bonus Action, or as part of the same Attack action if your Paired Strike was moved into that action by Ambidexterity or Nick. Following Strike has the following restrictions: use it only once per turn; the original Paired Strike and the additional attack must target different creatures; at least one attack you made with your Lead Weapon as part of the Attack action must target a third creature; do not add a positive ability modifier to the additional attack’s damage unless another rule explicitly permits it; the additional attack is not itself a Paired Strike; you cannot apply another Pair talent to the additional attack. #### Perfect Set-Up - Pair When you would make your Paired Strike, replace it with the Help action’s Assist an Attack Roll option. Choose one enemy within 5 feet of you. The next attack roll made by one of your allies against that enemy has Advantage. This benefit expires at the start of your next turn. Perfect Set-Up does not allow you to use the Help action’s ability-check option through this talent. #### Asynchronous Swing - Rhythm While holding Martial Focus, when you make attacks with both weapons from your Qualifying Pair during your turn, choose: the normal weapon damage die of either weapon; and one damage type normally dealt by either weapon. Until the end of the current turn, both weapons use the chosen normal weapon damage die and chosen damage type for their weapon attacks. Asynchronous Swing does not copy: Weapon Mastery properties; weapon properties; Reach; magic-item bonuses; extra damage dice; curses; attunement benefits; effects that trigger only from one named weapon. #### Critical Follow-Up - Rhythm Your Paired Strike scores a Critical Hit on a roll of 19 or 20 on the d20. Critical Follow-Up applies only to the Paired Strike. It does not change the Critical Hit range of your other attacks. #### Dual Opportunity - Guard Trigger: You make an Opportunity Attack while wielding a Qualifying Pair. Use Limit: Once per round. Make one melee weapon attack with each weapon from your Qualifying Pair instead of making one attack. These attacks: use the same Reaction that triggered the Opportunity Attack; are Opportunity Attacks; do not count as Paired Strikes; cannot receive Pair talents unless another feature explicitly allows it. #### Focusing Defense - Guard When you take the Dodge action while wielding a Qualifying Pair, the AC bonus from Balanced Defense increases from +1 to +3 until the start of your next turn. If you cease wielding a Qualifying Pair, you lose this increased bonus until you again satisfy the requirement. #### Greater Blades - Rhythm For the limited purpose of determining whether you can make the Light property’s extra attack and use Dual Wielding sphere features, you may treat a one-handed melee weapon that lacks the Two-Handed property as though it had the Light property. Greater Blades does not: add the Light property to the weapon for any unrelated feature; add or change a Weapon Mastery property; allow a Two-Handed weapon to qualify; allow a weapon used in two hands to qualify; grant proficiency with the weapon. #### High-Low Combination - Rhythm Trigger: During your turn, you hit the same creature with your Lead Weapon and your Answering Weapon. Cost: Expend Martial Focus. Use Limit: Once per turn. Immediately after resolving the second hit, make one Unarmed Strike against that creature using only the Shove option. This requires no additional action. Use the ordinary 5.5e Shove rules, including the target’s size limit and choice of Strength or Dexterity saving throw. #### Mixed Defense - Guard You may use a mixed weapon pair consisting of: one one-handed melee weapon in one hand; and one one-handed Ranged weapon or one melee weapon with the Thrown property in the other hand. While wielding that mixed pair: you do not have Disadvantage on ranged attacks with the paired Ranged or Thrown weapon solely because a hostile creature is within 5 feet of you; the paired Ranged or Thrown weapon counts as a melee weapon for Balanced Defense and other Dual Wielding sphere requirements; this does not cause the weapon to gain the Light property. When you use a Ranged weapon from the mixed pair to make a melee attack: treat it as an improvised melee weapon; it deals 1d4 Bludgeoning damage on a hit; add your Proficiency Bonus to the attack roll only if you are proficient with improvised weapons; it has Reach for that melee attack and for Opportunity Attacks made with it. A melee weapon with the Thrown property continues to use its ordinary melee profile and gains Reach while you wield it as part of a mixed pair. #### Synchronous Accuracy - Pair Trigger: During your Attack action, an attack with your Lead Weapon misses and you are eligible to make a Paired Strike. Cost: Expend Martial Focus. Use Limit: Once per turn. When you make your Paired Strike, make two attacks with your Answering Weapon instead of one. Resolve both attacks as part of the same Bonus Action, or as part of the same Attack action if the Paired Strike was moved into that action by Ambidexterity or Nick. You may apply one Pair talent to each of these attacks, but the two Pair talents must be different. The second attack: does not add a positive ability modifier to damage unless another rule explicitly permits it; counts as a Paired Strike for the Pair talent attached to it; does not allow a third Pair talent during the same turn. #### Tandem Offensive - Rhythm While holding Martial Focus, when an attack made with your Lead Weapon as part of the Attack action hits a creature, compare the numeric magic-item bonuses to attack and damage rolls granted by your two wielded weapons. Until the start of your next turn, your Answering Weapon may use the higher of those two numeric bonuses. Tandem Offensive copies only a numeric magic-item bonus to attack and damage rolls. It does not copy: Weapon Mastery properties; weapon properties; damage dice; extra damage dice; activated abilities; charges; curses; attunement benefits; sentience; a named weapon’s unique effects. ### Foundation Realm Dual Wielding Talents - CL 5+ #### Cyclone Cut - Realm Evolution Prerequisite: Dual Wielding sphere, CL 5+ Action Type: Action Factory Combat Bucket: action Factory Routing: combat_action_row Requirement: Wielding a Qualifying Pair Cost: Expend Martial Focus Area: 15-foot Emanation originating from you Twirl your paired weapons with enough force and precision to create a damaging cyclone of air. Each other creature in the area makes a Dexterity saving throw against your Cultivation Save DC. Roll the normal weapon damage die of each weapon in your Qualifying Pair once and add the results together. Failed Save: The creature takes Bludgeoning damage equal to the total. Successful Save: The creature takes half as much damage. Cyclone Cut does not add: your ability modifier; magic-item bonuses to damage; extra damage dice; Weapon Mastery effects; Pair talents; on-hit riders from either weapon. #### Three-Sword Style - Unique Dual Wielding Talent Prerequisite: Dual Wielding sphere, CL 5+ You learn to wield a third weapon. If you possess an additional hand, tail, prehensile limb, telekinetic grip, or another explicitly approved method, you may use it to wield the third weapon. If you possess no such method, you may wield the third weapon in your teeth. The third weapon must be a one-handed melee weapon that lacks the Two-Handed property. While holding a weapon in your teeth: you cannot provide Verbal spell components; you cannot speak clearly; you cannot make an ability check that requires clear speech or singing; you may still communicate in a garbled fashion when the GM determines that communication is possible. ##### Third Strike Trigger: You make your Paired Strike while wielding a third weapon. Cost: Expend your Reaction. Use Limit: Once per turn. Make one additional melee weapon attack with the third weapon as part of the same Bonus Action, or as part of the same Attack action if the Paired Strike was moved into that action by Ambidexterity or Nick. The Third Strike: does not add a positive ability modifier to damage unless another rule explicitly permits it; is not a Paired Strike; cannot receive a Pair talent; cannot be used if your Reaction is unavailable. ### Path Synergies #### Body Refining - Split-Meridian Coordination Use Constitution for Dual Wielding Cultivation Save DCs. Once per turn when Paired Rhythm restores Martial Focus, gain a +1 bonus to AC until the start of your next turn. This bonus ends early if you cease wielding a Qualifying Pair. #### Qi Cultivation - Alternating Qi Circuit Use Intelligence or Charisma for Dual Wielding Cultivation Save DCs, chosen according to your Qi Cultivation key ability. Once per turn when you expend Martial Focus on a Dual Wielding talent, choose one weapon from your Qualifying Pair. One weapon attack made with that weapon before the end of the current turn may deal Force damage instead of its normal damage type. This does not change the weapon’s properties, Weapon Mastery property, or other effects. #### Spirit Awakening - Two Hands, One Intent Use Wisdom for Dual Wielding Cultivation Save DCs. Once per turn, when an attack with one weapon from your Qualifying Pair misses a creature and an attack with the other weapon hits that same creature before the end of the turn, gain Advantage on your next attack roll against that creature before the end of your next turn. This represents sensing the response exposed by the first exchange. It does not read thoughts or reveal hidden information. ### Cultivation Insights #### Empty-Hand Twin Form Prerequisite: Dual Wielding sphere, an approved unarmed or natural-weapon discipline, CL 4+ Choose one Unarmed Strike, natural weapon, or explicitly approved body weapon. For Dual Wielding sphere requirements only, the chosen attack form may count as one one-handed melee weapon that lacks the Two-Handed property. Empty-Hand Twin Form does not: cause your body to hold an object; grant the Light property for unrelated features; create a free hand; allow the same hand to wield a weapon and count as a separate body weapon simultaneously; grant a natural weapon if you do not already possess one; alter the attack’s ordinary damage or damage type. If you know Greater Blades, the chosen attack form may qualify for the Light-property extra attack only for the limited purposes stated by Greater Blades. #### Paired-Weapon Instructor Prerequisite: Dual Wielding sphere, CL 6+ When training allies during downtime, you may use one Dual Wielding talent you know as the seed concept for a paired-weapon drill, school exercise, or Formation-assisted training project. This does not automatically grant the talent to another creature or create a permanent project. The final result still requires appropriate time, instruction, materials, and GM approval. #### Two-Moons Focus Prerequisite: Dual Wielding sphere, CL 8+ Once per Short Rest, when you would expend Martial Focus on a Dual Wielding talent, retain Martial Focus instead.

#### Set Foundation
Action Type: Action
Factory Combat Bucket: action
Factory Routing: combat_action_row
Range: 60 feet, subject to Path restrictions
Area: Up to two 5-foot Foundation Spaces
Duration: 1 minute
Cost: NoneConcentration: Not required
Tags: Foundation
You claim ground, body, or surface as an Earth Foundation.
Choose spaces on a legal solid or earthen surface you can see within range. The spaces may be connected or separate.
If your Earth is limited by Body Refining contact rules, the spaces must be legal for those rules.
The number of spaces you create increases as your cultivation deepens.
| Cultivation Level | Foundation Spaces Created |
| --- | --- |
| CL 1-4 | 2 spaces |
| CL 5-10 | 3 spaces |
| CL 11-16 | 4 spaces |
| CL 17-20 | 5 spaces |
When a creature you did not designate as safe willingly moves at least 10 feet across, out of, or through your Foundation Spaces during one turn, you may give that creature one Burden Mark. This can happen only once per creature per turn.

#### Weight-Seeking Clod
Action Type: Action
Factory Combat Bucket: action
Factory Routing: combat_action_row
Range: 60 feet, subject to Path restrictions
Target: One creature or object
Cost: None
Tags: Attack, Burden
You strike with compacted earth, a thrown clod, stone-grit, a stomp carried through the ground, or a body-originating weight pulse.
Make a ranged Earth Cultivation Attack. If your Earth is limited by Body Refining contact rules, this attack must originate from your body, a held object, or a touched surface, and the GM may require the target to be on a surface connected to you.
On a hit, the target takes Bludgeoning damage and gains one Burden Mark.
| Cultivation Level | Damage |
| --- | --- |
| CL 1-4 | 1d8 |
| CL 5-10 | 2d8 |
| CL 11-16 | 3d8 |
| CL 17-20 | 4d8 |
The damage is not the sphere’s identity. It is the visible sign of weight finding a place to land.

automatic_base_abilities.effect:
#### Spending a Burden Mark
Once per round, when a marked creature or object you can perceive performs a triggering act, you may spend its Burden Mark without using an Action. Choose one Earth Response appropriate to the trigger.
##### Anchor Step
Trigger: The marked target begins movement while touching a surface, including walking, climbing, burrowing, jumping, forced movement, or standing from Prone.
Reduce one of the target’s Speeds by 10 feet until the end of the current turn. At CL 11, this reduction becomes 20 feet.
This cannot reduce a Speed below 0.
If the movement is forced movement, reduce the forced movement distance by the same amount.
##### Drag Down
Trigger: The marked target willingly moves at least 5 feet, jumps, climbs, flies upward while within 10 feet of a solid surface, or attempts to stand from Prone.
The target makes a Strength saving throw.
Failed Save: The target falls Prone, or if already Prone, its Speed becomes 0 until the end of the current turn.
Successful Save: Reduce the target’s Speed by 5 feet until the end of the current turn.
A creature flying high in open air is affected only if it is within 10 feet of a solid surface, unless a talent says otherwise.
##### Bear the Blow
Trigger: The marked target deals damage to you, an ally, an object, or a Foundation Space while the damaged target is touching one of your Foundation Spaces or is within 5 feet of you.
Reduce the damage by:
1d8 + your Earth key ability modifier
At CL 5, this becomes 2d8 + modifier; at CL 11, 3d8 + modifier; at CL 17, 4d8 + modifier.
##### Shift the Load
Trigger: The marked target hits a creature with an attack roll while both are touching the ground or a legal Earth surface.
Before damage is rolled, choose one willing creature within 10 feet of the damaged creature, including yourself.
The chosen creature gains Temporary HP equal to your Proficiency Bonus + your Earth key ability modifier, minimum 1.
If the chosen creature is touching one of your Foundation Spaces, double the Temporary HP.
##### Raise the Ridge
Trigger: The marked target makes a ranged attack roll, casts a spell, uses a sphere talent, or creates a harmful line or area effect while touching a surface within 60 feet of you.
Raise a low ridge, berm, stone lip, packed-earth mound, or similar obstruction in one unoccupied 5-foot space touching the marked target or the triggering line of effect.
The ridge lasts until the start of your next turn. It grants Half Cover against one attack or effect that crosses through its space, then crumbles.
Raise the Ridge does not block movement unless a talent says otherwise.
##### Settle the Impact
Trigger: The marked target would push, pull, knock Prone, shove, move, teleport, or otherwise displace another creature or object.
Reduce the displacement by 10 feet. At CL 11, reduce it by 20 feet.
If this reduces the displacement to 0, the displaced creature or object may immediately move 5 feet without provoking Opportunity Attacks from the marked target.
Settle the Impact does not prevent planar travel or teleportation unless the distance is reduced to 0 and the effect is not a Domain, Secret Inheritance, artifact, or story-scale effect.

spheres.full_exact_source_text: # Sphere of Earth Qi Expression: Primary — Earth Qi; Supporting — Stone Qi, Soil Qi, Weight Qi, Stability Qi. “A sword may cut the air. A flame may rise. A river may flee. Earth waits beneath all three and asks what they are prepared to carry.” Common Name: Earth Sphere Sphere Type: Elemental Terrain / Foundation Sphere Rules Baseline: 2024 fifth-edition rules (5.5e) Primary Paths: Body Refining and Qi Cultivation Secondary Path: Spirit Awakening Resource: CP unless a feature says otherwiseCore Mechanic: Foundations and Burden MarksCommon Expressions: rooted stances, claimed ground, load-bearing earthworks, tremor-reading, grounding lines, sinking steps, raised ridges, earthen seals, patient endurance, battlefield reshaping through weight and foundation ### Earth Dao Earth is the cultivation of foundation and burden. A novice thinks Earth is dirt, stone, mud, and walls. An adept understands that Earth is the answer to a deeper question: What carries the weight? Every step requires a surface. Every tower requires a foundation. Every oath stands on something. Every army depends on roads, food, graves, banners, and ground. Every body survives because its bones and stance agree to bear the world a little longer. The Sphere of Earth does not merely throw rocks. It decides where force is allowed to rest, what must bear the weight of action, and when a creature has placed more burden on the ground than the ground is willing to accept. Earth cultivators cultivate patience, load, settlement, traction, weight, ground memory, and the line between stability and burial. The Sphere of Earth governs: claimed ground; load-bearing stance; weight and burden; roads, terraces, ridges, berms, and foundations; tremor-reading through contact; anchoring bodies and objects; resisting forced movement; making movement costly; turning impact into settling force; sinking, bracing, raising, and grounding; making the battlefield answer for what it is carrying. #### Sphere Sentence Earth cultivators claim a foundation, mark the burden placed upon it, and decide whether that burden is borne, anchored, shifted, or buried. ### Sphere Boundaries Earth overlaps with many spheres, but it does not replace them. | Sphere | Difference from Earth | | --- | --- | | Stone | Stone is the specific hardness, mineral body, and worked mass of rock. Earth is foundation, load, grounding, soil, terrain, and burden. | | Metal | Metal refines ore into edge, vessel, tool, and law of hardness. Earth bears the ore before it is taken and carries the weight of what is built. | | Wood | Wood grows, branches, heals, drinks, and spreads through life. Earth supports, buries, roots, and holds the place where growth happens. | | Water | Water flows, adapts, nourishes, and erodes. Earth receives flow, shapes banks, carries roads, and determines where things settle. | | Ice | Ice arrests motion into crystalline lines. Earth imposes load-bearing truth: what stands, sinks, anchors, or collapses under weight. | | Sand | Sand slips, abrades, obscures, buries, and shifts grain by grain. Earth is broader foundation and burden; Sand is a specialized unstable earth expression if treated as its own sphere. | | Force | Force answers impact directly. Earth decides where that force is grounded and what must bear it. | | Protection | Protection wards against harm. Earth stabilizes footing, raises terrain, bears impact, and anchors bodies through foundation. | | Creation | Creation makes objects broadly. Earth only shapes matter when doing so serves foundation, burden, ground, roads, walls, ridges, or seals. | | Formations | Formations prepare strategic arrays. Earth can provide ground, anchors, berms, and foundations for those arrays, but does not replace array design. | | Yin | Yin receives overextension and makes consequence incomplete. Earth receives burden and decides whether it is borne or buried. | | Yang | Yang kindles completion and surplus expression. Earth slows expression until it must rest on a foundation. | Earth may use bludgeoning damage, difficult terrain, prone, restraint, cover, tremors, walls, and burial as expressions. Those mechanics are not the sphere identity. The sphere identity is foundation and burden. ### Rules Retained from Fifth Edition This sphere uses the 2024 fifth-edition rules baseline. Earth talents supplement the normal rules for: movement; difficult terrain; Prone; Grappled and Restrained; Cover; objects and object damage; forced movement; falling; jumping; climbing; burrowing; tremorsense; Concentration; the Hide action; Opportunity Attacks; area effects; terrain and environmental hazards. An Earth feature replaces a normal rule only when it explicitly says so. #### Earth Does Not Automatically Do These Things Unless an Earth feature says otherwise, Earth does not automatically: create cover; create difficult terrain; knock creatures Prone; reduce Speed; restrain or grapple a creature; block line of sight; block line of effect; create permanent stone, soil, ore, gems, tunnels, walls, buildings, roads, or bridges; make a creature Hidden or Invisible; prevent teleportation; prevent flight; counter a spell, sphere talent, Domain, or technique; create breathable air underground; control plants; control metal; produce food or wealth; reshape a structure safely without an appropriate feature and GM approval. #### Earth Matter Earth features may create supernatural earth, packed soil, clay, dust, stone-grit, gravel, loam, mud-brick, terrace lines, rootlike mineral filaments, or pressure-darkened ground. Unless a feature says otherwise, such matter is temporary cultivation matter. It crumbles, settles, melts into dust, or becomes ordinary disturbed ground when the feature ends. It cannot be sold as valuable stone, ore, gems, or building material. #### Solid Ground and Contact Many Earth features require a solid or earthen surface. This may include natural ground, packed road, stone floor, clay, sand, soil, worked masonry, a cliff face, a wall, a ceiling, a large boulder, or similar terrain. A ship deck, wooden bridge, metal floor, ice shelf, giant beast’s shell, or similar surface is not automatically an Earth surface unless a feature, Path synergy, or GM ruling makes it one. However, a Body Refining Earth cultivator may use their own body, armor, and held objects as the foundation for body-originating Earth features. #### Body Refining and External Earth A Body Refining cultivator does not normally project qi outside the body. If your primary Path is Body Refining and you lack an explicit external projection feature, an Earth feature with range beyond touch must originate from one of these legal foundations: your own body; clothing, armor, shield, or a weapon you are wearing or holding; a creature or object you touch; your own space; a surface you are standing on or touching; Foundation Spaces contiguous with your own space or a surface you are touching. You may still use the Earth sphere, but your Earth begins as stance, weight, contact, impact, and ground-sharing rather than distant terrain command. A feature tagged Projected bypasses this limit only if you have Qi Cultivation, Spirit Awakening, a Cultivation Insight, a forged technique, a Realm evolution, or GM permission that explicitly allows projected Earth. ### Core Earth Rules The Earth sphere uses Foundations and Burden Marks. A Foundation is ground, body, or surface claimed by Earth cultivation. A Burden Mark is the record of weight, motion, impact, or obligation placed upon that foundation. Neither Foundation nor Burden Mark is a base-game condition. Immunity to a condition does not grant immunity to Burden Marks unless a feature says so. #### Earth Key Ability Use the key ability of the Path through which you cultivate Earth unless a feature says otherwise. Body Refining Earth usually uses Constitution. Qi Cultivation Earth usually uses Intelligence or Charisma. Spirit Awakening Earth usually uses Wisdom. Your Earth Save DC equals: 8 + your Proficiency Bonus + your Earth key ability modifier Your Earth Cultivation Attack Modifier equals: your Proficiency Bonus + your Earth key ability modifier #### Foundation Limit You can maintain a number of 5-foot Foundation Spaces equal to your Proficiency Bonus + your Earth key ability modifier, minimum 3. If you create a Foundation Space beyond this limit, choose one existing Foundation Space you created to end. A Foundation Space lasts for 1 minute, until you dismiss it, until it is destroyed, until you are no longer on the same plane of existence as it, or until the feature creating it says it ends. You may dismiss any number of your Foundation Spaces at any time, no Action required. #### Foundation Spaces Unless a feature changes them, Foundation Spaces have the following rules. They are visible or clearly felt supernatural ground pressure. They do not create cover. They do not block line of sight. They do not block line of effect. They do not prevent movement. They do not make creatures fall Prone by themselves. They do not damage creatures by themselves. They count as magical terrain created by your Earth sphere. You and willing creatures you choose when you create the spaces can move across those spaces without suffering difficult terrain from your Earth features. #### Breaking Foundation Spaces A creature can attack a Foundation Space. Unless a feature gives a different statistic, one 5-foot Foundation Space has AC 10 + your Proficiency Bonus and Hit Points equal to 5 + your Cultivation Level. It is immune to Poison and Psychic damage. When a Foundation Space is destroyed, only that 5-foot space ends. At the GM’s discretion, a Foundation Space made on unstable terrain may collapse if the underlying terrain is destroyed. #### Burden Mark Limit You can maintain a number of Burden Marks equal to your Proficiency Bonus. A creature or object can have only one Burden Mark from you at a time unless a feature says otherwise. It simply discovered what it had always been standing on.” Classification: Secret Earth Inheritance Prerequisite: CL 17+, Court of Bearing Ground, hidden earth-root scripture Action Type: Action Factory Combat Bucket: action Factory Routing: combat_action_row Area: 1-mile-radius region centered on a point on the ground you can perceive or have ritually marked Duration: 1 hour Cost: 15 CP Use Limit: Once per month or once per major story arc, as determined by the GM You claim the burden of a battlefield, valley, mountain pass, city gate, sect courtyard, mine, tomb complex, or other grounded region. Choose one principle when you activate this inheritance. #### Nothing Unmoored May Rule Creatures hostile to you cannot teleport into, teleport out of, burrow through, phase through, or use planar movement through the area unless they succeed on a Charisma saving throw against your Earth Save DC. On a success, the movement works, but the creature gains one Burden Mark and takes 6d10 Force damage as the world makes it pay the weight of departure. This does not block deity-scale movement, artifact-scale movement, or GM-declared story-scale passage. #### The Ground Bears the Innocent Choose any number of creatures you can name, see, or ritually identify as protected. While a protected creature touches ground in the area: it has Advantage on death saving throws; it cannot be moved against its will by ordinary forced movement; the first time each minute it would take damage, reduce that damage by 10d10; if it would be buried, trapped, crushed, or fall into a fissure caused by terrain, move it to the nearest safe ground you choose within 60 feet. #### The Burden Returns to the Violent The first time each round that a hostile creature in the area deals damage, forces movement, destroys terrain, collapses a structure, or kills a creature, it gains one Burden Mark. When you spend that mark, add 5d10 Bludgeoning damage or 5d10 Force damage to the Earth Response. If the creature is already marked, it instead makes a Strength saving throw. Failed Save: It falls Prone, its Speed becomes 0 until the end of its next turn, and it cannot teleport until the end of its next turn. Successful Save: It cannot take Reactions until the start of its next turn. The World Rests on My Palm does not create permanent political ownership, legal title, or divine authority over the region. It makes the region briefly answer your Dao of foundation and burden. ## Earth Drawbacks and Variant Scriptures Earth variants are optional cultivation scriptures that change how the sphere manifests. A variant grants a benefit only if it also imposes a real limitation. These are Tianxia-specific cultivation limits inspired by drawback design, not imported casting-tradition rules. Unless the GM says otherwise: choose at most one Earth variant when first learning Earth or undergoing a major Earth initiation; Earth variants are mutually exclusive; the variant applies to all Earth talents you use; if a variant grants a talent whose prerequisites are not yet met, you gain that talent when you meet them; if the variant is retrained or removed, lose the bonus talent or benefit. ### Mountain-Root Scripture You cultivate Earth as immovable root rather than distant terrain command. You gain Deep Root Stance as a bonus talent. If you already have it, gain Load-Bearing Back instead. Drawback: No Earth Beyond the Foot. You cannot create Foundation Spaces, walls, roads, seals, or other Earth effects except from your body, your worn or held objects, a creature or object you touch, your own space, or a surface contiguous with your own space. You cannot learn Projected Earth talents unless you first gain External Foundation Breakthrough or a GM-approved equivalent. ### Road-Builder Scripture You cultivate Earth as road, terrace, and passage. You gain Patient Roadmaker as a bonus talent. At CL 5, you also reduce the CP cost of Terraced Ascent by 1, minimum 0, once per short rest. Drawback: Earth Must Be Passable. Your Earth resists becoming a prison. When you create a wall, seal, ridge, or obstruction, you must leave at least one visible route around, over, through, or under it unless the feature is used to protect creatures from immediate harm. Hostile creatures gain Advantage on saving throws against your Earth features that would reduce their Speed to 0 or prevent teleportation if your effect offers no reasonable route of passage. ### Grave-Soil Scripture You cultivate Earth as burial, memory, and solemn return. You gain Buried Trace as a bonus talent. When using Buried Trace to preserve signs of death, burial, battle, or passage of the dead, its duration becomes 7 days. Drawback: The Dead Weigh First. The first time each combat you would place a Burden Mark on a living creature that has not damaged another creature, desecrated a body, disturbed a grave, broken a seal, or willingly caused a hostile supernatural effect since the start of its last turn, you must either deal no damage with the triggering Earth feature or forgo the Burden Mark. This does not restrict Earth features used against undead, constructs, objects, barriers, poisons, diseases, curses, corruption, hostile Formations, or environmental hazards. ### Quaking Scripture You cultivate Earth as tremor, warning, and collapse. You gain Tremor-Listening Palm as a bonus talent. When a creature you detect with Tremor-Listening Palm moves at least 10 feet before the start of your next turn, you may give it one Burden Mark once per round. Drawback: Stillness Deceives the Tremor. Your Earth senses and Burden features are weaker against creatures that do not rely on weight. Creatures that are flying more than 10 feet above a surface, incorporeal, hovering without contact, swimming without touching a surface, or magically weightless have Advantage on saving throws against your Earth talents unless you have a feature that specifically grounds them. ### Tiller’s Mercy Scripture You cultivate Earth as support for the living rather than punishment. You gain Earth Carries the Fallen when you meet its prerequisites. Until then, gain Load-Bearing Back as a bonus talent. Drawback: The Field Is Not a Grave. You cannot use Earth talents to deal damage to a living creature unless that creature has damaged another creature, forced another creature to make a saving throw, spent CP, used a spell slot, used a supernatural feature, or willingly caused a hostile supernatural effect since the start of its last turn. This restriction does not prevent you from: creating Foundations; placing non-damaging Burden Marks; reducing damage; preventing forced movement; creating roads, shelters, ridges, or seals; protecting allies; using Earth against undead, constructs, objects, barriers, poisons, diseases, curses, corruption, hostile Formations, hazards, and nonliving magical effects. ## Path Synergies ### Body Refining - Mountain Body Method Body Refining Earth begins with the body as foundation. When Earth is cultivated through Body Refining: use Constitution as your Earth key ability; your body, worn armor, held weapons, and shield count as legal Earth foundations for Body talents; while standing on a solid surface, your own space may count as a Foundation Space for Earth features that target yourself; you cannot use Projected talents unless you gain explicit projection permission. Once per short rest, when you use Deep Root Stance, regain Stamina equal to your Proficiency Bonus if you are below half your maximum Stamina. ### Qi Cultivation - Geomantic Circulation Qi Cultivation Earth commands terrain through meridian lines in the world. When Earth is cultivated through Qi Cultivation: use Intelligence or Charisma as your Earth key ability; use the listed range of Earth features unless a feature says otherwise; treat Projected Earth talents as legal for you; when you create at least three Foundation Spaces with one Action, reduce the CP cost of the next Earth talent you use before the end of your next turn by 1, minimum 0. At CL 10+, once per short rest, when you create a Domain or Settlement talent, create two additional 5-foot Foundation Spaces connected to it. ### Spirit Awakening - Burden-Listening Soul Spirit Awakening Earth reads the weight beneath intention. When Earth is cultivated through Spirit Awakening: use Wisdom as your Earth key ability; while touching a surface, you may use Tremor-Listening Palm to sense emotional pressure carried through movement, posture, and hesitation; when a creature with your Burden Mark willingly breaks a promise, abandons a protected creature, violates a declared duty, or acts against a role it publicly claimed within the scene, you may use one Earth Response against it even if the physical trigger is imperfect, subject to GM approval. This does not read private thoughts. It reads burden expressed through action. Once per round when you spend a Burden Mark, gain Temporary HP equal to your Proficiency Bonus if the marked creature’s action endangered an ally or dependent creature. ## Cultivation Insights ### External Foundation Breakthrough Prerequisite: Body Refining, Earth sphere, CL 5+ Your Body Refining Earth has begun to extend beyond immediate contact. You may use non-Domain Earth features with a listed range of 30 feet or less if the effect begins from your body, a stomp, a strike, a held object, or a surface connected to your footing. You still cannot create Earth effects in open air or on surfaces you cannot see unless a feature says otherwise. At CL 10+, increase this range to 60 feet for Foundation talents only. ### Burden-Mark Adept Prerequisite: Earth sphere, CL 4+ Increase your Burden Mark limit by 1. Once per round when you spend a Burden Mark, move 5 feet without provoking Opportunity Attacks from the marked creature, provided both of you are touching the same surface. ### Road-and-Wall Adept Prerequisite: Earth sphere, one Settlement talent, CL 6+ When you create a wall, road, ramp, shelter, ridge, or seal with an Earth talent, choose one: increase its Hit Points by your Cultivation Level; increase its duration by one step, from 1 minute to 10 minutes, 10 minutes to 1 hour, or 1 hour to 24 hours; create one additional 5-foot section or space. Use this Insight once per short rest. ### Tremor-Reader Adept Prerequisite: Earth sphere, Tremor-Listening Palm, CL 8+ When using Tremor-Listening Palm, you can distinguish between Small, Medium, Large, and Huge or larger creatures by weight and rhythm. You also gain Advantage on Wisdom (Survival) and Intelligence (Investigation) checks made to read tracks, collapsed ground, battle movement, digging, marching, falling, or dragging. ### Burden-Bearing Companion Prerequisite: Earth sphere, Companion feature or bonded companion, CL 8+ Your bonded companion can share your Foundation. While your companion is touching one of your Foundation Spaces: it gains Advantage on checks and saving throws against being moved or knocked Prone; once per round when it hits a creature, it may place one Burden Mark for you if you can perceive the target; when you use Bear the Blow on your companion, add your Proficiency Bonus to the damage reduction. ### Foundation Array Custodian Prerequisite: Earth sphere, Formations sphere, CL 8+ When designing a Formation, road, gate, wall, tomb, courtyard, sect foundation, battlefield camp, or long-term terrain project, use one Earth Foundation, Burden, or Settlement principle as a seed concept. This does not create the project automatically. The project still requires: appropriate terrain; preparation time; material costs; labor or Formation anchors; maintenance; a clear vulnerability or counterplay condition. ### Repeated Practitioner Behavior Every tier still asks the player to: set or stand on foundation; mark burden through movement, impact, or reliance; answer with stabilization, drag, cover, grounding, terrain, or settlement; scale from stance to battlefield to region. ### What Only Earth Should Be Known For Earth is the sphere that makes action accountable to what carries it. It is not simply stone walls, difficult terrain, or bludgeoning damage. ### Player Recognition Test A player should recognize an Earth cultivator because: the ground becomes tactically meaningful; forced movement fails against rooted stance; enemies become marked by the burden of their movement; roads, walls, ridges, shelters, and seals appear only as expressions of foundation; the Body Refiner stands like a mountain rather than throwing distant terrain for free.

| CL 5-10 | 2d8 |
| CL 11-16 | 3d8 |
| CL 17-20 | 4d8 |

#### Spending a Burden Mark
Once per round, when a marked creature or object you can perceive performs a triggering act, you may spend its Burden Mark without using an Action. Choose one Earth Response appropriate to the trigger.
##### Anchor Step
Trigger: The marked target begins movement while touching a surface, including walking, climbing, burrowing, jumping, forced movement, or standing from Prone.
Reduce one of the target’s Speeds by 10 feet until the end of the current turn. At CL 11, this reduction becomes 20 feet.
This cannot reduce a Speed below 0.
If the movement is forced movement, reduce the forced movement distance by the same amount.
##### Drag Down
Trigger: The marked target willingly moves at least 5 feet, jumps, climbs, flies upward while within 10 feet of a solid surface, or attempts to stand from Prone.
The target makes a Strength saving throw.
Failed Save: The target falls Prone, or if already Prone, its Speed becomes 0 until the end of the current turn.
Successful Save: Reduce the target’s Speed by 5 feet until the end of the current turn.
A creature flying high in open air is affected only if it is within 10 feet of a solid surface, unless a talent says otherwise.
##### Bear the Blow
Trigger: The marked target deals damage to you, an ally, an object, or a Foundation Space while the damaged target is touching one of your Foundation Spaces or is within 5 feet of you.
Reduce the damage by:
1d8 + your Earth key ability modifier
At CL 5, this becomes 2d8 + modifier; at CL 11, 3d8 + modifier; at CL 17, 4d8 + modifier.
##### Shift the Load
Trigger: The marked target hits a creature with an attack roll while both are touching the ground or a legal Earth surface.
Before damage is rolled, choose one willing creature within 10 feet of the damaged creature, including yourself.
The chosen creature gains Temporary HP equal to your Proficiency Bonus + your Earth key ability modifier, minimum 1.
If the chosen creature is touching one of your Foundation Spaces, double the Temporary HP.
##### Raise the Ridge
Trigger: The marked target makes a ranged attack roll, casts a spell, uses a sphere talent, or creates a harmful line or area effect while touching a surface within 60 feet of you.
Raise a low ridge, berm, stone lip, packed-earth mound, or similar obstruction in one unoccupied 5-foot space touching the marked target or the triggering line of effect.
The ridge lasts until the start of your next turn. It grants Half Cover against one attack or effect that crosses through its space, then crumbles.
Raise the Ridge does not block movement unless a talent says otherwise.
##### Settle the Impact
Trigger: The marked target would push, pull, knock Prone, shove, move, teleport, or otherwise displace another creature or object.
Reduce the displacement by 10 feet. At CL 11, reduce it by 20 feet.
If this reduces the displacement to 0, the displaced creature or object may immediately move 5 feet without provoking Opportunity Attacks from the marked target.
Settle the Impact does not prevent planar travel or teleportation unless the distance is reduced to 0 and the effect is not a Domain, Secret Inheritance, artifact, or story-scale effect.

This cannot reduce a Speed below 0.
If the movement is forced movement, reduce the forced movement distance by the same amount.
##### Drag Down
Trigger: The marked target willingly moves at least 5 feet, jumps, climbs, flies upward while within 10 feet of a solid surface, or attempts to stand from Prone.
The target makes a Strength saving throw.
Failed Save: The target falls Prone, or if already Prone, its Speed becomes 0 until the end of the current turn.
Successful Save: Reduce the target’s Speed by 5 feet until the end of the current turn.
A creature flying high in open air is affected only if it is within 10 feet of a solid surface, unless a talent says otherwise.
##### Bear the Blow
Trigger: The marked target deals damage to you, an ally, an object, or a Foundation Space while the damaged target is touching one of your Foundation Spaces or is within 5 feet of you.
Reduce the damage by:
1d8 + your Earth key ability modifier
At CL 5, this becomes 2d8 + modifier; at CL 11, 3d8 + modifier; at CL 17, 4d8 + modifier.
##### Shift the Load
Trigger: The marked target hits a creature with an attack roll while both are touching the ground or a legal Earth surface.
Before damage is rolled, choose one willing creature within 10 feet of the damaged creature, including yourself.
The chosen creature gains Temporary HP equal to your Proficiency Bonus + your Earth key ability modifier, minimum 1.
If the chosen creature is touching one of your Foundation Spaces, double the Temporary HP.
##### Raise the Ridge
Trigger: The marked target makes a ranged attack roll, casts a spell, uses a sphere talent, or creates a harmful line or area effect while touching a surface within 60 feet of you.
Raise a low ridge, berm, stone lip, packed-earth mound, or similar obstruction in one unoccupied 5-foot space touching the marked target or the triggering line of effect.
The ridge lasts until the start of your next turn. It grants Half Cover against one attack or effect that crosses through its space, then crumbles.
Raise the Ridge does not block movement unless a talent says otherwise.
##### Settle the Impact
Trigger: The marked target would push, pull, knock Prone, shove, move, teleport, or otherwise displace another creature or object.
Reduce the displacement by 10 feet. At CL 11, reduce it by 20 feet.
If this reduces the displacement to 0, the displaced creature or object may immediately move 5 feet without provoking Opportunity Attacks from the marked target.
Settle the Impact does not prevent planar travel or teleportation unless the distance is reduced to 0 and the effect is not a Domain, Secret Inheritance, artifact, or story-scale effect.
