spheres.full_exact_source_text: # Sphere of Equipment Qi Types: armor qi, battle-dress qi, lamellar qi, lacquer qi, padding qi, helmet qi, hidden-plate qi, mirror qi, mountain-pattern qi. Related methods may involve metal qi, talisman qi, formation qi, beast-hide qi, imperial qi, ancestral qi, or sect-uniform qi only when another sphere, item, Foundation, manual, or feature contributes them. "Armor is not a second character sheet. It is the promise that the body will still be there when the blow arrives." Common Name: Equipment Sphere Sphere Type: Martial Utility Sphere; Armor and Battle-Dress Sphere Primary Paths: Body Refining and Qi Cultivation Secondary Path: Spirit Awakening Key Themes: wearing armor well, fitting armor to breath and meridians, moving in armor, hidden armor, helmets and masks, lamellar and lacquered protection, brigandine robes, mirror-bright armor, mountain-pattern shells, armor as rank or oath, and simple armor support for other builds Primary Resource Hooks: armor proficiency, shields only when separately proficient, Fitted Armor, armor category, CP only where a talent says so, Stamina for Body Refining where active Tianxia rules allow Stamina to pay CP costs Core Chassis: Equipment Training, Fitted Armor, Equipment talents, armor-facing realm talents, and simple armor automation Common Effects: armor proficiency, shield proficiency, faster donning and doffing, ignoring armor Stealth disadvantage, ignoring armor speed penalties, sleeping in armor, concealing armor, reducing incoming damage, temporary hardening, named high-Realm armor techniques, Secret Inheritance armor upgrades, and GM-permission Forbidden armor branches ## Equipment Dao The Dao of Equipment is the Dao of wearing protection without being ruled by it. A beginner thinks armor is only Armor Class. A soldier learns that armor is also heat, straps, breath, sound, weight, helmet vision, sleeve clearance, and whether the body can still move when fear arrives. A cultivator goes further: armor becomes a training partner. It teaches the shoulders to carry burden, the ribs to breathe under pressure, and the meridians to circulate qi through cloth, leather, scales, plates, lacing, and lacquer. Equipment is not meant to become a whole build by itself. It is a support sphere. It helps armored cultivators, robe-armored duelists, talisman carriers, formation guards, cavalry warriors, shield users, and battlefield commanders do what their real build already wants to do. ## Sphere Boundary Equipment governs: - armor proficiency and shield proficiency; - fitting one suit of armor to your body and cultivation method; - moving, resting, hiding, and fighting more cleanly in armor; - simple helmet, padding, lacing, under-robe, brigandine, lamellar, mirror-plate, and mountain-pattern armor techniques; - short defensive reactions that reduce damage or improve armor readiness. Equipment does not govern: - weapon proficiency, weapon groups, weapon tricks, crossbow handling, thrown-weapon returns, unarmed scaling, or attack-style packages; use the Weapons sphere or a specialist weapon sphere; - active shield techniques, shield deflection chains, projected shield faces, or shield-as-weapon methods; use the Shield sphere; - permanent crafting, reforging, item creation, artifact birth, item spirits, squad logistics, supply networks, camp systems, or construction; use Blacksmith, item rules, artifact rules, or a future Quartermaster sphere; - supernatural metal command; use Metal; - talisman writing or formula magic; use Talismans; - formation construction or battlefield arrays; use Formations; - independent armor, flying armor, animated armor, or armor companions unless another sphere, item, or feature grants that power. Use this test: if the effect is about **wearing armor better**, Equipment may own it. If the effect is about **attacking, forging, commanding material, supplying a group, writing magic, building arrays, or making armor act on its own**, another system owns it. ## Equipment Access The Equipment sphere is ordinary and player-facing. When you first gain the Equipment sphere, choose one Equipment talent and gain it for free. You must meet the talent's prerequisites. ## Realm Progression **Mortal Realm.** Equipment is practical training. You learn armor proficiency, fit, stealth, speed, rest, concealment, helmets, padding, and basic maintenance. **Foundation Realm.** Armor becomes part of the cultivation base. It moves with breath, conducts qi, hides beneath robes, catches blows through many small layers, or declares the wearer through mirror-bright presence. **Core Formation Realm.** Armor becomes a circuit. A fitted suit can be awakened for short defensive surges, hardened against volleys, donned with supernatural speed, or built to carry other legal systems safely. **Nascent Soul Realm.** Armor becomes identity. A named battle dress may answer the soul, carry an oath, resist ruin, or briefly stand like a fortress. **Secret and Forbidden Techniques.** Secret Equipment talents are rare upgrades to ordinary armor methods. Forbidden Equipment talents are GM-permission branches where armor protects the wearer by violating bodies, spirits, corpses, vows, or fate. Both should stay simple at the table. ## 2024 Fifth-Edition Rules Baseline Equipment uses the active Tianxia and 2024 fifth-edition rules baseline. Use the normal meanings of Armor Class, armor proficiency, shield proficiency, Action, Bonus Action, Reaction, movement, Speed, Stealth, saving throws, Temporary Hit Points, Resistance, Concentration, donning and doffing armor, and carrying capacity unless a talent explicitly changes them. A character cannot stack multiple AC formulas. If several features set your AC, choose one formula. A shield, cover, magic item, or feature bonus applies only if its own rule says it applies. Armor style is descriptive unless a rule says otherwise. A suit may be described as armored robes, lacquered leather, scale, lamellar, brigandine, mirror-bright armor, mountain-pattern armor, beast-hide armor, iron lamellar, heavy cavalry armor, or another Tianxia style. The description does not change light, medium, or heavy armor category unless the GM assigns a different armor profile. ## Core Equipment Rules ### Equipment Key Ability Most Equipment talents use your Path key ability when they call for an Equipment check, Equipment Save DC, or Equipment modifier. - Body Refining uses Constitution. - Qi Cultivation uses Intelligence or Charisma, according to the character's cultivation key. - Spirit Awakening uses Wisdom. ### Equipment Check When a talent calls for an Equipment check, roll d20 + your Proficiency Bonus + your Equipment key ability modifier unless the talent states otherwise. ### Equipment Save DC Your Equipment Save DC equals 8 + your Proficiency Bonus + your Equipment key ability modifier. ### Fitted Armor During a long rest, or by spending 10 minutes with a suit of armor you are proficient with, you may make that armor your Fitted Armor. You can have only one Fitted Armor at a time. It remains fitted until you fit a different suit, lose proficiency with it, or the armor is destroyed. Fitted Armor is not magical by default. It is simply the armor your Equipment talents are trained around. ### Equipment Talent Tags **Armor.** Uses or improves armor. **Fitted.** Requires your Fitted Armor. **Mobility.** Helps movement, speed, Stealth, rest, or comfort in armor. **Concealed.** Hides armor or makes armor look like clothing. **Guard.** Reduces damage, improves AC for a moment, or protects against a hit. **Integration.** Lets armor safely carry another legal sphere, item, or cultivation feature. **Secret.** Requires GM permission, sect inheritance, scripture access, bloodline inheritance, or campaign reward. **Forbidden.** Requires explicit GM permission and carries corruption, social, karmic, sect, or tribulation consequences. ## Path Expression **Body Refining — Armor as Burden Training.** Body Refiners use Equipment to carry weight, absorb impact, and keep moving when armor is heavy, hot, dented, or blood-slick. **Qi Cultivation — Armor as Circuit.** Qi Cultivators use Equipment to circulate qi through plates, lacing, underlayers, mirror pieces, and hidden channels without turning the armor into a separate artifact. **Spirit Awakening — Armor as Vow.** Spirit Awakeners use Equipment to name armor, inherit armor, display rank, carry sect colors, and make battle dress part of the soul's visible promise. ## Base Sphere Abilities ### Equipment Training Action Type: Passive Canonical Action Type: Passive Factory Combat Bucket: passive Factory Routing: passive_or_modifier Range: Self Target: Self Cost: 0 When you gain the Equipment sphere, choose one Equipment talent and gain it for free. You also gain the ability to designate Fitted Armor. This sphere does not grant weapon proficiency. ## Mortal Realm Equipment Talents ### Armor Training Tags: Armor You gain proficiency with light armor. If you already have light armor proficiency, you instead gain medium armor proficiency. If you already have light and medium armor proficiency, you instead gain heavy armor proficiency. You may take this talent more than once. ### Shield Training Tags: Armor You gain shield proficiency. This does not grant Shield sphere talents, shield active defense, shield attacks, or shield deflection techniques. ### Armor Ease Tags: Armor, Mobility Choose light, medium, or heavy armor. You must be proficient with the chosen category. While wearing armor of that category, you ignore Disadvantage on Dexterity (Stealth) checks imposed by that armor. You may take this talent more than once, choosing a different armor category each time. ### Sure Harness Tags: Armor, Mobility While wearing armor you are proficient with, you ignore any Speed reduction caused by failing to meet that armor's Strength requirement. ### Quick Harness Tags: Armor, Mobility You don or doff armor you are proficient with in half the normal time. If the armor is your Fitted Armor, you may instead don or doff it in one quarter of the normal time. ### Sleep in Armor Tags: Armor, Mobility You can complete a long rest while wearing light or medium armor you are proficient with. If you are proficient with heavy armor, you can also complete a long rest while wearing heavy armor, but you must spend 10 minutes after waking to stretch, relace, and settle the suit before it counts as your Fitted Armor again. ### Hidden Plates Tags: Armor, Concealed While wearing light or medium armor you are proficient with, you may disguise it as ordinary clothing, travel robes, sect dress, court dress, or work garments. A creature that searches you must succeed on an Intelligence (Investigation) check against your Equipment Save DC to notice the armor. A physical search made by touch has Advantage on this check. This talent does not hide heavy armor unless a separate item, talent, armor profile, or explicit GM approval says that specific heavy armor can be concealed. ### Reinforced Robes Tags: Armor While you are wearing no armor and not using a shield, your AC equals 10 + your Dexterity modifier + your Equipment key ability modifier. This is an armor discipline expressed through robes, wraps, bracers, belts, boots, and guarded movement. It does not improve unarmed strikes or weapon attacks. ### Helmet Discipline Tags: Armor, Guard While wearing a helmet, mask, armored hood, or equivalent head protection with armor you are proficient with, you may turn one critical hit against you into a normal hit. You must use this feature before damage is rolled. Once you use it, you cannot use it again until you finish a long rest. ### Padded Layers Tags: Armor, Guard While wearing armor you are proficient with, once per round when you take bludgeoning damage, you may reduce that damage by your Proficiency Bonus. If the damage comes from falling or collision with an object or surface, reduce the damage by twice your Proficiency Bonus instead. ### Field Maintenance Tags: Armor You know how to keep armor usable without turning this sphere into a crafting system. You have Advantage on checks made to clean, oil, relace, patch, seal, dry, or safely remove armor you are proficient with. This talent does not create armor, improve armor, restore object hit points, or replace the Blacksmith sphere. ## Foundation Realm Equipment Talents ### Breath-Aligned Armor Prerequisite: Foundation Realm, Armor Training Tags: Armor, Fitted, Mobility While wearing your Fitted Armor, you may stand from prone by spending only 5 feet of movement. In addition, your Fitted Armor does not impose Disadvantage on Dexterity (Acrobatics) checks. ### Qi-Conductive Lacing Prerequisite: Foundation Realm Tags: Armor, Fitted, Integration Your Fitted Armor can carry a simple qi circuit without becoming a magic item. Once per turn, when you spend CP on an Equipment talent while wearing your Fitted Armor, you gain Temporary Hit Points equal to your Proficiency Bonus. ### Brigandine Robe Scripture Prerequisite: Foundation Realm, Hidden Plates Tags: Armor, Concealed, Guard While your armor is concealed by Hidden Plates, you may use your Reaction when you are hit by an attack. Increase your AC against that attack by your Proficiency Bonus. If this causes the attack to miss, your armor is revealed to the attacker. Once you use this talent, you cannot use it again until you finish a short or long rest. ### Lamellar Flow Prerequisite: Foundation Realm Tags: Armor, Fitted, Guard When you take bludgeoning, piercing, or slashing damage while wearing your Fitted Armor, you may use your Reaction and spend 1 CP to reduce the damage by 1d8 + your Proficiency Bonus. At Core Formation Realm, this reduction becomes 2d8 + your Proficiency Bonus. At Nascent Soul Realm, this reduction becomes 3d8 + your Proficiency Bonus. ### Mirror-Bright Armor Prerequisite: Foundation Realm Tags: Armor, Fitted, Guard As a Bonus Action while wearing your Fitted Armor, spend 1 CP and choose one creature within 30 feet that can see you. The target must make a Wisdom saving throw against your Equipment Save DC. On a failed save, the target has Disadvantage on the next attack roll it makes against a creature other than you before the start of your next turn. This is a visual challenge, not mind control. A creature that cannot see your armor is unaffected. ## Core Formation Realm Equipment Talents ### Circuit Armor Prerequisite: Core Formation Realm, Qi-Conductive Lacing Tags: Armor, Fitted, Guard As a Bonus Action while wearing your Fitted Armor, spend 2 CP to awaken its circuit for 1 minute. While the circuit is active, once per round when you take damage, reduce the damage by your Equipment key ability modifier, minimum 1. The circuit ends early if you remove the armor, become Incapacitated, or the armor is destroyed. ### Iron Rain Readiness Prerequisite: Core Formation Realm Tags: Armor, Fitted, Guard When you are hit by a ranged attack, or when you fail a Dexterity saving throw against an area effect, you may use your Reaction and spend 2 CP. Roll 2d8 + your Proficiency Bonus. Reduce the triggering damage by the result. ### Instant Harness Prerequisite: Core Formation Realm, Quick Harness Tags: Armor, Fitted, Mobility As an Action, you may don or doff your Fitted Armor if it is within your reach, unrestrained, and not locked, sealed, worn by another creature, or trapped. This talent moves straps, buckles, robes, plates, cords, and helmets into place. It does not teleport armor or call it from a distance. ### Underplate Channels Prerequisite: Core Formation Realm; Talismans sphere, Formations sphere, or GM permission Tags: Armor, Fitted, Integration Your Fitted Armor has safe channels for one legal talisman, formation marker, scripture strip, seal case, or similar small item. You may secure or remove that item during a short or long rest. While secured, the item counts as worn and does not require a free hand merely to carry it. This talent does not create the item, activate it for free, reduce its cost, grant extra charges, or make an illegal item legal. ### Mountain-Pattern Shell Prerequisite: Core Formation Realm Tags: Armor, Fitted, Guard While wearing medium or heavy Fitted Armor, you gain a +1 bonus to AC. You lose this bonus while Incapacitated or while using another Equipment talent that grants a persistent bonus to AC. ## Nascent Soul Realm Equipment Talents ### Walking Fortress Scripture Prerequisite: Nascent Soul Realm, Circuit Armor or Mountain-Pattern Shell Tags: Armor, Fitted, Guard As a Bonus Action while wearing your Fitted Armor, spend 4 CP to enter Walking Fortress stance for 1 minute. While in this stance, your Speed is reduced by 10 feet and you have Resistance to nonmagical bludgeoning, piercing, and slashing damage. The stance ends early if you remove the armor, become Incapacitated, or choose to end it. ### Ancestral Battle Dress Prerequisite: Nascent Soul Realm, Spirit Awakening path or GM permission Tags: Armor, Fitted Choose one named suit of armor, armored robe, helmet, or battle dress. It becomes your Ancestral Battle Dress. While wearing it as your Fitted Armor, once per long rest when you fail a saving throw, you may reroll the save. You must use the new result. ### Armor Answers the Soul Prerequisite: Nascent Soul Realm, Instant Harness or Ancestral Battle Dress Tags: Armor, Fitted, Mobility As an Action, you may call your Fitted Armor from within 60 feet and don it. The armor must be unattended, not locked away, not worn by another creature, and able to reach you along an open path. It cannot pass through total cover, sealed containers, dimensional barriers, antimagic restrictions, or effects that stop item movement. This talent does not let the armor attack, scout, carry objects, act independently, or become a companion. ### Soul-Sealed Armor Prerequisite: Nascent Soul Realm Tags: Armor, Fitted, Guard While wearing your Fitted Armor, it cannot be removed from you against your will unless you are Incapacitated, dead, or the effect specifically removes worn equipment. Once per long rest, when damage would reduce you to 0 HP but not kill you outright, you may instead drop to 1 HP. Your Fitted Armor becomes cracked, dimmed, spiritually strained, or visibly damaged until you finish a long rest. ## Armor Traditions These traditions are mainly descriptive. They help players and GMs describe armor without adding extra rules. **Lacquered Hide.** Flexible hardened hide, weatherproof layers, beast-hunter armor, border armor, and early war dress. **Lamellar Scale.** Rows of small plates tied by cord, moving as many little decisions rather than one rigid wall. **Jiǎzhòu Battle Dress.** Armor and helmet treated as one complete battle garment. **Mingguang Bright Armor.** Mirror-bright chest or back plates, polished presence, rank, visibility, and intimidation. **Mountain-Pattern Armor.** Interlocking plates that spread impact through a flexible shell. **Hidden Brigandine Robes.** Cloth outside, plates inside: court armor, assassin-resistant robes, caravan coats, and concealed sect dress. ## Secret Inheritances Secret Equipment inheritances are not a second talent list for every character. They are campaign rewards, sect secrets, clan armories, hidden scriptures, or named suits of armor that teach one clean upgrade. A Secret Inheritance talent counts as an Equipment talent, but a character cannot choose it unless the GM grants access. Unless a talent says otherwise, it follows all normal Equipment rules. ### Black Armor Legion Scripture Prerequisite: Foundation Realm, Armor Training; Secret Inheritance Tags: Armor, Fitted, Guard, Secret Your armor is trained for disciplined battle lines, guard rotations, and holding under pressure. When you roll initiative while wearing your Fitted Armor and you are not surprised, you gain Temporary Hit Points equal to your Proficiency Bonus + your Equipment key ability modifier, minimum 1. These Temporary Hit Points follow normal Temporary Hit Point rules. ### Hidden Brigandine Assassin-Robe Prerequisite: Foundation Realm, Hidden Plates; Secret Inheritance Tags: Armor, Concealed, Mobility, Secret Your hidden armor is cut for sudden violence, escape steps, and court ambushes. When Brigandine Robe Scripture causes an attack to miss, you may move up to 10 feet as part of the same Reaction. This movement does not provoke opportunity attacks from the creature that made the triggering attack. This talent does not make heavy armor easier to conceal unless Hidden Plates already allows that armor to be concealed. ### Mingguang Bright Armor Scripture Prerequisite: Foundation Realm, Mirror-Bright Armor; Secret Inheritance Tags: Armor, Fitted, Guard, Secret Your mirror-bright plates do not merely shine; they announce that the battlefield has a center. When a creature fails its saving throw against Mirror-Bright Armor, you gain Temporary Hit Points equal to your Proficiency Bonus. If the creature succeeds on the saving throw, you gain no Temporary Hit Points. ### Beast-Hide Harness Scripture Prerequisite: Foundation Realm, Padded Layers; Secret Inheritance Tags: Armor, Guard, Secret Your padding, hide, and underlayers are trained to catch tearing impacts before they reach the flesh. While wearing leather, hide, scale, lamellar, padded, or robe-style armor you are proficient with, your Padded Layers talent may trigger when you take slashing damage instead of bludgeoning damage. You still use Padded Layers only once per round. This does not change the fall or collision benefit from Padded Layers. ### Mountain-Pattern Grand Shell Prerequisite: Core Formation Realm, Mountain-Pattern Shell; Secret Inheritance Tags: Armor, Fitted, Guard, Secret Your interlocking plates settle into a stronger pattern after the first blow. Once per round while wearing medium or heavy Fitted Armor, when you take bludgeoning, piercing, or slashing damage, reduce that damage by your Proficiency Bonus. This reduction is passive and does not cost a Reaction. If another passive Equipment feature would also reduce the same damage, choose one passive Equipment reduction to apply. This talent does not apply while you are Incapacitated. ### Ancestral Battle Dress Scripture Prerequisite: Nascent Soul Realm, Ancestral Battle Dress; Secret Inheritance Tags: Armor, Fitted, Secret Your named armor remembers its line of wearers. When you use Ancestral Battle Dress to reroll a failed saving throw, you also gain Temporary Hit Points equal to your Proficiency Bonus + your Equipment key ability modifier, minimum 1. These Temporary Hit Points appear after the reroll is resolved. ## Forbidden Equipment Branches Forbidden Equipment is armor whose protection is bought through violation. It is not part of the ordinary player-facing sphere. It requires explicit GM permission. Forbidden Equipment talents count as Equipment talents, but they should come from corrupted armories, demonic battle dress, corpse-smithing, spirit-binding, tyrant sects, or desperate survival bargains. They may be stronger than ordinary talents at the same Realm, but they should always carry visible consequences: social exposure, spiritual stain, haunting, sect punishment, lawful retaliation, tribulation complications, or dependency on forbidden materials. ### Corpse-Lamellar Shell Prerequisite: Foundation Realm, Lamellar Flow; Forbidden Tags: Armor, Fitted, Guard, Forbidden Your armor is reinforced with plates, cords, or inner layers taken from the dead in a way Heaven does not forgive. When you use Lamellar Flow, add your Proficiency Bonus to the damage reduced. After you use this talent, your armor carries an obvious corpse-stain until you finish a long rest or the GM rules it has been ritually cleansed. The stain is visible to ordinary inspection and may be felt by corpse-sensitive, righteous, ancestral, or death-aware effects. ### Parasite Harness Prerequisite: Core Formation Realm, Circuit Armor; Forbidden Tags: Armor, Fitted, Guard, Forbidden Your armor drinks from you to keep you standing. When you activate Circuit Armor, you may choose to gain Temporary Hit Points equal to 2d8 + your Proficiency Bonus. When Circuit Armor ends, you take necrotic damage equal to your Proficiency Bonus. This damage cannot be reduced by Equipment talents. ### Oath-Cage Plates Prerequisite: Core Formation Realm, Circuit Armor or GM permission; Forbidden Tags: Armor, Fitted, Guard, Forbidden Your armor contains a bound oath, ghost, prisoner-spirit, or broken ancestor forced to take the edge of death for you. Once per long rest while wearing your Fitted Armor, when you fail a death saving throw, you may treat the roll as a success instead. Each time you use this talent, the bound presence becomes louder, more visible, or more unstable. The GM may attach haunting, social, sect, or tribulation consequences. ### Injury-Transfer Armor Prerequisite: Nascent Soul Realm, Lamellar Flow; Forbidden Tags: Armor, Fitted, Guard, Forbidden Your armor passes part of a blow into someone bound to the suit. When you take damage while wearing your Fitted Armor, you may use your Reaction and spend 4 CP to choose one creature within 60 feet that is bound to the armor by a curse, oath, blood tie, prison seal, or other GM-approved forbidden link. The target makes a Constitution saving throw against your Equipment Save DC. On a failed save, you have Resistance to the triggering damage, and the target takes necrotic damage equal to the damage prevented. On a successful save, this talent has no effect and the CP is spent. This talent cannot be used without an existing forbidden link. It does not create the link by itself. ### Heaven-Defying War Shell Prerequisite: Nascent Soul Realm, Walking Fortress Scripture; Forbidden Tags: Armor, Fitted, Guard, Forbidden Your armor refuses a wound that should have ended you, but the refusal is loud enough for Heaven to hear. When you activate Walking Fortress Scripture, you may spend 2 additional CP. If you do, you also have Resistance to one damage type of your choice other than force or psychic for the duration. When the stance ends, you cannot use Walking Fortress Scripture again until you finish a long rest, and the GM may mark the act as a tribulation complication, karmic debt, sect scandal, or visible forbidden sign. ## Path Synergies **Weapons.** Weapons owns weapon proficiency and attack technique. Equipment makes armor easier to wear while using those attacks. **Shield.** Shield owns active defense. Equipment can grant shield proficiency, but it does not grant Shield sphere techniques. **Blacksmith.** Blacksmith creates and improves gear. Equipment wears gear better. **Metal.** Metal commands material. Equipment manages worn armor. **Talismans.** Talismans writes effects. Equipment may provide safe armor channels for legal talismans. **Formations.** Formations builds arrays. Equipment may carry a legal small marker, but it does not create arrays. **Protection.** Protection creates supernatural wards. Equipment provides physical and battle-dress protection. **Athletics / Brute / Wrestling.** These spheres govern body force. Equipment helps an armored body stay usable. ## Cultivation Insights ### Armor Is Not a Cage You learned to breathe, step, and circulate qi while protected. This Insight may justify Armor Ease, Sure Harness, Quick Harness, or Breath-Aligned Armor. ### Cloth Can Hide Iron You learned that robes can lie. This Insight may justify Hidden Plates or Brigandine Robe Scripture. ### Many Plates, One Breath You understood lamellar, scale, padding, and mountain-pattern armor as linked protection. This Insight may justify Padded Layers, Lamellar Flow, Circuit Armor, or Mountain-Pattern Shell. ### The Helmet Is a Promise You learned that covering the head changes fear, identity, and survival. This Insight may justify Helmet Discipline, Ancestral Battle Dress, or Soul-Sealed Armor. ### Bright Armor Changes the Field You learned that visible armor can draw attention, challenge enemies, and steady allies. This Insight may justify Mirror-Bright Armor or a secret Mingguang inheritance. ## Automation Notes - Equipment effects should not be imported as weapon actions. - `Fitted Armor` is a persistent item-linked state. - No rest-defined loadout list, armor-weight mini-system, quartermaster inventory, squad logistics, construction, or weapon-discipline subsystem is used. - AC formulas and AC bonuses must be checked for stacking. - Damage-reduction reactions must record trigger, CP spent, dice rolled, and final damage. - Passive Equipment damage reductions should not stack with each other unless a talent explicitly says they do. - Temporary Hit Points from Equipment follow normal Temporary Hit Point rules and do not stack with other Temporary Hit Points. - Hidden armor effects should track concealed/revealed state. - Secret Inheritance talents should be flagged as GM permission or campaign reward content. - Forbidden Equipment should be flagged as explicit GM-permission content and should not appear as ordinary player choices.

#### Sense the Ledger
Action Type: Multi-Mode
Canonical Action Type: Multi-Mode
Factory Combat Bucket: action
Factory Routing: combat_action_plus_exploration_procedure
Split Review Decision: single_combat_action_plus_procedure_variant
Recommended Factory Realization: action_id=ACT_FATE_SENSE_THE_LEDGER_STUDY_ACTION->action; procedures=ONE_MINUTE_OBSERVATION
Timing Detail: Study action in encounter time, or 1 minute of observation in exploration time
Range: 30 feet
Cost: None
You read the local pressure of fate.
Choose one creature, object, oath, doorway, battlefield feature, game of chance, written name, or visible ritual within range. Make a Wisdom or Charisma Cultivation Check against a DC set by the GM.
Success: Learn one of the following, if present:
whether the target is affected by a Fate talent;
whether the target carries supernatural luck or misfortune;
whether a game of chance, drawing of lots, wager, or random selection is being supernaturally manipulated;
whether a visible oath, name, seal, contract, or red-thread bond is fate-active;
whether the place is auspicious, ominous, or strongly connected to a destined meeting or calamity;
whether a creature has recently altered fate within the scene.
Sense the Ledger does not reveal exact mechanics, full stat blocks, private thoughts, future events, or hidden locations automatically.
At CL 10, the range becomes 60 feet.

spheres.full_exact_source_text: # Sphere of Fate Qi Expression: Primary — Fate Qi; Supporting — Chance Qi, Thread Qi, Omen Qi, Time-Shadow Qi. “The ignorant call it luck. The wise call it a debt whose creditor has not yet arrived.” Sphere Type: Forbidden Restricted Power Sphere Primary Path: Spirit Awakening Secondary Path: Qi Cultivation Rare Path Access: Body Refining through the Fortune-Tempered Body Insight Resource: CP. Body Refiners with the Fortune-Tempered Body Insight use Stamina instead. Common Effects: Auspicious and ominous luck, fate dice, curses, blessings, vows, red-thread bonds, Heaven’s ledger, names, mandate, calamity, improbable survival, rewritten outcomes, forbidden correction of destiny ### Fate Dao Fate is the cultivation of the written-but-not-yet-arrived consequence. A mortal sees chance. A diviner sees omen. A karmic judge sees debt. A Fate cultivator sees the moment before Heaven’s brush finishes the stroke. In eastern cultivation terms, Fate is not merely random luck. It touches several overlapping ideas: Ming: the allotted shape of a life, talent, lifespan, calamity, and destined meeting. Yun: the moving fortune that rises and falls with timing, merit, place, preparation, and hidden currents. Yuanfen: the thread of destined connection between people, teachers, enemies, lovers, disciples, patrons, and debts. Yinguo: cause and consequence, especially when the result has not yet fully ripened. Jie: calamity, tribulation, and the disaster that arrives when cultivation exceeds its permitted measure. Tianming: Heaven’s mandate, the authority that says one person, dynasty, sect, or oath is permitted to stand at the center of events. A Fate cultivator does not simply bless allies and curse enemies. They touch ledgers, threads, names, auspicious hours, unlucky roads, owed kindness, inherited hatred, unfinished vows, and the narrow crack between possibility and outcome. For that reason, the Sphere of Fate is commonly forbidden. Many sects tolerate Divination, even when they distrust it. Divination observes Heaven’s writing. Fate dares to change where the brush lands. ### Why Fate Is Forbidden Fate techniques threaten social order, spiritual law, and Heavenly balance. A sect may forbid Fate because it can: steal the fortune of disciples before a trial; curse a rival’s breakthrough with minor failures until the tribulation arrives crooked; bind enemies through red-thread affinity; turn a lucky heir’s mandate into a public embarrassment; cause a sworn protector to arrive one breath too late; make a calamity choose a new path; preserve a life Heaven expected to collect; rewrite a critical success into disaster; make oaths and names behave like handles on the soul. Fate is not illegal everywhere. Some imperial astrologers, temple registrars, funeral priests, and oath-keeping clans practice lawful fragments of it. But complete Fate cultivation is often treated like contraband scripture. A character who openly practices this sphere should expect attention from censors, astrologer-bureaus, oath courts, demons who eat luck, jealous heirs, and Heaven itself. ### Forbidden Safeguards Fate is powerful because it changes outcomes. It must be narrow to remain playable. Unless a talent explicitly says otherwise: A roll can be affected by only one Fate talent from the same cultivator. A roll can be rerolled only once. A reroll must use the new result. A Fate talent cannot alter a roll after the outcome has been announced and consequences have begun resolving. A Fate talent cannot affect an event that has no roll unless the talent explicitly works on events. Fate cannot create objects, allies, evidence, memories, or locations from nothing. Fate cannot grant knowledge that nobody could plausibly possess. Fate cannot force an impossible coincidence. Fate cannot revive the dead unless a Secret Inheritance explicitly says how. Fate cannot undo a completed scene, completed Long Rest, completed breakthrough, or completed tribulation. Fate cannot overwrite a Domain, Secret Inheritance, divine decree, Heavenly Tribulation, artifact mandate, or scene-defining law without an opposed Cultivation Check or explicit GM permission. A natural 1 or natural 20 keeps its ordinary meaning unless a Fate talent explicitly changes that roll. A coincidence created by Fate must remain plausible within the scene, even if it is extremely unlikely. ### Heaven’s Notice Fate techniques leave traces. Whenever you use a Fate talent that does one of the following, gain 1 Heaven’s Notice: changes a natural 1 or natural 20; prevents a creature from dropping to 0 HP; changes failure into success or success into failure after the d20 is already visible; affects a creature’s name, lifespan, mandate, breakthrough, or tribulation; uses a Nascent Soul Fate talent; uses a Secret Inheritance. Heaven’s Notice is not a normal resource and does not vanish automatically. It is a story-facing pressure marker. At 3 or more Heaven’s Notice, the GM may introduce omens, investigators, backlash, rival Fate practitioners, karmic creditors, or a minor calamity related to the way you bent the ledger. A character can reduce Heaven’s Notice through confession, repayment, seclusion, fulfilling vows, accepting a deserved consequence, performing temple rites, or allowing a fate they could have avoided to arrive naturally. If your table does not want this pressure system, treat Heaven’s Notice as GM advice rather than a hard rule. ### Core Fate Rules #### Fate Key Ability When you learn Fate, choose Wisdom or Charisma as your Fate key ability. Wisdom represents reading omens, sensing threads, and hearing the pressure of Heaven. Charisma represents asserting mandate, speaking decrees, and forcing your name into the ledger. A Path synergy may allow another ability. #### Fate Die Several Fate talents use your Fate Die. CL 1-4: d4 CL 5-10: d6 CL 11-16: d8 CL 17-20: d10 Unless a talent says otherwise, add or subtract a Fate Die after the roll is made but before the outcome is known. A single roll can benefit from only one Fate Die from you. #### Fate Methods Fate techniques are divided into three methods. Edicts create a temporary area of auspicious or ominous law. Auspices place a star, thread, seal, or mandate on one creature. Words speak a single command into the ledger. When you first learn Fate, choose one Fate Method: Edict, Auspice, or Word. You learn one Mortal talent with that method’s tag. You can learn additional methods with the Threefold Ledger talent. #### Maintaining Fate Effects Unless a talent says otherwise: Edicts require Concentration and last up to 1 minute. Auspices require Concentration and last up to 1 hour. Words are instantaneous or last only as stated. A creature can benefit from only one Auspice from you at a time. A creature can suffer only one Curse Word from you at a time unless a talent says otherwise. Ending Concentration ends the effect normally. #### Releasing an Auspice Some Auspice talents include a Release effect. If the Auspice is active on a willing creature, that creature can end it as a Reaction to gain the Release effect. If the creature is Incapacitated, it can release an Auspice only if the talent explicitly permits it. An unwilling creature cannot choose to release an Auspice. ### Base Sphere Abilities #### Sense the Ledger Action Type: Multi-Mode Canonical Action Type: Multi-Mode Factory Combat Bucket: action Factory Routing: combat_action_plus_exploration_procedure Split Review Decision: single_combat_action_plus_procedure_variant Recommended Factory Realization: action_id=ACT_FATE_SENSE_THE_LEDGER_STUDY_ACTION->action; procedures=ONE_MINUTE_OBSERVATION Timing Detail: Study action in encounter time, or 1 minute of observation in exploration time Range: 30 feet Cost: None You read the local pressure of fate. Once per round, when an ally inside the Domain makes an attack roll, ability check, or saving throw, you may roll 1d6 and add it to the roll before the outcome is known. Enemies: When an enemy starts its turn inside the Domain, it makes a Charisma saving throw. Failed Save: Choose one: it cannot take Reactions until the start of its next turn; it subtracts 1d4 from its next attack roll before the start of its next turn; it subtracts 1d4 from its next saving throw before the start of its next turn; its Speed is reduced by 10 feet until the start of its next turn. Successful Save: Its Speed is reduced by 5 feet until the start of its next turn. You may affect a creature with the enemy portion of this Domain only once per turn. Using this Domain gains 1 Heaven’s Notice. #### Fortune Reversal Prerequisite: CL 10+ Action Type: Reaction Factory Combat Bucket: reaction Factory Routing: combat_action_row Trigger: A creature within 60 feet rolls a natural 1 or natural 20 on an attack roll, ability check, or saving throw Cost: 6 CP Use Limit: Once per Short Rest Choose one: change a natural 1 into a natural 20; change a natural 20 into a natural 1. An unwilling creature may make a Charisma saving throw. On a successful save, the roll is unchanged. A Legendary creature, Domain-bearing creature, or creature protected by a Secret Inheritance may force you to make an opposed Cultivation Check before this talent can affect the roll. Using this talent gains 1 Heaven’s Notice. #### Chain of Misfortune - Curse Prerequisite: CL 10+ Action Type: Action Canonical Action Type: Action Factory Combat Bucket: action Timing Detail: Magic Action Factory Routing: combat_action_row; preserve named 5.5e action detail Range: 60 feet Target: One creature Duration: Concentration, up to 1 minute Cost: 6 CP The target makes a Charisma saving throw. Failed Save: The first time each round the target misses an attack, fails a saving throw, fails an ability check, falls Prone, or takes damage from a hazard, choose one: it takes 2d8 Psychic damage; it cannot take Reactions until the start of its next turn; its Speed is reduced by 10 feet until the start of its next turn; one ally within 30 feet gains Advantage on the next attack roll against it before the start of your next turn. At the end of each of its turns, the target repeats the saving throw, ending the curse on a success. Successful Initial Save: The next time before the start of your next turn that the target misses an attack or fails a saving throw, it cannot take Reactions until the start of its following turn. #### Steal the Auspicious Hour Prerequisite: CL 10+ Action Type: Reaction Factory Combat Bucket: reaction Factory Routing: combat_action_row Trigger: An enemy within 60 feet gains Advantage, gains a bonus die, or receives a reroll from a non-Secret feature Cost: 5 CP The enemy makes a Charisma saving throw. Failed Save: The enemy loses the triggering benefit, and one ally within 60 feet gains that same benefit on the next valid roll before the start of your next turn. Successful Save: The enemy keeps the benefit, but your chosen ally gains your Fate Die on the next valid roll before the start of your next turn. This talent cannot steal class features that create extra actions, permanent features, or effects already resolved. #### Execration Word - Word, Curse Prerequisite: CL 10+, one Curse Word talent Action Type: Action Canonical Action Type: Action Factory Combat Bucket: action Timing Detail: Magic Action Factory Routing: combat_action_row; preserve named 5.5e action detail Range: 60 feet Target: One creature currently suffering a Curse Word from you that normally ends at the start or end of your next turn Cost: 6 CP The target makes a Charisma saving throw. Failed Save: Extend the curse’s duration to 1 minute, Concentration required. The target repeats the saving throw at the end of each of its turns, ending the curse on a success. Successful Save: The original curse ends normally. At CL 17, you may increase the cost by 6 CP. If you do, a failed save makes the curse last until dispelled, removed by a comparable cleansing effect, or ended by you. Using this option gains 1 Heaven’s Notice. #### Registrar Star Auspice - Auspice Prerequisite: CL 10+, one Auspice talent Action Type: Multi-Mode Canonical Action Type: Multi-Mode Factory Combat Bucket: action Timing Detail: 10 minutes, or Action by spending 2 CP Factory Routing: combat_action_plus_ritual_preparation_variant Split Review Decision: single_combat_action_plus_procedure_variant Recommended Factory Realization: procedures=TEN_MINUTE_AUSPICE, ACTION_FAST_CAST Range: Touch Target: One willing creature already bearing one other Auspice from you Duration: Concentration, up to 1 hour Cost: 4 CP Choose one other Auspice from you currently affecting the target. While this Auspice remains active, allies of the target within 30 feet gain the passive benefit of the chosen Auspice. They do not gain the chosen Auspice’s Release effect. Release: The target releases Registrar Star and the linked Auspice together. Allies within 30 feet gain the linked Auspice’s Release effect if it can legally apply to them. #### Complete Mandala Auspice - Auspice Prerequisite: CL 10+ Action Type: Multi-Mode Canonical Action Type: Multi-Mode Factory Combat Bucket: action Timing Detail: 10 minutes, or Action by spending 2 CP Factory Routing: combat_action_plus_ritual_preparation_variant Split Review Decision: single_combat_action_plus_procedure_variant Recommended Factory Realization: procedures=TEN_MINUTE_AUSPICE, ACTION_FAST_CAST Range: Touch Target: One willing creature Duration: Concentration, up to 1 hour Cost: 4 CP When the target makes an ability check using a skill or tool proficiency, it treats a d20 roll of 9 or lower as a 10. Release: The target releases this Auspice after an ally within 30 feet makes an ability check. If the d20 result was lower than 10, treat it as 10. #### Name Written in Red Ink - Curse Prerequisite: CL 10+ Action Type: Ritual Procedure Canonical Action Type: Ritual Procedure Factory Routing: procedure_ledger_not_combat_action Timing Detail: Ritual, 10 minutes Range: 1 mile, or any distance if you possess the target’s true name, blood, signature, oath-token, or personally written name Target: One creature Duration: 24 hours Cost: 8 CP You write the target’s name into an ominous ledger. The target makes a Charisma saving throw. If it is not present, the GM may roll secretly. Failed Save: The first time before the duration ends that the target rolls a natural 20 on an attack roll, ability check, or saving throw, treat it as a 10 instead. The target feels a cold brushstroke across its name when this occurs. Successful Save: The target is unaffected and feels watched. This talent gains 1 Heaven’s Notice whether it succeeds or fails. ### Nascent Soul Realm Fate Talents #### Fate-Sovereign Incarnation Prerequisite: CL 15+ Action Type: Bonus Action Factory Combat Bucket: bonus_action Factory Routing: combat_action_row Duration: 1 minute Concentration: Not required Cost: 15 CP Use Limit: Once per Long Rest You manifest as a sovereign of auspicious and ominous outcomes. Gain the following benefits: Fly Speed 40 feet and Hover. +3 AC. Advantage on saving throws. You cannot be Surprised while conscious. Your Fate Die becomes d10 if it is smaller. Once per round, you may use Twist of Fate without spending CP. At the start of each of your turns, choose one ally within 30 feet. Until the start of your next turn, that ally gains one of the following: +1 AC; +1 to saving throws; Advantage on its next attack roll or ability check. At the start of each enemy’s turn within 20 feet of you, that enemy makes a Charisma saving throw. Failed Save: Choose one: subtract 1d6 from its next attack roll before the start of its next turn; subtract 1d6 from its next saving throw before the start of its next turn; it cannot take Reactions until the start of its next turn; its Speed is reduced by 10 feet until the start of its next turn. Successful Save: Its Speed is reduced by 5 feet until the start of its next turn. Using this talent gains 1 Heaven’s Notice. #### Calamity Finds a Path Prerequisite: CL 15+ Action Type: Action Canonical Action Type: Action Factory Combat Bucket: action Timing Detail: Magic Action Factory Routing: combat_action_row; preserve named 5.5e action detail Range: 120 feet Target: One creature Cost: 10 CP Use Limit: Once per Long Rest The target makes a Charisma saving throw. Failed Save: A plausible chain of calamities strikes the target. It takes 10d10 damage. Choose the damage type that best fits the scene: Psychic, Force, Bludgeoning, Piercing, Slashing, Fire, Cold, Lightning, or Thunder. The target also suffers two of the following until the start of your next turn: falls Prone; drops one held object; cannot take Reactions; Speed becomes 0; AC is reduced by 2; healing it receives is halved. Successful Save: The target takes half damage and suffers one of the listed effects until the start of your next turn. The calamity must be described through the environment, enemy mistakes, broken tools, collapsing stone, ricochets, unstable formations, snapped ropes, bad footing, or similar plausible causes. Using this talent gains 1 Heaven’s Notice. #### Rewrite the Disaster Prerequisite: CL 15+ Action Type: Reaction Factory Combat Bucket: reaction Factory Routing: combat_action_row Trigger: One creature within 60 feet rolls an attack roll, ability check, or saving throw Cost: 12 CP Use Limit: Once per Long Rest After seeing the d20 but before the outcome is finalized, replace the d20 result with either a natural 1 or a natural 20. An unwilling creature may make a Charisma saving throw. On a successful save, the roll is unchanged. Rewrite the Disaster cannot affect a roll already resolved, an event without a roll, a Secret Inheritance without an opposed Cultivation Check, a Heavenly Tribulation result unless the tribulation rules allow it, or a divine decree beyond your scale. Using this talent gains 2 Heaven’s Notice. #### Golden Road of Fortune Prerequisite: CL 15+ Action Type: Ritual Procedure Canonical Action Type: Ritual Procedure Factory Routing: procedure_ledger_not_combat_action Timing Detail: Ritual, 1 hour Range: Touch Target: One caravan, expedition, army unit, sect compound, voyage, construction project, diplomatic mission, search party, or similar collective undertaking Duration: 24 hours Cost: 12 CP Choose three benefits: Advantage on checks made to avoid ambush. Advantage on checks made to navigate. Reduced chance of ordinary equipment failure. One minor fortunate coincidence during the undertaking. Improved weather timing when conditions are ordinary. Reduced losses from ordinary accidents. Advantage on checks made to negotiate routine obstacles. Improved chance of finding food, shelter, or a safe campsite. One warning when the group is about to make a dangerous mistake. Golden Road of Fortune does not guarantee success. It creates favorable conditions and plausible openings. Using this talent gains 1 Heaven’s Notice. #### Borrowed Lifespan Talisman Prerequisite: CL 15+ Action Type: Reaction Factory Combat Bucket: reaction Factory Routing: combat_action_row Trigger: A willing creature within 30 feet would drop to 0 HP Cost: 10 CP Use Limit: Once per Long Rest per creature The creature drops to 1 HP instead. Then choose one cost: you take Necrotic damage equal to twice your CL; the protected creature gains one Exhaustion level; you gain 2 Heaven’s Notice; the protected creature cannot benefit from this talent again until it completes a meaningful repayment oath. This talent cannot prevent death from old age, completed execution, disintegration, divine decree, or a Secret technique unless the GM permits an opposed Cultivation Check. #### Sever the Red Thread Prerequisite: CL 15+ Action Type: Action Canonical Action Type: Action Factory Combat Bucket: action Timing Detail: Magic Action Factory Routing: combat_action_row; preserve named 5.5e action detail Range: 60 feet Target: One visible magical bond, possession link, summoning tether, oath mark, red-thread effect, or comparable connection Cost: 10 CP Make an opposed Cultivation Check against the source of the bond or against a DC set by the GM. Success: Suppress the bond until the end of your next turn. If the bond is a non-Secret effect of your CL or lower, you may end it instead. Failure: The bond remains, and you gain 1 Heaven’s Notice. Sever the Red Thread does not erase genuine relationships, memories, bloodlines, or karmic debts. It affects active supernatural connections. ### Secret Inheritance #### Ink Brush That Corrects Heaven Classification: Secret Fate Inheritance Prerequisite: CL 17+, Fate-Sovereign Incarnation, hidden forbidden ledger scripture Action Type: Reaction Factory Combat Bucket: reaction Factory Routing: combat_action_row Trigger: A creature within 60 feet would fail a roll, suffer a critical hit, be reduced to 0 HP, or be caught in an immediate calamity Cost: 15 CP Use Limit: Once per week You write one correction into the margin of Heaven’s ledger. Choose one immediate, narrow, plausible alternative: turn one failed roll into a successful roll; turn one successful roll into a failed roll; turn one critical hit into a normal hit or normal miss; cause one creature reduced to 0 HP to remain at 1 HP; cause one destroyed ordinary object to remain intact at 1 HP; cause one attack targeting an ally to strike an unattended nearby object instead; place one creature in an adjacent safe space instead of inside a collapsing hazard. The correction must be narrow, immediate, plausible, and limited to one triggering event. Ink Brush That Corrects Heaven cannot: revive the dead; restore spent CP or Stamina; undo an entire encounter; erase a completed turn; restore an expended Legendary or Secret technique; create an impossible object or ally; remove permanent cultivation consequences; cancel a Heavenly Tribulation unless the tribulation rules explicitly allow it; overturn a divine decree without GM permission. After using this Secret Inheritance, gain 3 Heaven’s Notice. The next time you undergo a breakthrough or tribulation, the GM may treat this correction as an unresolved debt. ### Optional Variants #### Fortune-Tempered Body This is not the default version of Fate. You may learn Fate as a Body Refiner only if you possess the Fortune-Tempered Body Insight. When you do: use Constitution as your Fate key ability; spend Stamina instead of CP for Fate talents; Fate techniques must be expressed through the body, such as impossible dodges, lucky injuries, reflexive turns, bones that avoid fatal angles, blood that seals at the right moment, and scars that redirect calamity; you cannot learn Bound Edict, Consecrated Ground, Name Written in Red Ink, Golden Road of Fortune, or permanent Edict effects unless a later Insight allows it. Once per Short Rest, when you fail a Strength, Dexterity, or Constitution saving throw, roll your Fate Die and add it to the result, potentially turning failure into success. #### Mandate-Bound Astrologer You practice Fate under a public vow, temple office, imperial calendar bureau, ancestral hall, or sect registry. Restriction: You cannot learn Curse talents unless the target has violated a vow, attacked your protected institution, or been named in a lawful rite. Benefit: When you use Sense the Ledger, Auspicious Gathering, Golden Road of Fortune, Bound Edict, or Consecrated Ground for your institution or sworn charges, reduce the CP cost by 1, minimum 1. #### Severed Ledger Heretic You reject auspicious blessing and practice only omen-theft and misfortune. Restriction: You cannot learn Auspice talents that target willing allies, Purity Edict, Undo Harm Edict, Soothe Word, or Golden Road of Fortune. Benefit: Once per round when a creature fails a saving throw against one of your Curse talents, reduce its Speed by 5 feet and prevent it from taking Reactions until the start of its next turn. ### Path Synergies #### Spirit Awakening - Auspicious Soul Use Wisdom as your Fate key ability. When using Twist of Fate, increase its range by 30 feet. You may perceive a creature through a strong spiritual bond, vow, possession link, familiar bond, ancestral thread, or red-thread effect even if ordinary sight is blocked. This does not let you target through Total Cover unless the talent already allows it. Once per Short Rest, when you gain Heaven’s Notice, reduce the amount gained by 1, minimum 0, if the Fate technique protected a sworn bond, fulfilled a vow, or repaid a karmic debt. #### Qi Cultivation - Fortune-Circulation Art Use Intelligence or Charisma as your Fate key ability. Once per turn, reduce the CP cost of one Fate talent by 1, minimum 1. When you create an Edict, increase its radius by 5 feet. When you use Sense the Ledger, you may also identify whether the target is affected by a Qi technique, Formation, Talisman, or magical item that manipulates probability, curses, luck, oaths, or names. #### Body Refining - Fortune-Tempered Body Requires the Fortune-Tempered Body Insight. Use Constitution as your Fate key ability and Stamina as the resource for Fate talents. Once per Short Rest, when you fail a Strength, Dexterity, or Constitution saving throw, roll your Fate Die and add it to the result, potentially turning failure into success. When a Fate talent would move, protect, or preserve only yourself, reduce its Stamina cost by 1, minimum 1. ### Cultivation Insights #### Fortune-Tempered Body Prerequisite: Body Refining, CL 4+ You may learn the Sphere of Fate using the Fortune-Tempered Body variant. Use Constitution as your Fate key ability. Spend Stamina instead of CP for Fate talents. You gain the Body Refining Path synergy for Fate. #### Gambler’s Instinct Prerequisite: Fate, CL 8+ You have Advantage on checks made to recognize cheating, manipulated wagers, altered lots, loaded dice, cursed games, or supernatural probability influence. You cannot be Surprised by ordinary ambushes while conscious if the ambush relies on a game of chance, random patrol timing, or manipulated coincidence. #### Loaded Destiny Prerequisite: Fate, CL 8+ After completing a Long Rest, roll 1d20 and record the result. Before your next Long Rest, you may replace one attack roll, ability check, or saving throw you make with the recorded result. Using the recorded result does not count as rolling a natural 1 or natural 20 unless the recorded result was actually 1 or 20. #### Auspicious Companion Prerequisite: Fate, CL 8+ After completing a Long Rest, choose one willing creature. Once before your next Long Rest, when that creature fails an attack roll, ability check, or saving throw, it may roll 1d8 and add the result, potentially turning failure into success. #### Name-Sheltering Talisman Prerequisite: Fate, CL 8+ You learn a minor rite for protecting names. After a Long Rest, choose yourself or one willing creature whose name you write, seal, or ritually conceal. Until the next Long Rest, the chosen creature has Advantage on saving throws against Fate, curse, possession, domination, and name-targeting effects. #### Mandate-Bearing Voice Prerequisite: Fate, CL 12+ When you use a Word talent, increase its range by 30 feet. Once per Short Rest, if a creature succeeds on a saving throw against one of your Word talents, you may force it to subtract your Fate Die from the result. This can turn success into failure. Using this Insight to affect a natural 20 gains 1 Heaven’s Notice.

spheres.full_exact_source_text: # Sphere of Fire Qi Expression: Primary — Fire Qi; Supporting — Heat Qi, Transformation Qi, Yang Qi. Sphere Type: Power / Elemental / Escalation Sphere Primary Path: Qi Cultivation Secondary Path: Body Refining or Spirit Awakening through explicit Path synergy, bloodline, fire-body, or spirit-flame practice Resource: CP, Burn, Kindled targets, Fire Terrain, Overheat, and Concentration when a talent says so Core Chassis: Burn, Kindled, Fire Terrain, Overheat, flame attacks and fire pressure Fire cultivates ignition, escalation, and destructive appetite. Its basic loop is to apply Burn, exploit Kindled targets, create Fire Terrain, and decide when Overheat is worth the self-inflicted cost. ### Rules Baseline This player-facing sphere uses the 2024 fifth-edition rules baseline (5.5e) together with the Tianxia cultivation rules. Use the 2024 meanings of Action, Bonus Action, Reaction, Concentration, Cover, difficult terrain, Hide, Invisible, Bloodied, Exhaustion, and Damage Threshold unless this sphere explicitly replaces or expands a rule. #### Barriers, Domains, and Formation Anchors A Barrier is a temporary supernatural barrier, including a Protection-sphere Barrier or another effect that explicitly identifies itself as a Barrier. A Domain is a high-rank cultivation effect that says it is a Domain. Ordinary dispelling, sundering, or object-breaking text does not automatically remove a Domain unless the technique explicitly says otherwise. A Formation Anchor is an anchor point explicitly created by a Formation or identified by the GM as part of a Formation project. These spheres do not create Formation Anchors automatically. ### Core Fire Rules #### Burn Some Fire talents apply Burn. Unless a talent says otherwise: Burn lasts until the start of your next turn. A Burning creature takes Fire damage at the start of its turn. Burn damage is equal to your Proficiency Bonus. A creature may use an Action to extinguish one Burn affecting itself or an adjacent creature. Water, smothering material, vacuum, or an appropriate opposing technique may extinguish Burn at the GM’s discretion. Identical Burn effects from the same cultivator do not stack. Use the highest Burn value. #### Kindling A creature, object, or space is Kindled if it is currently Burning, standing in Fire Terrain, covered in flammable material, affected by one of your Fire talents, or was damaged by Fire since the start of your last turn. Some talents become stronger against Kindled targets. #### Fire Terrain Fire Terrain is ground, air, or spiritual space filled with active flames, burning heat, or combustive Qi. Unless a talent says otherwise: Fire Terrain is Lightly Obscured by heat shimmer and sparks. A hostile creature entering Fire Terrain for the first time on a turn or starting its turn there makes a Dexterity saving throw. On a failed save, take Fire damage equal to your Proficiency Bonus and become Burning. On a successful save, take no damage but become Kindled until the start of your next turn. A creature is affected only once per turn by the same Fire Terrain. Ordinary flammable unattended objects may ignite. #### Overheat Some Fire talents allow Overheat. Overheat increases attack pressure at a cost. Unless a talent says otherwise, when you Overheat: pay the listed additional CP cost; gain the listed offensive benefit; take Fire damage equal to your Proficiency Bonus after the effect resolves. This self-damage ignores Resistance but cannot reduce you below 1 HP unless the talent explicitly says otherwise. ### Base Sphere Abilities #### Ignite Action Type: Action Factory Combat Bucket: action Factory Routing: combat_action_row Range: 60 feet Cost: None Release a focused fire technique. Make a ranged Cultivation Attack. Hit: Deal Fire damage and apply Burn. | Cultivation Level | Damage | | --- | --- | | 1-4 | 1d10 | | 5-10 | 2d10 | | 11-16 | 3d10 | | 17-20 | 4d10 | Once per turn when Ignite hits, choose one: push the target 5 feet; create one 5-foot square of Fire Terrain adjacent to the target until the start of your next turn; increase Burn damage by your Path key ability modifier, minimum 1; add your Proficiency Bonus to the damage if the target is Kindled. ##### Overheat - Ignite Augment - 1 CP: Roll one additional damage die for Ignite. After the attack resolves, take Fire damage equal to your Proficiency Bonus. #### Conflagration Action Type: Action Factory Combat Bucket: action Factory Routing: combat_action_row Range: 60 feet Area: 15-foot-radius sphere Duration: Concentration, up to 1 minute Cost: 2 CP Create an area of Fire Terrain. When the area appears, creatures inside make Dexterity saving throws. Failed Save: Take Fire damage and become Burning. Successful Save: Take half damage and become Kindled until the start of your next turn. | Cultivation Level | Initial Damage | | --- | --- | | 1-10 | 2d6 | | 11-16 | 4d6 | | 17-20 | 6d6 | ##### Lingering Conflagration Augment - 2 CP: Conflagration persists for its remaining duration without Concentration. You may apply this augment after creating Conflagration on your turn without spending an Action. ### Fire Talent Tags #### Ignite Talents An Ignite talent modifies Ignite or provides a new way to exploit Burn and Kindling. Unless a talent says otherwise, apply only one Ignite augment to a single Ignite attack. #### Conflagration Talents A Conflagration talent modifies an area created through Conflagration. Only one Conflagration talent normally modifies one Conflagration. #### Overheat Talents An Overheat talent increases attack potential at a cost. #### Unique Fire Talents A Unique Fire Talent is a distinct technique that does not require Ignite or Conflagration. #### Augments An Augment modifies another Fire effect when its additional CP cost is paid. ### MORTAL REALM FIRE TALENTS #### Flame Lash - Unique Fire Talent Action Type: Action Factory Combat Bucket: action Factory Routing: combat_action_row Range: 30 feet Cost: None Make a melee or ranged Cultivation Attack. Hit: Deal Fire damage and pull or push the target 10 feet. | Cultivation Level | Damage | | --- | --- | | 1-4 | 1d8 | | 5-10 | 2d8 | | 11-16 | 3d8 | | 17-20 | 4d8 | If the target is Burning, Flame Lash has Advantage. #### Burning Weapon - Unique Fire Talent Action Type: Bonus Action Factory Combat Bucket: bonus_action Factory Routing: combat_action_row Range: Touch Duration: Concentration, up to 1 minute Cost: 1 CP Imbue one weapon, unarmed strike, or natural weapon with flame. Once per turn when the bearer hits with that weapon, add Fire damage: | Cultivation Level | Extra Damage | | --- | --- | | 1-10 | 1d6 | | 11-16 | 2d6 | | 17-20 | 3d6 | The hit applies Burn. #### Fire Ward - Unique Fire Talent Action Type: Reaction Factory Combat Bucket: reaction Factory Routing: combat_action_row Trigger: You or an ally within 30 feet takes damage Cost: 1 CP A burst of counterflame burns away part of the blow. Reduce the triggering damage: | Cultivation Level | Damage Reduction | | --- | --- | | 1-10 | 1d8 + Path key ability modifier | | 11-16 | 2d8 + Path key ability modifier | | 17-20 | 3d8 + Path key ability modifier | If the attacker is within 10 feet of the protected creature, it takes Fire damage equal to your Proficiency Bonus. #### Combustive Step - Unique Fire Talent Action Type: Bonus Action Factory Combat Bucket: bonus_action Factory Routing: combat_action_row Range: Self Cost: 1 CP Explode forward on jets of flame. Move up to half your Speed without provoking opportunity attacks. Until the end of your turn, your next Ignite or melee attack deals extra Fire damage equal to your Proficiency Bonus. This movement may leap across gaps but does not grant flight. #### Searing Brand - Ignite Augment Cost: +1 CP When Ignite hits, deepen the Burn. Until the start of your next turn: Burn damage becomes 1d6 + Proficiency Bonus; the target cannot benefit from ordinary invisibility against you because the flame outlines it; if the target uses its Action to extinguish the Burn, it takes Fire damage equal to your Proficiency Bonus. #### Hungry Flame - Ignite Augment Cost: +1 CP When Ignite hits a Kindled target, deal extra Fire damage: | Cultivation Level | Extra Damage | | --- | --- | | 1-10 | 1d6 | | 11-16 | 2d6 | | 17-20 | 3d6 | If this damage reduces a creature to 0 HP or destroys an object, create one 5-foot square of Fire Terrain in its space until the start of your next turn. #### Heat Haze - Conflagration Talent Cost: 1 CP Heat distortion fills the Conflagration. Creatures inside are Lightly Obscured. Ranged attacks passing through the area have Disadvantage unless the attacker can see through heat distortion or does not rely on sight. This does not hide creatures from tremorsense, blindsight, or similar senses. #### Banked Ember - Unique Fire Talent Action Type: Action Factory Combat Bucket: action Factory Routing: combat_action_row Range: Touch Duration: 1 hour Cost: 1 CP Place a dormant ember into one object, weapon, torch, campfire, brazier, or willing creature. As a Bonus Action while within 60 feet, cause the ember to flare. Choose one: ignite an unattended flammable object; cause the bearer’s next attack before the end of its turn to deal extra Fire damage equal to your Proficiency Bonus; create Bright Light in a 20-foot radius and Dim Light for another 20 feet for 1 minute; apply Burn to one creature touching the ember-bearing object. You may maintain a number of Banked Embers equal to your Proficiency Bonus. ### FOUNDATION REALM FIRE TALENTS #### Fireball Art - Unique Fire Talent Prerequisite: CL 5+ Action Type: Action Factory Combat Bucket: action Factory Routing: combat_action_row Range: 120 feet Area: 20-foot-radius sphere Cost: 5 CP A compressed fire pearl erupts. Creatures inside make Dexterity saving throws. Failed Save: Take Fire damage and become Burning. Successful Save: Take half damage. | Cultivation Level | Damage | | --- | --- | | 5-10 | 6d6 | | 11-16 | 8d6 | | 17-20 | 10d6 | Unattended flammable objects ignite. ##### Overheat - Fireball Art Augment - 2 CP: Increase damage by 2d6. After the attack resolves, take Fire damage equal to twice your Proficiency Bonus. #### Scorching Ray Art - Unique Fire Talent Prerequisite: CL 5+ Action Type: Action Factory Combat Bucket: action Factory Routing: combat_action_row Range: 90 feet Cost: 4 CP Create three rays of fire. Make a ranged Cultivation Attack for each ray. Each hit deals: 2d6 Fire damage At CL 11, create four rays. At CL 17, create five rays. A creature hit by two or more rays becomes Burning. ##### Overheat - Scorching Ray Art Augment - 1 CP: Create one additional ray. After all rays resolve, take Fire damage equal to your Proficiency Bonus. #### Explosive Combustion - Ignite Augment Prerequisite: CL 5+ Cost: +3 CP When Ignite hits, the target erupts. Creatures other than the target within 10 feet make Dexterity saving throws. Failed Save: Take Fire damage. Successful Save: Take half damage. | Cultivation Level | Splash Damage | | --- | --- | | 5-10 | 3d6 | | 11-16 | 5d6 | | 17-20 | 7d6 | The original target takes Ignite damage normally. #### Blazing Armor - Unique Fire Talent Prerequisite: CL 5+ Action Type: Bonus Action Factory Combat Bucket: bonus_action Factory Routing: combat_action_row Duration: Concentration, up to 1 minute Cost: 3 CP Wrap yourself or one willing creature within touch in defensive flame. For the duration: gain Resistance to Fire damage; hostile creatures that hit the bearer with a melee attack take Fire damage equal to 1d8 + your Path key ability modifier; the bearer sheds Bright Light in a 10-foot radius and Dim Light for another 10 feet; the bearer gains Advantage on saving throws against extreme cold. #### White-Hot Focus - Overheat Talent Prerequisite: CL 5+ Action Type: Bonus Action Factory Combat Bucket: bonus_action Factory Routing: combat_action_row Duration: Until the end of your turn Cost: 2 CP The next Fire talent you use this turn gains one: Advantage on one attack roll; one target has Disadvantage on its saving throw; add your Path key ability modifier to one Fire damage roll; ignore Resistance to Fire damage for one target. After the talent resolves, take Fire damage equal to your Proficiency Bonus. White-Hot Focus cannot ignore Immunity. #### Wildfire Trail - Conflagration Talent Prerequisite: CL 5+ Cost: 3 CP When you create Conflagration, choose up to six connected 5-foot spaces extending from its edge. Those spaces become Fire Terrain until the start of your next turn. As a Bonus Action on later turns, extend the trail by up to three connected 5-foot spaces. Wildfire Trail cannot spread through sealed barriers, vacuum, or areas that cannot support flame unless the Fire is explicitly spiritual. #### Burn Through - Unique Fire Talent Prerequisite: CL 5+ Action Type: Action Factory Combat Bucket: action Factory Routing: combat_action_row Range: Touch Cost: 3 CP Choose one object, Barrier, structure section, sealed door, ice wall, vine wall, or unattended obstacle. Deal Fire damage: | Cultivation Level | Damage | | --- | --- | | 5-10 | 5d10 | | 11-16 | 7d10 | | 17-20 | 9d10 | This damage ignores an ordinary object’s Damage Threshold. It must still affect the object’s AC and reduce its HP. If Burn Through destroys the target, creatures within 5 feet of the breach make Dexterity saving throws. Failed Save: Take Fire damage equal to your Proficiency Bonus and become Burning. Successful Save: No effect. Successful Save: Take half damage. | Cultivation Level | Damage | | --- | --- | | 10-16 | 8d8 | | 17-20 | 10d8 | Incinerating Lance ignores Resistance to Fire damage for one creature of your choice in the line. ##### Overheat - Incinerating Lance Augment - 2 CP: The line becomes 10 feet wide and damage increases by 2d8.
