spheres.full_exact_source_text: # Sphere of Glass Qi Expression: Primary — Glass Qi; Supporting — Fire-Refined Sand Qi, Reflection Qi, Fragile-Clarity Qi. “A dull wall says no. A clear pane asks whether your force understands the line it is about to cross.” Sphere Type: Power Sphere / Boundary Sphere Primary Paths: Body Refining, Qi Cultivation, and Spirit Awakening Resource: CP unless a feature says otherwiseCore Mechanic: Glass Surfaces, Faultline Marks, and Refraction ResponsesCommon Expressions: glass-bone skin, transparent guards, lenses, panes, visible faultlines, refraction, brittle counters, glass roads, shattering consequence, mirror-bright witnesses Glass is the cultivation of the visible boundary and the flaw revealed by pressure. Stone hides its inner grain until it breaks. Water yields before the blow can be judged. Ice catches motion in a lattice. Force answers impact with pressure. Glass does something stranger. It makes the boundary visible. It lets the enemy see what they wish to cross. Then, when force arrives, Glass shows where the world was already weak. A Glass cultivator does not merely make glass objects. A Glass cultivator cultivates the moment when pressure meets a clear line and reveals the fault that was always waiting. The Sphere of Glass governs: transparent boundaries; faultline reading; contact surfaces; glass-bone reinforcement; lenses and angles; refraction; brittle counters; shattering consequence; visible warnings; truth seen through a dangerous line; the difference between seeing through a boundary and being able to pass it safely. #### Sphere Sentence Glass cultivators refine transparent faultlines into the body or a claimed surface, reveal where force will break, and answer pressure by refracting or shattering the line. ### Sphere Boundaries Glass is not a generic barrier, object-creation, cold, mirror, or cutting sphere. Glass overlaps with nearby spheres only where its own chassis is present. Glass and Ice. Ice imposes crystalline order on motion through Frost Lattices and Fracture Marks. Glass makes a transparent boundary visible and reveals where pressure breaks. Glass and Force. Force answers impact with pressure, anchors, and counterpressure. Glass lets impact cross or strike a visible line, then bends or breaks the consequence along a faultline. Glass and Protection. Protection creates stable wards and defenses. Glass creates brittle, visible, conditional boundaries whose weakness is part of their power. Glass and Creation. Creation makes objects broadly. Glass does not own all object creation. Glass creates, claims, or transforms surfaces only to support transparent boundaries, refraction, and faultlines. Glass and Illusion. Illusion plants false premises. Glass is real and visible. A Glass surface may deceive through angle, glare, and refraction, but it is not a false image unless combined with Illusion. Glass and Mirror. If Mirror exists as its own sphere, Mirror governs identity, doubled selves, and reciprocal reflection. Glass governs transparent boundary, lens, pane, and visible fault. Glass and Body Refining. Body Refining Glass begins with the body as the pane. It does not project free-floating glass by default. ### Using This Sphere Except where a Glass feature explicitly says otherwise, ordinary Fifth Edition rules remain in force. Glass talents supplement the normal rules for: Armor Class; Cover; objects and object damage; line of sight; line of effect; Opportunity Attacks; Concentration; Hide and Invisible; Blinded; attack rolls; Dexterity saving throws; difficult terrain; falling; forced movement. A Glass talent changes a base rule only when it explicitly says so. ### Core Glass Rules #### Glass Is Real, Not Illusory Glass created or tempered by this sphere is real supernatural glass or a glass-like cultivated surface. Unless a talent says otherwise: Glass can be damaged; Glass may provide Cover if it physically blocks an attack line; Glass is transparent and does not block ordinary line of sight; Glass does not automatically block teleportation, planar travel, possession, gaze effects, or purely spiritual techniques; Glass does not hide creatures by itself; Glass does not create false images; Glass does not become a general-purpose construction material unless a talent says so. #### Glass Surfaces A Glass Surface is the legal surface through which your Glass talents operate. When you use a Glass feature, choose one Glass Surface permitted by that feature. Unless a talent, Path synergy, Insight, forged technique, or Realm evolution says otherwise, you may choose only one of the following: your own body; armor, clothing, or jewelry you are wearing; a weapon, shield, or object you are holding; a creature, object, wall, floor, door, barrier, or other solid surface you touch; an existing glass object, mirror, window, crystal, or pane within reach. By default, you cannot create a free-floating Glass Surface at range. #### Projected Glass Some talents have the Projected tag. A Projected talent can create a Glass Surface away from your body or beyond reach, such as a floating pane, suspended lens, glass road, or distant refraction point. A Body Refining cultivator cannot learn a Projected Glass talent unless one of the following explicitly permits external projection: a Cultivation Insight; a Path feature; a forged technique; a Realm evolution; a GM-granted breakthrough; a talent that specifically says Body Refining cultivators may learn it. If a Body Refiner would gain a Projected talent before gaining permission to project Glass outside the body, the talent remains dormant or must be retrained, as the GM decides. This restriction does not prevent a Body Refiner from using Glass through their own body, held objects, worn armor, touch, or surfaces they physically contact. #### Temper Glass Surface Action Type: Bonus Action Factory Combat Bucket: bonus_action Factory Routing: combat_action_row Range: Self, touch, or a held object Duration: 1 minute Cost: 0 CP Choose one legal Glass Surface: your body, worn armor, held weapon, held shield, held object, or a solid surface you are touching. Until the effect ends, the chosen surface becomes tempered by Glass cultivation. It may become transparent, crystalline, mirror-bright, veined with clear faultlines, or visibly glass-boned, as appropriate to the surface. A tempered surface is the anchor for your Faultline Marks and Refraction Responses. You may maintain one tempered Glass Surface at a time. This increases to two at CL 5, three at CL 11, and four at CL 17. If you temper your own body, this does not make you fragile by itself. Specific talents may create brittle benefits or risks. #### Faultline Strike Action Type: Action Factory Combat Bucket: action Factory Routing: combat_action_row Range: Melee or thrown/weapon range if using a held weapon or thrown shard talent Target: One creature or object Cost: 0 CP Make a melee Cultivation Attack, unarmed strike, weapon attack, or attack with a held object that is currently a tempered Glass Surface. On a hit, the attack deals its normal damage. You may choose for the damage to be Slashing or Piercing if the attack used a glass edge, shard, or crystalline strike. The target also gains a Faultline Mark. If you use your own body as the Glass Surface, this can be an unarmed strike or natural-body impact. It does not require external projection. #### Glass Shard Action Type: Action Factory Combat Bucket: action Factory Routing: combat_action_row Range: 30 feet Target: One creature or object Cost: 0 CP You break a shard from a legal Glass Surface you are touching or holding and throw it as a ranged Cultivation Attack. On a hit, the target takes 1d8 Piercing or Slashing damage and gains a Faultline Mark. The damage increases to 2d8 at CL 5, 3d8 at CL 11, and 4d8 at CL 17. Glass Shard does not create glass at range. It uses glass you have already tempered, touched, held, or cultivated into your body. A Body Refiner may use Glass Shard by casting off a shard from their glass-bone skin, armor, held weapon, or other legal surface. This is painful but not automatically damaging unless a talent says otherwise. #### Faultline Marks A Faultline Mark is the moment when pressure reveals where a line wants to break. You can have a number of Faultline Marks active at one time equal to your Proficiency Bonus. When you would create a Faultline Mark beyond this limit, choose one existing mark to end. A Faultline Mark lasts until the end of your next turn unless a talent says otherwise. You may place a Faultline Mark when one of the following happens: your Faultline Strike hits; your Glass Shard hits; a creature damages your tempered Glass Surface; a creature attacks you while your body, armor, or shield is your tempered Glass Surface; a creature attacks through, across, or against a Glass Surface you created or tempered; a creature willingly moves across Shattered Glass Terrain you created; a creature touches, breaks, or relies on a Glass Surface you control; a talent explicitly places a Faultline Mark. #### Refraction Responses When a creature, object, attack line, or Glass Surface with a Faultline Mark is involved in a triggering event, you may spend the mark to use one Refraction Response you know. Unless a talent says otherwise, you may use only one Refraction Response per triggering event. You know the following Refraction Responses when you learn Glass. ##### Turn the Angle Trigger: A marked creature hits you or an ally within 5 feet of one of your tempered Glass Surfaces. Reduce the triggering damage by 1d8 + your Proficiency Bonus. At CL 5, reduce it by 2d8 + your Proficiency Bonus. At CL 11, reduce it by 3d8 + your Proficiency Bonus. At CL 17, reduce it by 4d8 + your Proficiency Bonus. If this reduces the damage to 0, the attacker cannot make Opportunity Attacks until the start of its next turn. ##### Visible Crack Trigger: A marked creature attempts to Hide, become Invisible, benefit from Cover, or conceal the origin of an attack or technique. Until the start of your next turn, you and allies who can see one of your Glass Surfaces know the marked creature’s space, even if the creature is Invisible or hidden. This does not reveal a creature through Total Cover unless the Glass Surface also has line of sight to the creature. ##### Bitter Edge Trigger: A marked creature willingly moves 5 feet or more. The creature takes Slashing damage equal to your Proficiency Bonus and its Speed is reduced by 10 feet until the end of the current turn. At CL 11+, you may also make the first square of movement through your adjacent space or your Glass Surface count as difficult terrain. ##### Shatter Warning Trigger: A marked creature makes an attack roll through or against one of your Glass Surfaces. Impose a -2 penalty on the triggering attack roll. If the attack misses, the marked creature takes Piercing damage equal to your Proficiency Bonus. ##### Refracted Step Trigger: You spend a Faultline Mark on a creature within 5 feet of you or your tempered Glass Surface. Move 5 feet without provoking Opportunity Attacks from the marked creature. At CL 5, move 10 feet. At CL 11, move 15 feet. At CL 17, move 20 feet. ##### Break the Line Trigger: A marked object, barrier, weapon, shield, door, or Glass Surface takes damage. Add your Proficiency Bonus to the damage dealt to that object or surface. If the object is reduced to 0 HP, choose one creature within 5 feet of it. That creature takes Slashing damage equal to your Proficiency Bonus. #### Shattered Glass Terrain Some talents create Shattered Glass Terrain. Shattered Glass Terrain is difficult terrain. The first time a creature willingly moves through a 5-foot square of your Shattered Glass Terrain on a turn, it takes Slashing damage equal to your Proficiency Bonus. A creature can avoid this damage by moving at half speed through that square. Shattered Glass Terrain normally lasts until the end of your next turn unless a talent says otherwise. ## MORTAL REALM GLASS TALENTS ### Glass-Bone Guard Your body may serve as your primary Glass Surface. When you use Temper Glass Surface on your own body, choose one benefit until the effect ends: gain +1 AC while not wearing heavy armor; reduce the first Bludgeoning, Piercing, or Slashing damage you take each round by your Proficiency Bonus; when a creature hits you with a melee attack, place a Faultline Mark on that creature. This talent does not create glass outside your body. ### Held-Pane Method When you temper a shield, weapon, fan, staff, sleeve-weight, bracelet, ring, bowl, or other held object, it can serve as a Glass Surface for your Refraction Responses. While holding the tempered object: you may place a Faultline Mark on a creature that misses you with a melee attack; you may use Turn the Angle on yourself even if the marked creature is not adjacent to another Glass Surface; if the object is a shield, its transparent edge may provide the same Cover it normally would without blocking line of sight. ### Contact Pane Action Type: Action Factory Combat Bucket: action Factory Routing: combat_action_row Range: Touch Duration: Concentration, up to 1 minute Cost: 1 CP Touch a solid surface no larger than a 5-foot square or one Medium or smaller object. The touched surface becomes a Glass Surface. It remains in place and keeps its original size and shape. If a creature breaks, opens, crosses, strikes through, or relies on the surface for Cover, you may place a Faultline Mark on that creature. Contact Pane does not create a free-floating pane. It changes the behavior of a surface you physically touch. ### Raised Pane Scripture - Projected Prerequisite: Qi Cultivation, Spirit Awakening, or external-projection permission Action Type: Action Factory Combat Bucket: action Factory Routing: combat_action_row Range: 60 feet Duration: Concentration, up to 1 minute Cost: 1 CP Create one transparent Glass Pane in an unoccupied space you can see within range. The pane is a 5-foot-by-5-foot square. It must be vertical, horizontal, or angled, and must be anchored to a solid surface or another Glass Pane. The pane has: AC equal to 12 + your Proficiency Bonus; HP equal to 5 x your CL; immunity to Poison and Psychic damage; vulnerability to Thunder damage. When reduced to 0 HP, the pane shatters and creates Shattered Glass Terrain in its space until the end of your next turn. At CL 5, create two connected panes. At CL 11, create three connected panes. At CL 17, create four connected panes. ### Lens of the Honest Crack Action Type: Bonus Action Factory Combat Bucket: bonus_action Factory Routing: combat_action_row Range: 60 feet Target: One creature you can see through a Glass Surface Cost: 0 CP Study the target through a tempered Glass Surface. Until the start of your next turn, the first time the target makes an attack roll, casts a spell, spends CP, activates a supernatural feature, or attempts to Hide, you may place a Faultline Mark on it. ### Polished Warning When a creature you can see targets you with an attack, you may use your Reaction to angle a tempered Glass Surface. Gain +2 AC against the triggering attack. If the attack misses, place a Faultline Mark on the attacker. If you do not have a legal Glass Surface, you cannot use this talent. ### Shard Needle When you use Glass Shard, increase its normal range to 60 feet if the shard comes from a held, worn, or touched Glass Surface. If you are a Body Refiner using your own body as the source, you may keep the range at 30 feet and add your Constitution modifier to one damage roll from Glass Shard once per turn. ### Careful Feet on Broken Light You ignore difficult terrain from Shattered Glass Terrain you created. When you move through Shattered Glass Terrain you created, choose one creature that can see you. Until the start of your next turn, you have Advantage on the next Dexterity (Acrobatics) check or Dexterity saving throw you make against that creature’s effect. ### Mirror-Bright Witness When a creature with a Faultline Mark hits a creature other than you with an attack, you may use your Reaction to make the mark flare visibly. The attacked creature gains +2 AC against the triggering attack. If the attack misses, the marked creature cannot take Reactions until the start of its next turn. ### Clean Break When you reduce a Glass Surface, fragile object, mirror, window, crystal, or mundane glass item to 0 HP, choose one: create Shattered Glass Terrain in one 5-foot square adjacent to it; place a Faultline Mark on one creature within 5 feet of it; move 5 feet without provoking Opportunity Attacks from one creature that saw it break. ### Transparent Defense When you benefit from Cover granted by a transparent Glass Surface, you may still draw line of sight through that surface for your Glass talents. This does not let you draw line of effect through a surface that physically blocks the effect. ## FOUNDATION REALM GLASS TALENTS ### Walking Pane Body Prerequisite: Glass-Bone Guard, CL 5+ When your body is your tempered Glass Surface, you may maintain two Glass-Bone Guard benefits at once. In addition, once per round when a creature hits you with a melee attack, you may place a Faultline Mark on that creature without using your Reaction. If you spend that mark before the end of your next turn, gain Temporary HP equal to your Proficiency Bonus. ### Pane-Step Projection - Projected Prerequisite: Raised Pane Scripture, CL 5+ When you create a projected Glass Pane, you may create it within 10 feet of you without anchoring it to a solid surface. The pane collapses at the end of your next turn unless it becomes anchored before then. A Body Refining cultivator may learn this talent only if they have external-projection permission. ### Faultline Transfer Prerequisite: CL 5+ When you spend a Faultline Mark, you may move one different Faultline Mark from a creature within 30 feet to another creature, object, or Glass Surface within 5 feet of the original target. Use Faultline Transfer once per round. ### Prism Step Prerequisite: CL 5+ When you use Refracted Step, you may move through a space occupied by one willing ally or through one space adjacent to a Glass Surface you control without treating that space as difficult terrain. At the end of this movement, choose one creature you moved away from. That creature has Disadvantage on the next Opportunity Attack it makes before the start of your next turn. ### Lens of Stored Pressure Prerequisite: CL 5+ When you reduce damage with Turn the Angle, store part of the pressure in a legal Glass Surface. The next time before the end of your next turn that you hit with Faultline Strike or Glass Shard, add damage equal to your Proficiency Bonus. At CL 11+, add 1d8 + your Proficiency Bonus instead. ### Wall-Touch Scripture Prerequisite: Contact Pane, CL 5+ When you use Contact Pane, you may affect a continuous surface up to two 5-foot squares. At CL 11, this increases to three squares. At CL 17, this increases to four squares. A creature that willingly crosses a Contact Pane surface may gain a Faultline Mark even if it does not damage the surface. ### Refraction of the Obvious Blow Prerequisite: CL 7+ When a marked creature misses you with an attack roll, use one Refraction Response that targets that creature without spending your Reaction. Use Refraction of the Obvious Blow once per round. ### Hidden Crack Study Prerequisite: CL 7+ When you take the Study action to examine a creature, object, barrier, Formation, or supernatural effect through a Glass Surface, add your Proficiency Bonus to the check if it is not already included. On a success, place a Faultline Mark on the studied target or on one relevant object or surface connected to it. This reveals structural or tactical weakness, not private thoughts. ### Glass Road - Projected Prerequisite: Raised Pane Scripture, CL 7+ Action Type: Action Factory Combat Bucket: action Factory Routing: combat_action_row Range: 30 feet Duration: Concentration, up to 1 minute Cost: 2 CP Create a narrow transparent road of glass panels across open space, water, mud, broken ground, or a gap. The road can be up to 30 feet long and 5 feet wide. It must begin from a solid surface within range. Creatures may move across it normally. When a hostile creature willingly moves across the road, you may place a Faultline Mark on it once per turn. If the road is reduced to 0 HP or you dismiss it, creatures standing on it fall unless they have another legal support. A Body Refining cultivator may learn this talent only with external-projection permission. ## CORE FORMATION REALM GLASS TALENTS ### Glass Domain: Court of Visible Faults “Every pane showed a different angle. Every angle agreed on where the enemy was already broken.” Prerequisite: CL 10+ Action Type: Action Factory Combat Bucket: action Factory Routing: combat_action_row Area: 30-foot Emanation originating from you Duration: Concentration, up to 1 minute Cost: 4 CP Use Limit: Once per short rest Create a court of visible faultlines around yourself. For the duration: your body counts as a tempered Glass Surface; each ally inside may treat their worn armor, held weapon, or held shield as a Glass Surface for your Glass talents; the first time each round that a hostile creature inside damages an ally, crosses a Glass Surface, attacks through a Glass Surface, or damages a Glass Surface, you may place a Faultline Mark on that creature; once per round, you may use a Refraction Response without spending your Reaction; Shattered Glass Terrain you create inside the Domain lasts until the Domain ends. If you are a Body Refiner, this Domain manifests as glass-bone pressure radiating from your stance and contact points. It does not require you to create free-floating panes. ### Living Pane Sutra Prerequisite: Walking Pane Body, CL 10+ When your body is a tempered Glass Surface, gain the following benefits: Resistance to Slashing damage; Advantage on saving throws against being Blinded; when a creature scores a critical hit against you, place two Faultline Marks on that creature instead of one. Once per short rest, when you would be reduced to 0 HP but not killed outright, you may shatter your outer glass-bone shell and drop to 1 HP instead. When you do, create Shattered Glass Terrain in each space adjacent to you. ### Ten-Angle Refraction Prerequisite: CL 10+ When you spend a Faultline Mark, choose one ally within 30 feet who can see a Glass Surface you control. That ally may move 5 feet without provoking Opportunity Attacks from the marked creature. If the ally ends this movement behind Cover, holding a Glass Surface, or adjacent to Shattered Glass Terrain you created, the ally gains Temporary HP equal to your Proficiency Bonus. ### Spell-Line Crack Prerequisite: Hidden Crack Study, CL 10+ When a marked creature casts a spell, spends CP, or activates a supernatural feature while you can see it through a Glass Surface, use your Reaction and spend the mark. The creature makes a Wisdom saving throw. Failed Save: Choose one: reduce the damage of the triggering effect by 2d8 + your Proficiency Bonus against one target; one target of the effect gains Advantage on one saving throw against it; if the effect requires Concentration, the creature has Disadvantage on the first Constitution saving throw it makes to maintain that Concentration before the end of its next turn. Successful Save: The triggering creature cannot take Reactions until the start of its next turn. Spell-Line Crack does not cancel the triggering effect. ### Palace Lens Array - Projected Prerequisite: Raised Pane Scripture, CL 10+ When you create projected Glass Panes, you may arrange them as lenses rather than barriers. Choose one lens benefit when you create them: allies looking through the lenses ignore Half Cover from nonmagical objects; hostile creatures attacking through the lenses take a -2 penalty on the first attack roll each turn; a creature that teleports into or out of a space adjacent to a lens gains a Faultline Mark; invisible creatures adjacent to a lens leave visible distortions until the start of your next turn. A Body Refining cultivator may learn this talent only with external-projection permission. ### Break the Proud Weapon Prerequisite: CL 12+ When a marked creature hits with a weapon attack, you may use your Reaction and spend the mark. The creature makes a Strength saving throw. Failed Save: The weapon, natural weapon, or striking limb is fractured by clear lines until the start of your next turn. The attack still resolves, but the marked creature has Disadvantage on the next attack roll it makes with the same weapon or limb before the effect ends. If the attack was made with a nonmagical object or mundane weapon, also apply Break the Line to the weapon. Successful Save: Reduce the triggering damage by your Proficiency Bonus. ### Mirror-Clear Testimony Prerequisite: CL 12+ When a creature lies, hides a hostile action, or conceals the origin of an attack while reflected in or seen through one of your Glass Surfaces, you may force the surface to remember the contradiction. For the next hour, a creature studying that Glass Surface with a successful Intelligence (Investigation), Wisdom (Insight), or relevant Cultivation check against your Glass Save DC can perceive a brief visual echo of the contradiction. This does not reveal private thoughts. It preserves visible or spiritually reflected inconsistency. ## NASCENT SOUL REALM GLASS TALENTS ### Incarnation of the Transparent Fault Prerequisite: CL 15+ Action Type: Bonus Action Factory Combat Bucket: bonus_action Factory Routing: combat_action_row Duration: 1 minute Cost: 6 CP Use Limit: Once per long rest Your body, breath, meridians, and immediate surroundings become a single transparent faultline. For the duration: your body is always a tempered Glass Surface; you may maintain two additional tempered Glass Surfaces beyond your normal limit; when a hostile creature within 30 feet hits you or an ally, place a Faultline Mark on it; once per round, use one Refraction Response without spending a Reaction; when you spend a Faultline Mark, choose one creature within 30 feet. That creature either gains Temporary HP equal to your Proficiency Bonus or takes Slashing damage equal to your Proficiency Bonus; you have Resistance to Slashing and Piercing damage; you cannot be Blinded while you are conscious. This Incarnation does not automatically create free-floating panes. A Body Refiner remains a living pane unless another feature permits projection. ### Thousand-Pane Palace - Projected Prerequisite: Palace Lens Array, CL 15+ Action Type: Action Factory Combat Bucket: action Factory Routing: combat_action_row Range: 120 feet Area: Up to ten 5-foot panes arranged within range Duration: Concentration, up to 1 minute Cost: 6 CP Use Limit: Once per long rest Create a palace of suspended transparent panes, lenses, and angular roads. For the duration: each pane is a Glass Surface; hostile creatures that move through a space adjacent to two or more panes gain a Faultline Mark, once per turn; allies adjacent to a pane gain Half Cover against ranged attacks; you may use Refracted Step from one pane to another pane within 30 feet of it; when one pane breaks, create Shattered Glass Terrain in its space until the effect ends. A Body Refining cultivator may learn this talent only with external-projection permission. ### Flaw Within the Golden Technique Prerequisite: Spell-Line Crack, CL 15+ When a creature with a Faultline Mark uses a Domain, Realm Evolution, major forged technique, or other high-cost supernatural feature within 60 feet, use your Reaction and spend the mark. The creature makes a Wisdom saving throw. Failed Save: Choose one: reduce the triggering effect’s damage against all targets by 4d8; one ally affected by the triggering effect automatically succeeds on one saving throw against it; reduce the triggering effect’s duration by 1 round, minimum 1 round; the creature cannot use the same feature again until the end of its next turn. Successful Save: One ally affected by the triggering effect gains Resistance to one damage type dealt by the effect until the end of the current turn. Flaw Within the Golden Technique does not affect Secret Inheritances unless the GM says the inheritance has already exposed a visible faultline. ### Glass Coffin Without Death Prerequisite: CL 15+ Action Type: Action Factory Combat Bucket: action Factory Routing: combat_action_row Range: Touch Target: One willing, unconscious, Petrified, dying, cursed, poisoned, diseased, or spiritually unstable creature Duration: 24 hours Cost: 5 CP Encase the target in a transparent preservation shell. While encased: the target is Incapacitated and has Total Cover; the shell has AC 15 + your Proficiency Bonus and HP 10 x your CL; poison, disease, bleeding, ordinary decay, and ongoing environmental exposure do not worsen; the target does not need to breathe; hostile creatures can see the target clearly, but cannot touch the target without breaking the shell. You may end the shell as an Action while touching it. Glass Coffin Without Death preserves a state. It does not heal the target by itself. ## SECRET GLASS INHERITANCE ### Heaven Reveals the Single Faultline “The cultivator lifted one finger. Every pane in the world agreed where the impossible technique was already cracked.” Classification: Secret Glass Inheritance Prerequisite: CL 17+, Glass Domain: Court of Visible Faults, hidden glass scripture or equivalent inheritance Action Type: Reaction Factory Combat Bucket: reaction Factory Routing: combat_action_row Trigger: A creature you can see within 120 feet declares an attack, spell, sphere talent, Domain, Realm Evolution, Secret Inheritance, or other supernatural technique Cost: 8 CP Use Limit: Once per week Before the triggering effect resolves, choose one visible or spiritually perceptible faultline in the declared action. The triggering creature makes a Wisdom saving throw. Failed Save: Choose one: split the effect: one target of your choice is unaffected by it; refract the effect: choose one legal target within 30 feet of the original target to suffer half of the effect’s damage or consequence instead; shatter the effect’s path: reduce all damage dealt by the triggering effect by half; expose the technique: the triggering creature loses all benefits of Invisible, Hidden, or unseen-origin effects until the end of your next turn, and every enemy who can see it may place one narrative or tactical question to the GM about the technique’s visible weakness. Successful Save: The triggering effect resolves normally, but the creature gains three Faultline Marks. These marks can exceed your normal limit and last until the end of your next turn. This inheritance does not make Glass a universal counterspell. It works only because the declared action exposed a line, target, path, boundary, or contradiction that Glass can reveal. ## GLASS DRAWBACKS AND VARIANT SCRIPTURES Glass variants are optional cultivation scriptures that change how the sphere manifests. They are Tianxia-specific design tools inspired by drawback design, not imported casting-tradition rules. A Glass variant should grant a real benefit only if it also gives a real limitation. Unless the GM says otherwise: choose at most one Glass variant when first learning Glass or during a major Glass initiation; Glass variants are mutually exclusive; if a variant grants a bonus talent whose prerequisites you do not yet meet, you gain it when you meet those prerequisites; if you retrain or remove the drawback, you lose the bonus talent or benefit it granted. ### Glass-Bone Scripture You cultivate Glass through your own bones, skin, stance, and impact lines. You gain Glass-Bone Guard as a bonus talent. When your own body is your tempered Glass Surface, increase the damage reduction from Glass-Bone Guard by 1. #### Drawback: No Distant Pane You cannot learn Projected Glass talents unless a separate Cultivation Insight, forged technique, or major breakthrough explicitly permits external projection. Even if you later gain projection permission, your Projected Glass effects cost 1 additional CP unless they originate from your body, a held object, or a surface you are touching. ### Lens-Seer Scripture You cultivate Glass as perception rather than construction. You gain Lens of the Honest Crack as a bonus talent. When you take the Study action through a Glass Surface, treat a d20 roll of 9 or lower as a 10 once per short rest. #### Drawback: Must See the Line You cannot place a Faultline Mark on a creature you cannot see, that is behind Total Cover from all your Glass Surfaces, or whose action has no visible, reflected, or spiritually perceptible line. Your Glass talents do not help against a purely hidden source unless you first establish a Glass Surface that can witness it. ### Shard-Cutter Scripture You cultivate Glass as edge, wound, and decisive fracture. You gain Shard Needle as a bonus talent. Once per turn when you hit a creature with Glass Shard or Faultline Strike, add your Proficiency Bonus to the damage if the target already has a Faultline Mark. #### Drawback: Brittle Mercy Your Glass resists nonlethal expression. When you use a Glass talent to deal damage to a creature, you cannot choose to make that damage nonlethal unless you spend 1 CP. In addition, when you critically fail an attack roll with Glass Shard or Faultline Strike, one Glass Surface you control shatters, if any are available. ### Architect of Panes Scripture - Projected You cultivate Glass as projected boundary and crystalline architecture. You gain Raised Pane Scripture as a bonus talent. When you create projected panes, increase one pane’s HP by 2 x your Proficiency Bonus. #### Drawback: Rooted Pane Law Your projected panes must be anchored to a solid surface, an existing structure, another pane, or a Formation anchor. You cannot create free-floating panes unless a higher-Realm talent explicitly allows it. If all anchors for a projected pane are destroyed or moved beyond range, the pane shatters at the end of the current turn. Body Refining cultivators cannot choose this variant unless they already have external-projection permission. ### Mirror-Bright Witness Scripture You cultivate Glass as testimony, reflection, and public exposure. You gain Mirror-Bright Witness as a bonus talent. When a marked creature damages a creature other than you, you may use Mirror-Bright Witness without spending your Reaction once per short rest. #### Drawback: Witness Cannot Be Hidden When you use a Glass talent that places or spends a Faultline Mark, your Glass Surface visibly flashes, rings, reflects, or cracks. Until the start of your next turn, creatures that can see the surface know you are the source of the Glass effect. You cannot use Glass to conceal the origin of your own Glass talents unless another feature explicitly says so. ## PATH SYNERGIES ### Body Refining - Glass-Bone Body Body Refining is the natural path for internal Glass. Use Constitution as your Glass key ability if higher than the normal key ability. When your own body is your tempered Glass Surface: add your Constitution modifier to Glass Shard damage once per turn if the shard comes from your body; when you use Turn the Angle on damage dealt to yourself, gain Temporary HP equal to your Proficiency Bonus; at CL 10+, your unarmed strikes may count as tempered Glass Surfaces for Faultline Strike while Temper Glass Surface is active on your body. Body Refining Glass does not grant external projection by itself. ### Qi Cultivation - Projected Lens Method Qi Cultivation is the natural path for projected panes, lenses, glass roads, and palace arrays. Use Intelligence or Charisma as your Glass key ability. When you use a Projected Glass talent: reduce its CP cost by 1, minimum 0, once per turn; increase its range by 30 feet; at CL 10+, when a projected pane shatters, place a Faultline Mark on one creature within 5 feet of it. ### Spirit Awakening - Faultline Witness Spirit Awakening is the natural path for seeing cracks in intention, vows, emotions, and supernatural motion. Use Wisdom as your Glass key ability if higher. When you use Lens of the Honest Crack or Hidden Crack Study: you may ask whether the target is currently relying more on force, deception, fear, pride, duty, or desperation; once per round when a creature you have marked fails a saving throw, regain 1 CP, up to your normal maximum; at CL 10+, you may place a Faultline Mark on a creature that begins a hostile supernatural effect while reflected in a Glass Surface you control, even if the effect does not physically cross the surface. ## CULTIVATION INSIGHTS ### External Pane Breakthrough Prerequisite: Body Refining Path, Glass sphere, CL 5+ You have learned to project a narrow thread of glass qi outside the body without abandoning the Body Refining path. You may learn Projected Glass talents. However, when you use a Projected Glass talent, choose one: spend 1 additional CP; take damage equal to your Proficiency Bonus that cannot be reduced; the projected pane must remain within 10 feet of you. This Insight represents a major evolution and should not be assumed for all Body Refiners. ### Glass-Bone Adept Prerequisite: Glass sphere, Glass-Bone Guard, CL 4+ When your body is your tempered Glass Surface, gain one additional benefit: Advantage on saving throws against being pushed or knocked Prone; your unarmed strikes may deal Slashing damage; when a creature misses you with a melee attack, move 5 feet without provoking Opportunity Attacks from that creature. ### Lens-Reader Adept Prerequisite: Glass sphere, Lens of the Honest Crack, CL 6+ When you take the Study action through a Glass Surface, you may also learn one of the following: whether the target has Resistance or Immunity to Slashing damage; whether the target is currently concentrating; whether the target has used a Reaction since the start of its last turn; whether the target is protected by a barrier, ward, or Formation effect. ### Refraction Adept Prerequisite: Glass sphere, CL 8+ Once per short rest, when you spend a Faultline Mark, use two different Refraction Responses if both are legal for the same triggering event. ### Architect of Clear Roads Prerequisite: Glass sphere, Glass Road, CL 8+ When you create Glass Road, choose one: the road is 10 feet longer; allies do not provoke Opportunity Attacks from one creature of your choice while moving across it; the first hostile creature to move across it each round must make a Dexterity saving throw or fall Prone.

resolved_automatic_base_abilities.effect:
#### Refraction Responses
When a creature, object, attack line, or Glass Surface with a Faultline Mark is involved in a triggering event, you may spend the mark to use one Refraction Response you know.
Unless a talent says otherwise, you may use only one Refraction Response per triggering event.
You know the following Refraction Responses when you learn Glass.
##### Turn the Angle
Trigger: A marked creature hits you or an ally within 5 feet of one of your tempered Glass Surfaces.
Reduce the triggering damage by 1d8 + your Proficiency Bonus.
At CL 5, reduce it by 2d8 + your Proficiency Bonus. At CL 11, reduce it by 3d8 + your Proficiency Bonus. At CL 17, reduce it by 4d8 + your Proficiency Bonus.
If this reduces the damage to 0, the attacker cannot make Opportunity Attacks until the start of its next turn.
##### Visible Crack
Trigger: A marked creature attempts to Hide, become Invisible, benefit from Cover, or conceal the origin of an attack or technique.
Until the start of your next turn, you and allies who can see one of your Glass Surfaces know the marked creature’s space, even if the creature is Invisible or hidden.
This does not reveal a creature through Total Cover unless the Glass Surface also has line of sight to the creature.
##### Bitter Edge
Trigger: A marked creature willingly moves 5 feet or more.
The creature takes Slashing damage equal to your Proficiency Bonus and its Speed is reduced by 10 feet until the end of the current turn.
At CL 11+, you may also make the first square of movement through your adjacent space or your Glass Surface count as difficult terrain.
##### Shatter Warning
Trigger: A marked creature makes an attack roll through or against one of your Glass Surfaces.
Impose a -2 penalty on the triggering attack roll.
If the attack misses, the marked creature takes Piercing damage equal to your Proficiency Bonus.
##### Refracted Step
Trigger: You spend a Faultline Mark on a creature within 5 feet of you or your tempered Glass Surface.
Move 5 feet without provoking Opportunity Attacks from the marked creature.
At CL 5, move 10 feet. At CL 11, move 15 feet. At CL 17, move 20 feet.
##### Break the Line
Trigger: A marked object, barrier, weapon, shield, door, or Glass Surface takes damage.
Add your Proficiency Bonus to the damage dealt to that object or surface.
If the object is reduced to 0 HP, choose one creature within 5 feet of it. That creature takes Slashing damage equal to your Proficiency Bonus.

automatic_base_abilities.effect:
### Base Technique - External Weight Shift
Tag: Field Art.
Action Type: Action
Factory Combat Bucket: action
Factory Routing: combat_action_row
Range: 60 feet.
Duration: Concentration, up to 1 minute.
Cost: 1 CP or Stamina.
Choose one creature or object no larger than Large. If the target is willing, you may choose Body Lightening or Body Heavying for it. If the target is unwilling, choose Burden or Uplift.
Burden: The target makes a Strength saving throw. On a failed save, its Speed is reduced by 10 feet, its jump distance is halved, and it has Disadvantage on Strength (Athletics) and Dexterity (Acrobatics) checks. At the end of each of its turns, it repeats the save, ending the effect on itself on a success. On a successful initial save, its Speed is reduced by 10 feet until the start of its next turn.
Uplift: The target makes a Strength saving throw. On a failed save, its first movement on its next turn is unstable: it must spend 10 feet of movement to remain grounded, or it rises 10 feet upward and then falls at the end of the turn if nothing holds it aloft. On a successful save, it rises only 5 feet or may immediately fall Prone to avoid the rise.
Objects: The GM determines how increased or decreased weight affects doors, bridges, ropes, carts, armor, siege engines, or carried objects. Gravity does not automatically destroy objects without a talent that deals damage or causes structural stress.

automatic_base_abilities.effect:
### Base Ability - Weight Shift
Action Type: Bonus Action
Factory Combat Bucket: bonus_action
Factory Routing: combat_action_row
Range: Self.
Duration: Until the start of your next turn.
Cost: 0 for the basic self version.
Choose one mode: Body Lightening, Body Heavying, or Neutral Weight.
You may change modes only once on each of your turns unless a talent says otherwise. If you are Incapacitated, your Weight Shift becomes Neutral Weight.
#### Body Lightening
Until the start of your next turn, your body becomes lighter, quicker, and less bound to the ground.
Benefits:
Your Speed increases by 10 feet.
Your jump distance increases by a number of feet equal to 5 + your Proficiency Bonus.
You reduce any falling damage you take by an amount equal to 5 times your Proficiency Bonus.
You gain Advantage on Dexterity (Acrobatics) checks made to escape a Grapple or move across narrow, fragile, or unstable footing.
If you move at least 10 feet before making a melee attack on your turn, you may use your Gravity key ability in place of Strength or Dexterity for that attack roll if the weapon is an unarmed strike, simple melee weapon, monk-like martial implement, spear, sword, staff, or other GM-approved mobile martial weapon.
Body Lightening does not grant flight by itself.
#### Body Heavying
Until the start of your next turn, your body becomes denser, more rooted, and harder to displace.
Benefits:
Your Speed is reduced by 5 feet, to a minimum of 5 feet.
You count as one size larger when resisting Shove, Grapple, forced movement, and effects that would knock you Prone.
You gain Advantage on Strength checks and Strength saving throws made to resist forced movement or being knocked Prone.
Your carrying, dragging, lifting, and pushing capacity doubles.
If you do not move more than half your Speed on your turn, the first melee weapon attack or Unarmed Strike you hit with before the start of your next turn deals additional damage equal to your Proficiency Bonus. The damage type is the attack’s normal damage type, or Force if the attack is a supernatural Gravity technique.
Body Heavying does not increase your size and does not automatically increase weapon reach.
#### Neutral Weight
You return to normal weight. Ending Weight Shift early requires no action on your turn.

spheres.full_exact_source_text: # Sphere of Gravity Qi Expression: Primary — Weight Qi; Supporting — Earth Qi, Space Qi, Orbit/Relation Qi. Sphere Type: True Hybrid Sphere Primary Path: Body Refining or Qi Cultivation Secondary Path: Spirit Awakening through soul-weight, mandate-pressure, oath-gravity, or GM-approved spirit expression Resource: CP for external gravitic law; Stamina or Martial Focus only for internal body-heavying, body-lightening, or explicitly martial talents Core Chassis: Weight Shift, Spatial Awareness of down/anchor pressure, Weighted Strike, External Weight Shift ### Sphere Identity “The heavens do not fall because the world has agreed where down is. A gravity cultivator learns to renegotiate that agreement.” Gravity is the cultivation of weight, falling, anchoring, lightness, pressure, orbit, and the invisible law that tells bodies where they must go. In most sects, Gravity is not first taught as battlefield spellcasting. The common road is body-lightening and body-heavying: making the body light enough to cross rooftops, heavy enough to crack flagstones, weightless enough to leap like a moon-shadow, or dense enough that an enemy cannot move you from a stance. The rarer road is external gravitic law: wells, pressure fields, flight suppression, local down, crushing domains, falling-star rituals, and prisons where even space feels too heavy to cross. Gravity is therefore a true hybrid sphere. A novice changes their own weight. An adept borrows the fall of a mountain for a single punch. A master decides which way the battlefield believes down should be. ### Gravity Access Sphere Type: True Hybrid Sphere. Primary Common Practice: Body Refining through body-lightening and body-heavying. Primary Casting Practice: Qi Cultivation through external gravitic control. Rare Spiritual Practice: Spirit Awakening through the Gravitic Soul Insight. Default Resources: Body Refining uses Stamina for Gravity Weight Arts and may use Stamina for Field Arts if the GM allows the sphere as a Body Refining hybrid discipline. Qi Cultivation uses Qi for Gravity Field Arts and refined weight manipulation. Spirit Awakening uses Resonance only through the Gravitic Soul Insight or a similar initiation. Key Ability: Body Refining: Constitution. Qi Cultivation: Intelligence or Charisma, chosen by the Qi Path. Spirit Awakening: Wisdom, if the cultivator has legal access. Gravity is more common as a martial enhancement sphere than as a pure casting sphere. A village body cultivator may know Body Heavying and Body Lightening without ever learning how to create a Gravity Well. A royal observatory or mountain sect may train the rarer external arts. ### What Gravity Covers Gravity governs: body lightening; body heavying; falling; jumping; forced vertical or radial movement; attraction and repulsion around a point; weight and effective mass; flight suppression; anchoring; orbiting debris or pressure; pressure fields; localized directions of down; structure stress caused by multiplied weight. Gravity does not automatically govern: broad telekinesis; invisible hands; general pushing that ignores weight or falling; wind, vacuum, or pressure waves; earth shaping; time dilation; teleportation; fate, karma, or destiny. Overlap guidance: Force governs direct invisible pressure, barriers, impacts, and constructed force. Gravity governs how mass falls, weighs, or is drawn. Brute governs bodily overpowering, direct leverage, and strength. Gravity can make a blow heavy, but Brute remains the sphere of raw physical domination. Athletics governs natural movement skill. Gravity can lighten the body, but Athletics remains the sphere of trained jumping, climbing, and running. Earth governs stone and terrain. Gravity may stress stone or pull a creature down, but it does not shape earth by itself. Air governs wind, breath, lift, and medium-based movement. Gravity can deny flight or change falling direction, but it does not create wind. Space changes where things are. Gravity changes how strongly things are pulled, pressed, or allowed to fall. ### Gravity Tags Gravity talents may use these tags. Weight Art: A personal or close-range technique that changes the user’s body, gear, held weapon, or an adjacent creature’s effective weight. Weight Arts are common among Body Refiners. Field Art: A ranged, area, or external effect that changes gravitational law outside the user’s body. Field Arts are more common among Qi cultivators and sect specialists. Anchor Art: A technique that prevents movement, falling, forced movement, teleportation, or flight by increasing the binding force between a creature and the world. Fall Art: A technique that weaponizes descent, falling damage, vertical motion, or sudden changes in direction. Orbit Art: A technique that curves motion, circles debris, redirects near misses, or makes objects move around a center. Domain Art: A Core Formation or higher technique that imposes a local gravitational law on an area. ### Gravity Terminology Weight: Gravity techniques may increase or decrease effective weight. This can affect speed, jumping, falling, forced movement, carrying capacity, flight, grappling, and structural stress. Weight changes do not automatically change a creature’s size. Effective Weight: A game-facing measure of how heavy something acts for a specific purpose. A creature may count as heavier for resisting forced movement without literally increasing its mass enough to crush the floor. Body Lightening: A Weight Art that makes the cultivator quicker, easier to move, harder to pin, and safer while falling. Body Heavying: A Weight Art that makes the cultivator harder to move, stronger in rooted exchanges, and able to add crushing weight to melee strikes. Forced Movement: Gravity may pull, push, lift, drop, or pin creatures. Forced movement does not provoke Opportunity Attacks unless a technique says otherwise. Falling: A creature dropped by a Gravity technique takes normal falling damage unless the technique defines a different result. Flight Suppression: A flying creature whose Fly Speed becomes 0 falls unless it can Hover or a feature says otherwise. Local Down: Some high-Realm Gravity talents temporarily choose a direction that functions as down for affected creatures or objects. ### Learning Gravity When you first learn the Sphere of Gravity, you gain Weight Shift and learn one Gravity talent for which you meet the prerequisites. If your first Gravity talent has the Weight Art tag, you are assumed to have learned the common body-weight method. If your first Gravity talent has the Field Art tag, you are assumed to have learned the rarer gravitic-law method. This assumption has no mechanical effect unless a talent, Path synergy, Insight, or variant scripture refers to it. ### Base Ability - Weight Shift Action Type: Bonus Action Factory Combat Bucket: bonus_action Factory Routing: combat_action_row Range: Self. Duration: Until the start of your next turn. Cost: 0 for the basic self version. Choose one mode: Body Lightening, Body Heavying, or Neutral Weight. You may change modes only once on each of your turns unless a talent says otherwise. If you are Incapacitated, your Weight Shift becomes Neutral Weight. #### Body Lightening Until the start of your next turn, your body becomes lighter, quicker, and less bound to the ground. Benefits: Your Speed increases by 10 feet. Your jump distance increases by a number of feet equal to 5 + your Proficiency Bonus. You reduce any falling damage you take by an amount equal to 5 times your Proficiency Bonus. You gain Advantage on Dexterity (Acrobatics) checks made to escape a Grapple or move across narrow, fragile, or unstable footing. If you move at least 10 feet before making a melee attack on your turn, you may use your Gravity key ability in place of Strength or Dexterity for that attack roll if the weapon is an unarmed strike, simple melee weapon, monk-like martial implement, spear, sword, staff, or other GM-approved mobile martial weapon. Body Lightening does not grant flight by itself. #### Body Heavying Until the start of your next turn, your body becomes denser, more rooted, and harder to displace. Benefits: Your Speed is reduced by 5 feet, to a minimum of 5 feet. You count as one size larger when resisting Shove, Grapple, forced movement, and effects that would knock you Prone. You gain Advantage on Strength checks and Strength saving throws made to resist forced movement or being knocked Prone. Your carrying, dragging, lifting, and pushing capacity doubles. If you do not move more than half your Speed on your turn, the first melee weapon attack or Unarmed Strike you hit with before the start of your next turn deals additional damage equal to your Proficiency Bonus. The damage type is the attack’s normal damage type, or Force if the attack is a supernatural Gravity technique. Body Heavying does not increase your size and does not automatically increase weapon reach. #### Neutral Weight You return to normal weight. Ending Weight Shift early requires no action on your turn. ### Base Technique - Weighted Strike Tag: Weight Art. Trigger: You hit a creature with a melee weapon attack or Unarmed Strike while Body Lightening or Body Heavying is active. Cost: 1 CP or Stamina. Use Limit: Once per turn. Choose one rider. Heavying Blow: Add 1d6 Force damage. The target makes a Strength saving throw. On a failed save, it is pushed 5 feet, pulled 5 feet, or knocked Prone, chosen by you. On a successful save, it cannot take Reactions until the start of its next turn. Lightening Blow: Add 1d6 Force damage. After the attack resolves, you may move up to 10 feet without provoking Opportunity Attacks from the target of the attack. Scaling: CL 5: damage becomes 2d6. CL 11: damage becomes 3d6. CL 17: damage becomes 4d6. Weighted Strike is the most common battlefield expression of Gravity. External Gravity Arts are rarer, more costly, and more obvious. ### Base Technique - External Weight Shift Tag: Field Art. Action Type: Action Factory Combat Bucket: action Factory Routing: combat_action_row Range: 60 feet. Duration: Concentration, up to 1 minute. Cost: 1 CP or Stamina. Choose one creature or object no larger than Large. If the target is willing, you may choose Body Lightening or Body Heavying for it. If the target is unwilling, choose Burden or Uplift. Burden: The target makes a Strength saving throw. On a failed save, its Speed is reduced by 10 feet, its jump distance is halved, and it has Disadvantage on Strength (Athletics) and Dexterity (Acrobatics) checks. At the end of each of its turns, it repeats the save, ending the effect on itself on a success. On a successful initial save, its Speed is reduced by 10 feet until the start of its next turn. Uplift: The target makes a Strength saving throw. On a failed save, its first movement on its next turn is unstable: it must spend 10 feet of movement to remain grounded, or it rises 10 feet upward and then falls at the end of the turn if nothing holds it aloft. On a successful save, it rises only 5 feet or may immediately fall Prone to avoid the rise. Objects: The GM determines how increased or decreased weight affects doors, bridges, ropes, carts, armor, siege engines, or carried objects. Gravity does not automatically destroy objects without a talent that deals damage or causes structural stress. ### Mortal Realm Talents - CL 1+ #### Anchor Stance Tag: Weight Art, Anchor Art. While Body Heavying is active and you are touching a solid surface, you reduce forced movement affecting you by 10 feet. If this reduces the movement to 0, you may use your Reaction to regain Martial Focus, if your table uses Martial Focus for martial spheres. At CL 5, you may also extend this benefit to one willing adjacent ally until the start of your next turn. #### Feather Body Tag: Weight Art. Your Body Lightening improves. Benefits while Body Lightening is active: Your Speed increase becomes 15 feet. You ignore the first 30 feet of falling when calculating falling damage. You may stand from Prone by spending only 5 feet of movement. You may move across fragile surfaces, loose snow, thin branches, rooftiles, and similar footing without breaking them, if the GM agrees the surface could plausibly support supernatural lightness. At CL 5, you may run across liquid surfaces during your turn, but you sink if you end your turn unsupported. #### Mountain Body Tag: Weight Art. Your Body Heavying improves. Benefits while Body Heavying is active: Your carrying, dragging, lifting, and pushing capacity becomes four times normal instead of double. You may add your Proficiency Bonus to the damage of your first successful Grapple-related Slam, Shove, or Unarmed Strike each turn. You gain Advantage on checks made to hold a door, brace a barrier, resist a charging creature, or remain standing on unstable terrain. At CL 5, you count as two sizes larger rather than one size larger for resisting forced movement, but not for initiating Grapples or Shoves. #### Heavy Weapon Body Tag: Weight Art. You learn to make a weapon heavy only at the moment of impact. When you use Weighted Strike with Heavying Blow, you may change the extra damage dice from d6s to d8s if the attack is made with a melee weapon wielded in two hands or with an Unarmed Strike made while both feet are grounded. If you miss, no extra strain is applied and the resource is not spent. #### Light-Body Flurry Tag: Weight Art. When Body Lightening is active and you move at least 10 feet on your turn, you may use Weighted Strike with Lightening Blow without spending a resource once per short rest. At CL 5, regain the use of this talent when you roll initiative and have no uses remaining. #### Falling Hammer Tag: Weight Art, Fall Art. When you fall or descend at least 10 feet before hitting a creature with a melee attack on the same turn, you may activate Weighted Strike without requiring Body Heavying to be active. If the attack hits, add an extra 1d6 Force damage in addition to the normal Weighted Strike damage. You take no falling damage from the first 30 feet of the descent. At CL 11, the extra damage becomes 2d6. #### Weight-Borrowing Throw Tag: Weight Art. When you successfully Shove or Grapple a creature while Body Heavying is active, you may spend 1 CP or Stamina to move the target 5 feet in any horizontal direction or knock it Prone. If the target is already Grappled by you, increase the movement to 10 feet. This movement is forced movement and does not provoke Opportunity Attacks. #### Gravitic Pull Tag: Field Art. Action Type: Action Factory Combat Bucket: action Factory Routing: combat_action_row Range: 60 feet. Cost: 1 CP or Stamina. Choose one creature no larger than Large. The target makes a Strength saving throw. Failed Save: Pull the target up to 15 feet toward a point you can see. Successful Save: Pull the target 5 feet toward that point. A willing creature may choose to fail the save. At CL 5, you may target a Huge creature. At CL 11, you may target a Gargantuan creature, but the pull distance is halved unless the creature is willing or airborne. #### Gravitic Push Tag: Field Art. Action Type: Action Factory Combat Bucket: action Factory Routing: combat_action_row Range: 60 feet. Cost: 1 CP or Stamina. Choose one creature no larger than Large. The target makes a Strength saving throw. Failed Save: Push the target up to 15 feet away from a point you can see. Successful Save: Push the target 5 feet. At CL 5, you may target a Huge creature. At CL 11, you may target a Gargantuan creature, but the push distance is halved unless the creature is willing or airborne. #### Falling Line Tag: Field Art, Fall Art. Action Type: Action Factory Combat Bucket: action Factory Routing: combat_action_row Range: 60 feet. Cost: 1 CP or Stamina. Choose a 30-foot line you can see. Each creature in the line makes a Dexterity saving throw. Failed Save: The creature takes 1d8 Force damage and is pulled 10 feet along the line toward the direction you choose. Successful Save: The creature takes half damage and is not pulled. Damage increases to 2d8 at CL 5, 3d8 at CL 11, and 4d8 at CL 17. #### Orbiting Guard Tag: Weight Art, Orbit Art. Action Type: Bonus Action Factory Combat Bucket: bonus_action Factory Routing: combat_action_row Duration: 1 minute. Cost: 1 CP or Stamina. Create a close field of orbiting pressure, curved dust, small stones, sleeve weights, weapon tassels, or invisible directional pull around yourself. While active: You gain +1 AC. Once per round when a creature misses you with a melee attack, you may move 5 feet without provoking Opportunity Attacks from that creature. At CL 5, the AC bonus becomes +2 while Body Lightening or Body Heavying is active. #### Gravity Sense Tag: Field Art. You sense major gravitational distortions within 120 feet. You know when a creature or object within that range: changes weight supernaturally; falls through supernatural force; enters a Gravity Domain; uses levitation or flight; becomes anchored by supernatural weight; creates a gravity well, local down, orbit, or pressure field. You also gain a +2 bonus to Cultivation Checks made to identify or resist Gravity effects. ### Foundation Realm Talents - CL 5+ #### Reverse Gravity Step Tag: Weight Art, Fall Art. Action Type: Bonus Action Factory Combat Bucket: bonus_action Factory Routing: combat_action_row Duration: Until the end of your turn. Cost: 2 CP or Stamina. Choose one direction. Until the end of your turn, gravity treats that direction as down for you only. You may: run along walls; run across ceilings; leap upward as though falling sideways; move across gaps; drop sideways; avoid ordinary falling damage during this movement. At the end of the turn, normal gravity returns. If you are not standing on a surface or supported by another effect, you fall normally. #### Crushing Field Tag: Field Art. Action Type: Action Factory Combat Bucket: action Factory Routing: combat_action_row Range: 60 feet. Area: 15-foot-radius sphere. Duration: Concentration, up to 1 minute. Cost: 4 CP or Stamina. The area becomes difficult terrain for hostile creatures. When a hostile creature enters the area for the first time on a turn or starts its turn there, it makes a Strength saving throw. Limitation: Weight Shift costs 1 CP or Stamina if you maintain Body Lightening or Body Heavying for more than one consecutive round. You may learn Gravity as a Spirit Awakening sphere. Use Resonance for Gravity talents and Wisdom as your key ability. You gain the Spirit Awakening - Gravitic Soul synergy. #### Mountain Stance Prerequisite: Gravity sphere, CL 4+. While touching a solid surface and Body Heavying is active: You have Advantage against forced movement. You have Advantage against being knocked Prone. You count as one size larger for Grapple and Shove. You reduce forced movement affecting you by 5 feet. If you already have Anchor Stance, increase the total reduction by 5 feet. #### Falling Star Footwork Prerequisite: Gravity sphere, CL 8+. When using Reverse Gravity Step, Feather Body, or Body Lightening: you do not provoke Opportunity Attacks from creatures whose reach you leave during the first 10 feet of movement; you may move across liquid surfaces during your turn; you may move across fragile surfaces without breaking them; once per short rest, you may use Reverse Gravity Step without spending CP or Stamina. #### Crushing Focus Prerequisite: Gravity sphere, CL 8+. Once per turn when a creature fails a save against your Gravity talent, deal additional Force damage equal to your Proficiency Bonus. If the failed save was caused by a Weight Art delivered through a melee attack, you may instead regain Martial Focus, if your table uses Martial Focus. #### Body as Center Prerequisite: Body Refining, Gravity sphere, CL 8+. Your own body can serve as the center of nearby Gravity Field Arts. When you use Gravitic Pull, Gravity Well, Crushing Field, or Flight Suppression, you may center the effect on yourself. If you do, reduce the cost by 1 Stamina, minimum 1, but the area moves with you only until the start of your next turn unless the talent already says otherwise. #### Moon-Thread Weight Prerequisite: Gravity sphere, CL 8+. When Body Lightening is active, you may treat one weapon you hold as lighter than it is. Choose one benefit at the start of your turn: A two-handed melee weapon you wield does not prevent you from climbing, balancing, or moving across fragile surfaces. A non-heavy melee weapon you wield may be used with your Gravity key ability for attack and damage rolls until the start of your next turn. One thrown weapon you throw returns to your hand at the end of the turn by curving through a small orbit. #### Anchor Between Heaven and Earth Prerequisite: Gravity sphere, CL 12+. When you would be moved against your will, knocked Prone, or dropped from flight, you may use your Reaction and spend 2 CP or Stamina to anchor yourself. Until the start of your next turn: your Speed becomes 0; you cannot be moved against your will by effects of Core Formation or lower; you do not fall unless the surface supporting you is destroyed; attacks against you have Advantage until the start of your next turn.

### Base Ability - Weight Shift
Action Type: Bonus Action
Factory Combat Bucket: bonus_action
Factory Routing: combat_action_row
Range: Self.
Duration: Until the start of your next turn.
Cost: 0 for the basic self version.
Choose one mode: Body Lightening, Body Heavying, or Neutral Weight.
You may change modes only once on each of your turns unless a talent says otherwise. If you are Incapacitated, your Weight Shift becomes Neutral Weight.
#### Body Lightening
Until the start of your next turn, your body becomes lighter, quicker, and less bound to the ground.
Benefits:
Your Speed increases by 10 feet.
Your jump distance increases by a number of feet equal to 5 + your Proficiency Bonus.
You reduce any falling damage you take by an amount equal to 5 times your Proficiency Bonus.
You gain Advantage on Dexterity (Acrobatics) checks made to escape a Grapple or move across narrow, fragile, or unstable footing.
If you move at least 10 feet before making a melee attack on your turn, you may use your Gravity key ability in place of Strength or Dexterity for that attack roll if the weapon is an unarmed strike, simple melee weapon, monk-like martial implement, spear, sword, staff, or other GM-approved mobile martial weapon.
Body Lightening does not grant flight by itself.
#### Body Heavying
Until the start of your next turn, your body becomes denser, more rooted, and harder to displace.
Benefits:
Your Speed is reduced by 5 feet, to a minimum of 5 feet.
You count as one size larger when resisting Shove, Grapple, forced movement, and effects that would knock you Prone.
You gain Advantage on Strength checks and Strength saving throws made to resist forced movement or being knocked Prone.
Your carrying, dragging, lifting, and pushing capacity doubles.
If you do not move more than half your Speed on your turn, the first melee weapon attack or Unarmed Strike you hit with before the start of your next turn deals additional damage equal to your Proficiency Bonus. The damage type is the attack’s normal damage type, or Force if the attack is a supernatural Gravity technique.

Action Type: Bonus Action
Factory Combat Bucket: bonus_action
Factory Routing: combat_action_row
Range: Self.
Duration: Until the start of your next turn.

Choose one mode: Body Lightening, Body Heavying, or Neutral Weight.
You may change modes only once on each of your turns unless a talent says otherwise. If you are Incapacitated, your Weight Shift becomes Neutral Weight.
#### Body Lightening
Until the start of your next turn, your body becomes lighter, quicker, and less bound to the ground.
Benefits:
Your Speed increases by 10 feet.
Your jump distance increases by a number of feet equal to 5 + your Proficiency Bonus.
You reduce any falling damage you take by an amount equal to 5 times your Proficiency Bonus.
You gain Advantage on Dexterity (Acrobatics) checks made to escape a Grapple or move across narrow, fragile, or unstable footing.
If you move at least 10 feet before making a melee attack on your turn, you may use your Gravity key ability in place of Strength or Dexterity for that attack roll if the weapon is an unarmed strike, simple melee weapon, monk-like martial implement, spear, sword, staff, or other GM-approved mobile martial weapon.
Body Lightening does not grant flight by itself.
#### Body Heavying
Until the start of your next turn, your body becomes denser, more rooted, and harder to displace.
Benefits:
Your Speed is reduced by 5 feet, to a minimum of 5 feet.
You count as one size larger when resisting Shove, Grapple, forced movement, and effects that would knock you Prone.
You gain Advantage on Strength checks and Strength saving throws made to resist forced movement or being knocked Prone.
Your carrying, dragging, lifting, and pushing capacity doubles.

The damage type is the attack’s normal damage type, or Force if the attack is a supernatural Gravity technique.
Body Heavying does not increase your size and does not automatically increase weapon reach.
#### Neutral Weight
You return to normal weight. Ending Weight Shift early requires no action on your turn.

automatic_base_abilities.effect:
### Challenge Practice
You cultivate the art of becoming the enemy’s most immediate problem.
#### Challenge
Action Type: Bonus Action
Factory Combat Bucket: bonus_action
Factory Routing: combat_action_row
Range: 60 feet
Target: One creature that can perceive your challenge
Duration: 1 minute
Cost: None
Issue a challenge through words, stance, weapon intent, a visible gesture, killing pressure, or another method the target can perceive.
An unwilling creature makes a Charisma saving throw.
Failed Save: The creature becomes Challenged by you for the duration.
Successful Save: No effect.
A mindless creature cannot be Challenged unless a talent explicitly says otherwise.
While a creature is Challenged by you:
it has Disadvantage on attack rolls that do not include you as a target;
it has Advantage on attack rolls targeting only you;
if it cannot legally perceive, reach, or target you, it does not suffer Disadvantage merely because it attacks another creature;
when you successfully Challenge another creature, your previous Challenge ends unless a talent says otherwise.
A creature may be affected by Challenges from multiple cultivators.
If it attacks at least one creature that has Challenged it, it does not suffer Disadvantage merely because another challenger was not included.

automatic_base_abilities.effect:
### Patrol Practice
You cultivate the art of deciding which ground an enemy may cross only by answering you.
#### Patrol
Action Type: Action
Factory Combat Bucket: action
Factory Routing: combat_action_row
Duration: Until the start of your next turn
Cost: None
Establish a Patrol Zone centered on yourself.
The Patrol Zone extends a distance equal to:
your melee reach + 10 feet
When a hostile creature you can perceive moves into, out of, or through your Patrol Zone, you may make one Patrol Response.
#### Patrol Response
A Patrol Response allows you to:
move up to your remaining Patrol Movement into a legal space that brings the triggering creature within your melee reach;
make one opportunity attack against that creature.
The first Patrol Response you make before the start of your next turn requires your Reaction.
At higher Cultivation Levels, you gain additional Patrol Responses each round that do not require your Reaction:
| Cultivation Level | Additional Patrol Responses |
| --- | --- |
| 1-4 | 0 |
| 5-10 | 1 |
| 11-16 | 2 |
| 17-20 | 3 |
These additional Patrol Responses are explicit exceptions to the ordinary rule that a creature has only one Reaction between the starts of its turns. They may be used only for Patrol Responses.
These additional Patrol Responses:
may be used only while Patrol remains active;
are still treated as Reactions for rules that limit one response to one trigger;
cannot trigger another Reaction talent from the same triggering movement;
do not restore your ordinary Reaction;
cannot be used more than once during the same creature’s turn.
#### Patrol Movement
When you establish Patrol, your total Patrol Movement before the start of your next turn equals your Speed.
Movement spent through Patrol Responses:
reduces your remaining Patrol Movement;
follows a legal route;
provokes opportunity attacks normally;
cannot exceed your remaining Patrol Movement;
does not reduce your Speed during your own turn.
#### Patrol Attack Limits
A Patrol attack:
is an opportunity attack;
may be made only once per triggering creature’s turn;
cannot trigger itself;
does not deal Sneak Attack damage or comparable precision damage unless a talent explicitly permits it;
still requires a legal melee attack and a weapon, unarmed strike, or natural weapon able to reach the target.
#### Zone Talent Limit
Choose one Patrol Zone talent you know whenever you establish Patrol.
Only one Zone talent normally modifies one Patrol.
