spheres.full_exact_source_text: # Sphere of Guardian Qi Expression: Primary — Protective Qi; Supporting — Earth Qi, Shield Qi, Oath Qi, Body-Bearing Qi. “The strongest wall is the one that chooses where to stand.” Sphere Type: Martial Sphere Primary Path: Body Refining Secondary Paths: Qi Cultivation and Spirit Awakening Resource: Martial Focus Common Effects: Delayed harm, interception, challenges, patrol zones, bodyguard movement, holding ground, rescue vows, defensive reprisals ## GUARDIAN DAO Guardian is the cultivation of chosen burden. A wall does not protect anyone merely because it is difficult to break. A guardian protects because they decide where danger is allowed to stop, then place their body, weapon, breath, and will at that exact point. The Guardian Dao is not passive endurance. A Guardian cultivator: steps into the path of an attack; carries pain for one more breath before allowing it to become injury; makes aggression costly to direct elsewhere; patrols the space where an enemy must not pass; refuses displacement when another creature depends upon their position; answers calamity with presence rather than distance. Guardian rewards judgment. The practitioner must decide: Which attack is worth intercepting? Which injury can be carried until the end of the turn? Is the greater threat one enemy who must be challenged, or an entire route that must be patrolled? Should Martial Focus be spent to arrive faster, hold more ground, or punish an enemy for testing the line? When does survival matter less than ensuring someone behind the Guardian survives? After fighting a Guardian cultivator for two rounds, an enemy should understand one truth: Every attack must first answer the person who chose to stand in its way. ## CORE GUARDIAN RULES ### Martial Focus Guardian uses Martial Focus. you may hold one Martial Focus at a time; some talents expend Martial Focus; expending Martial Focus is not an Action; you cannot expend Martial Focus if you do not currently hold it; if a talent says you regain Martial Focus, regain it only if it is currently absent. Martial Focus represents vigilance, breath, posture, and the instant in which a protector recognizes where danger is truly going. ### Held Harm Guardian cultivators may refuse to let injury arrive immediately. You possess a Held Harm Pool with a maximum equal to: 3 × your Cultivation Level Whenever you would take damage, apply Resistance, Immunity, and ordinary reductions first. You may then redirect any amount of the remaining damage into your Held Harm Pool, up to its remaining capacity. Damage redirected into Held Harm is not taken immediately. At the end of each of your turns: take all damage stored in your Held Harm Pool as one damage instance; this damage bypasses Resistance, Immunity, and damage reduction; this damage cannot be redirected into Held Harm again; then reduce your Held Harm Pool to 0. Held Harm preserves urgency rather than erasing injury. Unless a talent says otherwise: additional effects of an attack or ability occur immediately even if all of its damage is held; damage stored in Held Harm retains no damage type after entering the pool; storing damage does not count as taking that stored damage for triggers that require you to take damage; taking the stored damage at the end of your turn counts as taking damage once; Temporary HP can absorb this end-of-turn damage normally unless a talent explicitly says otherwise; healing that would restore HP above your maximum instead reduces your Held Harm by the excess amount; Held Harm cannot be reduced below 0; if you lose access to Guardian, resolve your Held Harm at the end of your turn as normal. A Guardian may carry a spear through the chest for one breath, finish dragging a child behind a wall, and only then allow the wound to become real. ### Interpose Action Type: Reaction Factory Combat Bucket: reaction Factory Routing: combat_action_row Trigger: One ally within 10 feet is targeted by an attack roll Range: 10 feet Cost: None Move up to 10 feet into one legal unoccupied space adjacent to the ally. This movement does not provoke opportunity attacks. If you are a legal target for the triggering attack, become its target instead. Interpose does not automatically protect against: area effects; saving-throw effects; attacks that cannot legally target you; effects whose route cannot reach you after the movement; attacks you cannot perceive unless a talent says otherwise. Interpose is the simplest expression of the Guardian Dao: arrive where the danger is going. ### Guardian Practice When you learn Guardian, choose one Guardian Practice: Challenge Practice; Patrol Practice. You gain the corresponding base ability. You may later learn the other Practice through Expanded Guardian. ## BASE GUARDIAN PRACTICES ### Challenge Practice You cultivate the art of becoming the enemy’s most immediate problem. #### Challenge Action Type: Bonus Action Factory Combat Bucket: bonus_action Factory Routing: combat_action_row Range: 60 feet Target: One creature that can perceive your challenge Duration: 1 minute Cost: None Issue a challenge through words, stance, weapon intent, a visible gesture, killing pressure, or another method the target can perceive. An unwilling creature makes a Charisma saving throw. Failed Save: The creature becomes Challenged by you for the duration. Successful Save: No effect. A mindless creature cannot be Challenged unless a talent explicitly says otherwise. While a creature is Challenged by you: it has Disadvantage on attack rolls that do not include you as a target; it has Advantage on attack rolls targeting only you; if it cannot legally perceive, reach, or target you, it does not suffer Disadvantage merely because it attacks another creature; when you successfully Challenge another creature, your previous Challenge ends unless a talent says otherwise. A creature may be affected by Challenges from multiple cultivators. If it attacks at least one creature that has Challenged it, it does not suffer Disadvantage merely because another challenger was not included. ### Patrol Practice You cultivate the art of deciding which ground an enemy may cross only by answering you. #### Patrol Action Type: Action Factory Combat Bucket: action Factory Routing: combat_action_row Duration: Until the start of your next turn Cost: None Establish a Patrol Zone centered on yourself. The Patrol Zone extends a distance equal to: your melee reach + 10 feet When a hostile creature you can perceive moves into, out of, or through your Patrol Zone, you may make one Patrol Response. #### Patrol Response A Patrol Response allows you to: move up to your remaining Patrol Movement into a legal space that brings the triggering creature within your melee reach; make one opportunity attack against that creature. The first Patrol Response you make before the start of your next turn requires your Reaction. At higher Cultivation Levels, you gain additional Patrol Responses each round that do not require your Reaction: | Cultivation Level | Additional Patrol Responses | | --- | --- | | 1-4 | 0 | | 5-10 | 1 | | 11-16 | 2 | | 17-20 | 3 | These additional Patrol Responses are explicit exceptions to the ordinary rule that a creature has only one Reaction between the starts of its turns. They may be used only for Patrol Responses. These additional Patrol Responses: may be used only while Patrol remains active; are still treated as Reactions for rules that limit one response to one trigger; cannot trigger another Reaction talent from the same triggering movement; do not restore your ordinary Reaction; cannot be used more than once during the same creature’s turn. #### Patrol Movement When you establish Patrol, your total Patrol Movement before the start of your next turn equals your Speed. Movement spent through Patrol Responses: reduces your remaining Patrol Movement; follows a legal route; provokes opportunity attacks normally; cannot exceed your remaining Patrol Movement; does not reduce your Speed during your own turn. #### Patrol Attack Limits A Patrol attack: is an opportunity attack; may be made only once per triggering creature’s turn; cannot trigger itself; does not deal Sneak Attack damage or comparable precision damage unless a talent explicitly permits it; still requires a legal melee attack and a weapon, unarmed strike, or natural weapon able to reach the target. #### Zone Talent Limit Choose one Patrol Zone talent you know whenever you establish Patrol. Only one Zone talent normally modifies one Patrol. ## GUARDIAN TALENT TAGS ### Resilience Talents A Resilience talent modifies Held Harm or allows the Guardian to carry a new kind of burden temporarily. ### Challenge Talents A Challenge talent modifies Challenge or creates a new consequence for Challenged creatures. ### Patrol Talents A Patrol talent modifies Patrol, Patrol Responses, or Patrol Movement. ### Zone Talents A Zone talent modifies the area created through Patrol. Only one Zone talent normally modifies one Patrol. ### Rescue Talents A Rescue talent protects an ally through interception, shared injury, movement, or immediate sacrifice. ### Focus Talents A Focus talent regains, expends, or modifies Martial Focus. ### Rite Talents A Rite talent is a vow, bond, rescue practice, escort discipline, or longer-duration Guardian method. ### Unique Guardian Talents A Unique Guardian Talent is a distinct technique that does not fit another category. ## MORTAL REALM GUARDIAN TALENTS ### Deep Reservoir — Resilience Talent Increase your Held Harm Pool maximum by: your Cultivation Level You may learn Deep Reservoir twice. Its effects stack. ### Flush of Victory — Challenge Talent When a creature Challenged by you is reduced to 0 HP, gain Temporary HP equal to: your Cultivation Level The creature must be a meaningful threat. A creature with a Challenge Rating lower than half your Cultivation Level normally does not qualify unless the GM determines that its defeat mattered meaningfully in the scene. ### Steel Hide — Challenge Talent When a creature Challenged by you scores a critical hit against you, you may end your Challenge on that creature. If you do, the triggering attack deals ordinary damage instead of critical-hit damage. Steel Hide does not prevent additional effects caused specifically by a critical hit unless those effects depend on the additional critical-hit damage. ### Assist the Line — Zone Talent Allies inside your Patrol Zone gain: +1 AC A creature benefits from only one Assist the Line effect at a time. ### Clear Path — Zone Talent Allies other than you do not provoke opportunity attacks from hostile creatures for moving through your Patrol Zone. Clear Path does not protect movement outside the zone. ### Steel Hedge — Zone Talent Hostile creatures treat your Patrol Zone as difficult terrain. Steel Hedge does not increase the cost of forced movement. ### Guardian’s Focus — Focus Talent Use Limit: Once per round When one of the following occurs, regain Martial Focus if it is currently absent: a creature Challenged by you is reduced to 0 HP; you hit with a Patrol attack; you successfully use Interpose; you succeed on a Grapple or Shove attempt while Patrol is active. ### Swift Guardian — Focus Talent When activating Challenge or Patrol, expend Martial Focus to change its Action Type: activate Challenge without spending an Action during your turn; activate Patrol as a Bonus Action. If you possess Mass Challenge, expend Martial Focus to use Mass Challenge as a Bonus Action instead of an Action. ### Expanded Guardian Gain one Guardian Practice you do not already possess. You gain its base ability. ### Shield Companion — Rescue Talent When an ally adjacent to you makes a Dexterity saving throw against an effect that deals half damage on a successful save, use your Reaction. Grant the ally: + your Proficiency Bonus to the saving throw result, potentially turning failure into success. If the ally succeeds, you may move it 5 feet into one legal space adjacent to you after the effect resolves. This movement does not provoke opportunity attacks. ## FOUNDATION REALM GUARDIAN TALENTS ### Bodyguard — Rescue Talent Prerequisite: CL 5+ Interpose improves: its range increases to 20 feet; you may move up to 20 feet when using it; gain Resistance to the triggering attack’s damage until that attack resolves. ### Durable — Resilience Talent Prerequisite: CL 5+ When you fail a saving throw against one of the following, you may reserve 10 points of empty space in your Held Harm Pool: disease; one level of Exhaustion; poison; Blinded; Charmed; Deafened; Frightened; Paralyzed; Petrified; Poisoned; Restrained; Stunned; Unconscious. If you reserve the required space, delay the effect until the end of your next turn. The reserved space: counts against your Held Harm maximum; cannot be filled by damage; cannot be cleared through healing; is released when the delayed effect resolves or is removed. An effect that would ordinarily remove the delayed condition may remove it from Durable before it resolves. You may voluntarily release one Durable effect without spending an Action. It applies immediately. Durable delays one effect, not the entire ability that caused it. Damage and other consequences resolve normally. ### Cold Iron Call — Resilience Talent Prerequisite: CL 5+ When you would be affected by a supernatural effect that does not merely deal damage, you may reserve space in your Held Harm Pool equal to: 5 × the originator’s Proficiency Bonus If the source has no listed Proficiency Bonus, use the Proficiency Bonus appropriate to its Challenge Rating or Cultivation Level. If neither is available, the GM assigns a reasonable value. If you reserve the required space, delay the non-damaging portion of that effect until the end of your next turn. The reserved space follows the same rules as Durable. Cold Iron Call does not automatically delay: damage; an entire area of effect; an effect already active before you were targeted; a Domain; a Secret Inheritance; a major narrative calamity; an effect the GM determines cannot meaningfully be carried inside one body. A suitable removal effect may remove the delayed supernatural effect before it resolves. ### Mageguard — Challenge Talent Prerequisite: CL 5+ A creature Challenged by you has Disadvantage on saving throws made to maintain Concentration while it remains within your melee reach. ### Punishing Challenge — Challenge Talent Prerequisite: CL 5+ Use Limit: Once per turn per creature When a creature Challenged by you makes an attack roll with Disadvantage because it did not include you as a target, it takes your choice of Psychic or Radiant damage equal to: your Cultivation Level Choose the damage type when you learn this talent. ### Inescapable Challenge — Challenge Talent Prerequisite: CL 7+ When a creature Challenged by you willingly attempts to move farther away from you, it makes a Wisdom saving throw. Failed Save: Its attempted movement ends before carrying it farther away. Successful Save: It moves normally. If the movement is created by teleportation or another supernatural effect: a failed saving throw prevents that movement; the Action is spent; CP, spell slots, item charges, or comparable limited resources are not spent unless another effect says otherwise. Inescapable Challenge does not stop forced movement caused by another creature. ### Punishing Rebuke — Zone Talent Prerequisite: CL 5+ When a hostile creature inside your Patrol Zone makes an attack roll against an ally other than you, that creature provokes a Patrol Response from you after the attack resolves. Punishing Rebuke can trigger only once per creature’s turn. ### Stand Still — Zone Talent Prerequisite: CL 5+ When you hit a hostile creature with a Patrol attack, reduce its Speed to 0 until the start of its next turn. ### Disruptive Patrol — Zone Talent Prerequisite: CL 7+ When a hostile creature inside your Patrol Zone begins activating a supernatural effect that requires an Action, Bonus Action, or Reaction, it provokes a Patrol Response from you before completing the activation. If your Patrol attack deals damage, the creature makes a Constitution saving throw as though maintaining Concentration. Failed Save: The activation fails. The Action is spent, but CP, spell slots, and comparable limited-use resources are not spent. Successful Save: The activation resolves normally. Disruptive Patrol does not interrupt: passive effects; effects requiring no Action; Domains already active; Secret Inheritances unless they explicitly permit interruption. ### Complex Patrol — Focus Talent Prerequisite: CL 5+ When establishing Patrol, expend Martial Focus. Apply two Zone talents you know instead of one. ### Singularity Patrol — Zone Talent Prerequisite: CL 7+ Your Patrol Zone becomes spiritually heavy with your insistence that enemies answer you first. When a hostile creature starts its turn inside your Patrol Zone, it makes a Strength saving throw. Failed Save: Pull the creature 5 feet toward you, stopping when it becomes adjacent to you. Successful Save: No pull. Movement directed away from you costs a hostile creature 10 feet of movement for every 5 feet traveled while it remains inside the Patrol Zone. At CL 11, increase the pull distance to 10 feet. Singularity Patrol does not provoke opportunity attacks through its forced movement. ### Indomitable — Resilience Talent Prerequisite: CL 7+ Trigger: You are reduced to 0 HP Cost: Expend Martial Focus Use Limit: Once per long rest Do not fall Unconscious from HP loss until the end of your next turn. During that time: you act normally; you do not make death saving throws; you may receive healing; damage still affects you normally; Held Harm still resolves normally. If you remain at 0 HP when the effect ends, fall Unconscious and resume the ordinary rules for death saving throws. ## CORE FORMATION REALM GUARDIAN TALENTS ### Court of the Unbroken Gate — Guardian Domain “Behind me.” Prerequisite: CL 10+ Action Type: Bonus Action Factory Combat Bucket: bonus_action Factory Routing: combat_action_row Area: 30-foot-radius aura centered on you Duration: 1 minute Cost: Expend Martial Focus Use Limit: Once per short rest You become the living center of a defensive court. For the duration: #### You Increase your Held Harm Pool maximum by your Cultivation Level. Reduce forced movement affecting you by 20 feet. Gain Advantage on checks and saving throws made to resist Grappled, Prone, or Restrained. Use Interpose once per round without spending your Reaction. #### Allies Inside the Court Gain +1 AC. Gain Advantage on saving throws against Frightened. Reduce forced movement affecting them by 10 feet. Gain Half Cover while within 10 feet of you. #### Enemies Inside the Court Treat spaces adjacent to you as difficult terrain. Provoke opportunity attacks from you when entering your melee reach. Court of the Unbroken Gate ends early if you become Incapacitated. ### Take the Blow — Rescue Talent Prerequisite: CL 10+ Action Type: Reaction Factory Combat Bucket: reaction Factory Routing: combat_action_row Trigger: One ally within 30 feet takes damage Cost: None Take half of the triggering damage, rounded down, instead of the ally. The ally takes the remaining damage. Your portion: retains the original damage types until reductions are applied; may be reduced by your Resistance, Immunity, or ordinary damage reductions; may then be redirected into Held Harm normally; cannot be transferred again. After taking your portion, gain Temporary HP equal to your Proficiency Bonus. ### Guardian’s Reprisal — Rescue Talent Prerequisite: CL 10+ Trigger: You use Interpose or Take the Blow Cost: Expend Martial Focus Use Limit: Once per turn After the triggering effect resolves, make one melee weapon attack, unarmed strike, or natural weapon attack against the attacker if it remains within your melee reach. Hit: Deal the attack’s ordinary damage plus 2d8 additional damage of the same type. ### Fortress-Breaker’s Denial — Patrol Talent Prerequisite: CL 10+ Action Type: Reaction Factory Combat Bucket: reaction Factory Routing: combat_action_row Trigger: One hostile creature within 30 feet moves, teleports, or is forcibly moved Use Limit: Once per round Move up to half your Speed into one legal unoccupied space adjacent to the creature. This movement does not provoke opportunity attacks. The target makes a Strength saving throw. Failed Save: Choose one: its movement ends immediately; it falls Prone; it cannot take Reactions until the start of its next turn. Successful Save: Reduce its remaining movement by 10 feet. Fortress-Breaker’s Denial cannot prevent movement caused by a Secret Inheritance, major calamity, or effect that explicitly cannot be interrupted. ### Punishment Returned — Resilience Talent Prerequisite: CL 10+ Trigger: You hit one creature with a melee weapon attack, unarmed strike, or natural weapon attack while your Held Harm Pool contains damage Cost: Expend Martial Focus Use Limit: Once per round The target makes a Constitution saving throw. Failed Save: Take additional damage equal to the current damage stored in your Held Harm Pool. Successful Save: Take half as much additional damage. The additional damage has the same type as the triggering attack. Punishment Returned does not empty or reduce your Held Harm Pool. If you are delaying one effect through Durable or Cold Iron Call, you may choose to attempt to transmit one delayed effect instead of dealing the additional damage. The target makes the saving throw originally allowed by that effect, using its original DC where available or your Cultivation Save DC otherwise. Failed Save: The transmitted effect applies to the target. Successful Save: The transmission fails. Whether the transmission succeeds or fails, the delayed effect ends for you. A Domain, Secret Inheritance, curse, or major narrative effect cannot be transmitted this way unless it explicitly permits it. ### I Will Hear — Rite Talent Prerequisite: Interpose, CL 10+ Action Type: Ritual Procedure Canonical Action Type: Ritual Procedure Factory Routing: procedure_ledger_not_combat_action Timing Detail: Ritual Time: 10 minutes Range: Touch Target: One willing creature Duration: Until ended Form a guardian vow with the target. A creature carrying your vow may call your name, title, or agreed signal as a Reaction. While you remain on the same plane and within: 10 miles × your Cultivation Level you immediately know: that the creature called; its approximate direction; whether it is uninjured, Bloodied, Unconscious, or dying. You may maintain a number of I Will Hear vows equal to your Proficiency Bonus. If you exceed this limit, choose one older vow to end. You may end one vow without spending an Action. I Will Hear is a supernatural guardian bond, not telepathy. It does not reveal an exact square, transmit a conversation, or compel you to answer. ## NASCENT SOUL REALM GUARDIAN TALENTS ### Adamant Guardian Incarnation “The gate did not hold because it was made of stone. It held because I stood there.” Classification: Unique Guardian Talent Prerequisite: CL 15+ Action Type: Bonus Action Factory Combat Bucket: bonus_action Factory Routing: combat_action_row Duration: 1 minute Use Limit: Once per long rest Transform into a perfected defensive incarnation. For the duration: gain +4 AC; gain Resistance to all damage except Psychic and Force damage; gain Immunity to Prone; become immune to forced movement unless you willingly allow it; increase your melee reach by 5 feet; gain one additional Reaction each round; this explicitly overrides the ordinary one-Reaction limit; still use only one Reaction for any single trigger. #### Shelter the Weak At the start of each of your turns, choose a number of allies within 20 feet up to your Proficiency Bonus. Until the start of your next turn, each chosen ally gains Resistance to the first instance of damage it takes. ### I Will Come — Rite Talent Prerequisite: I Will Hear, CL 15+ Action Type: Action Factory Combat Bucket: action Factory Routing: combat_action_row Target: One creature carrying your I Will Hear vow that has called you Use Limit: Once per bonded creature per long rest Teleport into one legal unoccupied space within 10 feet of the calling creature. You may bring: equipment up to your ordinary carrying capacity; a number of willing creatures up to your Proficiency Bonus. Every creature traveling with you must remain in physical contact with you or with another creature in the traveling group. A Large creature counts as two creatures. A Huge creature counts as four. A Gargantuan creature counts as eight. I Will Come cannot cross planar boundaries until CL 17. At CL 17: I Will Hear functions across planar boundaries; you learn which plane contains the calling creature; I Will Come may cross planar boundaries if no specialized seal, Dimensional Lock, or comparable effect prevents it. ### Heaven-Defying Bulwark Classification: Rescue Talent Prerequisite: CL 15+ Action Type: Reaction Factory Combat Bucket: reaction Factory Routing: combat_action_row Trigger: You or allies within 30 feet would take damage from one effect Use Limit: Once per long rest Choose any number of affected creatures within 30 feet. Reduce the damage dealt to each chosen creature by: 5d10 + your key ability modifier If one chosen creature takes no damage after this reduction, it may move 5 feet without provoking opportunity attacks after the triggering effect resolves. Heaven-Defying Bulwark may reduce area damage. ### Stand Against the Calamity Classification: Unique Guardian Talent Prerequisite: CL 15+ Action Type: Action Factory Combat Bucket: action Factory Routing: combat_action_row Area: 30-foot-radius aura centered on you Duration: Concentration, up to 1 minute Use Limit: Once per long rest Plant your stance and refuse destruction. For the duration: you cannot willingly move; allies inside gain +2 AC; allies inside gain Advantage on saving throws; allies inside reduce all damage taken by your Proficiency Bonus; structures and Formation Anchors inside gain Resistance to all damage; an enemy attempting to forcibly move one creature inside makes a Strength saving throw. Failed Save: The forced movement fails. Successful Save: Move the target only half the normal distance. Stand Against the Calamity ends early if you become Incapacitated or willingly move. ## SECRET INHERITANCE — ONE BODY BEFORE HEAVEN “A thousand arrows descended. None reached the people behind him.” Classification: Secret Guardian Inheritance Prerequisite: CL 17+, Adamant Guardian Incarnation, hidden defensive scripture Action Type: Reaction Factory Combat Bucket: reaction Factory Routing: combat_action_row Trigger: One creature, area effect, Domain, or environmental calamity would damage one or more allies within 60 feet Use Limit: Once per week Choose any number of allies within 60 feet. Redirect all damage those allies would take from the triggering effect to yourself. The redirected damage: retains its original damage types until your Resistance is applied; is combined into one damage instance; cannot be redirected again; cannot be prevented through Immunity; may be reduced by Resistance; may be redirected into Held Harm if capacity remains; cannot reduce you below 1 HP. After resolving the redirected damage: gain one level of Exhaustion; end every Stance and Domain you are maintaining; you cannot use One Body Before Heaven again until the limit resets. One Body Before Heaven does not negate non-damaging consequences unless the GM determines that redirecting the damage naturally carries those consequences with it. ## OPTIONAL GUARDIAN VARIANTS ### Resilient — The Wall Without a Name You abandon Challenge and Patrol practice to cultivate pure refusal. When you learn Guardian through this variant: do not choose a Guardian Practice; gain Deep Reservoir as a bonus talent; you may learn Deep Reservoir one additional time beyond its normal limit; increase the amount of Held Harm removed by excess healing by your Proficiency Bonus whenever excess healing reduces Held Harm. You may still use Interpose and learn Rescue, Resilience, Focus, Rite, and Unique Guardian talents. You cannot learn: Challenge talents; Patrol talents; Zone talents; Expanded Guardian. You cannot possess both Resilient and Without Delay. ### Without Delay — The Immediate Sentinel You refuse to postpone pain. Every answer must be made in the present breath. When you learn Guardian through this variant: do not gain Held Harm; cannot learn Resilience talents; gain Swift Guardian as a bonus talent; gain Advantage on Initiative rolls while you are within 10 feet of one ally. You still choose Challenge Practice or Patrol Practice normally. You cannot possess both Without Delay and Resilient. ## PATH SYNERGIES ### Body Refining — Adamant Frame Use Constitution as your Guardian key ability. Once per round when you redirect damage into Held Harm: reduce forced movement caused by the same effect by 5 feet; gain Advantage on the next Strength (Athletics) check made to resist Grappled or Shoved before the start of your next turn. When Held Harm resolves at the end of your turn, remain standing even if that damage reduces you to 0 HP, unless another effect explicitly knocks you Prone. ### Qi Cultivation — Protective Qi Shell Use Intelligence or Charisma as your Guardian key ability, chosen when learning Guardian. When you use Interpose: you may protect against a ranged Cultivation Attack originating within 60 feet if you can perceive the attacker and become a legal target after moving; once per turn, after becoming the target through Interpose, gain Temporary HP equal to your Proficiency Bonus. These Temporary HP last until the start of your next turn. ### Spirit Awakening — Guardian Soul Use Wisdom as your Guardian key ability. Your protection answers danger directed at the soul as well as the body. Interpose gains an additional trigger: Trigger: One ally within 10 feet makes a saving throw against possession, forced soul displacement, spiritual binding, or Psychic damage. When triggered this way, do not move or become the target automatically. Instead, add your Proficiency Bonus to the triggering saving throw result, potentially turning failure into success. If you possess Bodyguard, increase this range to 20 feet. Guardian Soul does not automatically end an effect that is already active. ## CULTIVATION INSIGHTS ### Adamant Frame Scripture Prerequisite: Body Refining, Guardian, CL 4+ Gain the Body Refining — Adamant Frame synergy. Gain proficiency with shields. If already proficient with shields, gain: +1 AC while wielding a shield ### Protective Instinct Prerequisite: Guardian, CL 8+ Use Limit: Once per short rest Use Interpose without spending your Reaction. You still cannot use Interpose more than once for the same triggering attack. ### Anchor of the Party Prerequisite: Guardian, CL 8+ Allies within 5 feet of you add your Proficiency Bonus to checks and saving throws made to resist: Grappled; Shoved; forced movement. A creature benefits from only one Anchor of the Party effect at a time. ### Shield Sage Prerequisite: Guardian, shield proficiency, CL 8+ While wielding a shield: gain +1 AC; treat the shield as a magical melee weapon dealing 1d8 Bludgeoning damage; once per turn when you hit with the shield, push the target 5 feet if it does not exceed the ordinary size limit for a Shove. ### Vow-Keeper of Ten Thousand Li Prerequisite: I Will Hear, CL 12+ Increase the number of I Will Hear vows you may maintain by your Proficiency Bonus. When one creature carrying your vow calls you, you also learn whether it is affected by: Charmed; Frightened; Grappled; Restrained; possession.

### Patrol Practice
You cultivate the art of deciding which ground an enemy may cross only by answering you.
#### Patrol
Action Type: Action
Factory Combat Bucket: action
Factory Routing: combat_action_row
Duration: Until the start of your next turn
Cost: None
Establish a Patrol Zone centered on yourself.
The Patrol Zone extends a distance equal to:
your melee reach + 10 feet
When a hostile creature you can perceive moves into, out of, or through your Patrol Zone, you may make one Patrol Response.
#### Patrol Response
A Patrol Response allows you to:
move up to your remaining Patrol Movement into a legal space that brings the triggering creature within your melee reach;
make one opportunity attack against that creature.
The first Patrol Response you make before the start of your next turn requires your Reaction.
At higher Cultivation Levels, you gain additional Patrol Responses each round that do not require your Reaction:
| Cultivation Level | Additional Patrol Responses |
| --- | --- |
| 1-4 | 0 |
| 5-10 | 1 |
| 11-16 | 2 |
| 17-20 | 3 |
These additional Patrol Responses are explicit exceptions to the ordinary rule that a creature has only one Reaction between the starts of its turns. They may be used only for Patrol Responses.
These additional Patrol Responses:
may be used only while Patrol remains active;
are still treated as Reactions for rules that limit one response to one trigger;
cannot trigger another Reaction talent from the same triggering movement;
do not restore your ordinary Reaction;
cannot be used more than once during the same creature’s turn.
#### Patrol Movement
When you establish Patrol, your total Patrol Movement before the start of your next turn equals your Speed.
Movement spent through Patrol Responses:
reduces your remaining Patrol Movement;
follows a legal route;
provokes opportunity attacks normally;
cannot exceed your remaining Patrol Movement;
does not reduce your Speed during your own turn.
#### Patrol Attack Limits
A Patrol attack:
is an opportunity attack;
may be made only once per triggering creature’s turn;
cannot trigger itself;
does not deal Sneak Attack damage or comparable precision damage unless a talent explicitly permits it;
still requires a legal melee attack and a weapon, unarmed strike, or natural weapon able to reach the target.
#### Zone Talent Limit
Choose one Patrol Zone talent you know whenever you establish Patrol.
Only one Zone talent normally modifies one Patrol.

automatic_base_abilities.effect:
### Clean Harvest
Action Type: Ritual Procedure
Canonical Action Type: Ritual Procedure
Factory Routing: procedure_ledger_not_combat_action
Timing Detail: 10 minutes for ordinary work; Action only if a talent says so
Requirement: appropriate tools or a justified improvised method
Make a Gathering Check against the source’s Harvest DC.
Success: You harvest one usable Lot or specific ingredient from the source.
Success by 5 or More: Choose one benefit:
harvest one additional Lot if the source has enough material;
create a Pure Lot;
avoid harming the root, nest, vein, corpse, or future site;
learn one additional fact from Read the Sign;
avoid one minor hazard associated with the harvest.
Success by 10 or More: Create a Perfect Lot if the source can support it, or choose two benefits from Success by 5 or More.
Failure by 5 or Less: You harvest a Bruised Lot, or the Lot requires immediate sealing to remain useful.
Failure by More Than 5: The attempted Lot is lost, spoiled, contaminated, scattered, or destroyed.
Natural 1: The attempted Lot is lost and a hazard triggers if one exists. Examples include poisonous spores, biting insects, a guardian beast’s attention, a snapped root, spiritual backlash, corrosive sap, falling stone, bad air, or a broken tool.

automatic_base_abilities.effect:
### Seal the Essence
When you finish a Short Rest or spend 10 minutes with a harvested Lot, you may seal a number of Lots equal to your Proficiency Bonus + Gathering key ability modifier, minimum 1.
Sealed Lots do not spoil under ordinary travel conditions for 7 days.
At CL 5, your sealed Lots remain stable for 30 days.
At CL 10, your sealed Lots remain stable for 1 year if stored properly.
At CL 15, your sealed Lots remain stable indefinitely unless damaged, cursed, stolen, spiritually consumed, or exposed to an incompatible environment.
Sealing does not protect against every supernatural condition. Fire orchids may still require heat. Moon dew may still require darkness. Thunder fruit may still need copper seals. The GM may require special containers for Rare or higher materials.

spheres.full_exact_source_text: # Sphere of Harvesting Gathering Qi Expression: Primary — Gathering Qi; Supporting — Wood Qi, Earth-Yield Qi, Beast/Herb Qi, Seasonal Qi. Sphere Type: Mortal Utility Sphere with Cultivation Evolutions Primary Path: Any Path may learn the Mortal form Secondary Path: Qi Cultivation and Spirit Awakening are the cleanest higher-Realm access routes; Body Refining uses rugged harvesting and beast-dressing talents or Insights Resource: Time, proper tools, containers, route knowledge, permission or risk, CP for spiritual stabilization, and Stamina only for Body Refining variants that say so Core Chassis: Read the Sign, Clean Harvest, Harvest Lots, Lot Quality, Seal the Essence, Resource Sites “The mountain gives nothing twice to the hand that tears.” Common Names: Harvesting Sphere, Gathering Sphere, Herb-Gathering Sphere Sphere Type: Mortal Utility Sphere with Cultivation Evolutions Primary Users: farmers, herb-gatherers, hunters, gatherer disciples, medicine-field stewards, sect supply officers, wilderness scouts, alchemy assistants Primary Paths: Any Path may learn the Mortal form. Qi Cultivation and Spirit Awakening are the cleanest higher-Realm access routes. Body Refining can learn rugged harvesting and beast-dressing methods through specific talents or Insights. Resources: time, proper tools, containers, route knowledge, permission or risk, CP for spiritual stabilization, and Stamina for Body Refining variants Common Effects: locating useful materials, judging ripeness, safely harvesting herbs, gathering mundane crops, preserving spiritual essence, extracting beast materials, dressing cores, identifying hazards, mapping resource sites, maintaining herb stores, sect medicine-field logistics, and recovering usable alchemical ingredients ### Dao Check Harvesting and Gathering cultivates right taking. The Dao of the sphere is not growth. It is not refinement. It is not command over plants. It is the moment when a living field, mountain vein, corpse, dewfall, nest, or hidden spirit garden becomes usable material without being wasted. The central question of the sphere is: What may be taken, when, and how much may survive the taking? The recurring verb is Gather. A farmer gathers at the right season. A hunter gathers without spoiling the hide. A sect disciple gathers the Moonlit Grass before dawn burns away its yin dew. A medicine-field elder gathers one leaf and leaves the root alive for the next century. A reckless thief tears up the whole plant and ruins nine-tenths of the medicine. The sphere’s Dao must remain at the heart of the mechanics: Read the Sign. Find what is present, ripe, dangerous, guarded, or spoiled. Approach the Source. Avoid trampling, frightening, contaminating, or awakening it. Make the Clean Cut. Harvest without destroying the material’s essence. Seal the Essence. Preserve freshness, aura, dew, blood heat, mineral resonance, or beast-core stability. Record the Claim. Turn a scene resource into useful ingredients, trade goods, sect supply, or alchemical material. Talents should evolve one of these steps. If a talent does not help the cultivator find, approach, cleanly take, preserve, classify, transport, or responsibly claim materials, it probably belongs in another sphere. ### Sphere Boundary Harvesting and Gathering governs: mundane crop harvesting; herb gathering; foraging; identifying useful plants, fungi, minerals, dew, beast materials, shells, silk, resin, venom, blood, scales, bones, and cores; determining ripeness, age, grade, spoilage, and spiritual compatibility; safely harvesting spirit herbs and alchemical materials; preserving ingredients before Alchemy; dressing slain beasts for usable materials; finding and mapping resource sites; maintaining storage, route records, and sect supply ledgers; reducing waste during harvest; gathering without damaging a future crop or future site. Harvesting and Gathering does not govern: growing plants faster; creating crops from nothing; controlling plants in combat; making wood obey as a weapon; breeding spirit herbs into new species; refining pills, elixirs, smokes, or powders; cooking or alchemical transformation; broad beast taming; mining entire mountains as an industrial system; permanent formations; conjuring materials; claiming another creature’s cultivation base as a routine resource. The future Wood/Growth sphere should handle growth, plant animation, forced blooming, root control, and magical agriculture that changes how plants live. This sphere handles the moment of taking, storing, and supplying. Alchemy begins when the substance reaches the furnace. Harvesting and Gathering ends when the sealed bundle, core, herb, dew jar, mineral shard, venom ampoule, or spirit fruit is ready to hand over. ### Relation to Alchemy The current Alchemy sphere explicitly does not grow herbs, locate spiritual gardens, harvest beast cores, breed rare plants, farm medicinal fields, or create ingredients from nothing. This sphere fills that missing campaign role. Harvesting and Gathering may produce ingredients that Alchemy can refine, but it does not replace Alchemy Checks, cauldrons, recipes, Pill Saturation, Pill Impurity, Reagent Stock, or pill creation. If an Alchemy recipe requires 100 gp of suitable herbs, beast matter, mineral powder, or other ingredients, a compatible Harvest Lot from this sphere may satisfy part or all of that ingredient requirement at the GM’s discretion. ## Core Gathering Rules ### Key Ability When you learn Harvesting and Gathering, choose Wisdom or Intelligence as your Gathering key ability. Choose Wisdom if your method is field instinct, smell, weather sense, plant lore, animal tracks, farmer’s experience, or spiritual intuition. Choose Intelligence if your method is catalogues, ledgers, sect botany, taxonomy, recipe memory, mineral charts, or formal medicine-field training. Some Body Refining talents allow Constitution as the Gathering key ability for rugged endurance, beast dressing, and dangerous extraction. Gathering Check = d20 + Proficiency Bonus + Gathering key ability modifier Gathering Save DC = 8 + Proficiency Bonus + Gathering key ability modifier ### Training and Tools When you learn this sphere, gain proficiency with one of the following: herbalism kit; Nature; Survival; Medicine; land vehicles; an appropriate artisan’s tool such as woodcarver’s tools, mason’s tools, or cartographer’s tools. If you already have the chosen proficiency, choose one Mortal Realm Harvesting and Gathering talent for which you meet the prerequisites as a bonus talent. You also gain a basic gatherer’s kit if starting equipment is being assigned by class or background. A gatherer’s kit includes a small sickle, pruning knife, digging hook, cord, waxed paper, cloth wraps, small jars, simple gloves, and a field ledger. ### The Harvest Cycle The sphere uses the following engine. Step One: Read the Sign. Identify a source, its value, its danger, and whether it is ripe. Step Two: Approach the Source. Avoid disturbing the field, contaminating the plant, alerting a guardian beast, breaking a mineral vein, or losing spiritual dew. Step Three: Make the Clean Cut. Roll a Gathering Check to harvest a usable material. Step Four: Seal the Essence. Preserve the material so its value, freshness, aura, blood heat, dew, venom, or resonance does not fade. Step Five: Record the Claim. Convert the harvested material into Harvest Lots, specific ingredients, trade goods, sect credit, or quest objects. Most talents either improve one step or let one step feed another. ### Read the Sign Action Type: Multi-Mode Canonical Action Type: Multi-Mode Factory Combat Bucket: action Timing Detail: Search or Study action, or 10 minutes of field examination Factory Routing: combat_action_plus_field_examination_variant Split Review Decision: single_combat_action_plus_procedure_variant Recommended Factory Realization: procedures=TEN_MINUTE_FIELD_EXAMINATION Range: 60 feet for obvious signs; 1 mile during wilderness survey; special talents may extend this You examine plants, soil, tracks, insects, wind, dew, beast leavings, mineral seams, spirit pressure, local taboos, and terrain memory. Make a Gathering Check. The GM sets the DC by rarity, concealment, danger, and how much time you spend. On a success, learn up to three facts: whether useful materials are present; approximate rarity; whether the material is ripe, immature, spoiled, cursed, diseased, guarded, trapped, or spiritually unstable; the safest obvious method of harvest; whether the source can survive a careful harvest; whether the material is compatible with Alchemy, Medicine, Crafting, Beast Taming, Formations, Talismans, or another system; one obvious environmental danger connected to the harvest. On a failure, you learn only one incomplete fact. On a failure by 5 or more, the GM may give a misleading impression, reveal the source to a guardian, or cause the source to begin spoiling. ### Clean Harvest Action Type: Ritual Procedure Canonical Action Type: Ritual Procedure Factory Routing: procedure_ledger_not_combat_action Timing Detail: 10 minutes for ordinary work; Action only if a talent says so Requirement: appropriate tools or a justified improvised method Make a Gathering Check against the source’s Harvest DC. Success: You harvest one usable Lot or specific ingredient from the source. Success by 5 or More: Choose one benefit: harvest one additional Lot if the source has enough material; create a Pure Lot; avoid harming the root, nest, vein, corpse, or future site; learn one additional fact from Read the Sign; avoid one minor hazard associated with the harvest. Success by 10 or More: Create a Perfect Lot if the source can support it, or choose two benefits from Success by 5 or More. Failure by 5 or Less: You harvest a Bruised Lot, or the Lot requires immediate sealing to remain useful. Failure by More Than 5: The attempted Lot is lost, spoiled, contaminated, scattered, or destroyed. Natural 1: The attempted Lot is lost and a hazard triggers if one exists. Examples include poisonous spores, biting insects, a guardian beast’s attention, a snapped root, spiritual backlash, corrosive sap, falling stone, bad air, or a broken tool. ### Harvest DC and Rarity Use these DCs unless the source, terrain, or story sets a different number. Common material: DC 12. Typical value 25 gp as Alchemy-compatible ingredient value. Uncommon material: DC 15. Typical value 100 gp. Rare material: DC 18. Typical value 500 gp. Very Rare material: DC 22. Typical value 2,500 gp. Legendary material: DC 28. Typical value 10,000 gp plus story restrictions. Secret material: Special DC, special cost, and story consequences. These values match ingredient-cost language rather than guaranteed resale value. A harvested Lot can usually be sold for half its listed value in ordinary markets, more to the right buyer, or much less where the material is illegal, cursed, spoiled, common, or politically controlled. ### Harvest Lots A Harvest Lot is a sealed, usable portion of raw material. Examples include: a bundle of medicinal herbs; a spirit fruit; bark curls from a sacred tree; sealed dew from moon grass; a fungus cap harvested at the correct hour; powdered mineral scraped from a vein; venom in a waxed ampoule; beast gall, horn, claw, hide, bone, scale, silk, shell, or blood; a low-grade beast core; a jar of spirit soil; resin, incense wood, or aromatic root; petals, seeds, pollen, or bitter leaves. A Lot must come from a source that exists in the scene, downtime, market, sect field, wilderness route, or strategic project. This sphere does not create Lots from nothing. ### Lot Quality Bruised Lot. Usable, but unstable. If used for Alchemy, increase the Alchemy Check DC by 2 or count it as 25 percent less ingredient value. A Bruised Lot spoils at the end of your next Long Rest unless sealed. Normal Lot. Usable at listed value. Pure Lot. Exceptionally clean. If used for Alchemy, choose one: reduce the Alchemy Check DC by 1, count as 25 percent more ingredient value for one compatible recipe, or reduce backlash damage from that recipe by your Proficiency Bonus. Perfect Lot. Rarely wasted. If used for Alchemy, choose one: reduce the Alchemy Check DC by 2, count as 50 percent more ingredient value for one compatible recipe, reduce Pill Impurity gained by 1 if the recipe could do so, or permit a recipe quality improvement with GM approval. ### Seal the Essence When you finish a Short Rest or spend 10 minutes with a harvested Lot, you may seal a number of Lots equal to your Proficiency Bonus + Gathering key ability modifier, minimum 1. Sealed Lots do not spoil under ordinary travel conditions for 7 days. At CL 5, your sealed Lots remain stable for 30 days. At CL 10, your sealed Lots remain stable for 1 year if stored properly. At CL 15, your sealed Lots remain stable indefinitely unless damaged, cursed, stolen, spiritually consumed, or exposed to an incompatible environment. Sealing does not protect against every supernatural condition. Fire orchids may still require heat. Moon dew may still require darkness. Thunder fruit may still need copper seals. The GM may require special containers for Rare or higher materials. ### Resource Sites A Resource Site is a place that can produce Harvest Lots. Examples: village field; herb patch; forest grove; cliff fungus shelf; spirit spring; mineral seam; beast lair; medicine garden; ancient battlefield; secret realm meadow; sect supply mountain; corpse of a magical beast; storm-struck tree; moonlit pond; cursed marsh. The GM decides how many Lots a Resource Site can support. This sphere improves how much is recovered and how safely it is recovered; it does not force a depleted site to produce new material. ### Ripe, Immature, and Overripe Materials A material may be: Immature. Not ready. Harvesting it creates a Bruised Lot at best and usually harms the future site. Ripe. Ready. Harvest normally. Overripe. Powerful but unstable. Increase the Harvest DC by 2. On success by 5 or more, create a Pure Lot. On failure, trigger a hazard. Awakened. The material has instinct, spirit, mobility, omen, guardian behavior, or karmic attachment. It may require negotiation, combat, stealth, spiritual permission, or a special talent. ## Base Sphere Abilities This v1.10.5 section is a parsing map, not an additional feature grant. It names the rules below that should be treated as the sphere's base package during character creation, dashboard import, Roll20 export, and combat simulation. - Read the Sign is the base information-gathering ability for locating useful materials and judging site pressure. - Clean Harvest is the base ability for taking material without ruining the source. - Harvest Lots and Lot Quality define how much useful material is gained and how good it is. - Seal the Essence is the base preservation method for keeping gathered materials usable. - Resource Sites, ripe/immature/overripe materials, and Harvest DC are the default GM-facing constraints. ## Talent Tags Sign Talents. Improve Read the Sign, resource detection, classification, scouting, or hazard prediction. Approach Talents. Help reach or prepare a source without damaging it or waking its danger. Cut Talents. Improve Clean Harvest, extraction, field dressing, beast cores, or dangerous materials. Seal Talents. Preserve freshness, aura, dew, venom, blood heat, mineral resonance, or spirit pressure. Route Talents. Improve transport, maps, supply chains, markets, caches, and sect delivery. Steward Talents. Improve long-term harvest management without growing plants magically. Hazard Talents. Resist poison, spores, curses, backlash, guardian signs, bad air, and dangerous sites. Realm Evolution Talents. Open higher-Realm harvesting and spiritual resource command. Unique Talents. Rare techniques that may reshape campaigns. ## Mortal Realm Talents ### Farmer’s Eye - Sign, Steward You can judge ordinary crops, herbs, seed grain, soil moisture, rot, pests, mold, and harvest timing at a glance. After 10 minutes inspecting a mundane field, garden, orchard, storehouse, or herb bed, make a Gathering Check. DC 10: Learn whether the crop is healthy, threatened, ready, immature, or overripe. DC 15: Identify one practical mundane intervention such as drying, pruning, sorting, pest removal, drainage, shade, harvest timing, or storage adjustment. During downtime, if you supervise an ordinary farm or herb bed for at least 7 days during a season, reduce mundane spoilage, waste, or storage loss by a meaningful amount set by the GM. This does not make plants grow faster and does not create spiritual herbs. ### Common Herbcraft - Sign, Cut You have Advantage on Gathering Checks to identify and harvest Common medicinal herbs, edible plants, fungi, roots, berries, and ordinary field materials. When you succeed on Clean Harvest for a Common plant or fungus by 5 or more, you may create one additional Common Lot if the source contains enough material. ### Clean Sickle Method - Cut When you make a Clean Harvest check with proper tools, add +2 to the roll. If you harvest a plant, fungus, resin, fruit, bark, or root and succeed by 5 or more, the source survives unless the material can only be harvested destructively. This bonus does not stack with another item or talent bonus to the same check. Use the higher bonus. ### Root-Left-Alive Method - Cut, Steward When you harvest a plant, fungus, coral, moss, spirit grass, or comparable living source, you may choose to reduce the number of Lots gained by 1, minimum 0. On a success by 5 or more, improve the price, receive a useful rumor about a Resource Site, or gain minor sect credit. This talent does not guarantee a buyer for illegal, cursed, stolen, Rare, or politically restricted materials. ### Dew Jar Method - Seal You learn how to collect dew, sap, resin, honey, rainwater, mineral seep, brine, and other delicate liquids without wasting their essence. You may Clean Harvest liquids and delicate residues that ordinary harvesters would lose. When you seal a liquid Lot, it remains stable for twice the normal duration. ### Simple Beast Dressing - Cut When you harvest meat, hide, horn, bone, sinew, venom, gall, feathers, scale, shell, or other ordinary beast materials from a slain creature, make one Gathering Check. On a success, recover usable materials worth an amount set by the GM for the creature and scene. On a success by 5 or more, choose one: recover an additional minor Lot; avoid tainting the material with blood, bile, or rot; identify whether the creature carried poison, disease, spiritual residue, or useful organs. This talent does not harvest true beast cores unless you later learn Beast-Core Dressing. ### Camp Gatherer - Route During a Long Rest in the wilderness, you may gather ordinary food, fuel, water, and simple medicinal plants for a number of creatures equal to twice your Proficiency Bonus + your Gathering key ability modifier, minimum 2. If the terrain is barren, cursed, hostile, urban, or magically depleted, the GM may require a Gathering Check or declare the area unsuitable. ### First-Aid Poultice - Seal, Hazard During a Short Rest, spend one Common medicinal Lot to prepare poultices for up to your Proficiency Bonus creatures. A treated creature gains Advantage on the first saving throw it makes against poison, disease, or Exhaustion from travel before its next Long Rest. A creature can benefit from your First-Aid Poultice once per Long Rest. ## Foundation Realm Talents ### Spirit-Herb Appraisal - Sign, Realm Evolution Prerequisite: CL 5+. Take the moment in which the garden offers one leaf.” You may attempt to harvest a Secret material without destroying the source, even when ordinary doctrine says the source must be uprooted, slain, mined out, or consumed entirely. This requires a major scene, not a routine check. Declare one intended Secret harvest: one petal from a world lotus; one drop of dragon vein marrow; one fruit from a tree that blooms once per age; one thread from a heavenly silkworm cocoon; one scale from a sleeping sovereign beast; one ember from a tribulation-struck root; one tear from an ancient spring; one bone shaving from a willing saintly remnant. Make a Gathering Check against a DC set by the GM, usually 30 or higher. On success, gain the Secret material and preserve the source. On success by 5 or more, the Secret material is Perfect. On failure, choose one: gain nothing and preserve the source; gain the material in Bruised form but trigger a major consequence; abandon the attempt and owe the source, guardian, sect, or Heaven a debt. On Natural 1, the source rejects the harvest. Resolve a story consequence such as a guardian awakening, secret-realm collapse, curse mark, oath debt, sect alarm, beast pursuit, or heavenly omen. This inheritance should be rare. It changes how sects think about priceless materials. ## Variant Scriptures and Drawbacks Harvesting and Gathering variants are optional sphere-specific limitations. They are not imported from any other rules system. Unless the GM says otherwise: choose at most one Harvesting and Gathering drawback when first learning the sphere or undergoing major initiation; drawbacks are mutually exclusive; the drawback applies to all Harvesting and Gathering talents; if a drawback grants a bonus talent whose prerequisites are not yet met, gain the talent when you meet the prerequisites; if the drawback is removed or retrained, lose the bonus talent or benefit it granted. ### Mortal Agrarian Scripture “A thousand full bowls are also a kind of immortality.” #### Drawback: Field-Bound Practice Your sphere is rooted in farms, orchards, storehouses, village herb beds, and sect medicine fields. You cannot use Harvesting and Gathering talents to harvest beast cores, dangerous monster organs, Secret materials, or materials from active combat scenes unless you later receive separate wilderness or sect training. You have Disadvantage on Gathering Checks made in uncivilized wilderness, cursed ruins, secret realms, or monster lairs where your method does not apply. #### Benefit Gain Farmer’s Eye as a bonus talent. When supervising mundane farms or herb beds during downtime, increase the practical benefit of reduced spoilage, better timing, and cleaner storage. At CL 5, gain Sect Medicine-Field Steward as a bonus talent when you meet its prerequisites. ### Wild Herb-Seeker Scripture “The old root hides where maps become lies.” #### Drawback: No Garden Reliance Your method works through wilderness signs, cliffs, caves, marshes, old forests, beast territories, secret valleys, and spiritual weather. You have Disadvantage on downtime checks to manage farms, warehouses, market bundles, and large teams. You cannot gain Sect Medicine-Field Steward, Companion Gatherers, or Pill-Hall Supply Chain unless you retrain this scripture or receive sect logistics training. #### Benefit Gain Hidden Herb Scent as a bonus talent when you meet its prerequisites, or Common Herbcraft if you are below CL 5. When you successfully Read the Sign in uncultivated wilderness, learn one extra fact. ### Beast-Carver Scripture “Hide, horn, gall, and core: the hunt is not finished when the beast falls.” #### Drawback: Beast-Material Focus Your Harvesting and Gathering talents apply only to slain beasts, monster remains, shed materials, nests, eggshells, venom, blood, bone, hide, scale, feather, horn, core, and related animal resources. You cannot harvest living plants, spirit herbs, fungi, dew, mineral veins, or farm goods with sphere talents except for ordinary Survival checks. #### Benefit Gain Simple Beast Dressing as a bonus talent. At CL 5, gain Beast-Core Dressing as a bonus talent when you meet its prerequisites. When a beast-material harvest triggers backlash, reduce the damage by your Proficiency Bonus. ### Root-Respecting Scripture “The greedy gatherer returns to an empty mountain.” #### Drawback: Never Uproot Needlessly You cannot intentionally destroy a living Resource Site for extra yield unless the source is hostile, doomed, corrupted, invasive, or already dead. When a talent would give extra Lots, you must first choose an option that preserves the source if possible. If you knowingly kill a source for convenience, you lose the benefit of this scripture until you atone through restoration, repayment, or a new oath. #### Benefit Gain Root-Left-Alive Method as a bonus talent. At CL 10, gain Source-Sparing Harvest as a bonus talent when you meet its prerequisites. When you preserve a source while harvesting a Lot, the Lot counts as Pure if you succeeded by 5 or more. ### Sect Tithe Scripture “The mountain belongs to the sect. The sect permits your hand.” #### Drawback: Accounted Harvest You must record valuable harvests and tithe a portion to your sect, clan, office, village, or patron. If you hide or sell tithed materials without permission, you lose this scripture’s benefit until you repay the debt or resolve the social consequence. You have Disadvantage on checks to sell restricted materials outside approved channels. #### Benefit Gain Field Ledger as a bonus talent. At CL 5, gain Medicine Mountain Map as a bonus talent when you meet its prerequisites. When delivering Lots to your recognized patron, you may convert some market value into sect credit, favors, mission standing, or access to guarded Resource Sites. ### Hazard-Taker Scripture “The best herbs grow where sensible people die.” #### Drawback: Dangerous Preference You suffer Disadvantage on Gathering Checks for safe, mundane, routine, or farmed materials. You cannot benefit from Market Bundle or Camp Gatherer unless the situation involves a hazard, forbidden site, monster territory, cursed environment, or spiritual instability. #### Benefit Gain Bitter-Spore Caution as a bonus talent. At CL 5, gain Hazardous Harvest as a bonus talent when you meet its prerequisites. When you successfully harvest a material from a hazardous site, you may treat the Lot as Pure once per Short Rest. ## Path Synergies ### Qi Cultivation - Qi-Scent Gathering You may spend CP to steady Gathering Checks. Before making a Gathering Check for a spiritual material, spend up to your Proficiency Bonus CP. Each CP spent adds +1 to the check. If you spend at least 1 CP this way and succeed, you also learn the material’s broad qi tendency, such as hot, cold, dry, wet, yin, yang, thunder, wind, blood, mineral, poison, life, death, or neutral. ### Spirit Awakening - Listening to the Living Sign You may use Wisdom as your Gathering key ability even if you originally chose Intelligence. When you Read the Sign, you may sense emotional residue, old fear, guardian intent, pollution, spiritual resentment, or whether a source has been overharvested. Once per Long Rest, when you would trigger a source’s spiritual hazard on a failed Clean Harvest, reroll the check. You must use the new result. ### Body Refining - Hard-Hand Gatherer You may use Constitution as your Gathering key ability for checks involving endurance, dangerous terrain, poisonous materials, beast dressing, climbing to a harvest, carrying heavy bundles, resisting hazard exposure, or harvesting from slain creatures. You may spend Stamina instead of CP for Harvesting and Gathering talents that protect your body, steady your hands, or resist harvesting hazards. You cannot use this synergy to sense distant herbs, spiritually negotiate with living sources, or seal materials through qi projection unless another feature permits it. ## Cultivation Insights ### Herb-Gatherer’s Foundation Prerequisite: Harvesting and Gathering, CL 4+. Choose one Sign or Cut talent you know. Once per Short Rest, when you use that talent and roll a Gathering Check, add a d4 to the roll after seeing the d20 but before knowing the outcome. At CL 10, the die becomes a d6. ### Body of Thorns and Spores Prerequisite: Body Refining, Harvesting and Gathering, CL 4+. Gain the Body Refining path synergy for this sphere. You have Advantage on saving throws against poison, disease, spores, irritating pollen, thorns, heat, cold, hunger, thirst, bad air, and harvest-site hazards. ### Medicine-Field Steward Prerequisite: Harvesting and Gathering, CL 4+. Gain Farmer’s Eye or Sect Medicine-Field Steward as a bonus talent. If you do not yet meet the prerequisite for Sect Medicine-Field Steward, gain it when you reach CL 5. When you supervise a mundane farm or medicine field during downtime, workers under you have Advantage on ordinary checks to harvest without waste. ### Beast-Core Butcher Prerequisite: Harvesting and Gathering, Simple Beast Dressing, CL 8+. Gain Beast-Core Dressing as a bonus talent when you meet its prerequisites. When you harvest beast materials from a creature whose CR is no higher than your CL, a failure by 5 or less creates a Bruised Lot instead of losing the material. ### Sect Supply Officer Prerequisite: Harvesting and Gathering, Field Ledger, CL 8+. You may maintain twice as many active recorded sites in your Field Ledger. When you deliver Harvest Lots to a sect, clan, army, village, market, or pill hall, you may turn part of their value into favors, mission credit, safe lodging, or access to restricted information with GM approval. ### Jade-Seal Preserver Prerequisite: Harvesting and Gathering, Spirit-Sealing Wax, CL 8+. When you Seal the Essence of a Common or Uncommon Lot, you may treat one Bruised Lot as Normal quality. At CL 10, you may use this on Rare Lots. ### Thousand-Mile Forager Prerequisite: Harvesting and Gathering, CL 8+. Your travel pace is not reduced while foraging, mapping, or searching for Common Resource Sites in ordinary wilderness. During a journey, once per day you may make one Read the Sign check for the region without slowing the group. ### Ethical Gatherer Prerequisite: Harvesting and Gathering, CL 8+. When you preserve a living source that you could have destroyed for greater yield, gain Inspiration if the GM agrees the choice mattered. Once per Long Rest, when you use Root-Left-Alive Method or Source-Sparing Harvest, gain Advantage on the Gathering Check.

harvest one additional Lot if the source has enough material;
create a Pure Lot;
avoid harming the root, nest, vein, corpse, or future site;
learn one additional fact from Read the Sign;

### Seal the Essence
When you finish a Short Rest or spend 10 minutes with a harvested Lot, you may seal a number of Lots equal to your Proficiency Bonus + Gathering key ability modifier, minimum 1.
Sealed Lots do not spoil under ordinary travel conditions for 7 days.
At CL 5, your sealed Lots remain stable for 30 days.
At CL 10, your sealed Lots remain stable for 1 year if stored properly.
At CL 15, your sealed Lots remain stable indefinitely unless damaged, cursed, stolen, spiritually consumed, or exposed to an incompatible environment.
Sealing does not protect against every supernatural condition. Fire orchids may still require heat. Moon dew may still require darkness. Thunder fruit may still need copper seals. The GM may require special containers for Rare or higher materials.

spheres.full_exact_source_text: # Sphere of The Hidden Eye Qi Expression: Primary — Perception Qi; Supporting — Omen Qi, Water-Depth Qi, Light-Revelation Qi. “The careless hunter asks where the enemy went. The patient hunter asks what the enemy was forced to reveal by going there.” Common Name: Scout Sphere Sphere Type: Martial Sphere Primary Paths: All Paths Resource: Martial Focus Common Effects: Stealth, tracking, situational awareness, threat assessment, monster lore, forensic examination, counter-surveillance, ambushes, weakness exploitation, and battlefield profiling #### HIDDEN EYE DAO The Sphere of the Hidden Eye is the cultivation of decisive information. A Hidden Eye cultivator does not merely notice more things than other people. They learn which detail matters before anyone else understands that a decision has already been made. A broken reed may reveal the weight of a fleeing enemy. A faint medicinal smell may identify a concealed wound. A hesitation before a sword stroke may expose the technique that will follow. A scuffed tile may reveal the pressure plate beneath it. A false smile may reveal which question a sect elder most fears answering. The sphere’s recurring loop is: Approach carefully. Choose how you gather information. Observe or pursue. Search the scene, read the trail, question the witness, or study the opponent. Analyze the target. Convert clues into usable knowledge. Exploit the opening. Apply Research talents, stalk unseen, or advise allies. Keep watching. A skilled scout learns from every reaction the enemy makes. The Hidden Eye should support: sect outriders; ruin delvers; demon hunters; caravan pathfinders; battlefield observers; imperial inspectors; bodyguards trained to detect ambushes; assassins who study a target before striking; wandering cultivators who survive by noticing danger first; spirit investigators who identify curses, possession, or hostile surveillance. The sphere is intentionally broader than wilderness tracking. It is the sphere of the cultivated scout, investigator, stalker, and tactical analyst. #### USING THE HIDDEN EYE WITH 5.5E RULES Use the ordinary 2024 fifth-edition rules unless a Hidden Eye feature explicitly says otherwise. Search is a Wisdom-based Action used to discern something that is not obvious. Study is an Intelligence-based Action used to recall or deduce information. For Hidden Eye talents, hidden normally means that you currently benefit from the Invisible condition granted by a successful Hide Action. A talent may explicitly expand that meaning. Tremorsense pinpoints creatures and moving objects under its normal rules, but it does not count as sight. Truesight and Blindsight use their ordinary 2024 meanings. Hidden Eye does not automatically grant a free Search, Study, or Hide Action; reveal a target’s complete stat block; reveal an exact location through Total Cover; or let you remain hidden after an attack roll unless a feature explicitly says so. #### MARTIAL FOCUS The Hidden Eye uses Martial Focus. You may hold one Martial Focus at a time. Some talents expend Martial Focus. Expending Martial Focus is not an Action. You cannot expend Martial Focus if you do not currently hold it. If a talent says you regain Martial Focus, regain it only if it is currently absent. Martial Focus is a state of physical readiness, controlled breath, posture, and intent. It is not CP. #### CORE HIDDEN EYE RULES ##### Analyze Time: 10 minutes, or 1 Action by expending Martial Focus Range: 60 feet Target: One creature you can see within range, unless an Approach talent provides another valid method Duration: 24 hours, or until you finish a Long Rest Attempt Use Limit: Once per individual target per Long Rest, unless a talent says otherwise Choose Intelligence (Investigation) or Wisdom (Perception). Make the chosen ability check against the target’s Analyze DC. Analyze DC = 10 + the target’s Challenge Rating, rounded down. If a creature does not have a Challenge Rating but has a Cultivation Level, use half its CL, rounded down, in place of its Challenge Rating. For a creature built with ordinary character levels but no CL or Challenge Rating, use half its level, rounded down. Successful Check: Learn one Analyzable Characteristic of your choice. The target becomes Analyzed by you for the duration. Failed Check: Learn nothing. The attempt still counts against your limit for that individual target. Analyze is a special Hidden Eye feature. It is not automatically a Search action or Study action, even when it uses a skill associated with one of those actions. Unless a talent says otherwise: Analyze affects creatures, not objects, locations, traps, Formations, or techniques; the target does not automatically know that you attempted to Analyze it; being Analyzed does not reveal the target’s location; being Analyzed does not let you see an Invisible or hidden target; being Analyzed does not bypass cover, range, or targeting requirements; another Hidden Eye cultivator does not automatically benefit from your analysis; each characteristic choice reveals one entry, not an entire category; analysis reveals the target as it can currently be observed and understood; disguises, transformations, illusions, higher-Realm concealment, and false spiritual signatures may interfere unless a talent says otherwise. ##### Analyzed by You A creature is Analyzed by you after you successfully use Analyze on it. Research talents apply only to creatures Analyzed by you unless a talent explicitly allows you to share your analysis. This Inheritance does not automatically defeat a superior Realm, destroy an artifact, negate a Formation core, reveal a creature behind Total Cover, or overwrite another Secret Inheritance without a cultivation-scale contest. #### CULTIVATION VARIANTS These variants are optional starting alterations. A character normally chooses no more than one variant unless the GM approves a combined concept. ##### Alternative Approach You cannot use Intelligence (Investigation) or Wisdom (Perception) for Analyze by default. Learn one Approach talent as a bonus talent. ##### Hidden Eyes You do not gain Analyze and cannot learn Approach or Research talents. Learn Fast Stealth as a bonus talent. This variant supports pure infiltrators, assassins, and scouts who rely on concealment rather than tactical profiling. ##### Rivalrous A creature you successfully Analyze also treats you as Analyzed by it for the same duration. Whenever you learn one of its Analyzable Characteristics, it learns the corresponding characteristic about you if you possess one. It may apply any Research talents you possess against you as though it knew those talents. Learn Worthy Opponent as a bonus talent. ##### Seeker You do not gain Skill Affinity: Stealth. Learn Trained Awareness as a bonus talent. This variant supports investigators, sentinels, scholars, and ruin delvers who are not primarily infiltrators. #### PATH SYNERGIES ##### Body Refining - Predator’s Still-Blood Discipline A Body Refiner learns to still breath, pulse, footfall, and killing intent. Once per turn when the Body Refiner expends Martial Focus on a Stalker talent or Part-Breaker, they may spend 1 Stamina to move up to 10 feet without provoking Opportunity Attacks. This movement must end closer to cover, concealment, the analyzed target, or a tracked trail. ##### Qi Cultivation - Ten-Thousand-Thread Calculation A Qi Cultivator reads small details as a pattern of circulating causes. When the Qi Cultivator successfully Analyzes a creature, they may spend 1 Qi to learn one additional Analyzable Characteristic. Once per Long Rest, when they use Study to recall lore about a creature, Formation, magical effect, or ruin, they may spend 1 Qi to treat a d20 roll of 9 or lower as a 10. ##### Spirit Awakening - Soul-Scent Appraisal A Spirit Awakener learns to distinguish the pressure and emotional residue of individual souls. When the Spirit Awakener successfully Analyzes a creature, they may spend 1 Resonance to learn its current strongest emotion and whether its visible body is possessed, spiritually displaced, or carrying a foreign spiritual presence detectable by the GM. This does not identify the possessor, reveal hidden memories, or automatically overcome a higher-Realm concealment technique. #### CULTIVATION INSIGHTS ##### Patient Hunter Prerequisite: Hidden Eye sphere When you fail an Analyze check, you may repeat the attempt against that creature after 1 hour of observation, tracking, conversation, or investigation without waiting for a Long Rest. Use Patient Hunter once per creature per Long Rest. ##### Ruin Delver’s Habit Gain proficiency in either Investigation or Survival. When you take the Search or Study action to detect a trap, environmental hazard, unstable structure, hidden passage, or Formation component, add 1d4 to the check. ##### Veiled Breath Prerequisite: Hidden Eye sphere After you take the Hide action, you may remain hidden while speaking in a whisper to one creature within 5 feet of you or communicating through a similarly quiet agreed signal. This Insight does not let you cast a spell with a Verbal component without ending the hidden state. ##### Demon-Hunter’s Ledger Prerequisite: Hidden Eye sphere When you finish a Long Rest, choose one creature type other than Humanoid. The first time you successfully Analyze a creature of that type before your next Long Rest, learn one additional Analyzable Characteristic. ##### Lantern Against Ghosts Prerequisite: Hidden Eye sphere, Magical Cognizance or Spirit Awakening Path You have Advantage on Search checks made to detect possession, magical sensors, invisible spiritual entities, and lingering hostile spiritual residue. This Insight does not grant a sense, reveal exact locations through Total Cover, or identify an effect automatically.

### Taste the Qi
Action Type: Bonus Action
Factory Combat Bucket: bonus_action
Factory Routing: combat_action_row
Range: 30 feet
Target: One creature, corpse, meal, ingredient, beast core, spiritual dish, visible residue, or container you can perceive
Cost: None
Duration: Until the end of your next turn, or 1 minute outside combat
You taste the spiritual pressure of the target.
Choose one question:
- Is this target spiritually nourishing, poisonous, corrupted, empty, undead, demonic, beast-born, cultivator-born, artificial, or spiritually inert?
- Is this creature Bloodied?
- What is the strongest obvious qi expression in this target?
- Does this meal or ingredient contain Impurity?
- Is this creature or ingredient suitable for a Hunger talent you know?
- Is this target protected by an obvious anti-consumption ward, corpse seal, preservation formation, or oath-mark?
If the target is unwilling and actively concealing its nature, make a Hunger Check contested by the target's Charisma or Constitution saving throw, chosen by the GM.
Success: you learn the answer.
Failure: you learn only whether the target is spiritually nourishing or spiritually dangerous.
Taste the Qi does not reveal full stat blocks, secret names, exact levels, complete sphere lists, hidden plot information, or the full contents of a sealed storage treasure.

### Refine the Meal
Action Type: Multi-Mode
Canonical Action Type: Multi-Mode
Factory Routing: procedure_ledger_not_combat_action
Split Review Decision: procedure_only_not_combat_action
Recommended Factory Realization: procedures=TEN_MINUTE_REFINE, SHORT_REST_REFINE
Timing Detail: 10-minute ritual, or part of a short rest
Range: Touch
Target: One Essence Portion, prepared meal, spiritual ingredient, or suitable corpse portion
Cost: 1 CP, plus the ingredient
You spiritually prepare and consume an Essence Portion.
Make a Hunger Check.
Common Portion DC 12.
Notable Portion DC 15.
Mighty Portion DC 18.
Corrupted Portion increases the DC by 2.
A portion from a creature above your Realm increases the DC by 2.
Success: gain 1 Satiety charge tied to the meal source.
Success by 5 or More: gain 1 Satiety and choose one additional benefit:
- reduce Impurity by 1;
- gain Temporary HP equal to your Proficiency Bonus;
- the next Digestive Mantle using this Satiety costs 0 CP;
- learn one harmless sensory memory from the ingredient, such as fear, territory, prey, predator, season, death-sign, or last hunger.
Failure: you do not gain Satiety. The ingredient is consumed.
Failure by 5 or More: you do not gain Satiety and gain 1 Impurity.
