automatic_base_abilities.effect:
### Digestive Mantle
Action Type: Bonus Action
Factory Combat Bucket: bonus_action
Factory Routing: combat_action_row
Range: Self
Target: Self
Duration: 1 minute
Cost: 1 CP and 1 Satiety
You ignite one Satiety charge inside your meridians and wear its nourishment as a temporary cultivation state.
When you activate Digestive Mantle, gain Temporary HP equal to:
**twice your Proficiency Bonus + your Hunger key ability modifier**
Then choose one basic Mantle benefit appropriate to the consumed source.
Beast Strength: Gain Advantage on Strength checks and Strength saving throws. Once before the Mantle ends, when you hit with a melee attack or unarmed strike, add your Proficiency Bonus to the damage roll.
Predator Step: Your Speed increases by 10 feet. Once before the Mantle ends, when you move at least 10 feet straight toward a creature and hit it with an attack on the same turn, add your Proficiency Bonus to the damage roll.
Iron Stomach: Gain Advantage on saving throws against Poisoned and Disease. When you succeed on such a saving throw while the Mantle is active, gain Temporary HP equal to your Proficiency Bonus.
Thick Hide: Once per round when you take Bludgeoning, Piercing, or Slashing damage, reduce that damage by your Proficiency Bonus + your Hunger key ability modifier.
Venom Belly: Once per turn when you hit with an attack, deal extra Poison or Acid damage equal to your Proficiency Bonus + your Hunger key ability modifier.
Furnace Belly: Once per turn when you hit with an attack, deal extra Fire damage equal to your Proficiency Bonus + your Hunger key ability modifier.
Elemental Gut: Choose Acid, Cold, Fire, Lightning, Necrotic, Poison, or Thunder, as appropriate to the Satiety source. You gain Resistance to that damage type while the Mantle lasts. If the source was only weakly associated with the type, the GM may limit this Resistance to the first triggering damage instance each round.
Deep Nourishment: When you activate the Mantle, end one nonmagical hunger, thirst, forced-march, or travel-fatigue penalty that has not become Exhaustion. While the Mantle lasts, you have Advantage on Constitution saving throws against Exhaustion caused by travel, starvation, thirst, exposure, disease, or hostile terrain.
Demon-Beast Course: Choose two basic Mantle benefits above that fit the demon beast instead of one. Gain 1 Impurity when the Mantle ends unless another talent changes this.
Cultivator Course: If a Forbidden Hunger talent lets you create Forbidden Satiety, a Digestive Mantle using that Satiety may choose one basic Mantle benefit that fits the consumed cultivator's Path or known sphere. Some Forbidden Hunger talents improve this benefit.
You can benefit from only one Digestive Mantle at a time. Activating a new Digestive Mantle ends the previous one.

spheres.full_exact_source_text: # Sphere of Hunger Qi Types: hunger qi, nourishment qi, beast qi, blood-vitality qi, furnace qi, dross qi, impurity qi; forbidden methods add cultivator qi, dantian qi, soul-residue qi, and stolen-meridian qi. "The bowl is empty. That is why Heaven moves." Common Name: Hunger Sphere Sphere Type: Restricted Power Sphere; Gourmand Sphere; Beast-Consumption and Self-Temperance Sphere; Secret and Forbidden Inheritance Sphere Primary Path: Qi Cultivation Secondary Paths: Body Refining and Spirit Awakening Key Themes: appetite, spiritual digestion, nourishment, famine, monster meat, spirit-beast cuisine, demon-beast tempering, poison resistance, body-furnace refinement, banquet rites, illegal cultivator consumption, stolen essence, and the difference between eating and becoming what one eats Primary Resource Hooks: CP, Essence Portions, Satiety, Impurity, Appetite Stain, prepared meals, spiritual ingredients, spirit-beast portions, demon-beast portions, and forbidden cultivator residue Core Chassis: Taste the Qi, Refine the Meal, Digestive Mantle Common Effects: spiritual eating, spirit-beast meals, demon-beast digestion, self-buffing, temporary resistances, temporary damage expressions, survival, poison resistance, nourishment rites, shared meals, impurity management, monster-derived adaptations, and forbidden cultivator-devouring shortcuts ## Hunger Dao Hunger is the Dao of need becoming motion. Fire consumes because it changes what it touches. Wood hungers because life must grow. Earth stores grain because famine is real. Blood hungers because bodies must continue. The spirit hungers because desire outlives flesh. The Sphere of Hunger begins from one question: What does this essence want to become inside me? A cook prepares food. An alchemist refines medicine. A harvester gathers ingredients. A beastmaster bonds with beasts. A Hunger cultivator turns consumption itself into a cultivation method. Their stomach, dantian, marrow, meridians, soul, or appetite becomes a furnace. The recurring verbs of Hunger are: Taste. Learn what the essence is. Refine. Prepare it without wasting or poisoning the foundation. Digest. Convert the essence into a temporary mantle. Legal Hunger is the art of eating without becoming what one eats. Forbidden Hunger is the art of deciding that other cultivators are also ingredients. ## Sphere Boundary Hunger governs: - spiritual eating and cultivated digestion; - qi gourmand techniques; - preparation and consumption of spirit-beast and demon-beast ingredients; - temporary self-buffs from eaten essence; - sensing whether something is nourishing, poisoned, corrupted, demonic, beast-born, or spiritually empty; - survival through famine, forced march, harsh climate, and impure food; - poison, venom, disease, impurity, and hostile digestion themes; - shared meals and expedition rations; - temporary monster-derived adaptations; - forbidden cultivator-devouring rites when using the forbidden subsection. Hunger does not govern: - ordinary cooking without spiritual essence; - hospitality, cuisine, or culture as their own social systems; - pill refinement, alchemical recipes, cauldrons, or elixirs; - farming, growing herbs, or creating ingredients; - harvesting a corpse cleanly for many useful materials; - stable beast taming or companion bonds; - permanent shapeshifting; - permanent talent theft; - broad necromancy; - general blood control; - full Daemonic Cultivation corruption, mutation, domains, or limit-breaking. If a rule is mainly about obtaining materials, use Harvesting and Gathering. If it is mainly about refining medicine or pills, use Alchemy. If it is mainly about bonding with a living creature, use Beastmastery. If it is mainly about blood as a controllable substance, use Blood. If it is mainly about corruption, mutation, and forbidden second-engine power, use Daemonic Cultivation. ## Hunger Access Hunger is Restricted by default. It is not automatically forbidden, but many sects require registration, inspection, supervised kitchens, purity records, and ingredient ledgers. Qi Cultivation is the cleanest route. Qi gourmands use furnace breath, internal cauldron visualization, dantian digestion, spiritual seasoning, and qi circulation after meals. Body Refining expresses Hunger as stomach furnace, marrow digestion, iron belly, beast-bone broth, muscle nourishment, organ tempering, and demon-meat endurance. Spirit Awakening expresses Hunger as desire-reading, appetite pressure, soul craving, famine memory, taste of fear, and the spiritual meaning of need. A character may learn normal Hunger talents through ordinary sphere acquisition if the campaign permits Restricted spheres. Secret Hunger talents require a teacher, scripture, jade slip, sect kitchen inheritance, monster-hunter lineage, imperial banquet office, or other story permission. Forbidden Hunger talents require a forbidden source and carry Appetite Stain. ## 2024 Fifth-Edition Rules Baseline Hunger uses the 2024 Fifth Edition action economy unless a talent says otherwise. Action Type: Rules Reference Canonical Action Type: Rules Reference Timing Detail: A Hunger option states whether it uses an Action, Bonus Action, Reaction, Search action, Study action, 10-minute ritual, 1-hour ritual, short-rest activity, or long-rest activity Factory Routing: rules_reference_not_character_action Split Review Decision: rules_reference_not_character_action Recommended Factory Realization: no_character_action_row Attacks and Saves: Hunger attacks and Hunger Save DCs use the Hunger key ability. When a talent calls for a saving throw, the target rolls against your Hunger Save DC. Cover and Line of Effect: Hunger does not bypass Total Cover, sealed containers, warded kitchens, closed formations, or hidden corpses unless a talent explicitly says so. Concentration: Hunger talents do not require Concentration unless a talent says so. Digestive Mantle is not Concentration by default. Magical/Supernatural: Hunger talents are supernatural cultivation effects. They count as magical for overcoming ordinary Resistance and for interactions with anti-magic, suppression fields, consecrated wards, exorcism, heavenly seals, anti-cultivation formations, and similar effects. Food and Rest: Hunger does not replace the need for long rests, sleep, water, or normal recovery unless a talent explicitly says so. Hunger can help survival, but it does not make a cultivator immune to campaign logistics by default. No Ingredient Loops: Summoned creatures, conjured food, trivial pests, common livestock, illusions, projections, and temporary manifestations do not produce useful Essence Portions unless the GM explicitly rules that they are meaningful, persistent, and spiritually real. Expression Is Flexible; Mechanics Are Fixed: A player may describe Hunger as furnace breath, red chopsticks, iron stomach, spectral jaws, banquet smoke, beast-bone soup, inner cauldron, famine shadow, or refined appetite. This expression does not change action type, range, target, damage type, duration, cost, cover, saving throw, or prerequisites unless a talent says so. ## Core Hunger Rules ### Hunger Key Ability When you learn Hunger, use your Path key ability for Hunger Checks, Hunger attacks, and your Hunger Save DC. A Qi Cultivator normally uses Intelligence or Charisma. A Body Refiner normally uses Constitution. A Spirit Awakener normally uses Wisdom. If a character has a special tradition, scripture, background, or GM-approved rule, the GM may permit a different Hunger key ability. Once chosen, the Hunger key ability should remain stable unless the character rebuilds their method. ### Hunger Check When a Hunger talent calls for a Hunger Check, roll: **d20 + Proficiency Bonus + Hunger key ability modifier** You may spend CP before the roll to steady your digestion. Spend up to your Proficiency Bonus CP. Each CP spent adds +1 to the Hunger Check. ### Hunger Save DC Your Hunger Save DC equals: **8 + Proficiency Bonus + Hunger key ability modifier** ### Hunger Cultivation Attack Your Hunger Cultivation Attack Modifier equals: **Proficiency Bonus + Hunger key ability modifier** ### Essence Portions An Essence Portion is one meaningful portion of spiritual food, spirit-beast meat, demon-beast flesh, monster organ, beast core residue, rare herb broth, medicinal marrow, venom gland, furnace-roasted core, spiritual grain, heavenly fruit, or comparable nourishment. The GM classifies Essence Portions as Common, Notable, Mighty, or Corrupted. Common Portion: ordinary spiritual food, minor beast meat, common medicinal broth, spirit grain, low-grade preserved meat, or a sect ration. Notable Portion: spirit-beast meat, monster organ, beast core residue, rare dish, dangerous venom, armored hide broth, sect-grade meal, or a significant hunt reward. Mighty Portion: elite spirit beast, demon beast, rare monster, ancient beast fragment, dragon marrow, heavenly ingredient, or high-grade banquet material. Corrupted Portion: demon-beast meat, cursed flesh, polluted core, resentment-soaked ingredient, parasite-tainted meal, corpse-poisoned meat, abyssal beast residue, or any ingredient the GM marks as spiritually dangerous. A meaningful creature or ingredient lot normally yields one Essence Portion unless the GM decides it is large enough, rare enough, or ritually prepared enough to support more. ### Satiety Satiety is refined spiritual nourishment waiting in your body. You can hold a number of Satiety charges equal to your Proficiency Bonus. Satiety lasts until your next long rest unless a talent says otherwise. Each Satiety charge should be linked to a meal source, such as spirit beast, demon beast, medicinal plant, monster venom, armored hide, flying beast, burrowing beast, aquatic beast, furnace-roasted core, predator meat, spiritual grain, cultivator residue, Golden Core fragment, or Nascent Soul trace. Satiety is not ordinary fullness. You can be physically hungry while spiritually sated, or physically full while spiritually empty. Satiety has three default uses. **First, Satiety powers Digestive Mantle.** Digestive Mantle is the main combat expression of stored nourishment. Most Hunger talents improve what Satiety can do when spent this way. **Second, Satiety can feed Hunger techniques.** Once per turn when you spend CP on a Hunger talent other than Refine the Meal, you may consume 1 Satiety to reduce that talent's CP cost by 1, minimum 0. This does not replace any Satiety cost the talent already has. **Third, Satiety can be burned as reserve nourishment.** Once per short rest, when you roll Initiative or start your turn while Bloodied, you may consume 1 Satiety without using an action. Choose one: - regain CP equal to your Proficiency Bonus; - gain Temporary HP equal to twice your Proficiency Bonus; - remove one nonmagical hunger, thirst, forced-march, or travel-fatigue penalty that has not become Exhaustion; - gain Advantage on one Constitution saving throw before the end of your next turn. Forbidden Satiety, Golden Core Satiety, Nascent Soul Satiety, and Demon-Beast Satiety can be burned this way, but doing so carries their normal Impurity, Appetite Stain, or backlash rules if a talent assigns any. ### Impurity Impurity represents spiritual residue that your body has not safely digested. You may gain Impurity when you: - fail a Hunger Check by 5 or more; - Refine a Corrupted Portion; - eat demon-beast essence; - eat a creature above your Realm; - use a talent that says it adds Impurity; - use a Forbidden Hunger talent. Track Impurity separately from Satiety. When your Impurity equals or exceeds your Proficiency Bonus, your next Digestive Mantle becomes unstable. When that Mantle ends, make a Constitution saving throw against your own Hunger Save DC. On a success, reduce Impurity by 1. On a failure, choose or roll one consequence: - You become Poisoned until the end of your next short rest. - You cannot gain Satiety until you complete a short rest. - You gain one level of Exhaustion from spiritual indigestion. - Your Hunger techniques become visibly monstrous, giving you Disadvantage on Charisma checks other than Intimidation until you finish a long rest. A long rest reduces Impurity by your Proficiency Bonus. Proper cleansing food, Alchemy, Life, Water, Protection, sect purification, or relevant story rites may reduce it sooner. ### Hunger and Demon Beasts Demon-beast meals are legal only in some jurisdictions and usually require inspection. They are powerful because demon-beast essence is dense, adaptive, and aggressive. They are dangerous because the same essence resists digestion. Whenever a talent creates Satiety from a Corrupted Portion or demon-beast source, mark that Satiety as Demon-Beast Satiety. Unless a talent says otherwise, using Demon-Beast Satiety for Digestive Mantle causes you to gain 1 Impurity when the Mantle ends. ### Hunger and Beastmastery Consent Boundary Hunger does not treat bonded companions, intelligent spirit beasts, sworn mounts, sect guardian beasts, awakened beasts, or treaty-protected beasts as ordinary ingredients. Eating such a being is a major social, legal, spiritual, and karmic act. If the creature is sapient, oath-bound, a companion, or a recognized person under local law, the GM may treat the act as forbidden even if the body is not humanoid. ## Base Sphere Abilities When you acquire the Sphere of Hunger, you gain the following three base actions. Most Hunger talents modify one of these three actions. ### Taste the Qi Action Type: Bonus Action Factory Combat Bucket: bonus_action Factory Routing: combat_action_row Range: 30 feet Target: One creature, corpse, meal, ingredient, beast core, spiritual dish, visible residue, or container you can perceive Cost: None Duration: Until the end of your next turn, or 1 minute outside combat You taste the spiritual pressure of the target. Choose one question: - Is this target spiritually nourishing, poisonous, corrupted, empty, undead, demonic, beast-born, cultivator-born, artificial, or spiritually inert? - Is this creature Bloodied? - What is the strongest obvious qi expression in this target? - Does this meal or ingredient contain Impurity? - Is this creature or ingredient suitable for a Hunger talent you know? - Is this target protected by an obvious anti-consumption ward, corpse seal, preservation formation, or oath-mark? If the target is unwilling and actively concealing its nature, make a Hunger Check contested by the target's Charisma or Constitution saving throw, chosen by the GM. Success: you learn the answer. Failure: you learn only whether the target is spiritually nourishing or spiritually dangerous. Taste the Qi does not reveal full stat blocks, secret names, exact levels, complete sphere lists, hidden plot information, or the full contents of a sealed storage treasure. ### Refine the Meal Action Type: Multi-Mode Canonical Action Type: Multi-Mode Factory Routing: procedure_ledger_not_combat_action Split Review Decision: procedure_only_not_combat_action Recommended Factory Realization: procedures=TEN_MINUTE_REFINE, SHORT_REST_REFINE Timing Detail: 10-minute ritual, or part of a short rest Range: Touch Target: One Essence Portion, prepared meal, spiritual ingredient, or suitable corpse portion Cost: 1 CP, plus the ingredient You spiritually prepare and consume an Essence Portion. Make a Hunger Check. Common Portion DC 12. Notable Portion DC 15. Mighty Portion DC 18. Corrupted Portion increases the DC by 2. A portion from a creature above your Realm increases the DC by 2. Success: gain 1 Satiety charge tied to the meal source. Success by 5 or More: gain 1 Satiety and choose one additional benefit: - reduce Impurity by 1; - gain Temporary HP equal to your Proficiency Bonus; - the next Digestive Mantle using this Satiety costs 0 CP; - learn one harmless sensory memory from the ingredient, such as fear, territory, prey, predator, season, death-sign, or last hunger. Failure: you do not gain Satiety. The ingredient is consumed. Failure by 5 or More: you do not gain Satiety and gain 1 Impurity. ### Digestive Mantle Action Type: Bonus Action Factory Combat Bucket: bonus_action Factory Routing: combat_action_row Range: Self Target: Self Duration: 1 minute Cost: 1 CP and 1 Satiety You ignite one Satiety charge inside your meridians and wear its nourishment as a temporary cultivation state. When you activate Digestive Mantle, gain Temporary HP equal to: **twice your Proficiency Bonus + your Hunger key ability modifier** Then choose one basic Mantle benefit appropriate to the consumed source. Once before the Mantle ends, when you move at least 10 feet straight toward a creature and hit it with an attack on the same turn, add your Proficiency Bonus to the damage roll. Iron Stomach: Gain Advantage on saving throws against Poisoned and Disease. When you succeed on such a saving throw while the Mantle is active, gain Temporary HP equal to your Proficiency Bonus. Venom Belly: Once per turn when you hit with an attack, deal extra Poison or Acid damage equal to your Proficiency Bonus + your Hunger key ability modifier. Furnace Belly: Once per turn when you hit with an attack, deal extra Fire damage equal to your Proficiency Bonus + your Hunger key ability modifier. Elemental Gut: Choose Acid, Cold, Fire, Lightning, Necrotic, Poison, or Thunder, as appropriate to the Satiety source. You gain Resistance to that damage type while the Mantle lasts. If the source was only weakly associated with the type, the GM may limit this Resistance to the first triggering damage instance each round. Deep Nourishment: When you activate the Mantle, end one nonmagical hunger, thirst, forced-march, or travel-fatigue penalty that has not become Exhaustion. While the Mantle lasts, you have Advantage on Constitution saving throws against Exhaustion caused by travel, starvation, thirst, exposure, disease, or hostile terrain. Demon-Beast Course: Choose two basic Mantle benefits above that fit the demon beast instead of one. Gain 1 Impurity when the Mantle ends unless another talent changes this. Cultivator Course: If a Forbidden Hunger talent lets you create Forbidden Satiety, a Digestive Mantle using that Satiety may choose one basic Mantle benefit that fits the consumed cultivator's Path or known sphere. Some Forbidden Hunger talents improve this benefit. You can benefit from only one Digestive Mantle at a time. Activating a new Digestive Mantle ends the previous one. ## Hunger Talent Tags Taste talents modify Taste the Qi. Meal talents modify Refine the Meal. Mantle talents modify Digestive Mantle. Beast-Course talents improve spirit-beast and monster meals. Demon-Course talents improve demon-beast meals and usually risk Impurity. Survival talents help against starvation, thirst, exhaustion, poison, disease, harsh travel, and impure food. Banquet talents allow allies to benefit from your meals. Secret talents are rare inheritances. They are not automatically illegal. Forbidden talents involve cultivator flesh, dantian residue, soul residue, stolen meridians, bloodline remains, living essence, or comparable transgressions. They are illegal in most orthodox lands. ## Mortal Realm Hunger Talents ### Clean Palate - Taste When you use Taste the Qi on food, medicine, water, poison, beast meat, a corpse, or a spiritual ingredient, you may also learn whether it is safe to eat by ordinary standards. If you already know it is unsafe, you gain Advantage on the next saving throw you make against that specific poison, disease, or impurity before the end of your next long rest. ### Trail-Stomach Scripture - Survival, Meal You can use Refine the Meal during harsh travel without proper cooking tools, provided you have fire, water, salt, a knife, a heated stone, or a comparable survival method. When you successfully Refine a Common or Notable Portion during travel, choose one creature who shares the meal. That creature gains Advantage on its next Constitution saving throw against forced march, starvation, thirst, mundane cold, mundane heat, or spoiled food before its next long rest. ### Beast-Bone Broth - Meal, Beast-Course When you Refine a spirit-beast or monster portion with bones, shell, horn, claw, scale, carapace, or hide, you may store it as Bone Satiety. A Digestive Mantle using Bone Satiety may choose Thick Hide even if the original creature did not obviously have thick hide. At Foundation Realm, Thick Hide from Bone Satiety reduces damage by twice your Proficiency Bonus instead. ### Predator's Course - Mantle, Beast-Course When you activate Digestive Mantle using a predator, hunter, stalking beast, flying beast, serpent, spider, tiger, wolf, hawk, or comparable source, you may choose Predator Step. While Predator Step is active, your jump distance also increases by 10 feet, and you gain Advantage on Wisdom (Survival) checks to track Bloodied creatures. ### Bitter Medicine Belly - Survival, Mantle While Digestive Mantle is active, you have Advantage on saving throws against Poisoned. If you succeed on a saving throw against Poisoned while Digestive Mantle is active, you may spend 1 CP to gain Temporary HP equal to your Proficiency Bonus. ### Famine-Enduring Bowl - Survival, Meal When you successfully Refine the Meal using a Common Portion, you may choose not to gain Satiety. Instead, one willing creature who eats the meal ignores the effects of ordinary hunger and thirst for 24 hours. This does not remove Exhaustion already gained from starvation or dehydration. It also does not protect against magical famine, cursed thirst, poison, or disease. At Core Formation Realm, you may affect a number of willing creatures up to your Proficiency Bonus. ### Wolfing the Battlefield Scrap - Meal You may use Refine the Meal as a 1-minute ritual instead of a 10-minute ritual if the Essence Portion came from a creature reduced to 0 HP within the last minute. When you do, the DC increases by 2. On a failure by 5 or more, you gain 1 Impurity and cannot use Wolfing the Battlefield Scrap again until you finish a short rest. ### Hunger-Sense Meridian - Taste When you use Taste the Qi on a creature, you may also learn whether it has eaten a meaningful spiritual meal, pill, beast core, demon-beast portion, or forbidden essence within the last 24 hours. On a successful contested Hunger Check against a concealing target, you may learn whether the meal was beast-born, plant-born, pill-born, demon-born, undead, cultivator-born, or artificial. ### Empty-Bowl Guard - Mantle When you activate Digestive Mantle while you have no ordinary food remaining in your supplies, increase the Temporary HP gained by your Proficiency Bonus. This talent functions only once per long rest. If you later gain access to abundant food before your next long rest, the talent does not activate again. Empty-Bowl Guard rewards real deprivation, not staged bookkeeping. ## Foundation Realm Hunger Talents ### Demon-Beast Digestion - Demon-Course, Meal Prerequisite: Foundation Realm When you use Refine the Meal on a Corrupted Portion from a demon beast, you may accept 1 Impurity before rolling. If you do, gain Advantage on the Hunger Check. On a success, the Satiety created by this meal counts as Demon-Beast Satiety. A Digestive Mantle using Demon-Beast Satiety may choose two basic Mantle benefits instead of one. When that Mantle ends, make a Constitution saving throw against your Hunger Save DC. Failed Save: gain 1 Impurity. ### Battle Ration - Meal, Mantle Prerequisite: Foundation Realm You may prepare one stored Satiety as a battle ration at the end of a short rest. Until your next long rest, you may activate Digestive Mantle with that Satiety as part of the same Bonus Action used to consume it. When you do, the Mantle's Temporary HP increases by your Proficiency Bonus. ### Shared Bowl Method - Banquet, Meal Prerequisite: Foundation Realm When you successfully use Refine the Meal during a short rest, choose up to your Proficiency Bonus willing creatures who share the meal. Each chosen creature gains one of the following benefits until its next long rest: - Temporary HP equal to your Proficiency Bonus; - Advantage on its next Constitution saving throw; - +5 feet Speed for 1 hour; - Advantage on its next ability check to resist hunger, thirst, spoiled food, or forced march. A creature can benefit from only one Shared Bowl Method per long rest. ### Marrow-Furnace Pulse - Mantle Prerequisite: Foundation Realm While Digestive Mantle is active, once per turn when you spend CP on a Hunger talent, you may gain Temporary HP equal to your Proficiency Bonus. If the active Mantle came from a demon beast, you may instead add your Proficiency Bonus to one damage roll that turn and gain 1 Impurity when the Mantle ends. ### Monster-Core Simmer - Meal Prerequisite: Foundation Realm When you Refine the Meal using beast core residue, monster core fragments, demon core scrap, or a similar concentrated organ, you may spend 2 CP instead of 1 CP. On a success, gain 1 Satiety and choose the exact basic Mantle benefit it will support when later used for Digestive Mantle. On a success by 5 or more, that future Digestive Mantle also gains Temporary HP equal to your Proficiency Bonus when activated. On a failure by 5 or more, gain 2 Impurity instead of 1. ### Second Stomach Method - Meal Prerequisite: Foundation Realm Your maximum Satiety increases by 1. In addition, when you finish a short rest, you may preserve one Satiety charge that would otherwise expire at your next long rest. Preserved Satiety lasts until the end of your next long rest. You can preserve only one Satiety this way at a time. Forbidden Satiety cannot be preserved by this talent. ### Hunter's Victory Meal - Meal, Beast-Course Prerequisite: Foundation Realm When you help reduce a meaningful beast, spirit beast, monster, demon beast, monstrosity, dragon, or comparable creature to 0 HP, your first Refine the Meal check using one of its Essence Portions before your next long rest gains a +2 bonus. If the creature was a major threat for your party or your cultivation stage, gain Advantage instead. This talent does not apply if the creature was helpless, trapped only for farming, conjured, summoned, or not a meaningful opponent. ### Appetite Seal - Taste, Meal Prerequisite: Foundation Realm When you use Taste the Qi on a meal, corpse portion, or ingredient and identify Impurity, you may mark the impurity pattern for later correction. Forbidden Hunger is a crime against the body, soul, social order, and cultivation foundation. Orthodox Hunger eats beasts, monsters, herbs, medicine, spiritual grain, and demon beasts under ritual control. Forbidden Hunger eats cultivators. It consumes flesh, marrow, bloodline residue, dantian fragments, meridian patterns, Golden Core residue, Nascent Soul traces, soul broth, or living spiritual essence. This is one of the clearest capital crimes in orthodox cultivation society. Sects destroy practitioners of this method because it turns every cultivator into food, destabilizes inheritance, desecrates corpses, spreads heart demons, and creates famine logic inside the Dao. Forbidden Hunger is tempting because it works. It is not as strong as Daemonic Cultivation. It does not grant broad mutation, demonic domains, permanent talent theft, full second-engine power, or open-ended limit breaking. On a successful save, it is not Frightened and you regain no CP. You can use this Bonus Action once per Nascent Soul Feast. Failure: gain 3 Impurity and 3 Appetite Stain. Failure by 5 or More: the consumed trace answers from inside you. The GM may create a Heart Demon, possession pressure, karmic debt, sect beacon, soul-contamination scene, ancestral trial, revenge oath, or surviving remnant with a claim on your body. Nascent Soul Feast never grants permanent control over another soul, permanent talent theft, permanent memory theft, a second Path, or a new cultivation base. It is a terrifying shortcut, not a replacement for your own Dao. ## Hunger Drawbacks and Variant Scriptures Hunger variants are optional cultivation scriptures that change how the sphere manifests. A variant grants a benefit only if it also imposes a real limitation. These are Tianxia-specific cultivation limits inspired by drawback design, not imported casting-tradition rules. Unless the GM says otherwise: - choose at most one Hunger variant when first learning Hunger or undergoing a major Hunger initiation; - Hunger variants are mutually exclusive; - the variant applies to all Hunger talents you use; - if a variant grants a talent whose prerequisites are not yet met, you gain that talent when you meet those prerequisites; - if the variant is retrained, removed, or ritually broken, lose the bonus talent or benefit unless another feature preserves it; - talents sealed by a variant are Known - Restricted Use, not deleted, unless the variant says they are replaced. ### Monstrous Appetite Scripture Your Hunger method leaves obvious signs: sharpened teeth, heated breath, predator eyes, belly furnace, scent of broth, beast-shadow, ghostly chopsticks, or famine aura. Benefit: Once per long rest, when you activate Digestive Mantle using Satiety from a beast, monster, spirit beast, or demon beast, gain additional Temporary HP equal to your Proficiency Bonus. Drawback: You have Disadvantage on Charisma checks to appear harmless to creatures who understand cultivation unless you conceal the signs with clothing, medicine, illusion, etiquette, or a comparable method. When you use Digestive Mantle, the signs become obvious until the Mantle ends. ### Pure Vegetarian Furnace Scripture Your Hunger method refuses flesh, blood, corpse portions, and beast essence. Benefit: When you successfully Refine the Meal using spiritual grain, herbs, fruit, fungus, roots, tea, medicinal broth, mineral nourishment, or similar non-flesh ingredients, reduce Impurity by 1 on a success by 5 or more. Drawback: You cannot create Satiety from beasts, monsters, demon beasts, cultivators, bloodline remains, corpse portions, or comparable flesh sources. You cannot learn Forbidden Hunger talents unless you abandon this scripture through story consequences. ### Bloodless Kitchen Scripture Your Hunger method refuses blood and slaughtered flesh but permits eggs, milk, honey, spiritual dew, beast-shed antler, molted shell, shed scale, spiritual grain, herbs, fungi, prepared medicines, and other bloodless ingredients. Benefit: When you use Shared Bowl Method, each participant may also gain Advantage on its next saving throw against Frightened before its next long rest. Drawback: You cannot create Predator Step or Venom Belly from flesh portions unless the GM rules the ingredient was bloodless and ethically obtained. You cannot use a Hunger talent that requires fresh blood, butchered flesh, or violent consumption without suspending this scripture until you complete a cleansing rite during a long rest. ### Demon-Stove Scripture Your kitchen specializes in demon-beast meat. Benefit: When you use Refine the Meal on a demon-beast or Corrupted Portion, gain a +2 bonus to the Hunger Check. Drawback: Whenever you gain Impurity from Hunger, gain 1 additional Impurity unless you complete a short-rest cleansing rite with proper tools, salt, incense, water, and heat before the Impurity consequence is resolved. ### Stomach Furnace Scripture Prerequisite: Body Refining Path Your Hunger begins in the stomach, marrow, gut-fire, blood heat, teeth, breath, tendon furnace, and pressure of the living body. The body is the bowl; the body is the stove; the body is the first and last diner. Use Constitution as your Hunger key ability while practicing this scripture. #### Drawback: Body as the Only Bowl Your Hunger cannot project active appetite qi freely outside your body. Allowed Origin: Your Hunger effects must originate from your stomach, teeth, breath, blood heat, sweat, skin, muscles, bones, marrow, gut-fire, swallowed ingredient, held cooking tool, held weapon, bite, unarmed strike, grapple, shove, or a creature or object you are physically touching. Allowed Targets and Expressions: You may use Hunger on yourself, an ingredient you are eating, a meal you are consuming, a corpse or ingredient you are physically preparing, a creature you are touching, biting, grappling, shoving, striking with a melee attack, or contacting with your body or a held weapon. Sealed External Expression: You cannot use Hunger talents whose main effect targets an ally at range, targets an enemy at range, creates a battlefield area, creates free-floating appetite, stores magic in food for someone else, places a Mantle on someone else, creates a banquet field, releases a remote stolen-circuit echo, or reads a creature through purely spiritual distance. Sealed talents remain Known - Restricted Use. They can be opened by Open the Outer Maw, a printed talent, a personal-magic variant, an item, a Forged Technique, a Secret Inheritance, a major sect inheritance, or GM permission. #### Taste Restriction Taste the Qi has a range of Self, Touch, or 10 feet by smell, breath, blood-scent, cooked vapor, corpse-reek, visible saliva, open wound, obvious meal steam, or direct bodily pressure. Taste the Qi cannot read a concealed creature through walls, sealed containers, Total Cover, formation barriers, remote viewing, or purely spiritual distance. #### Meal Restriction Refine the Meal can create Satiety only for you. You may cook ordinary food for allies. Ordinary food is not a Hunger effect and does not carry your Satiety, Mantle, or stored magical benefits unless a legal external Hunger feature says otherwise. #### Mantle Restriction Digestive Mantle may be placed only on yourself. A Mantle benefit that damages, frightens, marks, drains, or pressures another creature works only through contact, a melee hit, a grapple, a shove, a bite, a creature striking your body, or a creature starting its turn in physical contact with you, and only if the talent text supports that interaction. #### Stomach Furnace Benefits Maximum Satiety: Your maximum Satiety increases by 1. At Core Formation Realm, it increases by 2 instead. Furnace Pulse: Once per turn, when you use a legal self-only or contact-based Hunger talent that costs CP, gain Temporary HP equal to your Proficiency Bonus. These Temporary HP do not stack with themselves. Hard Digestion: When you fail a Hunger Check while using Refine the Meal for yourself, reduce any Poison damage, Acid damage, or damage from Impurity backlash by your Constitution modifier plus your Proficiency Bonus. Predator Body: While Digestive Mantle is active, you have Advantage on Strength checks made to Grapple, Shove, climb, swim, jump, force open a barrier, hold a creature, or resist forced movement if the active Satiety came from a beast, monster, demon beast, predator, giant creature, armored creature, venomous creature, or comparable body-rich source. Demon Meat Tempering: When you gain Impurity from a demon-beast meal that you personally refined and consumed, you may spend 1 CP to delay one consequence of that Impurity until your current Digestive Mantle ends. Delayed Impurity is not removed. #### Removing the Drawback If Body as the Only Bowl is removed by Open the Outer Maw or another opening source, you gain normal access to external Hunger. Unless the opening source says otherwise, lose Maximum Satiety and Furnace Pulse from this scripture. Hard Digestion, Predator Body, and Demon Meat Tempering continue to apply to self-only or contact-based Hunger uses. ### Spirit of the Empty Bowl Scripture Prerequisite: Spirit Awakening Path Your Hunger listens to need before it consumes substance. Use Wisdom as your Hunger key ability while practicing this scripture. Benefit: When you use Taste the Qi on a creature, you may ask whether its current hunger is physical, emotional, spiritual, social, or Dao-related. On a successful contested Hunger Check against a concealing target, you may also learn whether that hunger is natural, cursed, daemonic, forbidden, oath-bound, ghost-born, or artificially cultivated. Drawback: When you exploit a creature's deepest hunger cruelly, the GM may assign Appetite Stain or karmic consequences even if you did not use a Forbidden Hunger talent. ## Path Synergies ### Body Refining - Stomach Furnace Body Body Refining Hunger is strongest when appetite is expressed through flesh, breath, gut, marrow, teeth, stance, and contact. Use Constitution as your Hunger key ability if Hunger is learned or expressed through Body Refining. When a Hunger talent originates from your body, a held tool, a held weapon, a swallowed ingredient, a creature you touch, or a creature you hit, bite, grapple, or shove, it is a Body Furnace expression. When you use Body Furnace expressions, apply the following rules: - After you hit, bite, grapple, shove, or otherwise physically touch a creature on your turn, you may use Taste the Qi on that creature once before the end of that turn without spending a Bonus Action. This free Taste can ask only whether the target is Bloodied, whether it is spiritually nourishing or dangerous, or whether it is suitable for a Hunger talent you know. - When you activate Digestive Mantle on yourself using beast, monster, spirit-beast, demon-beast, or body-rich Satiety, choose one Strength, Dexterity, or Constitution check you make before the end of your next turn. Add your Proficiency Bonus to that check. - Once per short rest, when a self-only or contact-based Hunger talent would give you Impurity from a non-Forbidden beast, monster, spirit-beast, demon-beast, poison, venom, disease, or harsh-ingredient source, reduce that Impurity by 1, minimum 0. - Hunger talents with range beyond Touch, ally Mantles, Banquet effects, remote appetite pressure, stored magical food for others, battlefield meal fields, and remote stolen-circuit echoes require Open the Outer Maw or another explicit opening source. This synergy does not delete sealed talents. It defines which Hunger expressions are legal before outward appetite has been opened. ### Qi Cultivation - Inner Cauldron Qi Qi Cultivation is the classic path of external gourmand cultivation: kitchen formations, dantian simmering, spiritual seasoning, furnace breath, refined utensils, banquet diagrams, and clean ingredient conversion. Use Intelligence or Charisma as your Hunger key ability. When you successfully use Refine the Meal with proper utensils, cooking fire, a cauldron, a spirit stove, a kitchen formation, or a prepared recipe, choose one: - the created Satiety does not count against your Satiety maximum until the end of your next short rest; - reduce the CP cost of the next Digestive Mantle using that Satiety by 1, minimum 0; - reduce Impurity gained from that meal by 1, minimum 0; - if the meal is shared through a Banquet talent before your next long rest, one participant gains additional Temporary HP equal to your Proficiency Bonus. You may gain only one of these benefits from a given use of Refine the Meal. ### Spirit Awakening - Appetite-Soul Perception Spirit Awakening Hunger tastes the meaning of need: fear of famine, desire for power, ghost craving, oath hunger, remembered starvation, soul longing, and the emptiness beneath a cultivator's Dao. Use Wisdom as your Hunger key ability. When you use Taste the Qi on a creature, spirit, ghost, possessed body, corpse, soul trace, forbidden residue, or emotionally charged meal, you may ask one additional question: - What kind of hunger is strongest here: physical, emotional, spiritual, social, ancestral, daemonic, forbidden, or Dao-related? - Is this hunger natural, cursed, cultivated, imposed, suppressed, or starving? - Would food, safety, recognition, revenge, power, release, memory, or obedience most easily tempt this hunger? - Has this target consumed cultivator essence, soul residue, demon-beast corruption, or forbidden nourishment within the last day? Once per short rest, after learning an answer with Taste the Qi, gain Advantage on one Insight, Persuasion, Intimidation, Investigation, Survival, or Medicine check before the end of the scene if the check acts on that answer. When you use Forbidden Hunger on soul residue, memory, vows, or Nascent Soul traces, the GM should treat Appetite Stain as spiritually obvious to appropriate witnesses even when the physical evidence is hidden. ## Cultivation Insights ### Clean-Tongued Disciple Prerequisite: Hunger sphere When you use Taste the Qi on food, drink, or medicine, you may also detect mundane spoilage, common poison, and obvious disease without rolling unless the substance is deliberately concealed. ### Camp Kitchen Adept Prerequisite: Hunger sphere During a short rest, if you prepare food for the party, choose one willing creature who eats it. That creature gains Temporary HP equal to your Proficiency Bonus. A creature can benefit from Camp Kitchen Adept only once per long rest. ### Iron Belly Foundation Prerequisite: Hunger sphere, Foundation Realm When you fail a Constitution saving throw against Poisoned, you may spend 1 CP to reroll the save. You must use the new result. You can use this Insight once per short rest. ### Monster-Taste Scholar Prerequisite: Hunger sphere You gain proficiency in Nature or Survival. If you already have both, choose Medicine or Cook's Utensils. When you use Taste the Qi on a beast, monstrosity, dragon, demon beast, or strange corpse, gain a +1 bonus to the Hunger Check if a roll is required. ### Banquet Etiquette of the Outer Court Prerequisite: Hunger sphere You gain proficiency in Persuasion or Cook's Utensils. When you share a legally prepared Hunger meal with a neutral or friendly cultivator, gain Advantage on one Charisma check made during that meal to discuss travel, supplies, hospitality, safe passage, or sect introductions. ### Refuse the Forbidden Bowl Prerequisite: Hunger sphere You have trained to reject predatory shortcuts. You gain Advantage on saving throws or ability checks made to resist the temptation of Forbidden Hunger, daemonic appetite, cursed food, cannibal scriptures, ghost famine, or comparable spiritual predation. If you ever willingly use a Forbidden Hunger talent, replace this Insight with another Hunger Insight chosen with GM approval. ### Open the Outer Maw Prerequisite: Hunger sphere, Body Refining Path, Foundation Realm, Constitution 16+, Stomach Furnace Scripture You have learned to let appetite leave the body without ceasing to be Body Refining. Your breath carries furnace heat, your blood-steam seasons the air, your bite teaches your qi how to travel, and your stomach becomes a cauldron whose lid can open toward the world. You remove Body as the Only Bowl from Stomach Furnace Scripture. You may use Hunger talents at their listed ranges and may learn or use Banquet, external Taste, external Meal, external Secret Hunger, and external Forbidden Hunger options if you otherwise meet their prerequisites. External Hunger remains visibly embodied. When you use an external Hunger effect, it must originate from one of the following signs unless a Secret Inheritance, item, or Forged Technique says otherwise: - breath, blood-steam, stomach thunder, cooking smoke, furnace heat, or visible appetite pressure; - thrown food, prepared dishes, a held utensil, a held weapon, a bite mark, or a meal you prepared; - a body-furnace sign such as red marrow heat, beast-shadow muscle, boiling sweat, or steaming wounds. First Projection Risk: Once per short rest, when you use an external Hunger effect that costs CP and affects a creature other than you, you may overfeed the projection. Increase one damage roll, Temporary HP grant, CP restoration, Satiety-created benefit, or Hunger Check from that effect by your Proficiency Bonus. After the effect resolves, gain 1 Impurity. Opening the outer maw does not grant Qi Cultivation, does not remove ingredient requirements, does not remove Appetite Stain from Forbidden Hunger, and does not make external Hunger subtle. ## Automation Notes The acquisition actions for this sphere are Taste the Qi, Refine the Meal, and Digestive Mantle. Every ordinary Hunger talent should modify at least one of these three actions. ### Taste the Qi
Action Type: Bonus Action
Factory Combat Bucket: bonus_action
Factory Routing: combat_action_row
Range: 30 feet
Target: One creature, corpse, meal, ingredient, beast core, spiritual dish, visible residue, or container you can perceive
Cost: None
Duration: Until the end of your next turn, or 1 minute outside combat
You taste the spiritual pressure of the target.
Choose one question:
- Is this target spiritually nourishing, poisonous, corrupted, empty, undead, demonic, beast-born, cultivator-born, artificial, or spiritually inert?
- Is this creature Bloodied?
- What is the strongest obvious qi expression in this target?
- Does this meal or ingredient contain Impurity?
- Is this creature or ingredient suitable for a Hunger talent you know?
- Is this target protected by an obvious anti-consumption ward, corpse seal, preservation formation, or oath-mark?
If the target is unwilling and actively concealing its nature, make a Hunger Check contested by the target's Charisma or Constitution saving throw, chosen by the GM.
Success: you learn the answer.
Failure: you learn only whether the target is spiritually nourishing or spiritually dangerous.
Taste the Qi does not reveal full stat blocks, secret names, exact levels, complete sphere lists, hidden plot information, or the full contents of a sealed storage treasure.

resolved_automatic_base_abilities.effect:
### Digestive Mantle
Action Type: Bonus Action
Factory Combat Bucket: bonus_action
Factory Routing: combat_action_row
Range: Self
Target: Self
Duration: 1 minute
Cost: 1 CP and 1 Satiety
You ignite one Satiety charge inside your meridians and wear its nourishment as a temporary cultivation state.
When you activate Digestive Mantle, gain Temporary HP equal to:
**twice your Proficiency Bonus + your Hunger key ability modifier**
Then choose one basic Mantle benefit appropriate to the consumed source.
Beast Strength: Gain Advantage on Strength checks and Strength saving throws. Once before the Mantle ends, when you hit with a melee attack or unarmed strike, add your Proficiency Bonus to the damage roll.
Predator Step: Your Speed increases by 10 feet. Once before the Mantle ends, when you move at least 10 feet straight toward a creature and hit it with an attack on the same turn, add your Proficiency Bonus to the damage roll.
Iron Stomach: Gain Advantage on saving throws against Poisoned and Disease. When you succeed on such a saving throw while the Mantle is active, gain Temporary HP equal to your Proficiency Bonus.
Thick Hide: Once per round when you take Bludgeoning, Piercing, or Slashing damage, reduce that damage by your Proficiency Bonus + your Hunger key ability modifier.
Venom Belly: Once per turn when you hit with an attack, deal extra Poison or Acid damage equal to your Proficiency Bonus + your Hunger key ability modifier.
Furnace Belly: Once per turn when you hit with an attack, deal extra Fire damage equal to your Proficiency Bonus + your Hunger key ability modifier.
Elemental Gut: Choose Acid, Cold, Fire, Lightning, Necrotic, Poison, or Thunder, as appropriate to the Satiety source. You gain Resistance to that damage type while the Mantle lasts. If the source was only weakly associated with the type, the GM may limit this Resistance to the first triggering damage instance each round.
Deep Nourishment: When you activate the Mantle, end one nonmagical hunger, thirst, forced-march, or travel-fatigue penalty that has not become Exhaustion. While the Mantle lasts, you have Advantage on Constitution saving throws against Exhaustion caused by travel, starvation, thirst, exposure, disease, or hostile terrain.
Demon-Beast Course: Choose two basic Mantle benefits above that fit the demon beast instead of one. Gain 1 Impurity when the Mantle ends unless another talent changes this.
Cultivator Course: If a Forbidden Hunger talent lets you create Forbidden Satiety, a Digestive Mantle using that Satiety may choose one basic Mantle benefit that fits the consumed cultivator's Path or known sphere. Some Forbidden Hunger talents improve this benefit.
You can benefit from only one Digestive Mantle at a time. Activating a new Digestive Mantle ends the previous one.

automatic_base_abilities.effect:
#### Crystallize Path
Action Type: Action
Factory Combat Bucket: action
Factory Routing: combat_action_row
Range: 60 feet
Area: Up to two 5-foot Lattice Spaces
Duration: 1 minute
Cost: NoneConcentration: Not required
Tags: Lattice
You create Ice Lattice on surfaces you can see within range. The spaces may be connected or separate.
The number of spaces you create increases as your cultivation deepens.
| Cultivation Level | Lattice Spaces Created |
| --- | --- |
| CL 1-4 | 2 spaces |
| CL 5-10 | 3 spaces |
| CL 11-16 | 4 spaces |
| CL 17-20 | 5 spaces |
When a creature you did not designate as safe moves at least 10 feet across, out of, or through your Lattice Spaces during one turn, you may give that creature one Fracture Mark. This can happen only once per creature per turn.

automatic_base_abilities.effect:
#### Shard Needle
Action Type: Action
Factory Combat Bucket: action
Factory Routing: combat_action_row
Range: 60 feet
Target: One creature or object
Cost: None
Tags: Attack, Fracture
You condense a line of frost into a needle of hard ice. Make a ranged Cultivation Attack. On a hit, the target takes Piercing or Cold damage, chosen when you make the attack, and gains one Fracture Mark.
| Cultivation Level | Shard Needle Damage |
| --- | --- |
| CL 1-4 | 1d8 |
| CL 5-10 | 2d8 |
| CL 11-16 | 3d8 |
| CL 17-20 | 4d8 |
The damage is not the sphere’s identity. It is the visible sign of motion being forced into a cutting shape.

automatic_base_abilities.effect:
#### Spending a Fracture Mark
Once per round, when a marked creature or object you can perceive performs a triggering act, you may spend its Fracture Mark without using an Action. Choose one Fracture Response appropriate to the trigger.
Catch Step.
Trigger: the marked target begins movement, including special movement or teleportation. Reduce one of the target’s Speeds by 10 feet until the end of the current turn, or reduce the distance of one teleportation effect by 10 feet. At CL 11, this reduction becomes 20 feet. This cannot reduce a Speed or teleportation distance below 0.
Brittle Opening.
Trigger: the marked target is hit by an attack. The triggering attack deals extra Piercing or Cold damage equal to 1d4 + your Proficiency Bonus. At CL 11, the die becomes 1d6.
Crack Aim.
Trigger: the marked target makes an attack roll or Dexterity saving throw. Subtract 1d4 from the triggering roll. At CL 11, subtract 1d6 instead.
Shatter Space.
Trigger: the marked target enters, starts its turn in, or ends its turn in one of your Lattice Spaces. One Lattice Space occupied by the target shatters. The target must succeed on a Dexterity saving throw or take Piercing or Cold damage equal to your Shard Needle damage and fall Prone. On a success, it takes half as much damage and does not fall Prone. The chosen Lattice Space ends.
Lock Grip.
Trigger: the marked target uses an object, weapon, tool, focus, or held item. Until the start of its next turn, the target has Disadvantage on the next ability check or attack roll it makes using that item. If the item is unattended, you may instead freeze it to an adjacent surface until the start of your next turn. A creature can free the item early by using an Action and succeeding on a Strength check against your Ice Save DC.
Crystal Guard.
Trigger: the marked target is a willing creature and takes damage. Reduce the damage by 1d6 + your Key Ability modifier. This reduction increases to 2d6 at CL 5, 3d6 at CL 11, and 4d6 at CL 17. The mark then ends.
