spheres.full_exact_source_text: # Sphere of Ice Qi Expression: Primary — Ice Qi; Supporting — Water Qi, Yin Qi, Stillness Qi, Preservation Qi. “Water remembers every path. Ice chooses one path and makes the world obey its shape.” Sphere Type: Elemental Terrain / Control Sphere Primary Path: Qi Cultivation Secondary Path: Body Refining Rare Variant: Spirit Awakening through the Crystal Stillness Scripture Resource: CPCore Mechanic: Frost Lattice and Fracture Marks Common Effects: crystalline terrain, arresting movement, brittle openings, ice bridges, ice walls, frozen seals, shattering lattice, sliding steps, cold as a symptom of crystallized motion, and battlefield control through structure The Sphere of Ice is the cultivation of motion forced into shape. An Ice cultivator does not merely make things cold. Cold is only the first breath of the art. The real practice is to take flowing motion - a footstep, a blade path, a river, a spell trajectory, a fleeing breath, a falling body - and impose crystalline order on it. Once motion has a shape, the cultivator can stand on it, cut along it, seal it, redirect it, or shatter it. Ice is therefore not a damage school. It is a battlefield grammar. The Ice cultivator writes a Frost Lattice onto the world, catches motion in its lines, then breaks those lines at the moment of greatest consequence. Sphere Sentence: Ice cultivators build a Frost Lattice, catch motion in its crystalline lines, and shatter those lines to control where force can go. ### Sphere Boundaries Ice overlaps with several spheres, but it does not replace them. | Sphere | Difference from Ice | | --- | --- | | Water | Water flows, nourishes, erodes, and adapts. Ice arrests flow and gives it hard structure. | | Yin | Yin receives overextension and makes consequence incomplete. Ice externalizes motion into a crystalline lattice that can catch, redirect, or shatter. | | Mist | Mist obscures, condenses, softens, and conceals. Ice clarifies boundaries, hardens surfaces, and makes paths dangerous. | | Cold | Cold lowers temperature and damages through chill. Ice may use cold, but the sphere identity is crystalline structure and arrested motion. | | Crystal / Glass | Crystal and Glass emphasize clarity, refraction, fragility, and cutting facets. Ice emphasizes frozen terrain, arrested movement, and temporary structures formed from captured motion. | | Earth / Stone | Earth and Stone endure through weight, mass, and foundation. Ice endures briefly through geometry, pressure, and frozen order. | | Force | Force answers impact directly. Ice catches impact in structure, then lets that structure break or hold. | | Protection | Protection blocks harm. Ice creates surfaces, barriers, and brittle paths that change how movement and force travel. | | Yang | Yang completes force by making it rise and express itself. Ice completes force by making it take a fixed shape. | ### Using This Sphere Except where an Ice feature explicitly says otherwise, ordinary Fifth Edition rules remain in force. Ice does not automatically: create cover; block line of sight; block line of effect; make a creature Hidden or Invisible; restrain, grapple, knock prone, or reduce Speed; create difficult terrain; create a climbable bridge, wall, object, or barrier; freeze water, blood, poison, breath, spells, or souls; deal Cold damage; make a surface slippery; extinguish fire; prevent teleportation; counter a spell, sphere talent, or technique. A feature must state any such effect directly. #### Ice, Objects, and Surfaces Many Ice features create supernatural ice. Unless a feature says otherwise, this ice is temporary cultivation matter. It melts, evaporates, or breaks apart when the feature ends. It does not produce valuable permanent water, gems, crystal, or crafted goods. A Frost Lattice may appear as frost, snow-grain ice, blue-white lines, black ice, clear plates, hoarfrost script, rime chains, or razor facets. The appearance does not change its rules. #### Fire, Heat, and Ice Fire damage does not automatically destroy Ice effects unless a feature says it does. However, the GM may rule that intense mundane heat, lava, a furnace, dragonfire, a Fire sphere technique, or a relevant environmental hazard can damage, weaken, or disperse exposed ice. When this happens, use the object rules listed by the feature or the GM’s ruling. #### Lattice and Terrain A Frost Lattice is not automatically difficult terrain unless a feature says it is. A Frost Lattice can be visible or subtle, but a creature that can see the space can usually tell that supernatural ice is present unless you have a talent that conceals it. ### Core Ice Rules The Ice sphere uses Frost Lattice and Fracture Marks. A Frost Lattice is the Ice cultivator’s imposed crystalline pattern on the battlefield. A Fracture Mark is a fault line in a creature, object, or motion that the lattice can catch or break. Neither Frost Lattice nor Fracture Marks are base-game conditions. Immunity to a condition does not grant immunity to Fracture Marks unless a feature says otherwise. #### Lattice Limit You can maintain a number of 5-foot Lattice Spaces equal to your Proficiency Bonus + your Key Ability modifier, minimum 3. If you create a Lattice Space beyond this limit, choose one existing Lattice Space you created to end. A Lattice Space lasts for 1 minute, until you dismiss it, until it is destroyed, or until you are no longer on the same plane of existence as it. You may dismiss any number of your Lattice Spaces at any time, no Action required. Unless a talent says otherwise, a Lattice Space must be placed on a solid or liquid surface within range. It can coat ground, water, a wall, stairs, a roof, a weapon-sized object, or a similar surface. It cannot normally float unsupported in open air. #### Lattice Spaces Unless a feature changes them, your Lattice Spaces have the following rules. They are visible supernatural ice or frost. They do not create cover. They do not block line of sight. They do not block line of effect. They do not prevent movement. They do not make creatures fall prone by themselves. They do not damage creatures by themselves. They count as magical terrain created by your Ice sphere. You and willing creatures you choose when you create the spaces can move across those spaces without slipping and without paying extra movement from your Ice features. #### Breaking Lattice Spaces A creature can attack a Lattice Space. Unless a feature gives a different statistic, one 5-foot Lattice Space has AC 10 + your Proficiency Bonus and Hit Points equal to 5 + your Cultivation Level. It is immune to Poison and Psychic damage. When a Lattice Space is destroyed, only that 5-foot space ends. If an area effect deals at least 10 Fire damage to a Lattice Space, that Lattice Space ends unless the feature creating it says otherwise. #### Fracture Mark Limit You can maintain a number of Fracture Marks equal to your Proficiency Bonus. A creature or object can have only one Fracture Mark from you at a time unless a feature says otherwise. A Fracture Mark lasts until the end of your next turn, until you spend it, until the marked target is no longer on the same plane of existence as you, or until you dismiss it. #### Creating Frost Lattice You gain the following base ability. #### Crystallize Path Action Type: Action Factory Combat Bucket: action Factory Routing: combat_action_row Range: 60 feet Area: Up to two 5-foot Lattice Spaces Duration: 1 minute Cost: NoneConcentration: Not required Tags: Lattice You create Ice Lattice on surfaces you can see within range. The spaces may be connected or separate. The number of spaces you create increases as your cultivation deepens. | Cultivation Level | Lattice Spaces Created | | --- | --- | | CL 1-4 | 2 spaces | | CL 5-10 | 3 spaces | | CL 11-16 | 4 spaces | | CL 17-20 | 5 spaces | When a creature you did not designate as safe moves at least 10 feet across, out of, or through your Lattice Spaces during one turn, you may give that creature one Fracture Mark. This can happen only once per creature per turn. #### Shard Needle Action Type: Action Factory Combat Bucket: action Factory Routing: combat_action_row Range: 60 feet Target: One creature or object Cost: None Tags: Attack, Fracture You condense a line of frost into a needle of hard ice. Make a ranged Cultivation Attack. On a hit, the target takes Piercing or Cold damage, chosen when you make the attack, and gains one Fracture Mark. | Cultivation Level | Shard Needle Damage | | --- | --- | | CL 1-4 | 1d8 | | CL 5-10 | 2d8 | | CL 11-16 | 3d8 | | CL 17-20 | 4d8 | The damage is not the sphere’s identity. It is the visible sign of motion being forced into a cutting shape. #### Spending a Fracture Mark Once per round, when a marked creature or object you can perceive performs a triggering act, you may spend its Fracture Mark without using an Action. Choose one Fracture Response appropriate to the trigger. Catch Step. Trigger: the marked target begins movement, including special movement or teleportation. Reduce one of the target’s Speeds by 10 feet until the end of the current turn, or reduce the distance of one teleportation effect by 10 feet. At CL 11, this reduction becomes 20 feet. This cannot reduce a Speed or teleportation distance below 0. Brittle Opening. Trigger: the marked target is hit by an attack. The triggering attack deals extra Piercing or Cold damage equal to 1d4 + your Proficiency Bonus. At CL 11, the die becomes 1d6. Crack Aim. Trigger: the marked target makes an attack roll or Dexterity saving throw. Subtract 1d4 from the triggering roll. At CL 11, subtract 1d6 instead. Shatter Space. Trigger: the marked target enters, starts its turn in, or ends its turn in one of your Lattice Spaces. One Lattice Space occupied by the target shatters. The target must succeed on a Dexterity saving throw or take Piercing or Cold damage equal to your Shard Needle damage and fall Prone. On a success, it takes half as much damage and does not fall Prone. The chosen Lattice Space ends. Lock Grip. Trigger: the marked target uses an object, weapon, tool, focus, or held item. Until the start of its next turn, the target has Disadvantage on the next ability check or attack roll it makes using that item. If the item is unattended, you may instead freeze it to an adjacent surface until the start of your next turn. A creature can free the item early by using an Action and succeeding on a Strength check against your Ice Save DC. Crystal Guard. Trigger: the marked target is a willing creature and takes damage. Reduce the damage by 1d6 + your Key Ability modifier. This reduction increases to 2d6 at CL 5, 3d6 at CL 11, and 4d6 at CL 17. The mark then ends. #### Ice Saves Some Ice features require a saving throw. Unless a feature says otherwise, your Ice Save DC equals your Cultivation Save DC. #### Willing Creatures and Safe Passage When you create a Lattice Space, you may designate a number of willing creatures up to your Proficiency Bonus. Those creatures treat that Lattice Space as safe. Safe creatures do not trigger your Fracture Marks by moving across that Lattice Space, and they do not suffer harmful effects from your Ice talents unless you choose otherwise. A willing creature may end your Fracture Mark on itself at any time, no Action required. ### Using the Frost Lattice A Mortal Ice cultivator usually plays like this: Use Crystallize Path to place a few Lattice Spaces where movement matters. Use enemy movement or Shard Needle to apply a Fracture Mark. Spend the mark to catch a step, crack aim, expose a brittle opening, or shatter the space beneath the target. Use talents to turn the lattice into bridges, walls, armor, prisons, mirrors, avalanches, or higher-Realm formations. The player should be watching paths, surfaces, and repeated movement, not only selecting a damage option. ### Mortal Realm Ice Talents #### Sure-Footed Disciple Action Type: Passive Factory Combat Bucket: passive Factory Routing: passive_or_modifier_row Cost: None You have trained your body and qi to read ice as a written path. You ignore difficult terrain created by ice, snow, frost, or your own Ice sphere features. When you create Lattice Spaces, you may designate two additional safe creatures. #### Ice Bridge Scripture Action Type: No Action Factory Combat Bucket: passive Factory Routing: passive_or_triggered_modifier_row Trigger: You use Crystallize Path Cost: None Your Lattice Spaces can form simple unsupported bridges, ramps, stairs, or narrow platforms instead of needing to coat an existing surface. Each unsupported Lattice Space must be connected to a solid surface or another Lattice Space that ultimately connects to a solid surface. A creature can stand on these spaces. Each 5-foot unsupported Lattice Space can support up to one Large creature or four Medium or smaller creatures. If a supporting Lattice Space is destroyed, unsupported spaces depending on it collapse and end. #### Mirror-Slick Floor Action Type: No Action Factory Combat Bucket: passive Factory Routing: passive_or_triggered_modifier_row Trigger: A creature gains a Fracture Mark because it moved across one of your Lattice Spaces Cost: None The marked creature must succeed on a Dexterity saving throw or fall Prone. A creature that moved half its Speed or less during the turn has Advantage on this save. A creature that succeeds on the save is immune to your Mirror-Slick Floor until the start of your next turn. #### Rime Hook Action Type: No Action Factory Combat Bucket: passive Factory Routing: passive_or_triggered_modifier_row Trigger: You spend a Fracture Mark with Catch Step or Shatter Space Cost: None You may move the marked target 5 feet to an unoccupied space that is part of your Frost Lattice or adjacent to it. This forced movement does not provoke Opportunity Attacks. At CL 11, you may move the target 10 feet instead. #### Frost-Sheathed Guard Action Type: Bonus Action Factory Combat Bucket: bonus_action Factory Routing: combat_action_row Range: 30 feet Target: You or one willing creature Duration: 1 minute Cost: 1 CP Tags: Guard, Lattice A thin lattice of ice forms over the target’s clothing, armor, skin, or aura. The target gains Temporary HP equal to your Proficiency Bonus + your Key Ability modifier. While any of these Temporary HP remain, the first creature that hits the target with a melee attack before the effect ends gains a Fracture Mark. A creature can benefit from only one Frost-Sheathed Guard at a time. #### Snow-Script Tool Action Type: Action Factory Combat Bucket: action Factory Routing: combat_action_row Range: Touch Duration: 10 minutes Cost: None You create a simple tool, wedge, spike, hook, cup, splint, key blank, mirror, measuring rod, or similar handheld object of ice. The object cannot function as a weapon unless the GM allows it to count as an improvised weapon. It melts or shatters when the duration ends. The object is clear enough to hold simple writing or a diagram within it. You may use this talent to preserve a footprint, seal impression, wound outline, drop of liquid, or similar physical trace inside ice for the duration. #### White Step Counter Action Type: Reaction Factory Combat Bucket: reaction Factory Routing: combat_action_row Trigger: A creature you can perceive moves out of a space within 10 feet of one of your Lattice Spaces Cost: None You make the path behind the creature crack in pursuit. The triggering creature gains a Fracture Mark. If the creature was moving away from you or from one of your allies, you may also move 5 feet onto one of your Lattice Spaces without provoking Opportunity Attacks. #### Bitter Edge Action Type: Bonus Action Factory Combat Bucket: bonus_action Factory Routing: combat_action_row Range: Touch Duration: 1 minute Cost: 1 CP You coat one weapon, natural weapon, or unarmed strike with hard ice. Once on each of the wielder’s turns, when it hits a creature with that weapon or strike, it may deal extra Cold or Piercing damage equal to your Proficiency Bonus. If the target is standing on one of your Lattice Spaces, it also gains a Fracture Mark. #### Ice Seals the Door Action Type: Action Factory Combat Bucket: action Factory Routing: combat_action_row Range: 60 feet Target: One door, chest, gate, window, latch, hinge, wheel, lever, or similar object no larger than a 10-foot cube Duration: 1 minute Cost: 1 CP You freeze a mundane mechanism in place. A creature must use an Action and succeed on a Strength check against your Ice Save DC to open, force, turn, or operate the object. This does not prevent magical opening, teleportation, incorporeal passage, or effects that ignore the object unless the GM rules the effect physically interacts with the frozen mechanism. At CL 11, the duration becomes 10 minutes. ### Foundation Realm Ice Talents #### Glacier Wall Prerequisite: Foundation Realm Action Type: Action Factory Combat Bucket: action Factory Routing: combat_action_row Range: 60 feet Duration: 1 minute Cost: 2 CP Tags: Barrier, Lattice You create a wall of solid ice on surfaces within range. The wall is made of up to six 5-foot panels. Each panel must be contiguous with another panel or a solid surface. A panel can be vertical, horizontal, or angled. Each panel is an object with AC 12 + your Proficiency Bonus, Hit Points equal to 10 + twice your Cultivation Level, Immunity to Poison and Psychic damage, and Vulnerability to Fire damage. A panel provides cover normally for a solid object of its size and blocks line of effect through its space. A Glacier Wall panel counts as one of your Lattice Spaces for talents that refer to your Frost Lattice, but it does not count against your Lattice Limit. #### Frozen Meridian Bind Prerequisite: Foundation Realm Action Type: No Action Factory Combat Bucket: passive Factory Routing: passive_or_triggered_modifier_row Trigger: You spend a Fracture Mark with Catch Step and the target is on or adjacent to one of your Lattice Spaces Cost: 1 CP The target must succeed on a Strength saving throw or become Restrained by ice until the end of its next turn. A Restrained creature can use its Action to repeat the saving throw, ending the effect on itself on a success. A creature that succeeds on the initial save has its Speed reduced by the Catch Step effect but is not Restrained. #### Shatter Bloom Prerequisite: Foundation Realm Action Type: Action Factory Combat Bucket: action Factory Routing: combat_action_row Range: 60 feet Area: One or more of your Lattice Spaces Cost: 2 CP Tags: Shatter Choose up to a number of your Lattice Spaces equal to your Proficiency Bonus within range. Each chosen space shatters and ends. Each creature in a chosen space or within 5 feet of one must make a Dexterity saving throw. On a failed save, a creature takes Cold or Piercing damage equal to your Shard Needle damage + your Key Ability modifier and falls Prone. On a success, it takes half as much damage and does not fall Prone. A creature can be affected by only one shattering space from this talent each time you use it. #### Crystal Step Prerequisite: Foundation Realm Action Type: Bonus Action Factory Combat Bucket: bonus_action Factory Routing: combat_action_row Range: Self Cost: 1 CP You move along your lattice as though sliding through a written line. Teleport from one of your Lattice Spaces you occupy to another of your Lattice Spaces within 60 feet that you can see. This movement does not provoke Opportunity Attacks. If you appear adjacent to a creature with a Fracture Mark, you may immediately move that mark to another creature within 10 feet of you. #### Avalanche Writing Prerequisite: Foundation Realm Action Type: Reaction Factory Combat Bucket: reaction Factory Routing: combat_action_row Trigger: A creature falls Prone, is pushed, pulled, knocked back, or moved by one of your Ice features Range: 60 feet Cost: 1 CP You extend the lattice along the creature’s failed path. Create a number of Lattice Spaces equal to your Proficiency Bonus. Each new space must be adjacent to the triggering creature’s path, destination, or starting space. These spaces last until the end of your next turn and do not count against your Lattice Limit. #### Rime Mirror Surface Prerequisite: Foundation Realm Action Type: Bonus Action Factory Combat Bucket: bonus_action Factory Routing: combat_action_row Range: 60 feet Target: One of your Lattice Spaces Duration: 1 minute Cost: 1 CP The chosen Lattice Space becomes a clear mirror of ice. While you are within 60 feet of it, you can see and hear from that space as if standing there. You are Blinded and Deafened to your own body’s senses while using the mirror in this way, unless you end the perception at any time. A creature that studies the mirror with the Study action and succeeds on an Intelligence (Arcana or Investigation) check against your Ice Save DC realizes it is being used as a sensory focus. #### Winter Stores the Blow Prerequisite: Foundation Realm Action Type: Reaction Factory Combat Bucket: reaction Factory Routing: combat_action_row Trigger: A creature you can see takes damage while standing on one of your Lattice Spaces Cost: 1 CP The lattice stores part of the impact. Reduce the triggering damage by your Proficiency Bonus + your Key Ability modifier. One Lattice Space under or adjacent to the creature gains a stored fracture. The next time you use Shatter Space or Shatter Bloom on that space before the end of your next turn, add the amount reduced by this talent to one damage roll against one creature affected by that shatter. #### Ice Coffin Prerequisite: Foundation Realm Action Type: Action Factory Combat Bucket: action Factory Routing: combat_action_row Range: 60 feet Target: One creature with a Fracture Mark that is on or adjacent to one of your Lattice Spaces Duration: Concentration, up to 1 minute Cost: 3 CP The target must make a Strength saving throw. On a failed save, it becomes Restrained inside a shell of ice. While Restrained this way, the creature has Cover against attacks from outside the shell, cannot move from its space, and its voice is muffled but not silenced. At the end of each of its turns, the target may repeat the saving throw, ending the effect on itself on a success. The shell is also an object with AC 12 + your Proficiency Bonus and Hit Points equal to 10 + twice your Cultivation Level. If the shell is destroyed, the effect ends. This talent does not paralyze the target, prevent teleportation, stop purely mental actions, or prevent features that do not require physical movement unless the feature says otherwise. ### Core Formation Realm Ice Talents #### Ice Domain: Palace of Written Winter Prerequisite: Core Formation Realm Action Type: Action Factory Combat Bucket: action Factory Routing: combat_action_row Area: 30-foot-radius aura centered on you Duration: Concentration, up to 1 minute Cost: 4 CP Tags: Domain, Lattice You unfold a crystalline palace of frozen lines. The ground, walls, water, and suitable surfaces in the area become your Frost Lattice for the duration. This does not count against your Lattice Limit. While the Domain lasts: you may use Fracture Responses against marked creatures anywhere in the Domain; a hostile creature that moves at least 10 feet inside the Domain gains a Fracture Mark at the end of that movement; your safe creatures ignore difficult terrain caused by ice or snow inside the Domain; when you spend a Fracture Mark inside the Domain, you may create one Lattice Space in the Domain without using an Action. When the Domain ends, all temporary Lattice Spaces created by it end. #### Ninefold Crack Calculation Prerequisite: Core Formation Realm Action Type: No Action Factory Combat Bucket: passive Factory Routing: passive_or_triggered_modifier_row Trigger: You spend a Fracture Mark Cost: 1 CP Choose a second Fracture Response that has a different trigger from the first but can reasonably apply to the same event. Apply both responses to the marked target. For example, when a marked creature moves across your lattice, you might use Catch Step and Shatter Space. When a marked creature is hit by an attack while standing on your lattice, you might use Brittle Opening and Shatter Space. You cannot choose the same response twice. #### Living Glacier Advance Prerequisite: Core Formation Realm Action Type: Bonus Action Factory Combat Bucket: bonus_action Factory Routing: combat_action_row Range: 120 feet Cost: 2 CP Move any number of your Lattice Spaces up to 10 feet each along surfaces they could legally occupy. A Lattice Space cannot move through a creature’s space unless the creature is willing or Incapacitated. A hostile creature whose space is entered by a moving Lattice Space must succeed on a Dexterity saving throw or be pushed 5 feet in the direction the lattice moved and gain a Fracture Mark. On a success, the creature chooses whether to move 5 feet to an unoccupied adjacent space or allow the lattice to pass harmlessly beneath it. #### Thousand-Facet Prison Prerequisite: Core Formation Realm, Ice Coffin Action Type: Action Factory Combat Bucket: action Factory Routing: combat_action_row Range: 90 feet Target: One creature with a Fracture Mark Duration: Concentration, up to 1 minute Cost: 5 CP The target must make a Strength saving throw. On a failed save, it is trapped in a many-faceted prison of ice and is Restrained. While Restrained this way, the target cannot benefit from teleportation that would move it outside the prison unless it first succeeds on a Charisma saving throw against your Ice Save DC as part of the teleportation effect. At the end of each of its turns, the target repeats the Strength saving throw, ending the prison on itself on a success. Each failed repeat save gives the target one additional Fracture Mark, ignoring your usual one-mark limit for that target. When the prison ends, all Fracture Marks on the target beyond one immediately end. The prison is an object with AC 15 + your Proficiency Bonus and Hit Points equal to 20 + three times your Cultivation Level. Destroying the prison ends the effect. #### Frozen River Reversal Prerequisite: Core Formation Realm Action Type: Reaction Factory Combat Bucket: reaction Factory Routing: combat_action_row Trigger: A creature with a Fracture Mark moves or teleports from one space in your Frost Lattice to another space within 120 feet Cost: 3 CP The target must make a Strength saving throw if it moved physically, or a Charisma saving throw if it teleported. On a failed save, the movement resolves, then the target is returned to the space where the triggering movement began, or the nearest unoccupied space if that space is occupied. On a success, the movement is not reversed, but the target’s Speed is reduced by 10 feet until the end of its next turn. This talent does not undo attacks, spellcasting, object interactions, or other effects performed before or after the movement. It only reverses the movement path. #### Crystal Weather Script Prerequisite: Core Formation Realm Action Type: Action Factory Combat Bucket: action Factory Routing: combat_action_row Range: 120 feet Area: 20-foot-radius sphere Duration: Concentration, up to 1 minute Cost: 4 CP Snow-grain ice and floating crystal lines fill the area. The area is Lightly Obscured and is difficult terrain for hostile creatures. When a hostile creature starts its turn in the area, it must succeed on a Constitution saving throw or take Cold damage equal to your Shard Needle damage and gain a Fracture Mark. A strong wind does not disperse this weather, but a Fire sphere technique, Weather sphere technique, or comparable effect of equal or higher Realm may end it at the GM’s discretion. #### Heaven-Sealing Ice Script Prerequisite: Core Formation Realm Action Type: Reaction Factory Combat Bucket: reaction Factory Routing: combat_action_row Trigger: A creature with a Fracture Mark within 60 feet begins casting a spell, using a sphere talent, spending CP, or activating a named supernatural feature Cost: 3 CP You do not counter the technique. Instead, you freeze its outer path. The target must succeed on a Constitution saving throw or choose one: the triggering effect’s range is reduced by 30 feet, to a minimum of touch; the triggering effect’s area is reduced by 10 feet in one dimension, to a minimum of 5 feet; the triggering effect cannot move creatures or objects more than 10 feet; the triggering effect’s first damage roll is reduced by your Cultivation Level. If none of these choices can apply, this talent has no effect and the CP is not spent. #### Diamond Rime Body Prerequisite: Core Formation Realm Action Type: Bonus Action Factory Combat Bucket: bonus_action Factory Routing: combat_action_row Range: Self Duration: 1 minute Cost: 3 CP Your body becomes lined with rime channels and crystalline qi. For the duration: you gain Resistance to Cold damage; you have Advantage on saving throws against being knocked Prone or moved against your will; when a creature hits you with a melee attack, you may create one Lattice Space under yourself or the attacker without using an Action; the first time each round you use Crystal Guard on yourself, you do not count it against your once-per-round limit on spending Fracture Marks. This talent does not make you immune to freezing, suffocation, restraint, or environmental hazards unless those hazards deal Cold damage and the Resistance applies. ### Nascent Soul Realm Ice Talents #### Nascent Soul: Glacier Soul Takes Shape Prerequisite: Nascent Soul Realm Action Type: Passive Factory Combat Bucket: passive Factory Routing: passive_or_modifier_row Your soul has learned to hold a crystalline outline even when the body is pressured. You gain the following benefits: your Lattice Limit increases by your Proficiency Bonus; you may maintain one additional Fracture Mark beyond your normal limit; you can perceive vibrations through your Frost Lattice within 120 feet, allowing you to know the location of creatures touching it unless they are protected by a higher-Realm concealment, Void effect, or similar countermeasure; your Ice effects can exist in extreme heat for at least 1 round before environmental heat can weaken or destroy them, unless the heat comes from a higher-Realm supernatural source. #### Palace Where Footsteps Become Walls Prerequisite: Nascent Soul Realm, Ice Domain: Palace of Written Winter Action Type: No Action Factory Combat Bucket: passive Factory Routing: passive_or_triggered_modifier_row Trigger: A hostile creature in your Ice Domain moves at least 10 feet Cost: 2 CP After the movement resolves, create a number of Glacier Wall panels equal to your Proficiency Bonus along spaces the creature moved through or adjacent to those spaces. These panels last until the start of your next turn and do not cost additional CP. The panels cannot appear in occupied spaces, but they may split groups, block retreat, seal doors, divide lines of sight, or create cover. #### World-Fang Icefall Prerequisite: Nascent Soul Realm Action Type: Action Factory Combat Bucket: action Factory Routing: combat_action_row Range: 150 feet Area: 30-foot-radius, 60-foot-high cylinder Cost: 6 CP Tags: Lattice, Shatter You call down a formation of falling ice spears, plates, and crystalline script. The area becomes Frost Lattice until the end of your next turn and does not count against your Lattice Limit. Each creature in the area must make a Dexterity saving throw. On a failed save, a creature takes Cold or Piercing damage equal to twice your Shard Needle damage, falls Prone, and gains a Fracture Mark. On a success, it takes half damage and does not fall Prone or gain a mark. Until the lattice ends, the area is difficult terrain for hostile creatures, and the first time a hostile creature moves at least 10 feet in the area, you may use Shatter Space against it without spending a Fracture Mark. You must still obey the once-per-round limit unless another feature changes it. #### Frozen Trajectory Seal Prerequisite: Nascent Soul Realm Action Type: Reaction Factory Combat Bucket: reaction Factory Routing: combat_action_row Trigger: A ranged attack, line effect, thrown object, or visible projectile passes through or within 5 feet of one of your Lattice Spaces Cost: 4 CP The projectile’s path crystallizes. Reduce the triggering attack roll by 1d10, or grant one target of the triggering line effect a +1d10 bonus to its saving throw. If this causes the attack to miss or the target to succeed on the saving throw, you may suspend the visible projectile or line in ice until the start of your next turn. During that time, the path is visible, harmless, and counts as Frost Lattice for your Ice talents. At the start of your next turn, the suspended path shatters and ends. This does not stop effects that have no visible path, no projectile, no line, or no trajectory through space. #### Winter Palace Remembers the Intruder Prerequisite: Nascent Soul Realm Action Type: Passive Factory Combat Bucket: passive Factory Routing: passive_or_modifier_row Whenever a creature with a Fracture Mark damages one of your Lattice Spaces, destroys a Glacier Wall panel, or escapes one of your Ice restraints, it remains written into your lattice for 1 minute. For that duration, the first time on each of your turns that the creature touches one of your Lattice Spaces, you may give it a Fracture Mark without using an Action. You always know whether that creature is touching your Frost Lattice while it is within 1 mile of you, unless blocked by a higher-Realm concealment or Void effect. #### Immortal Winter Crucible Prerequisite: Nascent Soul Realm Action Type: Action Factory Combat Bucket: action Factory Routing: combat_action_row Range: Self Duration: 1 minute Cost: 6 CP You become the center of a slow, grinding winter. For the duration: whenever you create one or more Lattice Spaces, create one additional Lattice Space; once on each of your turns, you may spend a Fracture Mark without counting against your once-per-round limit; when a Lattice Space you created is destroyed, you may deal Cold or Piercing damage equal to your Proficiency Bonus to one hostile creature within 5 feet of that space; you have Resistance to Cold and Piercing damage. When this talent ends, you must choose half of your active Lattice Spaces, rounded down, to end immediately. ### Secret Inheritance #### The World Becomes a Single Crystal Prerequisite: Nascent Soul Realm, GM permission Action Type: Action Factory Combat Bucket: action Factory Routing: combat_action_row Range: Self Area: 120-foot-radius sphere centered on you Duration: 1 minute Cost: 10 CPRecharge: Once per Long Rest Tags: Secret Inheritance, Domain, Lattice You reveal the forbidden completion of the Ice Dao: for one minute, every path in the battlefield is part of a single crystal. For the duration: all ground, walls, ceilings, liquids, bridges, stairs, and similar surfaces in the area count as your Frost Lattice; this lattice does not count against your Lattice Limit; hostile creatures cannot benefit from being safe on your lattice unless you choose them; the first time each hostile creature moves at least 5 feet on its turn, it gains a Fracture Mark; you may spend Fracture Marks twice per round instead of once per round; when you use Shatter Space, you may choose not to end the Lattice Space if that space is part of the Secret Inheritance’s area rather than a separate Lattice Space you created. Once during the duration, when a creature with a Fracture Mark within the area begins movement, makes an attack roll, forces a saving throw, teleports, or activates a named technique, you may declare that the world has found the crack in that act. The creature must make a saving throw appropriate to the act: Strength for physical movement or melee force, Dexterity for ranged attack or evasive motion, Constitution for breath/body/meridian pressure, Intelligence for spell geometry or Formation logic, Wisdom for spiritual pressure, or Charisma for teleportation, command, or soul assertion. On a failed save, the triggering act still begins, but its path freezes before completion. The movement is reduced to 0, the attack misses, one target automatically succeeds on the saving throw, the teleport fails to move the creature, or the named technique loses its first damage roll or movement effect, as appropriate to the trigger. On a success, the triggering act resolves normally, but the creature takes Cold or Piercing damage equal to twice your Shard Needle damage and loses its Fracture Mark. This Secret Inheritance cannot erase an event that has already fully resolved. It freezes the path before completion. When the duration ends, all ice created by this Secret Inheritance cracks at once. Each hostile creature of your choice standing on the lattice must succeed on a Dexterity saving throw or fall Prone. ### Ice Drawbacks and Variant Scriptures Ice variants are optional cultivation scriptures that change how the sphere manifests. They are Tianxia-specific design tools inspired by drawback design, not imported casting-tradition rules. A variant should grant a meaningful benefit only if it also carries a real limitation. The drawback should change how Ice behaves at the table, not merely add flavor. Unless the GM says otherwise: you may choose at most one Ice drawback when you first learn the Sphere of Ice or undergo a major Ice initiation; Ice drawbacks are mutually exclusive unless the GM permits a special lineage; the drawback applies to all Ice talents you use; if a drawback grants a bonus talent whose prerequisites you do not yet meet, you gain that talent when you meet the prerequisites; if the drawback is retrained or removed, you lose the bonus talent or benefit it granted. #### Still Glacier Scripture You cultivate Ice as defense, shelter, and endurance. You gain Glacier Wall as a bonus talent when you meet its prerequisites. When you create a Glacier Wall, each panel gains additional Hit Points equal to your Proficiency Bonus + your Key Ability modifier. Drawback: The Glacier Does Not Chase. Your Frost Lattice cannot apply Fracture Marks to creatures solely because they move across your Lattice Spaces. You may still apply Fracture Marks with Shard Needle, White Step Counter, talents, and reactions that answer attacks or hostile actions. Your Ice is excellent at holding ground, but poor at pursuing motion that has not threatened your position. #### Razor Rime Scripture You cultivate Ice as cutting fracture and sudden collapse. You gain Shatter Bloom as a bonus talent when you meet its prerequisites. When you use Shatter Space or Shatter Bloom, you may reroll one damage die and use the new result. Drawback: Brittle Doctrine. Your Lattice Spaces and Glacier Wall panels have Vulnerability to Bludgeoning damage as well as any other vulnerability they possess. In addition, when you use a Shatter talent, at least one Lattice Space involved must end. Your ice cuts beautifully, but it does not endure patient pressure. #### Mirror Ice Scripture You cultivate Ice as reflection, surveillance, and perfect surface. You gain Rime Mirror Surface as a bonus talent when you meet its prerequisites. When you perceive through a Rime Mirror Surface, you may also speak through it in a quiet voice audible within 10 feet of the mirror. Drawback: The Mirror Requires a Face. Your Lattice Spaces must be visible, reflective, or light-catching to carry your Ice talents. You cannot hide your Frost Lattice, create invisible ice, or use Ice talents through total darkness unless another light source, reflection, divination, or Spirit Awakening feature lets the lattice be perceived. Creatures have Advantage on checks to notice your Lattice Spaces. #### Black Ice Scripture You cultivate Ice as treacherous footing and hidden danger. You gain Mirror-Slick Floor as a bonus talent. When a creature fails its save against your Mirror-Slick Floor, it also loses 10 feet of Speed until the start of its next turn. Drawback: No Safe Road. You may designate only yourself as safe when creating Lattice Spaces. Allies are not automatically protected from your slippery terrain, Shatter Space, or other area effects. You can still avoid harming allies by careful placement or by choosing not to trigger effects, but your scripture does not easily distinguish friend from foe. #### Snow-Seal Scripture You cultivate Ice as sealing, preservation, and restraint. You gain Ice Seals the Door as a bonus talent. When you use Ice Seals the Door, its duration is 10 minutes, or 1 hour at CL 11. Drawback: Seal Before Shatter. You cannot use Shard Needle, Shatter Space, Shatter Bloom, or any Ice talent to deal damage to a creature unless that creature is on or adjacent to one of your Lattice Spaces, has a Fracture Mark, is trapped by one of your Ice effects, or has damaged one of your Ice structures since the start of its last turn. Your Ice must first write a seal before it breaks the target. ### Path Synergies #### Body Refining Body Refining Ice cultivators train frozen marrow, ice-bone stance, tendon stillness, and sliding footwork. Suggested expressions: Lattice Spaces as footing drills, wall-running paths, or frozen stepping stones. Frost-Sheathed Guard as a body-hardening technique. Diamond Rime Body as an ice-bone transformation. Crystal Step as a physical sliding step rather than teleportation, if the GM prefers a martial presentation. #### Qi Cultivation Qi Cultivation is the most common Ice path. Qi cultivators write frost script, calculate lattice angles, shape battlefield formations, and turn terrain into a crystalline diagram. Suggested expressions: Crystallize Path as geometric qi inscription. Glacier Wall as a temporary Formation wall. Ice Domain as a battlefield array. Heaven-Sealing Ice Script as frozen technique geometry. #### Spirit Awakening Spirit Awakening Ice cultivators perceive the emotional and spiritual paths creatures intend to take, then freeze the moment of commitment. Suggested expressions: Fracture Marks as visible soul-cracks or intent-lines. Rime Mirror Surface as a reflective spirit lens. Frozen Trajectory Seal as freezing hostile intent in the air. Winter Palace Remembers the Intruder as the lattice remembering spiritual contact. ### Cultivation Insights #### Ice-Sure Footwork Prerequisite: Ice sphere You ignore difficult terrain caused by mundane ice and snow. If you already have Sure-Footed Disciple, you may also stand from Prone while on one of your Lattice Spaces by spending only 5 feet of movement. #### Lattice Scholar Prerequisite: Ice sphere, Qi Cultivation or Intelligence 13+ When you use Crystallize Path, you may create one additional Lattice Space, but that additional space lasts only until the end of your next turn. You also have Advantage on Intelligence (Arcana or Investigation) checks made to understand magical terrain, ice structures, crystalline formations, or battlefield arrays that use lines, angles, or repeating patterns. #### Winter Tempered Body Prerequisite: Ice sphere, Body Refining or Constitution 13+ When you gain Temporary HP from Frost-Sheathed Guard or another Ice feature, increase the amount by your Proficiency Bonus. Once per Long Rest, when you would be knocked Prone while standing on ice, snow, or your Frost Lattice, you may choose not to fall Prone. #### Mirror of Frozen Breath Prerequisite: Ice sphere, Spirit Awakening or Wisdom 13+ You can use Rime Mirror Surface as if you knew it, but only to perceive through a Lattice Space within 30 feet and only for 1 round. Once you use this Insight, you cannot use it again until you finish a Short or Long Rest. If you already know Rime Mirror Surface, its range increases by 30 feet for you. #### Shatter Without Waste Prerequisite: Ice sphere, Foundation Realm Once per turn when one of your Lattice Spaces would end because you used Shatter Space or Shatter Bloom, you may instead reduce its remaining duration to the end of your next turn. If it would already end at or before that time, this Insight has no effect. You cannot use this Insight with Razor Rime Scripture unless the GM allows it.

#### Spending a Fracture Mark
Once per round, when a marked creature or object you can perceive performs a triggering act, you may spend its Fracture Mark without using an Action. Choose one Fracture Response appropriate to the trigger.
Catch Step.
Trigger: the marked target begins movement, including special movement or teleportation. Reduce one of the target’s Speeds by 10 feet until the end of the current turn, or reduce the distance of one teleportation effect by 10 feet. At CL 11, this reduction becomes 20 feet. This cannot reduce a Speed or teleportation distance below 0.
Brittle Opening.
Trigger: the marked target is hit by an attack. The triggering attack deals extra Piercing or Cold damage equal to 1d4 + your Proficiency Bonus. At CL 11, the die becomes 1d6.
Crack Aim.
Trigger: the marked target makes an attack roll or Dexterity saving throw. Subtract 1d4 from the triggering roll. At CL 11, subtract 1d6 instead.
Shatter Space.
Trigger: the marked target enters, starts its turn in, or ends its turn in one of your Lattice Spaces. One Lattice Space occupied by the target shatters. The target must succeed on a Dexterity saving throw or take Piercing or Cold damage equal to your Shard Needle damage and fall Prone. On a success, it takes half as much damage and does not fall Prone. The chosen Lattice Space ends.
Lock Grip.
Trigger: the marked target uses an object, weapon, tool, focus, or held item. Until the start of its next turn, the target has Disadvantage on the next ability check or attack roll it makes using that item. If the item is unattended, you may instead freeze it to an adjacent surface until the start of your next turn. A creature can free the item early by using an Action and succeeding on a Strength check against your Ice Save DC.
Crystal Guard.
Trigger: the marked target is a willing creature and takes damage. Reduce the damage by 1d6 + your Key Ability modifier. This reduction increases to 2d6 at CL 5, 3d6 at CL 11, and 4d6 at CL 17. The mark then ends.

#### Create Figment
Action Type: Action
Factory Combat Bucket: action
Factory Routing: combat_action_row
Range: 60 feet
Area: One 10-foot cube
Duration: Concentration, up to 10 minutes
Cost: None
Tags: Image, Figment, Premise
You create the image or sound of something that is not actually there. Examples include a wall, beast, cultivator, banner, footstep, voice, warning bell, spirit-lantern, falling stone, corpse, door, or patch of false terrain.
The figment’s maximum area increases with your Cultivation Level.
| CL | Maximum Figment Size |
| --- | --- |
| 1-4 | 10-foot cube |
| 5-10 | 15-foot cube |
| 11-16 | 20-foot cube |
| 17-20 | 25-foot cube |
As long as you are within range of the figment, you may use your Action to move it to another point within range. As it moves, you may alter its appearance so the movement seems natural, such as making a false beast run or a false guard gesture. If you do not use your Action to control it, the figment repeats a simple motion or remains still.
When a creature that can perceive the figment makes an attack roll, targets a creature with a harmful effect, moves willingly, takes a Reaction, or makes a Perception, Insight, Investigation, or Survival check while acting on the figment as if it were real, you may force that creature to make a Wisdom saving throw. On a failed save, the creature gains one False Premise from you until the start of your next turn.
Augment 1 CP: The figment includes both sight and sound. If you have Sensory talents, you may apply any of those sensory layers as part of the same figment.
Augment 1 CP: Increase the figment’s maximum area by one step: 20-foot cube at CL 1-4, 30-foot cube at CL 5-10, 40-foot cube at CL 11-16, and 50-foot cube at CL 17-20.
Augment 2 CP: The figment lasts for its remaining duration without Concentration. You may apply this augment on your turn after creating the figment without using an Action.

#### Misdirection Responses
When you trigger a Misdirection Response, choose one option from the list below.
| Response | Effect |
| --- | --- |
| False Opening | The next attack roll made against the target before the start of your next turn has Advantage. |
| Wrong Angle | The target has Disadvantage on the triggering attack roll or ability check. |
| Lost Timing | The target cannot take Reactions until the start of its next turn. If the triggering event was a Reaction, that Reaction fails. |
| Stolen Step | The target’s Speed is reduced by 10 feet until the start of its next turn, and one creature of your choice within 5 feet of the target may move 5 feet without provoking Opportunity Attacks from that target. |
| Misread Target | If the triggering event targets a creature and another legal target is within 5 feet of the original target, the triggering creature has Disadvantage on the triggering roll or saving throw pressure against the original target. This does not force the effect to target an illegal creature. |
You can trigger only one Misdirection Response per round unless a talent says otherwise.

spheres.full_exact_source_text: # Sphere of Illusion Qi Expression: Primary — Mirage Qi; Supporting — Light Qi, Dream Qi, Mind Qi, Xun-Subtle Qi. “The crude liar changes the answer. The master illusionist changes the question the enemy believes they were asked.” Sphere Type: Power Sphere Primary Path: Spirit Awakening Secondary Path: Qi Cultivation Rare Variant: Body Refining through the Mirage Body Insight Resource: CP Common Effects: false premises, figments, glamers, decoys, sensory overlays, misdirected targeting, altered witness memory, false terrain, psychic pressure, battlefield confusion, and spiritual misrecognition Illusion is the cultivation of the false premise. An Illusion cultivator does not need a lie to last forever. They need the enemy to make one real choice based on the wrong truth. The arrow is loosed at the wrong silhouette. The guard opens the wrong gate. The killer turns toward a false footstep. The spirit judges a borrowed face. By the time the illusion is disproved, the choice has already happened. Sphere Sentence: Illusion cultivators plant a false premise, let a creature act on it, and turn the mistaken choice into a tactical opening. ### Sphere Boundaries Illusion overlaps with several spheres, but it does not replace them. | Sphere | Difference from Illusion | | --- | --- | | Dreams | Dreams governs sleep, dreamscapes, nightmares, and dream logic. Illusion deceives waking perception and immediate interpretation. | | Mirrors | Mirrors governs reflection, reversal, copied appearance, identity inversion, and image-as-counterpart. Illusion creates false premises and sensory misdirection, not true mirrored doubles. | | Shadow | Shadow is the second silhouette created by light and form. Illusion may create false shadows, but it does not command real shadow substance unless a talent says so. | | Darkness | Darkness controls the absence of light. Illusion may make something appear dark, hidden, or obscured, but it does not automatically extinguish light or create real darkness. | | Mind | Mind directly alters thought, emotion, memory, compulsion, and cognition. Illusion influences perception and interpretation; it does not rewrite loyalty, personality, or desire unless a talent states a narrow exception. | | Space | Space changes distance, position, portals, and teleportation. Illusion can make distance appear false, but it does not move creatures through space unless a talent explicitly grants movement. | | Void | Void removes, negates, and hollows. Illusion does not erase truth; it covers truth with a false premise. | | Creation | Creation makes real objects or matter. Illusion may make a creature believe an object is present, but it does not make the object real. | ### USING THIS SPHERE Except where an Illusion talent explicitly says otherwise, ordinary fifth-edition rules remain in force. Illusion does not automatically: create physical matter; create a real wall, bridge, creature, item, weapon, trap, shelter, or tool; provide Cover; block line of effect; block movement; create real Difficult Terrain; create real light, darkness, fire, smoke, fog, water, poison, food, or medicine; make a creature Hidden; make a creature Invisible; teleport a creature; force a creature to take an action; alter a creature’s memories, loyalties, personality, statistics, or creature type; perfectly mimic a unique spiritual signature; bypass Truesight, Blindsight, divine senses, Secret Inheritances, Formations, or higher-Realm perception. A talent must state any such effect directly. ### USING ILLUSIONS IN PLAY Illusions require clear table expectations. The following rules are part of this sphere unless the GM changes them for a specific campaign. #### Belief and Disbelief A creature does not automatically disbelieve an illusion merely because magic exists. A guard who sees a new wall in a familiar alley may be suspicious, but the wall could be an illusion, a real wall created by another sphere, a Formation, or a temporary barrier. Suspicion gives a reason to Study or test the illusion; it does not automatically reveal it. A creature that knows it is facing an Illusion cultivator may act more aggressively against possible illusions, but that choice carries risk. If the illusionist first creates a false wall and later an ally creates a real wall, a creature that charges through without checking may suffer the consequences normally. #### Studying an Illusion A creature that can perceive an illusion may use the Study action to inspect it. The creature makes an Intelligence (Investigation) check against your Cultivation Save DC. On a success, the creature recognizes that specific illusion as false. It can perceive the illusion as a faint outline, false overlay, hollow echo, spiritual paint, mismatched scent, wrong pressure, or other obvious unreality. A creature that recognizes an illusion ignores that illusion’s mechanical penalties. Recognizing one illusion does not automatically reveal your other illusions. #### Physical Interaction and Proof Physical interaction with a visual figment usually reveals the contradiction because objects and creatures pass through it. A hand passing through a false door, an arrow passing through a false wall, or a creature walking through a false soldier may automatically prove the illusion false to witnesses who can perceive the contradiction. A creature does not need to stand next to an illusion to interact with it. Throwing a stone, firing an arrow, using a pole, sending a summoned creature, or watching another creature pass through it can be enough. Greater sensory talents can prevent casual touch from revealing the lie, but they do not create substance or weight unless a talent says so. A false hat may feel like cloth, but it cannot be removed from the wearer’s head as a real hat. #### Illusory Cover An illusory wall, fog bank, curtain, boulder, barricade, or creature can discourage attacks, block sight for creatures that believe it, and create a False Premise. It does not grant physical Cover unless a talent says so. If a creature attacks through an illusory wall and the attack succeeds, the creature sees the attack pass through the illusion and recognizes that the wall is not physical. The target did not gain Cover from the illusion unless a talent explicitly provided it. #### Covering Objects and Creatures A figment can be placed over an object, doorway, corpse, creature, trap, or passage to hide it or change its apparent shape. Unless a talent says otherwise, the figment does not automatically move with the object or creature. You must move or control the figment normally. A glamer is different: it attaches to a creature or object and moves with it. #### Alternative Uses Illusions can be useful even when no one is fooled in combat. You may use a sound to throw your voice, display a map you have seen, recreate a suspect’s face, create a warning sign, enhance a performance, make food seem more appealing, demonstrate a battle plan, or carry a whispered message through a false echo. The GM may allow an appropriate Illusion talent to grant Advantage on a relevant ability check when the illusion is used creatively and its limitations matter. #### Sensory Mismatch A creature that primarily relies on a sense your illusion does not affect may ignore the illusion or have Advantage to Study it. A wolf may disbelieve a false person that has no scent. A creature with Blindsight may ignore a purely visual decoy. A tremor-sensing creature may notice that the false giant has no footfall. Greater Illusion, Veiled Illusion, Intelligent Illusion, and similar talents exist to cover these gaps. ### CORE ILLUSION RULES #### False Premises A False Premise is the core chassis of this sphere. It is a short-lived illusion, phantasm, sensory cue, spiritual misreading, or social deception that causes a creature to act on the wrong assumption. A False Premise is not a condition. It does not control a creature’s mind. It does not force a creature to take an action. It changes what the creature perceives or how it interprets the immediate scene. Unless a talent says otherwise: a creature can be affected by only one False Premise from you at a time; a False Premise ends immediately after you trigger a Misdirection Response from it; a False Premise also ends if the target recognizes the relevant illusion as false; creatures immune to illusions, creatures that cannot perceive the relevant sensory channel, and creatures whose superior perception pierces the illusion ignore that False Premise; a False Premise cannot make a creature choose an illegal target, space, action, or effect. #### Figments A figment is an external illusion that creates the appearance, sound, scent, touch, taste, aura, or apparent presence of something that is not actually there. A figment does not have mass, Hit Points, AC, Strength, weight, or carrying capacity unless a talent says otherwise. A figment cannot attack, hold a door, carry a creature, block a corridor, catch falling objects, trigger pressure plates, or provide real Cover. Unless a talent says otherwise, you can move or alter a figment only as described by the ability that created it. #### Glamers A glamer is an illusion attached to a creature or object. It changes how that target is perceived. A glamer moves with its target. A glamer does not change the target’s statistics, true size, actual equipment, creature type, true spiritual signature, or physical capabilities unless a talent says so. A disguise may make a sword look like a walking stick, but the sword is still a sword. Unlike most figments, a glamer usually cannot be disproved merely by seeing that the false image is stationary. It follows the target, but contradictions can still reveal it. #### Obstructions An obstruction is an illusion that interferes with perception inside an area rather than presenting a single false object. It may blur sight, muffle sound, erase scent, hide auras, or confuse mental impressions depending on the talent. An obstruction is not physical matter and does not provide Cover or block movement unless a talent says so. A creature may Study the obstruction to identify it as illusory, but recognizing the obstruction does not automatically remove its sensory interference unless the talent says so. #### Superior Senses Truesight recognizes ordinary visual illusions within its range. It does not automatically protect against every mental, emotional, spiritual, or symbolic phantasm unless the talent says so. Blindsight can perceive normally within its range if the illusion is only visual and the creature can still sense the true position of creatures and objects. Tremorsense can pinpoint eligible creatures touching the same surface, but it does not count as sight. Secret Inheritances, higher-Realm illusions, artifact illusions, Formation-based illusions, and superior spiritual deception may require a Cultivation Check or GM ruling even against strong senses. #### Hidden and Invisible Some Illusion talents make a creature Invisible. This uses the ordinary Invisible condition. Becoming Invisible does not automatically make the creature Hidden. Other creatures may still know the target’s location from sound, tracks, scent, disturbance of water, displaced dust, spiritual pressure, or other clues. A creature that wants to become Hidden must still use the Hide action unless a talent says otherwise. #### Concentration Many Illusion talents require Concentration. A talent that requires Concentration follows the ordinary rules for Concentration. You cannot maintain two Concentration effects at the same time unless another rule explicitly allows it. #### Talent Tags Some Illusion talents have one or more of the following tags. | Tag | Meaning | | --- | --- | | Image | Creates false external sensory information. Usually defeated by Study, physical contradiction, Truesight, or superior senses. | | Figment | Creates an external illusion that is not attached to a real creature or object. | | Glamer | Alters how a creature or object appears. A glamer moves with its target. | | Obstruction | Interferes with one or more senses inside an area. | | Veil | Alters how a creature, object, place, or technique appears. A veil does not change physical statistics. | | Phantasm | Attacks or deceives perception from within. Physical interaction may not be enough to disprove it unless the talent says so. | | Decoy | Creates a false target or false position. Choose one premise that can be expressed in a single sentence, such as: “The bridge is safe.” “The assassin is behind you.” “The gate is already open.” “Your ally has betrayed you.” “The wound came from elsewhere.” “The elder’s command was spoken.” “The treasure is in my hand.” The target makes a Wisdom saving throw. Failed Save: Until the end of its next turn, the target treats the premise as true for the purpose of one immediate choice. The premise cannot force self-destruction, make the target choose an illegal action, rewrite long-term loyalty, create physical matter, teleport a creature, or override direct divine, artifact, or Secret Inheritance-level protection. When the target acts on the premise, choose up to two Misdirection Responses and apply them. The target then immediately recognizes that something impossible occurred, but may not know what part was false. Successful Save: The target is not affected and is immune to this Secret Inheritance until you finish a Long Rest. Overreach: If the premise contradicts something the target is currently touching, suffering, holding, or directly experiencing, the target has Advantage on the saving throw. ### ILLUSION DRAWBACKS AND VARIANT SCRIPTURES Illusion variants are optional cultivation scriptures that change how the sphere manifests. They are Tianxia-specific limitations, not imported casting-tradition rules. A variant should grant a real benefit only if it also gives a real limitation. The drawback should change how Illusion behaves at the table, not merely add flavor. Unless the GM says otherwise, choose at most one Illusion variant when you first learn the sphere or undergo a major Illusion initiation. Illusion variants are mutually exclusive unless the GM allows a specific combination. If a variant grants a bonus talent whose prerequisites you do not yet meet, you gain that talent when you meet its prerequisites. If you later remove the variant, you lose the bonus talent or special benefit it granted. #### Pure Stage Scripture You cultivate Illusion through theater, ceremony, misdirection, open performance, and social deception rather than direct psychic harm. Benefit. You gain Borrowed Voice or Illusory Disguise as a bonus talent. In addition, when you use an Illusion talent as part of open performance, ceremony, diplomacy, theater, ritual misdirection, or a public distraction, you have Advantage on one Charisma (Performance), Charisma (Deception), or Charisma (Persuasion) check made before the end of that scene. Drawback: No Blood on the Painted Stage. Your Illusion cultivation does not easily harm creatures that have not accepted the scene you paint. You cannot use an Illusion talent to deal damage to a creature unless at least one of the following is true: the creature currently has a False Premise from you; the creature failed a saving throw against one of your Illusion talents since the start of your previous turn; the creature has damaged another creature, forced another creature to make a saving throw, spent CP, used a spell slot, used a supernatural feature, or willingly caused a hostile supernatural effect since the start of its last turn. This drawback does not prevent you from creating False Premises, disguises, glamers, decoys, sensory cues, or non-damaging Misdirection Responses. #### Silent Mirage Scripture You cultivate Illusion through sight, posture, scent, color, heat-shimmer, spiritual pressure, and implied motion rather than sound. Benefit. Your Image and Veil talents do not automatically reveal you by sound unless the talent itself creates sound. You have Advantage on ability checks made to conceal the visual or spiritual signs of your Illusion talents. Drawback: Voiceless Art. Your Minor Illusion, Create Figment, and Borrowed Voice cannot create speech or named voices unless you spend 1 additional CP. You cannot perfectly imitate a named creature’s voice unless you have studied that voice for at least 1 minute or the creature is currently within 60 feet and speaking. In addition, whenever an Illusion talent of yours depends primarily on false sound, a creature has Advantage on the first check it makes to Study that sound unless the sound is paired with a visual, scent, tactile, or spiritual cue from the same illusion. #### Brutal Phantasm Scripture You cultivate Illusion as psychic pressure. Your lies do not merely mislead the senses; they bruise the mind that accepts them. Benefit. Once per turn when you trigger a Misdirection Response against a creature that failed a Wisdom saving throw against one of your Illusion talents since the start of your previous turn, you may deal Psychic damage to that creature equal to your Proficiency Bonus. Drawback: Cruel Illusion Announces Itself. Your illusions carry hostile psychic weight. When a creature succeeds on a saving throw against one of your Phantasm or Premise talents, it immediately knows that a supernatural illusion attempted to affect it. Until the end of its next turn, that creature has Advantage on the next saving throw or Study check it makes against one of your Illusion talents. In addition, when you use Illusory Disguise or Obscuring Glamer on a willing creature other than yourself, the target carries a faint unsettling aura. A creature that Studies the target has Advantage on its first check to recognize the illusion as supernatural. #### Honest Actor Scripture You cultivate Illusion as admitted art, ritual mask, and symbolic truth. Your falsehoods reveal meaning rather than stealing identity or rewriting memory. Benefit. You have Advantage on Charisma checks made as part of open performance, theater, ceremony, diplomacy, ritual misdirection, confession, or symbolic disguise. When you use Plant False Premise during such a scene, you may choose one witness that is not hostile to you. That witness has Disadvantage on the first Wisdom (Insight) or Intelligence (Investigation) check it makes against that specific performance before the scene ends. Drawback: No Stolen Face. You cannot use Illusion talents to impersonate a specific living creature without that creature’s permission, unless the impersonation is obviously theatrical, ceremonial, masked, or symbolic. You cannot learn Unreliable Witness, Thousand-Face Procession, or The One False Premise Beneath Heaven without GM permission or a major story initiation that breaks this scripture. You may still use generic disguises, masks, false uniforms, false voices, decoys, and symbolic roles, but you do not erase or steal a person’s identity. #### Anchored Mirage Scripture Your illusions are stronger when fastened to a visible object, talisman, painted banner, mirrorless tablet, incense trail, lantern, mask, or other physical anchor. Benefit. When you create a non-instantaneous Illusion talent with a duration of at least 1 minute, you may anchor it to an unattended object or worn focus within the talent’s range. While the anchor remains intact and within the talent’s range, creatures have Disadvantage on the first Study check they make against that illusion. Drawback: Break the Anchor, Break the Lie. If you use this benefit, the illusion depends on the anchor. The anchor is visibly or spiritually marked as the source of the illusion. A creature that can perceive the anchor may target it. Unless the GM gives the anchor better statistics, it has AC 13, Hit Points equal to twice your CL, and Immunity to Poison and Psychic damage. If the anchor is destroyed, removed more than 120 feet from the illusion, or suppressed by a suitable anti-magic, anti-formation, or anti-illusion effect, the Illusion talent immediately ends. #### Imageless Scripture You cultivate Illusion through sound, scent, touch, aura, misremembered pressure, and absence rather than visible images. Benefit. You gain Greater Illusion as a bonus talent. Creatures do not automatically disbelieve your figments merely by passing through a visual image, because your primary illusions have no image to pass through. Drawback: No Painted Form. You cannot create visual figments, visual disguises, visual decoys, false written text, false visible terrain, or visible false creatures. You may still use Obstructions that blur or remove sight, and you may still use glamers that suppress or obscure a target rather than give it a new appearance. You cannot learn False Double, Illusory Army, Mirage, Mirage City, Thousand-Face Procession, or any talent whose primary function is visual deception unless the GM allows a special nonvisual version. #### Veilbound Scripture You cultivate Illusion by changing what already exists rather than creating independent figments. Benefit. You gain Illusory Disguise, Obscuring Glamer, or Veiled Illusion as a bonus talent. When you apply a glamer to a willing creature or object, increase its duration by one step: 10 minutes becomes 1 hour, 1 hour becomes 8 hours, and 8 hours becomes 24 hours. Drawback: No Free Phantom. You cannot use Create Figment except to create Obstructions. Your Illusion talents must be attached to a creature, object, place, aura, Formation, or existing sensory event. You cannot learn Complex Figments, Illusory Army, Programmed Illusion, Mirage, Mirage City, or Permanent Illusion unless the GM allows you to anchor those talents to fixed objects or Formations. ### PATH SYNERGIES #### Spirit Awakening: Mind-Painted Premise You may use Wisdom as your Illusion key ability. Your illusions may create convincing spiritual impressions. Spirits, ghosts, possessing entities, and similar beings do not automatically ignore your illusions merely because the illusion is not physical. When an Illusion talent attempts to deceive a spirit, soul, possession effect, or supernatural sense that would normally ignore mundane sensory deception, you may make a Cultivation Check. The GM sets the DC or opposes the check with the relevant creature or effect. #### Qi Cultivation: Mirage Qi Once per turn, when you spend CP on an Illusion talent, reduce the CP cost by 1, to a minimum cost of 1 CP. In addition, increase the range of your Illusion talents by 30 feet, unless the talent has a range of Self, Touch, or Ritual. #### Body Refining: Mirage Body This synergy requires the Mirage Body Cultivation Insight. You may use Constitution as your Illusion key ability and spend Stamina instead of CP on Illusion talents. While False Double, Obscuring Glamer, Greater Invisibility, Sovereign Illusion Incarnation, or another Illusion talent that directly veils your body is active on you, you gain the following benefits: +1 bonus to AC; your Speed increases by 10 feet; once per turn when a creature misses you with an attack roll because of an Illusion talent, you may move 5 feet without provoking Opportunity Attacks from that creature. These benefits do not apply unless one of the listed effects is active on you. This synergy does not grant natural weapons, armor, extra attacks, teleportation, or automatic Hidden status. ### CULTIVATION INSIGHTS #### Mirage Body Prerequisite: Body Refining, CL 4+ You may learn Illusion talents. When using Illusion, you use Constitution as your key ability and spend Stamina instead of CP. You gain the Mirage Body Path synergy. #### Perfect Disguise Prerequisite: Illusion, CL 8+ Your Illusory Disguise improves. It lasts until you finish a Long Rest. It can alter apparent height by up to 2 feet. It can convincingly mimic a studied voice. Checks made to deceive ordinary visual, vocal, or social inspection with the disguise have Advantage. Perfect Disguise still does not change physical size, statistics, equipment, creature type, or true spiritual signature. #### Phantom Duelist Prerequisite: Illusion, CL 8+ Once per turn when a creature misses you because of False Double, Obscuring Glamer, False Obstruction, Greater Invisibility, Sovereign Illusion Incarnation, or another Illusion talent you created, choose one of the following effects: move 5 feet without provoking Opportunity Attacks; gain Advantage on your next attack roll against that creature before the end of your next turn; deal Psychic damage to that creature equal to your Proficiency Bonus. #### Illusion Breaker Prerequisite: Illusion, CL 8+ You have Advantage on checks and saving throws made to recognize, resist, or see through illusions. Once per Short Rest, when you identify an illusion, you may use your Reaction to attempt to suppress it until the start of your next turn. Make a Cultivation Check against the illusion’s Save DC. On a success, the illusion is suppressed for you and for allies within 10 feet of you until the start of your next turn. Suppressing an illusion does not dispel it permanently. #### Layered Premise Scripture Prerequisite: Illusion, CL 10+ You may maintain two Minor Illusion effects at the same time without Concentration. In addition, once per round when you trigger a Misdirection Response, you may spend 1 CP to avoid ending the False Premise that produced it. That False Premise still ends at its normal duration. #### Mind-Anchor Actor Prerequisite: Illusion, Spirit Awakening or proficiency in Deception, CL 10+ When a creature succeeds on a check to recognize one of your Illusion talents, you may spend 1 CP as a Reaction to force it to make a Wisdom saving throw. On a failed save, the creature recognizes that something is false but misidentifies the false element. For example, it may believe the sound is false but the image is real, or that the disguise is mundane rather than spiritual. This effect lasts until the end of the creature’s next turn. #### Programmed Stage Artist Prerequisite: Programmed Illusion, CL 10+ When you create a Programmed Illusion, its trigger may respond to one additional category of cue: scent, aura, pressure, written symbol, emotional tone, or spoken intent. The GM decides whether a trigger is too broad to be reliable. In addition, once per Long Rest, you may create one Programmed Illusion without spending CP. ### QUICK REFERENCE | Rule | Summary | | --- | --- | | Core loop | Plant a false premise, let the creature act on it, trigger a Misdirection Response. | | Figment | External false image, sound, or sensory event. Not physical. Does not move with a target unless controlled. | | Glamer | Illusion attached to a creature or object. Moves with the target. | | Obstruction | Area sensory interference. Not matter, not Cover, not movement blocking. | | Disbelief | Use Study with Intelligence (Investigation) against Cultivation Save DC. Obvious contradiction may reveal the illusion. | | Illusory cover | May block perceived sight but does not grant physical Cover unless a talent says so. | | Invisibility | Does not automatically make the target Hidden. | | Superior senses | Truesight, Blindsight, Tremorsense, and spiritual perception interact based on what the illusion actually deceives. | | Variants | Grant benefits only when paired with real drawbacks. |

#### Create Figment
Action Type: Action
Factory Combat Bucket: action
Factory Routing: combat_action_row
Range: 60 feet
Area: One 10-foot cube
Duration: Concentration, up to 10 minutes
Cost: None
Tags: Image, Figment, Premise
You create the image or sound of something that is not actually there. Examples include a wall, beast, cultivator, banner, footstep, voice, warning bell, spirit-lantern, falling stone, corpse, door, or patch of false terrain.
The figment’s maximum area increases with your Cultivation Level.
| CL | Maximum Figment Size |
| --- | --- |
| 1-4 | 10-foot cube |
| 5-10 | 15-foot cube |
| 11-16 | 20-foot cube |
| 17-20 | 25-foot cube |
As long as you are within range of the figment, you may use your Action to move it to another point within range. As it moves, you may alter its appearance so the movement seems natural, such as making a false beast run or a false guard gesture. If you do not use your Action to control it, the figment repeats a simple motion or remains still.
When a creature that can perceive the figment makes an attack roll, targets a creature with a harmful effect, moves willingly, takes a Reaction, or makes a Perception, Insight, Investigation, or Survival check while acting on the figment as if it were real, you may force that creature to make a Wisdom saving throw. On a failed save, the creature gains one False Premise from you until the start of your next turn.
Augment 1 CP: The figment includes both sight and sound. If you have Sensory talents, you may apply any of those sensory layers as part of the same figment.
Augment 1 CP: Increase the figment’s maximum area by one step: 20-foot cube at CL 1-4, 30-foot cube at CL 5-10, 40-foot cube at CL 11-16, and 50-foot cube at CL 17-20.
Augment 2 CP: The figment lasts for its remaining duration without Concentration. You may apply this augment on your turn after creating the figment without using an Action.

#### Misdirection Responses
When you trigger a Misdirection Response, choose one option from the list below.
| Response | Effect |
| --- | --- |
| False Opening | The next attack roll made against the target before the start of your next turn has Advantage. |
| Wrong Angle | The target has Disadvantage on the triggering attack roll or ability check. |
| Lost Timing | The target cannot take Reactions until the start of its next turn. If the triggering event was a Reaction, that Reaction fails. |
| Stolen Step | The target’s Speed is reduced by 10 feet until the start of its next turn, and one creature of your choice within 5 feet of the target may move 5 feet without provoking Opportunity Attacks from that target. |
| Misread Target | If the triggering event targets a creature and another legal target is within 5 feet of the original target, the triggering creature has Disadvantage on the triggering roll or saving throw pressure against the original target. This does not force the effect to target an illegal creature. |
You can trigger only one Misdirection Response per round unless a talent says otherwise.
