#### Misdirection Responses
When you trigger a Misdirection Response, choose one option from the list below.
| Response | Effect |
| --- | --- |
| False Opening | The next attack roll made against the target before the start of your next turn has Advantage. |
| Wrong Angle | The target has Disadvantage on the triggering attack roll or ability check. |
| Lost Timing | The target cannot take Reactions until the start of its next turn. If the triggering event was a Reaction, that Reaction fails. |
| Stolen Step | The target’s Speed is reduced by 10 feet until the start of its next turn, and one creature of your choice within 5 feet of the target may move 5 feet without provoking Opportunity Attacks from that target. |
| Misread Target | If the triggering event targets a creature and another legal target is within 5 feet of the original target, the triggering creature has Disadvantage on the triggering roll or saving throw pressure against the original target. This does not force the effect to target an illegal creature. |
You can trigger only one Misdirection Response per round unless a talent says otherwise.

one property the Vessel can receive safely;

whether the Vessel would suffer backlash if imbued carelessly.

spheres.full_exact_source_text: # Sphere of Imbuement Qi Expression: Primary — Infusion Qi; Supporting — Tool Qi, Pattern Qi, Metal/Wood Carrier Qi. “A thing is never only what it is. It is what the right command can make it remember.” Common Name: Imbuement Sphere Sphere Type: Power Sphere / Utility-Control Sphere Primary Path: Qi Cultivation Secondary Paths: Spirit Awakening; Body Refining through contact, worn gear, held tools, scars, tattoos, armor, and explicit Insights Resource: Cultivation Points, Concentration, and Mandate Load Common Effects: Temporary property commands, weapon and armor imbuement, object reinforcement, weight and speed alteration, silence and resonance mandates, focus and reflex adjustment, construct/object animation, vessel-spirit awakening, hostile degradation, suppressing equipment bonuses, and high-Realm law-like edicts. ### Imbuement Dao Imbuement is the cultivation of temporary authority over a vessel’s nature. A sword has an edge. A body has weight. A robe has silence. A mind has clarity. An Imbuement cultivator does not create these qualities from nothing. They place a brief command into the target’s pattern and force the world to remember that command until the mandate fades. ### Realm Progression Mortal Realm. The cultivator can read ordinary vessels, place one simple Mandate, degrade one exposed property, and improve or suppress mundane equipment. Mortal Imbuement is visible and practical: sharpened blades, muffled boots, lightened packs, hardened doors, slowed enemies, and awakened little tools. Foundation Realm. The cultivator learns to write Mandates into Qi rather than mere surface quality. Mandates can be set without constant concentration, carried through weapon strikes, layered in limited ways, or placed on supernatural equipment. Constructs and simple objects can be animated more reliably. Core Formation Realm. The cultivator establishes a local law of properties. A court of Mandates can make an area lighter, quieter, sharper, heavier, brittle, wakeful, or obedient. The cultivator can awaken vessel spirits, command large objects, and issue Mass Mandates. Nascent Soul Realm. The cultivator speaks to the true name of a vessel. A property can be rewritten at the level of concept for a short time: gravity can turn, a weapon can cut what it normally cannot, a city gate can remember it is dust, or an army’s armor can forget protection. Secret Inheritance. The cultivator issues an Edict that renames one battlefield property until Heaven corrects the lie. ### 2024 Fifth-Edition Rules Baseline This draft assumes the 2024 fifth-edition baseline used by Tianxia. Use the 2024 meanings of Action, Bonus Action, Reaction, Attack action, Unarmed Strike, Opportunity Attack, Advantage, Disadvantage, Cover, Concentration, Exhaustion, Grappled, Restrained, Stunned, Incapacitated, and object interaction unless this sphere explicitly replaces or expands them. #### Concentration and Sustained Mandates A Mandate with a duration of Concentration, up to 10 minutes follows normal Concentration rules. If your Concentration ends, the Mandate ends. If a feature says the Mandate is set, it no longer requires Concentration for the listed duration. #### Objects and Worn Equipment An unattended mundane object usually receives no saving throw. A creature carrying, wearing, wielding, or controlling an object may resist a hostile Mandate on that object. An intelligent item resists as a creature. A Mandate that alters a weapon, armor, shield, tool, or other equipment does not grant proficiency, attunement, weapon mastery, class features, or item command words unless the talent explicitly says so. #### Object Statistics If an object needs AC, hit points, damage thresholds, or break DCs, use the 2024 object and improvised-damage guidance chosen by the GM. This sphere gives local rules for animated objects and Mandate-bearing objects when needed. #### Magic Items and Artifacts A magic item can receive ordinary beneficial Imbuements if it is a legal vessel. Hostile Fray effects against magic items usually require an Imbuement Check or opposed Cultivation Check. Artifacts, sect treasures, soul-bound weapons, inheritance items, and plot-defining treasures may ignore ordinary Imbuement unless the feature or story explicitly permits a contest. #### Saving Throws Unless a talent states otherwise, an unwilling creature or a creature resisting a hostile effect on its possession makes a Wisdom saving throw against your Cultivation Save DC. Some physical mandates call for Strength, Dexterity, or Constitution saves when listed. ### Key Ability, Save DC, and Costs Use your Path key ability for Imbuement save DCs unless a Path synergy changes it. Cultivation Save DC: 8 + your Proficiency Bonus + your key ability modifier. Imbuement Check: d20 + your Proficiency Bonus + your key ability modifier. Use this to overwrite, counter, or contest a Mandate when a talent calls for it. CP Costs: If a feature lists a CP cost, spend CP from your Path’s cultivation pool. A character without a CP pool cannot use CP-costed Imbuement features unless a class feature, item, or GM ruling provides an alternative. ### Core Imbuement Rules #### Vessel A Vessel is a target capable of holding a Mandate. A Vessel can be: a creature; a weapon, natural weapon, or unarmed strike; armor, shield, clothing, or worn gear; a tool, instrument, lock, door, rope, chain, vehicle part, or other object; an unattended object; a construct; a corpse, plant, tree, or prepared body when a talent permits; a talisman, Formation Node, artifact housing, or other special medium when another sphere or feature permits. A Vessel must be physically present and within range. A creature behind Total Cover is not a valid target unless the talent says otherwise. #### Mandate A Mandate is a temporary command placed into a Vessel’s property. Mandates come in paired forms. Beneficial commands are usually called Imbue effects. Hostile, suppressive, or degrading commands are usually called Fray effects. Examples include: Sharpen / Dull; Harden / Brittle; Lighten / Burden; Quicken / Slow; Clarify / Cloud; Silence / Resound; Fortify / Expose; Animate / Still; Wake / Stupor; Elemental Mantle / Elemental Dimming; Function / Suppress Function. A Mandate is a magical or supernatural cultivation effect unless a talent says it is purely physical. #### Mandate Load You can sustain one active Mandate at a time by default. If you place a second active Mandate, the first ends unless a talent, Realm evolution, or feature increases your Mandate Load. Your Mandate Load is the number of separate Mandates you can sustain at once. Each target and each property usually counts separately. If one feature applies the same Mandate to several targets as a Mass Mandate, it tells you how much Load it uses. Set Mandates that no longer require Concentration still count against Mandate Load unless the feature says otherwise. #### Same-Property Rule A Vessel cannot benefit from two Mandates that alter the same property unless a talent says they can be layered. For example: two weapon-damage Imbuements do not stack; two armor-bonus Imbuements do not stack; two weight-altering Mandates do not stack; a Quicken Mandate and a Slow Mandate on the same movement mode oppose each other; a Silence Mandate and a Resound Mandate oppose each other. When a new Mandate would affect the same property, the caster chooses whether it replaces the old Mandate. If the old Mandate belongs to another cultivator or an unwilling target, use the Opposed Mandate rule. #### Opposed Mandates If you attempt to place a Fray effect on a target currently affected by the matching Imbue effect, or an Imbue effect on a target currently affected by the matching Fray effect, make an Imbuement Check against the existing effect’s DC. DC: the existing creator’s Cultivation Save DC, or 10 + Pattern Rank if the effect has no creator. Success: the existing Mandate ends. You may then apply your new Mandate if the original action and target remain legal. Failure: your action is spent and the new Mandate does not apply. CP is spent if the feature had a CP cost. #### Stored Statistics A Mandate uses your Cultivation Save DC, Cultivation Attack Modifier, key ability, Proficiency Bonus, and Cultivation Level at the time you place it. If it is set into an object, talisman, or prepared vessel, record those values. #### Identifying an Imbuement A creature can use the Study action to examine a visible or perceivable Mandate. The GM chooses Arcana, Investigation, Religion, Medicine, Insight, or a relevant tool proficiency. The DC is usually your Cultivation Save DC. Success reveals the Mandate family, whether it is beneficial or hostile, whether it requires Concentration, and one obvious way to disrupt it. #### Disrupting an Imbuement A Mandate can end because: its duration expires; the creator loses Concentration; the Vessel leaves legal range for an effect that requires range; the Vessel is destroyed; an opposed Mandate overwrites it; Qiweaving, Formations, Talismans, or another feature dispels, suppresses, or unweaves it; a listed physical vulnerability is exploited. ### Base Sphere Abilities #### Read the Vessel Action Type: Multi-Mode Canonical Action Type: Multi-Mode Factory Combat Bucket: action Timing Detail: Study action or 1 minute of examination Factory Routing: combat_action_plus_examination_variant Split Review Decision: single_combat_action_plus_procedure_variant Recommended Factory Realization: procedures=ONE_MINUTE_EXAMINATION Range: 30 feet, or touch for hidden internal properties Target: One creature, object, weapon, armor, tool, construct, or special vessel Cost: None You study a Vessel’s surface properties and qi-response. Success: the target gains lasting sentience or awakens as a story creature, item spirit, awakened beast, or vessel-person. Its exact stat block, loyalty, and rights are determined by the GM. It is initially friendly if treated well, but not mindlessly enslaved. Failure: the awakening fails and the GM chooses one backlash: a flawed spirit, hostile vessel, incomplete sentience, curse, possession opening, broken item spirit, or sect-level consequence. This talent is intentionally a story procedure, not a routine combat buff. #### Unmake the King’s Armor - Counter Prerequisite: Suppress Item Spirit, CL 15+ Action Type: Action Factory Combat Bucket: action Factory Routing: combat_action_row Range: 120 feet Target: One creature wearing, wielding, or carrying imbued, magical, spiritual, or artifact-like equipment Cost: 4 CP; once per long rest Choose one item or equipment layer you can perceive. Make an Imbuement Check against the target’s Cultivation Save DC or the item’s DC, whichever is higher. Success: suppress one equipment-based bonus, defensive property, weapon property, mobility property, or item activation until the end of your next turn. If the target is not artifact-grade or inheritance-grade, the suppression lasts 1 minute. Failure: the item flares in resistance. You take force damage equal to your Cultivation Level and cannot target that item again until after a long rest. #### Mandate Without Vessel - Domain Prerequisite: Sovereign of the True Name of Things, CL 15+ Once per long rest, when you create your Court of Ten Thousand Mandates, choose one property law rather than a target family: all unsecured metal is heavy; all blades are dull; all footfalls are silent; all speech resounds; all armor is brittle; all arrows seek; all doors resist opening; all tools remember precision; all fire-bearing weapons dim; all exhausted bodies ignore one level of fatigue. The law applies only inside the Court, only to valid Vessels, and only while the Court lasts. Creatures and attended items save normally if hostile. ### Secret Inheritance #### The Edict That Names the World Again Secret Imbuement Inheritance Prerequisite: Sovereign of the True Name of Things, CL 17+, inheritance scripture or equivalent story breakthrough Action Type: Action Factory Combat Bucket: action Factory Routing: combat_action_row Range: 300 feet Area: 120-foot-radius Sphere or one colossal visible Vessel Duration: Until the end of your next turn; some lesser effects last 1 minute Cost: 10 CP; once per week You speak an Edict that briefly renames one property of the battlefield. Choose one Edict: All Blades Remember Hunger. Willing allies’ weapons in the area count as magical, ignore Resistance to Bludgeoning, Piercing, and Slashing damage, and deal extra damage equal to your Cultivation Level once before the duration ends. Hostile weapons must save or become Dull. All Armor Forgets Mercy. Willing allies’ armor and shields reduce incoming damage by your Proficiency Bonus + key ability modifier. Hostile armor and shields must save or lose magical AC bonuses until the end of your next turn. All Weight Obeys My Palm. Choose up, down, inward, outward, or toward one visible point. Unsecured objects and creatures that fail a Strength saving throw fall or slide in that direction up to 60 feet, taking damage as appropriate if they collide. All Voices Are Mine to Permit. Willing allies can speak, transmit commands, and use verbal techniques through noise, silence, or distance inside the area. Hostile creatures must save or be unable to speak clearly, use verbal components, or issue command words until the end of your next turn. All Vessels Wake and Bow. Unattended objects up to Large size in the area animate until the end of your next turn and obey one simple command. Attended objects may save through their bearer. Magic items and artifacts may resist with opposed Cultivation Checks. All Weakness Becomes Obvious. Until the end of your next turn, you and allies in the area know which of Strength, Dexterity, Constitution, Intelligence, Wisdom, or Charisma is lowest for each hostile creature you can perceive. The first saving throw each hostile creature makes against that ability before the duration ends has Disadvantage. All False Nature Is Denied. Choose one ongoing enhancement, degradation, polymorph, item buff, weight change, speed alteration, false vigor, animated object, or similar property-changing effect on each hostile target in the area. Make one Imbuement Check against the highest relevant DC. On a success, suppress all chosen effects until the end of your next turn. Failure or Resistance. A creature, artifact, sect treasure, Secret Inheritance, or superior Realm effect may resist with an opposed Cultivation Check. On a failed Edict against a superior effect, you take psychic or force damage equal to twice your Cultivation Level and cannot use this inheritance again until you complete a major cultivation session. This inheritance does not permanently rewrite reality, create permanent sentience, forge artifacts, replace Talismans/Formations/Alchemy, or grant ownership of another cultivator’s soul-bound treasure. It is one impossible command, not a new world. ### Imbuement Drawbacks and Variant Scriptures A character may normally choose at most one Imbuement drawback when first learning the sphere or undergoing major Imbuement initiation. A drawback grants the listed bonus talent or benefit while changing how Imbuement works. If a drawback is removed, the bonus is lost. #### Personal Imbuement Scripture You can only target yourself and your own worn, held, carried, tattooed, scarred, armored, or equipped Vessels with Place Mandate and Fray Mandate. Mandates on an object end at the end of your turn if the object is no longer in your possession. Gain one Mandate talent as a bonus talent. #### Entropic Imbuement Scripture You cannot use Place Mandate except to counter an existing Fray effect on yourself or your equipment. You specialize in degradation, suppression, dulling, brittleness, burden, clouding, and hostile property commands. Gain one Fray-capable Mandate talent as a bonus talent. Your Fray Mandates impose a -1 penalty on the first saving throw made against them. #### Vessel-Focus Scripture Choose one vessel category: weapons, armor and shields, tools, constructs and objects, bodies, or awakened vessels. You can use Imbuement only on that vessel category unless a Secret Inheritance or Forged Technique says otherwise. Gain one talent that works with your chosen vessel category as a bonus talent. #### Touch-Only Inscription Your range for Place Mandate, Fray Mandate, Counter-Mandate, and Read the Vessel is touch. However, you may use Touch-Carried Mandate without spending CP once per short or long rest. Gain Touch-Carried Mandate as a bonus talent when you meet its prerequisite. #### Visible Mandate Scripture Your Imbuements are always obvious: glowing script, burning sigils, visible seals, ringing commands, metallic frost, or spirit-calligraphy. You cannot hide them without a separate technique. Gain Read the Vessel or Counter-Mandate as a bonus talent. If you already have both, gain one Mandate talent. ### Path Synergies #### Body Refining - Vessel-Body Imbuement Body Refining cultivators do not normally project detached property commands through external Qi. Their Imbuement is embodied: stance, scars, tattoos, breath, armor, held tools, weapons, bones, blood rhythm, and direct contact. When using Imbuement through Body Refining: you may use Constitution as your key ability for Imbuement save DCs and checks; your default range for Place Mandate and Fray Mandate is touch unless targeting yourself, worn gear, held gear, armor, shield, natural weapon, unarmed strike, or an object physically connected to you; you may treat your body as armor for Tempered Equipment, Harden and Brittle, Lighten and Burden, Physique and Weakness, False Vigor, and Fortify and Expose; when you hit with an Unarmed Strike, natural weapon, or held weapon bearing one of your Imbue Mandates, you may use Touch-Carried Mandate if you know it; you cannot animate distant objects, awaken vessel spirits at range, or issue Mass Mandates without an Insight, item, sect ritual, Forged Technique, or explicit feature. This is not a penalty. It is the Body Refining version of the sphere: the body is the furnace and the carried vessel is the command surface. #### Qi Cultivation - Pattern-Inscribing Qi Qi Cultivation is the most natural full user of Imbuement. When using Imbuement through Qi Cultivation: you may use Intelligence or Charisma as your key ability for Imbuement save DCs and checks; increase the range of Place Mandate, Fray Mandate, and Counter-Mandate by 30 feet; once per turn when you place a Mandate on an object or willing creature, you may move one visible thread of Qi between yourself and the target without an action; when you spend CP to set a Mandate, reduce the CP cost by 1, minimum 1, once per turn. #### Spirit Awakening - Vessel-Spirit Command Spirit Awakening cultivators speak to the intent, memory, and spirit of Vessels. When using Imbuement through Spirit Awakening: you may use Wisdom as your key ability for Imbuement save DCs and checks; Read the Vessel can detect whether an object has a vessel spirit, haunting, lingering owner-intent, resentment, loyalty, curse, or oath-mark; you have Advantage on checks to use Speak to the Vessel, Awaken Vessel Spirit, or Awaken True Vessel Spirit; when you Fray an item carried by a creature, you may choose whether the visible expression is physical damage, spiritual refusal, emotional recoil, or item-spirit rebellion; once per short or long rest, when you would fail an Imbuement Check against an awakened item or vessel spirit, reroll the check. ### Cultivation Insights #### Careful Inscription Prerequisite: Imbuement sphere, CL 4+ When you place a Mandate on a willing target outside combat, its duration is doubled, to a maximum of 1 hour. In addition, you have Advantage on checks to identify your own Mandates and on checks to teach another creature what your Mandate does. #### Vessel-Body Scripture Prerequisite: Imbuement sphere, Body Refining Path, CL 6+ You can externalize a Body Refining Imbuement through a held weapon, armor, shield, tattoo, scar, or wrapped talisman-strip. Your range for Place Mandate and Fray Mandate becomes 15 feet when the target is connected to you by a physical medium such as a chain, rope, weapon strike, thrown object, blood mark, armor plate, sash, or direct line of contact. Once per short or long rest, when a Mandate on your body or worn gear would end because your Concentration breaks, you may take damage equal to your Proficiency Bonus x your Cultivation Level to keep it active until the end of your next turn. This damage cannot be reduced or redirected. #### Efficient Mandate Prerequisite: Imbuement sphere, CL 6+ Once per short or long rest, when you spend CP to set a Mandate, reduce the CP cost by 1, minimum 0. At CL 11, you may use this Insight twice per short or long rest. #### Hidden Command Prerequisite: Imbuement sphere, Quiet and Resound or Read the Vessel, CL 8+ Your Mandates can be made subtle. When you place a Mandate, you may hide its visible signs. A creature must use Study or magical detection to notice it. If the Mandate is hostile and the target fails its first saving throw, it does not automatically know you placed the Mandate unless the effect is obvious, such as sudden weight, speech loss, weapon dulling, or armor rebellion. #### Dual Mandate Adept Prerequisite: Layered Mandate, CL 8+ Your Mandate Load increases by 1. When you use Layered Mandate, reduce the CP cost by 1, minimum 0. #### Awakener of Tools Prerequisite: Animate Minor Vessel or Speak to the Vessel, CL 8+ You may keep one Tiny or Small animated object active without it counting against Mandate Load. It cannot attack while excluded from Mandate Load, but it can follow, carry, fetch, point, open simple doors, hold a lantern, ring a bell, write simple marks, or assist with tool use. #### Mandate Breaker Prerequisite: Counter-Mandate, CL 10+ When you use Counter-Mandate and fail the Imbuement Check, you may spend 1 CP to turn the failure into a partial success. The target effect is suppressed until the start of your next turn, but not ended. Once per long rest, when you succeed on Counter-Mandate by 5 or more, you may immediately place a matching opposite Mandate without spending additional CP. #### Sect Imbuement Seal Prerequisite: Imbuement sphere, Talismans or Formations sphere, CL 12+ You can help create sect-standard temporary item seals. During downtime, you may contribute one Imbuement Mandate you know to a talisman, Formation Node, training hall, armory seal, vault mark, or ritual vessel project. The project still requires normal materials, time, maintenance, and GM approval. This Insight does not let you mass-produce permanent magic items by itself.

Action Type: Action
Factory Combat Bucket: action
Factory Routing: combat_action_row
Range: 30 feet
Target: One active Mandate or similar enhancement/degradation effect
Cost: 1 CP
You attempt to suppress or overwrite an active property-command effect. Make an Imbuement Check against the effect’s DC. If the effect has no listed DC, use 10 + its Pattern Rank or 10 + the creator’s Proficiency Bonus + key ability modifier.
Success: the target effect ends or is suppressed until the end of your next turn. If you know the matching opposite Mandate, you may immediately apply it as part of the same action if the target is legal and fails any required saving throw.

spheres.full_exact_source_text: # Sphere of Ink Qi Expression: Primary — Inscription Qi; Supporting — Record Qi, Water-Ink Qi, Law/Name Qi. Sphere Type: Power / Script / Record / Mark Sphere Primary Path: Qi Cultivation Secondary Path: Spirit Awakening Rare Access: Body Refining through Inked Body or comparable body-script practice Resource: CP, prepared ink or pigment, Press Marks, written surfaces, seals, and Concentration when a talent says so Core Chassis: Living Ink, Ink Lash, Press Mark, Read the Trace “The brush does not merely record the world. The brush leaves a trace the world must answer.” Ink cultivators refine intent until it can survive outside the body as a visible stroke. Their Dao is not simple writing. They cultivate the moment when thought leaves a trace, when a name clings to a surface, when a seal closes a path, and when a painted thing remembers enough life to move. #### Core Dao Ink is the cultivation of the trace that becomes law. A sword cut vanishes after it wounds. A flame dies when fuel is gone. A spoken curse fades when the breath ends. Ink remains. It marks. It records. It stains. It hides. It reveals. It binds what has been named and gives outline to what was only imagined. The Ink scripture asks five questions. What trace remains after intent leaves the body? What does a mark prove, conceal, or command? What can a written seal keep closed? What painted thing is real enough to matter? What name is so true that the world cannot ignore it? #### Sphere Type Ink is a Restricted Power Sphere. Primary Path: Qi Cultivation. Secondary Path: Spirit Awakening. Rare Body Access: Body Refining through the Inked Body Insight or a similar initiation. Resource: CP, unless a Path synergy or Insight says otherwise. Default Key Ability: Intelligence for careful calligraphy, sealcraft, and diagram logic. A Spirit Awakening cultivator may use Wisdom through Soul Ink. A Body Refiner using Inked Body usually uses Constitution. #### What Ink Covers Ink governs the following. Living Ink and spiritual calligraphy. Ink Marks placed on creatures, objects, doors, walls, terrain, and prepared surfaces. Concealing and revealing inscriptions. Binding scripts and written restraints. Brushstroke attacks and defensive strokes. Painted beasts, ink doubles, and temporary illustrations. Scripture walls, sealed passages, vault inscriptions, and written barriers. Scripted techniques stored in scrolls or paintings. Ink River passages between marked surfaces. True names, written forms, and identity-revealing calligraphy at high Realm. #### What Ink Does Not Cover Ink does not replace every written or painted discipline in the game. Ink and Talisman: Talisman is the sphere of prepared consumable writs, paper charms, sealed spells, and portable ritual devices. Ink can write, mark, and create limited Scripted Techniques, but it is not the main sphere for mass-producing talismans or talisman economy. Ink and Formations: Formations govern large prepared arrays, geomantic patterns, battlefield diagrams, and positional rituals. Ink can draw marks and short-lived scripture effects, but it does not replace full Formation arrays. Ink and Puppetry: Ink can animate simple painted beasts or doppelgangers. It does not create the full command architecture, body replacement, remote puppet warfare, or persistent puppet armies of Puppetry. Ink and Space: Ink River Passage folds distance only through prepared painted marks. It is not general teleportation and cannot replace Space as the sphere of spatial law. Ink and Fate: True Name Calligraphy can expose identity, but Ink does not normally rewrite destiny, mandate, luck, or karmic ledgers. Fate owns those themes. Ink and Wax: Wax receives impressions and seals through yielding form. Ink writes, stains, and commands through visible trace. A wax seal and an ink seal may overlap in fiction but use different Dao engines. #### Core Terminology Living Ink: Spiritual ink animated by cultivated intent. It may appear as black calligraphy, vermilion seals, golden scripture, painted animals, flowing shadows, brushstroke weapons, floating characters, or animated diagrams. Ink Mark: A mark placed by an Ink feature or talent. Ink Marks may be visible, concealed, glowing, disguised as ordinary writing, or hidden beneath spiritual pressure depending on the talent used. Stroke: A short-lived attack, defense, movement, or shaping effect produced by Living Ink. Script: A written effect that remains on a creature, object, surface, passage, or zone for its duration. Illustration: A temporary image made real enough to move, strike, distract, or guard. Seal: A script that closes, restricts, locks, preserves, reveals, or forbids a target. #### General Ink Rules Maximum Active Ink Marks: You may maintain a number of active Ink Marks equal to your Proficiency Bonus + your key ability modifier, minimum 1. Creating another Ink Mark beyond this limit causes your oldest Ink Mark to fade, unless a talent says otherwise. Default Ink Mark Duration: Unless a talent says otherwise, an Ink Mark lasts 1 hour. Ink Mark Visibility: When you create an Ink Mark, decide whether it is obvious or concealed. A concealed Ink Mark can be discovered with a Wisdom (Perception) or Intelligence (Investigation) check against your Cultivation Save DC, or by appropriate magical detection. Removing an Ink Mark: A creature adjacent to an Ink Mark may use an action to scrape, wash, cut, disrupt, or dispel it. This requires an appropriate ability check, tool check, or Cultivation Check against your Cultivation Save DC. Some marks may require special access, such as touching the marked creature or reaching the marked surface. Ink and Surfaces: Ordinary Living Ink can mark most solid surfaces. Marking running water, open air, fire, loose sand, mist, or other unstable media requires a specific talent, a prepared focus, or GM approval. Ink and Creatures: When a talent places an Ink Mark on an unwilling creature, that creature usually makes a Dexterity saving throw unless the talent says otherwise. On a success, the mark fails to take hold. Ink and Damage: Ink talents commonly deal Slashing, Psychic, Force, or Acid damage, depending on whether the technique cuts, assaults the mind through written form, hardens into spiritual structure, or dissolves like corrosive ink. Ink and Literacy: A creature does not need to read a language to be affected by Ink. The writing is spiritual pattern first and language second. Benefit: You may use Ink talents without speaking as long as you can move one hand, brush, sleeve, eye, or body inscription. Restriction: Effects that restrain your entire body, blind your spiritual perception, or prevent all gesture may still stop your Ink talents. Tradeoff: Your Ink Marks are easier to physically notice. Checks to find your Ink Marks gain a +2 bonus unless you spend +1 CP when creating the Mark. ### Path Synergies #### Qi Cultivation - Living Brush You refine the motion of breath, wrist, and meridian into a brush that does not hesitate. Benefits: Once per turn, reduce the CP cost of one Ink talent by 1, minimum 1. Increase your maximum active Ink Marks by your Proficiency Bonus. Additional Benefit: When you use Ink Lash from your own space, you may curve it around one obstacle that provides half cover, but not three-quarters cover or total cover. #### Spirit Awakening - Soul Ink You write on spirit before matter. Benefits: You may use Wisdom as your Ink key ability. Your Ink Marks can affect ghosts, spirits, incorporeal creatures, possessing entities, and similar beings normally, provided you can perceive or target them. When using Revealing Script or Soul-Staining Ink on one of these creatures, it has Disadvantage on the first saving throw. Additional Benefit: Read the Trace can identify whether a written effect is bound to a spirit, possession, oath, memory, or soul fragment. #### Body Refining - Inked Body Requires the Inked Body Insight or equivalent initiation. Benefits: You may inscribe a number of body Ink Marks on your skin equal to your Proficiency Bonus. Body Ink Marks last until your next long rest unless removed. Body Inscription Benefits: For each active body inscription, choose one benefit. +1 AC. Speed +5 feet. +1 to one saving throw category. Advantage on checks to escape Grappled or Restrained. Increase unarmed reach by 5 feet on your turn. Add your Proficiency Bonus to one calligrapher’s supplies, painter’s supplies, or tattooing check. Stacking: The same benefit may be chosen more than once only with GM approval. ### Cultivation Insights #### Inked Body Prerequisite: Body Refining, CL 4+. Effect: You may learn Ink. You use Stamina instead of CP for Ink talents, use Constitution as your Ink key ability, and gain the Body Refining - Inked Body synergy. #### Master Calligrapher Prerequisite: Ink sphere, CL 8+. Effect: Increase your active Ink Mark maximum by +2. Your Ink Marks last 8 hours instead of 1 hour unless the talent has a shorter duration. #### Living Illustration Adept Prerequisite: Painted Beast, CL 8+. Effect: Painted Beast gains +2 AC, additional HP equal to 2 x your CL, and one additional form benefit from Living Illustration. #### Scripture Breaker Prerequisite: Ink sphere, CL 8+. Effect: Gain Advantage on checks made to read magical writing, disable runes, identify seals, remove Ink Marks, break written curses, understand Formation inscriptions, or contest talismanic scripts. Reaction: Once per short rest, when a written magical effect activates within 30 feet, you may use your Reaction to attempt to suppress it. Make a Cultivation Check against the effect’s save DC. On a success, the effect is suppressed until the start of your next turn. #### Red Seal Authority Prerequisite: Ink sphere, CL 10+. Effect: When you create a Seal talent, you may mark it with vermilion authority. The first creature that fails a check or saving throw against that Seal takes Psychic damage equal to your Proficiency Bonus + your key ability modifier. Additional Benefit: You have Advantage on social checks made to present official, sect, bureaucratic, or ritual written authority when your claim is at least partly true. #### Brush-Armed Guard Prerequisite: Brushstroke Shield, CL 8+. Effect: When Brushstroke Shield reduces damage to 0, you may place a simple Ink Mark on the attacker if it is within 60 feet and you can see it. An unwilling creature makes a Dexterity saving throw to avoid the Mark. #### Patient Inscription Prerequisite: Ink sphere. Effect: When you spend at least 10 minutes creating an Ink Mark or Seal, choose one. Increase its duration by one step, from 1 hour to 8 hours, or from 8 hours to 24 hours. Give one creature Disadvantage on its first check to find or remove it. Allow it to survive ordinary rain, dust, handling, and minor abrasion. Hide one mundane message inside it that only a chosen creature or group can read.

#### Base Ability - Ink Lash
Action Type: Action
Factory Combat Bucket: action
Factory Routing: combat_action_row
Range: 60 feet.
Cost: None.
Target: One creature or object you can see.
Effect: Make a ranged Cultivation Attack roll. On a hit, the target takes Slashing or Psychic damage. Choose the damage type when you attack.
Damage: At CL 1-4, the damage is 1d8 + your key ability modifier. At CL 5-10, the damage is 2d8 + your key ability modifier. At CL 11-16, the damage is 3d8 + your key ability modifier. At CL 17-20, the damage is 4d8 + your key ability modifier.
Brush Shape: Ink Lash may appear as a cutting stroke, a hooked character, a whip of black ink, a vermilion slash, a painted fang, or a line of scripture.
Objects: Against unattended objects, Ink Lash may cut, stain, write across, or weaken the target at the GM’s discretion. It is not automatically a lockpick or disintegration tool.

Action Type: Action
Factory Combat Bucket: action
Factory Routing: combat_action_row
Range: Touch.
Duration: 1 hour.
Cost: None.
Target: One object, surface, doorway, container, weapon, tool, corpse, willing creature, or 5-foot section of wall, floor, or ceiling.

Combat Marking: A simple Ink Mark placed by Press Mark on a hostile creature is visible unless you spend 1 CP to conceal it as part of the same action.

Factory Combat Bucket: action
Factory Routing: combat_action_row
Range: Touch.
Cost: None.
Target: One written text, magical mark, seal, rune, painting, inscription, talisman, Formation mark, or Ink Mark.
Effect: You study the target and learn one of the following.
Whether it is ordinary, magical, spiritual, forged, or sphere-created.
Whether it contains an active Ink Mark, seal, curse, ward, or hidden script.
Whether it was written recently or long ago.
Whether it was written by a living hand, spirit, construct, item, formation, or sphere effect.
Whether it has been altered, forged, erased, or overwritten.
Check: For a concealed, hostile, or high-Realm inscription, make an Intelligence (Arcana), Intelligence (Investigation), Wisdom (Insight), calligrapher’s supplies, painter’s supplies, or Cultivation Check against the creator’s Cultivation Save DC or a GM-set DC.
