spheres.full_exact_source_text: # Sphere of Poison Qi Expression: Primary — Poison Qi; Supporting — Wood-Toxin Qi, Disease Qi, Water-Diffusion Qi, Antidote Qi. “The sword asks whether it struck deeply enough. Poison asks whether the enemy intends to keep breathing tomorrow.” Common Name: Poison Sphere Sphere Type: Restricted Toxin / Venom / Attrition Sphere Primary Path: Qi Cultivation Secondary Path: Spirit Awakening Rare Variant: Body Refining through Venom Body, toxic marrow, poison-breath boxing, and internal antidote scriptures Resource: CP, or Stamina for approved Body Refining accessCore Chassis: Dose Marks, Toxin Effects, Toxin Burden, Antidote Profiles, and Ingrained ToxinsCore Abilities: Appraise the Venom, Deliver the Dose, Ingrain the Toxin Common Effects: poison damage, acid damage, Poisoned, debuffs, delayed harm, antidotes, weapon coating, toxic clouds, venom body, attrition, cultivation-threatening toxins, and long-term toxic injury ### Poison Dao Poison is the cultivation of hostile measure. A Poison cultivator studies thresholds. One drop numbs the tongue. Two slow the blood. Three close the throat. Ten may kill a mortal but temper a venom body. A true master does not merely make something toxic; they decide how long the victim has, which meridian suffers first, which antidote fails, and what price the body pays for surviving. Poison is not automatically demonic. A poisoner may be an assassin, a physician, a monster hunter, a sect interrogator, a survivalist, an antidote specialist, a body refiner tempering the marrow, or an alchemist who knows that every medicine has a cruel shadow. Poison asks: What dose has entered, what path will it take, and what must be paid to make the body reject it? ### What Poison Does Poison cultivators study dose, delivery, resistance, antidote, and accumulation. They use venom, toxic qi, corrosive fluids, spiritual toxins, poison breath, coated weapons, needles, powders, spores, and hidden traces to weaken enemies over time. Poison talents commonly do one or more of the following: identify poison, toxic residue, venom patterns, and antidote opportunities; prepare Antidote Profiles and countermeasures; deliver immediate Poison or Acid damage; place, hide, spend, or deepen Dose Marks; convert repeated exposure into Toxin Burden; create delayed doses, toxic clouds, venom bodies, and spiritual poisons; develop long-term Ingrained Toxins that threaten recovery, meridians, breakthroughs, or cultivation stability; create antidotes, inoculations, and counter-poison methods when the cultivator follows a physician or toxicologist path. Poison is powerful because it rewards preparation. A single dose may hinder an enemy for a round. A layered poison, delivered with patience and protected by the right antidote knowledge, can shape an entire duel, assassination, monster hunt, or sect feud. Long-term cultivation-threatening poison requires serious investment. It should involve higher-Realm talents, repeated setup, rare materials, detectable symptoms, saving throws, treatment windows, and story consequences. ### The Poison Loop The intended loop is: Read the Trace -> Prepare the Dose -> Deliver the Venom -> Stack the Burden -> Choose Immediate Harm or Lingering Ruin -> Answer with Antidote. A Poison user should decide whether a scene calls for fast combat pressure or long-term attrition. A duelist uses Deliver the Dose for Poisoned, slowed movement, corroded defenses, and reaction denial. An assassin stacks Dose Marks, hides a Delayed Dose, then spends the setup on a decisive toxin. A venom physician uses Appraise the Venom and antidote talents to identify, neutralize, or reverse poisons. A long-term cultivator invests heavily into Ingrained Toxins that attack CP recovery, meridians, Hit Point maximum, or cultivation stability. ### Realm Progression Mortal. Sense poison, deliver toxic darts, coat weapons, impose brief poison effects, create simple antidotes, resist ordinary toxins, and plant minor lingering toxins. Foundation. Create toxic clouds, paralytic and corrosive doses, delayed toxins, refined antidotes, venom-body methods, and the first true lingering meridian poisons. Core Formation. Layer multiple venom effects, establish poison domains, survive as a thousand-poison body, craft serious cultivation-severing toxins, and poison spiritual or meridian systems. Nascent Soul. Become a venom sovereign, unleash battlefield poison winds, create perfected antidotes, found toxic cultivation sites, and create Dao-level poisons that threaten CP recovery, cultivation stability, or life itself. ### Sphere Boundaries Poison overlaps with many spheres but does not replace them. Disease. Disease is an adaptive hostile pattern that persists and spreads. Poison is dose, venom, toxin, acid, contact, and accumulation. A poison can cause sickness, but it does not automatically become an outbreak. Life. Life heals, purifies, restores, regenerates, and returns living continuity. Poison harms, weakens, corrodes, delays, and burdens. Poison can create antidotes and resistance, but it does not broadly heal wounds. Alchemy. Alchemy refines durable pills, reagents, cauldrons, formulas, and material preparations. Poison can use toxic substances in combat and cultivation, but it does not automatically replace laboratory crafting, pill refinement, or rare-ingredient economics. Blood. Blood governs circulation, bleeding, lineage, sacrifice, and internal flow. Poison can travel through blood, but it does not command blood as an element or lineage force. Flowers / Verdant Growth. Flowers can deliver pollen, fragrance, nectar, or toxic blossoms. Poison defines the toxin and its effects. Flowers define the plant expression and floral delivery. Flesh. Flesh reshapes organs, grows grafts, and alters bodies. Poison can numb, corrode, weaken, or harden through tolerance, but it does not redesign anatomy as a general art. Death. Death governs corpses, endings, grave qi, undead, and funerary authority. Poison can kill, rot, or suppress healing, but killing a target does not give the poisoner command over the dead. Ash / Decay. Ash and Decay erode, ruin, smother, and leave residue. Poison may corrode or leave toxic residue, but its identity is hostile substance and dose, not universal decay. Demonic Cultivation. Poison is tempting for cruel methods, assassination, and slow suffering. The sphere itself is not automatically demonic. Poisoning civilians, cultivating through mass suffering, or creating irreversible toxins for convenience is usually demonic or forbidden. ### Rules Baseline Use the campaign’s normal 2024 Fifth-Edition baseline unless a talent says otherwise. Poison does not automatically: bypass immunity to Poisoned, Poison damage, Acid damage, or disease; affect constructs, undead, elementals, spirits, or creatures without meaningful biology; create real-world toxins, recipes, materials, or instructions; poison a city, army, sect, water supply, or ecosystem without a strategic project or GM scene; permanently reduce ability scores; permanently reduce maximum Hit Points; permanently reduce maximum CP; scatter a cultivation base; prevent all healing or CP recovery; create pills, elixirs, or alchemical stockpiles; replace Alchemy, Disease, Life, Blood, Flesh, Death, or Demonic Cultivation. A talent must state any exception directly. ### Key Ability, Save DC, and Damage Poison usually uses the Path’s key ability. Qi Cultivation: normal Qi key ability.Spirit Awakening: Wisdom when the poison is spiritual, psychic, dreamborne, soulborne, or memory-borne.Body Refining: Constitution when using approved Venom Body access. Cultivation Save DC: 8 + your Proficiency Bonus + your key ability modifier. Cultivation Attack Modifier: your Proficiency Bonus + your key ability modifier. Poison talents usually deal Poison or Acid damage. Some spiritual or forbidden techniques may deal Necrotic or Psychic damage when a talent says so. Poison damage represents venom, toxin, dust, spores, alchemical irritants, toxic qi, serpent breath, marrow-venom, or nerve poison. Acid damage represents corrosive venom, caustic fluids, dissolving alchemical reagents, mineral acids, or body-melting toxins. ### Martial, Power, and Body Access Poison is a restricted toxin and attrition sphere. Martial users may access Poison through coated blades, needles, darts, animal venoms, toxic powders, pressure-point poison strikes, survivalist toxin lore, monster-hunter methods, or assassin training. Qi Cultivators externalize refined toxic qi, venom threads, toxic clouds, poisonous breath, alchemical vapor, spiritual spores, or corrosive fluids. Spirit Awakeners cultivate soul venom, nightmare toxins, memory poisons, aura contamination, and poisons that attack the spirit’s command over the body. Body Refiners do not usually project poison qi outside the body. A Body Refiner who learns Poison usually does so through Venom Body methods: resisting toxins, cultivating poison in the marrow, exhaling toxic breath at close range, sweating venom, poisoning through blood contact, toxic grappling, pressure-point venom, or storing poison harmlessly inside the body. ### Core Poison Rules #### Poisoned The Poisoned condition uses the normal Fifth-Edition rules. A Poisoned creature has Disadvantage on attack rolls and ability checks. Poison talents may also create Toxin Effects. A creature can be Poisoned and also suffer Toxin Effects. #### Toxin Effects A Toxin Effect is an additional penalty, condition, damage rider, or ongoing harm created by a Poison talent. Unless a talent says otherwise: the same Toxin Effect from the same source does not stack; different Toxin Effects may coexist; a creature repeats its saving throw at the end of each of its turns if the effect lasts longer than 1 round; a creature that ends a Toxin Effect cannot be affected by that same talent again until the start of the creator’s next turn; a Toxin Effect ends early if the target receives a successful antidote, Life purification, Alchemy treatment, or other appropriate countermeasure approved by the GM. #### Dose Marks Some Poison talents place Dose Marks. A Dose Mark represents toxic residue, venom lodged in a wound, a contaminated meridian point, a swallowed trace, or spiritual toxin clinging to the target’s aura. Unless a talent says otherwise: a creature can hold a number of Dose Marks from you equal to your Proficiency Bonus; a creature can gain at most one Dose Mark from you each turn; Dose Marks last for 1 minute; Dose Marks do nothing by themselves; Poison talents can spend Dose Marks to intensify effects; a successful antidote or purification may remove Dose Marks; Dose Marks are not contagious and do not spread outside the scene by default. #### Toxin Burden Toxin Burden represents poison that has begun settling deeper than a surface wound. Some talents convert Dose Marks into Toxin Burden. Unless a talent says otherwise: a creature can hold a number of Toxin Burden from you equal to your Proficiency Bonus; Toxin Burden lasts until the creature finishes a long rest or receives successful treatment; Toxin Burden does not stack with itself from the same creator beyond the limit; Toxin Burden is required for serious long-term Poison talents; Toxin Burden is detectable by Appraise the Venom, Life diagnosis, Alchemy checks, appropriate Medicine checks, or other suitable cultivation senses. A creature with any Toxin Burden from you has Disadvantage on the first Constitution check it makes before its next long rest. This is intentionally minor by itself; talents make it dangerous. #### Antidote Profiles An Antidote Profile is your understanding of a specific poison, target, sample, or toxin pattern. You can create an Antidote Profile with Appraise the Venom. Unless a talent says otherwise: you can maintain a number of Antidote Profiles equal to your Proficiency Bonus; an Antidote Profile lasts until you finish a long rest; you can dismiss a profile at any time; an Antidote Profile is not a physical antidote by itself; talents may use a profile to grant Advantage, neutralize poison, prepare medicine, or resist a known toxin. #### Ingrained Toxins An Ingrained Toxin is a lingering poison pattern set inside a creature’s body, meridians, spirit, or cultivation breath. A creature can suffer only one Ingrained Toxin from you at a time. If you create a new Ingrained Toxin on that creature, choose whether the old one ends or the new attempt fails. Ingrained Toxins are fantasy cultivation poisons. They are not real-world instructions for creating toxins, poisons, or biological harm. ### Poison Initiation When you first learn the Poison sphere, you gain the following three core abilities. #### Appraise the Venom Action Type: Action Factory Combat Bucket: action Factory Routing: combat_action_row Range: Touch, or 30 feet if you can clearly perceive the target Target: One creature, corpse, object, wound, food, drink, weapon, sample, patch of terrain, or visible contamination source Duration: Instantaneous Cost: None You read toxic traces, venom patterns, corrosion, and poisonous residue. You learn whether poison is present and one of the following facts: whether the poison is ordinary, alchemical, spiritual, demonic, plant-based, beast-based, mineral, corrosive, or unknown; whether the target is Poisoned; whether the target carries any of your Dose Marks; whether the target has Toxin Burden; whether the target suffers an Ingrained Toxin; whether the poison appears immediately dangerous, delayed, or long-term; whether an ordinary antidote might help; whether the poison can be safely handled in the current scene; whether the poison appears connected to Alchemy, Disease, Blood, Flowers, Death, or another sphere. When you use Appraise the Venom on a poison, a poisoned target, or a sample, you may create an Antidote Profile for it. If you spend 1 CP when using Appraise the Venom, learn three facts instead of one. Appraise the Venom does not automatically reveal exact formulas, hidden creators, secret techniques, rare antidote recipes, or the full history of a toxin. #### Deliver the Dose Action Type: Action Factory Combat Bucket: action Factory Routing: combat_action_row Range: 60 feet, or weapon range if delivered through a weapon Target: One creature or object Duration: Instantaneous Cost: None You deliver venom, toxic qi, corrosive fluid, a poisoned needle, mineral dust, spirit spores, toxic breath, or a coated strike. Make a ranged Cultivation Attack. If you deliver the dose through a weapon attack, make the weapon attack normally instead. On a hit, the target takes Poison or Acid damage, chosen when you attack. Mortal: 1d8Foundation: 2d8Core Formation: 3d8Nascent Soul: 4d8 Once per turn when you hit a creature with Deliver the Dose, the target makes a Constitution saving throw. Failed Save: The target gains 1 Dose Mark and has Disadvantage on its next ability check before the start of your next turn. Successful Save: The target does not gain a Dose Mark. Deliver the Dose cannot place Dose Marks on creatures immune to the delivery method, damage type, or Poison sphere effect used. #### Ingrain the Toxin Action Type: Action Factory Combat Bucket: action Factory Routing: combat_action_row Range: 60 feet, or touch for Body Refining use Target: One creature with at least 2 Dose Marks from you Duration: Until the target finishes a long rest or receives treatment Cost: 2 CP You spend 2 Dose Marks on the target and attempt to lodge a minor lingering toxin into the body, meridian flow, breath, or spirit. The target makes a Constitution saving throw. Failed Save: Choose one Minor Ingrained Toxin effect: Bitter Breath. The target has Disadvantage on its next Constitution saving throw before its next long rest. Numb Channels. The target’s Speed is reduced by 5 feet until its next long rest. Sour Blood. The next healing the target receives before its next long rest is reduced by your Proficiency Bonus. Clouded Senses. The target has Disadvantage on its next Wisdom (Perception) check before its next long rest. Heavy Pulse. The target cannot benefit from the Dash action on its next turn, and has Disadvantage on its next Dexterity saving throw before its next long rest. Successful Save: The Dose Marks are spent, but no Ingrained Toxin takes hold. A Minor Ingrained Toxin is intentionally limited. Serious long-term poison requires Foundation, Core Formation, or Nascent Soul talents. A creature can identify or treat a Minor Ingrained Toxin with appropriate Medicine, Alchemy, Life, Poison, or purification methods. The treatment DC equals your Cultivation Save DC. ## Mortal Talents Mortal Poison talents improve immediate delivery, simple antidotes, basic venom senses, and minor lingering poison. #### Antidote Art You can use Appraise the Venom as practical treatment. When you use Appraise the Venom on a creature, poison, food, drink, wound, or object, you may spend 1 CP and choose one: end the Poisoned condition caused by an ordinary poison; grant the target an immediate repeat saving throw against one Toxin Effect; remove one Dose Mark from the target; neutralize one ordinary poison dose on an object, weapon, food, or drink; grant Advantage on the target’s next saving throw against poison before its next short rest. If you have an Antidote Profile for the poison, the target also gains Temporary HP equal to your Proficiency Bonus. #### Coated Weapon Action Type: Bonus Action Factory Combat Bucket: bonus_action Factory Routing: combat_action_row Range: Touch Target: One weapon, natural weapon, unarmed strike, or set of up to 10 pieces of ammunition Duration: 1 minute Cost: 1 CP You coat the target with venom, toxic qi, corrosive fluid, or powdered toxin. Once per turn when the coated attack hits, it deals additional Poison or Acid damage equal to your Proficiency Bonus. The target then makes a Constitution saving throw. Failed Save: The target gains 1 Dose Mark. Successful Save: No Dose Mark. The coating ends after 1 minute or after it has applied a Dose Mark a number of times equal to your Proficiency Bonus. #### Numbing Dose When a creature fails its saving throw against Deliver the Dose, you may spend 1 CP to numb its nerves. Until the start of your next turn, the target suffers both effects: its Speed is reduced by 10 feet; it cannot take Reactions. If the target succeeds on the saving throw, you may still spend 1 CP to reduce its Speed by 5 feet until the start of your next turn. #### Venomous Strike Trigger: You hit with Deliver the Dose, a coated weapon, a natural weapon, or an unarmed strike carrying your Poison cultivation Cost: 1 CP Use Limit: Once per turn The attack deals additional Poison or Acid damage. Mortal: +1d6Core Formation: +2d6Nascent Soul: +3d6 The target makes a Constitution saving throw. Failed Save: The target becomes Poisoned until the start of its next turn. Successful Save: The target has Disadvantage on its next ability check before the start of its next turn. #### Poison Sense Your Appraise the Venom becomes a passive sense. You sense obvious poison and toxic contamination within 30 feet. You know whether: food or drink is poisoned; a visible creature is Poisoned; a visible wound carries venom; nearby air contains hazardous spores, gas, or toxic vapor; an object has been coated with poison; a corpse shows signs of toxic death. Poison Sense does not reveal exact formulas, secret toxins, hidden creatures, invisible poison, or alchemical recipes. At Core Formation Realm, the range increases to 60 feet. #### Bitter Trace When you hit a creature with Deliver the Dose, you may choose to deal no additional saving throw effect. If you do, the target gains 1 Dose Mark automatically on a hit, provided it is not immune to the effect. The Dose Mark created by Bitter Trace is subtle. A creature does not automatically realize it has been marked unless it uses Appraise the Venom, Life diagnosis, Alchemy, Medicine, or a similar method. Bitter Trace cannot be used with Coated Weapon unless you spend 1 CP. #### Mild Inoculation You can turn small doses into resistance. When you finish a short or long rest, choose yourself or one willing creature you treated during the rest. The chosen creature gains Advantage on the next saving throw it makes against poison before its next long rest. If you have an Antidote Profile for the poison, the chosen creature also gains Resistance to Poison damage from that poison until the start of its next long rest. #### Irritating Dust Action Type: Action Factory Combat Bucket: action Factory Routing: combat_action_row Range: 30 feet Area: 10-foot-radius sphere Duration: Until the start of your next turn Cost: 1 CP You release toxic powder, stinging vapor, irritant ash, mineral dust, or spirit spores. Creatures of your choice in the area make Constitution saving throws. Failed Save: The creature cannot take Reactions and has Disadvantage on Wisdom (Perception) checks until the start of your next turn. Successful Save: The creature cannot take Reactions until the start of your next turn. A creature that does not breathe may still be affected if the dust is corrosive, spiritual, or contact-based, at the GM’s discretion. ## Foundation Talents Foundation Poison talents add area delivery, delayed toxins, serious paralysis, corrosion, and the first cultivation-threatening toxins. #### Toxic Cloud Action Type: Action Factory Combat Bucket: action Factory Routing: combat_action_row Range: 60 feet Area: 15-foot-radius sphere Duration: Concentration, up to 1 minute Cost: 3 CP You create poisonous mist, spores, fumes, corrosive vapor, or toxic incense. When a creature enters the area for the first time on a turn or starts its turn there, it makes a Constitution saving throw. Failed Save: The creature takes Poison or Acid damage and becomes Poisoned until the start of its next turn. Successful Save: The creature takes half damage and is not Poisoned. Foundation: 3d6Core Formation: 5d6Nascent Soul: 7d6 A creature takes this damage only once per turn. Toxic Cloud is an alternate delivery method for Deliver the Dose. Talents that modify Deliver the Dose may modify Toxic Cloud if they make sense for an area effect and the GM approves. #### Paralytic Dose When a creature fails its saving throw against Deliver the Dose, you may spend 2 CP to paralyze movement without fully imposing the Paralyzed condition. Until the start of your next turn, the target suffers all effects: its Speed becomes 0; it cannot take Reactions; it has Disadvantage on Dexterity saving throws. If the Deliver the Dose effect already cost CP, reduce the cost of Paralytic Dose by 1, minimum 1 CP. At the end of each of its turns, if the effect lasts longer than 1 round due to another talent, the target repeats the saving throw and ends the effect on a success. #### Corrosive Dose When you deal Poison or Acid damage with Deliver the Dose or a Poison talent, you may spend 2 CP to make the venom corrosive. Add Acid damage to the damage roll. Foundation: +2d6Core Formation: +3d6Nascent Soul: +4d6 The target makes a Constitution saving throw. Failed Save: Until the start of your next turn, the target’s AC is reduced by 1, and one ordinary Resistance to Poison or Acid damage is suppressed. Successful Save: The target’s AC is reduced by 1 against the next attack targeting it before the start of your next turn. Corrosive Dose cannot suppress Immunity, Legendary defenses, Secret defenses, or an entire defensive Path. #### Delayed Dose You can hide poison until the right moment. When a creature gains a Dose Mark from you, you may spend 2 CP to make that Dose Mark dormant. A dormant Dose Mark lasts for 1 hour instead of 1 minute. While the mark remains, you may trigger it as a Bonus Action if the target is within 1 mile and you know the target’s direction. When triggered, the target makes a Constitution saving throw. Failed Save: The target takes 4d6 Poison or Acid damage and becomes Poisoned until the start of your next turn. Successful Save: The target takes half damage and is not Poisoned. A dormant Dose Mark can be detected through Appraise the Venom, Life diagnosis, Alchemy, Medicine, divination, or an appropriate Cultivation Check. #### Deepen the Burden When a creature has at least 2 Dose Marks from you, you may spend 1 CP and convert 2 Dose Marks into 1 Toxin Burden. The target makes a Constitution saving throw. Failed Save: The Toxin Burden remains until the target finishes a long rest or receives successful treatment. Successful Save: The Dose Marks are spent, but the Toxin Burden fades at the end of the current scene. Deepen the Burden is the bridge between combat poison and long-term poison. It does not create severe harm by itself. #### Lingering Meridian Venom Prerequisite: Deepen the Burden You can create a true lingering poison that threatens a cultivator’s daily recovery. Action Type: Multi-Mode Canonical Action Type: Multi-Mode Factory Combat Bucket: action Timing Detail: 1 minute, or Action against an incapacitated target Factory Routing: combat_action_plus_conditioned_procedure_variant Split Review Decision: single_combat_action_plus_procedure_variant Recommended Factory Realization: procedures=ONE_MINUTE_VENOM, ACTION_INCAPACITATED_TARGET Range: Touch, or 30 feet if the target has Toxin Burden from you Target: One creature with at least 1 Toxin Burden from you Duration: 7 days or until treated Cost: 4 CP The target makes a Constitution saving throw. Failed Save: Choose one Lingering Venom effect: Meridian Numbness. The target regains 1 fewer CP whenever it regains CP, minimum 0 from that recovery event. Bitter Foundation. The target has Disadvantage on the first Cultivation Check it makes each day. Closed Channels. The target cannot reduce CP costs below their printed values. Sour Recovery. Whenever the target regains Hit Points from a spending-limited feature, the healing is reduced by your Proficiency Bonus. Toxin Fatigue. The target gains 1 level of Exhaustion that cannot be removed until the Lingering Venom is treated. Successful Save: The Toxin Burden remains, but no Lingering Venom takes hold. A target suffering Lingering Meridian Venom repeats the saving throw at the end of each long rest. On a success, the venom ends. On a failure, it continues. Treatment can end the venom early. Appropriate treatment includes Antidote Art with an Antidote Profile, Life purification, Alchemy antidote, Poison counter-cultivation, Medicine supported by rare ingredients, or a suitable forged technique. The treatment DC equals your Cultivation Save DC. Lingering Meridian Venom is the first level of cultivation-threatening Poison. It is annoying and dangerous, but not usually campaign-ending by itself. #### Black Antidote Method When you successfully use Antidote Art to remove Poisoned, a Toxin Effect, a Dose Mark, Toxin Burden, or an Ingrained Toxin, you may store a trace of the neutralized poison until your next long rest. Once before your next long rest, when you use Deliver the Dose, you may release the stored trace to add Poison or Acid damage equal to your Proficiency Bonus + your key ability modifier. If the stored trace came from a poison for which you had an Antidote Profile, the target also gains 1 Dose Mark on a failed save. #### Venom Body Method You temper your body against poison. Gain Resistance to Poison damage and Advantage on saving throws against Poisoned and ordinary poison. Once per round, when you succeed on a saving throw against poison or a Toxin Effect, you gain Temporary HP equal to your Proficiency Bonus. Body Refiners may use this talent as their normal access point into Poison. If they do, they use Constitution and Stamina for Poison talents unless a feature says otherwise. #### Hidden Toxin Hand Your poison can be subtle. When you use Deliver the Dose through a weapon, touch, needle, powder, food, drink, or object, you may spend 1 CP to hide the signs of delivery. A creature that witnesses the act must succeed on a Wisdom (Perception) check or Wisdom (Insight) check against your Cultivation Save DC to notice that poison was involved. This does not make the poisoning legal, undetectable, or untraceable. Appraise the Venom, Life diagnosis, Alchemy, Medicine, or investigation can still reveal the toxin afterward. ## Core Formation Talents Core Formation Poison talents layer multiple toxins, turn poison into a domain, threaten cultivation more seriously, and allow spiritual toxins. #### Five-Venom Formula Action Type: Action Factory Combat Bucket: action Factory Routing: combat_action_row Range: 60 feet Target: One creature with at least 1 Dose Mark or Toxin Burden from you Duration: Concentration, up to 1 minute Cost: 5 CP The target makes a Constitution saving throw. Failed Save: Choose two Venom Effects. At the end of each of its turns, the target repeats the saving throw, ending all Venom Effects from this talent on a success. Successful Save: Choose one Venom Effect. It lasts until the start of your next turn. Serpent. The target takes 2d8 Poison damage at the start of each of its turns.Scorpion. The target cannot take Reactions.Spider. The target’s Speed is reduced by 20 feet.Toad. The target has Disadvantage on Constitution saving throws.Centipede. Healing the target receives is reduced by your Proficiency Bonus.Wasp. The target has Disadvantage on attack rolls.Moth. The target has Disadvantage on Wisdom saving throws.Corrosive Slime. The target’s AC is reduced by 1. Five-Venom Formula is a Toxin Effect. #### Poison Domain - Court of the Thousand Toxins Action Type: Action Factory Combat Bucket: action Factory Routing: combat_action_row Range: Self Area: 20-foot-radius aura Duration: Concentration, up to 1 minute Cost: 5 CP You establish a toxic court around yourself. Choose any number of creatures as protected creatures when you create the domain. Protected creatures gain Resistance to Poison damage and Advantage on saving throws against Poisoned and Toxin Effects while inside the domain. Enemies treat the area as lightly obscured by toxic vapor, incense, dust, or spiritual venom. The first time an enemy enters the area on a turn or starts its turn there, it makes a Constitution saving throw. Failed Save: The enemy takes 2d8 Poison or Acid damage and gains 1 Dose Mark. Successful Save: The enemy takes half damage and gains no Dose Mark. A creature is affected only once per turn. #### Thousand-Poison Immunity Your body and qi have adapted to countless toxins. Gain the following benefits: Immunity to ordinary poison. Resistance to Poison and Acid damage. Advantage on saving throws against Poisoned and Toxin Effects. You automatically recognize ordinary poisons by taste, smell, color, aura, or bodily reaction. You can store a number of ordinary poison doses equal to your Proficiency Bonus harmlessly inside your body or equipment. Once per short rest, when you succeed on a saving throw against a poison or Toxin Effect, you may gain Temporary HP equal to twice your Proficiency Bonus. #### Miasma Form Action Type: Bonus Action Factory Combat Bucket: bonus_action Factory Routing: combat_action_row Duration: Concentration, up to 1 minute Cost: 5 CP You become partly toxic vapor, poison mist, spirit spores, or corrosive breath. For the duration, gain: Fly Speed 30 feet and Hover; Resistance to nonmagical Bludgeoning, Piercing, and Slashing damage; Resistance to Poison and Acid damage; Advantage on checks made to escape Grappled or Restrained; ability to move through occupied spaces as difficult terrain; ability to pass through openings as narrow as 1 inch. You cannot pass through sealed barriers or solid objects. When you move through a hostile creature’s space for the first time on a turn, it makes a Constitution saving throw. Failed Save: The creature becomes Poisoned until the start of its next turn. Successful Save: No effect. #### Soul Venom Method Your poison can attack the spirit’s command over the body. When you use Deliver the Dose, Ingrain the Toxin, Lingering Meridian Venom, or Five-Venom Formula, you may choose to make the poison spiritual. A spiritual poison may affect spirits, ghosts, incorporeal creatures, possessing entities, and creatures without ordinary biology if they have a soul, animating spirit, or spiritual pattern. Against such targets, you may deal Psychic or Necrotic damage instead of Poison or Acid damage. Spirit Awakening cultivators may use Wisdom for this talent. Soul Venom Method does not automatically affect mindless constructs, soulless automata, or creatures protected by stronger spiritual authority. #### Cultivation-Severing Toxin Prerequisite: Lingering Meridian Venom You can create a serious cultivation poison. This is the core heavy-investment long-term poison engine. Action Type: Multi-Mode Canonical Action Type: Multi-Mode Factory Routing: procedure_ledger_not_combat_action Split Review Decision: procedure_only_not_combat_action Recommended Factory Realization: procedures=TEN_MINUTE_SEVERING_TOXIN, INGRAIN_CHAIN_COMPLETION Timing Detail: 10 minutes against a restrained, unconscious, willing, or incapacitated target; or 3 consecutive successful uses of Ingrain the Toxin against the same target within 24 hours Range: Touch Target: One creature with at least 2 Toxin Burden from you Duration: Until cured Cost: 8 CP and rare toxic materials worth at least 500 gp, consumed by the attempt The target makes a Constitution saving throw. Failed Save: The target suffers a Serious Ingrained Toxin at Stage 1. Successful Save: The target suffers Lingering Meridian Venom instead, and the rare materials are consumed. #### Serious Ingrained Toxin Stages A Serious Ingrained Toxin has stages. At the end of each long rest, the target makes a Constitution saving throw against your Cultivation Save DC. Success: The poison stage decreases by 1. If it would decrease below Stage 1, the poison ends. Failure: The poison stage increases by 1, to a maximum of Stage 4. A creature cannot suffer more than one Serious Ingrained Toxin at a time. Stage 1 - Bitter Channels. The target has Disadvantage on the first Cultivation Check it makes each day, and cannot reduce CP costs below their printed values. Stage 2 - Numb Meridian Flow. The target’s maximum CP is reduced by your Proficiency Bonus, and it has Disadvantage on concentration saving throws. This maximum CP reduction ends when the poison ends. Stage 3 - Foundation Corrosion. The target’s Hit Point maximum is reduced by your Cultivation Level, and the target regains only half as much CP from short-rest or scene-based recovery. This maximum Hit Point reduction ends when the poison ends. Stage 4 - Life-Gate Closing. The target cannot regain CP above half its maximum CP, cannot gain Temporary HP, and has Disadvantage on death saving throws. If the target fails three daily saves while at Stage 4, it dies unless the GM decides the poison instead triggers a major cultivation injury, coma, sealed meridians, or story crisis. #### Treating Serious Ingrained Toxin A Serious Ingrained Toxin is meant to be dangerous but answerable. Treatment may include: Core Formation or higher Life purification; a dedicated Alchemy antidote project; a Poison cultivator using Appraise the Venom and Antidote Art with an Antidote Profile; rare detoxifying materials worth at least 500 gp per treatment attempt; a sect infirmary project; a forged technique designed to purge cultivation poison; a successful adventure to retrieve the proper antidote. A treatment attempt normally requires 1 hour and a Cultivation Check, Medicine check, Alchemy check, or appropriate sphere check against your Cultivation Save DC. Success: Reduce the stage by 1. If this would reduce the poison below Stage 1, the poison ends. Failure: The poison remains. The GM may impose a complication if the treatment was reckless. Serious Ingrained Toxin should not permanently scatter a cultivation base unless the target fails repeatedly, the table wants that story, and the GM treats it as a major campaign event. #### Venom in the Wound When you damage a creature that is Bloodied, below half Hit Points, or suffering a wound-based condition, you may spend 2 CP to make the poison ride the injury. The target makes a Constitution saving throw. Failed Save: The target gains 1 Toxin Burden. Successful Save: The target gains 1 Dose Mark. If you have the Blood sphere or are using a forged Poison + Blood technique, the target has Disadvantage on the saving throw if it is currently bleeding. #### Perfected Counterdose When you create an Antidote Profile, you may spend 3 CP to create a counterdose. A counterdose lasts until you finish a long rest. You may maintain a number of counterdoses equal to your Proficiency Bonus. A creature can consume or receive a counterdose as an Action. Choose one benefit: end Poisoned; end one Toxin Effect; remove all Dose Marks from one creator; remove 1 Toxin Burden; grant Resistance to Poison and Acid damage for 1 hour; grant Advantage on saving throws against one known poison for 8 hours. A counterdose is tied to one Antidote Profile. It does not cure unrelated poisons. ## Nascent Soul Talents Nascent Soul Poison talents create sovereign venom bodies, battlefield-scale poison worlds, perfect antidotes, toxic cultivation sites, and Dao-level long-term poisons. #### Venom-Sovereign Incarnation Action Type: Bonus Action Factory Combat Bucket: bonus_action Factory Routing: combat_action_row Duration: 1 minuteConcentration: Not required Cost: 10 CP Use Limit: Once per long rest You transform into a perfected toxic incarnation. For the duration, gain: Fly Speed 40 feet and Hover; Immunity to Poison damage; Resistance to Acid and Necrotic damage; Immunity to Poisoned; Deliver the Dose deals 6d10 Poison or Acid damage instead of its normal damage; your Poison talents ignore ordinary Resistance to Poison and Acid damage. #### Virulent Presence While Venom-Sovereign Incarnation is active, when an enemy starts its turn within 20 feet of you, it makes a Constitution saving throw. Failed Save: Choose one: the enemy takes 4d8 Poison or Acid damage; the enemy becomes Poisoned until the start of its next turn; the enemy cannot take Reactions until the start of its next turn; healing the enemy receives is halved until the start of its next turn. Successful Save: The enemy takes half of 4d8 Poison or Acid damage, or suffers no effect if you chose a non-damaging option. A creature is affected only once per turn. #### Ten Thousand Poison Wind Action Type: Action Factory Combat Bucket: action Factory Routing: combat_action_row Range: 120 feet Area: 60-foot-radius sphere Duration: Concentration, up to 1 minute Cost: 8 CP Use Limit: Once per long rest You create a vast toxic storm of miasma, venom, poison rain, spirit spores, or caustic wind. When a creature enters the area for the first time on a turn or starts its turn there, it makes a Constitution saving throw. Failed Save: The creature takes 8d8 Poison, Acid, or Necrotic damage and becomes Poisoned until the start of its next turn. Successful Save: The creature takes half damage and is not Poisoned. A creature takes this damage only once per turn. Inside the storm: visibility beyond 30 feet is obscured; ordinary food and water become unsafe until purified; ordinary plants wither; ordinary flames become difficult to maintain; creatures have Disadvantage on checks made to track by scent; your Deliver the Dose range increases by 30 feet. Ten Thousand Poison Wind does not create permanent environmental contamination unless used as part of a strategic project or story event. #### Perfect Antidote Action Type: Ritual Procedure Canonical Action Type: Ritual Procedure Factory Routing: procedure_ledger_not_combat_action Timing Detail: 1 hour ritual Range: Touch Cost: 6 CP You create one dose of perfected antidote for a poison you have an Antidote Profile for. When consumed or administered, the antidote does all of the following: ends Poisoned; ends one Toxin Effect; removes all Dose Marks from one creator; removes all Toxin Burden from one creator; grants Resistance to Poison and Acid damage for 8 hours; grants Advantage on saving throws against poison for 8 hours; suppresses one Legendary poison for 1 hour; grants one treatment attempt against a Serious Ingrained Toxin with Advantage. A dose remains potent for 30 days. You may maintain a number of perfected antidote doses equal to your Proficiency Bonus. Perfect Antidote does not automatically cure a Secret poison, but it allows a Cultivation Check against that poison if treatment would otherwise be impossible. #### Valley of Poisonous Immortals Action Type: Strategic Project Canonical Action Type: Strategic Project Factory Routing: procedure_ledger_not_combat_action Timing Detail: 30-day strategic project Cost: 10 CP committed at the beginning of the project, plus 25,000 gp in rare toxins, plants, beast materials, mineral reagents, and alchemical equipment You create a permanent toxic cultivation site. Choose three benefits: produce rare poison ingredients worth 500 gp each month; support Poison and Alchemy projects; protect an area against ordinary vermin and hostile beasts; create concealed toxic defenses; grant +2 to checks made to identify, refine, resist, or treat poison in the site; provide a safe training environment for poison cultivators; allow antidote preparation in half the ordinary time; improve Flower, Blood, Disease, or Alchemy poison-related techniques; create a secure toxin archive; cultivate medicinal organisms useful for antidotes. You may maintain a number of Valleys equal to your Proficiency Bonus. A Valley of Poisonous Immortals is socially dangerous. Orthodox sects may require licenses, inspections, quarantine formations, and antidote reserves. #### Thousand-Day Dao Venom Prerequisite: Cultivation-Severing Toxin, Perfect Antidote or Venom-Sovereign Incarnation You can refine a long-term poison that threatens cultivation stability over months. Action Type: Strategic Project Canonical Action Type: Strategic Project Factory Routing: procedure_ledger_not_combat_action Timing Detail: Strategic project, 30 days Target: One creature already suffering a Serious Ingrained Toxin from you, or one prepared poison vessel intended for a named target Cost: 12 CP committed throughout the project, 50,000 gp in rare toxins and reagents, and a unique personal link to the target or lineage The target or final recipient makes a Constitution saving throw when the Thousand-Day Dao Venom takes hold. Failed Save: The target suffers a Dao Venom. Choose one effect: Closed Breath Venom. The target cannot regain CP above three-quarters of maximum CP. Bitter Breakthrough Venom. The target has Disadvantage on breakthrough-related Cultivation Checks. Meridian Rot Venom. The target’s maximum CP is reduced by twice your Proficiency Bonus. Medicine-Rejecting Venom. Healing and antidote treatment against the target require a successful Cultivation Check against your Save DC before they function. Life-Gate Venom. If the target drops to 0 Hit Points, it automatically fails its first death saving throw. Successful Save: The target suffers Lingering Meridian Venom for 7 days instead. At the end of every 10 days, the target repeats the saving throw. On a success, the Dao Venom becomes dormant for 10 days. On a second consecutive success, the Dao Venom ends. On a failure, it remains active. Thousand-Day Dao Venom is not a casual combat technique. It should require story, materials, access, investigation, social risk, antidote counterplay, and GM oversight. It should not permanently destroy a player character’s cultivation unless the table explicitly wants that story. ## Secret Inheritance ### Secret Inheritance: Poison That Kills the Dao “The body survived. The meridians survived. The technique failed because the poison had learned where cultivation lives.” Classification: Secret Poison Talent Prerequisite: Nascent Soul, Thousand-Day Dao Venom, Venom-Sovereign Incarnation, hidden primordial-venom inheritance Action Type: Action Factory Combat Bucket: action Factory Routing: combat_action_row Range: 90 feet Target: One creature with Dose Marks, Toxin Burden, a Serious Ingrained Toxin, or a Dao Venom from you Duration: Concentration, up to 1 minute Cost: 15 CP Use Limit: Once per week The target makes a Constitution saving throw. Failed Save: The target suffers Dao-corroding venom. At the start of each of its turns, it takes 4d10 Poison damage and 4d10 Necrotic damage. While the venom persists, the target suffers all effects: cannot regain Hit Points; cannot gain Temporary HP; cannot reduce CP costs below their printed values; cannot regain CP; has Disadvantage on concentration saving throws; has Disadvantage on breakthrough-related Cultivation Checks; cannot benefit from ordinary antidotes. At the end of each of its turns, the target repeats the saving throw, ending the effect on itself on a success. Successful Initial Save: The target takes 4d10 Poison damage and 4d10 Necrotic damage and cannot regain CP until the start of its next turn. #### Removing Poison That Kills the Dao This venom may be removed or suppressed by: Legendary Life purification; Legendary Alchemy antidote; Nascent Soul Poison counter-cultivation; a Secret purification technique; successful Cultivation Check against your Cultivation Save DC made as an Action by an appropriate healer; divine, immortal, or campaign-level intervention. Poison That Kills the Dao is a Secret inheritance and requires explicit GM approval. ## Poison Drawbacks and Variant Scriptures A Poison drawback is an optional sphere-specific limitation that grants a bonus Poison talent or benefit while changing how your Poison cultivation functions. Unless the GM says otherwise: choose at most one Poison drawback when first learning Poison or undergoing a major Poison initiation; Poison drawbacks are mutually exclusive; the drawback applies to all Poison talents you use; if a drawback grants a talent whose prerequisites you do not yet meet, you gain that talent when you meet the prerequisites; if the drawback is retrained or removed, the bonus talent or benefit is lost. These are Tianxia-specific cultivation limits, not imported casting traditions. #### Venom Body Scripture Your Poison cultivation lives in your own flesh. You cannot use Deliver the Dose at a range greater than touch, reach, breath range, weapon range, or a target in physical contact with your blood, sweat, saliva, breath, weapon, pressure point, or body. You gain Venom Body Method as a bonus talent. This scripture is common among Body Refiners. #### Bound Antidote Scripture Your poison and antidote are paired. Whenever you finish a long rest, choose one Antidote Profile or poison family you have studied. Your Poison talents function normally against that profile or family. Against all other poison families, whenever you spend CP on a Poison talent, make a Cultivation Check against DC 10 + twice the CP spent. Success: The talent functions normally. Failure: The Action and CP are spent, but the talent has no effect. You gain Antidote Art or Perfected Counterdose as a bonus talent. If you do not meet the prerequisite for Perfected Counterdose, you gain it when you qualify. #### One-Venom Scripture Your cultivation perfects one toxin instead of many. Choose one venom identity, such as serpent venom, mineral acid, ghost poison, orchid toxin, marrow venom, dream poison, or scorpion sting. Your Poison talents must express through that venom identity. You cannot freely change damage type, delivery flavor, or symptom style unless the GM agrees it still fits. You gain Venomous Strike or Deepen the Burden as a bonus talent. If you do not meet the prerequisite for Deepen the Burden, you gain it when you qualify. #### Merciful Toxicologist Scripture You cultivate poison to treat poison, hunt monsters, and restrain rather than kill. You cannot learn Cultivation-Severing Toxin, Thousand-Day Dao Venom, Poison That Kills the Dao, or any talent whose main purpose is long-term cultivation ruin or unavoidable death. You gain Antidote Art and Mild Inoculation as bonus talents. #### Delayed Hand Scripture Your poison is slow and subtle, but poor in open battle. Whenever you use Deliver the Dose without Delayed Dose, Bitter Trace, Ingrain the Toxin, or a prepared poison vessel, its damage dice are reduced by one step, minimum 1d6. You gain Delayed Dose as a bonus talent. At Core Formation, you gain Hidden Toxin Hand if you do not already know it. ## Path Synergies #### Qi Cultivation - Refined Venom Circulation Once per turn, when you spend CP on a Poison talent that modifies Deliver the Dose, reduce the CP cost by 1, minimum 1 CP. When a creature fails a saving throw against one of your Poison talents, add your key ability modifier to one Poison or Acid damage roll against that creature once per turn. Qi Cultivation Poison often appears as colored qi threads, venomous mist, alchemical breath, caustic droplets, spirit needles, or toxic seals. #### Spirit Awakening - Soul Venom You may use Wisdom as your Poison key ability when using spiritual poisons. Your Poison talents may affect spirits, ghosts, incorporeal creatures, possessing entities, and soul-bound targets through spiritual toxins if the talent can plausibly reach them. Against those creatures, you may deal Psychic, Necrotic, or Radiant damage instead of Poison or Acid when appropriate. Spirit Awakening Poison often appears as nightmare venom, memory bitterness, ghost stings, aura corrosion, or a toxin that makes the soul forget how to command the body. #### Body Refining - Venom Body Requires Venom Body Method or Venom Body Scripture. Use Constitution as your Poison key ability and Stamina for Poison talents. You gain Resistance to Poison damage. When you succeed on a saving throw against a poison or Toxin Effect, you may gain Temporary HP equal to your Proficiency Bonus once per round. Before the end of your next turn after succeeding on such a save, add your Constitution modifier to one Poison or Acid damage roll. Body Refining Poison is usually touch-based, breath-based, weapon-body based, or transmitted through blood, sweat, pressure points, grappling, and hardened toxic marrow. ## Cultivation Insights #### Venom Body Prerequisite: Body Refining, CL 4+ You may learn the Poison sphere through Body Refining access. You use Stamina and Constitution for Poison talents, and you gain the Body Refining - Venom Body path synergy. #### Venom Physician Prerequisite: Poison sphere, CL 5+ Antidote Art may be used as a Bonus Action. When you use Antidote Art, you may target a creature within 30 feet if you can clearly perceive it and have an Antidote Profile for the poison. Antidote Art grants Advantage on the immediate repeat saving throw it provides. You automatically identify ordinary poisons. #### Assassin’s Venom Prerequisite: Poison sphere, CL 5+ When you damage a creature that has not acted yet during the encounter, add your Proficiency Bonus to one Poison or Acid damage roll. Once per short rest, when you use Deliver the Dose against a creature that is Surprised, hidden from you, unaware of you, or socially unguarded, increase the Cultivation Save DC of that one Poison effect by 1. #### Corrosive Master Prerequisite: Poison sphere, CL 8+ Once per turn when you deal Acid damage with a Poison talent, add your Proficiency Bonus to one damage roll. Your Poison sphere Acid damage deals double damage to one unattended object or ordinary barrier. You ignore ordinary Resistance to Acid damage, but not Immunity, Legendary resistance, Secret defenses, or protected sect formations. #### Hidden Toxin Prerequisite: Poison sphere, Delayed Dose, CL 8+ Your Delayed Dose lasts 24 hours. A creature must make a Cultivation Check against your Cultivation Save DC to identify it. You may trigger Delayed Dose from anywhere on the same plane if you know the target’s direction and the target still carries the dormant mark. #### Sect Toxicologist Prerequisite: Poison sphere During a short rest, you may examine poison samples, wounds, monsters, poisoned weapons, food, drink, or contaminated objects. Choose one poison you examined. Until your next long rest, you and a number of allies equal to your Proficiency Bonus gain Advantage on the first saving throw each of you makes against that poison. If you also know Antidote Art, those allies may add your key ability modifier to that saving throw. ## Forged Technique Examples #### Blood-Venom Curse Spheres: Poison + Blood Suggested Realm: Foundation or Core Formation Your toxin rides an open wound or blood channel. When you deal Piercing, Slashing, or Blood sphere damage to a creature, you may use Deliver the Dose as part of the same Action by spending 1 additional CP. If the target is bleeding, Bloodied, or below half Hit Points, it has Disadvantage on the saving throw against the Dose Mark. #### Orchid Miasma Spheres: Poison + Flowers Suggested Realm: Foundation You cultivate poisonous fragrance and petal-borne toxins. Your Toxic Cloud may appear as flower pollen, incense, orchid scent, or drifting petals. Creatures that fail the saving throw against Toxic Cloud also have Disadvantage on Wisdom (Perception) checks relying on smell or sight until the start of your next turn. #### Corpse-Rot Poison Spheres: Poison + Death Suggested Realm: Core Formation You refine venom through corpse qi without commanding the dead. When a creature fails a saving throw against Deliver the Dose, you may spend 2 CP to deal Necrotic damage instead of Poison or Acid damage. Until the start of your next turn, healing the target receives is reduced by your Proficiency Bonus. #### Five-Venom Puppet Core Spheres: Poison + Puppetry Suggested Realm: Core Formation You install a stored toxin payload into a puppet vessel. When your puppet hits a creature or is destroyed within 5 feet of a creature, you may release Deliver the Dose from the puppet’s space. Use your Poison Save DC and Poison Attack Modifier. #### Thundercloud Venom Spheres: Poison + Weather Suggested Realm: Core Formation You suspend venom in storm vapor. Your Toxic Cloud may move 10 feet at the start of each of your turns. If the area is also affected by rain, storm, fog, or heavy wind from your own technique, increase its radius by 5 feet. #### Soul-Eroding Toxin Spheres: Poison + Spirit Awakening Suggested Realm: Core Formation or Nascent Soul Your venom attacks spiritual control. When a creature fails a saving throw against Soul Venom Method, it has Disadvantage on the next saving throw it makes against possession, fear, dream invasion, or forced soul movement before the start of your next turn. ## Strategic Project Seeds #### Antidote Archive Build a sect archive of known toxins, counterdoses, beast venoms, mineral poisons, alchemical notes, and treatment protocols. Possible benefits: reduce antidote preparation time; grant bonuses to identify poison; support Life and Alchemy treatment; provide story hooks when a rare poison appears; allow disciples to train safely against ordinary toxins. #### Venom Body Crucible Create a training chamber where Body Refiners temper flesh, breath, blood, and marrow against controlled toxins. Possible benefits: unlock Venom Body access; grant resistance training scenes; generate rival body-refiner challenges; create risk of cultivation deviation if misused. #### Poison Garden Cultivate a garden of toxic flowers, venomous beasts, mineral pools, antidote herbs, and spirit insects. Possible benefits: support Poison + Flowers techniques; produce rare materials; create a dangerous but profitable sect resource; attract thieves, alchemists, assassins, and monster hunters. #### Hidden Venom Investigation Trace a long-term poison through a court, clan, sect, or caravan. Possible scenes: diagnose subtle Dose Marks; protect a victim through antidote treatment; find the poisoner; distinguish Poison from Disease or curse work; decide whether to expose the scandal publicly.

The target makes a Constitution saving throw.

Bitter Breath. The target has Disadvantage on its next Constitution saving throw before its next long rest.
Numb Channels. The target’s Speed is reduced by 5 feet until its next long rest.
Sour Blood. The next healing the target receives before its next long rest is reduced by your Proficiency Bonus.
