spheres.full_exact_source_text: # Sphere of Pressure Points Qi Expression: Primary — Meridian Qi; Supporting — Needle Qi, Body-Gate Qi, Flow-Interruption Qi. “A fist may break the door. A finger finds the hinge.” Sphere Type: Martial Sphere Primary Paths: Body Refining and Spirit Awakening Secondary Path: Qi Cultivation Resource: Martial Focus; some Meridian and Path-synergy techniques may spend CP when explicitly stated Common Effects: precision contact, pressure-point taps, breath disruption, grip failure, stance breaks, short condition windows, concentration disruption, meridian locks, technical counters, nonlethal takedowns, emergency release touches ### Pressure Points Pressure Points is the cultivation of the small place that decides the whole body. Iron Fist teaches the body to become a complete weapon. Pressure Points teaches that a complete weapon is unnecessary when one finger, knuckle, needle, palm edge, elbow point, or heel tap lands at the exact gate where breath, nerve, tendon, blood, and spirit briefly agree to move. A novice learns where the body hurts. An adept learns where the body hesitates. A master learns that a technique also has pressure points: the moment before the word, the joint before the swing, the breath before the leap, the meridian before the spell completes. A sovereign learns that even Heaven has a pulse. The core loop is: Make Precision Contact. Strike, tap, needle, palm, or kick a readable point. Apply a Point. Place one short technical disruption on a hit. Close the Gate. If the target already bears one of your Points, consume it to apply a stronger Seal. Exploit the Window. The enemy loses a reaction, grip, stance, speech, breath, or technique timing long enough for the fight to turn. After fighting a Pressure Points cultivator for two rounds, an opponent should understand one truth: The body has switches it did not consent to having. ## RULES BASELINE This sphere uses the 2024 fifth-edition rules baseline together with Tianxia cultivation rules. ### Unarmed Strike Under the 2024 rules, an Unarmed Strike is a melee attack made with the body. When you use it, choose Damage, Grapple, or Shove. Pressure Points primarily requires the Damage option because the sphere needs a hit to place a Point. When a talent modifies Grapple or Shove, it says so explicitly. ### Grapple and Shove Under the 2024 rules, the Grapple and Shove options of Unarmed Strike normally use saving throws rather than contested Athletics checks. Pressure Points does not replace those default rules unless a talent says so. If a talent makes a target fall, drop, lock, or fail to move, that talent states its own saving throw and duration. ### Special Attack When a Pressure Points talent says Special Attack, replace one attack when you take the Attack action unless the talent explicitly uses a different Action Type. If you have Extra Attack, Multiattack, or another feature that gives more than one attack as part of the Attack action, replacing one attack does not consume the entire Attack action unless the feature says otherwise. ### Opportunity Attacks Opportunity Attacks use a Reaction. Many Pressure Points talents deny Opportunity Attacks because they disturb reflex, stance, or timing. A creature that cannot take Reactions cannot make Opportunity Attacks. ### Concentration Pressure Points can interfere with Concentration by imposing Disadvantage on Concentration saving throws, forcing a Concentration saving throw against your Pressure Points Save DC, or causing damage that triggers the ordinary Concentration rules. ### Conditions and Custom Restrictions When a talent uses a 2024 condition such as Grappled, Prone, Restrained, Stunned, Incapacitated, Poisoned, or Unconscious, use the ordinary rules for that condition. Some Pressure Points effects are not conditions. They are short technical restrictions such as “cannot take Opportunity Attacks,” “cannot speak clearly,” or “cannot use one held object.” These restrictions last only for the listed duration. Dazed is a Tianxia custom restriction when used here. A Dazed creature cannot take Reactions and may take either an Action or a Bonus Action on its turn, not both. ### Legal Contact and Total Cover A Precision Contact requires a legal route to the target. Pressure Points does not bypass Total Cover, a sealed Barrier, a Dimensional Lock, specialized concealment, or a superior anti-meridian defense unless a talent explicitly says so. ## CORE PRESSURE POINTS RULES ### Martial Focus Pressure Points uses Martial Focus. You may hold one Martial Focus at a time. Some talents expend Martial Focus. Expending Martial Focus is not an Action. You cannot expend Martial Focus if you do not currently hold it. If a talent says you regain Martial Focus, regain it only if it is currently absent. Martial Focus represents steady hands, calm breath, patient observation, and the instant when the correct point becomes obvious. ### Pressure Points Ability When you learn Pressure Points, choose Dexterity or Wisdom as your Pressure Points ability. Use your Pressure Points ability for: your Pressure Points Save DC; attack rolls made with pressure tools when this sphere allows you to use your Pressure Points ability; Wisdom (Medicine), Dexterity (Sleight of Hand), or Cultivation Checks made specifically to read or touch pressure points when a talent calls for such a check. Your Pressure Points Save DC equals: 8 + your Pressure Points ability modifier + your Proficiency Bonus A Path synergy may let you use another ability. ### Readable Body At Mortal Realm, a creature must have a readable body or readable equivalent: nerves, joints, muscles, breath, pulse, tendons, seams, hinges, structural channels, or visible animating force. Pressure Points normally cannot affect creatures with no stable body, no meaningful structure, or no readable channel. Foundation Realm talents begin reading meridians, spiritual seams, elemental flows, and animating patterns rather than ordinary anatomy alone. ### Precision Contact Action Type: Action Canonical Action Type: Action Factory Combat Bucket: action Timing Detail: Special Attack Factory Routing: combat_action_row; preserve attack-replacement detail Range: Your reach, unless a talent increases it Target: One creature with a readable body or readable equivalent Cost: None Replace one attack when you take the Attack action. Make one melee attack using one of the following methods: the Damage option of an Unarmed Strike; a light or finesse melee weapon used to touch a point rather than make a deep cut; an approved pressure tool, such as a healer’s needle, acupuncture pin, ring needle, pressure stylus, or sect needle. Use the normal attack roll and damage for the method used. If the method has no normal weapon profile, use your Pressure Points ability for the attack roll. On a hit, it deals 1 Piercing or Bludgeoning damage and qualifies for Touch the Point. It does not add your ability modifier to damage unless another feature says so. Hit: Deal the attack’s normal damage. You may then use Touch the Point. Miss: No effect. Precision Contact may be nonlethal when the triggering attack could be nonlethal. ### Touch the Point Trigger: Once per turn, when you hit a creature with Precision Contact Cost: None Choose one: Apply a Point. Apply one Point talent you know to the target. Close a Seal. If the target already bears one of your Pressure Points, remove one of your Pressure Points from it and apply one Seal talent you know. Read the Body. Use Reading Touch instead of applying a Point or Seal. Unless a talent says otherwise: choose the Point or Seal after the Precision Contact hits; apply only one Point or Seal to the triggering hit; a creature may bear only one of your Pressure Points at a time; a Pressure Point lasts until the end of your next turn; a creature cannot suffer more than one of your Seals during the same round; your Pressure Points end early if you become Incapacitated. A Pressure Point is not a condition, mark, or tracking effect. It does not reveal the target’s location, bypass concealment, or provide exact-square knowledge. ### Point Talents A Point talent is an immediate technical disruption applied through Touch the Point. Points are usually short, precise, and reliable. They create openings such as numbness, speech stutter, breath disruption, grip failure, impaired stance, or a weakened saving throw. ### Seal Talents A Seal talent is a stronger effect created by touching a target that already bears one of your Pressure Points. A Seal represents closing the same gate twice, striking a companion point, or locking the meridian line between two contacts. ### Counterpoint Talents A Counterpoint talent is usually a Reaction. Counterpoints exploit a creature that has already committed to an attack, movement, spell, technique, or recovery. ### Diagnostic Talents A Diagnostic talent reads anatomy, breath, pulse, meridians, injuries, poisons, or cultivated rhythm. Diagnostic talents are useful outside combat and can set up precise combat techniques. ### Meridian Talents A Meridian talent is supernatural. Meridian talents begin at Foundation Realm and affect Qi channels, spirit seams, breath shadows, magical speech, cultivation rhythm, body-enhancement effects, or active technique flow. Meridian talents do not automatically replace Blood, Spirit, Force, Qiweaving, or Restoration. ## BASE SPHERE ABILITIES ### Pressure Points Training When you learn Pressure Points: gain proficiency in Wisdom (Medicine) or Dexterity (Sleight of Hand); if already proficient in both, choose one Pressure Points talent for which you meet the prerequisites as a bonus talent; learn Precision Contact, Touch the Point, Numbing Point, and Reading Touch; choose one additional Mortal Realm Point talent for which you meet the prerequisites. ### Numbing Point - Point Trigger: You apply a Pressure Point through Touch the Point Save: None Duration: Until the start of your next turn You numb a shallow nerve, tendon, joint, seam, or meridian crossing. Choose one option: Numb Arm: The target has Disadvantage on the next weapon attack roll, Unarmed Strike attack roll, or attack made with a held object before the effect ends. Numb Leg: The target’s Speed is reduced by 10 feet, and it cannot take Opportunity Attacks. Numb Grip: The target has Disadvantage on the next Strength saving throw, Strength (Athletics) check, or D20 Test made to resist Disarm, maintain a Grapple, or keep hold of an object before the effect ends. Numb Reflex: The target has Disadvantage on the next Dexterity saving throw or Dexterity (Acrobatics) check it makes before the effect ends. ### Reading Touch - Diagnostic Trigger: You hit a creature with Precision Contact Cost: None Instead of applying a Point or Seal, read the body’s immediate response. Choose one fact to learn: whether the target is Bloodied; whether the target is Poisoned, Paralyzed, Stunned, Unconscious, or suffering Exhaustion; whether the target’s movement, speech, grip, sight, or breath is currently impaired; whether the target currently benefits from a visible, audible, or physically expressed body-enhancing cultivation effect; which of Strength, Dexterity, or Constitution appears most vulnerable to pressure-point disruption. Reading Touch does not reveal a complete stat block, hidden identity, class features, Path, Realm, secret technique, or invisible effect. ## MORTAL REALM TALENTS ### Point Talents #### Breath-Catching Point - Point Trigger: You apply a Pressure Point through Touch the Point Save: None Duration: Until the start of your next turn The target’s breath hitches. Until the effect ends, the target has Disadvantage on the next Constitution saving throw it makes to maintain Concentration, resist suffocation, resist inhaled poison, or activate a technique requiring steady breath. #### Grip-Severing Point - Point Trigger: You apply a Pressure Point through Touch the Point Save: Constitution Duration: Until the start of your next turn Choose one object the target is holding. Failed Save: The target drops the object. Successful Save: The target keeps hold of the object, but has Disadvantage on the next attack roll, ability check, or activation using that object before the effect ends. If the target holds the object with two or more hands, it has Advantage on this saving throw. #### Stance-Breaking Point - Point Trigger: You apply a Pressure Point through Touch the Point Save: Strength or Dexterity, target’s choice Duration: Until the start of your next turn You touch the ankle, knee, hip, root, seam, or balance gate. Failed Save: Choose one: the target falls Prone; the target is pushed 5 feet to a legal unoccupied space; the target cannot take Reactions; the target’s Speed becomes 0. Successful Save: The target’s Speed is reduced by 10 feet. This is a technical collapse, not a Brute collision. #### Speech-Knot Point - Point Trigger: You apply a Pressure Point through Touch the Point Save: Constitution Duration: Until the start of your next turn The target’s jaw, tongue, throat, breath, or vocal meridian stutters. The next time the target speaks clearly, issues a command, uses an ability requiring clear speech, or provides a Verbal component before the effect ends, it makes the saving throw. Failed Save: The speech falters. If the triggering ability requires clear speech or a Verbal component, the activation fails, but the action and resources are not spent unless the ability itself says otherwise. Successful Save: The target speaks normally, and this Point ends. #### Eye-Watering Point - Point Trigger: You apply a Pressure Point through Touch the Point Save: None Duration: Until the start of your next turn The target’s vision blurs. Until the effect ends, the target has Disadvantage on the next Wisdom (Perception) check, ranged attack roll, or attack roll made against a creature more than 10 feet away. A creature that does not rely on sight is unaffected unless the GM determines it has an analogous sensory point. #### Weak Pulse Point - Point Trigger: You apply a Pressure Point through Touch the Point Save: None Duration: Until the start of your next turn The target’s circulation, animating rhythm, or inner breath briefly weakens. The first time before the effect ends that the target regains HP or gains Temporary HP, reduce the amount gained by your Proficiency Bonus. This is not a Blood talent and does not create a Blood Thread. ### Seal Talents #### Joint Seal - Seal Trigger: You close a Seal through Touch the Point Save: Strength Duration: Until the end of the target’s next turn Choose one limb, wing, gripping appendage, leg, or analogous moving structure. Failed Save: That part cannot be used effectively. A disabled leg reduces Speed by half. A disabled arm or gripping limb cannot hold a weapon, Shield, focus, or tool effectively. A disabled wing may prevent flight if the creature needs that wing to fly. Successful Save: The target’s Speed is reduced by 10 feet until the start of your next turn. Creatures without meaningful body parts suffer the successful-save effect instead. #### Breath Seal - Seal Trigger: You close a Seal through Touch the Point Save: Constitution Duration: Until the end of the target’s next turn Failed Save: The target cannot speak clearly, cannot provide Verbal components, and has Disadvantage on Concentration saving throws. Successful Save: The target cannot take Opportunity Attacks until the start of your next turn. #### Falling Gate Seal - Seal Trigger: You close a Seal through Touch the Point Save: Dexterity Duration: Until the start of your next turn Failed Save: The target falls Prone and cannot stand until the effect ends. Successful Save: The target falls Prone. #### Grip Seal - Seal Trigger: You close a Seal through Touch the Point Save: Strength Duration: Until the end of the target’s next turn Choose one object the target is holding. Failed Save: The target drops the object. If the target has no held object, one hand, claw, tentacle, or similar appendage cannot be used to Grapple, hold, or manipulate objects until the effect ends. Successful Save: The target has Disadvantage on the next attack roll or ability check it makes with that object before the start of your next turn. ### Counterpoint Talents #### Intercepting Tap - Counterpoint Action Type: Reaction Factory Combat Bucket: reaction Factory Routing: combat_action_row Trigger: A creature within your reach hits you with a melee attack Cost: Expend Martial Focus Make one Precision Contact attack against the triggering creature. Hit: Reduce the triggering damage by your Proficiency Bonus and apply one Point talent you know. Miss: Reduce the triggering damage by 1. #### Retaliatory Nerve - Counterpoint Action Type: Reaction Factory Combat Bucket: reaction Factory Routing: combat_action_row Trigger: A creature within your reach misses you with a melee attack Cost: Expend Martial Focus Make one Precision Contact attack against the triggering creature. On a hit, deal the attack’s normal damage and apply one Point talent you know. #### Patient Hand - Focus When you take the Dodge, Search, or Study action and can perceive a hostile creature within 30 feet, regain Martial Focus. If you regain Martial Focus this way, choose one creature you can perceive within 30 feet. Before the end of your next turn, you have Advantage on the next Wisdom (Medicine), Dexterity (Sleight of Hand), or Cultivation Check you make to read or touch that creature’s pressure points. ### Diagnostic Talents #### Pulse Diagnosis - Diagnostic Action Type: Action Factory Combat Bucket: action Factory Routing: combat_action_row Range: Touch Target: One willing, Incapacitated, Restrained, Grappled by you, or unaware creatureCheck: Wisdom (Medicine) against a DC set by the GM Typical DCs: | Body Type | DC | | --- | --- | | Ordinary anatomy | 10 | | Unusual anatomy | 15 | | Alien, spiritual, heavily transformed, or concealed body | 20 | Success: Learn two of the following: whether the target is diseased or poisoned; whether the target is under an obvious mind-affecting condition; whether the target has a hidden injury affecting movement, speech, grip, sight, or breath; which saving throw among Strength, Dexterity, or Constitution appears weakest; whether the target’s breath, pulse, or meridian rhythm has been artificially altered; one safe pressure point that can numb pain or release breath. Failure: Learn one true but incomplete detail. #### Gentle Release - Diagnostic Action Type: Action Factory Combat Bucket: action Factory Routing: combat_action_row Range: Touch Target: One willing creature Cost: None Touch a safe point to release breath, ease cramps, or stabilize shallow circulation. Choose one: the target may immediately repeat one saving throw against being Poisoned; the target may immediately repeat one saving throw against being Frightened; the target ends one ordinary muscle cramp, numbness, or nonmagical paralysis-like effect at the GM’s discretion; the target gains Temporary HP equal to your Proficiency Bonus. A creature may benefit from your Gentle Release only once per short rest. ## FOUNDATION REALM TALENTS Foundation Realm begins the supernatural version of the art. The practitioner no longer needs ordinary anatomy alone. They can read Qi gates, spirit seams, breath shadows, and cultivation rhythm. ### Realm Evolutions #### Meridian-Sight Touch - Realm Evolution Prerequisite: CL 5+ Your Pressure Points may affect creatures with unusual bodies if they possess a readable spiritual, mechanical, elemental, necrotic, constructed, or animating structure. Examples include: joints in a Construct; spiritual seams in an Undead creature; circulating flame in a Fire spirit; growth nodes in plant creatures; pressure currents in Elementals; runic hinge-points in animated objects. A creature with no stable body, no readable animating structure, or a superior concealment technique may still be immune or require a successful Study, Search, Medicine, or Cultivation Check before you can apply Pressure Points. #### Meridian Flick - Realm Evolution Prerequisite: CL 5+ While holding Martial Focus, you may manifest a brief projected fingertip, needle glint, pulse thread, or pressure ripple whenever you use Precision Contact for this sphere. Your Precision Contact range for Pressure Points becomes 15 feet. This contact: must travel along a clear legal route; requires a target you can perceive; may apply Point and Seal talents normally; vanishes immediately after the contact resolves. Meridian Flick does not grant general telekinesis, ordinary object manipulation at range, or the ability to replace Force, Thread, Space, or Scoundrel. #### Twin Gate Method - Realm Evolution Prerequisite: CL 5+ A creature may bear up to two of your Pressure Points at a time. When you apply a Pressure Point to a creature that already bears one of your Pressure Points, choose either: leave both Points in place; or remove one Point and apply a Seal talent as normal. A creature still cannot suffer more than one of your Seals during the same round. ### Foundation Point and Seal Talents #### Qi-Needle Tap - Point, Meridian Prerequisite: CL 5+ Trigger: You apply a Pressure Point through Touch the Point Save: Constitution Duration: Until the start of your next turn Choose one ongoing body-enhancing, movement-enhancing, or breath-enhancing effect on the target that you can perceive. Failed Save: Suppress that effect until the effect ends. Successful Save: The effect remains, but the target cannot benefit from Advantage on the next Strength or Dexterity D20 Test it makes before the effect ends. This talent cannot suppress a Domain, Secret Inheritance, artifact, Path, Realm, or permanent transformation. #### Locked Breath Method - Seal, Meridian Prerequisite: Breath Seal, CL 5+ Trigger: You close a Seal through Touch the Point Save: Constitution Duration: Until the end of the target’s next turn Failed Save: The target cannot activate abilities that require clear speech, a Verbal component, a kiai, a chant, a roar, or steady breathing. If the target is concentrating, it immediately makes a Concentration saving throw against your Pressure Points Save DC. Successful Save: Until the start of your next turn, the target has Disadvantage on its next Concentration saving throw. #### Soft Paralysis Tap - Seal, Meridian Prerequisite: CL 5+ Trigger: You close a Seal through Touch the Point Save: Constitution Duration: Until the start of your next turn Failed Save: The target has the Restrained condition. Successful Save: The target’s Speed becomes 0. This is a meridian lock, not a Grapple. Forced movement can still move the target unless another effect prevents it. #### Empty-Hand Anesthetic - Point, Diagnostic Prerequisite: CL 5+ Trigger: You apply a Pressure Point to a willing creature through Touch the Point Save: None Duration: Until the start of your next turn You numb pain without dulling awareness. The creature gains Temporary HP equal to your Proficiency Bonus + your Pressure Points ability modifier. Until the effect ends, the creature also has Advantage on the next saving throw it makes against being Frightened or against a pain-based effect. A creature may benefit from your Empty-Hand Anesthetic only once per short rest. #### Stolen Pulse Step - Point Prerequisite: CL 5+ Trigger: You apply a Pressure Point through Touch the Point Save: None Move 10 feet without provoking Opportunity Attacks from the target. If the target already bore one of your Pressure Points before the hit, you may instead move up to half your Speed without provoking Opportunity Attacks from the target. This movement represents stepping through the target’s collapsed rhythm, not teleportation. #### Sealed Grip Scripture - Seal Prerequisite: Grip Seal, CL 5+ Trigger: You close a Seal through Touch the Point Save: Strength Duration: Until the end of the target’s next turn Choose one held object, weapon, tool, focus, or Shield. Failed Save: The target cannot use that object. If the object is not secured, the target also drops it. Successful Save: The target keeps hold of the object but has Disadvantage on attack rolls or ability checks made with it until the start of your next turn. ### Foundation Counterpoint Talents #### Interrupting Point - Counterpoint, Meridian Prerequisite: CL 5+ Action Type: Reaction Factory Combat Bucket: reaction Factory Routing: combat_action_row Trigger: A creature bearing one of your Pressure Points within 30 feet activates a spell, technique, talent, stance, guard, or other ability Cost: Expend Martial Focus The target makes a Constitution saving throw. Failed Save: The activation falters. The target’s action, Bonus Action, Reaction, and any CP or resource spent are not lost, but the ability does not resolve until immediately after the triggering creature’s current turn ends. Successful Save: The ability resolves normally, but the target cannot take Reactions until the start of its next turn. Interrupting Point delays timing; it does not counter the effect outright. #### Needle Meets Blade - Counterpoint Prerequisite: CL 5+ Action Type: Reaction Factory Combat Bucket: reaction Factory Routing: combat_action_row Trigger: A creature bearing one of your Pressure Points hits you with a melee attack Cost: Expend Martial Focus Reduce the damage by 1d8 + your Pressure Points ability modifier. If this reduces the damage to 0, apply one Point talent you know to the attacker. At CL 11, reduce the damage by 2d8 + your Pressure Points ability modifier. At CL 17, reduce the damage by 3d8 + your Pressure Points ability modifier. ## CORE FORMATION REALM TALENTS Core Formation turns Pressure Points from isolated taps into a technical map of the battlefield. The practitioner begins to see gates, pulses, and meridian answers before bodies move. ### Domain #### Chamber of Nine Gates - Domain, Realm Evolution Prerequisite: CL 10+ Action Type: Bonus Action Factory Combat Bucket: bonus_action Factory Routing: combat_action_row Area: 20-foot Emanation originating from you Duration: 1 minute Cost: Expend Martial Focus Use Limit: Once per short rest Create a technical pressure-point court around yourself. The air fills with faint diagrams, pulse echoes, flickering acupuncture stars, or invisible alignment lines. For the duration: your Meridian Flick range increases to 30 feet inside the Domain; you may maintain up to two Pressure Points on each hostile creature inside the Domain; once during each of your turns, when you hit with Precision Contact inside the Domain, you may apply one Point talent without counting against Touch the Point’s once-per-turn limit; once during each of your turns, when a creature bearing one of your Pressure Points inside the Domain misses an attack, fails a saving throw, or loses Concentration, you may apply Numbing Point to it without spending an Action; you may use a Seal talent against a creature bearing two of your Pressure Points inside the Domain without making a new attack, removing both Points as part of the Seal; when you use a Seal talent inside the Domain, regain Martial Focus if it is absent. The Domain does not reveal hidden creatures, bypass Total Cover, create permanent medical seals, or suppress all techniques automatically. ### Core Formation Talents #### Technique-Closing Point - Seal, Meridian Prerequisite: Interrupting Point, CL 10+ Trigger: You close a Seal through Touch the Point Save: Constitution or Wisdom, target’s choice Duration: Until the end of the target’s next turn Choose one non-Secret active talent, spell, stance, guard, or technique you have seen the target use during this encounter. Failed Save: The target cannot use that ability. Successful Save: The target can use the ability normally, but if it does so before the start of your next turn, it has Disadvantage on the first attack roll or saving throw involved in that activation. This talent does not remove known abilities permanently and cannot suppress a Path, Realm, Domain, Legendary Action, Lair Action, artifact, or Secret Inheritance. #### Nine-Needle Cascade - Point, Meridian Prerequisite: CL 10+ Trigger: You apply a Pressure Point through Touch the Point Save: Dexterity Choose one additional creature within 10 feet of the target and within your Meridian Flick range. Failed Save: Apply Numbing Point to the second creature. Successful Save: No effect. If both creatures already bear your Pressure Points, you may expend Martial Focus to apply the same Seal talent to both creatures. Each creature saves separately. #### Reversing Pulse - Counterpoint, Meridian Prerequisite: CL 10+ Action Type: Reaction Factory Combat Bucket: reaction Factory Routing: combat_action_row Trigger: A creature bearing one of your Pressure Points within 30 feet would regain HP, gain Temporary HP, or end a condition affecting itself The target makes a Constitution saving throw. Failed Save: Halve the HP or Temporary HP gained, or delay the condition removal until the end of the target’s next turn. Successful Save: Reduce the HP or Temporary HP gained by your Proficiency Bonus, or no effect if the trigger was condition removal. This talent cannot delay recovery caused by a Secret Inheritance, superior restoration, or explicit immunity-breaking cure unless the GM allows an opposed Cultivation Check. #### Life Gate Touch - Diagnostic, Meridian Prerequisite: Gentle Release, CL 10+ Action Type: Action Factory Combat Bucket: action Factory Routing: combat_action_row Range: Touch Target: One willing creature Cost: 2 CP or expend Martial Focus Touch the body’s life gate and force the breath to return. Choose one: the target immediately spends one Hit Die and adds your Pressure Points ability modifier to the HP regained; end one Poisoned, Frightened, or ordinary Paralyzed condition affecting the target; reduce the target’s Exhaustion by 1 if the Exhaustion was gained during the last hour; restore one use of a non-Secret technique that recharges on a short rest, if that technique has been unavailable for at least 1 minute and the GM agrees it is bodily or breath-based. A creature may benefit from your Life Gate Touch only once per long rest. #### Meridian Diagram Memory - Diagnostic Prerequisite: CL 10+ When you successfully use Pulse Diagnosis on a creature, you may create a mental meridian diagram of that creature for 24 hours. While the diagram remains: your first Precision Contact attack against that creature during each encounter has Advantage; the creature’s first saving throw against one of your Seal talents during each encounter has Disadvantage; you can recognize obvious disguises, shape changes, or possession attempts that fail to alter the creature’s underlying meridian rhythm. You may maintain a number of meridian diagrams equal to your Proficiency Bonus. ## NASCENT SOUL REALM TALENTS Nascent Soul Pressure Points techniques treat bodies, spirits, spells, and battlefield rhythm as meridian maps. The practitioner can touch the point before the movement becomes visible. ### Nascent Soul Form #### Sovereign Nine-Gate Hand - Realm Evolution Prerequisite: CL 15+ Action Type: Bonus Action Factory Combat Bucket: bonus_action Factory Routing: combat_action_row Duration: 1 minute Cost: Expend Martial Focus Use Limit: Once per long rest Manifest a sovereign pressure-point form: nine spectral fingers, a halo of acupuncture stars, a translucent meridian diagram overlaid on reality, or another suitable expression. For the duration: your Meridian Flick range becomes 60 feet; you may maintain up to three Pressure Points on the same creature; once during each of your turns, you may apply Numbing Point to one creature you can perceive within range without making an attack; when a creature bearing one of your Pressure Points fails a saving throw, misses an attack, or loses Concentration, you may move one of your Pressure Points from that creature to another creature you can perceive within range; when you use a Seal talent, you may choose for the Seal to last until the end of the target’s next turn instead of the start of your next turn, unless the talent already lasts longer; gain one additional Reaction each round, usable only for Counterpoint talents. Sovereign Nine-Gate Hand does not provide general paralysis, automatic technique cancellation, or permanent meridian control. ### Nascent Soul Talents #### Shut the Heaven Gate - Seal, Meridian Prerequisite: CL 15+ Trigger: You close a Seal through Touch the Point Save: Constitution Duration: Until the start of your next turn Failed Save: The target has the Stunned condition. Successful Save: The target is Dazed until the effect ends. While Dazed this way, the target cannot take Reactions and may take either an Action or a Bonus Action on its turn, not both. A creature that cannot be Stunned but has a readable meridian, animating, or spiritual structure suffers the successful-save effect on a failed save instead. #### Steal the Breath Between Actions - Counterpoint, Meridian Prerequisite: CL 15+ Action Type: Reaction Factory Combat Bucket: reaction Factory Routing: combat_action_row Trigger: A creature bearing one of your Pressure Points within 60 feet takes a Bonus Action or Reaction Cost: Expend Martial Focus Use Limit: Once per long rest The target makes a Wisdom saving throw. Failed Save: The triggering Bonus Action or Reaction fails and is wasted. Successful Save: The triggering act resolves, but the target cannot take another Bonus Action or Reaction until the end of its next turn. This talent steals timing, not memory or permission to act permanently. #### Meridian Stillness Field - Domain, Meridian Prerequisite: Chamber of Nine Gates, CL 15+ Action Type: Action Factory Combat Bucket: action Factory Routing: combat_action_row Area: 30-foot-radius sphere centered on a point you can see within 60 feet Duration: Concentration, up to 1 minute Cost: 4 CP, or expend Martial Focus and 2 CP Create a field of hovering meridian diagrams and suspended pressure lines. Hostile creatures inside the field that bear one of your Pressure Points suffer the following effects: Speed reduced by 10 feet; cannot benefit from Advantage on Concentration saving throws; cannot take Opportunity Attacks; the first time each round they activate a non-Secret technique, they make a Constitution saving throw. Failed Save: The activation completes, but the creature takes Psychic or Force damage equal to 2d8 + your Pressure Points ability modifier and cannot take Reactions until the start of its next turn. Successful Save: No damage. Meridian Stillness Field does not create a physical Barrier and does not stop teleportation unless the teleportation technique itself requires stable bodily or meridian flow and the GM calls for a contest. #### Return the Broken Pulse - Diagnostic, Meridian Prerequisite: Life Gate Touch, CL 15+ Action Type: Action Factory Combat Bucket: action Factory Routing: combat_action_row Range: Touch Target: One creature that died within the last round Cost: 6 CP Use Limit: Once per long rest You strike, press, or needle the last unclosed point of life. If the creature’s soul is free and willing, it returns to life with 1 HP. This technique cannot restore a creature that died of old age, whose body has been destroyed beyond recognition, whose soul is trapped or unwilling, or whose death was caused by a superior soul-destroying effect unless a separate story, ritual, or contest resolves that obstacle. Return the Broken Pulse is emergency resuscitation, not broad resurrection magic. ## SECRET PRESSURE POINTS INHERITANCE ### The Point Between Heartbeats “The immortal prepared ten thousand answers. The master touched the silence before the first one began.” Classification: Secret Pressure Points Inheritance Prerequisite: Sovereign Nine-Gate Hand, CL 17+, hidden meridian scripture or personal enlightenment Action Type: Action Factory Combat Bucket: action Factory Routing: combat_action_row Range: 90 feet Cost: Expend Martial Focus and 6 CP Use Limit: Once per week Choose one creature you can perceive. A single impossible point appears in its body, spirit, technique, shadow, or fate-like rhythm for one breath. The target makes a Constitution saving throw. If the target lacks ordinary anatomy but has a readable spiritual, mechanical, elemental, or conceptual structure, it makes a Wisdom saving throw instead. #### Failed Save The target is sealed until the end of its next turn. While sealed this way: it is Incapacitated; its Speed is 0; it cannot speak clearly or provide Verbal components; it loses Concentration; ongoing non-Secret body-enhancing, movement-enhancing, and technique-channeling effects on it are suppressed; it cannot take Reactions, Bonus Actions, Legendary Actions, or similar extra actions; the next attack roll made against it before the seal ends has Advantage and deals an extra 6d10 Force or Psychic damage on a hit. #### Successful Save The target is partially sealed until the start of your next turn. While partially sealed this way: it cannot take Reactions; its Speed is halved; it has Disadvantage on Concentration saving throws; the next attack roll made against it before the partial seal ends has Advantage. #### Limits The Point Between Heartbeats cannot permanently disable a creature, erase a Path, remove a Realm, destroy a soul, suppress a Secret Inheritance automatically, or rewrite destiny. A creature of superior Realm, divine office, or narrative-scale authority may convert the failed-save result into the successful-save result by winning an opposed Cultivation Check, at the GM’s discretion. ## VARIANTS ### Physician’s Hand You learn Gentle Release instead of Numbing Point as your automatic base talent. Your Pressure Points techniques may still be used offensively, but when you use a Seal talent against an unwilling creature, you must expend Martial Focus. ### Killer’s Hand You cannot use Gentle Release, Life Gate Touch, or Return the Broken Pulse. When a creature bearing one of your Pressure Points is Bloodied, the first Point talent you apply to it each round deals extra Psychic or Necrotic damage equal to your Proficiency Bonus. ### Weapon-Point Stylist You do not gain proficiency in Medicine or Sleight of Hand from Pressure Points Training. Instead, choose dagger, dart, shortsword, spear, whip, or another GM-approved precise weapon. You may treat melee attacks with that weapon as Precision Contact for this sphere. This variant is suitable for needle rings, short blades, pressure rods, medical needles, and sect weapons designed to touch meridian gates. ## PATH SYNERGIES These synergies describe common ways each Path expresses Pressure Points. A class feature, forged technique, Insight, or GM-approved build option may reference these rules. ### Body Refining Body Refiners express Pressure Points through conditioned fingers, iron knuckles, thumb locks, palm-edge strikes, tendon knowledge, and painful practice. If a Body Refining feature lets you use Constitution for a martial sphere’s save DC, you may use Constitution as your Pressure Points ability. A Body Refining technique may spend Stamina instead of CP for a Pressure Points Meridian talent if the technique is built around tendons, joints, breath, or iron-body conditioning. When a Body Refiner also knows Iron Fist, a forged technique may allow one Iron Fist Opening and one Pressure Point to be applied by the same successful unarmed strike. ### Qi Cultivation Qi Cultivators express Pressure Points through fine Qi needles, pulse threads, projected finger light, and meridian diagramming. A Qi Cultivation technique may spend CP to extend Meridian Flick range for one use. A Qi Cultivation technique may change a Pressure Points talent’s supernatural expression to Force, Radiant, Necrotic, or Psychic damage when the scripture supports it. Pressure Points may serve as a precise delivery method for Qi support or disruption techniques that require touch. ### Spirit Awakening Spirit Awakening cultivators express Pressure Points through soul rhythm, intent pulses, spirit gates, and possession-disrupting touches. Spirit Awakening uses Wisdom naturally with this sphere and often treats spiritual seams as readable meridians. Meridian talents may affect ghosts, possessed bodies, and spiritual projections when they have readable spirit structure. Counterpoint talents may be used as part of forged techniques against possession attempts, fear techniques, and soul-pressure attacks. ## CULTIVATION INSIGHTS ### Acupuncture Scripture Memorist Prerequisite: Pressure Points sphere When you finish a long rest, choose one creature type you studied during the rest, such as humanoids, beasts, dragons, undead, constructs, or elementals. Until your next long rest, your first Wisdom (Medicine), Dexterity (Sleight of Hand), or Cultivation Check each encounter to identify or apply pressure points to that creature type has Advantage. ### Gentle But Exact Prerequisite: Pressure Points sphere When you apply a Point talent to a willing creature, you may do so without dealing damage from the triggering Precision Contact. In addition, when you use Gentle Release, the target may also stand from Prone without spending movement. ### Two-Finger Doctrine Prerequisite: Twin Gate Method Once per turn when you apply a Pressure Point to a creature that already bears one of your Pressure Points, you may move 5 feet without provoking Opportunity Attacks from that creature. If you then use a Seal talent before the end of the same turn, gain Temporary HP equal to your Proficiency Bonus. ### Pulse Breaker Prerequisite: CL 10+, Pressure Points sphere When a creature bearing one of your Pressure Points begins Concentration, regains Concentration through a feature, or succeeds on a Concentration saving throw, you may expend Martial Focus. The creature must repeat the Concentration saving throw against your Pressure Points Save DC. Once a creature repeats a saving throw because of this Insight, it cannot be affected by this Insight again until the start of your next turn. ### Closed-Gate Mercy Prerequisite: CL 10+, Gentle Release When you reduce a creature to 0 HP with Precision Contact, you may seal its collapse instead of injuring it further. The creature becomes stable, Unconscious, and unable to wake for 1 minute unless it takes damage or another creature uses an Action to awaken it. A creature awakened this way is Prone, has Speed 0 until the end of its next turn, and remembers the touch that ended the fight.

automatic_base_abilities.effect:
#### Barrier Ward
When you learn the Protection sphere, you learn this Ward talent automatically.
Create a mostly transparent wall along the Ward’s perimeter.
The Barrier blocks:
movement through its edge;
attacks crossing its edge;
breath weapons crossing its edge;
destructive blasts crossing its edge;
ghost strikes crossing its edge;
other effects that must physically travel to their destination. The Barrier does not automatically block teleportation, mind-affecting effects, gaze attacks, or abilities that do not travel through the wall.
##### Barrier Placement
If the Barrier cuts through a creature’s space when it appears, the creature chooses one side and is pushed into the nearest legal space on that side.
If the Barrier and another solid surface would completely enclose a creature, it may make a Dexterity saving throw.
Successful Save: The creature may use its Reaction to move up to its Speed into the nearest legal space outside the enclosure.
Failed Save: The creature remains enclosed.
The Barrier extends into the Ethereal Plane.
##### Barrier Statistics
If the Barrier reaches 0 HP, the Ward ends.
##### Overflow Damage
If an attack deals more damage than the Barrier’s current HP, the attacker may burst through.
Subtract the Barrier’s remaining HP from the attack’s damage.
If the attack can legally continue to a creature on the other side, make a new attack roll against one target within range.
On a hit, deal the remaining damage.
Area damage that bursts through affects creatures on the other side with its remaining damage.
##### Crushing Through
A creature may use an Action to attempt to shove or overrun the Barrier.
Make a Strength (Athletics) check against your Cultivation Save DC.
Successful Check: The Barrier shatters and the Ward ends.
Failed Check: The Barrier remains.

spheres.full_exact_source_text: # Sphere of Protection Qi Expression: Primary — Ward Qi; Supporting — Earth Qi, Formation Qi, Oath Qi, Light Qi. “A wall is not merely what refuses the enemy. It is the promise that something behind it will still exist when the enemy is gone.” Sphere Type: Power Sphere Primary Path: Qi Cultivation Secondary Path: Spirit Awakening Rare Variant: Body Refining through Living Bulwark Body Resource: CP Common Effects: Aegises, sacrificial defenses, barriers, threshold control, battlefield shelter, resistance, protection from hostile cultivation The Sphere of Protection teaches active defense. Its practitioners place Aegises on creatures, sacrifice prepared defenses through Succor, and create Wards that shelter an area. Protection creates active defenses. Permanent fortifications and prepared infrastructure belong to Formation projects. ### CORE PROTECTION RULES #### Aegis An Aegis is a protective cultivation effect placed on one creature. Unless a talent says otherwise: A creature may benefit from only one Aegis created by the same cultivator at a time. An Aegis uses Concentration unless made Persistent. An Aegis may be ended early by its creator without spending an action. An unwilling creature may make a Wisdom saving throw to resist receiving an Aegis. Aegis talents replace the Armored Aegis unless the talent explicitly says it augments another Aegis. #### Succor A Succor is a sacrificial rescue. The base Protection sphere does not grant a Succor effect automatically; Succor talents provide the triggers and effects. To use Succor, a trigger stated by one Succor talent you know must occur and that talent must have an eligible target. The target must currently benefit from one of your Persistent Aegises. The detailed Reaction procedure appears under the base Succor ability below. #### Ward A Ward is a temporary protected area. Unless a talent says otherwise: a Ward is centered within range; a Ward remains where it was created; a Ward uses Concentration unless made Persistent; you may reduce its size when creating it; you may maintain only one Ward at a time. Ward talents replace Barrier Ward unless the talent explicitly modifies Barrier Ward. #### Barrier A Barrier is the translucent protective wall created by Barrier Ward. A Barrier may block attacks, movement, breath weapons, and effects that must physically travel to their destination. A Barrier does not automatically stop: teleportation; gaze attacks; mind-affecting effects; effects that originate inside the protected area; effects that do not travel through the Barrier. ### BASE SPHERE ABILITIES #### Aegis Action Type: Action Factory Combat Bucket: action Factory Routing: combat_action_row Range: Touch Target: One creature Duration: Concentration, up to 1 hour Cost: None Grant the target one Aegis talent you know. An unwilling creature makes a Wisdom saving throw. Failed Save: The target receives the Aegis. Successful Save: No effect. ##### Persistent Aegis Augment - 2 CP: The Aegis persists for its remaining duration without Concentration. You may apply this augment after creating the Aegis on your turn without spending an action. #### Armored Aegis When you learn the Protection sphere, you learn this Aegis talent automatically. Protective barriers wrap the target. The target’s base AC becomes equal to your Cultivation Save DC. The target does not add its Dexterity modifier to this AC. Armored Aegis does not stack with worn armor, but the target may still benefit from a shield. #### Succor Action Type: Reaction Factory Combat Bucket: reaction Factory Routing: combat_action_row Trigger: A trigger stated by one Succor talent you know occurs, and that talent has an eligible target Range: 300 feet Target: One creature benefiting from one of your Persistent Aegises Cost: Sacrifice one Persistent Aegis you created on the target When the chosen Succor talent's trigger occurs, use your Reaction before the triggering event finishes resolving unless that talent says otherwise. Choose one Succor talent you know whose trigger and target requirements are satisfied. Immediately end one Persistent Aegis you created on the target, then resolve that Succor talent's effect. The sacrificed Aegis ends even if the Succor effect is later prevented or produces no benefit. You cannot activate the base Succor wrapper without a Succor talent whose trigger has occurred. #### Ward Action Type: Action Factory Combat Bucket: action Factory Routing: combat_action_row Range: Self Area: 20-foot-radius, 10-foot-tall cylinder centered within range Duration: Concentration, up to 1 minute Cost: None Create one Ward talent you know. The Ward remains where it was created. You may reduce the height or radius when you create it. Ward size increases by Realm: ##### Persistent Ward Augment - 2 CP: The Ward persists for its remaining duration without Concentration. You may apply this augment after creating the Ward on your turn without spending an action. #### Barrier Ward When you learn the Protection sphere, you learn this Ward talent automatically. Create a mostly transparent wall along the Ward’s perimeter. The Barrier blocks: movement through its edge; attacks crossing its edge; breath weapons crossing its edge; destructive blasts crossing its edge; ghost strikes crossing its edge; other effects that must physically travel to their destination. The Barrier does not automatically block teleportation, mind-affecting effects, gaze attacks, or abilities that do not travel through the wall. ##### Barrier Placement If the Barrier cuts through a creature’s space when it appears, the creature chooses one side and is pushed into the nearest legal space on that side. If the Barrier and another solid surface would completely enclose a creature, it may make a Dexterity saving throw. Successful Save: The creature may use its Reaction to move up to its Speed into the nearest legal space outside the enclosure. Failed Save: The creature remains enclosed. The Barrier extends into the Ethereal Plane. ##### Barrier Statistics If the Barrier reaches 0 HP, the Ward ends. ##### Overflow Damage If an attack deals more damage than the Barrier’s current HP, the attacker may burst through. Subtract the Barrier’s remaining HP from the attack’s damage. If the attack can legally continue to a creature on the other side, make a new attack roll against one target within range. On a hit, deal the remaining damage. Area damage that bursts through affects creatures on the other side with its remaining damage. ##### Crushing Through A creature may use an Action to attempt to shove or overrun the Barrier. Make a Strength (Athletics) check against your Cultivation Save DC. Successful Check: The Barrier shatters and the Ward ends. Failed Check: The Barrier remains. ### PROTECTION TALENT TAGS #### Aegis Talents An Aegis talent provides an alternative personal protection effect. #### Succor Talents A Succor talent provides an effect that may be triggered by sacrificing one of your Persistent Aegises. #### Ward Talents A Ward talent provides an alternative protected-area effect. #### Barrier Talents A Barrier talent modifies Barrier Ward. Unless a talent says otherwise, apply only one Barrier augment when creating a Barrier Ward. #### Augments An Augment modifies another Protection effect when its additional CP cost is paid. ### MORTAL REALM PROTECTION TALENTS #### Shielded - Aegis Create a weightless translucent shield. The shield functions as an ordinary shield. It does not interfere with material or somatic components. If the bearer uses the shield-hand to hold another object, the shield is suppressed until the start of the next turn in which that hand is free. Augment - 1 CP: The bearer is treated as proficient with the shield. #### Slippery - Aegis Protect the bearer from physical restraint and manipulation. The bearer gains Advantage on: saving throws against being Restrained; saving throws against forced movement; checks made to avoid being shoved; checks made to escape a Grapple; checks made to squeeze through a tight space; checks made to escape bonds. #### Energy Resistance - Aegis, Ward Choose one damage type: Acid; Cold; Fire; Lightning; Radiant; Thunder. ##### Aegis The bearer gains Resistance to the chosen damage type. ##### Ward Creatures inside gain Resistance to the chosen damage type while they remain inside. #### Protected Health - Aegis, Ward ##### Aegis The bearer gains: Resistance to Poison damage; Advantage on saving throws against poison; Advantage on saving throws against disease. ##### Ward Creatures inside gain those benefits while they remain inside. #### Impedance - Aegis, Ward ##### Aegis A creature attempting to enter a space within 5 feet of the bearer makes a Wisdom saving throw. Failed Save: It cannot enter that space until the start of its next turn. Successful Save: It may move normally. Augment - 1 CP: Increase the protected distance to 10 feet. ##### Ward A creature makes a Wisdom saving throw when it attempts to enter the Ward or move closer to the Ward’s center for the first time on a turn. Failed Save: It cannot enter or move closer to the center until the start of its next turn. Successful Save: It may move normally. Impedance affects movement only. It does not stop attacks. #### Obscurity - Aegis, Ward Protected creatures appear unremarkable and unimportant. A creature attempting to notice a protected creature makes an Intelligence saving throw before making any Wisdom (Perception) check. Failed Save: It fails to notice the protected creature. Successful Save: It may perceive the creature normally until the protected creature leaves its sight or successfully Hides. A creature automatically succeeds if it: is already in combat with the protected creature; is specifically searching for that creature; has been clearly told the creature is present; possesses a talent that explicitly bypasses Obscurity. #### Impartiality - Aegis, Ward Protected creatures are treated as having no alignment for magical effects. This does not disguise alignment. It creates an absence. The Aegis or Ward also conceals the creature type of: Celestials; Fiends; Fey; Undead. A creature still remains its actual creature type for effects that do not rely on detection. #### Status You always know: the direction and distance to creatures benefiting from one of your Aegises; whether they are unharmed, wounded, disabled, frightened, unconscious, dying, poisoned, diseased, stunned, or similarly afflicted. This awareness ends if a target dies or leaves the plane. #### Bulwark - Succor Trigger: A protected ally is targeted by an attack roll Sacrifice one Persistent Aegis on that ally. The ally gains Resistance to all damage dealt by the triggering attack. #### Luck - Succor Trigger: A protected creature makes a saving throw Sacrifice one Persistent Aegis on that creature. The creature rerolls the saving throw and must use the new result. #### Punishment - Aegis, Succor ##### Aegis A creature that hits the bearer with an attack takes Psychic damage based on your CL. Punishment Damage: • CL 1-4: Psychic damage equal to your Proficiency Bonus. • CL 5-10: 1d6 + your Proficiency Bonus Psychic damage. • CL 11-16: 2d6 + your Proficiency Bonus Psychic damage. • CL 17-20: 3d6 + your Proficiency Bonus Psychic damage. ##### Succor Trigger: A protected ally takes damage from an attack Sacrifice one Persistent Aegis on that ally. The attacker takes Psychic damage based on your CL, using the Punishment Damage table. Punishment Succor stacks with Punishment Aegis. #### Continuous Barrier - Barrier When creating Barrier Ward, you may shape it into: a hemispherical dome; a sealed sphere. The Barrier is fully sealed. If it passes through an ordinary object, it cuts harmlessly through the material without damaging it, but the object cannot be moved through the Barrier. Creatures and animated objects are shunted normally. Burrowing, Ethereal travel, and unusual movement cannot bypass the sealed Barrier. #### Greater Barrier - Barrier When creating Barrier Ward, you may form a flat vertical plane. The wall: must be contiguous; must include one point adjacent to you; may extend up to 30 feet away; contains a maximum number of 10-foot x 10-foot panels equal to twice your Proficiency Bonus. ##### Reinforced Barrier Augment - 1 CP: Increase the Barrier’s maximum HP to 10 x CL. Increase the DC to shove or overrun the Barrier by 5. A Reinforced Barrier does not renew HP automatically, even while maintained through Concentration. ##### Expanded Panels Augment - 1 CP: Increase the maximum number of panels to four times your Proficiency Bonus. ##### Grand Panels Augment - 2 CP: Increase panel size to 20-foot x 20-foot. #### Buttress Action Type: Action Factory Combat Bucket: action Factory Routing: combat_action_row Range: 300 feet Target: One Barrier Ward you created Cost: 1 CP Restore HP to the Barrier equal to: 5 x CL You cannot restore a Barrier above its maximum HP. ##### Swift Buttress Augment - 1 CP: Use Buttress as a Bonus Action. ##### Emergency Buttress Augment - 2 CP: Use Buttress as a Reaction when an attack would destroy the Barrier. Add the restored HP before resolving the triggering damage. ### FOUNDATION REALM PROTECTION TALENTS #### Clarity - Ward Attempts to conceal, disguise, or obfuscate creatures inside the Ward are hindered. When the Ward appears, make one Cultivation Check against each: illusion; concealment effect; magical disguise; magical item creating those effects. Successful Check: Suppress that effect while it remains inside the Ward. Failed Check: The effect continues normally. A creature attempting to activate an illusion, concealment effect, or disguise inside the Ward must succeed on a Cultivation Check against your Cultivation Save DC. A creature inside also makes a Wisdom saving throw. Failed Save: It cannot activate ordinary abilities that disguise or conceal itself while it remains inside. Successful Save: It may use nonmagical concealment normally, but supernatural concealment still faces the Cultivation Check. #### Exclusion - Ward Choose one common material, element, or physical property when creating the Ward. Examples include: stone; metal; water; acid; fire; light; poisonous material; living material. A creature made of or carrying the excluded substance must make a Strength check against your Cultivation Save DC to cross the Ward’s edge. Failed Check: The creature cannot cross while carrying or embodying the excluded substance. Successful Check: The creature crosses normally. A creature may drop carried excluded material before attempting to cross. An attack crossing into the Ward while composed primarily of the excluded substance has Disadvantage. Exclusion does not remove material already inside. #### Peacebound - Aegis, Ward ##### Aegis A creature attempting a violent action or offensive supernatural effect against the bearer makes a Wisdom saving throw. Failed Save: The action fails. Any CP or limited-use resource spent is lost. Successful Save: The Peacebound Aegis ends immediately. If the bearer takes an offensive action, the Aegis ends immediately. ##### Ward A creature attempting a violent action or offensive supernatural effect while inside the Ward makes a Wisdom saving throw. Failed Save: The action fails. Any CP or limited-use resource spent is lost. Successful Save: The Peacebound Ward ends for all creatures. When a creature breaks your Peacebound Ward in this way, creatures inside become immune to your Peacebound Ward until the next dawn. #### Repel Spirit-Kin - Ward Choose one or more creature families appropriate to the setting: Celestials; Fiends; Fey; Undead. A chosen creature attempting to cross the Ward’s edge makes a Charisma saving throw. Failed Save: It cannot cross. Successful Save: It may cross and becomes immune to your Repel Spirit-Kin Ward until the next dawn. A creature already inside when the Ward appears is unaffected. #### Spell Ward - Aegis Cost: 1 CP The bearer gains Advantage on saving throws against supernatural effects. #### Spell Ward - Ward Cost: 3 CP When the Ward appears, make one Cultivation Check against each supernatural effect, magic item, or summoned creature inside. Successful Check: Suppress that effect, item, or summoned creature while it remains inside. Failed Check: It functions normally. A cultivator attempting to activate a supernatural effect inside the Ward, target a creature inside from outside, or send a summoned creature across the Ward’s threshold makes a Cultivation Check against your Cultivation Save DC. Successful Check: The effect functions normally. Failed Check: The effect is suppressed or the summoned creature cannot cross. Time spent suppressed still counts against the effect’s duration. #### Community Whenever a creature benefiting from one of your Aegises takes damage, you may transfer up to half of that damage to another willing creature benefiting from one of your Aegises. No action is required. Transferred damage: keeps its original damage type; cannot be transferred again; cannot be redirected by another effect. ### CORE FORMATION REALM PROTECTION TALENTS #### Adaptation - Aegis Prerequisite: Energy Resistance and one future environmental-protection Aegis, CL 10+ Cost: +4 CP When applying the required environmental-protection Aegis, improve it. The bearer becomes immune to: extreme heat; extreme cold; toxic air; drowning; vacuum exposure. The bearer gains Resistance to: Acid; Cold; Fire; Lightning; Radiant; Thunder. Additional Resistances may be added if you know future talents that explicitly provide them. Source gap: Adaptation remains provisional because the supplied source did not include the referenced environmental-protection talents. #### Anti-Magic Aura - Ward Prerequisite: Spell Ward, CL 12+ Action Type: Action Factory Combat Bucket: action Factory Routing: combat_action_row Range: Self only Duration: Concentration, up to 1 minute Cost: 5 CP Create a Spell Ward centered on yourself. No Cultivation Check is required. Inside the Ward: ordinary supernatural effects are suppressed; ordinary magic items cease functioning; summoned creatures temporarily disappear; new supernatural effects fail automatically. Anti-Magic Aura does not automatically suppress: Domains; Secret Inheritances; Formation cores; Realm-defining transformations; artifacts; effects explicitly written to resist anti-magic suppression. Those require a contested Cultivation Check or a separate ruling. #### Sanctuary Without Borders - Ward Prerequisite: Peacebound or Impedance, CL 12+ Action Type: Action Factory Combat Bucket: action Factory Routing: combat_action_row Duration: Concentration, up to 1 minute Cost: 5 CP Choose one Ward you create. When a willing creature enters the Ward for the first time on a turn or starts its turn inside, it may immediately end one of the following: Frightened; Grappled; Restrained; one ordinary forced-movement effect; one ordinary ongoing damage effect caused by a talent. A creature may benefit once per activation. Sanctuary Without Borders does not end curses, Domains, Secret effects, or permanent injuries. ### NASCENT SOUL REALM PROTECTION TALENTS #### Unplottable - Aegis Prerequisite: Obscurity, CL 15+ Cost: +3 CP When applying Obscurity Aegis, make the bearer undetectable through ordinary divination. Attempts to gather information directly about the bearer automatically fail. This includes ordinary: scrying; supernatural tracking; effects that reveal Invisible; alignment detection; creature-type detection. Area scans still function normally, but the bearer does not appear inside them. Unplottable does not automatically defeat: Secret divination inheritances; artifacts; Domains; direct observation; effects explicitly written to overcome it. #### Citadel of One Breath - Ward Prerequisite: Barrier Ward, Greater Barrier, Buttress, CL 15+ Action Type: Reaction Factory Combat Bucket: reaction Factory Routing: combat_action_row Trigger: A Barrier Ward you created would be destroyed Cost: 10 CP Use Limit: Once per long rest The Barrier remains at 1 HP instead of being destroyed. Until the start of your next turn: it cannot lose HP; it cannot be shoved or overrun; teleportation crossing its boundary requires a successful Cultivation Check against your Cultivation Save DC; creatures inside gain Half Cover against attacks originating outside. At the start of your next turn, the Barrier resumes functioning normally. #### Heaven-Sheltering Aegis Prerequisite: Armored Aegis, Bulwark, Luck, CL 15+ Action Type: Action Factory Combat Bucket: action Factory Routing: combat_action_row Range: Touch Duration: 1 minute Cost: 12 CP Use Limit: Once per long rest Grant one willing creature an exalted Aegis. For the duration: its base AC becomes your Cultivation Save DC + 2; it gains Advantage on all saving throws; it gains Resistance to all damage; once during the duration, when it would drop to 0 HP, it drops to 1 HP instead and the Aegis ends. Heaven-Sheltering Aegis cannot be made Persistent. ### SECRET PROTECTION INHERITANCE #### The Wall That Remains After Heaven Breaks “When the formation shattered, the mountain burned, and every oath failed, the wall remained because one cultivator had not yet agreed to let the people behind it die.” Classification: Secret Protection Inheritance Prerequisite: CL 17+, Barrier Ward, Buttress, Bulwark, hidden guardian inheritance Action Type: Reaction Factory Combat Bucket: reaction Factory Routing: combat_action_row Trigger: One of the following: you or an ally benefiting from your Aegis would drop to 0 HP; a Barrier Ward you created would be destroyed; a creature inside one of your Wards would fail a saving throw against an effect that would incapacitate it. Cost: 15 CP Use Limit: Once per week Choose one: The protected creature drops to 1 HP instead of 0 HP. The Barrier remains at 1 HP and negates overflow damage from the triggering effect. The protected creature succeeds on the triggering saving throw. Sacrifice one Aegis on the protected creature without requiring it to be Persistent and activate one Succor talent you know. Immediately create Barrier Ward centered on the protected creature without spending an Action or CP. Until the end of your next turn: your Barrier Wards cannot be shoved or overrun; Buttress restores maximum possible HP; creatures benefiting from your Aegises gain Resistance to all damage; your Wards cannot be made permanent or converted into Formation infrastructure through this effect. ### OPTIONAL PROTECTION CULTIVATION VARIANTS A Protection cultivation variant changes what the cultivator believes preservation requires. These variants are mutually exclusive. They do not automatically grant bonus talents. #### Limited Protection Choose Aegis or Ward. You lose access to the unchosen base ability. If you choose Aegis, you may still learn and use Succor talents. ##### Benefit When you spend CP on the chosen ability, reduce its CP cost by 1, minimum 0. ##### Limitation You cannot learn talents requiring the unchosen base ability. #### Protected Soul “The first wall must be built around the self.” You may apply Aegises only to yourself. Any Ward you create ends immediately if you end your turn outside it. ##### Benefits Increase the duration of your self-applied Aegises to 8 hours. Once per turn when you spend CP on an Aegis or Ward, reduce the cost by 1, minimum 0. Gain Advantage on Concentration checks made to maintain a Protection effect. ### PATH SYNERGIES #### Qi Cultivation - Refined Barrier Circulation Use Intelligence or Charisma as your Protection key ability. Once per turn, reduce the CP cost of one Protection talent by 1, minimum 1. Increase Buttress healing by your Proficiency Bonus. #### Spirit Awakening - Guardian-Spirit Mantle Use Wisdom as your Protection key ability. Your Aegises and Wards affect: spirits; ghosts; astral projections; incorporeal creatures; possessing entities normally. When you apply an Aegis to a spirit or a creature currently sharing space with a spirit, you know whether that spirit is willing, hostile, frightened, or compelled. #### Body Refining - Living Bulwark Body Requires the Living Bulwark Body Cultivation Insight. Use Constitution and Stamina for Protection talents. While you benefit from one of your Aegises: gain +1 AC; gain Advantage on checks and saving throws against being shoved or moved; once per round when Stamina Guard reduces damage to 0, recover 1 Stamina. ### CULTIVATION INSIGHTS #### Living Bulwark Body Prerequisite: Body Refining, Protection sphere, CL 4+ Learn Protection as a Body Refining discipline. Use Constitution and Stamina for Protection talents. Gain the Living Bulwark Body synergy. #### Succor Adept Prerequisite: Protection sphere, one Succor talent, CL 6+ Increase Succor range to 1 mile. Once per long rest, activate one Succor talent without ending the sacrificed Persistent Aegis. #### Ward-Script Custodian Prerequisite: Protection sphere, Formations sphere, CL 8+ When designing a Formation project, you may use one Ward talent you know as a seed effect. This does not create the Formation automatically. The project still requires: preparation time; anchors; materials; a core or power source; maintenance; Formation-specific vulnerabilities. #### Shared Burden Adept Prerequisite: Protection sphere, Community, CL 8+ When using Community, transfer up to three-quarters of the triggering damage instead of half. A creature may receive transferred damage from Shared Burden Adept only once per round. ### SOURCE GAP The supplied Protection source referenced Breathless, Deathless, and Inner Peace without providing their rules. They are not included in this player-facing draft. Adaptation remains provisional until those talents are supplied or intentionally redesigned. Patch v1.10.2 Note: Punishment now has explicit Psychic damage scaling for both its Aegis and Succor uses. This resolves the known Punishment parser gap but does not supply Breathless, Deathless, or Inner Peace.

resolved_automatic_base_abilities.effect:
#### Barrier Ward
When you learn the Protection sphere, you learn this Ward talent automatically.
Create a mostly transparent wall along the Ward’s perimeter.
The Barrier blocks:
movement through its edge;
attacks crossing its edge;
breath weapons crossing its edge;
destructive blasts crossing its edge;
ghost strikes crossing its edge;
other effects that must physically travel to their destination. The Barrier does not automatically block teleportation, mind-affecting effects, gaze attacks, or abilities that do not travel through the wall.
##### Barrier Placement
If the Barrier cuts through a creature’s space when it appears, the creature chooses one side and is pushed into the nearest legal space on that side.
If the Barrier and another solid surface would completely enclose a creature, it may make a Dexterity saving throw.
Successful Save: The creature may use its Reaction to move up to its Speed into the nearest legal space outside the enclosure.
Failed Save: The creature remains enclosed.
The Barrier extends into the Ethereal Plane.
##### Barrier Statistics
If the Barrier reaches 0 HP, the Ward ends.
##### Overflow Damage
If an attack deals more damage than the Barrier’s current HP, the attacker may burst through.
Subtract the Barrier’s remaining HP from the attack’s damage.
If the attack can legally continue to a creature on the other side, make a new attack roll against one target within range.
On a hit, deal the remaining damage.
Area damage that bursts through affects creatures on the other side with its remaining damage.
##### Crushing Through
A creature may use an Action to attempt to shove or overrun the Barrier.
Make a Strength (Athletics) check against your Cultivation Save DC.
Successful Check: The Barrier shatters and the Ward ends.
Failed Check: The Barrier remains.

### Raise the Vessel
Action Type: Action
Factory Combat Bucket: action
Factory Routing: combat_action_row
Range: 30 feet, or touch for Body Refining unless using Projected Puppetry
Duration: 1 minute
Cost: 1 CP
Target: One suitable puppet vessel
You claim one puppet vessel and set a control thread to it.
The vessel becomes active for the duration.
When you activate the vessel, and as a Bonus Action on later turns, you may move it up to its Speed.
This movement may include climbing, crawling, hopping, rolling, skittering, or walking as appropriate for its form.
The vessel cannot fly, swim, burrow, squeeze through impossible spaces, or climb smooth surfaces unless a talent, construction, or feature allows it.
You may dismiss the vessel on your turn without an Action.
If you raise a second vessel, the first vessel becomes inactive unless a talent allows you to control more than one.
