spheres.full_exact_source_text: # Sphere of Sand Qi Expression: Primary — Sand Qi; Supporting — Earth Qi, Wind Qi, Erosion Qi, Glass-Origin Qi. “A mountain is only a patient desert.” Cultivation Names: Scripture of the Ten Thousand Grains; Dune-Heart Method; Scripture of Grinding Earth; The Desert That Remembers Sphere Type: Power Sphere / Elemental Terrain Sphere Primary Path: Qi Cultivation Secondary Paths: Body Refining and Spirit Awakening Resource: Cultivation Power (CP) Common Effects: Sand terrain, difficult terrain, light obscurement, scouring damage, burial, blinds, glass, desiccation, terrain shaping, moving dunes, footprint-reading, sand armor, area denial Sand cultivates erosion, accumulation, unstable ground, scouring grains, burial, glass, desiccation, and terrain-memory. ### Player-Facing Rules ### Sand Dao Sand is the cultivation of erosion, accumulation, and the many becoming one. A sword decides in a single line. A fist answers through one body. A stone wall says no. Sand asks how many refusals a thing can survive before it becomes dust. Sand’s Dao has four faces: Grain: the smallest part, overlooked until countless grains move together. Dune: terrain as a living decision, shifting under every step. Scour: the slow cut that does not need to be deep if it never stops. Burial: the law that every shape, name, body, road, and ruin may be covered. A Sand cultivator at low level throws grit, reshapes loose earth, and steals footing. At Foundation, they awaken Dune-Heart Sand that moves by command. At Core Formation, they establish a court where every grain listens. At Nascent Soul, they become the desert storm, difficult to kill because no one grain is the whole self. At Secret Inheritance, they teach mountains and cities that all forms are temporary. ### Realm Progression Mortal Realm: Control loose sand, dust, powdered stone, dry soil, grit, gravel, and similar mineral grains. Create Sand Terrain, blind with grit, scour exposed flesh, shelter behind dunes, read tracks, and drag enemies through unstable ground. Foundation Realm: Awaken Dune-Heart Sand, allowing conjured grains, longer range, supernatural movement, sand armor, burial techniques, and the first glass transformations. Core Formation Realm: Establish the Court of Ten Thousand Dunes, a battlefield domain where sand remembers every step, dunes rise and fall by command, and enemies are ground down by terrain logistics. Nascent Soul Realm: Manifest the Sand-Sovereign Incarnation, becoming a walking desert storm, sand-bodied cultivator, or dune-crowned monarch whose body and territory blur together. Secret Inheritance: Invoke The Mountain Remembers It Is Dust, an apex scripture that erodes one decisive structure, formation, army-line, or battlefield advantage into sand and commands the result. ### Rules Baseline This sphere uses the 2024 fifth-edition rules baseline and the Tianxia cultivation rules. Use the 2024 meanings of Action, Bonus Action, Reaction, Attack action, Opportunity Attack, Advantage, Disadvantage, Cover, Concentration, Difficult Terrain, Blinded, Restrained, Prone, Grappled, Incapacitated, Exhaustion, Saving Throw, and Object unless this sphere specifically changes them. #### Difficult Terrain Sand Terrain often creates Difficult Terrain. A creature moving through Difficult Terrain spends 1 extra foot of movement for every foot it moves there. Multiple sources of Difficult Terrain do not normally stack unless a talent says so. #### Lightly Obscured and Heavily Obscured Dust and sand can obscure vision. A lightly obscured area usually imposes Disadvantage on Wisdom (Perception) checks that rely on sight. A heavily obscured area blocks sight for many purposes and may effectively impose the Blinded condition when a creature tries to see something inside or beyond it. This sphere states when an area is lightly or heavily obscured. #### Cover A dune, wall of sand, hardened glass ridge, or raised bank can grant Half Cover or Three-Quarters Cover only when a talent says so and the geometry makes sense. Sand cover is physical unless a talent says otherwise. Loose sand does not automatically block line of effect. #### Blinded Sand talents that Blind a target usually represent grit in the eyes, scouring spiritual sight, or a cloud of grains. Creatures without eyes or sight can be immune to some Mortal effects, but Foundation and higher talents may affect spiritual perception, tremorsense-like senses, or exposed sensory organs if stated. #### Restrained and Buried Restrained is a 2024 condition. Buried is a Sand-specific state defined below. Some Sand talents impose Restrained while buried, but Buried is not automatically the same as Restrained. #### Suffocation and Breathing This sphere does not use full suffocation rules unless a talent explicitly says so. Short-duration sand choking usually imposes Disadvantage, prevents speech, or blocks breath-dependent techniques rather than immediately suffocating a target. #### Objects and Structures Sand can damage or bury objects. If a talent affects an object, use the object’s AC, Hit Points, Damage Threshold, immunity, or special rules where applicable. A door, wall, bridge, vehicle, or formation anchor may require an opposed Cultivation Check, project-scale work, or GM adjudication if it is scene-defining. #### Falling and Unstable Ground Sand can cause Prone, sliding, sinking, or forced movement. If a talent causes a creature to fall from height, use normal falling rules. Sand does not automatically negate fall damage unless a talent says it cushions the fall. #### Burrowing Sand talents may allow limited movement through sand or loose earth. This is not broad Earth burrowing through stone, metal, wood, force barriers, or worked floors unless a talent explicitly allows it. ### Core Sand Rules #### Sand Technique Save DC When a Sand talent calls for a saving throw, use your Cultivation Save DC unless the Path, class feature, or technique grants another DC. Cultivation Save DC = 8 + Proficiency Bonus + your key ability modifier. The default key ability for Sand is the key ability of the Path through which you learned or use the sphere. Qi Cultivation commonly uses Intelligence or Charisma depending on tradition; Body Refining commonly uses Constitution; Spirit Awakening commonly uses Wisdom. #### Sand Source A Sand Source is a legal physical medium from which Sand techniques can draw grains. Examples include: loose sand; dust; dry soil; powdered stone; grit, gravel, or loose mineral fragments; desert ground; shattered pottery, crushed brick, ground glass, or similar mineral particulate; dry ash-like particulate only if the GM agrees the effect is physical grain-work rather than Ash sphere fire-remnant magic. A Sand Source is not normally: solid stone that has not been powdered; living flesh; flowing water; pure air; metal objects that have not been filed, shattered, or powdered; magical barriers; another creature’s body unless a talent specifically allows dust, bone, or corpse-grit manipulation. #### Created Sand Some talents create sand even where no Sand Source exists. Created sand is real for the duration of the effect, but it is cultivation-shaped and collapses into ordinary dust or harmless dry grit when the effect ends unless a talent says it remains. Created sand cannot be sold as trade goods, used as a permanent construction material, or used to create unlimited glass, rare minerals, or precious substances. #### Sand Terrain Sand Terrain is a Sand-specific terrain state. Unless a talent says otherwise, a 5-foot square of Sand Terrain has the following properties: It is Difficult Terrain for hostile creatures of your choice. A creature that enters the square for the first time on a turn or starts its turn there can be affected by some Sand talents you know. The square counts as a Sand Source for your Sand talents. Sand Terrain lasts for the duration of the talent that created it. A square can hold only one strength of Sand Terrain from you at a time: Shallow, Deep, or Storming. Shallow Sand Terrain is the default. It creates loose footing and provides enough grains for most Mortal talents. Deep Sand Terrain is unstable and dragging. A hostile creature that enters Deep Sand Terrain for the first time on a turn or starts its turn there treats the square as Difficult Terrain and cannot take the Dash action while it remains in that square unless it succeeds on a Strength or Dexterity saving throw, its choice, against your Cultivation Save DC. A creature that succeeds is immune to this Dash restriction from your Deep Sand Terrain until the start of its next turn. Storming Sand Terrain is filled with airborne grains. It is lightly obscured. Some talents can make it heavily obscured. #### Burial Buried is a Sand-specific state. A Buried creature is partially covered, pinned, or swallowed by sand, dust, grit, or glassy grain. Unless a talent says otherwise: the creature’s Speed is reduced by 10 feet; the creature cannot benefit from being invisible against creatures that can perceive the sand covering it; the creature has Disadvantage on Dexterity (Acrobatics) checks and Dexterity saving throws made to avoid being knocked Prone or moved by Sand talents; the creature can end the Buried state by using an Action to make a Strength (Athletics) or Dexterity (Acrobatics) check against your Cultivation Save DC. If a talent says a creature is Buried and Restrained, it suffers the Restrained condition while the Buried state lasts. Ending the Buried state ends that Restrained condition. Burial does not automatically suffocate a creature unless a talent explicitly says it blocks breathing. #### Scouring Scouring is grain-based abrasion. Scouring damage is usually Slashing damage, Bludgeoning damage, or Force damage if the sand is spiritually charged. Some glass talents deal Piercing damage. Scouring is not fire, acid, or necrotic damage unless a talent says otherwise. #### Glass At Foundation Realm and higher, some Sand talents create Glass effects. Glass is heated, fused, spiritually hardened, or pressure-shaped sand. Glass effects are still part of the Sand sphere. Glass talents may deal Piercing or Slashing damage, create fragile barriers, bind targets in cutting shells, or reflect light. They do not replace the Light, Fire, or Earth sphere. #### Sand Control Limit To keep the sphere manageable, you may maintain a number of separate non-instantaneous Sand effects equal to your Proficiency Bonus at one time, unless a talent or Domain says otherwise. A separate Sand effect is one talent or ability with its own duration, such as one Gather Sand area, one Sand Veil, one Glass Wall, or one Sand Servitor. If you create a new non-instantaneous Sand effect beyond this limit, choose one of your previous Sand effects to end. Instantaneous effects, damage, and permanent environmental consequences approved by the GM do not count against this limit. ### Base Sphere Abilities When you first gain the Sand sphere, you gain Gather Sand and Scouring Hand. You also gain one Mortal Realm Sand talent of your choice. #### Gather Sand Action Type: Action Factory Combat Bucket: action Factory Routing: combat_action_row Range: 60 feet Area: Up to two contiguous 5-foot squares Duration: 1 minute Cost: 0 CP if drawing from an existing Sand Source; 1 CP if creating sand where no Sand Source exists You call loose grains together, raise dust from dry ground, powder small mineral fragments, or conjure a controlled spill of cultivation-shaped sand. Choose up to two contiguous 5-foot squares within range. Those squares become Shallow Sand Terrain for the duration. As a Bonus Action on later turns, you may move one square of Sand Terrain created by this use up to 10 feet along a surface you can perceive. A square cannot move through a creature’s space unless a talent allows it. At CL 5, this creates up to four contiguous 5-foot squares. At CL 11, up to six. At CL 17, up to eight. #### Scouring Hand Action Type: Action Factory Combat Bucket: action Factory Routing: combat_action_row Range: 60 feet Target: One creature or unattended object within range and within 5 feet of a Sand Source or Sand Terrain Saving Throw: Dexterity Duration: Instantaneous Cost: 0 CP You lash a target with cutting grit, rising dust, or a snapping rope of sand. The target makes a Dexterity saving throw. On a failed save, it takes 1d8 Slashing damage and suffers one of the following minor effects of your choice: it cannot take Opportunity Attacks until the start of your next turn; its Speed is reduced by 10 feet until the start of your next turn; it has Disadvantage on the next Wisdom (Perception) check relying on sight it makes before the start of your next turn. On a successful save, the target takes half damage and suffers no minor effect. Damage increases to 2d8 at CL 5, 3d8 at CL 11, and 4d8 at CL 17. #### Sand Talent Tags Sand talents use the following tags. Terrain: Creates, modifies, moves, or strengthens Sand Terrain. Scour: Deals damage or applies abrasive penalties. Veil: Obscures sight, hides movement, creates mirage-like physical concealment, or disrupts perception. Burial: Covers, sinks, restrains, drags, or entombs. Glass: Fuses sand into cutting, reflective, or fragile structures. Desiccation: Dries, cracks, drains moisture, interrupts healing, or punishes water-dependent bodies. Dune-Step: Alters movement through sand, loose ground, or terrain you control. Realm Evolution: A core progression talent that changes how the sphere works at a new Realm. Domain: Creates a Core Formation battlefield court or domain. ### Mortal Realm Talents #### Dust Veil - Veil, Terrain Action Type: Bonus Action Factory Combat Bucket: bonus_action Factory Routing: combat_action_row Range: 60 feet Area: One Sand Terrain area you control Duration: Until the start of your next turn Cost: 0 CP You stir the surface of your sand into a choking veil. The chosen Sand Terrain becomes lightly obscured until the start of your next turn. A creature inside the area has Disadvantage on Wisdom (Perception) checks relying on sight. If the Sand Terrain is Storming Sand Terrain, you may instead make the area heavily obscured until the start of your next turn, but doing so ends the Storming state at the end of that duration. #### Grit in the Eyes - Scour, Veil Action Type: Special Trigger Canonical Action Type: Special Trigger Factory Combat Bucket: passive Timing Detail: When you use Scouring Hand Factory Routing: triggered_passive_modifier_row Target: The same target Saving Throw: Constitution Duration: Until the start of your next turn Cost: 0 CP If the target fails its Dexterity save against Scouring Hand, you may force it to make a Constitution saving throw. On a failed save, it is Blinded until the start of your next turn. A creature without eyes or comparable exposed sensory organs has Advantage on this saving throw. A creature that does not rely on sight may be immune at the GM’s discretion. #### Loose Footing - Terrain When a hostile creature enters Sand Terrain you control for the first time on a turn, you may use your Reaction to make the ground slip. The creature must succeed on a Dexterity saving throw or fall Prone. A creature that succeeds is immune to your Loose Footing until the start of its next turn. #### Dune Bank - Terrain Action Type: Reaction Factory Combat Bucket: reaction Factory Routing: combat_action_row Trigger: You or a creature within 5 feet of Sand Terrain you control is targeted by an attack roll Cost: 0 CP You raise a short bank of sand between the attack and its target. The target gains Half Cover against the triggering attack. The sand bank collapses immediately after the attack resolves. At CL 11, if the target is standing in Deep or Storming Sand Terrain you control, the target instead gains Three-Quarters Cover against the triggering attack. #### Sand Drag - Terrain, Burial Action Type: Action Factory Combat Bucket: action Factory Routing: combat_action_row Range: 60 feet Target: One creature standing on Sand Terrain you control Saving Throw: Strength or Dexterity, target’s choice Cost: 0 CP The sand grips a target’s ankles and drags. On a failed save, move the target up to 10 feet along the ground within contiguous Sand Terrain you control. This movement does not provoke Opportunity Attacks. If the movement ends in Deep Sand Terrain, the target is Buried until the start of your next turn. On a successful save, the target is not moved, but its Speed is reduced by 10 feet until the start of your next turn. #### Sand Shell - Terrain Action Type: Bonus Action Factory Combat Bucket: bonus_action Factory Routing: combat_action_row Range: Self Duration: 1 minute Cost: 1 CP You wrap your skin, clothing, or armor in a shifting shell of sand. For the duration, you gain Temporary HP equal to your Proficiency Bonus + your key ability modifier. While any of these Temporary HP remain, the first creature that hits you with a melee attack on each round takes Slashing damage equal to your Proficiency Bonus. The shell ends early if you are submerged in water, restrained in a sealed fluid medium, or lose all Temporary HP from the shell. #### Track-Speaking Sand - Veil Action Type: Action Factory Combat Bucket: action Factory Routing: combat_action_row Range: Self or one Sand Terrain area you touch Duration: Instantaneous Cost: 0 CP You read disturbances in sand, dust, loose soil, or powder. Choose one question about tracks, movement, or recent disturbance in the area: How many creatures crossed this area recently? Which direction did the most recent creature travel? Was a creature running, limping, carrying weight, dragging something, or hiding its steps? Was a heavy object moved through this area? Was cultivation, flight, teleportation, or incorporeal movement obviously involved? The GM answers truthfully based on available traces. This does not reveal identity, Path, Realm, exact stat block, or secret technique unless the evidence would clearly show it. #### Sand Step - Dune-Step You ignore Difficult Terrain created by sand, dust, gravel, or dry loose earth. In addition, while you are standing on Sand Terrain you control, Opportunity Attacks against you are made with Disadvantage. #### Dune Slide - Dune-Step Action Type: Bonus Action Factory Combat Bucket: bonus_action Factory Routing: combat_action_row Requirement: You are standing on Sand Terrain or loose dry ground Cost: 0 CP You slide on a controlled wave of grains. Move up to 10 feet without provoking Opportunity Attacks from creatures whose spaces are adjacent to Sand Terrain you control. This movement must remain along a surface. At CL 5, the movement increases to 15 feet. At CL 11, 20 feet. At CL 17, 30 feet. #### Abrading Ward - Scour Whenever a hostile creature starts its turn in Sand Terrain you control, you may deal Slashing damage to it equal to your Proficiency Bonus. A creature can take this damage from you only once per round. #### Hidden Cache of Grains - Terrain You can carry a small ritual gourd, sash pouch, sleeve-pocket, hollow anklet, paper talisman packet, or similar container of prepared sand. As long as you possess this cache, you always count as having a Sand Source for Mortal Realm Sand talents. If the cache is lost, destroyed, soaked, sealed away, or stolen, you can prepare a new one during a short or long rest using dry mineral material. This cache is not required for the sphere unless you take a drawback that says so. ### Foundation Realm Talents At Foundation Realm, Sand stops needing perfect environmental permission. The cultivator awakens Dune-Heart Sand: grains that remember command, crawl against gravity, rise from stone dust, and answer the breath. #### Dune-Heart Sand - Realm Evolution Prerequisite: CL 5+ Your Sand techniques become openly supernatural. You gain the following benefits: You may use Gather Sand without an existing Sand Source by spending 1 CP, even on worked floors, stone, rooftops, ships, or other surfaces that contain mineral dust or can bear conjured sand. Sand Terrain you create may climb low obstacles, flow up stairs, and pass through gaps at least 1 inch wide. You may move one Sand Terrain square you control up to 20 feet when you use Gather Sand’s Bonus Action movement. Your Sand Terrain can affect creatures with magical flight if grains can physically reach them, but it does not automatically ground them unless a talent says so. Your Sand talents count as magical or cultivation effects for overcoming resistance to nonmagical damage. Dune-Heart Sand still cannot pass through sealed Barriers, sealed containers, Total Cover without a route, or a creature’s intact body unless a talent says otherwise. #### Quicksand Gate - Burial, Terrain Prerequisite: CL 5+ Action Type: Action Factory Combat Bucket: action Factory Routing: combat_action_row Range: 60 feet Area: One 10-foot square of Sand Terrain you control Saving Throw: Strength Duration: 1 minute Cost: 1 CP You deepen controlled sand into a hungry gate. The area becomes Deep Sand Terrain for the duration. When a hostile creature starts its turn in the area or enters it for the first time on a turn, it must make a Strength saving throw. On a failed save, it is Buried until it escapes. If it was already Buried, it is Buried and Restrained until it escapes. A creature can use an Action to make a Strength (Athletics) or Dexterity (Acrobatics) check against your Cultivation Save DC, ending Buried and Restrained on a success. #### Sand Coffin - Burial Prerequisite: CL 5+ Action Type: Action Factory Combat Bucket: action Factory Routing: combat_action_row Range: 60 feet Target: One Buried creature in Sand Terrain you control Saving Throw: Strength or Constitution, target’s choice Duration: Until the end of your next turn Cost: 1 CP Sand closes around the target’s limbs, throat, or torso. On a failed save, the target is Restrained and cannot speak clearly until the end of your next turn. It cannot provide verbal components, mantras, roars, or other activation requirements that require clear breath or speech. On a successful save, the target is not Restrained, but it cannot take Reactions until the start of your next turn. This does not automatically suffocate the target. #### Sand Needle Volley - Scour, Glass Prerequisite: CL 5+ Action Type: Action Factory Combat Bucket: action Factory Routing: combat_action_row Range: 90 feet Target: Up to three creatures within range, each within 10 feet of Sand Terrain or a Sand Source Saving Throw: Dexterity Cost: 1 CP You harden grains into cutting darts. Each target makes a Dexterity saving throw. On a failed save, a target takes 2d8 Piercing damage and its Speed is reduced by 10 feet until the start of your next turn. On a successful save, it takes half damage and suffers no Speed reduction. Damage increases to 3d8 at CL 11 and 4d8 at CL 17. #### Glass Edge Scripture - Glass Prerequisite: CL 5+ Your Sand Scour talents may deal Slashing or Piercing damage, chosen each time you use the talent. In addition, when you deal Scouring damage to a creature that is Buried, you may cause glassy grains to cling to it. Until the start of your next turn, the first time the creature moves 5 feet or more, it takes Piercing damage equal to your Proficiency Bonus + your key ability modifier. #### Dune Wall - Terrain Prerequisite: CL 5+ Action Type: Action Factory Combat Bucket: action Factory Routing: combat_action_row Range: 60 feet Area: A straight line up to 30 feet long, 5 feet thick, and 10 feet high Duration: Concentration, up to 1 minute Cost: 1 CP You raise a dune wall of packed sand. The wall grants Three-Quarters Cover against attacks and effects that pass through it. The wall is not solid enough to block movement completely, but its spaces are Deep Sand Terrain. A creature moving through the wall must spend 4 feet of movement for every 1 foot moved. A Large or larger creature may force through a 5-foot section by using an Action and succeeding on a Strength (Athletics) check against your Cultivation Save DC. A section also collapses if it takes damage equal to 10 + your CL. #### Desert Skin Method - Desiccation Prerequisite: CL 5+ Action Type: Bonus Action Factory Combat Bucket: bonus_action Factory Routing: combat_action_row Duration: 1 minute Cost: 1 CP You dry your surface Qi and learn to shed heat, grit, and thirst. For the duration: you have Resistance to Fire damage caused by environmental heat, hot sand, or mundane flame; you have Advantage on saving throws against Exhaustion caused by heat, thirst, forced marches through desert, or dry environments; hostile Sand Terrain does not count as Difficult Terrain for you; your unarmed strikes and weapon attacks may leave harmless visible sand marks or dry cracked prints. This talent does not replace broad Fire resistance against magical fire unless the fire is clearly desert, sand, or heat-exposure based. #### Sand Mirror Mirage - Veil Prerequisite: CL 5+ Action Type: Bonus Action Factory Combat Bucket: bonus_action Factory Routing: combat_action_row Range: Self Duration: Until the start of your next turn Cost: 1 CP Heat shimmer and dust reflection blur your position. Until the start of your next turn, attack rolls against you have Disadvantage while you are within 5 feet of Sand Terrain you control or while you are in bright light, desert heat, furnace heat, or a visibly dusty environment. This is a physical mirage, not a mental illusion. A creature that does not rely on sight is immune. #### Sand Burrow Step - Dune-Step Prerequisite: CL 5+ Action Type: Bonus Action Factory Combat Bucket: bonus_action Factory Routing: combat_action_row Requirement: You are standing on Sand Terrain or loose earth Cost: 1 CP You sink into one patch of sand and emerge from another. Teleport up to 30 feet to an unoccupied space you can see that is also on Sand Terrain, loose earth, dust, gravel, or dry soil. This movement does not provoke Opportunity Attacks. You cannot pass through sealed Barriers, cross planar boundaries, or enter a space too small for your body. #### Thousand-Grain Grip - Burial Prerequisite: CL 5+ Action Type: Reaction Factory Combat Bucket: reaction Factory Routing: combat_action_row Trigger: A creature Buried by your Sand talent attempts to escape or move 5 feet or more Cost: 0 CP The grains tighten. The creature makes its escape check or relevant saving throw with Disadvantage. If it fails, it takes Slashing damage equal to your Proficiency Bonus + your key ability modifier. ### Core Formation Realm Talents At Core Formation, Sand becomes territory. The cultivator does not merely create hazards; they establish a desert court in which every step is a legal argument and every grain is a witness. #### Court of Ten Thousand Dunes - Domain Prerequisite: CL 11+ Action Type: Action Factory Combat Bucket: action Factory Routing: combat_action_row Range: Self Area: 30-foot Emanation Duration: 1 minute Cost: 3 CP; once per short or long rest You establish a domain of commanded sand, mirage heat, unstable dunes, and listening grains. For the duration, the area around you becomes your Court. The Court moves with you. Within the Court: ground spaces of your choice become Shallow Sand Terrain when they enter the Court; as a Bonus Action, you may change a number of Sand Terrain squares in the Court up to your Proficiency Bonus into Deep or Storming Sand Terrain until the start of your next turn; hostile creatures treat all Sand Terrain in the Court as Difficult Terrain; once on each of your turns, you may use Scouring Hand, Sand Drag, Dust Veil, or Dune Bank without spending an Action, Bonus Action, or Reaction; you know the location of any creature touching Sand Terrain in the Court unless it is protected by a stronger concealment, Void effect, or superior stealth technique; when a hostile creature falls Prone, becomes Buried, or fails a saving throw against your Sand talent in the Court, you may move one Sand Terrain square up to 20 feet. The Court does not create solid walls, block teleportation, prevent flight by itself, or suppress other Domains automatically. If two Domains contest the same area, use the campaign’s Domain conflict rules or an opposed Cultivation Check. #### Dune Sea Advance - Terrain, Dune-Step Prerequisite: CL 11+ Action Type: Bonus Action Factory Combat Bucket: bonus_action Factory Routing: combat_action_row Range: 90 feet Area: Up to six Sand Terrain squares you control Cost: 1 CP You command the dune-line to advance. Move each chosen Sand Terrain square up to 30 feet along surfaces you can perceive. A square may pass through a hostile creature’s space during this movement. The first time this movement passes through a hostile creature’s space on a turn, that creature must make a Strength saving throw. On a failed save, it is pushed 10 feet in the direction the sand moved and is Buried until the start of your next turn. On a successful save, it is not pushed but cannot take Opportunity Attacks until the start of your next turn. #### Glass Prison - Glass, Burial Prerequisite: CL 11+ Action Type: Action Factory Combat Bucket: action Factory Routing: combat_action_row Range: 60 feet Target: One Buried creature or one creature standing in Deep Sand Terrain you control Saving Throw: Dexterity Duration: Concentration, up to 1 minute Cost: 2 CP You fuse the surrounding grains into a cutting glass shell. On a failed save, the target is Restrained inside a fragile glass prison. While restrained this way, it has Half Cover, cannot move from its space, and takes Piercing damage equal to your CL the first time each turn it makes an attack, casts a technique with somatic or whole-body movement, or attempts to escape. The target or an adjacent creature can use an Action to attack the prison. The prison has AC equal to your Cultivation Save DC and Hit Points equal to 10 + your CL. If destroyed, the target is freed and takes Piercing damage equal to your Proficiency Bonus. On a successful save, the target is not restrained, but glass cuts reduce its Speed by 10 feet until the end of your next turn. #### Erosion Scripture - Scour, Desiccation Prerequisite: CL 11+ Action Type: Action Factory Combat Bucket: action Factory Routing: combat_action_row Range: 90 feet Target: One object, structure, Barrier surface, formation anchor, armor, shield, weapon, or construct touching Sand Terrain or a Sand Source Cost: 2 CP You command grains to grind the target’s edges, seams, joints, inscriptions, or surface Qi. Choose one effect: Object Wear: Deal 4d8 Slashing damage to an object or structure. This damage ignores resistance to nonmagical damage. Armor Abrasion: A creature wearing armor or bearing a shield must make a Constitution saving throw. On a failed save, its AC is reduced by 1 until the end of your next turn. This cannot reduce AC below 10 + Dexterity modifier unless the armor is broken or removed by other means. Anchor Scour: Make a Cultivation Check against a formation anchor, Barrier surface, or ongoing terrain effect. On a success, suppress one 5-foot section or one minor anchor benefit until the start of your next turn. Scene-defining structures, artifacts, major formations, and superior barriers may require an extended project or opposed Cultivation Check. #### Sand Clone Decoy - Veil Prerequisite: CL 11+ Action Type: Bonus Action Factory Combat Bucket: bonus_action Factory Routing: combat_action_row Range: 30 feet Duration: Until the start of your next turn Cost: 1 CP You raise a hollow sand silhouette that copies your posture for a heartbeat. Until the start of your next turn, the first attack roll against you that misses may instead strike the decoy. If the attack misses you by 5 or more, you may move up to 15 feet without provoking Opportunity Attacks, and the decoy collapses into Storming Sand Terrain in one 5-foot square. A creature with truesight, tremorsense, blindsight, or a superior perception technique may make a Wisdom saving throw against your Cultivation Save DC when it attacks you. On a success, it ignores this decoy. #### Devouring Dune Mouth - Burial Prerequisite: CL 11+ Action Type: Action Factory Combat Bucket: action Factory Routing: combat_action_row Range: 90 feet Area: 15-foot-radius area of Sand Terrain Saving Throw: Strength Duration: Concentration, up to 1 minute Cost: 3 CP A pit-like dune mouth opens and pulls creatures inward. The area becomes Deep Sand Terrain. When a hostile creature starts its turn in the area or enters it for the first time on a turn, it makes a Strength saving throw. On a failed save, it is pulled 10 feet toward the center and becomes Buried. If already Buried, it is Buried and Restrained. On a successful save, it is not pulled but its Speed is reduced by 10 feet until the start of its next turn. As a Bonus Action while the effect lasts, you may force each hostile Buried creature in the area to repeat the save. On a failure, it takes 3d8 Bludgeoning damage as the dune compresses. #### Sand Memory Witness - Veil Prerequisite: CL 11+ Action Type: Ritual Procedure Canonical Action Type: Ritual Procedure Factory Routing: procedure_ledger_not_combat_action Timing Detail: 10 minutes Range: Touch Target: One area of sand, dust, ash-like grain, powdered stone, or dry soil no larger than a 30-foot cube Duration: Instantaneous Cost: 1 CP You read the memory of disturbed grains. Ask up to three questions about events that physically disturbed the area within the last 24 hours. Examples: What creatures crossed here? What was carried, dragged, buried, or unearthed? Was blood spilled here? Was a body buried here? Did a formation, teleportation, flight, burrow, or Void technique disturb the grains? Which way did the strongest disturbance go? The answer appears as tactile impressions, heat traces, grain-flow diagrams, or brief sand silhouettes. This does not reveal private thoughts, secret names, unseen future events, or facts that left no physical trace. At CL 17, you may read up to the last 7 days. #### Glass Mirage Reflection - Glass, Veil Prerequisite: CL 11+ Action Type: Reaction Factory Combat Bucket: reaction Factory Routing: combat_action_row Trigger: A creature you can perceive targets you with an attack roll or single-target visible technique while you are within 5 feet of Sand Terrain or glass you created Cost: 2 CP You flash a mirror of fused sand and false angle. The triggering creature makes a Wisdom saving throw. On a failed save, the attack or technique targets a sand-glass reflection in an unoccupied space within 10 feet of you and automatically misses you. On a successful save, you gain Half Cover against the triggering effect. This does not redirect area effects, effects that do not require targeting, or Secret Inheritances unless the GM allows an opposed Cultivation Check. ### Nascent Soul Realm Talents At Nascent Soul, Sand becomes self. The cultivator is no longer merely surrounded by a desert; the desert recognizes them as a possible body. #### Sand-Sovereign Incarnation - Realm Evolution Prerequisite: CL 15+ Action Type: Bonus Action Factory Combat Bucket: bonus_action Factory Routing: combat_action_row Duration: 1 minute Cost: 5 CP; once per long rest You manifest as a sovereign of dunes, a storm-robed immortal, a glass-crowned desert monarch, a body of flowing grains, or a silent burial king. For the duration: you gain a Burrow Speed of 40 feet through sand, dust, dry soil, gravel, and loose earth; you may move through spaces occupied by Sand Terrain you control as though they were not Difficult Terrain; you have Resistance to Bludgeoning, Piercing, and Slashing damage from non-artifact weapons; you can move through a space as narrow as 1 inch wide if the entire route is filled with sand, dust, or loose grain and your carried equipment can transform with you; once on each of your turns, you may create up to two Shallow Sand Terrain squares within 60 feet without spending an Action; when a creature misses you with a melee attack, you may move 10 feet without provoking Opportunity Attacks and leave one Shallow Sand Terrain square in your previous space; your Sand Control Limit increases by your Proficiency Bonus. You cannot pass through sealed Barriers, airtight containers, solid stone, living bodies, or consecrated anti-transform zones without an appropriate talent, opposed Cultivation Check, or GM permission. #### Thousand-Mile Sandstorm Body - Veil, Scour Prerequisite: CL 15+ Action Type: Action Factory Combat Bucket: action Factory Routing: combat_action_row Range: Self Area: 30-foot Emanation Duration: Concentration, up to 1 minute Cost: 4 CP Your body becomes the eye of a controlled sandstorm. The area is Storming Sand Terrain and lightly obscured for creatures of your choice. Hostile creatures that start their turn in the area or enter it for the first time on a turn make a Constitution saving throw. On a failed save, a creature takes 4d8 Slashing damage and is Blinded until the start of its next turn. On a successful save, it takes half damage and is not Blinded. While the effect lasts, ranged weapon attacks that pass through the area are made with Disadvantage unless the attacker is you or a creature you designate. #### Burial of the Nameless Army - Burial, Domain Prerequisite: CL 15+ Action Type: Action Factory Combat Bucket: action Factory Routing: combat_action_row Range: 120 feet Area: 30-foot-radius area of Sand Terrain, loose earth, dust, or mineral ground Saving Throw: Strength Duration: Concentration, up to 1 minute Cost: 5 CP You command the battlefield to remember every army it has swallowed. Hostile creatures of your choice in the area make a Strength saving throw. On a failed save, a creature is Buried and Restrained. On a successful save, it is Buried until the start of your next turn. While the effect lasts, a hostile creature that starts its turn Buried in the area takes 3d8 Bludgeoning damage and cannot take Reactions until the start of its next turn. A creature can use an Action to make a Strength (Athletics) or Dexterity (Acrobatics) check against your Cultivation Save DC, ending Buried and Restrained on a success. A creature that succeeds may move up to half its Speed immediately as part of that Action. #### Glass Desert Judgment - Glass, Scour Prerequisite: CL 15+ Action Type: Action Factory Combat Bucket: action Factory Routing: combat_action_row Range: 120 feet Area: 20-foot-radius area of Sand Terrain Saving Throw: Dexterity Duration: Instantaneous, then 1 minute Cost: 4 CP You flash-fuse a field of sand into jagged glass and command it to bloom upward. Creatures in the area make a Dexterity saving throw. On a failed save, a creature takes 6d8 Piercing damage and is Restrained by glass until the end of your next turn. On a successful save, it takes half damage and is not Restrained. The area then becomes Glass Terrain for 1 minute. Glass Terrain is Difficult Terrain. A creature that moves more than 5 feet through Glass Terrain on a turn takes Piercing damage equal to your CL. A creature can take this damage only once per turn. Glass Terrain counts as Sand Terrain and a Sand Source for your Sand talents, but it cannot be moved by talents that move loose sand unless you first shatter it. #### Desert Drinks the River - Desiccation Prerequisite: CL 15+ Action Type: Action Factory Combat Bucket: action Factory Routing: combat_action_row Range: 120 feet Target: One creature, object, area of water, water-based effect, plant mass, ooze, or fluid-bodied creature Saving Throw: Constitution Cost: 4 CP You invoke the dry law of the desert. Choose one: Dry the Body: One creature makes a Constitution saving throw. On a failed save, it takes 5d8 Necrotic or Force damage, your choice, and cannot regain Hit Points until the start of your next turn. On a success, it takes half damage and healing it receives before the start of your next turn is halved. Break the Water: Make a Cultivation Check against one ongoing water, fog, mist, rain, slime, plant-growth, or fluid terrain effect. On a success, suppress a 20-foot-radius section until the start of your next turn. Desiccate the Object: One nonmagical plant, rope, paper, leather, wooden object, wet clay object, or similar moisture-dependent object becomes brittle. It takes 6d8 damage and has Vulnerability to the next Fire, Slashing, or Bludgeoning damage it takes before the end of your next turn. This talent does not broadly replace Water, Life, or Death. It is a dry-law interference technique. #### Erode the Path of Return - Scour, Veil Prerequisite: CL 15+ Action Type: Reaction Factory Combat Bucket: reaction Factory Routing: combat_action_row Trigger: A creature you can perceive teleports, burrows, turns invisible, or leaves your Sand Terrain by magical movement Range: 120 feet Cost: 3 CP You send grains into the departing line of motion. The triggering creature makes a Dexterity or Charisma saving throw, its choice. On a failed save, choose one: the movement fails and the triggering resource is spent; the creature moves only half the intended distance and appears Buried in the nearest legal Sand Terrain or loose ground along its route; the creature completes the movement, but you learn its destination direction and distance, and it leaves a visible trail of sand-marks until the end of your next turn. On a successful save, the movement succeeds, but the creature cannot benefit from being Invisible against you until the start of your next turn if any sand or dust can cling to it. Secret Inheritances, superior Space effects, and major escape artifacts may require an opposed Cultivation Check. ### Secret Sand Inheritance #### The Mountain Remembers It Is Dust Secret Sand Inheritance Prerequisite: Sand-Sovereign Incarnation, CL 17+, discovery of a desert-ending scripture, burial of a mountain oath, or inheritance from an ancient dune sovereign Action Type: Action Factory Combat Bucket: action Factory Routing: combat_action_row Range: 300 feet Area: One battlefield feature, formation section, structure, army-line, massive creature, or 60-foot-radius terrain area Duration: Instantaneous, then 1 minute Cost: 8 CP; once per week You speak the first erosion scripture: the law that every shape is temporary. Choose one legal target within range. The target must be a battlefield-scale physical feature, a structure, a terrain zone, a formation section with physical anchors, a siege engine, a wall, a bridge, a gate, a vehicle, a mass of troops, or one Huge or larger creature touching a surface. Pure ideas, souls, memories, laws, oaths, and nonphysical effects are not legal targets unless the GM treats them as having a physical anchor. Resolve one of the following modes. ##### Grind the Shape A structure, wall, gate, bridge, siege engine, vehicle, or formation anchor section takes 12d10 Force damage. This damage represents supernatural erosion and ignores resistance to nonmagical damage. If this reduces the target to 0 Hit Points or overcomes its threshold, it collapses into Sand Terrain under your control. If the target is a major formation, artifact-reinforced structure, city wall, sect gate, or scene-defining object, make an opposed Cultivation Check. On a success, suppress or breach one meaningful section for 1 minute instead of automatically destroying the whole target. ##### Bury the Line Choose a 60-foot-radius ground area. It becomes Deep and Storming Sand Terrain for 1 minute. Hostile creatures of your choice in the area make a Strength saving throw. On a failed save, a creature is Buried and Restrained for 1 minute. While restrained this way, it is also Blinded by sand unless it does not rely on sight. It may repeat the saving throw at the end of each of its turns, ending the effects on itself on a success. On a successful save, it is Buried until the start of your next turn and its Speed becomes 0 until the start of your next turn. ##### Erode the Giant Choose one Huge or larger creature touching a surface. It makes a Constitution saving throw. On a failed save, it takes 10d10 Force damage, loses any Burrow Speed or Climb Speed until the end of your next turn, cannot regain Hit Points until the end of your next turn, and falls Prone if it can be knocked Prone. On a successful save, it takes half damage and cannot regain Hit Points until the start of your next turn. ##### Claim the Desert For 1 minute, all ground in a 60-foot-radius area becomes your Sand Terrain. You decide whether each square is Shallow, Deep, or Storming whenever a creature starts its turn there. Your Sand Control Limit does not apply to this area for the duration. Once during each of your turns while the inheritance lasts, you may use Gather Sand, Scouring Hand, Sand Drag, Dune Bank, Dust Veil, or Quicksand Gate in the area without spending an Action, Bonus Action, Reaction, or CP. When the inheritance ends, created sand collapses into ordinary loose ground or remains as a changed battlefield feature if the GM rules the terrain was permanently altered. #### Secret Inheritance Limits The Mountain Remembers It Is Dust cannot automatically destroy artifacts, divine palaces, world-pillars, living gods, complete cities, permanent cosmic laws, sect-protecting grand formations, or narrative-scale fortresses. Such targets may be weakened, breached, delayed, exposed, or forced into a campaign objective rather than simply erased. ### Sand Drawbacks and Variant Scriptures A Sand drawback is an optional sphere-specific limitation that grants a bonus Sand talent or benefit while changing how Sand cultivation functions. Unless the GM says otherwise: choose at most one Sand drawback when first learning Sand or undergoing a major Sand initiation; Sand drawbacks are mutually exclusive unless stated otherwise; the drawback applies to all Sand talents you use; if a drawback grants a talent whose prerequisites you do not yet meet, you gain that talent when you meet them; if the drawback is retrained or removed, the bonus talent or benefit is lost. These drawbacks are Tianxia-specific cultivation limits inspired by drawback design, not imported Pathfinder casting drawbacks. #### Gourd-Bound Sand Scripture Your Sand cultivation requires a prepared vessel: gourd, jar, urn, sash-pouch, coffin-box, hourglass, prayer wheel, or sealed sleeve of ancestral sand. Drawback: If you do not possess or wear your prepared vessel, you cannot create sand where no Sand Source exists and cannot use talents with a CP cost greater than 0. If the vessel is broken, stolen, sealed, soaked, or sundered, ongoing Sand effects with durations longer than instantaneous end at the end of your next turn unless you recover or replace it. Benefit: Gain Hidden Cache of Grains and one additional Mortal Realm Sand talent. #### Dry-Basin Scripture You refuse false conjuration and cultivate only sand that has a physical basis. Drawback: You cannot use the 1 CP option of Gather Sand to create sand where no Sand Source exists. All your Sand talents must draw from an existing Sand Source, Sand Terrain, loose earth, dust, or powdered material. Benefit: When you use Gather Sand from an existing Sand Source, create one additional 5-foot square of Sand Terrain. At CL 11+, create two additional squares instead. #### Mercy of the Open Dune Your scripture forbids sealing the living beneath the earth. Drawback: You cannot make a living creature Buried and Restrained, cannot prevent a living creature from speaking through Sand Coffin, and cannot use Burial of the Nameless Army on living creatures. You may still Buried living creatures without Restrained. Benefit: Gain Dust Veil. When you use Dust Veil, one ally of your choice in the area may immediately move 5 feet without provoking Opportunity Attacks. #### Glass-Blood Scripture Your sand fuses too readily into cutting glass. Drawback: Whenever you create Sand Terrain by spending CP, choose one 5-foot square created by that effect to become hazardous glass. The first creature to enter that square before the start of your next turn, including you or an ally, takes Piercing damage equal to your Proficiency Bonus. You cannot suppress this damage. Benefit: Gain Glass Edge Scripture. Once per turn when you deal Sand sphere damage, you may change the damage type to Piercing or Slashing and add your key ability modifier to one damage roll. #### Wandering-Dune Scripture Your sand refuses to remain still. Drawback: Non-instantaneous Sand effects you create cannot remain in exactly the same area for more than 1 round unless they are part of a Domain or Secret Inheritance. At the start of each of your turns, move each such effect at least 5 feet if there is a legal space. If no legal movement is possible, the effect ends. Benefit: Gain Dune Slide. Once per round after moving one of your Sand Terrain squares, you may move 5 feet without provoking Opportunity Attacks. ### Path Synergies #### Body Refining - Desert-Hardened Frame A Body Refining Sand cultivator carries dunes in the stance and grit in the skin. When you are standing on Sand Terrain you control, you gain the following benefits: your Speed cannot be reduced by Sand Terrain; you have Advantage on Strength saving throws against being moved or knocked Prone by creatures also touching Sand Terrain you control; once per turn when a hostile creature takes Scouring damage from your Sand talent within 5 feet of you, gain Temporary HP equal to your Proficiency Bonus. You may use Constitution as your Sand key ability for saving throw DCs if Sand is learned through Body Refining. #### Qi Cultivation - Grain-Command Circulation A Qi Cultivation Sand practitioner refines command through countless grains. Once per turn when you spend CP on a Sand talent, choose one: move one Sand Terrain square you control up to 10 feet; increase the range of that Sand talent by 30 feet; change one Shallow Sand Terrain square affected by the talent into Deep or Storming Sand Terrain until the start of your next turn; reduce the CP cost of one Sand Forged Technique you use this turn by 1, minimum 1 CP. You may use Intelligence or Charisma as your Sand key ability for saving throw DCs if Sand is learned through Qi Cultivation. #### Spirit Awakening - Desert Memory Soul A Spirit Awakening Sand cultivator hears what the grains remember. While touching Sand Terrain, dust, loose earth, or dry soil, you may use Wisdom as your Sand key ability. In addition: when a creature enters Sand Terrain you control within 60 feet, you know whether it is walking, flying, burrowing, incorporeal, or carried by a technique; once per round when a hostile creature fails a saving throw against your Sand talent, you may learn whether it is Bloodied, whether it is resistant to Slashing or Piercing damage, or whether it is currently protected by an ongoing terrain, movement, or concealment effect; your Track-Speaking Sand and Sand Memory Witness can detect obvious spiritual disturbances if they physically disturbed the grains. This does not reveal private thoughts, complete stat blocks, hidden identities, or secret techniques. ### Cultivation Insights #### Sand-Born Footwork Prerequisite: Sand sphere, CL 4+ You gain the following benefits: Sand Terrain you create is never Difficult Terrain for you. Once per short or long rest, when a creature misses you with an Opportunity Attack, you may create one Shallow Sand Terrain square in a space adjacent to you. You have Advantage on Dexterity (Stealth) checks made to hide in dusty, sandy, desert, ruin, or dry-earth environments. #### Gourd of the First Dune Prerequisite: Sand sphere, Hidden Cache of Grains or Gourd-Bound Sand Scripture, CL 6+ Your prepared sand cache becomes a minor cultivation vessel. Once per short or long rest, you may use Gather Sand without spending CP even if no Sand Source exists. If you already could do so, you instead create two additional 5-foot squares of Sand Terrain with that use. If your vessel is lost or broken, recreating it requires a long rest and access to dry mineral material. #### Glass-Cutting Palm Prerequisite: Sand sphere, Glass Edge Scripture, CL 8+ When you hit a creature with an unarmed strike or melee weapon attack while both you and the target are touching Sand Terrain or glass you created, you may deal additional Piercing damage equal to your Proficiency Bonus. You may use this benefit once per turn. At CL 15+, if the target is Buried, the additional damage becomes equal to your Proficiency Bonus + your key ability modifier. #### Dune Court Architect Prerequisite: Sand sphere, Court of Ten Thousand Dunes, CL 12+ When you design a Formation, battlefield, desert fortress, burial pit, glass garden, caravan route, training ground, or ambush site, you may use one Sand technique as the conceptual seed. The project may include one Sand-themed benefit, such as: warning tracks; collapsing dunes; sand-hidden vault doors; glass alarm chimes; concealed burial traps; heat-mirage screens; quicksand corridors; sand-memory witness zones. This Insight does not create the project automatically. It requires materials, time, anchors, labor, maintenance, and vulnerabilities appropriate to the campaign’s project rules. #### Dune-Sovereign’s Mercy Prerequisite: Sand sphere, Sand-Sovereign Incarnation, CL 15+ When you use a Sand Burial talent, you may choose any number of creatures affected by it to be preserved rather than crushed. A preserved creature does not take Scouring or compression damage from that talent, has Advantage on death saving throws while Buried by you, and can breathe through a narrow thread of sand for up to 1 minute. In addition, once per long rest when you would be reduced to 0 Hit Points while touching Sand Terrain you control, you may fall apart into sand and re-form in an unoccupied Sand Terrain square within 30 feet. You instead drop to 1 Hit Point. You cannot use this benefit if you are Incapacitated before the damage resolves, sealed in a Barrier that blocks Sand movement, or prevented from transforming.

Describe the method: throw grit into its eyes, knot a sleeve, stamp on a foot, box its ears, loosen a belt, hook a leg, slap a talisman across its vision, overturn a stool beneath it, or use another plausible tactic.
Make a Scoundrel Check against the target.
Success: Choose one appropriate result:
Eyes Spoiled. The target has the Blinded condition until the start of your next turn.
Ears Ringing. The target has the Deafened condition until the start of your next turn.
Tangled Footwork. Halve the target’s Speed until the start of your next turn.
Low Sweep. The target has the Prone condition.
Jammed Guard. The target cannot take Reactions until the start of your next turn.
Open the Guard. Apply Exploited Opening.
The GM may approve a comparable effect when the description, anatomy, and surroundings support it. A base Dirty Trick should not inflict a stronger condition than those listed above.
A creature without the relevant anatomy or vulnerability is immune to an inappropriate effect.
If a talent extends a physical Dirty Trick beyond the start of your next turn, the target or an adjacent creature can normally take the Utilize action to end that physical hindrance early.

automatic_base_abilities.effect:
#### STEAL
Action Type: Action
Factory Combat Bucket: action
Factory Routing: combat_action_row
Range: Natural reach
Cost: None
Choose one accessible object. Attempt to take it, reposition it, or plant one Tiny object in an accessible location.
##### Aware Target
Make a Scoundrel Check against the creature.
##### Unaware Target
Make a Dexterity (Sleight of Hand) check against the target’s Passive Perception.
##### Difficult Object
Make your check with Disadvantage if the object is securely fastened, worn tightly, held in two hands, or similarly difficult to remove.
##### Success
Choose one appropriate result:
take the object into a free hand;
cause the object to fall into an unoccupied space within your reach;
reposition the object to another accessible location on the same target;
plant one Tiny object in an accessible location on the target.
You may use Steal to remove an object from a creature’s hand as a local Scoundrel disarm rule.
Steal does not automatically activate, identify, attune to, or safely handle the object.
