It favors travel, battlefield pins, and warning signs. **Buried-Light Eye.** Seeing source qi as shine, color, dust, pressure, or shadow in mineral matter. **Sealstone Scholarship.** Reading old prisons, coffin-stones, source-preserved beings, and inscriptions without automatically becoming a Formation master or Talisman writer. **Stone-Bone Body Methods.** Body Refining Source through soles, ribs, teeth, marrow, scars, armor plates, held stone tokens, and impact. This is not remote geomancy unless a feature allows projection. ## Secret Source Inheritances Secret Source inheritances are not common talents. The consequence should matter in the campaign: sour water, cracked walls, hostile local spirits, poisoned source dust, sect investigation, or tribulation complications. ## Source Limitations and Optional Variant Scriptures These are optional Source scriptures. They borrow the useful design idea of a drawback framework—clear method, clear weakness, and clear table expectations—but they are written for Tianxia. They do not use spell-point drawback accounting, boon math, or generic casting-tradition rules. A GM may grant a variant as part of a sect lineage, Foundation, manual, Secret inheritance, item initiation, or character history. A variant should simplify identity, not create a bookkeeping tax. ### Stone-Bone Source Body Common Path: Body Refining. You learn to make soles, bones, teeth, scars, armor plates, and held stones carry Source pressure. Restriction: - You have Disadvantage on Source checks made to force open, rush, gamble, or deliberately destabilize a sealed mineral object for gain. - This limit does not apply when opening the seal is necessary to rescue a creature, end an immediate hazard, or escape a prison. ### Bright Source Method Common Path: Qi Cultivation or Spirit Awakening. You perceive source as buried light. Your Source Pulse deals radiant damage, and your Source Reading often appears as dust-light, jade shine, mineral halo, star-glints, or pressure shining under stone. Benefit: - This is the default safe expression of Source Pulse. - When your Source Pulse damages an undead, construct, or creature sustained by a mineral seal, corpse-stone, or source prison, you may change the damage type to force for that attack if the GM agrees the target is being held together by a seal or mineral vessel. Restriction: - Your Source effects are rarely subtle. In dim light or darkness, creatures within 30 feet usually notice that source-light moved unless you have cover, concealment, or a specific stealth feature. ### Heavy Vein Method Common Path: Body Refining or Earth-adjacent Qi Cultivation. You perceive source as pressure rather than light. Benefit: - When you learn this variant, your Source Pulse deals bludgeoning damage instead of radiant damage. - Once per turn when your Source Pulse hits a creature touching a mineral surface and deals bludgeoning damage through this variant, the Speed reduction from Source Pulse becomes 15 feet instead of 10 feet. Restriction: - You cannot freely switch Source Pulse back to radiant damage during combat unless a talent, item, scripture, or GM ruling allows it. - Creatures not touching a mineral surface are not legal targets for the Speed reduction unless another feature makes them legal Source Pulse targets. ### Blood-Dust Source Scripture Common Path: forbidden mine sects, desperate tomb breakers, and corpse-vein heresies. This is a Forbidden variant. It uses blood, corpse dust, bone powder, or living pain as a source medium. Benefit: - Once per short or long rest, when you use Source Lock, Closing the Forbidden Door, Living Stone Prison, or World-Nail Source Seal, you may increase the Source Save DC by 1. If the talent creates a breakable shell, you may instead increase the damage required to break that shell by 1. Restriction: - Each use marks the scene with visible forbidden residue: blood-dust, corpse-stain, sour source-light, ancestral cold, or a similar sign. - The GM may attach social, sect, karmic, ghost, land-corruption, or tribulation consequences. - This variant is never ordinary character-creation content. #### Stone Greed Some Source students become unable to leave a promising stone unopened. This should usually be handled as roleplay, NPC pressure, sect reputation, lost time, poor bargains, or temptation scenes rather than forced player behavior. #### Dry Ground Limitation A stricter campaign may rule that many Source combat talents fail on ships, wooden floors, deep snow, open air, or places cut off from earth. This is a terrain limitation, not a character flaw. ## Path Synergies ### Body Refining - Stone-Bone Source Body Requires the Stone-Bone Source Body Insight or equivalent access unless Source was learned through the optional Stone-Bone Source Body variant. When you use Source through Body Refining: - use Constitution as your Source key ability; - use Stamina instead of CP for legal body-bound Source talents; - your body, worn armor, held weapon, held tool, held source token, and touched mineral surfaces count as legal origins for body-bound Source talents; - you may use Source Reading through touch, breath, stance, pressure, bite marks, scar sensation, or held mineral samples; - you cannot use Projected talents unless you gain explicit projection permission. Once per short rest, when Grounded Guard reduces damage to 0, regain Stamina equal to your Proficiency Bonus if you are below half your maximum Stamina. ### Qi Cultivation - Refined Source Circulation Qi Cultivators are the most common full Source users. When you use Source through Qi Cultivation: - use Intelligence or Charisma as your Source key ability; - use Qi for Source talents; - you may use the listed range of Projected Source talents unless the talent says otherwise; - once per turn when you use Source Pulse, Source Seal, Source Lock, Earth-Line Snare, or a Source talent that modifies one of them, reduce the CP cost by 1, minimum 0. This cost reduction cannot reduce the cost of Secret or Forbidden talents unless that talent says so. ### Spirit Awakening - Buried-Omen Soul Spirit Source treats stone as memory, warning, and old witness. When you use Source through Spirit Awakening: - use Wisdom as your Source key ability; - use Resonance for Source talents; - your Source Reading may identify whether a mineral seal or source hazard feels protective, hungry, wounded, ancestral, resentful, empty, unusually blank, masked, or unable to give an impression, if that impression is present; - once per round when you succeed on a saving throw against a source hazard, cursed stone, opened seal, or sealed mineral object the GM has established contains or restrains a creature, or stone-borne spiritual effect, gain Temporary Hit Points equal to your Proficiency Bonus. This does not read private thoughts. It reads impressions carried by source, stone, and seal. ## Optional Mechanical Insights ### Stone-Bone Source Body Prerequisite: Body Refining, CL 4+, Constitution 15+ You may learn Source as a Body Refining cultivator. Use Constitution as your Source key ability. You may spend Stamina instead of CP on Source talents that originate from your body, worn armor, held weapon, held tool, held source token, a creature or object you touch, your own space, or a mineral surface you are standing on or touching. You gain the Body Refining - Stone-Bone Source Body synergy. ### External Vein Projection Prerequisite: Body Refining, Source sphere, Stone-Bone Source Body, CL 6+ Your body-bound Source has begun to travel through contact lines. You may use non-Domain Source talents with the Projected tag if the effect begins from your body, a stomp, a strike, a held object, a thrown source token, a worn armor plate, or a surface connected to your footing. The maximum range for those Projected talents is 30 feet unless the talent's range is shorter. At CL 10+, the maximum range becomes 60 feet for Foundation talents only. You still cannot create Source effects in open air, through total cover, or on surfaces you cannot perceive unless a feature says otherwise. ### Seal-Reader Adept Prerequisite: Source sphere, Seal-Tapping Hand or Sealstone Reader, CL 4+ When Source Reading reveals a seal, mark, prison, or preservation effect, you may ask one additional question from the following list: what kind of target it protects or contains, whether opening it is likely to harm nearby creatures, whether the seal is older than a century, or whether the seal was recently disturbed. This does not reveal command words, full formulae, formation schematics, or names. ### Stone-Gambler Nerve Prerequisite: Source sphere, Safe Cut or Source Appraiser, CL 4+ Once per short or long rest, when you make a Source check to appraise, cut, open, or safely handle an existing mineral object, you may add 1d4 to the roll after seeing the d20 but before the GM announces the result. This does not create better contents. ### Vein-Seal Adept Prerequisite: Source sphere, Source Lock, CL 8+ When you use Source Lock, choose one benefit: - increase the duration to 10 minutes; - increase the size limit to a 10-foot section of mineral surface; - or allow the sealed target to include one mundane metal lock, hinge, handle, or latch attached to the same mineral object. This still does not affect creatures, worn or carried items, active Formations, talisman seals, soul seals, oath seals, or artifacts. ### Pulse-and-Seal Circuit Prerequisite: Source sphere, Source Circuit, CL 10+ Once per turn when your Source Pulse hits a target touching a mineral surface, you may place a Warning Seal or Reading Seal on that target's space without spending an Action. The seal lasts until the start of your next turn and follows the Source Seal limit. This does not place a seal on the creature. ### Gentle Cutter Doctrine Prerequisite: Source sphere, Safe Cut, CL 6+ When Safe Cut prevents a failure by 5 or less from ruining an existing material, you may also prevent one harmless cosmetic break, dust discharge, surface crack, or obvious waste mark caused by the failed attempt. This does not prevent damage, traps, curses, sealed creature release, or failure consequences unrelated to material handling. ## Source Synergies **Earth.** Earth provides terrain, foundation, burden, anchoring, walls, roads, and ground command. Source reads veins within terrain, borrows short pressure, and seals mineral objects. Earth can make the battlefield; Source can tell whether the battlefield is sleeping on a prison. **Metal and Blacksmith.** Metal and Blacksmith refine ore into tools, armor, weapons, and artifacts. Source finds and judges spiritually active ore or sealed mineral risk. Source does not forge. **Formations.** Formations build strategic arrays and site-grade structures. Source identifies vein pressure and short source locks. Source can provide clues or stabilization but does not replace Formation construction. **Talismans.** Talismans write formulae and stored techniques. Source can read mineral seals and place short vein marks. Source does not write talisman formulae. **The Hidden Eye and Fate.** These spheres reveal hidden truth or destiny. Source reveals what stone, vein, and seal can plausibly carry. Source is grounded and material, not universal divination. **Space and Void.** Space moves through distance; Void denies or hollows presence. Source may briefly prevent teleportation through a grounded seal, but it does not become the teleportation or anti-existence sphere. **Equipment.** Equipment pairs with Body Refining Source through armor plates, mine harnesses, helmets, boots, and carried source tokens. ## Story Prompts **The Mountain Has a Pulse.** You learned that stone is not dead; it merely speaks slowly. **Do Not Open Every Bright Thing.** You survived because you treated treasure as a possible prison. **The Vein Points Both Ways.** A source line can lead to wealth, danger, ancestry, or a hungry sealed thing. **Heaven Buries Its Mistakes.** Some mineral treasures are not gifts. They are locks. **A Good Cut Is Mercy.** The cleanest source reader takes what is present without wounding the land more than necessary. **The Mine Remembers Blood.** Power taken from corpse, curse, or sacrifice never stays quiet forever. **Your Bones Became the Compass.** A Body Refiner of Source learns that direction can be felt as pressure in the skeleton. ## Automation Notes - Source Reading should import as a utility action with Action and 10-minute modes. - Source Pulse should import as the base combat action: Action, 60 feet, one eligible target, Source attack roll, radiant damage by default, Realm scaling. - Source Seal should import as a utility action with four modes: Warning Seal, Stillness Seal, Reading Seal, and Fetter Seal. - Source seals should import as temporary states with explicit target, option, duration, active-seal limit, trigger condition, and cleanup; they are not permanent formation objects. - Mineral Surface should import as an eligibility condition, not a tracked resource counter. - Projected should import as a tag checked against Body Refining variant permissions. - Dragon-Vein Glimpse and Earth Remembers the Cut require GM adjudication and should produce prompts rather than deterministic treasure output. - Forbidden talents should be tagged GM-permission and should not be offered in ordinary character creation unless campaign access is explicitly enabled. - Source Appraiser, Safe Cut, Stone-Within-Stone, and Gentle Cutter Doctrine should never generate loot. They only evaluate or protect against existing objects. - Qi Types: source qi, buried-light qi, vein qi, dragon-vein qi, quarry qi, spirit-stone qi, jade qi, mineral qi, sealed-stone qi, earth-pulse qi.

resolved_automatic_base_abilities.effect:
### Source Reading
Source Reading is the basic act of inspecting stone, earth, ore, jade, crystal, a mine face, a source object, a sealed stone, or a mineral surface.
As an Action, you may inspect one unattended mineral object, one visible seal on a mineral object, or one 5-foot section of mineral surface within reach. The GM tells you whether it has obvious active qi, obvious instability, obvious artificial sealing, obvious spiritual contamination, or obvious recent disturbance.
By spending 10 minutes, you may make a Source check against a DC set by the GM to learn one useful fact about one mineral object, chamber, vein, quarry face, ruin wall, mine tunnel, source deposit, sealed stone, or similar feature you can examine. Examples include whether it is natural or worked, whether it contains active source qi, whether it is unstable, whether it has been cut recently, whether a stronger vein lies in a visible direction, whether a seal is present, whether opening it is obviously dangerous, or whether a seal is meant to contain, preserve, warn, lock, hide, or punish.
Source Reading does not reveal exact treasure value, full maps, hidden creatures behind total cover, secret doors automatically, command words, sealed creature identities, or the full rules of another sphere. It gives one grounded fact through stone and source.

### Source Pulse
Action Type: Action
Canonical Action Type: Action
Factory Combat Bucket: action
Factory Routing: combat_action
Range: 60 feet
Target: One creature touching a mineral surface, or one unattended mineral object
Cost: 0
Make a Source attack roll against the target. On a hit against a creature, the target takes 1d8 radiant damage as buried source-light snaps through the ground, wall, crystal, jade, ore, or stone under it, and its Speed is reduced by 10 feet until the start of your next turn. On a hit against an unattended object, the object takes the damage only.
The damage becomes 2d8 at Foundation Realm, 3d8 at Core Formation Realm, and 4d8 at Nascent Soul Realm.
The Speed reduction from Source Pulse does not stack with itself. Source Pulse cannot target a creature that is not touching an eligible mineral surface unless another talent, variant, item, or GM ruling says otherwise. Source Pulse does not damage the ground, create difficult terrain, open seals, or break objects beyond its listed damage unless a talent says it does.

resolved_automatic_base_abilities.effect:
### Source Seal
Action Type: Action
Canonical Action Type: Action
Factory Combat Bucket: action
Factory Routing: combat_action
Range: Touch
Target: One unattended mineral object no larger than a 5-foot cube, one closed mineral container, one closed stone or metal door, one visible seal on a mineral object, or one 5-foot section of mineral surface
Duration: 1 minute
Cost: 0
You place a faint source seal on the target. The seal is visible as dust-light, pressure lines, mineral frost, dull jade script, or another obvious Source mark unless a talent says otherwise.
Choose one basic effect:
- **Warning Seal.** If the target is opened, broken, moved, or spiritually disturbed while you are within 60 feet, you know that the seal was disturbed.
- **Stillness Seal.** The target has Advantage on the next saving throw or check it makes before the seal ends to avoid cracking, discharging, collapsing, or releasing stored pressure. If the target does not normally make such a roll, this has no effect.
- **Reading Seal.** The next Source Reading check you make against the target before the seal ends has Advantage.
- **Fetter Seal.** This option can be placed only on a 5-foot section of mineral surface. The first time a creature of your choice enters that section or starts its turn there before the seal ends, you may end the seal. If you do, that creature's Speed is reduced by 10 feet until the end of that turn.
Source Seal does not lock the target, prevent movement except through Fetter Seal, restrain a creature, suppress a magic item, dispel a talisman, overwrite a Formation, prevent teleportation, or create a permanent mark. Talents create stronger seals by modifying or replacing this basic effect.
You can maintain a number of active Source Seals equal to your Proficiency Bonus. If you create another Source Seal beyond this limit, choose one existing Source Seal you created to end.

If you do, that creature's Speed is reduced by 10 feet until the end of that turn.

Tag: Fold Art.
Action Type: Bonus Action
Factory Combat Bucket: bonus_action
Factory Routing: combat_action_row
Range: Self.
Cost: 1 CP.
Teleport up to 20 feet to an unoccupied space you can see.
You may bring worn and carried equipment.
Fold Step does not provoke Opportunity Attacks because you do not move through the intervening spaces.
Fold Step cannot pass through Dimensional Lock, a sealed formation, a closed spatial boundary, or a stronger Space effect.
Scaling:
Fold Step does not gain automatic range from CL. Its ordinary range improves through Extended Fold and similar explicit talents. This keeps the base technique reliable while making investment matter.
Ordinary Cap: Unless a higher-Realm talent, anchor, Domain, or variant explicitly says otherwise, ordinary unassisted Fold Step cannot exceed 50 feet. Fifty feet of uninterrupted teleportation with no path drawback is already a powerful battlefield movement tool.
Fold Step is a battlefield step, not long-distance travel magic.

### Base Ability - Spatial Awareness
Tag: Anchor Art.
Action Type: Multi-Mode
Canonical Action Type: Multi-Mode
Factory Combat Bucket: split_required
Split Candidate Buckets: action, passive
Timing Detail: Passive and Action
Factory Routing: split_modes_before_character_action_programming
Split Review Decision: split_required_distinct_combat_buckets
Recommended Factory Realization: modes=PASSIVE_SPATIAL_AWARENESS->passive, ACTION_ACTIVE_INSPECTION->action
Range: 60 feet.
Cost: 0 CP for passive awareness; 1 CP to inspect actively.
Passive Effect: You sense obvious spatial disturbances within range. You know when a creature you can perceive teleports, opens a portal, enters or exits a pocket space, uses extradimensional storage, crosses a planar boundary, or forces a space wider or narrower than it should be.
Active Inspection: As an Action, spend 1 CP and choose one creature, object, doorway, area, or visible spatial effect within range. Make a Cultivation Check against the effect’s creator or against a DC set by rarity and concealment.
On a success, learn up to two of the following:
whether the target is spatially sealed;
whether the target has teleported within the last hour;
whether the target carries extradimensional storage;
whether the target is linked to an anchor;
whether a doorway or surface hides a pocket space;
whether a barrier blocks teleportation;
the approximate CL of the spatial effect;
whether the disturbance is stable, decaying, trapped, or contested.
Spatial Awareness does not reveal secret doors unless they are spatially distorted, and it does not identify ordinary locks.

spheres.full_exact_source_text: # Sphere of Space Qi Expression: Primary — Space Qi; Supporting — Distance Qi, Void Qi, Direction Qi, Boundary Qi. “Near and far are customs. The world repeats them until a space cultivator teaches it hesitation.” ## Sphere Identity Space is the cultivation of distance, openings, boundaries, folded roads, hidden interiors, dimensional seals, short steps through emptiness, and the dangerous art of refusing to cross the space between two points. In Tianxia, Space is powerful because it changes the battlefield’s assumptions. A cultivator who can stand where they were not, seal an enemy’s escape, fold a corridor into a sleeve, or turn a room into a maze of near and far is feared even when they never throw a single blast. But Space is not ordinary long-range teleportation. True teleportation - vanishing from one province and arriving in another by intent alone - belongs to Immortal-level inheritances, lost celestial arrays, imperial-grade treasures, or epic post-20 play. A mortal or Foundation space cultivator blinks across a courtyard, slips past a blade, hides objects in folded sleeves, locks doors that do not exist, and opens brief gates between places already visible or prepared. A novice steps three paces without crossing the ground. An adept folds a battlefield until enemies cannot trust distance. A master builds a sect around anchors, gates, pockets, and seals. An immortal ignores the question of where. ### Space Access Sphere Type: Restricted Power Sphere. Primary Path: Qi Cultivation. Secondary Path: Spirit Awakening. Rare Body Practice: Body Refining through the Spatial Meridian Body Insight. Default Resource: CP. Key Ability: Qi Cultivation: Intelligence or Charisma, chosen by the Qi Path. Spirit Awakening: Wisdom, if the cultivator has legal access. Body Refining: Constitution, only through Spatial Meridian Body or a similar initiation. Common Users: Qi cultivators who specialize in folds, gates, storage, barriers, and spatial law. Spirit cultivators who move through liminal boundaries, astral seams, and soul-adjacent distance. Rare Body Refiners who temper their meridians until their own body can survive short spatial displacement. Space is restricted because careless use kills people, tears rooms open, misplaces limbs, collapses stored goods, or attracts things that live between places. ### The Hard Teleportation Rule Space cultivators can teleport often, but ordinary teleportation remains local. Unless a talent explicitly says otherwise: Space teleportation must end in an unoccupied space you can see. A teleport cannot pass through a spatial seal, dimensional lock, sealed formation, closed Domain boundary, or stronger opposing spatial law. A teleport cannot carry unwilling creatures. A teleport cannot enter a space too small to safely hold the traveler. A teleport cannot enter an unknown room merely because the cultivator knows it exists. A teleport cannot cross planes, realms, or sealed pocket spaces. A teleport cannot target a destination by memory alone. A failed teleport does not spend CP unless the failure was caused by an enemy’s contesting technique, a trap, a hidden seal, or a deliberate risk chosen by the user. True Teleport is defined as instant travel to a distant location by name, memory, map, sympathetic item, or spiritual impression without line of sight and without a prepared visible gate. True Teleport is not part of normal Mortal, Foundation, Core Formation, or Nascent Soul Space sphere play. It appears only in the Immortal and Epic Space section of this draft. ### What Space Covers Space governs: short-range teleportation; visible blinks; swapping positions; local portals; folded corridors; spatial storage; pocket chambers; dimensional locks; portal suppression; folded distance; expanded or compressed rooms; spatial barriers; exile into sealed pocket spaces; spatial perception; anchor networks; travel through prepared gates; battlefield Domains of near and far. Space does not automatically govern: gravitational pull; weight, falling, or local down; direct invisible force; time travel; prophecy or fate; astral projection by itself; general stealth; illusions of location; summoning creatures from elsewhere; unlimited teleportation; planar travel without special high-Realm techniques. Overlap guidance: Force creates barriers, impacts, and invisible pressure. Space changes distance, openings, adjacency, and boundaries. Gravity changes weight, falling, and attraction. Space changes where a creature may stand. Void denies, erases, hollows, or cuts off presence. Space folds, opens, seals, or displaces presence. Stars provides navigation and stellar anchoring. Space provides the gate or folded road, but Stars may help aim it. Formations build stable infrastructure. Space may create a gate, but a sect-scale travel network usually requires Formations. Illusion deceives perception of where things are. Space actually changes the relationship between locations. ### Space Tags Space talents may use these tags. Fold Art: A short-range teleport, blink, swap, displacement, or folded step. Gate Art: A temporary portal, doorway, corridor, or linked opening. Pocket Art: A folded interior, storage space, sanctuary, or sealed chamber. Seal Art: A dimensional lock, anchor, anti-teleportation ward, or boundary restriction. Edge Art: A cutting or attacking technique that harms by misaligning space. Anchor Art: A technique that marks a location, object, creature, or path for later spatial use. Domain Art: A Core Formation or higher technique that changes the local spatial rules of an area. Forbidden Art: A technique that risks exile, void exposure, spatial backlash, or permanent misplacement. ### Space Terminology Teleportation: Instant relocation without crossing the intervening distance. In this sphere, ordinary teleportation is short-range and visible unless a talent says otherwise. Blink: A short teleport normally within sight and battlefield scale. Fold: A temporary shortening of distance. A fold may let a creature move farther, attack oddly, or travel quickly along a route without being true long-distance teleportation. Gate: A linked opening between two nearby or prepared points. A gate may allow multiple creatures to pass, but it is visible, contestable, and normally limited by range or anchors. Spatial Anchor: A prepared point, talisman, inscription, room, doorway, mirror, threshold, gate-stone, or ritual mark that supports later Space techniques. Anchors allow longer range than raw line-of-sight blinking, but they do not create true teleport by themselves. Dimensional Lock: A spatial seal that blocks teleportation, portals, extradimensional travel, pocket entry, and similar effects. Spatial Storage: A folded space used to store objects. Ordinary spatial storage is not safe for living creatures. Pocket Space: A folded chamber that can hold creatures, air, and time for a limited duration. Pocket spaces are risky and cannot be nested casually. Invalid Destination: A destination that is occupied, unseen when sight is required, sealed, too small, outside the technique’s range, or blocked by stronger spatial law. Spatial Backlash: Damage or narrative consequence caused by forcing space through a seal, contesting stronger law, entering an invalid destination deliberately, or using forbidden techniques. ### Learning Space When you first learn the Sphere of Space, you gain Fold Step and learn one Space talent for which you meet the prerequisites. Most Space cultivators begin with Fold Step, Spatial Awareness, Spatial Storage, or Dimensional Seal. If you are a Body Refiner, you must have Spatial Meridian Body or a similar initiation before learning Space talents that cost Stamina. ### Base Ability - Fold Step Tag: Fold Art. Action Type: Bonus Action Factory Combat Bucket: bonus_action Factory Routing: combat_action_row Range: Self. Cost: 1 CP. Teleport up to 20 feet to an unoccupied space you can see. You may bring worn and carried equipment. Fold Step does not provoke Opportunity Attacks because you do not move through the intervening spaces. Ordinary Cap: Unless a higher-Realm talent, anchor, Domain, or variant explicitly says otherwise, ordinary unassisted Fold Step cannot exceed 50 feet. Fifty feet of uninterrupted teleportation with no path drawback is already a powerful battlefield movement tool. Fold Step is a battlefield step, not long-distance travel magic. ### Base Ability - Spatial Awareness Tag: Anchor Art. When you use Fold Step, Short Swap, Blink Guard, Close Gate, or another Space effect to leave a space, you may erase the visible trace of your departure. Until the start of your next turn, creatures have Disadvantage on checks made to track your immediate spatial path unless they possess Spatial Awareness, Divination, Stars, or an equivalent sense. Once per long rest, you may also use Cut the Road Behind You without spending CP.

### Base Ability - Fold Step
Tag: Fold Art.
Action Type: Bonus Action
Factory Combat Bucket: bonus_action
Factory Routing: combat_action_row
Range: Self.
Cost: 1 CP.
Teleport up to 20 feet to an unoccupied space you can see.
You may bring worn and carried equipment.
Fold Step does not provoke Opportunity Attacks because you do not move through the intervening spaces.
Fold Step cannot pass through Dimensional Lock, a sealed formation, a closed spatial boundary, or a stronger Space effect.
Scaling:
Fold Step does not gain automatic range from CL. Its ordinary range improves through Extended Fold and similar explicit talents. This keeps the base technique reliable while making investment matter.
Ordinary Cap: Unless a higher-Realm talent, anchor, Domain, or variant explicitly says otherwise, ordinary unassisted Fold Step cannot exceed 50 feet. Fifty feet of uninterrupted teleportation with no path drawback is already a powerful battlefield movement tool.
Fold Step is a battlefield step, not long-distance travel magic.

### Base Ability - Spatial Awareness
Tag: Anchor Art.
Action Type: Multi-Mode
Canonical Action Type: Multi-Mode
Factory Combat Bucket: split_required
Split Candidate Buckets: action, passive
Timing Detail: Passive and Action
Factory Routing: split_modes_before_character_action_programming
Split Review Decision: split_required_distinct_combat_buckets
Recommended Factory Realization: modes=PASSIVE_SPATIAL_AWARENESS->passive, ACTION_ACTIVE_INSPECTION->action
Range: 60 feet.
Cost: 0 CP for passive awareness; 1 CP to inspect actively.
Passive Effect: You sense obvious spatial disturbances within range. You know when a creature you can perceive teleports, opens a portal, enters or exits a pocket space, uses extradimensional storage, crosses a planar boundary, or forces a space wider or narrower than it should be.
Active Inspection: As an Action, spend 1 CP and choose one creature, object, doorway, area, or visible spatial effect within range. Make a Cultivation Check against the effect’s creator or against a DC set by rarity and concealment.
On a success, learn up to two of the following:
whether the target is spatially sealed;
whether the target has teleported within the last hour;
whether the target carries extradimensional storage;
whether the target is linked to an anchor;
whether a doorway or surface hides a pocket space;
whether a barrier blocks teleportation;
the approximate CL of the spatial effect;
whether the disturbance is stable, decaying, trapped, or contested.
Spatial Awareness does not reveal secret doors unless they are spatially distorted, and it does not identify ordinary locks.

spheres.full_exact_source_text: # Sphere of Spear Qi Expression: Primary — Spear Qi; Supporting — Metal Qi, Direction Qi, War Qi, Line Qi. “The spear does not ask where the enemy wishes to stand. It draws one line and teaches the battlefield to respect it.” Sphere Type: Martial Sphere with Projected Spear-Qi Evolutions Primary Path: Body Refining Secondary Paths: Qi Cultivation and Spirit Awakening Resources: Martial Focus for ordinary martial spear techniques; CP for projected Spear-Qi techniques used by Qi Cultivators and Spirit cultivators; Stamina for Body Refiners only when a Spear feature, variant, Insight, or Path synergy explicitly grants Stamina access. When a talent offers more than one payment method, use only the method your Path expression permits. Common Effects: Reach, interception, approach denial, Spear Intent, committed thrusts, pursuit, spear-light, dragon-spear charges, spear formations, formation breaking, Heart of the Spear, Spear Soul #### Spear Dao Spear is the cultivation of the line. A sword divides the world at the moment of decision. A spear tells the world where the decision must occur. Its shaft measures distance. Its point gives that distance meaning. Its wielder learns that a battlefield is not an open field but a web of approaches, lanes, thresholds, and forbidden steps. A novice learns to thrust. An adept learns to hold a line. A master learns that the line begins before the enemy enters reach. A sovereign learns that one point may extend far enough to pierce Heaven. The Spear sphere rewards: - reach; - timing; - directness; - interception; - commitment; - pursuit along a chosen route; - the difference between advancing and overextending; - holding one narrow line so completely that the enemy must reshape their entire plan around it. #### Spear Intent Spear Intent is the pressure of an established line. It is the sense that one route has already been measured, the point is already waiting, and the next careless step will become the beginning of the thrust. #### Spear Qi and Spear Light Spear Qi is the force carried through the entire weapon and projected beyond its physical tip. When condensed into visible or nearly invisible penetration, it is often called Spear Light. Spear Light is not a volley. It is one line made longer, faster, and more difficult to deny. #### Heart of the Spear Heart of the Spear is unwavering directness. It is not stubbornness. It is clarity about what must be held, what must be pierced, and when the cultivator must advance rather than retreat. A spear cultivator with a stable Spear Heart is difficult to lure away from the line that matters. #### Spear Soul Spear Soul is the moment the cultivated weapon begins to embody the wielder’s path. It may appear as: - a dragon coiled around the haft; - an ancient battlefield standard; - a spectral spear point hanging behind the wielder; - a bonded physical spear carrying accumulated intent; - a spiritual manifestation that answers when the wielder commits to one decisive thrust. #### Sphere Boundaries - Spear governs reach, line control, interception, approach denial, thrust geometry, committed pursuit, Spear Intent, Spear Qi, Spear Light, Heart of the Spear, Spear Soul, and formation anchoring. - Sword governs edge, decision, sword drawing, Sword Intent, Flying Swords, Sword Heart, Sword Soul, and severing cuts. - Barrage governs repeated ranged cadence, projectile rhythm, and volley pressure. - Athletics governs traversal, tumbling, jumping, climbing, and movement doctrine. - Brute governs leverage, shoves, collisions, and positional displacement. - Berserker governs committed impact, accepted openings, and structure-breaking force. - Protection governs preservation and barriers. Spear governs the line from which danger is denied entry. - Space governs rewritten distance and dimensional movement. Spear Light merely extends one cultivated thrust unless a Forged Technique explicitly adds Space. - Formations converts known spear principles into prepared defensive lines, cavalry courts, training terraces, and battlefield arrays. #### Spear and Sword Sphere / Primary Theme: - Spear: Line, reach, interception, approach denial, committed thrusts - Sword: Decision, edge, draw timing, severing cuts, Sword Intent - Spear + Sword: Weapon-master scriptures, edge-and-line dueling arts, sect weapon courts #### Spear and Barrage Sphere / Primary Theme: - Spear: One thrust controlling a line - Barrage: Repeated ranged pressure and projectile cadence - Spear + Barrage: Meteor-thrust nets, thrown-spear fusillades, spear-shadow storms #### Spear and Formations Spear creates active line techniques, short-lived spear courts, and temporary Spear-Qi arrays. Formations turns spear principles into infrastructure. A Spear talent does not automatically create: - a permanent sect defensive line; - a maintained spear-wall array; - an automatic city-gate killing field; - a cavalry mustering Formation; - a permanent spear tomb; - a self-firing battlefield array; - a training terrace that generates Spear Intent without an instructor. Spear talents that attack a creature entering, crossing, or moving inside your Spear Line are special Intercept talents and function only when the talent says they do. Spear Intent represents measured distance, disrupted confidence, anticipated movement, and a route that has become dangerous because you have claimed it. #### Spear Line Your Spear Line is the physical reach of one approved Spear weapon you are wielding. Some talents expand or project that line. ### Temporary Scene Bond
As an Action, you may spend 1 CP to create a temporary bond with a willing minor spirit, a spirit bearing your Spirit Regard, or a spirit whose Need you immediately satisfy.
The bond lasts for 1 scene.
During that scene, you may ask the spirit for one minor service, one piece of advice, one omen, one safe passage, one momentary manifestation, or one simple Nature Expression approved by the GM.
Temporary Scene Bonds do not count against your Major Spirit Bond limit unless the spirit fights for you or uses a major sphere effect.

### Temporary Scene Bond
As an Action, you may spend 1 CP to create a temporary bond with a willing minor spirit, a spirit bearing your Spirit Regard, or a spirit whose Need you immediately satisfy.
The bond lasts for 1 scene.
During that scene, you may ask the spirit for one minor service, one piece of advice, one omen, one safe passage, one momentary manifestation, or one simple Nature Expression approved by the GM.
Temporary Scene Bonds do not count against your Major Spirit Bond limit unless the spirit fights for you or uses a major sphere effect.

#### Starbolt
Action Type: Action
Factory Combat Bucket: action
Factory Routing: combat_action_row
Range: 90 feet
Cost: 0 CP
Target: One creature or object you can target
Release a distant ray, comet fragment, constellation needle, pale astral bolt, star-metal spark, or cold point of starlight.
Make a ranged Cultivation Attack roll. On a hit, choose Radiant, Force, or Cold damage and deal:
CL 1-4: 1d8 damage;
CL 5-10: 2d8 damage;
CL 11-16: 3d8 damage;
CL 17-20: 4d8 damage.
Once per turn when Starbolt hits, you may apply Stellar Mark to the target until the start of your next turn.
Aligned Benefit: If you are Aligned, Starbolt’s range increases by 30 feet.

spheres.full_exact_source_text: # Sphere of Stars Qi Expression: Primary — Star Qi; Supporting — Light Qi, Fate Qi, Distance Qi, Memory Qi. “The stars are distant only to those who think distance is the same as separation.” Common Name: Stars Sphere Sphere Type: Restricted Power Sphere / Celestial Orientation, Starlight, and Astral-Positioning Sphere Primary Path: Spirit Awakening Secondary Path: Qi Cultivation Rare Variant: Body Refining through Star-Blooded Body, natal-star marrow, open-sky tempering, and body-as-constellation techniques Resource: Cultivation Points, Star Anchors, Stellar Marks, Sky References, and celestial positioning Common Effects: Navigation, distant light, stellar perception, constellation marks, falling-star attacks, star-road movement, celestial relays, astral survey, anti-teleportation pressure, open-sky empowerment, observatory projects, and night-sky domain authority. ### Stars Dao Stars are the cultivation of distant certainty. Light reveals what is near. Space folds what is far. Divination asks what a sign means. Fate asks which road might open. Stars answer a different question: Where is it, and what line connects it to Heaven? A Stars cultivator studies fixed lights, wandering stars, cold astral currents, sky palaces, star maps, natal constellations, heavenly compasses, observatory stones, meteor scars, star-metal, and the invisible grid by which night remembers direction. To cultivate Stars is to understand that distance does not erase relationship. A mountain across the world, an enemy behind a wall, a sect gate under another sky, and a vow made beneath one constellation all have positions in the greater pattern. The Dao question of Stars is: What remains connected across distance? ### Restricted-Sphere Access Stars may be learned through ordinary sphere advancement only if the campaign allows restricted Power spheres. Otherwise, unlocking Stars normally requires one or more of the following: a celestial scripture, star chart, observatory inheritance, or star-metal tablet; initiation under an open sky during an eclipse, meteor shower, astral tide, or great conjunction; instruction from a Celestial Hall, Star Palace, Astral Observatory, or old navigator sect; Spirit Awakening that can perceive astral bodies and celestial spirits; Qi Cultivation that has opened a stable stellar meridian; a Star Anchor network, constellation formation, or sect observatory to study; a natal-star omen, fallen-star treasure, or bloodline connected to the night sky; GM approval. Stars is restricted because it combines combat, perception, navigation, and long-distance anchoring. Its best effects should feel earned through initiation, maps, preparation, and relationship with the heavens. ### Realm Progression Mortal Realm. The cultivator learns to perceive direction, create temporary Star Anchors, place short-lived Stellar Marks, fire Starbolts, move along small lines of starlight, ward with constellation flashes, and navigate by sky reference. Foundation Realm. The cultivator opens stable celestial meridians. Star Anchors last longer, Stellar Marks can be sustained, starlight attacks gain range and precision, constellation guards circle the body, and messages can travel between anchors. Core Formation Realm. The cultivator forms a Star Palace or Celestial Compass Court. Within the Domain, directions become assigned, hidden movement becomes difficult, teleportation and displacement are pressured, and marks pull targets into the logic of the constellation. Nascent Soul Realm. The cultivator becomes a living star map. They may lower an artificial sky, project awareness through distant anchors, open star roads, call Heaven-Falling impacts, and embody the Star-Sovereign Incarnation. Secret Inheritance. The cultivator names an unreachable target by constellation and makes distance answer for one decisive minute. ### 2024 Fifth-Edition Rules Baseline This draft assumes the 2024 fifth-edition baseline used by Tianxia. Use the 2024 meanings of Action, Bonus Action, Reaction, Attack action, Opportunity Attack, Advantage, Disadvantage, Concentration, Cover, Invisibility, Invisible, Restrained, Prone, Grappled, Incapacitated, Teleportation, Long Rest, Short Rest, Exhaustion, Dying, Temporary HP, object interaction, and magical object rules unless this sphere explicitly replaces or expands them. #### Saving Throws Stars effects usually use one of the following saving throws: Dexterity against falling stars, meteor impacts, star needles, and line attacks that can be dodged. Charisma against Stellar Marks, constellation prisons, astral naming, anti-teleportation pressure, and effects that assert celestial position over identity or location. Wisdom against perception distortion, astral misdirection, or attempts to resist celestial orientation. Strength against being pushed, pulled, knocked Prone, or pinned by falling-star force. Unless a talent states otherwise, a creature affected by a sustained hostile Stars effect repeats the saving throw at the end of each of its turns, ending the effect on itself on a success. #### Damage Type Stars usually deals Radiant, Force, or Cold damage. Radiant represents starlight, celestial fire, and falling Heaven-brightness. Force represents astral impact, comet force, void-pressure, and a line of position striking from impossible distance. Cold represents deep night, starless void, frozen starlight, and the chill between heavens. A Stars talent should not deal Fire damage unless it is specifically a meteor, sun-star, or tribulation-flame technique. #### Cover, Range, and Marks Stars is allowed to care about distance, but it should not ignore all obstacles for free. Unless a talent states otherwise: Stars attacks still require a valid target and line of effect. Stellar Mark may improve targeting but does not automatically bypass Total Cover. Stars does not attack through mountains, sealed vaults, dimensional barriers, or stronger concealment techniques unless a Secret technique or Forged Technique says so. Star Anchors can extend perception and targeting only when a talent permits it. Open sky improves many talents but is not required unless stated. #### Teleportation and Displacement Stars can resist, reveal, or pressure teleportation because it establishes position. It does not automatically prevent all teleportation. When a Stars talent interferes with teleportation, planar movement, forced displacement, or spatial folding, the effect should usually allow a Charisma saving throw, an opposed Cultivation Check, or a stated limitation. ### Key Ability, Save DC, and Costs Use your Path key ability for Stars save DCs unless a Path synergy changes it. Cultivation Save DC: 8 + your Proficiency Bonus + your key ability modifier. Cultivation Attack Modifier: Proficiency Bonus + your key ability modifier. Stars Check: d20 + your Proficiency Bonus + your key ability modifier. Use this to read distorted skies, contest another celestial mark, identify a hidden Star Anchor, maintain a star road under pressure, or overcome rival astral concealment when a talent calls for it. CP Costs: If a feature lists a CP cost, spend CP from your Path’s cultivation pool. ### Core Stars Rules #### Sky Reference A Sky Reference is the celestial source by which a Stars technique establishes orientation. A valid Sky Reference may be: open night sky; visible stars; a clear artificial celestial projection; a Star Anchor you created; a constellation formation; a celestial observatory; a star chart or star map prepared by a talent; a realm where stars remain spiritually perceptible; a Forged Technique or item that stores a true star pattern. A Stars talent does not fail merely because the cultivator is indoors, underground, or beneath clouds unless the talent says so. However, many Stars talents improve when you act beneath open sky or within range of a Star Anchor. #### Open Sky You are beneath Open Sky when you can see the sky directly or through a spiritually clear window, courtyard, cave-mouth, skylight, mirror-pool, astral projection, or prepared observatory lens that the GM accepts as a valid celestial reference. Clouds, smoke, or daylight do not automatically remove Open Sky for a Stars cultivator. A sealed chamber, deep cave, anti-divination vault, false-sky prison, or starless demiplane usually does. #### Star Anchor A Star Anchor is a prepared mark, crystal, talisman, inscribed stone, star-metal nail, observatory point, mirror-basin, tattooed compass, or location attuned to a constellation. Unless a talent states otherwise: creating a Star Anchor takes 10 minutes; a Star Anchor lasts 24 hours; you may maintain a number of Star Anchors equal to your Proficiency Bonus; a Star Anchor may be detected through Stars, Divination, Formations, Spirit Awakening, or an appropriate Cultivation Check; a destroyed Star Anchor stops functioning; a Star Anchor is not automatically a teleportation circle, safe house, or formation node; placing a Star Anchor in a hostile creature’s worn gear requires a talent, touch, or successful contested check. #### Stellar Mark A Stellar Mark is a short-lived celestial designation placed on a creature, object, or location. A target bearing your Stellar Mark: emits a faint star-like glimmer visible to you; cannot benefit from ordinary Invisible against you; reveals its direction to you while it remains within 1 mile unless blocked by a stronger concealment effect; may be targeted by certain Stars talents at increased range; may count as a valid endpoint for star-road movement or constellation lines when a talent says so; knows it has been marked unless another effect conceals the mark. A Stellar Mark normally lasts until the start of your next turn unless a talent says otherwise. A creature can bear multiple Stellar Marks from different cultivators, but only one Stellar Mark from the same cultivator unless a feature says otherwise. #### Constellation Line A Constellation Line is an invisible or visible path drawn between you, a Star Anchor, a Stellar Mark, a star map point, or a valid Sky Reference. Constellation Lines are used for movement, targeting, protection, warning, and prison talents. They are not physical ropes and cannot usually be cut unless a talent makes them manifest. However, they can be disrupted by destroying an anchor, breaking concentration, severing line of effect, entering a starless ward, or winning an opposed Cultivation Check when the GM allows it. #### Star Alignment Some Stars talents refer to being Aligned. You are Aligned if at least one of the following is true: you are beneath Open Sky; you are within 30 feet of one of your Star Anchors; you are inside a Stars Domain you created; you are holding a prepared star map created by one of your Stars talents; the target bears your Stellar Mark; a talent says you are Aligned. When a talent has an Aligned Benefit, apply it only if you are Aligned when you use the talent. #### Star Anchor Network A Star Anchor Network is two or more active Star Anchors created by the same cultivator and recognized by the same constellation. A network can support Celestial Relay, Astral Survey, Star Roads, warning systems, and observatory projects. A Star Anchor Network is not automatically a Formation, but Formations can build on it. #### Natal Star Some Stars cultivators cultivate a Natal Star: a star, constellation, astral palace, or symbolic heavenly position associated with their soul, bloodline, oath, or cultivation method. A Natal Star is primarily narrative unless a talent, Insight, Path synergy, or Secret Inheritance gives it mechanics. It can justify unusual initiation, Body Refining access, a sect title, or a recurring Dao mark. ### Base Sphere Abilities #### Celestial Orientation Action Type: Special Trigger Canonical Action Type: Special Trigger Factory Combat Bucket: passive Timing Detail: No action for passive awareness; 10-minute ritual for detailed reading Factory Routing: triggered_passive_modifier_row Range: Self Cost: None, or 1 CP for detailed reading Duration: Instantaneous or 8 hours You can sense basic celestial orientation. You always know whether you are under a valid Sky Reference, whether the local sky is natural, distorted, sealed, artificial, or spiritually false, and the general direction of the nearest Star Anchor you created within 1 mile. As a 10-minute ritual, spend 1 CP to perform a detailed reading. For 8 hours, you gain the following benefits: you know true north; you know the approximate time until sunrise or sunset if the local realm has such cycles; you have Advantage on checks made to navigate outdoors, through wilderness, across wasteland, or through strange terrain where celestial orientation applies; you can recognize ordinary celestial navigation errors; you know whether the local sky has been supernaturally distorted, concealed, or replaced; you know the direction of each Star Anchor you created within 10 miles. Celestial Orientation does not reveal hidden rooms, invisible creatures, secret portals, or unknown destinations by itself. #### Starbolt Action Type: Action Factory Combat Bucket: action Factory Routing: combat_action_row Range: 90 feet Cost: 0 CP Target: One creature or object you can target Release a distant ray, comet fragment, constellation needle, pale astral bolt, star-metal spark, or cold point of starlight. Make a ranged Cultivation Attack roll. On a hit, choose Radiant, Force, or Cold damage and deal: CL 1-4: 1d8 damage; CL 5-10: 2d8 damage; CL 11-16: 3d8 damage; CL 17-20: 4d8 damage. Once per turn when Starbolt hits, you may apply Stellar Mark to the target until the start of your next turn. Aligned Benefit: If you are Aligned, Starbolt’s range increases by 30 feet. #### Mark the Distant Star Action Type: Bonus Action Factory Combat Bucket: bonus_action Factory Routing: combat_action_row Range: 60 feet Cost: 1 CP Saving Throw: Charisma Choose one creature, object, or location you can target. An unwilling creature makes a Charisma saving throw. Failed Save: The target bears your Stellar Mark for 1 minute. At the end of each of its turns, it repeats the saving throw, ending the mark on a success. Successful Save: The target bears your Stellar Mark until the start of your next turn. Objects and locations that are not held, worn, or spiritually concealed do not receive a saving throw. #### Draw the Star Line Action Type: Bonus Action Factory Combat Bucket: bonus_action Factory Routing: combat_action_row Range: 30 feet Cost: 1 CP Duration: Until the end of your turn Draw a brief Constellation Line between yourself and one valid endpoint: a creature bearing your Stellar Mark, one of your Star Anchors, an unoccupied space beneath Open Sky, or a point you can see. Until the end of your turn, one Stars talent you use may treat that endpoint as Aligned. If the talent involves movement, you may move along the line without provoking Opportunity Attacks, but the movement cannot pass through solid barriers. ### Talent Tags Attack. Direct damage or offensive pressure.Anchor. Creates, modifies, protects, or consumes Star Anchors.Mark. Creates or exploits Stellar Marks.Line. Uses Constellation Lines or star-road geometry.Ward. Protects, guards, reveals, or resists displacement.Survey. Perception, navigation, mapping, or distant awareness.Relay. Communication or warning through anchors.Domain. Creates an area of celestial authority.Astral. Interacts with spirits, astral bodies, planar boundaries, or celestial realms.Body-Star. Requires or modifies Body Refining access.Realm Evolution. Represents a major Realm threshold feature. ### Mortal Realm Talents - CL 1+ #### Celestial Bearings Tags: Survey Action Type: Ritual Procedure Canonical Action Type: Ritual Procedure Factory Routing: procedure_ledger_not_combat_action Timing Detail: Ritual Time: 10 minutes Duration: 8 hours Cost: 1 CP Choose yourself and up to your Proficiency Bonus willing creatures. For the duration, each chosen creature gains: Advantage on checks made to navigate outdoors; the ability to know true north; the ability to estimate time until sunrise, sunset, moonrise, or local nightfall if such cycles exist; Advantage on checks made to notice ordinary celestial-navigation errors; the ability to know the direction of the nearest active Star Anchor you created within 1 mile. Aligned Benefit: Beneath Open Sky or within 30 feet of a Star Anchor, the creatures may also estimate approximate latitude, identify major known landmarks by direction, and notice whether the sky is supernaturally distorted. #### Starpath Step Tags: Line, Movement Action Type: Bonus Action Factory Combat Bucket: bonus_action Factory Routing: combat_action_row Range: 20 feet Cost: 1 CP Move along a brief line of starlight to an unoccupied space you can see. This movement: does not provoke Opportunity Attacks; ignores nonmagical difficult terrain; may carry you vertically up to 10 feet; does not pass through solid barriers; is rapid celestial movement, not teleportation. Aligned Benefit: Increase the range by 10 feet. #### Falling Spark Tags: Attack Action Type: Action Factory Combat Bucket: action Factory Routing: combat_action_row Range: 60 feet Area: 10-foot-radius sphere Cost: 2 CP Saving Throw: Dexterity Call down a cluster of tiny falling stars. Creatures in the area make Dexterity saving throws. Failed Save: The creature takes 2d6 Radiant or Force damage and cannot take Reactions until the start of your next turn. Successful Save: The creature takes half damage. Damage increases to 4d6 at CL 11 and 6d6 at CL 17. Aligned Benefit: One creature bearing your Stellar Mark in the area has Disadvantage on the save. #### Starlight Ward Tags: Ward Action Type: Reaction Factory Combat Bucket: reaction Factory Routing: combat_action_row Trigger: You or an ally within 30 feet takes damage Cost: 1 CP A small constellation flashes between the harm and the target. Reduce the triggering damage by: CL 1-10: 1d8 + key ability modifier; CL 11-16: 2d8 + key ability modifier; CL 17-20: 3d8 + key ability modifier. Aligned Benefit: Add your Proficiency Bonus to the reduction. #### Star Map Tags: Survey, Anchor Action Type: Ritual Procedure Canonical Action Type: Ritual Procedure Factory Routing: procedure_ledger_not_combat_action Timing Detail: Ritual Time: 10 minutes Duration: 24 hours Cost: 1 CP Create a moving star map of one area you can observe, remember clearly, or study through a reliable map. The map may record: major roads; settlements; mountain ridges; rivers; known Star Anchors; known portals; known dangerous regions; approximate direction of celestial disturbances; the direction of sunrise, sunset, and major visible constellations. The map updates ordinary celestial orientation automatically. Star Map does not reveal hidden locations, secret doors, unseen enemies, concealed portals, or unknown terrain beyond your knowledge. #### Guiding Star Tags: Mark, Survey Action Type: Bonus Action Factory Combat Bucket: bonus_action Factory Routing: combat_action_row Range: 90 feet Duration: Until the start of your next turn Cost: 1 CP Choose one ally, enemy, object, or visible location. A harmless guiding star appears above or near it. If the target is willing, carried by you, or unattended, no save is required. An unwilling creature makes a Charisma saving throw. Failed Save: The target bears your Stellar Mark until the start of your next turn. For the duration, one ally who can see the guiding star may add 1d4 to one attack roll, ability check, or saving throw made to reach, strike, protect, or avoid the marked target. A creature can benefit from only one Guiding Star die per round. #### Star-Needle Aim Tags: Attack, Mark Action Type: Bonus Action Factory Combat Bucket: bonus_action Factory Routing: combat_action_row Duration: Until the end of your turn Cost: 1 CP Your next Starbolt or ranged weapon attack this turn follows a needle-thin constellation line. If the target bears your Stellar Mark, the attack ignores Half Cover. If the target does not bear your Stellar Mark, the attack gains +1 to hit. This talent does not ignore Total Cover. #### Night-Sight Meridian Tags: Survey Action Type: Bonus Action Factory Combat Bucket: bonus_action Factory Routing: combat_action_row Duration: 1 hour Cost: 1 CP Starlight opens a quiet meridian behind your eyes. For the duration: Dim Light does not impose Disadvantage on your Wisdom (Perception) checks relying on sight; you can see normally through nonmagical darkness out to 60 feet; you have Advantage on checks made to identify constellations, celestial distortions, Star Anchors, or astral signs. This does not see through magical darkness unless the darkness is weaker than your Stars effect and you succeed on a Stars Check against its DC. #### Warning Star Tags: Ward, Anchor, Relay Action Type: Ritual Procedure Canonical Action Type: Ritual Procedure Factory Routing: procedure_ledger_not_combat_action Timing Detail: Ritual Time: 1 minute Range: Touch Duration: 8 hours Cost: 1 CP Place a faint warning star on a doorway, campsite, wagon, ship, or small area no larger than a 20-foot-radius sphere. When a creature you did not designate enters the area, you receive a brief warning if you are within 1 mile and on the same plane. The warning tells you the direction of the star and whether the intruder is Tiny, Small, Medium, Large, or larger. It does not identify the creature. A creature using Stealth may avoid triggering the warning by succeeding on a Dexterity (Stealth) check against your Cultivation Save DC. #### Cold Star Mantle Tags: Ward Action Type: Bonus Action Factory Combat Bucket: bonus_action Factory Routing: combat_action_row Duration: 1 minute Cost: 2 CPConcentration: Required Cold starlight settles over your body or one willing creature within 30 feet. For the duration, the target gains: resistance to Cold damage; Advantage on saving throws against being lost, disoriented, or magically misdirected; once per turn, when the target deals Radiant, Force, or Cold damage, it may add your Proficiency Bonus to one damage roll. ### Foundation Realm Feature - Celestial Meridian Opening At Foundation Realm, your Stars cultivation can hold a stable line between body, anchor, and heaven. Constellation Road cannot cross planes, cannot cross a Dimensional Lock, requires at least two active Star Anchors, and remains detectable through Stars, Divination, or Formations. #### Heaven-Mirror Star Map Tags: Survey, Anchor Action Type: Ritual Procedure Canonical Action Type: Ritual Procedure Factory Routing: procedure_ledger_not_combat_action Timing Detail: Ritual Time: 1 hour Duration: Until your next long rest Cost: 6 CP Create an advanced Star Map tied to one Star Anchor Network. The stars had already written the path.” Classification: Secret Stars Talent Prerequisite: CL 17+, Star-Sovereign Incarnation, hidden primordial-constellation inheritance Action Type: Action Factory Combat Bucket: action Factory Routing: combat_action_row Range: Special Duration: 1 minute Cost: 15 CPConcentration: Required Use Limit: Once per week Choose one creature, object, or location you can perceive through one of the following: direct sight; active Star Anchor; Astral Survey; Divination effect; strong spiritual connection; reliable celestial map; a Star Anchor Network tied to the target’s region. Successful Initial Save: Until the start of your next turn, the creature bears your Stellar Mark, cannot teleport, and cannot benefit from ordinary Invisible against you. #### Object or Location You know its exact direction and approximate distance. You may create one temporary Star Anchor at that location if physically possible and if no stronger ward prevents it. The temporary anchor lasts until the Secret ends. #### Limits Constellation That Names the Unreachable does not: bypass planar boundaries; bypass Dimensional Locks; bypass Total Cover automatically; strike through entire mountains without a suitable Forged Technique; reveal a target whose existence is protected by a stronger Secret concealment effect; replace exploration, investigation, or travel entirely; override GM-placed campaign mysteries without the correct narrative key. ### Stars Drawbacks and Variant Scriptures A Stars drawback is an optional sphere-specific limitation that grants a bonus talent or benefit while changing how Stars cultivation functions. Choose at most one Stars drawback when first learning Stars or undergoing a major Stars initiation unless the GM says otherwise. If a drawback grants a talent whose prerequisites are not yet met, you gain that talent when you meet the prerequisites. If the drawback is retrained or removed, the bonus talent or benefit is lost. #### Open-Sky Reliance Scripture You require Open Sky or one of your Star Anchors to use Stars talents that cost CP. Starbolt and Celestial Orientation still function normally. You gain one Stars talent as a bonus talent. #### Anchor-Bound Stargazer Your Stars talents cannot receive Aligned Benefits from Open Sky alone. You must be within 30 feet of one of your Star Anchors or inside a Stars Domain you created. Your Star Anchors last twice as long, and you may maintain one additional Star Anchor. #### Cold Star Scripture Your Stars attacks may deal only Cold or Force damage unless a talent specifically requires another type. You cannot choose Fire damage for Heaven-Falling Star. When you deal Cold damage with a Stars talent, you may reduce one target’s Speed by 5 feet until the start of your next turn once per turn. #### No-Falling-Star Vow You cannot learn Falling Spark, Meteor Shower, Falling Star, or Heaven-Falling Star. Your Stars cultivation refuses destructive descent and focuses on navigation, marking, warding, and survey. You gain one Survey, Ward, Anchor, or Relay Stars talent as a bonus talent. #### Astral Hermit Chart You must spend 10 minutes preparing a star chart after each long rest. Until you do, you cannot create new Star Anchors or use Survey talents that cost CP. After preparing the chart, your first Survey or Anchor talent each day costs 1 fewer CP, minimum 0. #### False-Sky Survivor You were initiated under an artificial or corrupted sky. You have Advantage on Stars Checks to identify false skies, starless wards, celestial distortions, and counterfeit Star Anchors. However, whenever you fail such a check by 5 or more, you suffer Disadvantage on your next Stars attack or Survey check before the end of your next turn. ### Path Synergies #### Spirit Awakening - Celestial Soul Spirit Awakening is the primary Path for Stars. Use Wisdom as your Stars key ability. Your Stars talents can affect spirits, ghosts, incorporeal creatures, astral bodies, possessing entities, and projected souls normally unless a specific creature feature says otherwise. You may perceive the faint celestial outline of a spirit within 30 feet of one of your Star Anchors or within your Stars Domain. This does not reveal hidden thoughts or true names by itself. #### Qi Cultivation - Refined Stellar Circulation Qi Cultivation uses refined celestial Qi, star-metal resonance, and circulating astral meridians to shape Stars techniques. You may use Intelligence or Charisma as your Stars key ability. Once per turn, reduce the CP cost of one Stars talent by 1, minimum 1. Starbolt’s range increases by 30 feet. When you create a Star Anchor, you may make it as a visible crystal point, invisible qi knot, star-metal pin, or talismanic coordinate. #### Body Refining - Star-Blooded Body Body Refiners do not normally manipulate distant celestial patterns as freely as Spirit Awakening or Qi Cultivation cultivators. A Body Refiner must learn the Star-Blooded Body Cultivation Insight or receive a comparable bloodline, inheritance, sect ritual, or Forged Technique. When you use Stars through Body Refining: use Constitution as your Stars key ability; spend Stamina instead of CP for Stars talents unless your table uses a unified pool; your body, scars, marrow, breath, tattoos, armor, or held weapon serve as your primary Sky Reference; you can use Starbolt, Starpath Step, Starlight Ward, Cold Star Mantle, and other self/weapon/near-field Stars talents normally; long-distance Survey, Relay, Astral Body, and Star Anchor Network talents require Open Sky, a physical Star Anchor, or prepared ritual tools; you cannot create invisible remote Star Anchors by pure external Qi unless a talent, item, sect ritual, or Forged Technique permits it. While beneath Open Sky or within 30 feet of a Star Anchor, you gain +1 AC and Advantage on saving throws against forced teleportation or spatial displacement. Once per turn, when you deal damage with a Stars talent, you may add your Constitution modifier to one Stars damage roll. ### Cultivation Insights #### Star-Blooded Body Prerequisite: Body Refining, CL 4+ You may learn Stars through Body Refining. Use Stamina and Constitution for Stars talents. Gain the Body Refining - Star-Blooded Body Path synergy. Your Star Anchors must be physical marks, scars, weapons, armor plates, star-metal nails, bone inscriptions, or visible talismanic points unless another feature permits otherwise. #### Celestial Navigator Prerequisite: Stars, CL 8+ Celestial Bearings no longer costs CP, lasts until your next long rest, and may affect twice as many creatures. In addition, Celestial Bearings grants Advantage on checks made to navigate through portals, strange realms, distorted landscapes, moving islands, mist seas, and false-sky territories. #### Star-Walking Immortal Prerequisite: Stars, CL 8+ Starpath Step range increases by 20 feet. Once per short rest, when you use Starpath Step, you may carry one willing creature of your size or smaller. You may end Starpath Step adjacent to one of your active Star Anchors within range without ordinary visibility, but the path cannot cross Total Cover or a spatial barrier. #### Comet Adept Prerequisite: Stars, CL 8+ Once per turn when you deal Radiant, Force, or Cold damage through a Stars talent, add your Proficiency Bonus to one damage roll. If the target bears your Stellar Mark, you may also push it 5 feet. #### Constellation Keeper Prerequisite: Stars, CL 8+ You may maintain two additional Star Anchors. Astral Survey range increases to 20 miles. When one of your Star Anchors is destroyed, you immediately know which anchor was destroyed and the direction from you. #### Astral Cartographer Prerequisite: Stars, CL 8+ When you create a Star Map, you may include one layer of supernatural information you have personally confirmed, such as known portals, known Star Anchors, known ley lines, known sect boundaries, known forbidden zones, or known celestial disturbances. Your Star Maps have Advantage on checks made to resist being falsified by ordinary illusion or mundane forgery. #### Seven-Star Battle Rhythm Prerequisite: Stars, CL 8+ When you use Starpath Step or Seven-Star Step, your next attack before the end of your turn gains +1 to hit. If the attack hits a creature bearing your Stellar Mark, you may move 5 feet without provoking Opportunity Attacks. #### Cold Star Heart Prerequisite: Stars, CL 8+ You gain resistance to Cold damage. When you deal Cold damage with a Stars talent, you may ignore resistance to Cold damage once per turn. If a creature is immune to Cold damage, this Insight does not bypass the immunity unless a Secret effect or Forged Technique says otherwise. #### Name the Distant Enemy Prerequisite: Stars, CL 12+ When you successfully apply Stable Stellar Mark to a creature, you may learn one of the following: its current direction from you; whether it is on the same plane; whether it is under a teleportation, invisibility, or concealment effect; whether it has damaged you or an ally since your last long rest; whether it is protected by a Star Anchor, Formation, or spatial ward. You can use this Insight a number of times equal to your Proficiency Bonus per long rest. #### Observatory Heir Prerequisite: Stars, CL 12+ You may treat one permanent observatory, sect tower, star platform, or celestial altar you helped create as one of your Star Anchors without counting against your normal limit. When you finish a long rest there, choose one Stars talent you know with a CP cost of 2 or less. You may use that talent once before your next long rest without spending CP.
