spheres.full_exact_source_text: # Sphere of Thread Qi Expression: Primary — Thread Qi; Supporting — Binding Qi, Fate Qi, Silk Qi, Control Qi. Sphere Type: Hybrid Martial-Power / Line / Binding / Stitching Sphere Primary Path: Body Refining, Qi Cultivation, or Spirit Awakening Resource: Martial Focus for mundane thread techniques when a talent says so; CP for qi-thread, spirit-thread, or clearly supernatural effects; Stamina only through explicit Body Refining expression Core Chassis: Spool and Strand, Draw the Line, Threaded Strike, Listen Through Tension “A blade cuts once. A fist lands once. A thread remains after the hand has moved. It remembers the pull, follows the breath, and binds two points into one consequence.” Thread cultivators learn that a line is not weak because it is thin. A line can cut because all force is concentrated. A line can bind because it is continuous. A line can guide a weapon, seal a wound, tug a limb, close a gate, or stitch qi back into the meridian it tried to flee. At lower Realms, most Thread disciples carry silk, cord, needles, hooks, spools, garrotes, weighted lines, and hidden sleeves of wire. At higher Realms, these tools become less separate from the body. Breath leaves the fingertips as qi-silk. Meridian pressure becomes a line. A gaze catches a target like a strand. A battlefield becomes a loom. #### Core Dao Thread is the cultivation of continuous connection. The Thread scripture asks five questions. What two points have been joined? What travels along the line? What happens when tension is accepted instead of resisted? What does the thread bind, guide, stitch, or sever? When the world tries to come apart, what can still be held together? Thread is not simply rope, string, or web. The Dao at its heart is continuity. Thread cultivators create relationships between points: hand and weapon, needle and wound, target and ground, ally and ally, enemy and consequence, meridian and sealed knot. Their talents should modify that connection engine rather than become unrelated silk-themed powers. #### Sphere Type Thread is a Hybrid Might and Power Sphere. Common Practice: Body Refining and mundane threadcraft. Most Thread cultivators begin with real thread, silk, cord, wire, needles, anchors, sleeves, spools, hooks, weighted knots, and hidden garrotes. Qi Practice: Qi Cultivation extends thread beyond mundane limits. Qi Threads can reach farther, resist mundane cutting, pass around corners through anchors, transmit pressure, and bind meridians. Spirit Practice: Spirit Awakening allows thread to carry intent, memory, oath, and soul-pressure. Spirit Thread can sense unseen bonds, restrain spiritual movement, and perform limited red-thread or oath-thread work. Default Key Ability: Dexterity for mundane thread combat and needle work. Constitution for Body Refiners who cultivate tendon-silk, breath tension, and body-as-loom techniques. Intelligence for technical weavers, physicians, and trap-like thread arrays. Wisdom for Spirit Thread and bond-sensing techniques. Choose when first learning the sphere, or use the key ability of your Path if your Path feature requires it. Resource: Martial Focus for mundane thread techniques when a talent says so. CP for qi-thread, spirit-thread, or clearly supernatural effects. Some talents can be used either way with different limits. #### What Thread Covers Thread governs the following. Silk, cord, wire, sutures, needles, hooked lines, garrotes, weighted threads, and hidden spools. Qi Threads projected from fingers, weapons, needles, breath, hair, sleeves, wounds, or anchors. Binding, tripping, pulling, lifting, redirecting, disarming, and tying. Cutting threads and razor silk. Melee combat enhanced by body-light tension, weighted knots, wrapping lines, and weapon-guiding threads. Meridian stitching, pressure binding, emergency sutures, and qi circulation repair. Puppet-like limb guidance in limited form, especially on willing allies or temporarily marked enemies. Webs, looms, thread zones, thread domains, and battlefield tension fields. Oath threads, pursuit threads, and red-thread symbolism as limited Spirit-side techniques. #### What Thread Does Not Cover Thread and Puppetry: Thread can pull, guide, restrain, and briefly force motion through a line. Puppetry owns full remote body command, constructed puppets, puppet armies, replacement bodies, autonomous marionettes, and long-term control architecture. Thread and Trap: Thread can create trip lines, snaring lines, and prepared knots. Trap owns broad prepared hazards, mechanisms, battlefield rigging, and triggered devices. Thread lines are a combat and connection engine, not the whole trap discipline. Thread and Fate: Red-thread imagery can mark bonds and obligations, but Thread does not rewrite luck, destiny, mandate, or karmic ledgers. Fate owns those themes. Thread and Space: Thread can pull, reel, swing, anchor, and create line-of-connection movement. It does not teleport, fold space, create gates, or replace Space. Thread and Ink: Ink writes law through trace and mark. Thread binds points through tension and continuity. A written thread diagram belongs to Ink or Formation unless the active effect is produced by thread. Thread and Healing: Thread can stitch wounds, bind meridians, and preserve life briefly. It does not replace Life, Medicine, Alchemy, or full restorative cultivation unless talents explicitly allow limited healing. Thread and Beastmastery: Thread can use silk beasts, spider silk, or worm-silk reagents as materials, but it does not breed, tame, command, grow, or harvest creatures. Growing, harvesting, and silk production belong to other spheres or setting systems. #### Core Terminology Thread: Any usable strand of mundane or supernatural material. Examples include silk, hemp cord, hair, wire, gut cord, spiritual silk, qi line, blood-suture, shadow-thread, red-thread, or soul-thread. Mundane Thread: Physical thread, cord, silk, wire, sutures, or line. It can be cut, burned, grabbed, noticed, tangled, or stolen like an object. Quality matters. Qi Thread: A supernatural thread made, reinforced, or extended by cultivated qi. It is visible or invisible at the user’s choice unless a talent says otherwise. A Qi Thread is magical for rules purposes. Spirit Thread: A thread carrying intent, oath, memory, fear, affection, debt, soul-pressure, or red-thread symbolism. Spirit Thread is magical and often noticeable to spiritual senses. Thread Line: A maintained line connecting two points. One end is usually you, your weapon, your needle, or an anchor you control. The other end may be a creature, object, surface, weapon, wound, knot, or another anchor. Anchor: A place where a Thread Line is fixed. Anchors may be knots, needles, hooks, wrapped weapons, marked surfaces, embedded sutures, wall pins, weighted spools, or qi knots. Tension: A Thread Line under meaningful pull. Many Thread talents require tension. If neither side is connected to anything that can pull or resist, the line is slack. Knot: A temporary condition of a Thread Line that restricts, reinforces, seals, or remembers a pattern. Some talents create named knots. Loom: A prepared pattern of multiple Thread Lines. Looms are larger effects such as thread zones, webs, domains, and battlefield arrays. #### General Thread Rules Thread Line Restriction: You can maintain a number of active Thread Lines equal to your Proficiency Bonus. If you create a Thread Line beyond this limit, the oldest line fades, snaps, or goes slack. Some talents increase this limit. Default Thread Line Duration: A Thread Line lasts until the end of your next turn unless a talent says otherwise. If you spend 1 CP when creating or maintaining it, it lasts for 1 minute without requiring further maintenance, or until severed. Mundane Line Range: A mundane Thread Line can normally extend up to 20 feet from you or from an anchor you control. It requires actual thread, cord, silk, or wire. Qi Line Range: A Qi Thread can normally extend up to 30 feet from you or from an anchor you control. At CL 5 this becomes 45 feet. At CL 11 this becomes 60 feet. At CL 17 this becomes 90 feet. Talents may use other ranges. Line of Effect: You need a path for the thread unless a talent says otherwise. A mundane line cannot pass through a closed wall. A Qi Thread can curve around obstacles you can see or have anchored, but it cannot pass through sealed solid barriers without a talent. Cutting a Thread Line: A creature adjacent to a visible mundane Thread Line may attack it. Unless a talent says otherwise, mundane combat thread has AC equal to your Cultivation Save DC and hit points equal to your Proficiency Bonus + your key ability modifier, minimum 1. A Qi Thread cannot normally be cut by mundane attacks unless it is made visible and substantial, but it can be dispelled, disrupted, or severed by appropriate magic, cultivation, or anti-qi effects. Detecting Thread Lines: Obvious threads are visible. Hidden mundane threads require a Wisdom (Perception) or Intelligence (Investigation) check against your Cultivation Save DC. Hidden Qi Threads require appropriate perception, spiritual sense, magical detection, or a successful check against your Cultivation Save DC. Thread Attacks: When a Thread talent calls for a Thread Attack, use either a melee weapon attack with a thread-eligible weapon, a ranged weapon attack with a needle or thrown thread tool, or a Cultivation Attack roll. Choose the mode when you use the talent. A creature cannot use a shield or heavy armor to ignore the attack unless the chosen attack mode allows it. Thread and Grapples: Thread can impose Grappled or Restrained only through talents. If a Thread talent gives a creature an escape chance, the target may use Strength (Athletics), Dexterity (Acrobatics), or an appropriate Cultivation Check against your Cultivation Save DC unless the talent says otherwise. Thread and Forced Movement: Thread pulls, slides, tugs, trips, or reels. Unless a talent says otherwise, forced movement from Thread does not provoke Opportunity Attacks. Thread and Size: If a Thread talent moves or restrains a creature, creatures two or more sizes larger than you have advantage on the initial saving throw or contest unless the talent says otherwise. Some high-Realm talents remove this limit. Thread Stock: You are assumed to carry ordinary thread, silk, cord, hooks, needles, and spools suitable for your techniques unless deprived of gear. Rare materials such as spirit silk, moon silk, dragon tendon, golden wire, ghost hair, and karmic red thread must be purchased, earned, harvested through another system, or awarded by the GM. Investment Ceiling: Thread has a high material ceiling. Better thread can improve durability, concealment, damage type, resistance to cutting, storage, range, or the number of prepared anchors. Expensive thread improves reliability and breadth, but it should not bypass Realm prerequisites. #### Base Ability - Spool and Strand Action Type: Special Trigger Canonical Action Type: Special Trigger Factory Combat Bucket: passive Timing Detail: No action for ordinary handling; part of the action for Thread talents Factory Routing: triggered_passive_modifier_row Range: Self. Cost: None for mundane thread; 1 CP to create or reinforce Qi Thread for combat use. Effect: You can prepare, draw, control, and conceal combat-ready strands. You may use mundane thread, silk, wire, cord, needles, and hooks as thread tools. If you spend 1 CP, you can create Qi Thread from your fingertips, breath, weapon, sleeve, hair, blood, or dantian pressure for 1 minute. Ordinary Uses: You can sew, bind, stitch, tie knots, mend cloth, mark a path with thread, set a simple cord, prepare a hidden sleeve spool, or handle fine threadwork without a check unless the situation is difficult. Combat Use: Spool and Strand enables your Thread talents. It does not by itself restrain creatures, deal damage, or create traps. #### Base Ability - Draw the Line Action Type: Multi-Mode Canonical Action Type: Multi-Mode Factory Combat Bucket: action Timing Detail: Action, or replace one attack when you take the Attack action Factory Routing: combat_action_row_with_attack_replacement_mode Split Review Decision: same_bucket_attack_replacement_mode Recommended Factory Realization: modes=ACTION_DRAW_THE_LINE->action, ATTACK_REPLACEMENT_DRAW_THE_LINE->action Range: Mundane 20 feet, Qi Thread 30 feet. Steel-Silk Scripture for durable physical thread. Dao-Spinning Cocoon as body refinement and emergency defense. #### Qi Cultivation - External Qi Silk Qi cultivators externalize meridian circulation into visible or invisible threads. Their lines can stretch farther, bind techniques, stitch qi, and create web fields. Suggested Qi Techniques: Qi Thread Scripture as the main expansion. Meridian Snare and Meridian Lock for channel control. Silk Web Field and Heaven-Net Casting for battlefield control. Severing Silk for cutting hostile techniques. World-Spanning Loom Seed for high-Realm anchor work. #### Spirit Awakening - Soul Thread and Red Bonds Spirit cultivators use Thread to sense relationships, promises, fear, debt, loyalty, and spiritual pressure. Their thread is not Fate’s ledger, but it can reveal and tug on the bonds people already carry. Suggested Spirit Techniques: Soul-Silk Thread for emotional direction. Red Thread of Debt for willing bonds. Puppet-Line Correction for support or pressure. Sever the Battle Line for tactical bond disruption. The Single Thread Through Heaven as a secret inheritance. ### Cultivation Insights #### Silk-Reeling Foundation Prerequisite: Thread sphere. Your body is trained in coiling silk force. When you use Draw the Line or Threaded Strike, you may move 5 feet once per round without provoking Opportunity Attacks from the target of that feature. #### Hidden Spool Discipline Prerequisite: Thread sphere. You can hide thread tools on your body even under inspection. You have advantage on Dexterity (Sleight of Hand) checks to conceal thread, needles, thin wire, hooks, or small spools. Once per Long Rest, if deprived of equipment, you may reveal that you retained enough thread stock to use one mundane Thread talent. #### Threaded Weapon Adept Prerequisite: Thread sphere and proficiency with at least one melee or thrown weapon. Choose one weapon you are proficient with. It is always thread-eligible for you. Once per turn when you use Threaded Strike with that weapon, you may choose both Follow the Sleeve and Draw the Guard instead of one benefit. #### Meridian Needle Training Prerequisite: Thread sphere and Surgeon’s Stitch. You can use healer’s kit, acupuncture needles, tailor’s tools, or weaver’s tools as a focus for Thread healing talents. When you use Surgeon’s Stitch, the target may reroll one Hit Die result of 1 and must use the new result. #### Red Thread Sensitivity Prerequisite: Thread sphere and Spirit Awakening or GM approval. You can sense willing emotional bonds. As an action, you may study two creatures you can see within 60 feet and learn whether a strong bond, debt, rivalry, loyalty, fear, or oath exists between them. This does not reveal exact details and fails against hidden, warded, or Fate-protected bonds unless the GM allows a check. #### Cut the Snare Prerequisite: Thread sphere. When you are Grappled, Restrained, or physically tied, you may use a Bonus Action to make a Dexterity, Strength, or Cultivation Check against the effect’s DC. On a success, you end one physical binding effect on yourself. Once you succeed with this Insight, you cannot use it again until you finish a Short Rest. #### Thousand-Knot Memory Prerequisite: Thread sphere. You can encode information into knots, braids, stitch patterns, or thread colors. You can store a short message, map route, password, technique clue, or emotional warning in a thread object. A creature trained in Thread or given the key can read it. Others must succeed on an Intelligence (Investigation), Wisdom (Insight), or appropriate tool check against your Cultivation Save DC. #### No Loose Ends Prerequisite: Thread sphere, CL 10+. When one of your Thread Lines ends, you may choose to have it leave no mundane trace. If the line was magical, observers must succeed on an Intelligence (Arcana), Wisdom (Perception), or Cultivation Check against your Cultivation Save DC to reconstruct where it was anchored.

#### Base Ability - Draw the Line
Action Type: Multi-Mode
Canonical Action Type: Multi-Mode
Factory Combat Bucket: action
Timing Detail: Action, or replace one attack when you take the Attack action
Factory Routing: combat_action_row_with_attack_replacement_mode
Split Review Decision: same_bucket_attack_replacement_mode
Recommended Factory Realization: modes=ACTION_DRAW_THE_LINE->action, ATTACK_REPLACEMENT_DRAW_THE_LINE->action
Range: Mundane 20 feet, Qi Thread 30 feet.
Cost: None for mundane thread if you have thread stock; 1 CP for Qi Thread or to ignore mundane stock.
Target: One creature, object, weapon, surface, or unattended item within range.
Effect: Make a Thread Attack. On a hit, you create a Thread Line between yourself or an anchor you control and the target. The line lasts until the end of your next turn. Choose one basic effect.
Pull: Move the target 5 feet toward you or toward the anchor if it is your size or smaller. Larger creatures are not moved unless they fail a Strength saving throw.
Snare: The target’s speed is reduced by 10 feet until the start of your next turn.
Guide: The next attack roll you make against the target before the end of your next turn ignores half cover.
Trip: The target must succeed on a Dexterity saving throw or fall Prone. This option requires the target to be no more than one size larger than you.
Disarm: The target must succeed on a Strength saving throw or drop one held object of your choice in its space. This option requires a mundane line, Qi Thread, or needle to reach the object.
Damage: Draw the Line does not deal damage unless you choose Cutting Thread or another talent modifies it.

#### Base Ability - Threaded Strike
Action Type: Linked Modifier
Canonical Action Type: Linked Modifier
Factory Combat Bucket: passive
Factory Routing: linked_modifier_row
Split Review Decision: linked_modifier_not_standalone_action
Recommended Factory Realization: modes=ON_HIT_THREADED_STRIKE->passive
Timing Detail: Part of a melee weapon attack or Unarmed Strike
Range: The attack’s normal reach.
Cost: None.
Effect: When you hit a creature with a melee weapon attack or Unarmed Strike, you may wrap, hook, guide, or tension a thread as part of the hit. Until the start of your next turn, you gain one of the following benefits against that target.
Follow the Sleeve: You may move 5 feet without provoking Opportunity Attacks from that target.
Tighten the Wrist: The target has disadvantage on the next Opportunity Attack it makes before the start of your next turn.
Draw the Guard: Your next Thread Attack against the target before the end of your next turn has advantage.
Weighted Knot: Add your Proficiency Bonus to the damage of the triggering attack. You can use Weighted Knot only once per round.
Threaded Strike is the common martial face of this sphere. Many Body Refiners learn Thread this way before ever projecting visible Qi Thread.

#### Base Ability - Listen Through Tension
Action Type: Bonus Action
Factory Combat Bucket: bonus_action
Factory Routing: combat_action_row
Range: One active Thread Line you maintain.
Cost: None.
Effect: You read vibration, breath, resistance, and movement through a Thread Line. Until the end of your next turn, choose one benefit against the connected target or object.
You know whether the target is moving closer, farther, or staying still.
You know whether the target is holding the line, cutting the line, or ignoring it.
You have advantage on one Wisdom (Insight), Wisdom (Perception), or Dexterity (Sleight of Hand) check involving the line.
If the target is Invisible but physically connected by a mundane or Qi Thread, you know its space until the line ends, though this does not by itself let you see the target.

### Dart Mechanism — Dart Pattern
Construct a spring, wire, blade, needle, bolt, or comparable projectile mechanism.
When triggered, choose one space occupied by the trap as the point of origin. The dart flies in a straight line up to 90 feet in a direction chosen when you set the trap.
The projectile stops at the first solid surface or creature in its path.
If the first creature in the path would be struck, make a ranged Cultivation Attack against that creature.
Hit: Deal Piercing damage.
Dart damage:
CL 1–4: 1d6
CL 5–10: 2d6
CL 11–16: 3d6
CL 17–20: 4d6

If the first creature in the path would be struck, make a ranged Cultivation Attack against that creature.
Hit: Deal Piercing damage.

spheres.full_exact_source_text: # Sphere of Trap Qi Expression: Primary — Prepared-Mechanism Qi; Supporting — Earth Qi, Metal Qi, Pattern Qi, Hidden Qi. “The first mistake was choosing a path. The second was believing it remained empty.” Sphere Type: Martial Sphere Primary Paths: Body Refining and Qi Cultivation Secondary Path: Spirit AwakeningOptional Power Variant: Script-Sealed Mechanist Resource: Martial Focus. Script-Sealed Mechanist uses CP instead. Common Effects: Temporary traps, darts, tripwires, snares, alarms, nets, consumable payloads, concealed deployment, battlefield preparation, trap chains, aerial rigging ### Trap Dao Trap is the cultivation of prepared consequence. A Trap cultivator studies routes, habits, impatience, pursuit, and the assumptions that make one square feel safer than another. A blade swung by hand is danger in the present moment. A trap is danger that was taught to wait. Ordinary Trap techniques remain physical mechanisms: wire, springs, blades, nets, hooks, alarms, irritants, consumable payloads, and preassembled devices. The optional Script-Sealed Mechanist variant changes Trap into a Restricted Power Sphere for practitioners who cultivate supernatural trapcraft. ## CORE TRAP RULES ### Trap Key Ability When you learn Trap, choose Dexterity or Intelligence as your Trap key ability. Use that ability for your Trap Cultivation Save DC and Trap Cultivation Attacks. A Path synergy may allow a different ability. ### Martial Focus Trap uses Martial Focus. you may hold one Martial Focus at a time; some talents expend Martial Focus; expending Martial Focus is not an Action; you cannot expend Martial Focus if you do not currently hold it; if a talent says you regain Martial Focus, you regain it only if it is currently absent. ### Trap Training When you learn Trap: gain proficiency with thieves’ tools; if already proficient, learn one Mortal Realm Trap talent for which you meet the prerequisites as a bonus talent; learn Set Trap; learn the Dart Mechanism, Tripwire, and Activation Trap patterns automatically. ### Set Trap Action Type: Ritual Procedure Canonical Action Type: Ritual Procedure Factory Routing: procedure_ledger_not_combat_action Timing Detail: 1 minute Range: Natural reach Requirement: Thieves’ tools and one solid surface or physically viable anchor point Duration: 1 hour or until triggered Cost: None Create one temporary trap in an unoccupied space within your reach. You may instead expend Martial Focus to set the trap as an Action. A trap placed this way lasts for 1 minute or until triggered. Choose: one trap pattern you know; one legal orientation, if the pattern requires one; one Trigger talent you know, if any; one Deployment talent you know, if any. Unless a talent says otherwise, a trap is destroyed after it triggers. #### Active Trap Limit You may maintain a number of active temporary traps equal to your Proficiency Bonus. If you exceed this limit, choose one older temporary trap to harmlessly fall apart. #### Trap Footprint A temporary trap occupies one or more contiguous 5-foot spaces. Maximum footprint: Mortal Realm, CL 1–4: one 5-foot space; Foundation Realm, CL 5–9: two contiguous 5-foot spaces; Core Formation Realm, CL 10–14: three contiguous 5-foot spaces; Nascent Soul Realm, CL 15+: four contiguous 5-foot spaces. Two of your traps cannot occupy the same space unless a talent explicitly allows it. #### Default Trigger Unless a talent says otherwise, a creature triggers one of your traps when it enters one of the trap’s spaces for the first time on a turn. A trap triggers only once from one creature’s movement, even if that creature crosses several spaces occupied by the same trap. #### Awareness A creature that sees you set a trap knows its spaces and obvious physical nature unless you use Sneaky Trapper. You may point out a trap to another creature without spending an Action if communication is possible. Knowing a trap’s location does not automatically disable it or allow a creature to ignore it. #### Finding a Concealed Trap A creature may take the Search Action and make a Wisdom (Perception) check against your Cultivation Save DC to notice one concealed trap within a physically reasonable search area. The GM may use Passive Perception to determine whether a creature notices a trap without actively searching. #### Disarming a Trap A creature aware of one of your traps may take the Utilize Action and make a Dexterity check using thieves’ tools against your Cultivation Save DC. Successful Check: The trap is disarmed and harmlessly falls apart. Any unused recoverable payload remains intact. Failed Check: The trap remains armed. If the failure is by 5 or more, the trap triggers if its pattern can legally affect the creature attempting to disarm it. You always succeed when disarming one of your own traps. #### Destroying a Trap A temporary trap is an object. Trap statistics: AC: Your Cultivation Save DC HP: 2 × your CL Object Rules: The trap follows ordinary object rules unless a talent says otherwise. Destroying a trap also destroys fragile payloads attached to it unless the GM rules that a particular item survives. #### Poison and Consumable Payloads A damage-dealing Dart Mechanism may carry one legal poison as though it were a weapon. Activation Trap may carry ordinary consumables as described in that pattern. A magical consumable, charged magic item, or technique-bearing item requires the Script-Sealed Mechanist variant and an appropriate Script talent. ## BASE TRAP PATTERNS ### Dart Mechanism — Dart Pattern Construct a spring, wire, blade, needle, bolt, or comparable projectile mechanism. When triggered, choose one space occupied by the trap as the point of origin. The dart flies in a straight line up to 90 feet in a direction chosen when you set the trap. The projectile stops at the first solid surface or creature in its path. If the first creature in the path would be struck, make a ranged Cultivation Attack against that creature. Hit: Deal Piercing damage. Dart damage: CL 1–4: 1d6 CL 5–10: 2d6 CL 11–16: 3d6 CL 17–20: 4d6 ### Tripwire — Snare Pattern Stretch wire, rope, thread, or a comparable low obstruction through the trap’s spaces. When a creature enters one of those spaces for the first time on a turn, it makes a Dexterity saving throw. Failed Save: The creature has the Prone condition. Successful Save: The creature avoids the effect and becomes aware of the trap. Tripwire is not destroyed when triggered. A creature aware of the Tripwire has Advantage on its saving throw against it. A creature that already has the Prone condition does not trigger Tripwire. ### Activation Trap — Snare Pattern Rig one ordinary consumable item to activate when the trap is triggered. Examples include: Alchemist’s Fire; Acid; Ball Bearings; Caltrops; dyes; perfumes; smoke pellets; noise-makers; appropriate ordinary Alchemy or Tinker consumables. When triggered, the item activates. If the item normally requires a target, target the triggering creature. If the item creates an area, its point of origin is one of the trap’s spaces, chosen when you set the trap. You may load multiple copies of the same consumable. Each trigger activates only one loaded item. Activation Trap remains armed while at least one loaded item remains. Unused recoverable items may be removed from a disarmed or expired trap. ## TRAP TALENT TAGS ### Dart Talents A Dart talent modifies Dart Mechanism. Unless a talent says otherwise, apply only one Dart talent to one Dart Mechanism. ### Snare Talents A Snare talent provides a new snare pattern or modifies one snare pattern. Unless a talent says otherwise, apply only one Snare talent to one trap. ### Trigger Talents A Trigger talent changes when or how one trap activates. Unless a talent says otherwise, apply only one Trigger talent to one trap. ### Deployment Talents A Deployment talent changes placement, duration, concealment, recovery, or physical delivery. ### Focus Talents A Focus talent recovers, expends, or modifies Martial Focus. ### Script Talents A Script talent is supernatural. Only a cultivator using Script-Sealed Mechanist may learn or use Script talents. ### Realm Evolutions A Realm Evolution represents wuxia trapcraft beyond ordinary mortal skill. ## MORTAL REALM TRAP TALENTS ### Aimed Shot — Dart Talent When you set Dart Mechanism, choose to target the creature that triggers the trap instead of firing along a fixed line. Increase the Dart damage die from d6 to d8. If you know a compatible Sniper talent, the GM may allow you to apply one compatible Sniper talent chosen when setting the trap. ### Blunt Dart — Dart Talent Your Dart Mechanism deals Bludgeoning damage and increases its damage die from d6 to d10. When this trap reduces a conscious and stable creature to 0 HP, you may choose for that creature to become Unconscious and stable rather than dying. ### Deadly Dart — Dart Talent Your Dart Mechanism deals Piercing or Slashing damage, chosen when the trap is set, and increases its damage die from d6 to d10. ### Net — Dart Talent, Snare Talent Create a weighted net, cable bundle, or entangling mechanism. #### Dart Use Replace the Dart Mechanism attack roll and damage with a Dexterity saving throw by the targeted creature. #### Snare Use A creature triggering the snare makes a Dexterity saving throw. #### Failed Save The creature has the Restrained condition until it escapes or the net is destroyed. A Restrained creature may take the Utilize Action to make a Strength (Athletics) or Dexterity (Acrobatics) check against your Cultivation Save DC, ending the condition on itself on a success. The net uses your trap’s AC and HP. ### Alarm Trap — Snare Talent Create a bell, clacker, whistle, snapped line, or comparable alarm. When triggered, the trap produces a loud noise audible within 300 feet. In a particularly quiet environment, the GM may increase this range. Alarm Trap does not harm the triggering creature. ### Flash Trap — Snare Talent Create a burst of powder, sparks, mirrored fragments, or another physically plausible blinding mechanism. When triggered, each creature within 5 feet of one of the trap’s spaces makes a Dexterity saving throw. Failed Save: The creature has the Blinded condition until the end of its next turn. Flash Trap is not magical unless a separate effect makes it magical. ### Noose — Snare Talent Create a tightening noose, cable loop, or constricting catch. When a creature triggers the snare, it makes a Dexterity saving throw. Failed Save: The creature has the Restrained condition. While Restrained by this noose, it also cannot speak, supply Verbal components, or breathe normally. The creature may escape as described by Net. A creature that does not breathe is still Restrained but ignores the breathing restriction. ### Terrain Trap — Snare Talent Create a scattered field of wire, hooks, caltrops, debris, or comparable hindering material. When triggered, create a 10-foot-radius area of Difficult Terrain centered on one corner of one trap space chosen when you set the trap. The Difficult Terrain lasts for 1 minute. You may choose to trigger Terrain Trap immediately when you set it. ### False Trigger — Trigger Talent Create a delayed trigger. The first time the trap would trigger, it instead produces an audible and obvious warning such as a click, snap, or sudden shift. The trap does not activate at that time. The next time it triggers before expiring: Dart Mechanism has Advantage on its attack roll; creatures have Disadvantage on saving throws caused by the trap. ### Remote Trigger — Trigger Talent While within 30 feet of one of your traps, use a Reaction to trigger it when one creature comes within 30 feet of the trap. The trap must still have a legal target or area for its pattern. Alternatively, when a creature makes a Dexterity saving throw against one of your traps within 30 feet, use a Reaction to impose Disadvantage on that saving throw. ### Warning Trigger — Trigger Talent When you set a trap, designate any number of creatures you can see and warn. A warned creature does not trigger that trap unless it chooses to. A creature may be warned later if it can see and hear you and you can identify the relevant trap clearly. ### Opportunist — Unique Trap Talent Action Type: Reaction Factory Combat Bucket: reaction Factory Routing: combat_action_row Trigger: A creature you can perceive triggers one of your traps within your weapon’s legal range Make one weapon attack or Unarmed Strike against that creature. Opportunist is not an Opportunity Attack unless another rule explicitly says otherwise. ### Persistent Trap — Deployment Talent You may spend 10 minutes setting a trap instead of 1 minute. A trap set this way lasts for 24 hours or until triggered. ### Razor Wire — Snare Talent When you set Tripwire, choose for it to deal Slashing damage to a creature that fails its saving throw. Razor Wire damage: CL 1–4: 1d6 CL 5–10: 2d6 CL 11–16: 3d6 CL 17–20: 4d6 ### Sneaky Trapper — Deployment Talent When you set a temporary trap while observed, make a Dexterity (Sleight of Hand) check contested by each observer’s Passive Perception. On a success against an observer, that observer does not automatically notice you setting the trap. Sneaky Trapper does not make a trap invisible. A creature may still notice the concealed trap normally. ### Trap Expert — Deployment Talent Gain Expertise with thieves’ tools. ### Trapper’s Recovery — Focus Talent Action Type: Reaction Factory Combat Bucket: reaction Factory Routing: combat_action_row Trigger: A creature you can perceive fails a saving throw against one of your traps or takes damage from one of your traps Regain Martial Focus. ## FOUNDATION REALM TRAP TALENTS ### Aerial Rigging — Trigger Talent, Realm Evolution Prerequisite: CL 5+ Your traps may threaten flying creatures above their occupied spaces. Aerial trigger height: CL 5–9: 10 feet CL 10–14: 20 feet CL 15+: 30 feet A trap can threaten aerial spaces only when its wires, hooks, launched net, overhead anchors, suspended mechanism, or terrain make that threat physically plausible. When an aerial trap causes a flying creature to gain the Prone condition or reduces its Fly Speed to 0, that creature falls unless it can Hover. When Net or Noose affects a hovering creature, pull that creature harmlessly into one of the trap’s spaces before applying the remaining effect. ### Stop, Drop, and Control — Deployment Talent Prerequisite: CL 5+ When you take the Disengage Action, expend Martial Focus to set one trap in an unoccupied space you move through during that turn. The trap lasts for 1 minute or until triggered. This placement does not require an additional Action. ### Trap Launcher — Deployment Talent Prerequisite: CL 5+ When you expend Martial Focus to set a trap as an Action, use a Bonus Action to launch the trap kit onto one physically viable surface within the normal range of one ranged weapon you wield. The projectile must have a legal route. Trap Launcher does not allow a trap to pass through Total Cover or attach to an unsupported space. ### Trap Wielder — Deployment Talent Prerequisite: CL 5+ When you expend Martial Focus to set a trap as an Action, place it directly in the space of one creature within your reach. The trap immediately triggers against that creature and then falls apart. A Snare affecting multiple creatures in one space affects each of those creatures normally. Trap Wielder does not leave an active trap behind. ### Trapped Shield — Deployment Talent Prerequisite: CL 5+ When you expend Martial Focus to set Dart Mechanism as an Action, attach that mechanism to a shield you wield instead of placing it on a surface. Action Type: Reaction Factory Combat Bucket: reaction Factory Routing: combat_action_row Trigger: A creature misses you with a melee attack while you wield the shield Trigger the Dart Mechanism against that attacker. If you know a compatible Shield-sphere technique, a Forged Technique may allow the trap to trigger through an appropriate Deflect effect without requiring an additional Reaction. ### Layered Mechanism — Deployment Talent Prerequisite: CL 7+ When setting a trap, expend Martial Focus to apply one additional compatible Dart, Snare, or Trigger talent to that trap. You cannot apply the same talent twice unless it explicitly says otherwise. The GM decides whether two physical mechanisms are compatible. ### Chained Mechanism — Trigger Talent Prerequisite: CL 7+ When one of your traps triggers, choose one other trap you set within 30 feet. If the second trap has a legal target or area, it triggers immediately after the first trap resolves. A trap may trigger only once per turn through Chained Mechanism. ## CORE FORMATION REALM TRAP TALENTS ### Court of the Hidden Nail — Martial Domain “The battlefield was not empty when you arrived. You were merely allowed to believe it was.” Prerequisite: CL 10+ Action Type: Bonus Action Factory Combat Bucket: bonus_action Factory Routing: combat_action_row Duration: 1 minute Cost: Expend Martial Focus Use Limit: Once per short or long rest Establish a 30-foot-radius Emanation centered on yourself. While the Court persists: your active trap limit increases by your Proficiency Bonus; once per turn, set one trap in an unoccupied space within your reach without spending an Action; a trap set this way lasts until the Court ends or until triggered; your warned allies do not trigger your traps inside the Court; when one of your traps triggers, move up to 5 feet without provoking Opportunity Attacks, or regain Martial Focus if it is absent; you know which of your traps inside the Court triggered, was disarmed, or was destroyed. Court of the Hidden Nail ends early if you have the Incapacitated condition. ### Interlocking Lattice — Deployment Talent Prerequisite: CL 10+ Increase your active temporary-trap limit by your Proficiency Bonus. When one of your traps is disarmed or destroyed, one other trap you set within 10 feet may remain concealed from the creature responsible until that creature takes the Search Action or triggers it. ### Pursuit Lattice — Deployment Talent Prerequisite: Stop, Drop, and Control, CL 10+ When you use Stop, Drop, and Control, set up to two traps in different unoccupied spaces you move through during that turn. Both traps count against your active trap limit. ### Falling-Sky Mechanism — Dart Talent, Realm Evolution Prerequisite: Aerial Rigging, CL 10+ When you set Dart Mechanism, orient it upward, downward, or diagonally through aerial spaces. If the dart hits a flying creature, that creature makes a Strength saving throw. Failed Save: Its Fly Speed becomes 0 until the start of its next turn. A creature that cannot Hover falls normally. ### Prepared Escape Route — Deployment Talent Prerequisite: CL 10+ When a trap you set triggers within 30 feet of you, use a Reaction to move up to half your Speed. This movement does not provoke Opportunity Attacks from the triggering creature. ## NASCENT SOUL REALM TRAP TALENTS ### Hundred-Mechanism Scripture — Realm Evolution Prerequisite: CL 15+ When you expend Martial Focus to set one trap as an Action, set up to three traps instead. Each trap must occupy different legal spaces within your reach. Each trap counts against your active trap limit. You may use Hundred-Mechanism Scripture once per short or long rest. ### Heaven-Net Battlefield — Snare Talent, Realm Evolution Prerequisite: Aerial Rigging, CL 15+ When you set Net or Terrain Trap, create a physically anchored lattice extending upward through the full height of Aerial Rigging. The trap affects legal aerial spaces throughout that height. A creature with a Fly Speed treats those spaces as Difficult Terrain while the lattice remains. A creature restrained by Heaven-Net Battlefield is pulled to the nearest legal anchored space rather than automatically falling. ### Trap Within the Trap — Trigger Talent Prerequisite: False Trigger, CL 15+ When False Trigger produces its warning sound, immediately place one additional trap in one unoccupied space within 5 feet of the original trap. The additional trap: must use a pattern you know; counts against your active trap limit; lasts for 1 minute or until triggered; cannot also use Trap Within the Trap. ### The Route Was Chosen Already — Deployment Talent Prerequisite: CL 17+ When Initiative is rolled, reveal up to your Proficiency Bonus concealed traps that you prepared during the previous hour. Each revealed trap must occupy a legal space within 60 feet that you could physically have reached during your preparation. A revealed trap counts against your active trap limit. This talent does not conjure traps into impossible locations. It represents advance planning, cached mechanisms, disguised components, and preparation so subtle that the battlefield seemed empty until the first breath of violence. Use this talent once per long rest. ## SECRET INHERITANCE ### The Empty Road Was Never Empty “A careless enemy enters a battlefield. A wise enemy asks who decided where the battlefield begins.” Prerequisite: Trap sphere, Court of the Hidden Nail, CL 17+ Action Type: Reaction Factory Combat Bucket: reaction Factory Routing: combat_action_row Trigger: Initiative is rolled, or one hostile creature enters a space within 60 feet that you can perceive Use Limit: Once per long rest For 1 minute, establish a 60-foot-radius Emanation centered on yourself. When you activate the inheritance, place a number of temporary traps equal to your Proficiency Bonus in legal unoccupied spaces within the Emanation. For the duration: your active trap limit increases by your Proficiency Bonus; each trap you set may use two compatible Trigger talents without expending Martial Focus; once per turn, after a hostile creature moves at least 5 feet inside the Emanation, relocate one untriggered trap you set to one legal unoccupied space within 10 feet of its previous location; a relocated trap remains physical and must have a plausible route, anchor, and mechanism; warned allies do not trigger your traps; you immediately know when one of your traps inside the Emanation triggers, is disarmed, or is destroyed. This inheritance does not create permanent infrastructure. It expresses preparation at mythic speed and scale for one decisive scene. ## OPTIONAL CULTIVATION VARIANTS ### Battle Trapper You may not leave inactive temporary traps on the battlefield. Gain Trap Wielder as a bonus talent, ignoring its CL prerequisite. Whenever you set a trap, it must immediately trigger against a legal creature or area and then fall apart. You may not learn Slow Worker. ### Focused Trapper Choose Dart or Snare. You may not set or use traps of the chosen category. Gain Trapper’s Recovery as a bonus talent. ### Slow Worker You cannot expend Martial Focus to set a trap as an Action. Gain Persistent Trap as a bonus talent. You may not learn Battle Trapper. ### Script-Sealed Mechanist Your Trap sphere becomes a Restricted Power Sphere for you. Use CP instead of Martial Focus. Whenever a Trap talent instructs you to expend Martial Focus, spend 1 CP instead. You may learn Script talents. Script-Sealed Mechanist does not automatically allow a trap to reproduce arbitrary Power-sphere effects. A Script talent, Forged Technique, item, or Formation project must explicitly permit the stored effect. A Body Refiner requires the Script-Bearing Body Cultivation Insight to learn Script-Sealed Mechanist. ## SCRIPT-SEALED MECHANIST TALENTS ### Magic Trigger — Script Talent Prerequisite: Script-Sealed Mechanist, CL 5+ Rig one magic item that requires activation into Activation Trap. If activating the item takes longer than an Action, setting the trap takes at least that long. If activation requires an ability check, make that check when setting the trap. When triggered: a targeted effect targets the triggering creature if legal; an area effect originates from one of the trap’s spaces chosen when set; a Cone or Line uses an orientation chosen when set; one charge or use is consumed normally. The trap remains armed while the item has legal remaining uses. When the trap ends, recover the item with its remaining charges or uses. Magic Trigger is magical. ### Scripted Release — Script Talent Prerequisite: Script-Sealed Mechanist, Magic Trigger, CL 10+ When you set Activation Trap, spend the CP cost of one compatible technique you know and store that technique inside the trap. The technique must: have an activation time of one Action or Bonus Action; target one creature or create an area with a legal point of origin; have an instantaneous duration or Concentration duration no longer than 1 minute; be approved by the GM as physically and metaphysically compatible with a prepared trigger. When the trap triggers, release the technique from the trap’s space. If the technique requires Concentration, you begin Concentrating when the trap triggers. If you cannot Concentrate at that moment, the technique fails. A trap can store only one technique through Scripted Release. ### Thaumic Sink — Script Talent, Secret Technique Prerequisite: Script-Sealed Mechanist, CL 17+ Cost: 8 CP Use Limit: Once per long rest Create an antimagic trap. Choose one form when setting the trap. #### Dart Form On a hit, the target is affected as though inside an Antimagic Field until the end of your next turn. A creature may take the Utilize Action to remove the embedded dart, ending the effect on itself and taking Piercing damage equal to the Dart Mechanism’s minimum possible damage. #### Snare Form When triggered, create a 10-foot-radius Sphere centered on one trap space. The area functions as Antimagic Field until the end of your next turn. Thaumic Sink is a magical effect. ## PATH SYNERGIES ### Body Refining — Muscle-Memory Rigging You may use Constitution as your Trap key ability. When you expend Martial Focus to set a trap as an Action, place it in one legal unoccupied space within your reach or one legal unoccupied space you moved through during the current turn. Your ordinary Trap sphere remains Martial and does not require a Cultivation Insight. ### Qi Cultivation — Measured Mechanism You may use Intelligence as your Trap key ability. When you set Dart Mechanism, choose its fixed orientation when the trap triggers rather than when you set it. You must be able to perceive the trap when choosing its orientation. This represents prepared swivels, tension control, and refined timing. It does not allow the dart to bend around corners or pass through Total Cover. ### Spirit Awakening — Patient Hunter’s Awareness You may use Wisdom as your Trap key ability. When one of your traps within 1 mile triggers, is disarmed, or is destroyed, you know: which trap was affected; its approximate direction; whether it triggered, was disarmed, or was destroyed. This awareness does not reveal the identity, exact square, or current location of any creature involved. ## CULTIVATION INSIGHTS ### Script-Bearing Body Prerequisite: Body Refining, Trap sphere You may learn Script-Sealed Mechanist. Use Constitution as your key ability and Stamina instead of CP for Script talents. This Insight does not make a magical trap body-contained. It is an explicit rare-access exception allowing a Body Refiner to cultivate supernatural trap scripts outside the body. ### Formation Trapwright Prerequisite: Trap sphere Gain Advantage on Cultivation Checks made to design, repair, study, or contribute to long-term trap arrays and defensive Formation projects. This Insight does not create a permanent array automatically. ### Prepared Arsenal Prerequisite: Trap sphere Increase your active temporary-trap limit by 1. Learn one Mortal Realm Deployment or Trigger talent for which you meet the prerequisites. ### Battlefield Engineer Prerequisite: Trap sphere Gain proficiency in one: Sleight of Hand; Investigation; Perception; Survival; one appropriate artisan’s tool. If already proficient in the chosen option, gain Expertise instead.

When triggered, choose one space occupied by the trap as the point of origin. The dart flies in a straight line up to 90 feet in a direction chosen when you set the trap.
The projectile stops at the first solid surface or creature in its path.
If the first creature in the path would be struck, make a ranged Cultivation Attack against that creature.
Hit: Deal Piercing damage.
Dart damage:
CL 1–4: 1d6
CL 5–10: 2d6
CL 11–16: 3d6
CL 17–20: 4d6

When a creature enters one of those spaces for the first time on a turn, it makes a Dexterity saving throw.

Successful Save: The creature avoids the effect and becomes aware of the trap.
Tripwire is not destroyed when triggered.
A creature aware of the Tripwire has Advantage on its saving throw against it.
A creature that already has the Prone condition does not trigger Tripwire.

automatic_base_abilities.effect:
### Black Trace
**Action Type:** Action
**Range:** 30 feet
**Target:** One creature or object you can see
**Cost:** None
Make a ranged Cultivation Attack.
On hit, the target takes Ruin damage based on your Realm.
| Realm | Safe Black Trace Damage |
|---|---:|
| Mortal | 1d10 + your Unmaking key ability modifier |
| Foundation | 2d10 + your Unmaking key ability modifier |
| Core Formation | 3d10 + your Unmaking key ability modifier |
| Nascent Soul | 4d10 + your Unmaking key ability modifier |
On hit, choose one Trace effect:
**Fray.** The target cannot regain HP until the start of your next turn.
**Crack.** If the target is an object, construct, armor, shield, barrier, or temporary qi structure, it takes additional Ruin damage equal to your Proficiency Bonus.
**Sting.** The target cannot take Reactions against you until the start of your next turn.
**Mark.** The next Unmaking talent that damages the target before the end of your next turn deals additional Ruin damage equal to your Proficiency Bonus.
You may Overdraw when Black Trace hits.
#### Unbound Trace
Before making the Black Trace attack, you may make the Trace unstable.
On hit, the damage becomes the Unbound Trace value instead.
| Realm | Unbound Trace Damage |
|---|---:|
| Mortal | 2d10 + your Unmaking key ability modifier |
| Foundation | 4d10 + your Unmaking key ability modifier |
| Core Formation | 6d10 + your Unmaking key ability modifier |
| Nascent Soul | 8d10 + your Unmaking key ability modifier |
After the attack resolves, whether it hits or misses, choose one:
- gain 1 Black Vein Strain;
- take Ruin self-damage equal to **1d6 + your Proficiency Bonus**;
- one suitable focus, needle, talisman, weapon, or External Channel gains 1 Crack.
You may Overdraw when Unbound Trace hits.
---

automatic_base_abilities.effect:
### Ruin Channel
**Action Type:** Bonus Action
**Range:** Self or touch
**Cost:** None
**Duration:** Until the start of your next turn
You run Unmaking qi through one Channel you are touching.
Choose one:
- a held weapon;
- an unarmed strike;
- one hand or limb;
- a talisman, needle, chain, or tool;
- another object the GM agrees can briefly hold Unmaking qi.
The next time before the duration ends that you hit with that Channel, deal additional Ruin damage based on your Realm.
| Realm | Ruin Channel Bonus Damage |
|---|---:|
| Mortal | 2d8 |
| Foundation | 3d8 |
| Core Formation | 5d8 |
| Nascent Soul | 7d8 |
After the attack resolves, choose one cost:
- the Channel gains 1 Crack if it is an External Channel;
- you gain 1 Black Vein Strain if it is an Internal Channel;
- you take Ruin self-damage equal to **1d6 + your Proficiency Bonus**, and the Channel does not gain Crack or Strain.
If the attack misses, the Channel remains active until the duration ends. If the duration ends without a hit, you take Ruin self-damage equal to your Proficiency Bonus.
Ruin Channel may be applied to a ranged weapon, thrown weapon, or ammunition only if you are touching it when you use the feature.
You may Overdraw when a Ruin Channel attack hits.
