### Base Sphere Abilities
When you first gain the Sphere of Wax, you gain Mold Wax, Press Seal, and Kindle Wax.
You also learn one Wax talent of your choice.
#### Mold Wax
Action. Range 60 feet. Cost 1 CP. Duration Concentration, up to 1 minute.
You create or awaken cultivated wax in an unoccupied space, on a surface, or over an unattended object within range. Choose one form.
Soft Spread. You create a 10-foot square of Soft Wax on a surface. The area is Difficult Terrain for hostile creatures. The first hostile creature each round that enters the area or starts its turn there must succeed on a Dexterity saving throw or become impressed by the wax until the end of your next turn.
Set Shape. You create a Set Wax panel, ramp, handhold, brace, small bridge, shield plate, low wall, or similar structure that fits within two contiguous 5-foot cubes. It must be supported by a surface unless a talent says otherwise. It can provide cover, block a narrow passage, support weight, or create a short ramp or platform.
Fine Work. Outside initiative, you can shape wax into seals, molds, masks, tablets, candle forms, practice tools, ritual counters, labels, evidence casts, and small sculptures. Fine Work cannot create valuable trade goods, magical items, living organs, or permanent infrastructure unless the GM says otherwise.
At CL 5, your Soft Spread can cover a 15-foot square, or your Set Shape can fit within four contiguous 5-foot cubes.
At CL 10, your Soft Spread can cover a 20-foot square, or your Set Shape can fit within six contiguous 5-foot cubes.
At CL 15, your Soft Spread can cover a 25-foot square, or your Set Shape can fit within eight contiguous 5-foot cubes.
#### Press Seal
Action. Range 30 feet. Cost 1 CP. Duration 1 minute.
You press or throw a cultivated Wax Seal onto one creature, object, surface, or 5-foot space within range. A willing creature, unattended object, or surface is sealed automatically. An unwilling creature or attended object makes a Dexterity saving throw. On a failure, the seal attaches. On a success, the seal fails.
When you place the seal, choose one base seal.
Clinging Seal. The sealed creature’s Speed is reduced by 10 feet while the seal remains. If placed on an object, the object adheres to the surface it touches and requires an Action and a successful Strength check against your Cultivation Save DC to remove.
Witness Seal. The seal records the next creature other than you that touches, opens, damages, moves, or passes through the sealed target. You know that the seal was triggered if you are within 1 mile, and you can later inspect the seal to see the outline, handprint, footprint, tool mark, weapon shape, or other physical Impression left behind.
Closing Seal. The seal holds a door, lid, drawer, container, wound wrapping, sheath, scroll case, coffin, or similar closure shut. Opening it requires an Action and a successful Strength check or Dexterity check with appropriate tools against your Cultivation Save DC. A creature can also destroy the seal normally.
Preserving Seal. The sealed object, corpse, medicine, food, blood sample, written page, track, footprint, wound dressing, or physical clue resists decay, contamination, smearing, and ordinary weather while the seal remains.
#### Kindle Wax
Bonus Action. Range 60 feet. Cost 0 CP.
You burn one Wax form, Wax Seal, candle, or wax object you created within range. The chosen wax is consumed. Choose one base release.
Candleflare. One creature within 5 feet of the kindled wax makes a Dexterity saving throw. On a failure, it takes fire damage equal to 1d6 + your Proficiency Bonus. On a success, it takes half damage.
Smoke Puff. The wax releases thick smoke in a 5-foot radius until the start of your next turn. The area is Lightly Obscured. This smoke is ordinary smoke once released and can be dispersed by strong wind.
Release Seal. If the kindled wax was a Wax Seal on an ally, the ally gains temporary hit points equal to your Proficiency Bonus. If it was a Wax Seal on an enemy, that enemy takes fire damage equal to your Proficiency Bonus.
Mark the Wick. You learn whether the wax had been touched, moved, damaged, or disturbed since you created it. If it held an Impression, you preserve a brief sensory image of the Impression before the wax burns.

automatic_base_abilities.effect:
#### Press Seal
Action. Range 30 feet. Cost 1 CP. Duration 1 minute.
You press or throw a cultivated Wax Seal onto one creature, object, surface, or 5-foot space within range. A willing creature, unattended object, or surface is sealed automatically. An unwilling creature or attended object makes a Dexterity saving throw. On a failure, the seal attaches. On a success, the seal fails.
When you place the seal, choose one base seal.
Clinging Seal. The sealed creature’s Speed is reduced by 10 feet while the seal remains. If placed on an object, the object adheres to the surface it touches and requires an Action and a successful Strength check against your Cultivation Save DC to remove.
Witness Seal. The seal records the next creature other than you that touches, opens, damages, moves, or passes through the sealed target. You know that the seal was triggered if you are within 1 mile, and you can later inspect the seal to see the outline, handprint, footprint, tool mark, weapon shape, or other physical Impression left behind.
Closing Seal. The seal holds a door, lid, drawer, container, wound wrapping, sheath, scroll case, coffin, or similar closure shut. Opening it requires an Action and a successful Strength check or Dexterity check with appropriate tools against your Cultivation Save DC. A creature can also destroy the seal normally.
Preserving Seal. The sealed object, corpse, medicine, food, blood sample, written page, track, footprint, wound dressing, or physical clue resists decay, contamination, smearing, and ordinary weather while the seal remains.

spheres.full_exact_source_text: # Sphere of Wax Qi Expression: Primary — Wax Qi; Supporting — Soft-Form Qi, Fire-Melt Qi, Seal Qi, Preservation Qi. Sphere Type: Restricted Power / Material Memory / Sealing Sphere Primary Path: Qi Cultivation Secondary Path: Spirit Awakening Rare Access: Body Refining through Wax-Tempered Body, Candle-Flesh Body, or comparable internal wax practice Resource: CP, prepared wax, candles, impressions, seals, effigies, sacrificial burning, and Concentration when a talent says so Core Chassis: Yielding form, wax medium, impressions, sealing, molded barriers, effigies Wax does not win by being harder than the world. Wax wins by receiving the world’s pressure, remembering its shape, and deciding when that shape becomes law. Sphere Type: Restricted Power Sphere with strong utility, battlefield control, sealing, preservation, and effigy branches. Primary Path: Qi Cultivation. Secondary Path: Spirit Awakening. Rare Body Access: Body Refining through Wax-Tempered Body or Candle-Flesh Body. Core Dao: Wax is the cultivation of yielding form. Common Effects: molded wax, adhesive terrain, temporary walls, seals, impressions, masks, preservation, candles, sacrificial burning, funeral rites, waxen armor, and sympathetic effigies. ### Player Summary Wax cultivators practice the art of material memory. They soften wax, receive an impression, set the chosen shape, seal what must remain, and burn what has been prepared. Wax is clever, tactile, and deliberate. Its strongest effects are visible or prepared, and enemies can answer them by cutting, burning, melting, breaking, scraping, bypassing, or avoiding the wax before the seal sets. ### Sphere Boundaries Wax governs soft material that can be shaped, sealed, impressed, preserved, hardened, softened, and burned. Wax does not broadly create any object in the world. Wax can make temporary wax objects, seals, masks, ramps, walls, coatings, and ritual forms. It cannot replace the full Creation sphere. Wax does not control all fire. Wax may kindle its own wax, candles, seals, and prepared wicks. It does not hurl generic fire, control enemy flames, or become a broad Fire sphere. Wax does not replace Protection. Wax can create material shelter and preservation rites, but its barriers are visible, breakable, burnable, and shaped from a specific substance. Wax does not replace Puppetry. Wax effigies create sympathetic links, memory vessels, or temporary wax attendants. Ordinary Wax talents do not seize a living creature’s actions. Wax does not replace Illusion. Wax masks, figures, and false bodies are physical objects. They can deceive by craft, not by rewriting perception. Wax does not replace Blood or Spirit. Wax can preserve a trace, impression, name-seal, or funeral candle, but it does not read bloodlines or command souls unless a talent explicitly says so. Wax can support Formations. Wax is excellent for seal halls, evidence archives, candle roads, funeral vaults, preserving clinics, and wax labyrinths. Permanent sect infrastructure requires GM approval unless a talent explicitly creates a temporary combat-scale effect. ### Wax and Fire Wax and Fire overlap at the wick. Wax uses fire as a trigger, sacrifice, warning, and release. A Wax cultivator may burn their own prepared wax or candle structures to release a talent’s effect. That does not grant general command over flame. Fire is also Wax’s most obvious counter. Ordinary wax burns. Cultivated wax resists casual flame, but Fire techniques, intense heat, and focused attacks can melt, soften, or destroy Wax structures unless the Wax cultivator has Temper talents. ### Wax and Protection Wax protects by shaping material into a useful answer. Protection protects because the cultivator has declared what must not break. A wax wall, shroud, or shell can keep someone alive, but it remains a material solution. It can be cut, scorched, opened, bypassed, or broken. Protection should remain better at pure warding, sacred shelter, and reliable defense. Wax should be better at seals, evidence, temporary shaped structures, preservation, and preparation. ### Wax and Effigies Effigy work is the most dangerous part of Wax. A wax figure may preserve a likeness, receive a name-seal, carry a message, hold a trace, or serve as a ritual focus. It does not automatically control the creature it resembles. Any Wax talent that affects a creature through an effigy must say so explicitly. Compulsory action, possession, mind control, and remote bodily domination are outside ordinary Wax and require Puppetry, Mind, Spirit, Blood, Fate, or a forbidden Wax talent approved by the GM. ### Core Wax Rules #### Wax Save DC When a Wax talent requires a saving throw, use your Cultivation Save DC unless a feature says otherwise. #### Cultivated Wax Wax talents produce or awaken cultivated wax. This wax can appear as beeswax, white sealing wax, red legal wax, black funerary wax, golden medicinal wax, translucent spirit-wax, or another form appropriate to the cultivator’s scripture. Cultivated wax is visibly supernatural. It may carry fragrance, faint candlelight, embedded script, cold funeral stillness, medicinal warmth, or sect-colored seals. Unless a talent says otherwise, cultivated wax created for combat lasts for 1 minute, until destroyed, or until you dismiss it with no action on your turn. #### Soft Wax Soft Wax yields and clings. Soft Wax is used for adhesive terrain, impressions, ramps, footprints, cushioning, and shaping. Areas of Soft Wax are normally Difficult Terrain for hostile creatures. A creature that falls Prone in Soft Wax or is pushed through it may be targeted by talents that require an impressed creature. #### Set Wax Set Wax holds shape. Set Wax is used for barriers, shells, seals, cages, ramps, plaques, masks, and temporary structures. It is not as hard as stone or metal, but it is quick to shape and excellent at receiving written law. Unless a talent gives a different value, each 5-foot section of Set Wax has AC 12 + your Proficiency Bonus and hit points equal to 5 + twice your Cultivation Level. It is immune to poison and psychic damage. It has vulnerability to fire damage unless you have a Temper talent that removes this vulnerability. #### Tempered Wax Some talents create Tempered Wax. Tempered Wax does not have vulnerability to fire damage. It resists casual melting, rain, minor heat, and ordinary handling. Tempered Wax still remains wax. It can be destroyed, dispelled, cut, shattered, or overcome by sufficient magical fire, heat, force, or specialized tools. #### Impressions When a creature, object, weapon, hand, foot, key, face, wound, or aura presses into cultivated wax, it may leave an Impression. An Impression is not a full divination. It is physical and symbolic evidence. A Wax cultivator can use it to identify shapes, preserve tracks, build masks, prove a contact, trigger seals, or support effigy rites. A creature is impressed by your Wax when one of the following happens: it starts its turn in an area of your Soft Wax; it enters your Soft Wax for the first time on a turn; it fails a save against one of your Wax talents; it is hit by one of your Wax talents; it willingly presses a body part, object, or token into your cultivated wax; a talent explicitly says it creates an Impression. Unless a talent says otherwise, a combat Impression lasts for 1 minute. #### Wax Seals A Wax Seal is a patch, stamp, ribbon, bead, plaque, cord, candle-mark, or written strip of wax bearing the cultivator’s qi. A Wax Seal may be placed on a willing creature, unattended object, surface, door, container, corpse, wound, weapon, or area without a saving throw. When placed on an unwilling creature or an attended object, the target makes a Dexterity saving throw. On a failure, the seal adheres. On a success, the seal fails to attach. A sealed creature can use its Action to scrape, break, burn, or tear away one Wax Seal affecting it by succeeding on a Strength (Athletics), Dexterity (Sleight of Hand), or Dexterity saving throw against your Cultivation Save DC. A creature adjacent to the sealed creature can use its Action to attempt the same check. #### Kindle Wax Many Wax talents have the Wick tag. A Wick talent burns prepared wax to release a stored effect. Unless a talent says otherwise, kindling your own Wax effect requires a Bonus Action and affects one Wax form, Wax Seal, candle, effigy, or wax object you created within 60 feet. The chosen wax is consumed, destroyed, or reduced to harmless residue after the Wick effect resolves. Kindling Wax is not general fire control. It uses wax as fuel, trigger, and ritual medium. #### Wax and Light Wax candles can shed dim or bright light as described by the talent that creates them. Ordinary illumination is not the main power of Wax. Candlelight matters because it marks thresholds, wakes memories, anchors funeral rites, guides allies, and burns seals. #### Wax and Prepared Stock Wax cultivators are expected to carry wax, stamps, oils, wicks, seal-knives, molds, and small storage boxes. These are ordinary implements, not expensive components, unless a talent or GM says otherwise. A Wax cultivator deprived of all wax implements can still create cultivated wax through CP, but may be unable to use mundane crafting, legal seals, disguise work, or ritual preparation until tools are replaced. ### Base Sphere Abilities When you first gain the Sphere of Wax, you gain Mold Wax, Press Seal, and Kindle Wax. You also learn one Wax talent of your choice. #### Mold Wax Action. Range 60 feet. Cost 1 CP. Duration Concentration, up to 1 minute. You create or awaken cultivated wax in an unoccupied space, on a surface, or over an unattended object within range. Choose one form. Soft Spread. You create a 10-foot square of Soft Wax on a surface. The area is Difficult Terrain for hostile creatures. The first hostile creature each round that enters the area or starts its turn there must succeed on a Dexterity saving throw or become impressed by the wax until the end of your next turn. Set Shape. You create a Set Wax panel, ramp, handhold, brace, small bridge, shield plate, low wall, or similar structure that fits within two contiguous 5-foot cubes. It must be supported by a surface unless a talent says otherwise. It can provide cover, block a narrow passage, support weight, or create a short ramp or platform. Fine Work. Outside initiative, you can shape wax into seals, molds, masks, tablets, candle forms, practice tools, ritual counters, labels, evidence casts, and small sculptures. Fine Work cannot create valuable trade goods, magical items, living organs, or permanent infrastructure unless the GM says otherwise. At CL 5, your Soft Spread can cover a 15-foot square, or your Set Shape can fit within four contiguous 5-foot cubes. At CL 10, your Soft Spread can cover a 20-foot square, or your Set Shape can fit within six contiguous 5-foot cubes. At CL 15, your Soft Spread can cover a 25-foot square, or your Set Shape can fit within eight contiguous 5-foot cubes. #### Press Seal Action. Range 30 feet. Cost 1 CP. Duration 1 minute. You press or throw a cultivated Wax Seal onto one creature, object, surface, or 5-foot space within range. A willing creature, unattended object, or surface is sealed automatically. An unwilling creature or attended object makes a Dexterity saving throw. On a failure, the seal attaches. On a success, the seal fails. When you place the seal, choose one base seal. Clinging Seal. The sealed creature’s Speed is reduced by 10 feet while the seal remains. If placed on an object, the object adheres to the surface it touches and requires an Action and a successful Strength check against your Cultivation Save DC to remove. Witness Seal. The seal records the next creature other than you that touches, opens, damages, moves, or passes through the sealed target. You know that the seal was triggered if you are within 1 mile, and you can later inspect the seal to see the outline, handprint, footprint, tool mark, weapon shape, or other physical Impression left behind. Closing Seal. The seal holds a door, lid, drawer, container, wound wrapping, sheath, scroll case, coffin, or similar closure shut. Opening it requires an Action and a successful Strength check or Dexterity check with appropriate tools against your Cultivation Save DC. A creature can also destroy the seal normally. Preserving Seal. The sealed object, corpse, medicine, food, blood sample, written page, track, footprint, wound dressing, or physical clue resists decay, contamination, smearing, and ordinary weather while the seal remains. #### Kindle Wax Bonus Action. Range 60 feet. Cost 0 CP. You burn one Wax form, Wax Seal, candle, or wax object you created within range. The chosen wax is consumed. Choose one base release. Candleflare. One creature within 5 feet of the kindled wax makes a Dexterity saving throw. On a failure, it takes fire damage equal to 1d6 + your Proficiency Bonus. On a success, it takes half damage. Smoke Puff. The wax releases thick smoke in a 5-foot radius until the start of your next turn. The area is Lightly Obscured. This smoke is ordinary smoke once released and can be dispersed by strong wind. Release Seal. If the kindled wax was a Wax Seal on an ally, the ally gains temporary hit points equal to your Proficiency Bonus. If it was a Wax Seal on an enemy, that enemy takes fire damage equal to your Proficiency Bonus. Mark the Wick. You learn whether the wax had been touched, moved, damaged, or disturbed since you created it. If it held an Impression, you preserve a brief sensory image of the Impression before the wax burns. ### Wax Talent Tags Mold talents improve Mold Wax or add new wax forms. Seal talents improve Press Seal or add new seals. Wick talents improve Kindle Wax or add new releases. Temper talents change how wax resists fire, cold, cutting, dispelling, time, or pressure. Effigy talents use physical likenesses, impressions, masks, funeral figures, or wax attendants. Rite talents are stronger preparation or noncombat techniques. A Rite usually takes 10 minutes or more unless used through a special combat talent. Forbidden talents are marked when they create sympathetic harm, tamper with identity, or disturb the dead. ### Mortal Realm Wax Talents #### Adhesive Pool - Mold Talent When you create Soft Spread, you may make it adhesive. The first hostile creature each round that enters the area, starts its turn there, or is knocked Prone there must succeed on a Strength saving throw or have its Speed reduced to 0 until the start of its next turn. A creature affected by Adhesive Pool is impressed by the wax. #### Wax Rampart - Mold Talent When you create Set Shape, you may create a sturdier rampart. The Set Wax gains additional hit points equal to your Cultivation Level, and creatures behind it may use it as half cover if its position would reasonably protect them. At CL 5, a rampart can instead provide three-quarters cover to a creature directly behind it, but each 5-foot section used this way counts as two sections of your Set Shape. #### Sculpted Implements - Mold Talent You may use Fine Work to create temporary wax tools, keys, wedges, handles, medical splints, practice weapons, stamps, labels, ritual counters, lock impressions, and evidence casts. These implements are not metal and cannot replace specialized high-quality tools for every purpose. They can, however, grant advantage on checks to preserve evidence, copy an impression, mark a sealed object, splint an injury, create a temporary handle, or test whether a key shape fits a lock. #### Waxen Trail - Seal Talent When a sealed creature moves, you may choose to have the seal leave a faint wax thread, scent, footprint line, or candle-colored trace. For the duration, you have advantage on Wisdom (Survival) or Intelligence (Investigation) checks made to track that creature through ordinary terrain. If the creature teleports, turns invisible, or changes shape while sealed, the seal snaps and leaves an obvious wax mark at the point of departure. #### Quiet Seal - Seal Talent You can place a Wax Seal without obvious light, heat, scent, or sound. A creature observing the target can still notice the seal with a Wisdom (Perception) or Intelligence (Investigation) check against your Cultivation Save DC. You have advantage on checks made to hide Wax Seals among legal seals, candle drippings, wax repairs, cosmetics, medicine, funeral wrappings, or household objects. #### Clinging Seal - Seal Augment When a creature fails its saving throw against Press Seal, you may spend 1 additional CP to strengthen the seal. Until the seal ends, the target cannot benefit from the Dash action unless it first uses its Action to attempt to remove the seal. #### Lingering Seal - Seal Augment When a Wax Seal would end because its duration expires, you may spend 1 CP to extend it for 10 minutes if it is on a surface, object, willing creature, corpse, or unattended item. This cannot extend a hostile creature’s combat seal unless a higher-Realm talent says otherwise. #### Seal Wound - Unique Wax Talent Action. Touch. Cost 1 CP. You seal a wound with medicinal wax, pressure, and qi. The target gains temporary hit points equal to 1d6 + your Proficiency Bonus. If the target is bleeding, suffering from a mundane open wound, or taking ongoing damage from a wound effect that can be physically sealed, the GM may allow the target to make a new saving throw or ability check to end that effect. This is not general healing. It is emergency closure, preservation, and stabilization. #### Waxen Shell - Unique Wax Talent Action. Range Touch. Cost 1 CP. Duration 1 minute. You coat a willing creature in a flexible wax shell. The target gains temporary hit points equal to your Proficiency Bonus + your key ability modifier. While any of these temporary hit points remain, the target has advantage on saving throws against being moved by wind, water, ordinary slippery terrain, or minor forced movement caused by unstable footing. The shell is visible and may impose disadvantage on checks requiring delicate touch if the GM judges the wax would interfere. #### Wax Mask - Effigy Rite Rite. 10 minutes. Range Touch. Cost 1 CP. You sculpt a physical wax mask, prosthetic feature, false scar, false handprint, or ceremonial face. A creature wearing the mask gains advantage on one Charisma (Deception), Dexterity (Sleight of Hand), or disguise kit check made to pass a casual visual inspection. The mask does not change voice, body shape, scent, gait, aura, cultivation pressure, or behavior. Close inspection can reveal it as a physical disguise. If made from a true Impression of a creature’s face, hand, or identifying feature, the mask is more convincing but may be considered suspicious, illegal, or forbidden in many sects. #### Smoke Wick - Wick Talent When you use Smoke Puff, the smoke fills a 10-foot radius instead of a 5-foot radius. The area is Heavily Obscured until the start of your next turn, then becomes Lightly Obscured until the end of your next turn. Creatures that do not need to breathe can still have their sight blocked by the smoke. #### Guiding Candle - Wick Talent You can create a small cultivated candle as part of Mold Wax or Press Seal. The candle burns for 1 hour, sheds bright light in a 10-foot radius and dim light for another 10 feet, and is visible only as ordinary candlelight unless examined with supernatural senses. As a Bonus Action, you may cause one Guiding Candle within 60 feet to flare. Until the start of your next turn, allies who can see the candle ignore nonmagical Difficult Terrain in a 10-foot radius around it. #### Melting Rebuke - Wick Talent Reaction. Trigger: A creature within 5 feet of one of your Wax forms damages it with a melee attack or starts to tear away one of your Wax Seals. You kindle that wax. The triggering creature makes a Dexterity saving throw. On a failure, it takes fire damage equal to 1d8 + your Proficiency Bonus and is impressed by the wax until the end of its next turn. On a success, it takes half damage and is not impressed. #### Medicinal Wax - Unique Wax Talent When you use Seal Wound or Waxen Shell, choose one of the following medicinal preparations. Cooling Wax. The target has advantage on the next saving throw it makes before the end of your next turn against fire, poison, or disease. Stimulating Wax. The target’s Speed increases by 10 feet until the end of its next turn. Numbing Wax. The first time before the end of your next turn that the target takes damage, reduce that damage by your Proficiency Bonus. ### Foundation Realm Wax Talents #### Greater Mold - Mold Evolution Prerequisite: CL 5. Your Mold Wax improves. When you create Soft Spread, increase one side of the area by 10 feet. When you create Set Shape, you may create two separate Set Wax structures within range, each no larger than half your normal Set Shape limit. You may also create stairs, handrails, short bridges, wax curtains, false walls, ramps, seals across multiple panels, or simple furniture appropriate to the available volume. #### Wax Cage - Mold Talent Prerequisite: CL 5. Action. Range 60 feet. Cost 2 CP. Duration Concentration, up to 1 minute. You create bars, sheets, cords, or lattices of Set Wax around one Large or smaller creature within range. The target makes a Dexterity saving throw. On a failure, it is Restrained by the wax. On a success, it moves to the nearest unoccupied space of its choice outside the cage and is not restrained. A restrained creature can use its Action to attempt a Strength (Athletics) or Dexterity (Acrobatics) check against your Cultivation Save DC, ending the restraint on a success. The cage can also be destroyed. Wax Cage is visibly material. It can be cut, burned, broken, or bypassed by teleportation unless another talent prevents that. #### Waxen Bulwark - Mold Talent Prerequisite: CL 5. When you create a Wax Rampart, you may spend 1 additional CP to make it a bulwark. Allies adjacent to the bulwark when it appears gain temporary hit points equal to your Proficiency Bonus. Until the bulwark is destroyed or the effect ends, the first ally each round who starts their turn adjacent to it may choose to gain half cover until the start of their next turn, even if the bulwark would normally provide only partial protection. #### Flowing Wax Step - Unique Wax Talent Prerequisite: CL 5. Bonus Action. Cost 1 CP. You soften wax under your own feet and ride its yielding surface. Until the end of your turn, you ignore Difficult Terrain created by wax, mud, snow, shallow water, slick stone, or similar yielding surfaces. If you move through your own Soft Wax this turn, your movement does not provoke Opportunity Attacks from creatures standing in that wax. #### Borrowed Countenance - Effigy Talent Prerequisite: CL 5, Wax Mask. When you create a Wax Mask from a true Impression of a creature’s face, hand, or identifying mark, the wearer may also imitate one physical sign of that creature: a handprint, a facial profile, a scar pattern, a lip shape, a bite pattern, or similar visible evidence. The mask still does not alter voice, aura, cultivation pressure, memories, scent, or actual identity. Magical scrutiny, close social interaction, or careful inspection can expose the deception. Using this talent for impersonation may be illegal, dishonorable, or forbidden in many sects. #### Preserving Shroud - Seal Rite Prerequisite: CL 5. Rite. 10 minutes. Range Touch. Cost 2 CP. Duration 24 hours. You wrap a willing creature, corpse, medicine, rare specimen, document, spiritual trace, or physical clue in preserving wax and cloth. For the duration, the target resists ordinary decay, contamination, rot, weathering, insects, drying, smearing, and casual handling. If used on a living creature, the target gains advantage on saving throws against disease and poison for the duration, but its Speed is reduced by 10 feet while fully shrouded. If used on a corpse or trace, the shroud preserves evidence. It does not prevent resurrection limits, command souls, or halt supernatural decay unless the GM allows it. #### Wax Effigy - Effigy Rite Prerequisite: CL 5. Rite. 10 minutes. Range Touch. Cost 2 CP. Duration 24 hours. You sculpt a small wax effigy of a creature, place, object, wound, oath, or event. The effigy must be based on a true Impression, eyewitness description, personal token, name-seal, or significant physical sample. Choose one function. Memory Vessel. A creature who studies the effigy has advantage on one Intelligence check made to recall, recognize, reconstruct, or explain the subject represented by the effigy. Message Vessel. You may record a short spoken message, image, gesture, or emotional impression into the effigy. The first creature you designate who touches the effigy receives the message. Ritual Focus. The effigy can serve as a focus for a later Wax, Spirit, Fate, Blood, Divination, or Formation ritual if the GM agrees the link is appropriate. Wax Effigy does not harm or control the subject by itself. #### Candle Procession - Wick Talent Prerequisite: CL 5. Action. Cost 1 CP. Duration Concentration, up to 10 minutes. You create up to six small cultivated candles in spaces you can see within 60 feet. The candles may float inches above the ground, cling to walls, or rest on surfaces. They shed dim light in a 10-foot radius. As a Bonus Action, you may move each candle up to 20 feet. A candle cannot attack, carry objects, provide flanking, or occupy a creature’s space. Allies who begin their turn within 5 feet of one of your procession candles may ignore the first 5 feet of Difficult Terrain they enter that turn. #### Seal of Preservation - Seal Talent Prerequisite: CL 5. When you place a Preserving Seal on a living willing creature, choose one condition or danger: poison, disease, bleeding, exhaustion from exposure, suffocation from smoke, or ordinary environmental contamination. For the seal’s duration, the target gains advantage on saving throws against that danger. If the target is already suffering from the chosen danger, it may immediately make one new saving throw or ability check to resist or stabilize it if the GM judges the effect permits repeated attempts. #### Searing Seal - Wick Talent Prerequisite: CL 5. When you kindle a Wax Seal on a hostile creature, you may spend 1 CP to make it sear. The creature makes a Constitution saving throw. On a failure, it takes 2d8 fire damage and cannot take Reactions until the start of its next turn. On a success, it takes half damage and suffers no Reaction loss. A creature cannot lose Reactions from your Searing Seal more than once per round. #### Molten Snare - Mold Talent Prerequisite: CL 5. When a creature fails a saving throw against Adhesive Pool or Wax Cage, you may spend 1 CP to make the wax molten and dragging. Until the start of your next turn, the creature takes fire damage equal to your Proficiency Bonus whenever it moves willingly or is moved through the wax. This is heated wax, not broad fire control. #### Returning Wax - Temper Talent Prerequisite: CL 5. When one of your Wax forms is destroyed by damage, you may use your Reaction and spend 1 CP to have part of it flow back to you. You regain temporary hit points equal to your Proficiency Bonus, or you may immediately create a 5-foot square of Soft Wax in an unoccupied space within 30 feet of the destroyed form. #### Tempered Sealant - Temper Talent Prerequisite: CL 5. Your Set Wax and Wax Seals no longer have vulnerability to fire damage unless the fire comes from a creature whose Cultivation Level, Challenge Rating, or spell level is higher than your Cultivation Level or the GM decides the heat is overwhelming. Your wax also resists ordinary rain, desert heat, cold rooms, household flame, and casual attempts to melt it. ### Core Formation Realm Wax Talents #### Court of Ten Thousand Candles - Wax Domain Prerequisite: CL 10. Action. Cost 4 CP. Duration Concentration, up to 1 minute. You establish a candle court in a 30-foot radius centered on a point you can see within 60 feet. The court fills with wax seals, thin candlelight, slow-falling droplets, and soft places waiting to harden. Allies in the court gain the following benefits. They ignore Difficult Terrain created by your Wax talents. The first time each round an ally would be moved against their will, they may reduce that movement by 10 feet. An ally who starts their turn adjacent to one of your Wax forms or candles gains temporary hit points equal to your Proficiency Bonus. Enemies in the court suffer the following effects. The area is Difficult Terrain for them. The first time each round an enemy fails a saving throw against one of your Wax talents, you may place a Wax Seal on that enemy without spending additional CP. An enemy that damages one of your Wax forms is impressed by the court until the end of its next turn. The court is visible and material. Fire, wind, dispelling, and object destruction can weaken parts of it, but do not end the entire Domain unless the central candle seal is destroyed or your concentration ends. #### Palace Raised From One Drip - Mold Evolution Prerequisite: CL 10, Greater Mold. When you use Mold Wax, you may create more elaborate connected structures: multiple walls, a low maze, a stairwell, a short bridge, a sealed booth, a temporary clinic bay, a wax gatehouse, or a layered rampart. The total volume cannot exceed your Mold Wax limits, but you may divide the wax into any number of connected sections. The structure must remain physically plausible: it needs support, cannot hover freely, and cannot create machinery with complex moving parts unless another talent permits it. #### Wax Tomb - Seal Talent Prerequisite: CL 10. Action. Range 60 feet. Cost 3 CP. Duration Concentration, up to 1 minute. You attempt to seal one Large or smaller creature inside a wax sarcophagus, cocoon, pillar, or coffin. The target makes a Dexterity saving throw. On a failure, it is Restrained and Blinded while sealed. On a success, it is not sealed, but the space it occupies becomes Soft Wax until the end of your next turn. A sealed creature can use its Action to attempt a Strength saving throw against your Cultivation Save DC, breaking free on a success. The tomb can also be destroyed as a Set Wax object. A creature reduced to 0 hit points inside the tomb is stabilized rather than killed unless you choose to kindle the tomb with a Wick talent. Wax Tomb is a containment technique. It does not suffocate a creature unless the GM rules the creature remains sealed long enough for that to matter. #### Living Wax Form - Unique Wax Talent Prerequisite: CL 10. Bonus Action. Cost 2 CP. Duration 1 minute. You cultivate your own body as wax without losing your living nature. Choose one form when you activate this talent. Soft Body. You can move through spaces as narrow as 1 inch wide if you are not carrying rigid equipment that cannot pass. You have advantage on ability checks and saving throws made to escape Grappled or Restrained. You have disadvantage on saving throws against effects that would push, pull, or knock you Prone. Set Body. You gain temporary hit points equal to twice your Cultivation Level. While these temporary hit points remain, you reduce forced movement by 10 feet and have advantage on saving throws against being knocked Prone. Wick Body. The first time each round a creature hits you with a melee attack, you may use your Reaction to deal fire damage equal to your Proficiency Bonus and shed bright candlelight in a 10-foot radius until the start of your next turn. You may change forms as a Bonus Action by spending 1 CP. #### Effigy of the Absent - Effigy Rite Prerequisite: CL 10, Wax Effigy. Rite. 1 hour. Cost 4 CP. Duration 7 days. You create an advanced effigy of a missing creature, forgotten oath, lost object, dead witness, or sealed event. Choose one vessel. Message Vessel. If the subject willingly gave you an Impression, name-seal, or token, the effigy can carry a message that reaches them in a dream, candle reflection, or moment of stillness if they are on the same plane and not protected against such contact. Recognition Vessel. You may compare a creature, corpse, object, handwriting sample, wound, footprint, key, or aura trace against the effigy. The GM may grant advantage on checks to determine whether it matches the subject. Funeral Vessel. If used in a respectful funeral rite, the effigy helps preserve a departing trace, name, or final memory long enough for Spirit, Fate, Dream, or ancestral rites to interact with it. Effigy of the Absent cannot compel the subject to answer, appear, suffer harm, or reveal secrets by itself. #### Procession of Wax Attendants - Effigy Talent Prerequisite: CL 10. Action. Cost 3 CP. Duration 1 hour. You shape up to three Small wax attendants. They are fragile ritual helpers, not combat summons. Each attendant has AC 10, 1 hit point, Speed 20 feet, and can carry a light object, hold a candle, bear a seal, deliver a message to a visible creature within 300 feet, open an unlocked door, pour medicine, hold a bandage, or perform another simple task. In combat, an attendant acts on your turn and can take only the Dash, Disengage, Help, Hide, Search, or Use an Object action. It cannot attack. If it takes damage, it is destroyed. #### Hundred-Seal Conflagration - Wick Talent Prerequisite: CL 10. Action. Range 60 feet. Cost 3 CP. You ignite any number of your Wax Seals within range. Choose up to three creatures bearing those seals or adjacent to those seals. Each target makes a Dexterity saving throw. On a failure, it takes 4d8 fire damage and is pushed 10 feet away from the nearest ignited seal. On a success, it takes half damage and is not pushed. All ignited seals are consumed. #### Unmelting Scripture - Temper Talent Prerequisite: CL 10, Tempered Sealant. Your cultivated wax can be made unmelting for short periods. When you create a Wax form or Wax Seal, you may spend 1 additional CP to make it unmelting for its duration. Unmelting wax has resistance to fire damage and cannot be softened by ordinary heat. Magical fire can still damage it, and Dispel effects can still end it. #### Sealed Archive - Rite Talent Prerequisite: CL 10. Rite. 1 hour. Cost 4 CP. Duration 30 days. You create a wax-sealed archive for evidence, memories, letters, maps, relics, ingredients, court records, medical notes, or corpse-tags. The archive may be a chest, wall, rack, candle hall, ledger, or sealed cabinet. While the archive remains undamaged, its contents resist ordinary decay, tampering, weather, vermin, and casual theft. A creature that opens the archive without your permission must succeed on a Dexterity saving throw or become marked by a Witness Seal for 24 hours. This creates a temporary protected archive, not a permanent sect vault. Permanent archives require GM-approved sect-scale work. ### Nascent Soul Realm Wax Talents #### Waxen City of One Breath - Sovereign Mold Technique Prerequisite: CL 15. Action. Cost 5 CP. Duration Concentration, up to 10 minutes. You exhale a sovereign quantity of cultivated wax, shaping a battlefield district in a 60-foot radius centered on a point you can see within 120 feet. Choose up to four features when you create it. Soft avenues that are Difficult Terrain for enemies. Set Wax ramparts providing half cover. Candle roads that allow allies to ignore your wax terrain. Sealed doors, walls, or booths that require checks to open. Raised platforms, bridges, stairs, or channels. Preserving alcoves where allies gain temporary hit points equal to your Proficiency Bonus when they first enter. Witness seals that mark the first enemy each round to damage a wax structure. The city is temporary, visible, and material. It is not a real settlement and cannot create valuable goods. It can, however, transform a battlefield into a wax-sealed court, clinic, maze, barricade, or funeral avenue. #### Sovereign Seal of the Chosen Shape - Seal Talent Prerequisite: CL 15. Action. Range 60 feet. Cost 4 CP. Duration Concentration, up to 1 minute. You place a sovereign Wax Seal on one creature or object. An unwilling creature makes a Charisma saving throw. On a failure, choose one chosen shape. Shape of Stillness. The target’s Speed becomes 0, and it cannot teleport unless it first succeeds on a Charisma saving throw at the end of its turn. Shape of Truth. The target cannot benefit from mundane disguise, physical masks, or shapechanging to conceal its basic body outline. Illusions are not dispelled, but creatures have advantage on checks to notice that something is being hidden. Shape of Preservation. The target cannot be reduced below 1 hit point by damage from a source you can see, once during the duration. When this protection triggers, the seal ends and you gain one level of exhaustion or lose CP equal to your Proficiency Bonus, your choice. Shape of Closure. One object, portal, container, wound, door, or threshold becomes sealed. Opening or crossing it requires a successful check or saving throw against your Cultivation Save DC, as appropriate to the situation. A creature can repeat the saving throw at the end of each of its turns, ending the seal on a success. #### Candle That Remembers Every Footstep - Rite Talent Prerequisite: CL 15. Rite. 10 minutes. Cost 4 CP. Duration 24 hours. You prepare a sovereign tracking candle from an Impression. While the candle burns, it remembers the path of the creature or object that left the Impression. You can ask the candle one of the following questions each hour. Did the subject pass within 1 mile of this location in the last 24 hours? Which direction did the subject most recently travel from here? Did the subject cross a threshold, gate, river, road, wall, or formation nearby? Is the subject currently protected by a strong anti-divination, anti-tracking, or identity-concealing effect? The candle answers by flame direction, scent, smoke pattern, wax flow, or script emerging in melted wax. It does not reveal exact location unless the GM decides the Impression is unusually strong and the subject is nearby. #### Funeral Candle Shelter - Wick Rite Prerequisite: CL 15. Reaction. Trigger: A creature you can see within 60 feet would die, have its corpse destroyed, or have its departing trace scattered. Cost 5 CP. You ignite a funeral candle and wrap the target in white wax light. Choose one effect. Shelter the Dying. If the creature would die from damage, it instead falls to 0 hit points and becomes stable, provided the damage did not destroy the body outright. The candle ends. Shelter the Departing Trace. If the creature dies, you preserve a respectful departing trace, final breath, name, or memory for 1 hour. This does not trap the soul or prevent resurrection. It gives allies time to perform Spirit, Fate, Dream, Medicine, funeral, or ancestral rites. A creature can benefit from Funeral Candle Shelter only once per long rest. #### Thousand-Faced Wax Sovereign - Effigy Talent Prerequisite: CL 15. Action. Cost 4 CP. Duration 1 hour. You surround yourself with many refined masks, hand impressions, name plaques, and wax figures. For the duration, you gain the following benefits. You have advantage on checks made to create, detect, or analyze physical disguises, false bodies, forged handprints, seals, and masks. When a creature hits you with an attack, you may use your Reaction to cause one wax false-face to break. The attack still hits, but the attacker becomes impressed by your Wax until the end of your next turn. You may create a Wax Mask as an Action without the normal Rite time. Once during the duration, when you would fail a Charisma check based on appearance, etiquette, legal identity, or ceremonial presence, you may reroll the check. This does not alter your soul, aura, memories, voice, cultivation signature, or true identity. #### Candle Procession Across the Night - Wick Evolution Prerequisite: CL 15, Candle Procession. Your Candle Procession can carry allies along prepared candle routes. Rite. 10 minutes. Cost 4 CP. Duration 1 hour. You arrange a line of candles between two points you have physically visited within the last 24 hours, no farther apart than 1 mile per Proficiency Bonus. During the duration, you and up to six willing creatures may travel between those points as part of a quiet procession. The journey takes 10 minutes regardless of normal travel difficulty, provided the route is physically passable by some path. This is not teleportation. It is a supernatural procession that finds the safe candle-lit way through streets, halls, forests, ruins, grave roads, or sect grounds. Barriers, sealed gates, warded borders, hostile patrols, or impossible terrain can still interrupt it. #### White Wax Edict of Stillness - Seal Talent Prerequisite: CL 15. Action. Cost 5 CP. Duration Concentration, up to 1 minute. Choose a 30-foot radius area within 120 feet. White wax seals spread across the ground, walls, weapons, and thresholds. Hostile creatures treat the area as Difficult Terrain. The first time each round a hostile creature attempts to teleport, become invisible, change shape, or pass through a sealed threshold inside the area, it must succeed on a Charisma saving throw or the attempt fails and the creature becomes impressed by the wax until the end of its next turn. On a successful save, the attempt works, but the creature still leaves a visible wax Impression at the point of departure. ### Secret Inheritance #### The Last Candle Refuses to Forget the Departed Prerequisite: CL 17 or higher, GM permission. Forbidden Rite. 1 minute. Cost 8 CP. You light the last candle for a creature, place, oath, family, sect, battlefield, or vanished event that should have been forgotten. The candle burns with wax made from memory, evidence, grief, and refusal. Choose one miracle. Name Preserved. A creature whose name has been erased, denied, or ritually suppressed can be spoken again by those present. This does not defeat all curses, but it creates a true foothold for later Spirit, Fate, Dream, Blood, or ancestral restoration. Trace Sheltered. A departing soul-trace, ancestral echo, final memory, or oath-fragment is preserved for 24 hours even if ordinary rites would fail. This does not imprison the dead. It prevents immediate scattering. Evidence Refuses Fire. One physical record, body, trace, wound pattern, seal, footprint, weapon mark, or corpse-tag destroyed within the last day reappears as a wax Impression clear enough to be examined. Door Remembered. A sealed, hidden, burned, moved, or forgotten threshold briefly appears as a wax outline. For 1 minute, creatures present can see where the passage was, what opened it, and what kind of seal closed it. After using this inheritance, the candle leaves a permanent mark on your cultivation base. Until you complete a significant funeral, justice, remembrance, or reconciliation deed, you cannot use this inheritance again. ### Optional Cultivation Variants These variants are Tianxia-specific cultivation scriptures and limitations. A character normally chooses at most one Wax variant when first learning Wax or during a major Wax initiation. If a variant grants a bonus talent whose prerequisites are not yet met, the talent is gained when the prerequisites are met. If the variant is later removed or retrained, its granted benefit is lost. #### Candle-Flesh Body Body Refining variant. You cultivate wax through your flesh, skin, breath, and marrow rather than through external spellcasting. Benefit: You may use Constitution as your key ability for Wax talents. You gain Waxen Shell or Living Wax Form when you meet its prerequisites. Restriction: Your Mold Wax range is reduced to Touch or 10 feet unless the talent affects your own body, armor, carried items, adjacent terrain, or a creature you are grappling. You cannot create distant large structures without a Qi or Spirit method. Special: When fire damage destroys one of your Wax effects, you take fire damage equal to your Proficiency Bonus unless you have Unmelting Scripture or the effect was not connected to your body. #### Inner Wax Body Self-restricted Body variant. Your wax cultivation turns inward. You become difficult to seize, reshape, or break, but your external wax arts are limited. Benefit: You gain Wax-Tempered Body as a bonus Cultivation Insight when eligible. You may use Waxen Shell without spending CP once per short rest. Restriction: You cannot use Mold Wax to create structures more than 5 feet away from you. You cannot learn Waxen City of One Breath, Palace Raised From One Drip, or Candle Procession Across the Night unless you retrain this variant. #### Sealkeeper’s Practice Restrictive legal/ritual variant. Your Wax cultivation is bound to seals, evidence, vows, and thresholds. Benefit: You gain Quiet Seal or Waxen Trail as a bonus talent. Restriction: Your Wick talents cannot deal direct damage unless used against a creature that has broken, violated, destroyed, or crossed one of your Wax Seals during the current scene. #### Funeral Candle Practice Support and memorial variant. Your Wax cultivation is devoted to the dying, the dead, preserved names, and respectful traces. Benefit: You gain Guiding Candle or Preserving Shroud as a bonus talent. You have advantage on checks related to funeral etiquette, corpse preservation, memorial records, and identifying disturbed remains. Restriction: You cannot learn forbidden sympathetic harm through effigies. Your Effigy talents cannot be used to curse, injure, or impersonate the dead without GM permission. #### Honeyed Soft Wax Scripture Control variant. Your wax remains soft, fragrant, sticky, and alive with yielding qi. Benefit: You gain Adhesive Pool as a bonus talent. Enemies impressed by your Soft Wax have disadvantage on the first check they make before the end of their next turn to hide tracks, conceal movement, or escape your Wax terrain. Restriction: Your Set Wax structures have half the normal hit points unless created as part of a Rite or Domain. ### Path Synergies #### Qi Cultivation - Perfect Temper Qi cultivators are the most common Wax practitioners. They learn to heat, cool, shape, and set wax through refined qi control. Qi Wax is precise, scalable, and excellent for seals, barriers, architecture, and legal marks. Qi cultivators often build sect seal halls, archives, clinics, candle formations, and battlefield ramparts. Possible synergy talents include Perfect Temper, Unmelting Scripture, Palace Raised From One Drip, and Court of Ten Thousand Candles. #### Spirit Awakening - Wax Remembers More Than Shape Spirit Awakening makes Wax more than material. The wax can hold grief, intention, memory, ritual presence, and traces of the departed. Spirit Wax is used for funeral candles, ancestral name plaques, evidence that remembers pressure, and effigies that carry messages or recognition. Spirit Wax should be watched carefully when it approaches possession, soul binding, or forced sympathetic harm. Possible synergy talents include Effigy of the Absent, Funeral Candle Shelter, Candle That Remembers Every Footstep, and The Last Candle Refuses to Forget the Departed. #### Body Refining - Wax-Tempered Body Body Refiners cultivate Wax through skin, marrow, tendons, breath, and pain tolerance. They become flexible under pressure and harden at the moment of impact. Body Wax is not as good at distant structures. It excels at personal armor, grappling counterplay, slipping through restraints, bracing against forced movement, and sealing wounds. Possible synergy talents include Waxen Shell, Seal Wound, Living Wax Form, Candle-Flesh Body, and Inner Wax Body. ### Cultivation Insights #### Wax-Tempered Body Prerequisite: Body Refining or GM permission. You have cultivated your flesh to soften under pressure and set before breaking. Once per short rest, when you would be Grappled, Restrained, pushed, pulled, or knocked Prone, you may gain advantage on the saving throw or ability check made to resist or escape that effect. If you succeed, you may leave a harmless wax Impression on the creature or object that attempted to restrain or move you. #### Master Seal Engraver Prerequisite: Wax sphere. You gain proficiency with calligrapher’s supplies, seal-carving tools, or a similar artisan’s tool. If you already have the proficiency, you may add your Proficiency Bonus twice to checks made to create, identify, preserve, or verify seals. Once per long rest, you may place a Witness Seal or Preserving Seal without spending CP. #### Keeper of the Funeral Wick Prerequisite: Wax sphere or Spirit Awakening. You know rites for respectful preservation of the dead. You have advantage on checks related to funeral etiquette, corpse handling, identifying disturbed remains, and preserving final messages. Once per long rest, when a creature dies within 30 feet of you, you may create a harmless funeral candle as a Reaction. The candle preserves a final visible sign, name, handprint, breath, or symbolic Impression for 1 hour. #### Sect Waxwright Prerequisite: Wax sphere, CL 5. You are trained in practical sect infrastructure: seals, labels, archives, medical wax, evidence preservation, temporary walls, candle paths, and ritual fixtures. During downtime, you may complete Wax-related mundane construction, repair, cataloging, or preservation work in half the normal time if the GM agrees wax is an appropriate medium. #### Sympathetic Effigy Worker Prerequisite: Wax sphere, CL 5, GM permission. You understand the dangerous edge of effigy work. When you create a Wax Effigy from a true Impression, you may treat it as a valid ritual focus for one approved Spirit, Fate, Blood, Dream, Curse, Divination, or Formation technique that normally requires a sympathetic link. This Insight does not grant those spheres or techniques by itself. It only makes the effigy a better link. #### Unmelting Temper Prerequisite: Wax sphere, CL 10. Once per long rest, when one of your Set Wax structures or Wax Seals would be destroyed by fire damage, you may cause it to survive with 1 hit point instead. When you use this Insight, the wax becomes visibly changed: blackened, white, glassy, fragrant, or script-covered. Anyone who examines it can tell it endured supernatural heat.

### Base Sphere Abilities
When you first gain the Sphere of Wax, you gain Mold Wax, Press Seal, and Kindle Wax.
You also learn one Wax talent of your choice.
#### Mold Wax
Action. Range 60 feet. Cost 1 CP. Duration Concentration, up to 1 minute.
You create or awaken cultivated wax in an unoccupied space, on a surface, or over an unattended object within range. Choose one form.
Soft Spread. You create a 10-foot square of Soft Wax on a surface. The area is Difficult Terrain for hostile creatures. The first hostile creature each round that enters the area or starts its turn there must succeed on a Dexterity saving throw or become impressed by the wax until the end of your next turn.
Set Shape. You create a Set Wax panel, ramp, handhold, brace, small bridge, shield plate, low wall, or similar structure that fits within two contiguous 5-foot cubes. It must be supported by a surface unless a talent says otherwise. It can provide cover, block a narrow passage, support weight, or create a short ramp or platform.
Fine Work. Outside initiative, you can shape wax into seals, molds, masks, tablets, candle forms, practice tools, ritual counters, labels, evidence casts, and small sculptures. Fine Work cannot create valuable trade goods, magical items, living organs, or permanent infrastructure unless the GM says otherwise.
At CL 5, your Soft Spread can cover a 15-foot square, or your Set Shape can fit within four contiguous 5-foot cubes.
At CL 10, your Soft Spread can cover a 20-foot square, or your Set Shape can fit within six contiguous 5-foot cubes.
At CL 15, your Soft Spread can cover a 25-foot square, or your Set Shape can fit within eight contiguous 5-foot cubes.
#### Press Seal
Action. Range 30 feet. Cost 1 CP. Duration 1 minute.
You press or throw a cultivated Wax Seal onto one creature, object, surface, or 5-foot space within range. A willing creature, unattended object, or surface is sealed automatically. An unwilling creature or attended object makes a Dexterity saving throw. On a failure, the seal attaches. On a success, the seal fails.
When you place the seal, choose one base seal.
Clinging Seal. The sealed creature’s Speed is reduced by 10 feet while the seal remains. If placed on an object, the object adheres to the surface it touches and requires an Action and a successful Strength check against your Cultivation Save DC to remove.
Witness Seal. The seal records the next creature other than you that touches, opens, damages, moves, or passes through the sealed target. You know that the seal was triggered if you are within 1 mile, and you can later inspect the seal to see the outline, handprint, footprint, tool mark, weapon shape, or other physical Impression left behind.
