The damage is not the sphere’s identity. It is the visible symptom of qi becoming too bright, too hot, or too forceful to remain unfinished.
#### Spending a Rising Mark
Once per round, when a marked subject you can perceive performs a triggering act, you may spend its Rising Mark without using an Action. Choose one Completing Response appropriate to the mark.
#### Kindled Responses
You may use these responses when you spend a Kindled Mark.
Complete Force.
Trigger: the marked subject deals damage. Add 1d6 + your Key Ability modifier to one damage roll. This bonus increases to 2d6 at CL 5, 3d6 at CL 11, and 4d6 at CL 17.
Complete Aim.
Trigger: the marked subject makes an attack roll or forces one or more creatures to make a saving throw. Add 1d4 to the attack roll, or choose one target making the saving throw and subtract 1d4 from that saving throw. At CL 11, the die becomes 1d6.
Complete Step.
Trigger: the marked subject begins movement during its turn. Increase one of the subject’s Speeds by 10 feet until the end of the current turn, or allow it to stand from Prone without spending movement. At CL 11, the Speed increase becomes 20 feet.
Complete Breath.
Trigger: the marked subject regains Hit Points or gains Temporary HP. Increase the amount gained by your Proficiency Bonus + your Key Ability modifier.
Complete Resolve.
Trigger: the marked subject makes a saving throw against an effect that would reduce its Speed, prevent it from taking Reactions, impose Frightened, Paralyzed, Restrained, Stunned, or Unconscious, or suppress its ability to act. Add 1d4 to the saving throw. At CL 11, the die becomes 1d6.
Complete Revelation.
Trigger: the marked subject makes an attack roll, Wisdom (Perception) check, or Intelligence (Investigation) check against a creature or effect that is Hidden, Invisible, heavily obscured, disguised by illusion, or concealed by a Yin-like technique. The marked subject ignores Disadvantage from not seeing the target for that roll, provided it can still identify the target’s space or general location.
#### Overkindled Responses
You may use these responses when you spend an Overkindled Mark.
Overheat Force.
Trigger: the marked subject deals damage, makes an attack roll, or forces one or more creatures to make a saving throw. After the triggering act resolves, the subject takes Fire or Radiant damage equal to 1d6 + your Key Ability modifier. This damage increases to 2d6 at CL 5, 3d6 at CL 11, and 4d6 at CL 17.
Overexpose.
Trigger: the marked subject becomes Hidden, becomes Invisible, creates concealment, creates an illusion, or benefits from a feature that prevents others from perceiving it. Until the start of your next turn, the subject cannot benefit from being Hidden or Invisible against you, and allies you choose within 60 feet know the subject’s current space if they can perceive the area.
Overcommit Step.
Trigger: the marked subject moves at least 10 feet, teleports, or uses special movement. After the movement resolves, the subject cannot take Reactions until the start of its next turn. If the movement was teleportation and the destination is within 120 feet of you, you know the destination space.
Overgrown Recovery.
Trigger: the marked subject regains Hit Points, gains Temporary HP, restores CP, or benefits from regeneration. Until the start of your next turn, the first damage roll against that subject gains a bonus equal to your Proficiency Bonus.
Overstrain Technique.
Trigger: the marked subject spends CP, uses a spell slot, activates a limited feature, or uses a named cultivation technique. If the subject uses the same named spell, sphere talent, forged technique, monster action, or cultivation ability again before the end of its next turn, it gains a Rising Mark immediately after the repeated ability resolves.
#### Yang Saves
Some Yang features require a saving throw. Unless a feature says otherwise, your Cultivation Save DC equals your Cultivation Save DC.

#### Mark Limit
You can maintain a number of Rising Marks equal to your Proficiency Bonus. A creature, object, or ongoing effect can have only one Rising Mark from you at a time unless a feature says otherwise.

A Rising Mark has one of two expressions.
Kindled Mark. A Rising Mark on you, a willing creature, an unattended object, or an effect you created is a Kindled Mark. You spend Kindled Marks to help an action complete.
Overkindled Mark. A Rising Mark on an unwilling creature, hostile object, enemy effect, or creature that rejects your assistance is an Overkindled Mark. You spend Overkindled Marks to make hostile exertion overcomplete, exposing or straining the source.

Trigger: the marked subject regains Hit Points, gains Temporary HP, restores CP, or benefits from regeneration. Until the start of your next turn, the first damage roll against that subject gains a bonus equal to your Proficiency Bonus.
Overstrain Technique.
Trigger: the marked subject spends CP, uses a spell slot, activates a limited feature, or uses a named cultivation technique. If the subject uses the same named spell, sphere talent, forged technique, monster action, or cultivation ability again before the end of its next turn, it gains a Rising Mark immediately after the repeated ability resolves.

spheres.full_exact_source_text: # Sphere of Yang Qi Expression: Primary — Yang Qi; Supporting — Fire Qi, Life-Heat Qi, Motion Qi, Assertion Qi. “Yin teaches an action how to end. Yang teaches an unfinished thing that Heaven must make room for its completion.” Sphere Type: Metaphysical Power Sphere Primary Path: Qi Cultivation Secondary Path: Body Refining Rare Variant: Spirit Awakening through the Solar Soul Insight Resource: CPCore Mechanic: Rising Marks Common Effects: kindling unfinished force, completing actions, overcompleting hostile exertion, exposing concealment, breaking stillness, vital pressure, heat as a symptom of rising qi, motion, recovery, assertion, and dangerous surplus The Sphere of Yang is the cultivation of assertive completion. A Yang cultivator does not merely burn, heal, shine, or move quickly. Those are visible symptoms. The true art is more dangerous: the cultivator kindles an unfinished force, marks it as rising, and makes its next expression become complete or overcomplete. Yang is metaphysical because it interferes with insufficiency. A weak strike reaches further than it should. A failing breath becomes a battle cry. A hidden enemy becomes too bright to remain concealed. A dying body finds one more beat. A sealed gate feels the sun pressing through every crack. Yang is not automatically heroic. It is life-force without apology, motion that refuses to stay small, revelation that does not ask whether the revealed thing wanted privacy, and surplus that can heal an ally or burn out a tyrant’s meridians. ### Sphere Boundaries Yang overlaps with several spheres, but it does not replace them. | Sphere | Difference from Yang | | --- | --- | | Fire | Fire creates flame, burning terrain, ignition, and elemental destruction. Yang may appear as heat or flame when force becomes excessive, but fire is not the sphere identity. | | Radiance | Radiance governs light, revelation, brilliance, purification, and blinding. Yang may expose or shine, but it does so because rising force refuses concealment, not because it is automatically holy light. | | Life | Life governs healing, restoration, living essence, and biological renewal as a dedicated discipline. Yang can kindle survival and recovery, but it does not replace broad restoration. | | Brute | Brute is direct strength, grappling, shoving, bodily domination, and raw force. Yang may intensify exertion, but it is not the full martial sphere of physical overpowering. | | Wood | Wood governs plants, roots, growth patterns, and living natural structures. Yang can force growth or seasonal abundance, but it does not shape plants with Wood’s precision. | | Destruction | Destruction turns power into direct blasts. Yang may provide a Destruction expression, but ordinary Yang talents are not blast talents by default. | | Force | Force stores, answers, and transmits impact through resistance. Yang completes exertion and makes surplus consequence press outward. | | Time | Time changes sequence and duration. Yang can hasten completion or make a moment overfull, but it does not rewrite chronology. | | Yin | Yin receives force, marks it as waning, and makes its next expression incomplete. Yang kindles force, marks it as rising, and makes its next expression complete or overcomplete. | ### USING THIS SPHERE Except where a Yang feature explicitly says otherwise, ordinary Fifth Edition rules remain in force. Yang does not automatically: create bright light, sunlight, magical light, or fire; ignite worn or carried objects; overcome Fire Resistance, Radiant Resistance, or Immunity; restore Hit Points; revive a dead creature; grant Resistance, Immunity, armor, or a bonus to AC; increase Strength, Speed, jump distance, carrying capacity, or weapon damage; remove Exhaustion or conditions; end Frightened, Charmed, Poisoned, Blinded, Paralyzed, Stunned, Unconscious, Grappled, Restrained, or Incapacitated; prevent death, aging, disease, poison, or decay; reduce the action cost of attacks; grant extra attacks; counter Yin, dispel magic, or negate a technique. A feature must state any such effect directly. ### BASE SPHERE ABILITIES The Yang sphere uses Rising Marks. A Rising Mark is not a condition. Immunity to a condition does not grant immunity to Rising Marks unless a feature says otherwise. A Rising Mark represents a motion, wound, breath, oath, technique, or intention that has begun to swell toward completion. #### Mark Limit You can maintain a number of Rising Marks equal to your Proficiency Bonus. A creature, object, or ongoing effect can have only one Rising Mark from you at a time unless a feature says otherwise. A Rising Mark lasts until the end of your next turn, until you spend it, or until the marked subject is no longer on the same plane of existence as you. #### Kindled and Overkindled Marks A Rising Mark has one of two expressions. Kindled Mark. A Rising Mark on you, a willing creature, an unattended object, or an effect you created is a Kindled Mark. You spend Kindled Marks to help an action complete. Overkindled Mark. A Rising Mark on an unwilling creature, hostile object, enemy effect, or creature that rejects your assistance is an Overkindled Mark. You spend Overkindled Marks to make hostile exertion overcomplete, exposing or straining the source. A willing creature may end your Rising Mark on itself at any time, no Action required. #### Applying a Rising Mark You can apply a Rising Mark in three basic ways. Kindle the Rising. As a Bonus Action, choose yourself or one willing creature, unattended object, or ongoing effect you created within 60 feet that you can perceive. The target gains one Kindled Mark. Force the Rising. As a Reaction when a creature, object, or effect within 60 feet that you can perceive hits with an attack, forces a saving throw, regains Hit Points, gains Temporary HP, spends CP, uses a spell slot, uses a limited feature, teleports, becomes Hidden, becomes Invisible, creates concealment, creates an illusion, or moves at least 10 feet during its turn, you may apply one Overkindled Mark to the source after the triggering event resolves. Rising Thread. As an Action, make a ranged Cultivation Attack against one creature or object within 60 feet. On a hit, the target takes Fire, Radiant, or Force damage, chosen when you make the attack, and gains one Overkindled Mark. | Cultivation Level | Rising Thread Damage | | --- | --- | | CL 1-4 | 1d6 | | CL 5-10 | 2d6 | | CL 11-16 | 3d6 | | CL 17-20 | 4d6 | The damage is not the sphere’s identity. It is the visible symptom of qi becoming too bright, too hot, or too forceful to remain unfinished. #### Spending a Rising Mark Once per round, when a marked subject you can perceive performs a triggering act, you may spend its Rising Mark without using an Action. Choose one Completing Response appropriate to the mark. #### Kindled Responses You may use these responses when you spend a Kindled Mark. Complete Force. Trigger: the marked subject deals damage. Add 1d6 + your Key Ability modifier to one damage roll. This bonus increases to 2d6 at CL 5, 3d6 at CL 11, and 4d6 at CL 17. Complete Aim. Trigger: the marked subject makes an attack roll or forces one or more creatures to make a saving throw. Add 1d4 to the attack roll, or choose one target making the saving throw and subtract 1d4 from that saving throw. At CL 11, the die becomes 1d6. Complete Step. Trigger: the marked subject begins movement during its turn. Increase one of the subject’s Speeds by 10 feet until the end of the current turn, or allow it to stand from Prone without spending movement. At CL 11, the Speed increase becomes 20 feet. Complete Breath. Trigger: the marked subject regains Hit Points or gains Temporary HP. Increase the amount gained by your Proficiency Bonus + your Key Ability modifier. Complete Resolve. Trigger: the marked subject makes a saving throw against an effect that would reduce its Speed, prevent it from taking Reactions, impose Frightened, Paralyzed, Restrained, Stunned, or Unconscious, or suppress its ability to act. Add 1d4 to the saving throw. At CL 11, the die becomes 1d6. Complete Revelation. Trigger: the marked subject makes an attack roll, Wisdom (Perception) check, or Intelligence (Investigation) check against a creature or effect that is Hidden, Invisible, heavily obscured, disguised by illusion, or concealed by a Yin-like technique. The marked subject ignores Disadvantage from not seeing the target for that roll, provided it can still identify the target’s space or general location. #### Overkindled Responses You may use these responses when you spend an Overkindled Mark. Overheat Force. Trigger: the marked subject deals damage, makes an attack roll, or forces one or more creatures to make a saving throw. After the triggering act resolves, the subject takes Fire or Radiant damage equal to 1d6 + your Key Ability modifier. This damage increases to 2d6 at CL 5, 3d6 at CL 11, and 4d6 at CL 17. Overexpose. Trigger: the marked subject becomes Hidden, becomes Invisible, creates concealment, creates an illusion, or benefits from a feature that prevents others from perceiving it. Until the start of your next turn, the subject cannot benefit from being Hidden or Invisible against you, and allies you choose within 60 feet know the subject’s current space if they can perceive the area. Overcommit Step. Trigger: the marked subject moves at least 10 feet, teleports, or uses special movement. After the movement resolves, the subject cannot take Reactions until the start of its next turn. If the movement was teleportation and the destination is within 120 feet of you, you know the destination space. Overgrown Recovery. Trigger: the marked subject regains Hit Points, gains Temporary HP, restores CP, or benefits from regeneration. Until the start of your next turn, the first damage roll against that subject gains a bonus equal to your Proficiency Bonus. Overstrain Technique. Trigger: the marked subject spends CP, uses a spell slot, activates a limited feature, or uses a named cultivation technique. If the subject uses the same named spell, sphere talent, forged technique, monster action, or cultivation ability again before the end of its next turn, it gains a Rising Mark immediately after the repeated ability resolves. #### Yang Saves Some Yang features require a saving throw. Unless a feature says otherwise, your Cultivation Save DC equals your Cultivation Save DC. ### USING RISING MARKS A Mortal Yang cultivator usually plays like this: Place a Kindled Mark on yourself or an ally, or place an Overkindled Mark on an enemy that overextends. Wait for the marked subject to act. Spend the mark to complete an ally’s action or overcomplete an enemy’s action. Use talents to turn completion into movement, revelation, survival, pressure, or backlash. The player should be watching for unfinished momentum: the ally who needs one more step, the wounded friend who needs one more breath, the enemy who hides too late, or the hostile technique that has become too bright to control. ### MORTAL REALM YANG TALENTS #### Dawn Refuses Restraint Action Type: No Action Factory Combat Bucket: passive Factory Routing: passive_or_triggered_modifier_row Trigger: You spend a Kindled Mark with Complete Resolve Cost: None If the marked creature succeeds on the triggering saving throw, it may also end one effect currently reducing one of its Speeds or preventing it from taking Reactions, provided that effect is not from a higher Realm, Secret Inheritance, artifact, Formation, curse, or narrative seal. If no such effect can end, the marked creature gains Temporary HP equal to your Proficiency Bonus. #### Surplus Step Action Type: No Action Factory Combat Bucket: passive Factory Routing: passive_or_triggered_modifier_row Trigger: You spend a Kindled Mark with Complete Step Cost: None The marked creature may ignore nonmagical Difficult Terrain until the end of the current turn. If the marked creature moves at least 20 feet during that turn, it gains Temporary HP equal to your Proficiency Bonus at the end of the movement. #### Sunlit Opening Action Type: No Action Factory Combat Bucket: passive Factory Routing: passive_or_triggered_modifier_row Trigger: You spend a Kindled Mark with Complete Aim Cost: None If the triggering attack hits, or if at least one target fails the triggering saving throw, one ally of your choice within 30 feet of the marked creature gains Advantage on the next attack roll it makes against one affected target before the start of your next turn. #### Overbright Trail Action Type: No Action Factory Combat Bucket: passive Factory Routing: passive_or_triggered_modifier_row Trigger: You spend an Overkindled Mark with Overexpose or Overcommit Step Cost: None Until the start of your next turn, the marked creature leaves heat shimmer, bright dust, a spiritual afterimage, or a sunlit footprint. It cannot benefit from nonmagical concealment against you while it remains within 60 feet of you. This does not remove total cover or reveal a creature through a solid barrier. #### Furnace Backlash Action Type: No Action Factory Combat Bucket: passive Factory Routing: passive_or_triggered_modifier_row Trigger: You spend an Overkindled Mark with Overheat Force Cost: 1 CP The marked creature must make a Constitution saving throw. On a failed save, it cannot take Reactions until the start of its next turn. On a successful save, it takes no additional effect beyond Overheat Force. #### Kindle the Wounded Breath Action Type: Bonus Action Factory Combat Bucket: bonus_action Factory Routing: combat_action_row Range: 60 feet Cost: 2 CP Use Limit: Once per Short Rest per creature Choose one creature within range that has at least 1 Hit Point. The target gains a Kindled Mark and regains Hit Points equal to 1d8 + your Key Ability modifier. At CL 11, the healing becomes 2d8 + your Key Ability modifier. At CL 17, it becomes 3d8 + your Key Ability modifier. This talent cannot restore Hit Points to a creature at 0 Hit Points. #### Summer Pressure Action Type: Passive Factory Combat Bucket: passive Factory Routing: passive_or_modifier_row Cost: None When you spend a Kindled Mark on yourself, you may choose to emit bright light in a 10-foot radius and dim light for an additional 10 feet until the start of your next turn. This light is magical light, but it is not sunlight unless another feature says otherwise. While emitting this light, you have Advantage on saving throws against natural extreme cold and ordinary environmental cold. #### No Shelter for Stagnation Action Type: No Action Factory Combat Bucket: passive Factory Routing: passive_or_triggered_modifier_row Trigger: You apply an Overkindled Mark to a creature that has not willingly moved since the end of its last turn Cost: None Until the end of your next turn, the first time you spend that mark, choose one: the damage from Overheat Force increases by your Proficiency Bonus; Overcommit Step reduces the creature’s Speed by 10 feet until the start of its next turn after the triggering movement resolves; Overexpose lasts until the end of your next turn instead of the start of your next turn. This talent represents Yang pressure forcing stagnant force to declare itself. ### FOUNDATION REALM YANG TALENTS #### Twofold Rising Action Type: Bonus Action Factory Combat Bucket: bonus_action Factory Routing: combat_action_row Cost: 2 CP Use Kindle the Rising against two different willing targets within range instead of one. Alternatively, use Rising Thread against one target. On a hit, after applying the Overkindled Mark to the target, you may apply a Kindled Mark to yourself. #### Seal-Breaking Warmth Action Type: No Action Factory Combat Bucket: passive Factory Routing: passive_or_triggered_modifier_row Trigger: You spend a Kindled Mark with Complete Resolve or Complete Step Cost: 2 CP The marked creature may immediately repeat one saving throw against an effect currently reducing its Speed, preventing it from taking Reactions, making it Restrained, making it Paralyzed, making it Stunned, or preventing it from willingly moving. On a success, the effect ends. On a failure, the effect continues, but the marked creature gains Temporary HP equal to your Proficiency Bonus + your Key Ability modifier. This talent cannot end a stronger Realm effect, Secret Inheritance, artifact effect, curse, Formation, or narrative seal unless the GM rules your Yang cultivation is an appropriate counter. #### Radiant Overpressure Action Type: No Action Factory Combat Bucket: passive Factory Routing: passive_or_triggered_modifier_row Trigger: You spend an Overkindled Mark Cost: 2 CP The marked creature emits bright light in a 10-foot radius and dim light for an additional 10 feet until the start of your next turn. While emitting this light, it cannot benefit from the Invisible condition against any creature that can see the light. This light is not sunlight unless another feature says otherwise. #### Force Completion Action Type: No Action Factory Combat Bucket: passive Factory Routing: passive_or_triggered_modifier_row Trigger: You spend a Kindled Mark with Complete Force Cost: 2 CP After the triggering damage resolves, choose one target damaged by the attack or effect. Push that target up to 10 feet directly away from the source of the damage. If the target is more than one size larger than the source, it makes a Strength saving throw. On a successful save, it is not pushed. #### Unfinished Bloom Action Type: Action Factory Combat Bucket: action Factory Routing: combat_action_row Range: 60 feet Area: 10-foot-radius sphere Duration: Concentration, up to 1 minute Cost: 3 CP You place a Kindled Mark on an area containing soil, roots, seeds, moss, fertile mud, living wood, or another suitable natural medium. The area swells with summer pressure and impatient growth. Choose one mode when you use the talent. Grasping Bloom. Hostile creatures treat the area as Difficult Terrain. When a hostile creature starts its turn in the area, it gains an Overkindled Mark. Nourishing Bloom. Allies that start their turns in the area gain Temporary HP equal to your Proficiency Bonus. A creature can gain these Temporary HP only once per turn. Unfinished Bloom does not create permanent plant structures or replace the Wood sphere. #### Solar Pursuit Action Type: No Action Factory Combat Bucket: passive Factory Routing: passive_or_triggered_modifier_row Trigger: You spend an Overkindled Mark with Overexpose Cost: 2 CP Until the end of your next turn, you know the marked creature’s direction while it remains within 300 feet of you, even if it later becomes Hidden or Invisible. This does not reveal the creature through planar boundaries, sealed Barriers, lead-lined vaults, anti-divination effects, or superior concealment. #### Completing Flame Mantle Action Type: Bonus Action Factory Combat Bucket: bonus_action Factory Routing: combat_action_row Range: Self Duration: Concentration, up to 1 minute Cost: 4 CP You wrap yourself in rising heat, bright breath, and surplus meridian force. For the duration: when you use Kindle the Rising on yourself, you may also apply a Kindled Mark to one willing creature within 10 feet; once per turn when you spend a Kindled Mark with Complete Force, the bonus damage may be Fire, Radiant, or Force damage; a creature that starts its turn Grappling you takes Fire or Radiant damage equal to your Proficiency Bonus + your Key Ability modifier; you emit bright light in a 10-foot radius and dim light for an additional 10 feet. Completing Flame Mantle does not count as sunlight. ### CORE FORMATION REALM YANG TALENTS #### Yang Domain: Court of Unfinished Noon “Within my court, nothing is allowed to remain almost done.” Action Type: Action Factory Combat Bucket: action Factory Routing: combat_action_row Area: 30-foot-radius aura centered on you Duration: Concentration, up to 1 minute Cost: 7 CP You establish a Domain where incomplete force is compelled toward completion. While inside the Domain, you gain the following benefits: Your Mark Limit increases by your Key Ability modifier, minimum 1. Once per round, when an ally inside the Domain hits with an attack, forces a saving throw, regains Hit Points, gains Temporary HP, moves at least 10 feet, or succeeds on a saving throw against a suppressive effect, you may apply a Kindled Mark to that ally without using your Bonus Action. Once per round, when an enemy inside the Domain becomes Hidden, becomes Invisible, creates concealment, creates an illusion, teleports, spends CP, uses a spell slot, uses a limited feature, or remains in the same space for its whole turn, you may apply an Overkindled Mark to that enemy without using your Reaction. When you spend a Rising Mark inside the Domain, choose one creature within 10 feet of the marked subject. That creature emits dim light until the start of your next turn. If it is unwilling, it may make a Constitution saving throw to avoid emitting the light. Allies inside the Domain gain the following benefit: the first time each round they benefit from a Kindled Response, they gain Temporary HP equal to your Proficiency Bonus. Enemies inside the Domain suffer the following effect: if they begin their turn with one of your Overkindled Marks, they cannot benefit from being Hidden or Invisible against you until the start of their next turn. The Domain is not a Fire, Radiance, or Life effect by default. It may appear as golden heat, sunrise pressure, summer breath, a furnace court, or red-gold scripture, but its mechanics are the compulsion of force toward completion. #### The Action Becomes More Real Action Type: No Action Factory Combat Bucket: passive Factory Routing: passive_or_triggered_modifier_row Trigger: You spend a Kindled Mark Cost: 3 CP Choose one of the following effects appropriate to the triggering response: if you used Complete Force, the bonus damage is maximized instead of rolled; if you used Complete Aim, the die is treated as its maximum result; if you used Complete Step, the Speed increase lasts until the start of the marked creature’s next turn; if you used Complete Breath, the marked creature also gains Temporary HP equal to your Proficiency Bonus; if you used Complete Resolve, the marked creature gains Advantage on the next saving throw it makes before the start of your next turn. You can use The Action Becomes More Real only once on each of your turns. #### Meridian Overcompletion Action Type: No Action Factory Combat Bucket: passive Factory Routing: passive_or_triggered_modifier_row Trigger: You spend an Overkindled Mark from a creature that spent CP, used a spell slot, activated a limited feature, or used a named cultivation technique Cost: 4 CP Saving Throw: Constitution The target makes a Constitution saving throw. On a failed save, its meridians flare beyond safe measure. It takes 4d8 Fire, Radiant, or Force damage, chosen when you use this talent, and cannot take Reactions until the start of its next turn. On a successful save, it takes half as much damage and suffers no other effect. This talent does not counter, dispel, or interrupt the triggering effect. Yang does not stop the act; it makes the act too complete for the source to remain unchanged. #### Life Refuses Closure Action Type: Reaction Factory Combat Bucket: reaction Factory Routing: combat_action_row Trigger: A willing creature within 60 feet would be reduced to 0 Hit Points but not killed outright Cost: 6 CP Use Limit: Once per Long Rest per creature The target gains a Kindled Mark and drops to 1 Hit Point instead of 0. Until the end of the target’s next turn: its Speed increases by 10 feet; it has Advantage on saving throws against Frightened and effects that would reduce its Speed; the first time it deals damage, it may spend its Kindled Mark with Complete Force without counting against your once-per-round limit. Life Refuses Closure cannot protect a creature whose soul is destroyed or a creature killed by an effect that explicitly prevents death prevention. #### Noon Reveals the Hidden Work Action Type: Action Factory Combat Bucket: action Factory Routing: combat_action_row Range: Self Area: 60-foot-radius aura centered on you Duration: Concentration, up to 1 minute Cost: 6 CP You fill the area with revealing Yang pressure. The area is brightly lit by magical light. This light is not sunlight unless another feature says otherwise. When an enemy in the area becomes Hidden, becomes Invisible, creates concealment, creates an illusion, or benefits from magical darkness, you may apply an Overkindled Mark to that enemy without using your Reaction. You can do this once per round. While an enemy in the area has one of your Overkindled Marks, it cannot benefit from being Invisible against you unless the Invisibility is created by a higher Realm effect, Secret Inheritance, artifact, or similarly superior source. #### Summer Orders the Seed Action Type: Ritual Procedure Canonical Action Type: Ritual Procedure Factory Routing: procedure_ledger_not_combat_action Timing Detail: Ritual Time: 10 minutes Range: Touch Duration: 24 hours Cost: 5 CP Touch one seed, egg, cocoon, sealed wound, dormant talisman, inactive Formation node, sleeping beast core, or other unfinished living or spiritual process. For the duration, the subject is protected from ordinary cold, rot, stagnation, and accidental spoilage. At the end of the ritual, ask the GM one question about what the subject needs in order to safely complete its next natural or intended stage. The answer should be brief but truthful from the subject’s available traces. Summer Orders the Seed does not force immediate growth, heal a creature, hatch an egg, repair an item, or activate a Formation by itself. ### NASCENT SOUL REALM YANG TALENTS #### Sovereign Yang Incarnation “I do not chase dawn. I am the command that makes the horizon answer.” Action Type: Bonus Action Factory Combat Bucket: bonus_action Factory Routing: combat_action_row Duration: 1 minuteConcentration: Not required Cost: 15 CP Use Limit: Once per Long Rest You become a sovereign vessel of assertive completion. For the duration, you gain the following benefits: Your Mark Limit doubles. Once on each of your turns, you may use Kindle the Rising without using a Bonus Action. You may spend Rising Marks twice per round instead of once per round. When you spend a Kindled Mark, choose one: gain Temporary HP equal to your Proficiency Bonus + Key Ability modifier; move 10 feet without provoking Opportunity Attacks; or emit bright light in a 20-foot radius until the start of your next turn. When you spend an Overkindled Mark, the marked creature cannot benefit from being Hidden or Invisible against you until the start of its next turn. Sovereign Yang Incarnation does not create fire or sunlight by itself. It is the pressure of incompletion being forced toward expression. #### The Action Cannot Stay Small Action Type: Reaction Factory Combat Bucket: reaction Factory Routing: combat_action_row Trigger: A marked creature within 90 feet completes an Action, Bonus Action, Reaction, spell, sphere talent, forged technique, monster action, or cultivation ability Cost: 10 CP Use Limit: Once per Short Rest Saving Throw: Constitution if the creature is unwilling Spend the creature’s Rising Mark. If the creature is willing, choose one complete result appropriate to the triggering action: one damage roll from the action gains an additional 4d10 Fire, Radiant, or Force damage; one healing or Temporary Hit Point effect from the action gains an additional 4d10 Hit Points or Temporary HP; one movement effect from the action increases by 30 feet; one condition the action would end cannot be reimposed by the same source until the start of the creature’s next turn; one Barrier, construct, summoned creature, or created effect from the action appears with additional Hit Points equal to 5 x your CL. If the creature is unwilling, it makes a Constitution saving throw. On a failed save, the action completes with dangerous surplus. Choose one overcomplete result: the creature takes 6d10 Fire, Radiant, or Force damage after the action resolves; the creature cannot benefit from being Hidden or Invisible until the end of your next turn; the creature cannot take Reactions and cannot willingly repeat the same named action until the end of its next turn; one created, summoned, or conjured effect from the action emits bright light in a 20-foot radius and has Vulnerability to the next damage roll that hits it before the start of your next turn. On a successful save, the action functions normally, but the target gains a Rising Mark immediately after the action resolves. Declare this talent immediately when the trigger occurs. #### No Seal Holds the Sun Action Type: Action Factory Combat Bucket: action Factory Routing: combat_action_row Range: 90 feet Cost: 10 CP Use Limit: Once per Long Rest Saving Throw: Wisdom Choose one creature, object, Barrier, Formation Anchor, sealed door, spiritual lock, or ongoing suppressive effect within range that has one of your Rising Marks. The target makes a Wisdom saving throw if it is a creature or if its creator is present and able to contest the effect. On a failed save, choose one appropriate effect: one non-Secret effect reducing Speed ends; one non-Secret effect preventing Reactions ends; one non-Secret effect imposing Restrained, Paralyzed, Stunned, or Incapacitated ends; one mundane or lower-Realm seal opens enough to allow passage for one creature before closing again; one Barrier, ward, or Formation Anchor loses Hit Points equal to 5 x your CL; one concealed object or hidden passage emits bright light until the end of your next turn. On a successful save, the effect is not ended, but the target gains a Rising Mark that lasts for 1 minute. This talent cannot automatically break Secret Inheritances, artifacts, divine seals, Realm-defining Domains, or higher-Realm suppressive effects. #### Dawn Commands the Fallen Breath Action Type: Reaction Factory Combat Bucket: reaction Factory Routing: combat_action_row Trigger: You or an ally within 60 feet would die Cost: 12 CP Use Limit: Once per Long Rest The target drops to 1 Hit Point instead of dying and gains a Kindled Mark that lasts for 1 minute. It may immediately stand if Prone. Until the end of the target’s next turn: its Speed increases by 20 feet; Opportunity Attacks against it are made with Disadvantage; the first time it hits with an attack or forces a creature to fail a saving throw, it may spend its Kindled Mark with Complete Force or Complete Aim without counting against your once-per-round limit. This cannot protect a creature whose soul is destroyed, whose body is completely annihilated, or whose death is caused by an effect that explicitly prevents death prevention or revival. #### Ten-Thousand Motions Become Noon Action Type: Action Factory Combat Bucket: action Factory Routing: combat_action_row Range: 120 feet Area: 60-foot-radius sphere Duration: Concentration, up to 1 minute Cost: 12 CP Use Limit: Once per Long Rest You create an area where all hidden momentum is pulled toward expression. While in the area: allies that start their turn in the area may gain one Kindled Mark; enemies that start their turn Hidden, Invisible, heavily obscured, or under an illusion gain one Overkindled Mark; when any creature in the area moves at least 20 feet during its turn, it emits dim light until the start of its next turn; when you spend a Rising Mark in the area, increase one die rolled by the response to its maximum result. The area is not sunlight unless the GM rules that your cultivation method is specifically solar. ### Secret Inheritance - The Completed Action Beneath Heaven “You began. Heaven will not permit you to remain unfinished.” Classification: Secret Yang Talent Prerequisite: CL 17+, Yang Domain, secret solar scripture or forbidden furnace inheritance Action Type: Reaction Factory Combat Bucket: reaction Factory Routing: combat_action_row Range: 120 feet Cost: 18 CP Use Limit: Once per week Saving Throw: Constitution if the source is unwilling Trigger: A creature, object, Barrier, Formation, Domain, spell, sphere talent, forged technique, monster action, cultivation ability, or supernatural event you can perceive begins to produce a consequence. You declare that the consequence must complete itself beneath Heaven. If the source is willing or the triggering event is your own effect, choose one consequence of the event. That consequence becomes complete: one damage roll is maximized for one target; one healing or Temporary Hit Point effect is maximized for one target; one teleportation, movement, or forced movement effect reaches its intended legal destination despite lower-Realm reduction; one condition-removal effect removes the condition from one target despite lower-Realm suppression; one Barrier, Domain, Formation, summoned creature, or created object appears with full normal Hit Points and duration despite lower-Realm weakening; one revealing effect pierces lower-Realm darkness, concealment, or illusion for one target; one spoken command, oath, kiai, mantra, or declaration reaches all intended legal listeners within range despite lower-Realm silence or muffling. If the source is unwilling, the source makes a Constitution saving throw. On a failed save, the event completes with forbidden surplus. Choose one consequence: the source takes 12d10 Fire, Radiant, or Force damage after the event resolves; the source cannot benefit from being Hidden, Invisible, or magically concealed until the end of your next turn; the source cannot use the same named spell, talent, monster action, forged technique, or cultivation ability again until the end of its next turn; a created Barrier, Domain, Formation effect, summon, or object appears overbright and unstable, losing half its Hit Points or duration after its first turn or first activation; one resource the source spent becomes visible as spiritual expenditure, allowing you to learn whether it used CP, a spell slot, charges, a limited use, or an external patron. On a successful save, the event completes normally, but the source gains a Rising Mark that lasts for 1 minute, and you may immediately spend that mark without counting against your once-per-round limit. The Completed Action Beneath Heaven cannot force a plot-level miracle, override superior Realm law by default, compel a god, restore a destroyed soul, or guarantee a whole scene outcome. Against artifacts, divine interventions, Realm-defining Domains, Secret Inheritances, and superior cultivation-scale effects, the GM may reduce the failed-save result to partial completion or dangerous overcompletion rather than full effect. This inheritance is forbidden because it proves that incompletion is not safety. ### YANG DRAWBACKS AND VARIANT SCRIPTURES Yang variants are optional cultivation scriptures that change how the sphere manifests. They are Tianxia-specific limitations, not imported casting-tradition rules. Unless the GM says otherwise: choose at most one Yang variant when you first learn Yang or undergo a major Yang initiation; Yang variants are mutually exclusive; the drawback applies to all Yang talents and Rising Marks you use; if a variant grants a talent whose prerequisites are not yet met, you gain that talent when you meet its prerequisites; if the variant is retrained or removed, you lose its bonus talent and benefits. A Yang variant grants a real benefit only when it also gives a real limitation. The drawback changes how Yang behaves at the table, not merely how it looks. #### Gentle Sun Scripture You cultivate Yang as warmth, encouragement, recovery, and patient completion. Benefit. You gain Kindle the Wounded Breath as a bonus talent. When you use Kindle the Rising on a willing creature that has fewer than half its Hit Points, you may choose for the mark to last until the end of your following turn instead of until the end of your next turn. Drawback: Vow of Gentle Completion. Your Yang refuses to become the first cruelty. Your Rising Thread damage die is reduced from d6 to d4. In addition, you cannot spend an Overkindled Mark to deal damage to a living creature unless that creature has damaged another creature, forced another creature to make a saving throw, spent CP, used a spell slot, used a limited feature, used a supernatural feature, or willingly caused a hostile supernatural effect since the start of its last turn. This restriction does not prevent you from: placing Overkindled Marks without dealing damage; spending Overkindled Marks for Overexpose, Overcommit Step, Overstrain Technique, pursuit, revelation, or non-damaging backlash; using Yang against undead, constructs, objects, barriers, hostile Formations, curses, poisons, diseases, environmental hazards, or nonliving magical effects; using Yang to protect, heal, reveal, encourage, preserve momentum, or complete an ally’s action. Gentle Sun cultivators can still fight. They must answer harmful motion rather than initiating harm without cause. #### Scarlet Furnace Scripture You cultivate Yang through blood heat, pain tolerance, and organs that burn like a sealed furnace. Benefit. Once per round, when you spend a Kindled Mark on yourself with Complete Force or Complete Step, you may take Fire or Radiant damage equal to your Proficiency Bonus + your Key Ability modifier, minimum equal to your Proficiency Bonus. If you do, the mark is not expended. This damage cannot be reduced by Resistance or Immunity, cannot be redirected, and cannot be prevented by Temporary HP. Drawback: Furnace Turns Inward. Your Yang gathers first in your own body and only poorly nourishes others. You cannot use Kindle the Rising on a willing creature other than yourself unless that creature is within 5 feet of you. When you use Complete Breath on a creature other than yourself, halve the additional Hit Points or Temporary HP granted by the response, rounded down. Scarlet Furnace cultivators are terrifying engines of self-completion, but they are weaker as distant healers, commanders, or gentle benefactors. #### Revealing Noon Scripture You cultivate Yang as exposure, testimony, pursuit, and the impossibility of hiding what has begun. Benefit. You gain Overbright Trail as a bonus talent. When you spend an Overkindled Mark with Overexpose, the effect lasts until the end of your next turn instead of the start of your next turn. Drawback: Witness Cannot Be Hidden. Your Yang declares itself whenever it acts. Whenever you apply or spend a Rising Mark, you emit bright light in a 10-foot radius and dim light for an additional 10 feet until the start of your next turn. If you are Hidden when you apply or spend a Rising Mark, you cease being Hidden. Until the start of your next turn after using a Yang talent, you have Disadvantage on Dexterity (Stealth) checks and cannot benefit from being Invisible against creatures that can see the light you emit. This light is not sunlight unless another feature says otherwise. Revealing Noon cultivators are excellent hunters of concealment, lies, and secret techniques, but their own Yang is almost impossible to practice discreetly. #### Relentless Summer Scripture You cultivate Yang as growth, seasonal abundance, ripening pressure, and the life-force that refuses dormancy. Benefit. You gain Unfinished Bloom as a bonus talent when you reach Foundation Realm. When you use Summer Orders the Seed, increase its duration to 7 days. If the duration is already 7 days or longer from another feature, increase it by one step at the GM’s discretion. Drawback: Rooted Season. Your Yang is strongest when it has something living, growing, or ripening to answer. You cannot choose Complete Revelation or Overexpose unless the marked subject is within 10 feet of soil, plants, living wood, fertile water, a living creature, a beast core, a seed, an egg, or a natural ecosystem. In sterile, sealed, lifeless, void-scoured, or wholly artificial environments, the CP cost of your Yang talents increases by 1 CP, unless the talent targets yourself, a living creature, or a natural object you are carrying. This increase cannot raise a cost above 1 additional CP per use. Relentless Summer cultivators are powerful in battlefields where life remains present, but their revelation and abundance falter in places cut off from seasonal breath. #### Unforgiving Noon Scripture You cultivate Yang as judgment, conquest, unbearable clarity, and action that refuses retreat. Benefit. Once per round, when you apply an Overkindled Mark to a creature that damaged you or an ally since the start of its last turn, you may immediately deal Fire, Radiant, or Force damage to that creature equal to your Proficiency Bonus. Drawback: No Backward Sun. You cannot willingly spend a Kindled Mark to increase movement away from a hostile creature you can perceive, and you cannot use Complete Breath on a creature that has not made an attack roll, forced a saving throw, moved at least 10 feet, spent CP, used a spell slot, or used a limited feature since the start of its last turn. In addition, when you roll Initiative, if you have no Rising Marks active, your first Rising Mark of the encounter must be an Overkindled Mark unless no enemy is present or no enemy can be perceived. Unforgiving Noon cultivators are strong punishers and duelists, but their Yang resists retreat, rest, and passive recovery. ### PATH SYNERGIES #### Qi Cultivation: Furnace Meridian Your qi runs upward, outward, and toward completion. Once per turn when you spend CP on a Yang talent that applies, spends, or modifies a Rising Mark, reduce the CP cost by 1, to a minimum cost of 1 CP. When you spend a Kindled Mark with Complete Force or Complete Breath, add +1 to one die rolled by that response. #### Body Refining: Overfull Vessel Body This synergy requires the Overfull Vessel Body Insight. You may use Constitution as your Yang key ability and spend Stamina instead of CP for Yang talents. When you spend a Kindled Mark on yourself with Complete Step, increase the Speed bonus by 5 feet. When you spend a Kindled Mark on yourself with Complete Force, you may push one damaged creature 5 feet directly away from you. This synergy does not grant Resistance, Immunity, armor, natural weapons, or extra attacks unless a separate feature says so. #### Spirit Awakening: Solar Soul This synergy requires the Solar Soul Insight. When you apply an Overkindled Mark to a spirit, ghost, undead, possessing entity, incorporeal creature, or creature currently possessing another creature, the mark lasts for 1 minute instead of until the end of your next turn. Once per round when you spend an Overkindled Mark from such a creature, you may choose Radiant damage for any damage dealt by the response, even if that response would normally use another listed Yang damage type. ### CULTIVATION INSIGHTS #### Overfull Vessel Body Prerequisite: Body Refining, CL 4+ You may learn Yang talents. When using Yang, you use Constitution as your key ability and spend Stamina instead of CP. You gain the Overfull Vessel Body Path synergy. #### Solar Soul Prerequisite: Spirit Awakening, CL 4+ You may learn Yang talents. When using Yang, use Wisdom as your key ability and spend Resonance instead of CP. You gain the Solar Soul Path synergy. #### Dawn Foundation Prerequisite: Yang sphere, CL 4+ When you roll Initiative and have no Rising Marks active, you may place one Kindled Mark on yourself. If you are surprised, you cannot use this Insight until after your first turn in combat. #### Completion Under Pressure Prerequisite: Yang sphere, CL 8+ Once per Long Rest, when you would fail a Constitution saving throw made to maintain Concentration on a Yang talent, you may choose to succeed instead. #### Noon-Eye Witness Prerequisite: Yang sphere, CL 8+ When you spend an Overkindled Mark with Overexpose, you may also learn whether the concealment came from a mundane Hide action, spell, sphere talent, item, creature trait, illusion, Yin-like technique, or environmental feature. This does not identify the exact feature unless other evidence supports that conclusion. #### Sun-Over-Moon Countermark Prerequisite: Yang sphere, CL 12+ When a creature you can perceive places a Waning Mark, suppression mark, curse mark, or similar diminishing mark on you or a willing ally within 60 feet, you may spend 2 CP as a Reaction to place a Kindled Mark on the same target. The two marks do not cancel each other by default. If both are spent on the same triggering action, resolve the higher-Realm effect first. If both effects are the same Realm, resolve the older mark first unless the GM rules otherwise. ### DESTRUCTION CROSSOVER: VITAL OVERLOAD Yang can provide a Destruction blast expression for cultivators who possess the Sphere of Destruction. #### Vital Overload Type: Destruction Blast Type Prerequisite: Sphere of Destruction Destruction Die: d6 Damage: Radiant or Fire, chosen when the blast is used A creature damaged by Vital Overload gains an Overkindled Mark until the start of your next turn. The mark does not count against your normal Mark Limit, but you can spend it only on Overheat Force or Overcommit Step. #### Meridian Overstrain Type: Foundation Refinement Prerequisite: Vital Overload, Foundation Realm When you spend the Overkindled Mark from Vital Overload with Overheat Force, add one additional Destruction Die to the backlash damage. #### Unceasing Exertion Type: Nascent Soul Refinement Prerequisite: Meridian Overstrain, Nascent Soul Realm The Overkindled Mark from Vital Overload lasts until the end of your next turn instead of until the start of your next turn.

### BASE SPHERE ABILITIES
The Yang sphere uses Rising Marks. A Rising Mark is not a condition. Immunity to a condition does not grant immunity to Rising Marks unless a feature says otherwise.
A Rising Mark represents a motion, wound, breath, oath, technique, or intention that has begun to swell toward completion.
#### Mark Limit
You can maintain a number of Rising Marks equal to your Proficiency Bonus. A creature, object, or ongoing effect can have only one Rising Mark from you at a time unless a feature says otherwise.
A Rising Mark lasts until the end of your next turn, until you spend it, or until the marked subject is no longer on the same plane of existence as you.
#### Kindled and Overkindled Marks
A Rising Mark has one of two expressions.
Kindled Mark. A Rising Mark on you, a willing creature, an unattended object, or an effect you created is a Kindled Mark. You spend Kindled Marks to help an action complete.
Overkindled Mark. A Rising Mark on an unwilling creature, hostile object, enemy effect, or creature that rejects your assistance is an Overkindled Mark. You spend Overkindled Marks to make hostile exertion overcomplete, exposing or straining the source.
A willing creature may end your Rising Mark on itself at any time, no Action required.
#### Applying a Rising Mark
You can apply a Rising Mark in three basic ways.
Kindle the Rising. As a Bonus Action, choose yourself or one willing creature, unattended object, or ongoing effect you created within 60 feet that you can perceive. The target gains one Kindled Mark.
Force the Rising. As a Reaction when a creature, object, or effect within 60 feet that you can perceive hits with an attack, forces a saving throw, regains Hit Points, gains Temporary HP, spends CP, uses a spell slot, uses a limited feature, teleports, becomes Hidden, becomes Invisible, creates concealment, creates an illusion, or moves at least 10 feet during its turn, you may apply one Overkindled Mark to the source after the triggering event resolves.
Rising Thread. As an Action, make a ranged Cultivation Attack against one creature or object within 60 feet. On a hit, the target takes Fire, Radiant, or Force damage, chosen when you make the attack, and gains one Overkindled Mark.
| Cultivation Level | Rising Thread Damage |
| --- | --- |
| CL 1-4 | 1d6 |
| CL 5-10 | 2d6 |
| CL 11-16 | 3d6 |
| CL 17-20 | 4d6 |
The damage is not the sphere’s identity. It is the visible symptom of qi becoming too bright, too hot, or too forceful to remain unfinished.
#### Spending a Rising Mark
Once per round, when a marked subject you can perceive performs a triggering act, you may spend its Rising Mark without using an Action. Choose one Completing Response appropriate to the mark.
#### Kindled Responses
You may use these responses when you spend a Kindled Mark.
Complete Force.
Trigger: the marked subject deals damage. Add 1d6 + your Key Ability modifier to one damage roll. This bonus increases to 2d6 at CL 5, 3d6 at CL 11, and 4d6 at CL 17.
Complete Aim.

Overkindled Mark. A Rising Mark on an unwilling creature, hostile object, enemy effect, or creature that rejects your assistance is an Overkindled Mark. You spend Overkindled Marks to make hostile exertion overcomplete, exposing or straining the source.

#### Overkindled Responses
You may use these responses when you spend an Overkindled Mark.
Overheat Force.
Trigger: the marked subject deals damage, makes an attack roll, or forces one or more creatures to make a saving throw. After the triggering act resolves, the subject takes Fire or Radiant damage equal to 1d6 + your Key Ability modifier. This damage increases to 2d6 at CL 5, 3d6 at CL 11, and 4d6 at CL 17.
Overexpose.
Trigger: the marked subject becomes Hidden, becomes Invisible, creates concealment, creates an illusion, or benefits from a feature that prevents others from perceiving it. Until the start of your next turn, the subject cannot benefit from being Hidden or Invisible against you, and allies you choose within 60 feet know the subject’s current space if they can perceive the area.
Overcommit Step.
Trigger: the marked subject moves at least 10 feet, teleports, or uses special movement. After the movement resolves, the subject cannot take Reactions until the start of its next turn. If the movement was teleportation and the destination is within 120 feet of you, you know the destination space.
Overgrown Recovery.
Trigger: the marked subject regains Hit Points, gains Temporary HP, restores CP, or benefits from regeneration. Until the start of your next turn, the first damage roll against that subject gains a bonus equal to your Proficiency Bonus.
Overstrain Technique.
Trigger: the marked subject spends CP, uses a spell slot, activates a limited feature, or uses a named cultivation technique. If the subject uses the same named spell, sphere talent, forged technique, monster action, or cultivation ability again before the end of its next turn, it gains a Rising Mark immediately after the repeated ability resolves.

automatic_base_abilities.effect:
### BASE SPHERE ABILITIES
The Yin sphere uses Waning Marks. A Waning Mark is not a condition. Immunity to a condition does not grant immunity to Waning Marks unless a feature says otherwise.
A Waning Mark represents a motion, technique, wound, breath, or intention that has begun to decline before it finishes expressing itself.
#### Mark Limit
You can maintain a number of Waning Marks equal to your Proficiency Bonus. A creature can have only one Waning Mark from you at a time unless a feature says otherwise.
A Waning Mark lasts until the end of your next turn, until you spend it, or until the marked creature is no longer on the same plane of existence as you.
#### Marking a Creature
You can apply a Waning Mark in three basic ways.
Mark the Waning. As a Bonus Action, choose one creature within 60 feet that you can see, hear, or otherwise perceive clearly. The target gains one Waning Mark.
Receive Overextension. As a Reaction when a creature within 60 feet that you can perceive hits with an attack, forces a saving throw, regains Hit Points, gains Temporary HP, spends CP, uses a spell slot, teleports, or moves at least 10 feet during its turn, you may apply one Waning Mark to that creature after the triggering event resolves.
Withdrawing Thread. As an Action, make a ranged Cultivation Attack against one creature or object within 60 feet. On a hit, the target takes Cold or Necrotic damage, chosen when you make the attack, and gains one Waning Mark.
| Cultivation Level | Withdrawing Thread Damage |
| --- | --- |
| CL 1-4 | 1d6 |
| CL 5-10 | 2d6 |
| CL 11-16 | 3d6 |
| CL 17-20 | 4d6 |
The damage is not the sphere’s identity. It is the visible symptom of qi cooling as the target’s action begins to wane.
#### Spending a Waning Mark
Once per round, when a marked creature you can perceive performs a triggering act, you may spend its Waning Mark without using an Action. Choose one Diminishing Response appropriate to the trigger.
**Diminish Force**
Trigger: the marked creature deals damage. Reduce one damage roll by 1d6 + your Key Ability modifier. This reduction increases to 2d6 at CL 5, 3d6 at CL 11, and 4d6 at CL 17.
**Diminish Aim**
Trigger: the marked creature makes an attack roll. Subtract 1d4 from the attack roll. At CL 11, subtract 1d6 instead.
**Diminish Power**
Trigger: the marked creature forces one or more creatures to make a saving throw. Choose one creature making that saving throw. The chosen creature adds 1d4 to the saving throw. At CL 11, the bonus becomes 1d6.
**Diminish Step**
Trigger: the marked creature begins movement, including teleportation. Reduce one of the creature’s Speeds by 10 feet until the end of the current turn, or reduce the distance of one teleportation effect by 10 feet. At CL 11, the reduction becomes 20 feet.
**Diminish Recovery**
Trigger: the marked creature regains Hit Points, gains Temporary HP, restores CP, or benefits from regeneration. Reduce the amount gained or restored by your Proficiency Bonus + your Key Ability modifier, to a minimum of 0.
**Diminish Readiness**
Trigger: the marked creature takes a Reaction or would gain Advantage on a roll. The creature cannot take Reactions until the start of its next turn, or the triggering Advantage is canceled for that roll.
#### Yin Saves
Some Yin features require a saving throw. Unless a feature says otherwise, your Cultivation Save DC equals your Cultivation Save DC.
#### Marked Allies
You may place a Waning Mark on a willing ally. When you do, the mark represents preservation rather than harm. You may spend that mark only for Diminish Force, Diminish Power, Diminish Step, or Diminish Recovery if doing so benefits the ally.
A willing creature may end your Waning Mark on itself at any time, no Action required.

### BASE SPHERE ABILITIES
The Yin sphere uses Waning Marks. A Waning Mark is not a condition. Immunity to a condition does not grant immunity to Waning Marks unless a feature says otherwise.
A Waning Mark represents a motion, technique, wound, breath, or intention that has begun to decline before it finishes expressing itself.
#### Mark Limit
You can maintain a number of Waning Marks equal to your Proficiency Bonus. A creature can have only one Waning Mark from you at a time unless a feature says otherwise.
A Waning Mark lasts until the end of your next turn, until you spend it, or until the marked creature is no longer on the same plane of existence as you.
#### Marking a Creature
You can apply a Waning Mark in three basic ways.
Mark the Waning. As a Bonus Action, choose one creature within 60 feet that you can see, hear, or otherwise perceive clearly. The target gains one Waning Mark.
Receive Overextension. As a Reaction when a creature within 60 feet that you can perceive hits with an attack, forces a saving throw, regains Hit Points, gains Temporary HP, spends CP, uses a spell slot, teleports, or moves at least 10 feet during its turn, you may apply one Waning Mark to that creature after the triggering event resolves.
Withdrawing Thread. As an Action, make a ranged Cultivation Attack against one creature or object within 60 feet. On a hit, the target takes Cold or Necrotic damage, chosen when you make the attack, and gains one Waning Mark.
| Cultivation Level | Withdrawing Thread Damage |
| --- | --- |
| CL 1-4 | 1d6 |
| CL 5-10 | 2d6 |
| CL 11-16 | 3d6 |
| CL 17-20 | 4d6 |
The damage is not the sphere’s identity. It is the visible symptom of qi cooling as the target’s action begins to wane.
#### Spending a Waning Mark
Once per round, when a marked creature you can perceive performs a triggering act, you may spend its Waning Mark without using an Action. Choose one Diminishing Response appropriate to the trigger.
**Diminish Force**
Trigger: the marked creature deals damage. Reduce one damage roll by 1d6 + your Key Ability modifier. This reduction increases to 2d6 at CL 5, 3d6 at CL 11, and 4d6 at CL 17.
**Diminish Aim**
Trigger: the marked creature makes an attack roll. Subtract 1d4 from the attack roll. At CL 11, subtract 1d6 instead.
**Diminish Power**
Trigger: the marked creature forces one or more creatures to make a saving throw. Choose one creature making that saving throw. The chosen creature adds 1d4 to the saving throw. At CL 11, the bonus becomes 1d6.
**Diminish Step**
Trigger: the marked creature begins movement, including teleportation. Reduce one of the creature’s Speeds by 10 feet until the end of the current turn, or reduce the distance of one teleportation effect by 10 feet. At CL 11, the reduction becomes 20 feet.
**Diminish Recovery**
Trigger: the marked creature regains Hit Points, gains Temporary HP, restores CP, or benefits from regeneration. Reduce the amount gained or restored by your Proficiency Bonus + your Key Ability modifier, to a minimum of 0.
**Diminish Readiness**
Trigger: the marked creature takes a Reaction or would gain Advantage on a roll. The creature cannot take Reactions until the start of its next turn, or the triggering Advantage is canceled for that roll.
#### Yin Saves
Some Yin features require a saving throw. Unless a feature says otherwise, your Cultivation Save DC equals your Cultivation Save DC.
#### Marked Allies
You may place a Waning Mark on a willing ally. When you do, the mark represents preservation rather than harm. You may spend that mark only for Diminish Force, Diminish Power, Diminish Step, or Diminish Recovery if doing so benefits the ally.
A willing creature may end your Waning Mark on itself at any time, no Action required.
