spheres.full_exact_source_text: # Sphere of Yin > Player-facing rewrite overlay. This text preserves the current Waning Mark mechanics while cleaning formatting, duplicated names, and draft-style presentation. Qi Expression: Primary — Yin Qi; Supporting — Water Qi, Stillness Qi, Hidden Qi, Preservation Qi. “Yang completes itself by force. Yin waits for the force to overreach, receives it, and teaches it how to end.” Sphere Type: Forbidden Power Sphere Primary Path: Spirit Awakening Secondary Path: Qi Cultivation Rare Variant: Body Refining through the Still Vessel Body Insight Resource: CP Core Mechanic: Waning Marks Common Effects: receiving force, diminishing completed actions, suppressing repetition, preserving unfinished states, concealment through withdrawal, spiritual stillness, cold as a symptom of waning qi, and forbidden interference with the completion of events The Sphere of Yin is the forbidden cultivation of receptive decline. A Yin cultivator wins by letting force overextend, marking that force as waning, and then making its consequence arrive smaller, slower, quieter, or incomplete. Yin is not simply ice, darkness, silence, death, or negation. Those may appear as symptoms, but the sphere’s identity is **receiving and diminishing a consequence that has already begun**. A blow lands with less force. A command reaches fewer ears. A wound refuses to close. A step begins and discovers that stillness has already claimed part of it. ### PLAYER SUMMARY Use Yin if you want a reactive control sphere that rewards timing, patience, and reading the enemy. Your basic loop is: 1. Place or receive a **Waning Mark**. 2. Wait for the marked creature to attack, move, heal, spend power, or repeat a technique. 3. Spend the mark to diminish that consequence. 4. Convert the diminished action into concealment, preservation, anti-healing, anti-repetition, or counterpressure. Yin is forbidden because it interferes with completion itself: the action begins, but Heaven is not required to let it fully arrive. ### Sphere Boundaries Yin overlaps with several spheres, but it does not replace them. | Sphere | Difference from Yin | | --- | --- | | Cold | Cold freezes, creates ice, and controls temperature directly. Yin may create cold as a sign that motion and life-force are waning, but cold is not the sphere identity. | | Dark | Dark controls light and the absence of light. Yin may conceal what has withdrawn from the world’s attention, but it does not automatically create darkness. | | Death | Death governs souls leaving bodies, corpses, ghosts, undead, and mortality. Yin can preserve, delay, and diminish life-force, but does not automatically command death. | | Moon | Moon governs cycles, tides, reflection, phases, and lunar change. Yin is the receptive principle beneath waning, concealment, and inward return. | | Shadow | Shadow is the second silhouette created by light and form. Yin can hide what withdraws, but does not automatically create shadow constructs. | | Void | Void removes, hollows, and negates. Yin receives, diminishes, preserves, and returns force to stillness. | | Time | Time changes order, sequence, or duration. Yin can delay completion or preserve a state, but does not rewrite chronology. | | Protection | Protection blocks harm. Yin receives harm and makes its consequence smaller or incomplete. | | Yang | Yang asserts, rises, accelerates, reveals, and completes itself through outward force. Yin receives, draws inward, dims, delays, and completes things by returning them to stillness. | ### WHAT YIN DOES NOT DO BY DEFAULT Except where a Yin feature explicitly says otherwise, ordinary Fifth Edition rules remain in force. Yin does not automatically: create Darkness, Dim Light, or supernatural darkness; make a creature Hidden or Invisible; grant Resistance or Immunity; stop verbal components; prevent healing; stop teleportation; reduce Speed below 0; create ice terrain; preserve a corpse indefinitely; counter a spell, sphere talent, or technique; refund or steal CP; affect a creature that is immune to the relevant condition, damage type, or movement restriction. A feature must state any such effect directly. ### BASE SPHERE ABILITIES The Yin sphere uses Waning Marks. A Waning Mark is not a condition. Immunity to a condition does not grant immunity to Waning Marks unless a feature says otherwise. A Waning Mark represents a motion, technique, wound, breath, or intention that has begun to decline before it finishes expressing itself. #### Mark Limit You can maintain a number of Waning Marks equal to your Proficiency Bonus. A creature can have only one Waning Mark from you at a time unless a feature says otherwise. A Waning Mark lasts until the end of your next turn, until you spend it, or until the marked creature is no longer on the same plane of existence as you. #### Marking a Creature You can apply a Waning Mark in three basic ways. Mark the Waning. As a Bonus Action, choose one creature within 60 feet that you can see, hear, or otherwise perceive clearly. The target gains one Waning Mark. Receive Overextension. As a Reaction when a creature within 60 feet that you can perceive hits with an attack, forces a saving throw, regains Hit Points, gains Temporary HP, spends CP, uses a spell slot, teleports, or moves at least 10 feet during its turn, you may apply one Waning Mark to that creature after the triggering event resolves. Withdrawing Thread. As an Action, make a ranged Cultivation Attack against one creature or object within 60 feet. On a hit, the target takes Cold or Necrotic damage, chosen when you make the attack, and gains one Waning Mark. | Cultivation Level | Withdrawing Thread Damage | | --- | --- | | CL 1-4 | 1d6 | | CL 5-10 | 2d6 | | CL 11-16 | 3d6 | | CL 17-20 | 4d6 | The damage is not the sphere’s identity. It is the visible symptom of qi cooling as the target’s action begins to wane. #### Spending a Waning Mark Once per round, when a marked creature you can perceive performs a triggering act, you may spend its Waning Mark without using an Action. Choose one Diminishing Response appropriate to the trigger. **Diminish Force** Trigger: the marked creature deals damage. Reduce one damage roll by 1d6 + your Key Ability modifier. This reduction increases to 2d6 at CL 5, 3d6 at CL 11, and 4d6 at CL 17. **Diminish Aim** Trigger: the marked creature makes an attack roll. Subtract 1d4 from the attack roll. At CL 11, subtract 1d6 instead. **Diminish Power** Trigger: the marked creature forces one or more creatures to make a saving throw. Choose one creature making that saving throw. The chosen creature adds 1d4 to the saving throw. At CL 11, the bonus becomes 1d6. **Diminish Step** Trigger: the marked creature begins movement, including teleportation. Reduce one of the creature’s Speeds by 10 feet until the end of the current turn, or reduce the distance of one teleportation effect by 10 feet. At CL 11, the reduction becomes 20 feet. **Diminish Recovery** Trigger: the marked creature regains Hit Points, gains Temporary HP, restores CP, or benefits from regeneration. Reduce the amount gained or restored by your Proficiency Bonus + your Key Ability modifier, to a minimum of 0. **Diminish Readiness** Trigger: the marked creature takes a Reaction or would gain Advantage on a roll. The creature cannot take Reactions until the start of its next turn, or the triggering Advantage is canceled for that roll. #### Yin Saves Some Yin features require a saving throw. Unless a feature says otherwise, your Cultivation Save DC equals your Cultivation Save DC. #### Marked Allies You may place a Waning Mark on a willing ally. When you do, the mark represents preservation rather than harm. You may spend that mark only for Diminish Force, Diminish Power, Diminish Step, or Diminish Recovery if doing so benefits the ally. A willing creature may end your Waning Mark on itself at any time, no Action required. ### HOW TO PLAY WANING MARKS A Mortal Yin cultivator usually plays like this: Place a Waning Mark with a Bonus Action, Reaction, or Withdrawing Thread. Wait for the marked creature to overextend. Spend the mark to diminish one consequence. Use talents to turn the spent mark into concealment, preservation, counterpressure, or deeper suppression. The player should be watching enemy behavior, not just selecting a damage option. ### MORTAL REALM YIN TALENTS #### Quiet Reception Action Type: Reaction Factory Combat Bucket: reaction Factory Routing: combat_action_row Trigger: A creature within 60 feet that you can perceive misses you or an ally with an attack roll Cost: None You receive the failed motion and mark its decline. The triggering creature gains one Waning Mark. If the attack missed because of Disadvantage, concealment, cover, or a penalty imposed by one of your Yin features, the mark lasts for 1 minute instead of until the end of your next turn. #### Moon-Drawn Step Action Type: No Action Factory Combat Bucket: passive Factory Routing: passive_or_triggered_modifier_row Trigger: You spend a Waning Mark with Diminish Step Cost: None After the Diminish Step effect resolves, you may move up to 10 feet without provoking Opportunity Attacks. If you end this movement in Dim Light, Darkness, behind cover, or in an area of concealment created by a Yin feature, you may immediately take the Hide action as part of the same movement. #### Wound That Refuses Dawn Action Type: No Action Factory Combat Bucket: passive Factory Routing: passive_or_triggered_modifier_row Trigger: You spend a Waning Mark with Diminish Recovery Cost: None The target’s recovery continues to wane. Until the start of your next turn, the first time the target would regain Hit Points or gain Temporary HP, reduce that amount by your Proficiency Bonus. At CL 11, the reduction applies to each instance of healing or Temporary HP the target receives before the start of your next turn. #### Still the Bright Strike Action Type: No Action Factory Combat Bucket: passive Factory Routing: passive_or_triggered_modifier_row Trigger: You spend a Waning Mark with Diminish Force or Diminish Aim Cost: None A pale chill gathers around the target’s attacking limb, weapon, spell focus, breath, or qi channel. The target’s Speed is reduced by 10 feet until the start of its next turn. This cannot reduce Speed below 0. #### Preserving Yin Action Type: Reaction Factory Combat Bucket: reaction Factory Routing: combat_action_row Trigger: A willing creature within 30 feet would be reduced to 0 Hit Points but not killed outright Cost: 2 CP You place a Waning Mark on the triggering creature and suspend the final collapse of its breath. The creature drops to 1 Hit Point instead of 0. Until the start of your next turn, it cannot regain Hit Points, but damage it takes is reduced by your Proficiency Bonus. Once a creature benefits from Preserving Yin, it cannot benefit from your Preserving Yin again until it finishes a Long Rest. #### Moonlit Preservation Action Type: Ritual Procedure Canonical Action Type: Ritual Procedure Factory Routing: procedure_ledger_not_combat_action Timing Detail: Ritual Time: 10 minutes Range: Touch Duration: 24 hours Cost: 2 CP You preserve one corpse, herb bundle, beast core, food supply, alchemical ingredient, fragile object, document, wound pattern, footprint, bloodstain, scent trace, or Small room. The subject does not rot, decay, spoil, dry out, mold, fade, or lose ordinary potency for the duration. At CL 10, the duration becomes 7 days. At CL 15, the duration becomes 30 days. Moonlit Preservation does not restore life, repair destroyed objects, halt a soul’s departure, or prevent magical corruption unless another feature says so. #### Veil of Waning Breath Action Type: Action Factory Combat Bucket: action Factory Routing: combat_action_row Range: 60 feet Area: 15-foot-radius sphere Duration: Concentration, up to 1 minute Cost: 2 CP You create an area of inward-turning breath, cold haze, and spiritual quiet. The area is Lightly Obscured. When a creature inside the area gains a Waning Mark, you may choose for the area to become Heavily Obscured for that creature until the start of your next turn. This heavier concealment represents the world withdrawing from the marked creature’s attention; it does not automatically make any creature Hidden. A creature with Blindsight, Truesight, or an appropriate revealing technique may ignore this concealment within that sense or technique’s range. #### The Quiet After Speech Action Type: No Action Factory Combat Bucket: passive Factory Routing: passive_or_triggered_modifier_row Trigger: You spend a Waning Mark from a creature that spoke, shouted, used a verbal spell component, issued a command, or activated a sound-based technique during the current turn Cost: 1 CP The target’s voice trails into stillness. Until the start of its next turn, it has Disadvantage on Charisma checks relying on speech, and creatures more than 30 feet away cannot hear its voice unless it uses magical amplification or a cultivation technique with a higher CL than yours. This does not prevent verbal components by itself. At Foundation Realm, you may take Silence Receives the Name to make this effect stronger. #### Patient Moon Method Action Type: Passive Factory Combat Bucket: passive Factory Routing: passive_or_modifier_row Cost: None When you apply a Waning Mark to a creature and do not spend it before the end of your next turn, you may either move the mark to another creature within 30 feet of the original target or extend the mark’s duration until the end of your following turn. You can use this talent once per round. ### FOUNDATION REALM YIN TALENTS #### Twofold Waning Action Type: Bonus Action Factory Combat Bucket: bonus_action Factory Routing: combat_action_row Cost: 2 CP Use Mark the Waning against two different creatures within range instead of one. Until the end of your next turn, the first time you spend a Waning Mark from either target, you may immediately move the other mark to a creature within 30 feet of the second marked target. #### Borrowed Consequence Action Type: No Action Factory Combat Bucket: passive Factory Routing: passive_or_triggered_modifier_row Trigger: You reduce damage with Diminish Force Cost: None You gain Temporary HP equal to half the damage reduced, rounded down. These Temporary HP vanish at the start of your next turn. If the triggering damage was Fire, Radiant, Thunder, or Yang-aspected, add your Proficiency Bonus to the Temporary HP gained. #### Silence Receives the Name Action Type: No Action Factory Combat Bucket: passive Factory Routing: passive_or_triggered_modifier_row Trigger: You use The Quiet After Speech Cost: 2 CP The target must make a Wisdom saving throw. On a failed save, until the start of its next turn, it cannot use verbal components or activate techniques that require a spoken command, chant, kiai, mantra, or audible oath. On a successful save, the target can still speak and use verbal requirements, but its voice cannot be heard more than 10 feet away until the start of its next turn. This feature does not create an area of silence. #### Seal the Repetition Action Type: No Action Factory Combat Bucket: passive Factory Routing: passive_or_triggered_modifier_row Trigger: You spend a Waning Mark from a creature that used a named spell, sphere talent, forged technique, monster action, or cultivation ability Cost: 3 CP Saving Throw: Wisdom The target must make a Wisdom saving throw. On a failed save, the target cannot use the same named spell, sphere talent, forged technique, monster action, or cultivation ability again until the end of its next turn. On a successful save, the target can repeat the ability, but if it does so before the end of its next turn, it gains a Waning Mark immediately after the repeated ability resolves. #### Yin Sinking Step Action Type: Bonus Action Factory Combat Bucket: bonus_action Factory Routing: combat_action_row Range: Self Duration: Until the end of the current turn Cost: 2 CP Until the end of your turn, you can move through spaces occupied by marked creatures, and marked creatures cannot make Opportunity Attacks against you. If you spend a Waning Mark during this movement, you may move through one solid object or barrier no more than 5 feet thick. This movement is not teleportation. If you end your turn inside an object, you are shunted to the nearest unoccupied space and take 2d10 Force damage. This feature cannot pass through a ward, Formation, Barrier, or sealed boundary designed to block incorporeal or spiritual movement unless your CL exceeds the effect’s CL or the GM rules otherwise. #### Stillness Has Teeth Action Type: No Action Factory Combat Bucket: passive Factory Routing: passive_or_triggered_modifier_row Trigger: You spend a Waning Mark Cost: 1 CP The marked creature takes Cold or Necrotic damage equal to your Proficiency Bonus + your Key Ability modifier. This damage is a consequence of the mark collapsing. It is deliberately modest: the talent rewards repeated diminishing without turning Yin into a primary damage sphere. #### Grave-Quiet Archivist Action Type: Passive Factory Combat Bucket: passive Factory Routing: passive_or_modifier_row Cost: None When you use Moonlit Preservation on a corpse, record, herb, beast core, alchemical ingredient, spiritual remnant, weapon, talisman, or scene of violence, you may also preserve one clear trace connected to it. Examples include the last scent on a cloak, the final wound pattern on a corpse, the color of qi in a broken talisman, or the taste of poison in a cup. A creature examining the preserved subject has Advantage on one Investigation, Medicine, Nature, Arcana, Survival, or appropriate skill check related to that preserved evidence. #### No Dawn in the Wound Action Type: Action Factory Combat Bucket: action Factory Routing: combat_action_row Range: 60 feet Duration: Concentration, up to 1 minute Cost: 4 CP Saving Throw: Constitution Choose one creature that currently has one of your Waning Marks. The target makes a Constitution saving throw. On a failed save, the Waning Mark becomes a Dormant Wound for the duration. The first time each round that the target regains Hit Points, gains Temporary HP, restores CP, or benefits from regeneration, reduce the amount by your Proficiency Bonus + your Key Ability modifier. At the end of each of the target’s turns, it repeats the save, ending the effect on itself on a success. On a successful initial save, the Waning Mark remains, but the effect ends. ### CORE FORMATION REALM YIN TALENTS #### Yin Domain: Court of Waning Return “Within my court, every bright act must bow before its ending.” Action Type: Action Factory Combat Bucket: action Factory Routing: combat_action_row Area: 30-foot-radius aura centered on you Duration: Concentration, up to 1 minute Cost: 7 CP You establish a Domain where actions begin to return to stillness before they fully complete. While inside the Domain, you gain the following benefits: Your Mark Limit increases by your Key Ability modifier, minimum 1. Once per round, when an enemy inside the Domain hits with an attack, forces a saving throw, regains Hit Points, gains Temporary HP, spends CP, uses a spell slot, teleports, or moves at least 10 feet during its turn, you may apply a Waning Mark to that enemy without using your Reaction. When you spend a Waning Mark from an enemy inside the Domain, the enemy takes Cold or Necrotic damage equal to your Proficiency Bonus. Enemies inside the Domain suffer the following effects: they cannot benefit from Advantage against you while they have one of your Waning Marks; the first time each round they repeat the same named spell, sphere talent, forged technique, monster action, or cultivation ability they used on their previous turn, they gain one Waning Mark after the repeated ability resolves; if they begin their turn with a Waning Mark, their Speed is reduced by 10 feet until the start of their next turn. The Domain is not darkness or silence. It may appear as moonless stillness, pale frost, a muffled court, or ink-black breath, but its mechanics are the waning of repeated force. #### Return the Overextension Action Type: No Action Factory Combat Bucket: passive Factory Routing: passive_or_triggered_modifier_row Trigger: You reduce damage with Diminish Force Cost: 2 CP The creature whose damage you reduced takes Psychic, Cold, or Necrotic damage equal to the amount reduced, to a maximum of 3 x your CL. This damage represents the creature’s excess force returning inward through its own meridians. #### Moon-Ending Meridian Seal Action Type: Action Factory Combat Bucket: action Factory Routing: combat_action_row Range: 60 feet Duration: 1 minute Cost: 6 CP Saving Throw: Wisdom Choose one creature within range that currently has one of your Waning Marks. Choose one trait you know the target possesses: a damage Resistance, condition Resistance, movement mode, sense, regeneration trait, healing trait, or CP recovery trait. The target makes a Wisdom saving throw. On a failed save, apply one appropriate suppression effect: | Known Trait | Suppression Effect | | --- | --- | | Damage Resistance | The target loses that Resistance. | | Condition Resistance | The target loses that condition Resistance. | | Movement mode | The chosen movement mode is reduced by 20 feet, minimum 0. | | Sense | The chosen sense’s range is reduced by 20 feet, minimum 0. | | Regeneration or healing trait | The target cannot use that trait to regain Hit Points. | | CP recovery trait | The target reduces CP recovered from that trait by your Proficiency Bonus + Key Ability modifier. | At the end of each of the target’s turns, it repeats the save, ending the effect on itself on a success. A creature can be affected by only one Moon-Ending Meridian Seal from you at a time. This talent cannot remove Immunity unless the target is lower Realm than you or a Secret Inheritance, artifact, or GM-approved countermeasure allows it. #### Preserve the Unfinished State Action Type: Reaction Factory Combat Bucket: reaction Factory Routing: combat_action_row Trigger: A creature, object, corpse, wound, spell residue, Formation trace, or spiritual imprint within 60 feet would decay, vanish, close, disperse, or become impossible to examine Duration: 1 hour Cost: 5 CP You preserve the subject in its current unfinished state. The subject does not heal, rot, fade, disperse, close, or become further corrupted for the duration. This can preserve evidence, hold open a wound for later diagnosis, maintain a fading magical aura long enough to study it, or delay the collapse of a spiritual imprint. This does not keep a living creature alive, prevent damage, restrain a target, or stop a hostile effect from functioning unless another feature says so. At CL 15, you may spend 10 CP to extend the duration to 24 hours. #### Incomplete Departure Action Type: Reaction Factory Combat Bucket: reaction Factory Routing: combat_action_row Trigger: A marked creature within 90 feet teleports, enters another plane, becomes incorporeal, or uses a feature that would move it without crossing the intervening distance Cost: 6 CP Saving Throw: Wisdom Spend the creature’s Waning Mark. The target makes a Wisdom saving throw. On a failed save, the movement is diminished. The target completes only half the distance, rounded down to the nearest 5 feet, and must appear in the nearest unoccupied legal space along the intended path or at the nearest legal partial destination. If no legal partial destination exists, the movement fails. On a successful save, the movement succeeds, but the target cannot take Reactions until the start of its next turn. This feature cannot interrupt a Secret Inheritance, divine intervention, artifact effect, or higher-Realm spatial technique unless the GM rules your Yin cultivation is an appropriate counter. #### Black Moon Reads the Flame Action Type: No Action Factory Combat Bucket: passive Factory Routing: passive_or_triggered_modifier_row Trigger: You apply a Waning Mark to a creature that dealt Fire, Radiant, Lightning, Thunder, or Yang-aspected damage during the current turn Cost: None You learn one of the following facts about the triggering effect, chosen by you: whether it was a spell, sphere talent, forged technique, item, innate feature, or monster action; whether the effect spent CP, a spell slot, item charges, or another limited resource; whether the creature can use the same effect again before the end of its next turn; whether the effect came from the creature’s body, soul, weapon, item, Formation, or external patron. This feature does not identify every detail of the effect, but it tells you how the overextension entered the world. ### NASCENT SOUL REALM YIN TALENTS #### Sovereign Yin Incarnation “I do not chase the world. The world tires, and returns to me.” Action Type: Bonus Action Factory Combat Bucket: bonus_action Factory Routing: combat_action_row Duration: 1 minuteConcentration: Not required Cost: 15 CP Use Limit: Once per Long Rest You become a sovereign vessel of receptive stillness. For the duration, you gain the following benefits: Your Mark Limit doubles. Once on each of your turns, you may use Mark the Waning without using a Bonus Action. You may spend Waning Marks twice per round instead of once per round. When you spend a Waning Mark, choose one: gain Temporary HP equal to your Proficiency Bonus + Key Ability modifier; move 10 feet without provoking Opportunity Attacks; or become Lightly Obscured until the start of your next turn. A creature that starts its turn within 20 feet of you while marked by you must make a Constitution saving throw. On a failed save, it cannot take Reactions and its Speed is reduced by 20 feet until the start of its next turn. On a successful save, its Speed is reduced by 10 feet until the start of its next turn. Sovereign Yin Incarnation does not create darkness or silence by itself. It is the pressure of motion returning to stillness. #### The Action Arrives Incomplete Action Type: Reaction Factory Combat Bucket: reaction Factory Routing: combat_action_row Trigger: A marked creature within 90 feet completes an Action, Bonus Action, Reaction, spell, sphere talent, forged technique, monster action, or cultivation ability Cost: 10 CP Use Limit: Once per Short Rest Saving Throw: Wisdom Spend the creature’s Waning Mark. The target makes a Wisdom saving throw. On a failed save, choose one incomplete result appropriate to the triggering action: one damage roll from the action is reduced by half; one target of the action gains Advantage on its saving throw; healing or Temporary HP granted by the action are reduced to 0 for one target; teleportation or special movement granted by the action is reduced by half; one condition the action would end continues until the start of the target’s next turn; one Advantage granted by the action is canceled; one summoned, created, or conjured effect from the action appears with half its normal Hit Points or duration. On a successful save, the action functions normally, but the target gains a Waning Mark immediately after the action resolves. This talent does not undo an action after the table has moved on. Declare it immediately when the trigger occurs. #### The World Receives the Blow Action Type: Reaction Factory Combat Bucket: reaction Factory Routing: combat_action_row Trigger: A creature within 120 feet deals damage to two or more creatures with the same effect Cost: 12 CP Use Limit: Once per Long Rest You spread the consequence of the attack into the receptive world. Choose a number of damaged creatures up to your Key Ability modifier, minimum 1. Reduce the damage each chosen creature takes by 4d10 + your CL. The damaging creature gains a Waning Mark. If the effect dealt Fire, Radiant, Thunder, or Yang-aspected damage, the mark lasts for 1 minute. #### The Still Corpse Remembers Action Type: Ritual Procedure Canonical Action Type: Ritual Procedure Factory Routing: procedure_ledger_not_combat_action Timing Detail: Ritual Time: 10 minutes Range: Touch Duration: Until your next Long Rest Cost: 10 CP Touch a corpse, severed limb, destroyed construct, broken talisman, shattered weapon, spent Formation node, or collapsed spiritual remnant. You preserve its final state and draw one answer from the stillness. Ask the GM one question about the subject’s final hour, final injury, final technique, final owner, final command, final emotion, final destination, or final visible enemy. The answer must be brief but truthful from the subject’s available traces. This does not speak with the dead, summon a soul, compel a spirit, or reveal information the subject left no trace of knowing. #### No Dawn Repeats Itself Action Type: No Action Factory Combat Bucket: passive Factory Routing: passive_or_triggered_modifier_row Trigger: A creature inside your Yin Domain or affected by one of your Waning Marks uses the same named spell, sphere talent, forged technique, monster action, or cultivation ability on consecutive turns Cost: 8 CP Saving Throw: Wisdom The target makes a Wisdom saving throw. On a failed save, the repeated ability fails to activate, but the target does not spend CP, spell slots, charges, or limited uses for the failed attempt. The action used to attempt it is still spent. On a successful save, the ability functions normally, but the target gains a Waning Mark after it resolves and cannot benefit from Advantage until the start of its next turn. This is a high-Realm anti-repetition technique. It does not prevent basic weapon attacks unless the attack is part of a named technique or special action. ### Secret Inheritance - The Unfinished Action Beneath Heaven “You may begin. Heaven is not required to let you finish.” Classification: Secret Yin Talent Prerequisite: CL 17+, Yin Domain, hidden Yin scripture or forbidden lunar inheritance Action Type: Reaction Factory Combat Bucket: reaction Factory Routing: combat_action_row Range: 120 feet Cost: 18 CP Use Limit: Once per week Saving Throw: Wisdom Trigger: A creature, object, Barrier, Formation, Domain, spell, sphere talent, forged technique, monster action, cultivation ability, or supernatural event you can perceive begins to produce a consequence. You declare that the action has begun to return to stillness before it fully enters the world. The source of the triggering event makes a Wisdom saving throw. If the source is not a creature, use the creator’s Cultivation Save DC, spell save DC, Formation DC, item DC, or an appropriate GM-assigned DC. On a failed save, choose one consequence of the event. That consequence becomes incomplete: damage from the event is reduced to 0 for one target; healing from the event is reduced to 0 for one target; teleportation or planar travel from the event fails for one target; a condition the event would end does not end for one target; a condition the event would impose lasts only until the start of the affected creature’s next turn; a Barrier, Domain, or Formation created by the event appears with half its normal Hit Points, radius, or duration; a summoned or created creature appears with half its normal Hit Points and cannot take Reactions until the start of its next turn; a resource recovery effect restores nothing to one target; a declaration, oath, command, or spoken technique reaches only creatures within 10 feet of the speaker. On a successful save, the event completes, but its source gains a Waning Mark that lasts for 1 minute, and you may immediately spend that mark without counting against your once-per-round limit. The Unfinished Action Beneath Heaven cannot erase a whole scene, undo past events, negate an entire Secret Inheritance, or cancel a higher-Realm mandate by default. Against artifacts, divine interventions, Realm-defining Domains, superior cultivation-scale effects, and plot-level calamities, the GM may reduce the failed-save result to a partial weakening instead of full incompletion. This inheritance is forbidden because it proves that completion is not guaranteed. ### OPTIONAL CULTIVATION VARIANTS Some Yin traditions narrow how the sphere manifests. If a variant grants a bonus talent or improves a core feature, it also includes a drawback. Each variant changes table play by adding a benefit and, when needed, a drawback. #### Preserving Yin Tradition You cultivate Yin as preservation rather than harm. Your Yin receives decline, holds evidence, protects the dying, and prevents harmful motion from completing. It does not easily hasten death on its own. Benefit. You gain Moonlit Preservation as a bonus talent. When you use Moonlit Preservation, increase its duration by one step: 24 hours becomes 7 days, 7 days becomes 30 days, and 30 days becomes 1 year. When you use Withdrawing Thread, you may choose to deal no damage. If you do, the target still gains a Waning Mark on a hit. Drawback: Vow of Preservation. You cannot use Withdrawing Thread or a Yin talent to deal damage to a living creature unless that creature has damaged another creature, forced another creature to make a saving throw, spent CP, used a spell slot, used a supernatural feature, or willingly caused a hostile supernatural effect since the start of its last turn. This drawback does not prevent you from: placing Waning Marks without dealing damage; spending Waning Marks to reduce damage, healing, movement, attack rolls, saving throw pressure, CP recovery, or other consequences; using Yin against undead, constructs, objects, barriers, poisons, diseases, curses, corruption, hostile Formations, environmental hazards, or nonliving magical effects; using Yin to preserve evidence, stabilize decline, conceal refugees, protect allies, or suppress an ongoing harmful effect. If there is doubt about whether a target has recently caused hostile supernatural harm, the GM decides. Preserving Yin is meant to answer violence, corruption, and collapse. It is not meant to be a free damage tradition with better preservation. #### Moonless Auditor You cultivate Yin as investigation, hidden judgment, and patient witnessing. You gain Grave-Quiet Archivist as a bonus talent. You may use Mark the Waning on a creature that lies to you, breaks an oath in your presence, destroys evidence, or attempts to conceal a spiritual trace within 60 feet. This does not reveal whether the creature lied or what evidence was hidden; it only lets your Yin mark the act of concealment. #### Waning Assassin You cultivate Yin through ambush and the final breath before violence. When you hit a creature that cannot see or hear you with Withdrawing Thread or a weapon attack, you may apply a Waning Mark without using Mark the Waning. However, your Mark Limit is reduced by 1, minimum 1. This variant is better at beginning a decline than maintaining a court of stillness. ### PATH SYNERGIES #### Spirit Awakening: Receptive Soul Your spirit receives the shape of an action before your body moves. Once per round when a creature you can perceive spends CP, uses a spell slot, or activates a supernatural feature, you may apply a Waning Mark to that creature without using your Reaction. You cannot do this if you are Incapacitated. While a creature has one of your Waning Marks, you have Advantage on Wisdom saving throws against that creature’s possession, fear, charm, dream intrusion, or forced soul movement effects. #### Qi Cultivation: Sinking Meridian Your qi flows inward, down, and back toward stillness. Once per turn when you spend CP on a Yin talent that spends or modifies a Waning Mark, reduce the CP cost by 1, to a minimum cost of 1 CP. In addition, when you maintain Concentration on a Yin talent, you may add +1 to Constitution saving throws made to maintain that Concentration. #### Body Refining: Still Vessel Body This synergy requires the Still Vessel Body Insight. You may use Constitution as your Yin key ability and spend Stamina instead of CP for Yin talents. When you spend a Waning Mark with Diminish Force against damage that would affect you, reduce the damage by an additional amount equal to your Proficiency Bonus. This synergy does not grant Resistance, Immunity, armor, natural weapons, or extra attacks unless a separate feature says so. ### CULTIVATION INSIGHTS #### Still Vessel Body Prerequisite: Body Refining, CL 4+ You may learn Yin talents. When using Yin, you use Constitution as your key ability and spend Stamina instead of CP. You gain the Still Vessel Body Path synergy. #### Patient Foundation Prerequisite: Yin sphere, CL 4+ When you roll Initiative and have no Waning Marks active, choose one creature you can perceive. That creature gains a Waning Mark. If you are surprised, you cannot use this Insight until after your first turn in combat. #### Quiet Foundation Prerequisite: Yin sphere, CL 8+ Once per Long Rest, when you would fail a Constitution saving throw made to maintain Concentration on a Yin talent, you may choose to succeed instead. #### No Excess Within Prerequisite: Yin sphere, CL 8+ When you spend a Waning Mark on a willing ally, the ally may immediately end one effect that grants it Advantage on attack rolls or increases its damage. If it does, the ally gains Temporary HP equal to your Proficiency Bonus + your Key Ability modifier. This Insight is used by austere Yin sects that reject overextension even in themselves. #### Black-Moon Archivist Prerequisite: Yin sphere, CL 8+ When you preserve evidence with Moonlit Preservation or Grave-Quiet Archivist, you may also preserve one spiritual impression. A creature examining the preserved subject may make one appropriate skill check with Advantage to learn the emotional tone, qi texture, Realm category, or sphere resonance of the preserved trace. This does not identify a creature by name unless other evidence supports that conclusion. #### Waning Counter-Scripture Prerequisite: Yin sphere, CL 12+ When a creature with one of your Waning Marks repeats a named technique, spell, sphere talent, or monster action it used since the start of its previous turn, you may spend the mark to impose Disadvantage on one attack roll made by that ability or grant Advantage to one saving throw against that ability. If the ability has neither attack rolls nor saving throws, reduce one damage roll, healing roll, or distance of movement from the ability by your Proficiency Bonus + Key Ability modifier.

resolved_automatic_base_abilities.effect:
### BASE SPHERE ABILITIES
The Yin sphere uses Waning Marks. A Waning Mark is not a condition. Immunity to a condition does not grant immunity to Waning Marks unless a feature says otherwise.
A Waning Mark represents a motion, technique, wound, breath, or intention that has begun to decline before it finishes expressing itself.
#### Mark Limit
You can maintain a number of Waning Marks equal to your Proficiency Bonus. A creature can have only one Waning Mark from you at a time unless a feature says otherwise.
A Waning Mark lasts until the end of your next turn, until you spend it, or until the marked creature is no longer on the same plane of existence as you.
#### Marking a Creature
You can apply a Waning Mark in three basic ways.
Mark the Waning. As a Bonus Action, choose one creature within 60 feet that you can see, hear, or otherwise perceive clearly. The target gains one Waning Mark.
Receive Overextension. As a Reaction when a creature within 60 feet that you can perceive hits with an attack, forces a saving throw, regains Hit Points, gains Temporary HP, spends CP, uses a spell slot, teleports, or moves at least 10 feet during its turn, you may apply one Waning Mark to that creature after the triggering event resolves.
Withdrawing Thread. As an Action, make a ranged Cultivation Attack against one creature or object within 60 feet. On a hit, the target takes Cold or Necrotic damage, chosen when you make the attack, and gains one Waning Mark.
| Cultivation Level | Withdrawing Thread Damage |
| --- | --- |
| CL 1-4 | 1d6 |
| CL 5-10 | 2d6 |
| CL 11-16 | 3d6 |
| CL 17-20 | 4d6 |
The damage is not the sphere’s identity. It is the visible symptom of qi cooling as the target’s action begins to wane.
#### Spending a Waning Mark
Once per round, when a marked creature you can perceive performs a triggering act, you may spend its Waning Mark without using an Action. Choose one Diminishing Response appropriate to the trigger.
**Diminish Force**
Trigger: the marked creature deals damage. Reduce one damage roll by 1d6 + your Key Ability modifier. This reduction increases to 2d6 at CL 5, 3d6 at CL 11, and 4d6 at CL 17.
**Diminish Aim**
Trigger: the marked creature makes an attack roll. Subtract 1d4 from the attack roll. At CL 11, subtract 1d6 instead.
**Diminish Power**
Trigger: the marked creature forces one or more creatures to make a saving throw. Choose one creature making that saving throw. The chosen creature adds 1d4 to the saving throw. At CL 11, the bonus becomes 1d6.
**Diminish Step**
Trigger: the marked creature begins movement, including teleportation. Reduce one of the creature’s Speeds by 10 feet until the end of the current turn, or reduce the distance of one teleportation effect by 10 feet. At CL 11, the reduction becomes 20 feet.
**Diminish Recovery**
Trigger: the marked creature regains Hit Points, gains Temporary HP, restores CP, or benefits from regeneration. Reduce the amount gained or restored by your Proficiency Bonus + your Key Ability modifier, to a minimum of 0.
**Diminish Readiness**
Trigger: the marked creature takes a Reaction or would gain Advantage on a roll. The creature cannot take Reactions until the start of its next turn, or the triggering Advantage is canceled for that roll.
#### Yin Saves
Some Yin features require a saving throw. Unless a feature says otherwise, your Cultivation Save DC equals your Cultivation Save DC.
#### Marked Allies
You may place a Waning Mark on a willing ally. When you do, the mark represents preservation rather than harm. You may spend that mark only for Diminish Force, Diminish Power, Diminish Step, or Diminish Recovery if doing so benefits the ally.
A willing creature may end your Waning Mark on itself at any time, no Action required.

resolved_automatic_base_abilities.effect:
#### Spending a Waning Mark
Once per round, when a marked creature you can perceive performs a triggering act, you may spend its Waning Mark without using an Action. Choose one Diminishing Response appropriate to the trigger.
**Diminish Force**
Trigger: the marked creature deals damage. Reduce one damage roll by 1d6 + your Key Ability modifier. This reduction increases to 2d6 at CL 5, 3d6 at CL 11, and 4d6 at CL 17.
**Diminish Aim**
Trigger: the marked creature makes an attack roll. Subtract 1d4 from the attack roll. At CL 11, subtract 1d6 instead.
**Diminish Power**
Trigger: the marked creature forces one or more creatures to make a saving throw. Choose one creature making that saving throw. The chosen creature adds 1d4 to the saving throw. At CL 11, the bonus becomes 1d6.
**Diminish Step**
Trigger: the marked creature begins movement, including teleportation. Reduce one of the creature’s Speeds by 10 feet until the end of the current turn, or reduce the distance of one teleportation effect by 10 feet. At CL 11, the reduction becomes 20 feet.
**Diminish Recovery**
Trigger: the marked creature regains Hit Points, gains Temporary HP, restores CP, or benefits from regeneration. Reduce the amount gained or restored by your Proficiency Bonus + your Key Ability modifier, to a minimum of 0.
**Diminish Readiness**
Trigger: the marked creature takes a Reaction or would gain Advantage on a roll. The creature cannot take Reactions until the start of its next turn, or the triggering Advantage is canceled for that roll.

talents.exact_heading: #### Breath Beyond the Skin - Realm Evolution
talents.full_description:
Prerequisite: CL 5+
Your Air Qi can exist outside your lungs and limbs as a stable local current.
Gain the following benefits:
Your Gather Current duration becomes 1 minute if you maintain Concentration.
You may maintain two Air Currents at the same time.
Wind Lash’s forced movement options can affect creatures up to two sizes larger than you.
Your Air techniques can affect magical smoke, spiritual mist, ghost-breath, corpse-wind, and similar supernatural airlike phenomena if the GM agrees they have an exposed current.
You may create temporary breathable air for yourself for 10 minutes once per short or long rest.
Breath Beyond the Skin does not grant unrestricted flight, vacuum immunity, or control over all weather.

talents.exact_heading: #### Court of the Four Winds - Domain
talents.full_description:
Prerequisite: CL 12+, Breath Beyond the Skin
Action Type: Bonus Action
Factory Combat Bucket: bonus_action
Factory Routing: combat_action_row
Range: Self
Area: 60-foot Emanation
Duration: 1 minute
Cost: 2 CP
Use Limit: Once per short or long rest
You establish a court of moving air around yourself. Choose four winds when the court appears: North, South, East, and West. Each wind is assigned one Vector: Lift, Press, Cut, Carry, Turn, or Scatter. You cannot assign the same Vector to more than two winds.
For the duration:
You may maintain up to four Air Currents without counting them against your Air Control Limit.
Once on each of your turns, you may use Gather Current without an action.
When a creature starts its turn inside the court, you may move one active Current up to 20 feet.
Your Wind Lash may originate from any active Current inside the court.
Allied creatures inside one of your Currents gain +10 feet to Speed while moving in the direction you choose.
Hostile creatures moving against one of your Currents treat the space as Difficult Terrain.
Once per round when an ordinary ranged weapon attack passes through one of your Currents, you may impose Disadvantage on that attack without using your Reaction.
The court ends early if you are Incapacitated or if you enter an airless sealed region that prevents currents from existing.

talents.exact_heading: #### Breath of No Distance - Breath, Current
talents.full_description:
Prerequisite: CL 15+
You can carry breath through the world’s air.
As an Action, choose one creature you know on the same plane within 10 miles. You must have a clear symbolic or physical connection: name, token, blood mark, talisman, familiar scent, active formation link, or current line of sight.
You may send a spoken message of up to one hundred words to that creature. If the creature is willing, it may answer with up to one hundred words.
If the path between you is blocked by sealed barriers, underground isolation, planar interference, a stronger Formation, or Void concealment, make an Air Check against the obstacle’s DC. On a failure, the message scatters and both creatures hear only wind.

talents.full_description:
Secret Air Inheritance
Prerequisites: Sky-Sovereign Incarnation, CL 17+, access to a true sky scripture, storm-gate inheritance, or heavenly breath revelation
Action Type: Action
Factory Combat Bucket: action
Factory Routing: combat_action_row
Range: Self
Area: 1-mile-radius sky and ground region centered on you
Duration: Instantaneous, with aftermath until the end of your next turn
Cost: 5 CP
Use Limit: Once per week
You make the sky exhale once.
Choose up to three of the following decrees. Each hostile creature, projectile, flying object, or active windlike technique in the area is affected as appropriate.
The Breath Returns: Breath-dependent hostile creatures make a Constitution saving throw. On a failure, they cannot speak, shout, chant, command, or use breath-required techniques until the end of your next turn. On a success, they cannot take Reactions until the start of your next turn.
The Arrows Lose Their Road: Ordinary ranged weapon attacks, thrown weapons, volleys, and non-Secret physical projectile techniques in the area fail against targets you choose until the start of your next turn.
The Sky Rejects Weight: Allied creatures you choose gain a Fly Speed of 60 feet and Hover until the end of your next turn.
The Ground Receives the Proud: Hostile flying creatures make a Strength saving throw. On a failure, they descend up to 300 feet, land if possible, and fall Prone. On a success, their Fly Speed is halved until the end of their next turn.
The World Turns Sideways: Choose a direction. Hostile creatures and unattended objects not anchored to the ground are pushed 60 feet in that direction. A creature may make a Strength saving throw to halve the distance.
The Gate Opens: Create a Sky Road up to 1 mile long that lasts until the end of your next turn without Concentration.
After resolving the decrees, you may immediately move up to your Speed or Fly Speed without provoking Opportunity Attacks.
Limits: When Heaven Exhales does not create regional weather permanently, erase mountains, move sealed buildings, kill breathless creatures automatically, or bypass stronger domain-scale authority without an opposed Cultivation Check. Creatures inside airtight sealed structures are affected only if the chosen decree can reach them through an air path or through a superior inheritance-level contest.

talents.full_description:
You learn the Furnace Vent Field Formula.
Action Type: Action
Canonical Action Type: Action
Factory Combat Bucket: action
Timing Detail: Field Formula
Factory Routing: combat_action_row; field_formula_detail
Area: 15-foot cone.
Cost: 1 CP and one Reagent Stock.
You crack a sealed heat-packet, smoke tube, or small furnace vent, releasing scalding medicinal vapor and bitter fumes. Each creature in the area makes a Constitution saving throw.
Failed Save: The creature takes Poison or Fire damage equal to 1d8 + your Alchemy key ability modifier, chosen when you use this formula, and has Disadvantage on the next Constitution saving throw it makes before the start of your next turn.
Successful Save: Half damage and no Disadvantage.
The damage increases to 2d8 at CL 5, 3d8 at CL 11, and 4d8 at CL 17.

A Pill Spirit is not a familiar, servant, combat creature, or permanent companion unless another feature says otherwise.

talents.exact_heading: ### Court of the Three-Legged Cauldron - Alchemy Domain
talents.full_description:
Prerequisite: CL 10+.
Action Type: Bonus Action
Factory Combat Bucket: bonus_action
Factory Routing: combat_action_row
Range: Self.
Area: 30-foot-radius Emanation.
Duration: 1 minute.
Cost: Expend Martial Focus if you have it, or spend 5 CP if you do not.
Use Limit: Once per Short Rest.
You manifest an alchemical court of furnace heat, rotating medicinal smoke, floating pill sigils, and visible dregs of failed refinement.
While the Domain lasts:
your Alchemy Checks gain +2;
your Field Formula range increases by 30 feet;
once per turn when you use Field Formula, reduce its CP cost by 1, minimum 0;
allies of your choice who start their turns in the Domain gain Temporary HP equal to your Proficiency Bonus;
hostile creatures of your choice treat the Domain as lightly obscured by medicinal steam, though this does not hide you from creatures that can still see you clearly;
the first time each turn a hostile creature fails a saving throw against one of your Alchemy techniques in the Domain, it takes extra Acid, Fire, Poison, or Force damage equal to your Alchemy key ability modifier.
The Domain is magical.

Prerequisite: CL 10+.
Learn one Eternal Pill Formula. You may learn this talent multiple times, choosing a different formula each time.
Each Eternal Pill is Very Rare, costs 2,500 gp in ingredients, costs 10 CP to refine, requires 7 days, and benefits a creature only once per Realm.
Choose one:
Longevity Pill: Slow ordinary aging and stabilize bodily decline. The exact lifespan effect is campaign-facing and set by the GM.
Vitality Pill: Increase maximum HP by 5.
Meridian Pill: Increase maximum CP by 2.
Resistance Pill: Gain Resistance to one damage type chosen when the pill is refined. The GM may forbid Force, Psychic, Radiant, Necrotic, or another rare type unless the ingredients justify it.
Ability-Refining Pill: Increase one ability score by 1, within the campaign’s Realm maximum.
These pills are Enhancement pills and count against Pill Saturation.

When you create the area, choose Acid, Fire, or Poison.
Hostile creatures of your choice that start their turns in the area make a Constitution saving throw.
Failed Save: The creature takes 5d6 damage of the chosen type and suffers one of the following effects, chosen when you create the area:
Burn Away Dross: The creature cannot regain HP until the start of its next turn.
Numb the Meridians: The creature cannot take Reactions until the start of its next turn.
Clog the Breath: The creature cannot speak above a whisper or supply Verbal components until the start of its next turn.
Successful Save: Half damage and no additional effect.
Allies of your choice that start their turns in the area gain Temporary HP equal to your Proficiency Bonus + your Alchemy key ability modifier.
The area is not a wall and does not provide cover.

Prerequisite: CL 17+, Heaven-Defying Pill, lost scripture, GM approval.
DC: 32 or higher.
Ingredient
Cost: 100,000 gp, three Heavenly Materials, one Realm-specific treasure, and one personal karmic price chosen by the GM.
Refinement
Time: 1 year.
Use Limit: Once per lifetime per alchemist and once per lifetime per consumer.
You refine a pill that condenses an entire Realm crossing into one dangerous miracle.
If the refinement succeeds and the consumer survives the administration, the consumer immediately advances to the first CL of the next Realm.
Then resolve:
a Heavenly Tribulation;
a foundation-stability check;
a Pill Impurity crisis;
any story consequences of forcing Heaven to answer.
Foundation-Stability Check: Constitution, Wisdom, or the consumer’s Path key ability, chosen by the GM based on the consumer’s method.
DC: 20 + the number of CLs effectively skipped.
Failure: The consumer advances but gains a severe lasting flaw, unstable foundation, damaged meridian, warped soul mark, corrupted body, or comparable defect.
Realm Ascension Pill cannot bypass a sealed destiny, destroyed soul, divine prohibition, Secret curse, campaign-specific cultivation lock, or GM-declared impossibility.
This Secret Inheritance should be legendary, feared, politically explosive, and rarely safe.

#### Read the Ruins - Unique Ash Talent
Action Type: Ritual Procedure
Canonical Action Type: Ritual Procedure
Factory Routing: procedure_ledger_not_combat_action
Timing Detail: Ritual
Time: 10 minutes
Range: Touch
Cost: 1 CP
Study ash, soot, cinders, cremation residue, or burned remains.
Learn broad information:
whether the source was ordinary, magical, alchemical, or spiritual;
approximate age of the residue;
whether a creature died nearby;
whether Fire, Magma, Lightning, Sun, or another major heat effect contributed;
whether spiritual residue remains;
whether destruction was sudden or gradual.
Read the Ruins provides evidence, not perfect historical reconstruction.

talents.full_description:
You may enter, move through, and fight inside a hostile creature’s space.
To enter its space, make:
Dexterity (Acrobatics)
contested by the creature’s:
Strength (Athletics) or Dexterity (Acrobatics)
The creature chooses which skill to use.
Failed Check: Your movement ends in the previous space and the creature may make an opportunity attack against you.
Attacks you make while sharing a hostile creature’s space have Disadvantage unless made with:
Light weapons;
natural weapons;
unarmed strikes.
Cover If you and the hostile creature are the same size, each grants the other Half Cover against creatures outside the shared space.
If one creature is larger, the smaller creature gains Three-Quarters Cover and the larger creature gains no cover.
If this cover causes an outside attack to miss, resolve the attack against the other creature using the original attack roll.

talents.full_description:
Secret Axes Inheritance
Prerequisites: CL 17+, Mountain-Felling Axe Body, One Axe Opens the Gate, access to a true headsman's scripture, mountain-felling inheritance, ancestral execution axe, or heavenly woodcutter revelation
Action Type: Action
Factory Combat Bucket: action
Factory Routing: combat_action_row
Range: Self
Area: 120-foot Emanation centered on you
Duration: Instantaneous, with aftermath until the end of your next turn
Cost: 5 CP or 5 Stamina
Use Limit: Once per week
You raise the axe and demand that Heaven show the root of what stands before you.
Choose up to three decrees.
**The Guard Was a Branch.** Hostile creatures of your choice in the area that are benefiting from shields, defensive stances, Half Cover, Three-Quarters Cover, or non-Secret temporary guard effects make a Strength saving throw. On a failure, one such benefit is suppressed until the end of your next turn. On a success, that benefit is suppressed until the start of your next turn.
**The Gate Had a Grain.** Choose one visible barrier, gate, ward panel, wall section, formation node, conjured shell, or comparable structure in the area. Make an Axes Check against its DC. On success, open a 15-foot passage through it until the end of your next turn. On failure, mark its weakest visible point; the next attack or check made by you or an ally against that point before the end of your next turn has Advantage.
**The Oath Had a Neck.** Choose one visible command object, oath banner, officer focus, talisman standard, summoner's control mark, or spirit-binding token in the area. The controlling creature makes a Wisdom saving throw. On a failure, that object cannot be used to issue commands, maintain morale benefits, or direct summoned assets until the end of your next turn. On a success, its next such use before the end of your next turn is made with Disadvantage or grants Advantage on the first saving throw against it.
**The Giant Had a Knee.** Choose up to three creatures larger than you in the area. Each makes a Strength saving throw. On a failure, its Speed is halved, it cannot take Reactions, and if flying without hover within 60 feet of a surface, it descends to that surface and falls Prone. On a success, its Speed is reduced by 10 feet until the end of its next turn.
**The Blood Had a Door.** Choose one Bloodied creature in the area that you can see. It makes a Constitution saving throw. On a failure, it cannot regain HP, gain Temporary HP, teleport, or become Invisible until the end of your next turn. On a success, it cannot regain HP until the start of your next turn.
**The Forest Fell Away.** Choose a 120-foot line or 60-foot cone in the area. Mundane roots, brambles, barricades, rope fields, wooden obstacles, fragile cover, deadwood, bone thickets, and similar obstructions in that area are cut, scattered, or opened enough to remove difficult terrain and clear a 10-foot-wide route until the end of your next turn. Cultivated obstructions require an Axes Check against their DC.
After resolving the decrees, you may immediately move up to half your Speed and make one Hewing Strike without spending an additional action.
Limits: When Heaven Chooses the Root does not kill creatures automatically, fell mountains casually, erase Domains, destroy ancient formations, bypass Total Cover without a path, or sever abstract concepts without an appropriate target object, oath focus, spirit mark, or exposed structure. Stronger authorities may require opposed Cultivation Checks or may be immune.

talents.full_exact_source_text:
#### Stair Shot - Realm Evolution
Prerequisite: CL 5+
Action Type: Action
Factory Combat Bucket: action
Factory Routing: combat_action_row
Requirement: Ammunition suitable for embedding into a surface
Spend 10 pieces of ammunition to create a temporary stair, bridge, or ledge of projectiles along a mostly vertical surface.
The structure:
extends up to 5 feet x CL;
may travel horizontally, upward, or downward;
cannot rise or descend more steeply than 45 degrees;
requires a wall, cliff, structure, large creature, or comparable surface;
supports ordinary movement at the GM’s discretion. Expend Martial Focus to create the structure as a Reaction, such as when catching a falling creature or building an emergency platform.
Stair Shot normally requires arrows, bolts, or comparable ammunition.

Excess weapons land in unoccupied spaces near you.

talents.exact_heading: #### Court of Falling Stars - Martial Domain “The sky did not become crowded. The cultivator simply stopped accepting empty angles.”
talents.full_description:
The cultivator simply stopped accepting empty angles.”
Prerequisite: CL 10+
Action Type: Bonus Action
Factory Combat Bucket: bonus_action
Factory Routing: combat_action_row
Duration: 1 minute
Cost: Expend Martial Focus
Use Limit: Once per short rest
For the duration:
You
increase ranged and thrown weapon normal range by 30 feet;
ignore Half Cover;
draw ammunition and thrown weapons without spending an Action;
regain Martial Focus once per turn when at least two Barrage attacks hit;
make one ranged opportunity attack each round without expending your Reaction when a hostile creature willingly moves more than 10 feet within your normal weapon range.
Allies Choose up to your Proficiency Bonus allies when activating the Court.
They gain:
+2 to Wisdom (Perception) checks against visible creatures you have attacked this round;
Advantage on one attack roll against a creature hit by at least two of your Barrage attacks before the start of your next turn. Court of Falling Stars ends early if you become Incapacitated.

talents.exact_heading: #### One Arrow Becomes Ten Thousand “The master did not loose a volley. The master released the certainty that one projectile had ever been alone.”
talents.full_description:
“The master did not loose a volley. The master released the certainty that one projectile had ever been alone.”
Classification: Secret Barrage Inheritance
Prerequisite: CL 17+, Sovereign Arsenal Incarnation, hidden projectile scripture
Action Type: Action
Factory Combat Bucket: action
Factory Routing: combat_action_row
Range: Weapon range or 300 feet, whichever is greater
Cost: Expend Martial Focus
Use Limit: Once per week
Make one ranged weapon attack against one creature, object, Barrier, or structure section.
On a hit, the single projectile becomes a perfect converging storm.
Creature
Deal:
12 weapon damage dice + twice your ability modifier
Then choose three:
push the target 20 feet;
knock it Prone;
reduce Speed to 0 until the end of your next turn;
prevent Reactions until the end of your next turn;
ignore ordinary Resistance to the weapon’s damage type;
strike up to three additional hostile creatures within 30 feet for half damage;
create a 20-foot-radius Sky-Net Suppression area centered on the target until the start of your next turn.
Object, Barrier, or Structure Deal:
16 weapon damage dice + twice your ability modifier
This damage ignores ordinary hardness.
Miss
On a miss, the projectile divides imperfectly.
Choose one hostile creature within 30 feet of the original target and make one additional ranged weapon attack against it.
One Arrow Becomes Ten Thousand does not reproduce artifacts, talismans, rare ammunition, or unique payloads.

“The beasts did not become soldiers. The soldiers finally learned to move like a pack.”

gain +10 feet Speed;
gain Advantage on checks against being shoved or moved;

use the highest Passive Perception among allies within 60 feet;
move through allied spaces normally.

take Help as a Reaction;
gain Temporary HP equal to your Proficiency Bonus. Court of Fang and Rein ends early if you become Incapacitated.

talents.full_description:
Prerequisite: CL 10+
Trigger: You score a critical hit with a melee weapon
Cost: Expend Martial Focus
Choose one recognizable limb, wing, tail, or similar anatomical structure.
The target makes a Constitution saving throw.
Failed Save: The chosen structure becomes disabled until the target completes a short or long rest or receives sufficient restorative healing.
Examples:
| Targeted Structure | Effect |
| --- | --- |
| Arm | Disadvantage on attacks made with that arm; cannot effectively use two-handed weapons |
| Leg | Speed reduced by 10 feet; Disadvantage on Dexterity saving throws |
| Wing | Lose ordinary flight dependent on that wing |
| Tail or similar appendage | Lose attacks or movement features primarily dependent on it |
Creatures without recognizable anatomy are immune.
Optional Severe Injury Module
At tables using lasting-injury rules, the GM may allow Meridian-Rending Blow to sever or permanently destroy the chosen structure on a failed save.
Literal dismemberment is not the default player-facing rule.

#### Court of the Unbroken Warpath - Martial Domain
“The battlefield did not become smaller. The warrior simply stopped recognizing obstacles as reasons to stop.”
Prerequisite: CL 12+

Factory Combat Bucket: bonus_action
Factory Routing: combat_action_row

Cost: Expend Martial Focus

For the duration:
activate one Adrenaline talent without taking the normal -2 AC penalty;
ignore nonmagical difficult terrain;
gain Resistance to forced movement;
deal double damage to unattended objects and temporary Barriers;
after reducing a creature to 0 HP or critically hitting, move 10 feet without provoking opportunity attacks;
once per turn when Batter hits a Battered target, regain Martial Focus.
Court of the Unbroken Warpath ends early if you become Incapacitated.

talents.exact_heading: #### The Blow Heaven Refused to Receive
talents.full_exact_source_text:
#### The Blow Heaven Refused to Receive
“The cultivator did not strike harder than Heaven. The cultivator struck after Heaven understood that it could not step aside.”
Classification: Secret Berserker Inheritance
Prerequisite: CL 17+, Heaven-Crushing Exertion, hidden war-god scripture
Action Type: Action
Factory Combat Bucket: action
Factory Routing: combat_action_row
Range: Reach or thrown-weapon range
Cost: Expend Martial Focus
Use Limit: Once per week
Make one Batter attack.
Before rolling:
gain Advantage;
ignore Disadvantage;
choose up to four Exertion talents you know;
treat the target as already Battered;
ignore Resistance to the attack’s damage;
ignore ordinary object Damage Thresholds.
Hit: Add:
12d10 Force damage
The target makes a Constitution saving throw.
Failed Save: It is Stunned until the end of your next turn and pushed up to 30 feet.
Successful Save: It cannot take Reactions until the start of your next turn.
If the attack strikes an object, structure, or temporary Barrier, deal double total damage.
The Blow Heaven Refused to Receive does not automatically destroy:
artifacts;
Formation cores;
Domains;
Secret Inheritances;
Realm-defining structures.
Those may still be meaningfully damaged or contested according to the GM.

talents.display_name: Furnace Court of the Thousandfold Temper
talents.exact_heading: ### Furnace Court of the Thousandfold Temper - Domain
talents.full_description:
“Every strike in the court became a hammer blow. Every breath became bellows. Every flaw had nowhere left to hide.”
Prerequisite: CL 10+
Action Type: Action
Factory Combat Bucket: action
Factory Routing: combat_action_row
Area: 30-foot Emanation originating from you
Duration: 1 minute
Cost: 4 CP
Use Limit: Once per short rest
Create a mobile furnace court around yourself.
For the duration:
you can maintain up to three current workpieces;
once at the start of each of your turns, place 1 Forge Mark on one current workpiece inside the area;
allies inside the area gain Advantage on checks made to repair, maintain, draw, stow, fit, or use prepared equipment;
the first time each round that an ally inside hits with a weapon bearing your Forge Mark, add your Proficiency Bonus to the damage roll;
the first time each round that an ally inside is hit while wearing armor or carrying a shield bearing your Forge Mark, reduce the damage by your Proficiency Bonus;
hostile unattended objects, barriers, traps, locks, and constructs inside the area reveal obvious flaws to you.
While the Domain lasts, you may use Hammer the Mark once per round without spending a Bonus Action.
Furnace Court does not create permanent equipment and does not replace a workshop for long-term crafting.

Prerequisite: CL 10+
When a workpiece has at least 3 Forge Marks from you, you may spend all of them to perform a Tempering Sequence.
Choose one:
Hardening Sequence
The workpiece gains a Temporary Temper lasting 10 minutes.
If armor or shield, it grants +1 AC.
If weapon or tool, it gains +1 to attack rolls or relevant checks.
Softening Sequence
The workpiece becomes easier to reshape.
The next repair, crafting, modification, or disarm attempt involving it before the end of the scene has Advantage.
Purifying Sequence
Reduce one mundane impurity, rust, poison residue, rot, corrosion, instability, or crafting complication affecting the workpiece.
A magical curse or artifact flaw is only reduced if the GM allows it.
Awakening Sequence
The workpiece gains the first sign of an item spirit seed until the end of the next long rest.
During that time, once when used for its named purpose, it grants Advantage on one roll.
A true awakening requires a project.

### Ten-Thousand Temper Armory - Project
Prerequisite: Sect Armorer’s Ledger, CL 15+
You can maintain a serious armory for a sect branch, expedition, guard corps, caravan fleet, or player faction.
During downtime, establish an armory with:
a secure workspace;
assistants or disciples;
inventory records;
materials;
repair protocols;
tools;
GM-approved upkeep.
While the armory is maintained, choose one armory doctrine:
#### Expedition Doctrine
Travel gear, weapons, and armor maintained by the armory ignore ordinary weather wear and reduce one travel equipment complication per journey.
#### Guard Doctrine
A number of guards or allies approved by the GM begin each prepared mission with one Temporary Temper on a weapon or armor piece.
#### Sect Duel Doctrine
A number of named duelists equal to your Proficiency Bonus may each prepare one named weapon or defensive item with Name the Purpose after a long rest.
#### Repair Doctrine
Downtime repair times for mundane equipment are reduced by half, and the armory can preserve damaged magic items until a proper repair project begins.
Ten-Thousand Temper Armory creates infrastructure, not free treasure.

• CL 1-4: Up to 1d8 + your key ability modifier.

Vital Transfusion does not restore missing limbs or remove major injuries by itself.

talents.exact_heading: #### Court of the Moving Mountain - Martial Domain
talents.full_exact_source_text:
#### Court of the Moving Mountain - Martial Domain
“The mountain did not chase its enemies. It merely decided that every direction led downhill.”
Prerequisite: CL 12+
Action Type: Bonus Action
Factory Combat Bucket: bonus_action
Factory Routing: combat_action_row
Duration: 1 minute
Cost: Expend Martial Focus
Use Limit: Once per short rest
For the duration:
gain Advantage on Strength (Athletics) checks;
count as one size larger for Shove, Grapple, and Overrun;
reduce forced movement affecting you by 10 feet;
ignore nonmagical difficult terrain created by rubble, debris, and broken ground;
when Brutal Shove succeeds, move the target 5 additional feet;
once per turn when a creature collides with terrain or another creature, regain Martial Focus.
Court of the Moving Mountain ends early if you become Incapacitated.

talents.full_description:
Prerequisite: CL 15+
Use Limit: Once per creature per long rest
When Brutal Shove succeeds, the target makes a Charisma saving throw.
Failed Save: Hurl the target into the Ethereal Plane for rounds equal to your Proficiency Bonus.
Successful Save: No additional effect.
At the end of each of its turns, the target repeats the saving throw, returning early on a success.
While Ethereal:
move in any direction;
each foot of vertical movement costs one additional foot;
see and hear the original plane within 60 feet as gray and indistinct;
affect and be affected only by Ethereal creatures and effects;
pass through ordinary objects from the original plane.
When the effect ends, return to the original plane in the corresponding space.
If occupied, shunt to the nearest legal space and take Force damage equal to twice the feet moved.
Soul Sunder has no effect when used from a plane that does not border the Ethereal Plane.

talents.full_description:
Prerequisite: Mountain-Swing Throw, CL 15+
Action Type: Action
Canonical Action Type: Action
Factory Combat Bucket: action
Timing Detail: Special Attack
Factory Routing: combat_action_row; preserve attack-replacement detail
Cost: Expend Martial Focus
Use Limit: Once per long rest
Make one Brutal Shove.
On a success:
throw the target up to 60 feet in any legal direction;
ignore ordinary size limits;
the target and creatures within 10 feet of its landing space make Dexterity saving throws.
Failed Save: Take 8d10 Bludgeoning or Force damage and fall Prone.
Successful Save: Take half damage and remain standing.
The thrown target automatically fails its save if it collides with a solid surface before landing.
Heaven-Crashing Throw does not automatically move:
artifacts;
Formation cores;
Domains;
creatures protected by a stronger immovability effect.
Those may require a contested Cultivation Check.

talents.full_description:
Tags: Tether, Lash
Action Type: Action
Factory Combat Bucket: action
Factory Routing: combat_action_row
Range: 60 feet
Cost: 1 CP
You use Set the Tether to drag a target or object.
Choose one creature or unattended object within range.
If the target is a creature, it makes a Strength saving throw.
Failed Save: Pull the target up to 15 feet toward you or toward one anchored point you can see.
Successful Save: Pull the target 5 feet.
If the target is an unattended object, you may pull an object weighing no more than 50 pounds x your CL up to 30 feet.
Pulling Chain cannot move a target into a solid object. If movement would place the target in an obviously lethal hazard, the GM may grant Advantage on the save.

talents.full_description:
Tags: Anchor, Lash
Action Type: Bonus Action
Factory Combat Bucket: bonus_action
Factory Routing: combat_action_row
Range: 30 feet
Cost: 1 CP
You hook a chain to a surface, object, enemy, ally, or anchor and move along the line.
Move up to 15 feet toward a point you can see within range without provoking opportunity attacks from creatures other than the target of the hook.
If the hook is attached to an unwilling creature, the creature makes a Strength saving throw.
Failed Save: You may move as described, and the target’s Speed is reduced by 5 feet until the start of your next turn.
Successful Save: You may move only 5 feet.
This movement must end in an unoccupied space you can occupy.

talents.full_description:
Tags: Anchor, Rescue
Action Type: Reaction
Factory Combat Bucket: reaction
Factory Routing: combat_action_row
Range: 30 feet
Trigger: A creature you can see is hit by a melee attack, ranged attack, or Chain Lash-like attack
Cost: 1 CP
You snap a chain across the blow.
Reduce the damage by 1d8 + your key ability modifier.
At Foundation Realm, reduce the damage by 2d8 + your key ability modifier.
At Core Formation Realm, reduce the damage by 3d8 + your key ability modifier.
At Nascent Soul Realm, reduce the damage by 4d8 + your key ability modifier.
If the damage is reduced to 0, you may attach a harmless Link to the attacker until the start of your next turn.
This talent protects by interception, not by general warding. It should not replace Protection sphere defensive scaling.

talents.full_description:
Tags: Tether
Action Type: Action
Factory Combat Bucket: action
Factory Routing: combat_action_row
Range: Touch
Duration: 1 minute
Cost: 1 CP
You form manacles, cuffs, rope-links, pressure-point bands, or seal-shackles on one willing, incapacitated, Grappled, Restrained, or Prone creature.
If the target is unwilling and not incapacitated, it makes a Strength saving throw.
Failed Save: The target is Bound for the duration.
Successful Save: The chains do not attach.
A Bound target may use its Action to make a Strength (Athletics) or Dexterity (Acrobatics) check against your Cultivation Save DC, ending the effect on a success.
If you use Manacle Method on a target already Restrained by one of your Chains effects, it has Disadvantage on the first escape check it makes against Manacle Method.

impose Disadvantage on one enemy’s Opportunity Attack;
deal Psychic damage equal to your Proficiency Bonus to one Frightened creature within 30 feet;
carry a whispered message of up to ten words to a creature within 60 feet.

talents.exact_heading: #### The Demon That Ate Its Own Name
talents.full_exact_source_text:
#### The Demon That Ate Its Own Name
“The first demon was chained by name. The last demon escaped by devouring the word that could command it.”
Classification: Secret Daemonic Inheritance
Prerequisite: CL 17+, Demon Emperor Incarnation, Ten-Thousand Demon Sutra, a hidden nameless demon scripture, and a personal catastrophe caused by hunger
Action Type: Special Trigger
Canonical Action Type: Special Trigger
Factory Combat Bucket: passive
Timing Detail: No Action when you would die, be sealed, have your soul destroyed, lose your cultivation base, or fail a decisive saving throw
Factory Routing: triggered_passive_modifier_row
Cost: All remaining CP, all Devoured Essence, and 3 Corruption
Use Limit: Once per campaign arc, or once ever unless the GM permits the demon’s return
Erase one immediate defeat by feeding it to the nameless demon.
Choose one:
instead of dying, remain at 1 HP and immediately activate Demon Emperor Incarnation;
instead of being sealed, break one ordinary seal and teleport to a visible space within 120 feet;
instead of losing your cultivation base, suppress the base-scattering effect until the end of the scene;
instead of failing a decisive saving throw, succeed and unleash World-Devouring Maw centered on yourself without harming chosen allies;
instead of having your soul destroyed, split off a daemonic remnant that can be recovered through a future quest.
Afterward:
Corruption becomes 10;
gain 3 Demonic Debt;
every trained Fate, Spirit, Protection, Heavenly Punishment, or Daemonic cultivator of equal or higher Realm within a vast narrative distance may sense that something forbidden survived;
the GM creates a permanent consequence tied to your name, shadow, reflection, or future tribulation.
This inheritance should save a character in a legendary moment, not become a weekly panic button.

Prerequisite: Step Through Darkness, Core Formation Realm, CL 12+
Action Type: Action
Factory Combat Bucket: action
Factory Routing: combat_action_row
Target: Self
Duration: Concentration, up to 10 minutes
Cost: 2 CP
Become an area of your own Darkness.
You become Incorporeal, gain a Fly Speed of 30 feet, and Hover.
You may move through creatures and objects as though they were difficult terrain. If you end your turn inside an object, take 1d10 Force damage.
You cannot make attacks, manipulate objects, or use your items. You may still activate sphere effects that do not require a physical action, focus, tool, weapon, or other component your incorporeal form cannot provide.
You gain Resistance to nonmagical Bludgeoning, Piercing, and Slashing damage.
As a Bonus Action, change your radius from 5 feet up to the maximum radius of one area of Darkness you control.
When you activate this talent, you may imbue yourself with one Darkness talent by paying its normal CP cost. As an Action, replace the active Darkness talent by paying the normal CP cost of the new talent.
End One With The Night early as a Bonus Action and rematerialize in one unoccupied space inside your personal Darkness area.
